title: The Great Song Dynasty Female Assassin (Hidden Shadows)
author: Xiu Tang
synopsis:
A modern elite assassin dies and returns to the Song Dynasty, becoming the formidable female assassin An Jiu. Injured during a mission, she encounters a kind and gentle girl named Mei Jiu. Mei Jiu is found by her long-lost mother, who also takes An Jiu with her.

After enrolling at the Mei Family Academy, An Jiu discovers numerous suspicious points, forcing her to conceal her abilities. Soon after, she uncovers the Mei family’s secret—training secret guards for the royal family (in reality, one of the Song Dynasty’s hidden assassin families). Meanwhile, she and Mei Jiu gradually go from misunderstanding each other to becoming good friends, and she also develops feelings for her martial arts teacher.

Just as things are going well, the Mei family is suddenly wiped out, and Mei Jiu is killed. An Jiu investigates the truth to avenge her friend and gradually becomes more and more involved in the vortex of conspiracy and love. At the same time, An Jiu also develops feelings for her master who taught her martial arts.

chapters.title: Twin Souls
chapters.content: The night was deep. A thick fog hung in the air, and hurried footsteps echoed through the grass. A dozen or so girls in pink dresses ran aimlessly across the open field. Their hair was disheveled, sweat clinging to their faces, and their skirts were torn by dry branches. A frail girl lagged behind, panting heavily. Her breath mingled with the thick fog, and her eyes were filled with fear and despair. Another girl rushed back and grabbed her. “Run! Run! Ah Jiu, they will catch up!” “Ah Shun…” the girl called Ah Jiu gasped for breath, tears streaming uncontrollably. “I… I cannot go on. You have to go.” Ah Shun pursed her lips and pulled her along, running as fast as she could. Ah Jiu was already at her limit, her legs weak, and the sudden tug caused her to collapse to the ground, too exhausted to get up. “Ah! There’s a house! There’s a house!” The group of girls could no longer be seen ahead; only their joyful shouts could be heard. Ah Shun pulled Ah Jiu up from the ground with all her might. “Did you hear that? There’s a house ahead! Hold on a little longer.” Ah Jiu’s tears flowed like a broken dam; her body was limp, and she could not take a single step. Ah Shun saw the flickering lights in the thick fog behind them, knowing their pursuers were close. She gritted her teeth, hoisted Ah Jiu onto her back, and ran as fast as she could. They had been brought from Yangzhou by human traffickers. The traffickers had tricked them into believing they were being sold to wealthy families as maids, but instead, they had been sold to the Xingxiang Brothel! Xingxiang Brothel was the most famous brothel in Bianjing, its reputation so great that even these young girls from faraway Yangzhou had heard of it. It was unclear who egged them on, but they seized the opportunity to escape en masse, without even considering what to do afterward. Ah Shun had been sold into a brothel in Yangzhou at the age of five and raised there for seven years. Initially, she did menial work in the kitchen, but the Mama noticed her growing beauty and raised her as a young lady. Therefore, she was more worldly and stronger than the other girls. Wealthy families would not want a maid bought from a brothel like her. From the beginning, she only saw this resale as an opportunity to escape, but she needed a backup plan—Ah Jiu was already very beautiful at a young age, and the Mama would definitely value her highly. If she could win Ah Jiu’s favor, even if she were unfortunately caught and taken back, as long as Ah Jiu pleaded for her, she would not be carelessly dismissed. Seeing the thatched hut, Ah Shun rushed inside in one breath, put Ah Jiu down, and breathed a long sigh of relief. By the dim light, Ah Shun saw the girls lying haphazardly and asked, “Is no one here?” One of the girls replied, “No, it seems to be a hunter’s resting place.” Were they waiting to be captured? Ah Shun glanced down at Ah Jiu, who lay sprawled like a rag doll, her eyes flickering. She turned and saw a bow and arrow hanging on the wall near the door, so she picked it up. “I will go see if anyone’s chasing us.” Ah Jiu lay sprawled on the ground, her violent chest heaving until it gradually calmed, but her gaze grew increasingly unfocused. “Ah—” The piercing scream from afar abruptly stopped halfway through, and Ah Shun’s outstretched foot retracted. The girls huddled together like a group of frightened animals, their faces filled with terror. The despair, pain, and fear in that scream were so clear; it smelled of death. Ah Shun, pale-faced, remained silent for a moment, then rushed out, followed by the girls scrambling to their feet and running away. A dozen dark figures silently landed around the courtyard in the thick fog. “Who is Mei Jiu?” a black-clad man asked, standing before the dilapidated door. These men exuded a murderous aura; they were definitely not the guards of the brothel. Ah Shun hurriedly slipped inside. “Hand over Mei Jiu, and I will spare your lives,” a cold, harsh voice rang out again. One of the bolder girls lowered her voice hesitantly. “Mei Jiu… could it be Ah Jiu they are talking about?” Ah Jiu—no one knew her surname. The people outside had no patience. Through the hazy fog, the leader of the black-clad men slightly raised his chin. A black-clad man to his right leaped into the courtyard like an eagle. Like an arrow, he darted into the house, a cold blade gleaming. He shouted at the remaining girls, “If you do not want to die by my sword, get out!” He clearly pointed in only one direction, yet everyone felt he was threatening their lives. The girls’ minds went blank; all they knew was to cry out. Without hesitation, the black-clad man swung his sword and killed the girl closest to him. Finally, someone could not bear the sight and ran out in panic. With one person leading the way, the rest followed in a daze. Seeing that only a few people remained inside, Ah Shun, holding a bow and arrow, stood out. She tightened her grip on the bow, gritted her teeth, dropped her only weapon, and ran out as well. The black-clad man with the sword saw a girl lying on the ground inside, her eyes wide open, pupils dilated, her chest no longer rising and falling. Out of habit, he bent down to check her pulse. His fingers touched the girl’s delicate skin, as if touching cool silk. She was indeed dead. He strode out. Outside, in the pitch-black night, a group of girls huddled together, trembling and making shivering sobs. “Who is Mei Jiu?” the leader of the black-clad men demanded. No one answered. Ah Shun’s face was pale, and she bit her lip tightly. A nearby black-clad man easily killed a girl with a single sword stroke. “Who is Mei Jiu?” the man asked again. The girls looked at each other in terror, trying to see if Ah Jiu was nearby so they could push her out. In that brief moment of hesitation, two more girls fell. How could they remain calm seeing the person they had spent months with splattered with blood, especially since they were just teenagers! In an instant, they scattered like frightened birds, crying and screaming, creating chaos. … “She’s inside!” Ah Shun shouted, crouching down beside the unconscious girl. She thought she was being discreet, but she had not escaped their eyes. The leader of the black-clad men asked, “Is there anyone else inside?” The man who had been ordered to enter the house bowed slightly and said, “Yes, but dead.” “Drag her out,” the leader of the black-clad men ordered. The man turned to obey. Suddenly! With a whoosh. He watched helplessly as an ordinary arrow pierced his heart, leaving him no time to react. The leader of the black-clad men standing at the door slightly opened his eyes. A spray of blood. Inside the room, Ah Jiu lay quietly by the window, her dark eyes calm and unwavering, showing no sign of fear, her entire being blending into the darkness. Sweat trickled down her temples, and the splitting pain in her head made her furrow her brow slightly. She was a lingering soul, imprisoned in a certain place since death, unable to wander or reincarnate. As time passed, her consciousness grew increasingly blurred, but now, the overwhelming killing intent around her had fully awakened her. She did not know what was happening before her, but she had an instinctive sense of danger. She discovered she could control this body, but it was severely exhausted, and she was only holding on by sheer willpower. Fortunately, a bamboo bow hung on the wall. Bows had once been her passion; before becoming a sniper, she had been a competitive archer. Unfortunately, she only had five arrows… In this situation, escape was impossible! Having been imprisoned for too long, this moment of freedom, this touch of something so familiar before death, was enough. With the mindset of “I will take down as many as I can,” she silently assessed the wind speed and humidity. With such poor visibility and equipment, it was unlikely she could kill two people with one arrow. Moreover, she could only roughly estimate the bow’s rate of fire and range. The only loophole was that her opponents did not know how many arrows she had. Thinking, she released the bowstring, accurately shooting down the black-clad figure near the window. The leader of the black-clad figures shouted, “Come out! Or I will kill them!” She recognized the girls and had no intention of accepting the threat, but just as she was about to release the arrow, she suddenly found her fingers out of control. “I want to save Ah Shun, I want to save Ah Shun…” A weak yet stubborn voice suddenly appeared in her mind. She was stunned. Could it be that she had not been reborn but was merely a ghost possessing another body?! A moment of surprise caused her to completely lose control of her body, but this time she did not lose consciousness as usual; instead, she could clearly see everything happening before her. Mei Jiu seemed to also sense the abnormality within her body, but she had no time to ponder it. She immediately dropped her bow and arrows and prepared to rush out.

chapters.title: Mei Mansion
chapters.content: Angel tried to control her body but found she could not and could not help but curse, “Idiot!” Ah Jiu paused, both frightened and strangely clinging to a sliver of hope. “Who…are you?” “You can hear me?” Angel asked in surprise, but instantly remembered the situation. “Listen to me; go back to the window and look outside.” She could see what Mei Jiu saw, but could not control her eyes. “I…” Mei Jiu gritted her teeth, wavering. “If you do not listen to me, do not even mention Ah Shun; you will not even be able to protect yourself!” Angel said coldly, but she lazily thought that even if she listened, she might not get out alive… She simply could not understand and could not stand people who were so stupid that ten oxen could not pull them back. It was just dying, but she wanted to die with some semblance of dignity. Ah Jiu wanted to go out and save people, but Angel’s voice seemed to come from the heart, and she was involuntarily bewitched. Angel could sense the inner struggle within her, so she scoffed indifferently, “If you want to be a fool who harms yourself and others, then get out!” This girl was weak-willed, and Angel was certain she would obey. But things took an unexpected turn—Mei Jiu moved her feet and slowly walked away! Angel wanted to glare, but now she could only try to regain control of the body. However, human control over the limbs was an innate instinct; there were no tricks to it. It existed naturally, but once lost, it was difficult to regain. Even though she once had a hundred times greater control than the average person, she was now helpless. As she struggled against Mei Jiu’s will, she suddenly felt a splitting headache, a flash of white light in her mind, and then abruptly plunged into darkness. She could hear a man’s voice not far away, but could not make out what he was saying. Finally, she heard Ah Shun’s heart-wrenching wails, “Sister!” ….. Dawn was approaching; a pale crescent moon adorned the night sky. Frost covered the green tiles of the rooftops, reflecting the dim moonlight, making them glisten like brocade woven with silver threads. Warm orange lights were already on, intertwining with the frosty moonlight, highlighting the layers of buildings. A mansion in the north of the city was brightly lit. The courtyard was filled with jagged rocks and winding corridors. Passing through a moon gate, one entered a spacious courtyard. The characters “Yuwei Residence” on the plaque above the main hall were elegant and prominent. As Mei Jiu awoke, Angel also saw a middle-aged woman with tears streaming down her face. Her hair was slightly disheveled, her porcelain-like skin was bloodless, and she wore a dark blue long jacket, which made her face appear even paler. “Mother!” Mei Jiu, seeing the woman, struggled to get up. The woman quickly pressed her down, choking back tears. “My child, do not be afraid; Mother is here.” At the same time, Angel, watching from the void, felt her soul slowly being permeated by a strange memory, scene after scene, all about this woman. The woman was named Mei Yanran, from the Mei family. Unlike other families, the Mei family never allowed their daughters to marry out; they only took in sons-in-law. Therefore, Mei Jiu took her mother’s surname. Aside from that, all the other memories were of the mother and daughter relying on each other for survival when they were wandering the streets. Angel was filled with vigilance; was she about to be devoured? But she possessed only a keen sense of awareness, powerless to stop it. “Jiu’er, let’s go home.” Mei Yanran’s smile held a hint of sorrow, her exquisitely beautiful face like a pear blossom in the rain, fluttering as if about to fall. Mei Jiu, oblivious to Mei Yanran’s strange behavior, was instead delighted by her words. “I can see Father?” Mentioning him, Mei Yanran’s delicate expression softened with a hint of strength. “He’s gone. He passed away several years ago.” Angel could not fathom the reason for this strange attitude, nor did she bother to speculate. She simply gazed listlessly through Mei Jiu’s eyes at the beautiful face so close to her. Frankly, she had never seen such a beautiful woman in her entire life. “Fourteenth Young Lady is awake?” a clear, melodious voice rang out. Mei Jiu looked up and saw a girl of about fifteen or sixteen years old part the curtains and enter. A gentle smile graced her round face, and two deep dimples adorned her lips, making her appear very approachable. “Yanran, Fourteenth Young Lady,” the girl greeted with a joyful bow. “Get up.” Mei Yanran took out a handkerchief and gently dabbed her eyes before saying to Mei Jiu, “This is Wen-Cui, the maid the old lady of Bixiang Residence assigned to you.” Before Mei Jiu could speak, Mei Yanran glanced at Wen-Cui indifferently. “Jiu’er does not understand the situation at home, so I will have to trouble Miss Wen-Cui to take good care of her from now on.” “This servant does not deserve such praise.” Wen-Cui quickly bowed. “You rest well; Mother is going back to sleep for a while.” Mei Yanran gently patted Mei Jiu’s hand and whispered, “Do not be afraid.” Mei Jiu felt uneasy, but seeing her mother Mei Yanran’s pale face and swollen eyes, she swallowed her words. Angel clearly sensed the unusual mood in Mei Yanran’s expression and knew that the so-called “going back” might not be a pleasant thing. “Fourteenth Young Lady, are you hungry? This servant will have someone warm some porridge and bring it to you?” Wen-Cui asked. “Yes,” Mei Jiu replied. Wen-Cui called out, “Prepare the meal.” She placed her hand on Mei Jiu’s wrist and checked it for a moment. “Fourteenth Young Lady is much better now, but she has not eaten in a while, so she can only eat light, soft foods. Shall I help you up?” Mei Jiu was stunned that a maid could take her pulse. It took her a while to react, and she said awkwardly, “Yes… Thank you.” Mei Jiu had suddenly become a lady of high society, a far cry from her former commoner status, and she could not adjust. She did not even know where to put her hands. A moment later, six maids brought in washing utensils and helped Mei Jiu tidy up. Wen-Cui helped her to the outer room. “It’s just past noon, not yet time for lunch. Please make do with this for now. Please forgive any inconvenience.” Mei Jiu nodded awkwardly. Angel, seeing her so cautious, could not help but scoff. Mei Jiu froze, stopping abruptly in her tracks. “Fourteenth Young Lady?” Wen-Cui asked with concern, “What’s wrong?” Mei Jiu lowered her eyes, suppressing her doubts, and softly replied, “Nothing.” Having heard Wen-Cui’s earlier words, Mei Jiu assumed the meal would consist only of porridge. She was astonished to see the table laden with fragrant and delicious light dishes. Wen-Cui stood beside Mei Jiu, seemingly oblivious to her surprise, and smilingly served her food. “Young Lady, I do not know your tastes. Please tell me if you prefer anything.” “I am not picky,” Mei Jiu said softly. She had never dreamed of eating such good food in her life; what was there to be picky about? The deliciousness of the food spread across her taste buds, and both Angel and Mei Jiu were simultaneously stunned. The two souls’ craving for food made Mei Jiu forget her inhibitions, and she began to eat heartily. “Young Lady has a weak stomach; it’s better to chew carefully,” Wen-Cui reminded her. “Do not eat too much.” Angel subconsciously glanced back at the noisy person. Wen-Cui stiffened, a chill running through her body, but a strange joy quickly appeared on her face, and her attitude became even gentler. After finishing her meal, Angel suddenly remembered that she had unintentionally taken control of Mei Jiu’s body for a fleeting moment! So… she had a chance to possess this body? Mei Jiu was trying hard to adapt to her new identity, completely unaware of the ill intentions lurking beneath the surface. Wen-Cui had a kind face, and her deliberate gentleness made Mei Jiu quickly accept her, even boldly striking up a conversation. “Wen-Cui, where is this?” “This is Mei Mansion,” Wen-Cui explained with a smile. “Our place is called Meihua Lane, totaling over two hundred mu1, plus a large lake of about a hundred mu. All of this belongs to Mei Mansion. There are a total of nine hundred and seventy-three people in Meihua Lane, but our household only has less than four hundred. There are sixty-four mistresses, and now that Yan-niang has brought you and Fifteenth Young Lady home, three more have joined us.” She spoke unhurriedly, continuing, “Leaving aside the affairs of the front courtyard, in this back courtyard, the Old Madams of Shayun Residence and Bixiang Residence are the most respected. The head mistress, the Third Madam, is the legitimate daughter-in-law of the old lady of Shayun Residence. For now, this is enough for you, Young Lady.” Mei Jiu had never imagined a household could have so many people. Her mind was a jumbled mess, and she nodded dizzily. Seeing that Mei Jiu looked tired, Wen-Cui considerately said, “Please rest a little longer, Young Lady. You will be more energetic to greet the Old Madam tomorrow morning.” Wen-Cui helped her lie down on the bed and tucked her in. “I will stand guard outside the door. Just call if you need anything.” “Mm,” Mei Jiu was tired but not very sleepy. The maids all left with Wen-Cui, and the room returned to silence. Mei Jiu climbed out of bed and peeked into the outer room. Seeing that no one was there, she breathed a sigh of relief. She sat down on the edge of the bed and tentatively asked, “Are you there?”

chapters.title: Going in the Wrong Direction
chapters.content: Angel snorted. Mei Jiu tensed upon hearing this. “You, are you a human or a ghost?” “Guess.” Angel would never have paid attention to her nonsense if she were not trying to confirm her own existence. Recalling the various instances of her body losing control earlier, Mei Jiu had a guess, her face paling. “What are you trying to achieve by hiding in my body?” “To be able to say something so plausible is truly astonishing. I thought you were brainless,” Angel replied with cool sarcasm. This girl had not asked a single question since waking up, her carefree attitude drawing utter contempt from Angel. Mei Jiu pondered, her grip on the bedside slowly relaxing, a bit of color returning to her face. “Whether you are a human or a ghost, I feel you have no ill intentions towards me.” “Your feeling is correct.” Angel was not lying, but in her understanding, whether someone harbored ill will towards another person and whether they would kill them were not necessarily related. Hearing her words, Mei Jiu felt slightly relieved, but because humans and ghosts were different, her voice remained tense. “What’s your name? Why are you following me?” This time it was Angel’s turn to be confused. The girl in front of her had just been pounding her heart, yet she had let her guard down because of some unseen and intangible feeling! It was truly inexplicable. After waiting for a long time, Mei Jiu heard no reply. “Are you still there?” “Name…” Angel was a little dazed. She only remembered the codename and had no recollection of her real name. “Angel.” “An Jiu?” Mei Jiu’s tone became more familiar, and she whispered, “My name is Mei Jiu, the ‘Jiu’ in ‘Chang Shun Jiu An2.’ Do you also have this character?” An Jiu it is; it did not matter anyway. She was too lazy to explain and only said lightly, “Your parents’ wishes are good, but with your intelligence, I am afraid it will not last long.” Mei Jiu did not quite understand, but she could tell it was not a nice thing to say, and her face immediately turned red. “Hey, do not get excited!” An Jiu said angrily. She could sense Mei Jiu’s feelings; that unfamiliar emotional fluctuation made her uncomfortable. It was like wanting to curse someone but accidentally cursing yourself as well—the feeling was too bizarre! An Jiu felt that seizing the body was urgent. “You’ve gone too far!” Mei Jiu said angrily. Wen-Cui, who was waiting outside the door, heard the sudden voice and immediately replied, “Fourteenth Young Lady, do you need any servants?” “No, no,” Mei Jiu said in a panic. An Jiu sighed deeply into the distance. She must have committed too many sins in her past life to be suffering this punishment in this one. “This sister,” a familiar voice faintly came from outside the house. Mei Jiu’s spirits lifted, and she jumped out of bed, running excitedly to the door to open it. “Ah Shun!” Wen-Cui smiled. “Fifteenth Young Lady just woke up and came right over! The two young ladies are truly sisters.” Mei Jiu pulled Ah Shun’s hand and led her into the room. Seeing their excited and eager expressions, Wen-Cui wisely refrained from disturbing them, gently closing the door behind her. “Ah Jiu, you have to save me!” Ah Shun’s tears suddenly streamed down her face, the fear in her phoenix eyes genuine. Mei Jiu paused for a moment, then smiled. “Do not be afraid. Mother said this is my home; no one will harm you.” An Jiu could not help but chuckle, and Mei Jiu froze at the sound. Ah Shun, flustered, did not notice her subtle change. “Last night, those black-clad men tried to kill me. When I saw they did not intend to harm you and even wanted to take you away, I… said I was your younger sister…” Ah Shun had assumed Mei Jiu had no close relatives and that she could simply tell her when the opportunity arose. Who would have thought Mei Jiu’s mother was still alive! If she were exposed, would she even survive? “After I was separated from my mother, I was only able to survive thanks to your care. I’ve always considered you my own sister.” Mei Jiu pulled her to sit on the edge of the bed. “Do not worry, I will tell my mother in a bit.” An Jiu had absolutely no interest in this pointless display of sisterly affection. She had previously thought that the Mei family had rescued them from those black-clad men, but it turned out that those black-clad men belonged to the Mei family! Recalling the situation at the time, those people definitely did not intend to save anyone. An Jiu did not doubt her keen sense of danger. Considering Mei Yanran’s reaction, An Jiu guessed that the Mei family might have originally intended to kill her to silence her, but for some reason, they spared her. “I cannot thank you enough!” Ah Shun rose and knelt before Mei Jiu. “What are you doing? Please get up quickly.” Mei Jiu quickly bent down to help her up. The two girls held hands and talked, the warm, soft touch making An Jiu incredibly awkward. If it were not for their close-quarters combat, she had rarely touched anyone’s body like this in her entire life. She hated that she could not shake off Ah Shun’s hand! Adding to that, she had to listen to their tedious conversation, which nearly drove An Jiu to a mental breakdown! So, as soon as Ah Shun stepped away, she immediately said, “Can you please not have physical contact with other people so casually in the future?!” “What is…physical contact?” Meijiu asked, puzzled. “It means do not shake hands, hug, kiss, or sleep with other people casually!” An Jiu said. Meijiu blushed. “You, you…” She was too embarrassed to talk about such a topic. “Ah Shun is a woman.” “Not even women!” An Jiu had no leverage over her now, so she resorted to threatening her. “You know I am a ghost. If you do not behave, I will kill your mother!” “I will behave, I will behave; please do not hurt my mother,” Mei Jiu said hastily. An Jiu realized she had overestimated the girl. The way she had so easily intimidated her was almost disheartening. “Think about your current situation! I bet Wen-Cui overheard your whispered conversation with that girl outside,” An Jiu warned. After all, they shared a body, and she did not want it to be damaged before she understood the relationship between soul and body. “But she did not ask anything?” Mei Jiu asked, somewhat incredulous. An Jiu snapped, “She did not react, so she did not hear? Is your head filled with nothing but intestines?! Someone like you is only good for nothing!” An Jiu never thought being unintelligent was a mistake—the girl was not bothering her! But now, sharing a body with Mei Jiu, she could not ignore her; she had to communicate deeply! At this moment, rather than hating Mei Jiu’s naiveté, she felt a profound sense of powerlessness regarding her current situation. She did not even have the chance to shoot herself! “You are utterly unreasonable!” Even a clay idol like Mei Jiu could not help but show some temper after being insulted like that. She angrily got up to leave, forgetting that An Jiu was right beside her. “Fourteenth Young Lady, you have not fully recovered yet; please do not go out,” Wen-Cui said with a gentle smile, stopping her. Mei Jiu was stunned. “Why can Ah Shun leave the room?” “Fifteenth Sister is perfectly fine,” Wen-Cui said. Mei Jiu did not insist on leaving, lowering her head and saying, “I want to see Mother.” “Coward,” An Jiu’s cold voice inexplicably sounded resentful.

chapters.title: A Heartbreaking Past
chapters.content: “Fourteenth Young Lady, Lady Yan will be having dinner with you.” Wen-Cui’s gentle demeanor remained unchanged, her stance in front of the door unwavering. Mei Jiu had no choice but to retreat inside. An Jiu sensed her grievance and sadness, but instead of offering comfort, she snapped, “Give me a break! It’s nothing!” Mei Jiu thought angrily, “Are you trying to kill me?! Can I not even be sad?!” “Then tell me, what’s there to be upset about?” An Jiu, after all, was a professionally trained individual, adept at controlling her emotions; she could be calm and collected if she wanted to. Mei Jiu was surprised to find that An Jiu could hear what she was thinking. An Jiu’s tone was not kind, but Mei Jiu desperately wanted to confide in someone, so she remained silent, silently repeating in her mind, “I thought I’d see my father when I got home, but who knew he was already gone?” An Jiu immediately received a memory about a man; it turned out that Mei Jiu had to recall a certain memory for her to receive it. “Ha, you have quite the leisurely mood. Why are you not grateful you survived? You only see the hardships, not the good fortune, and you even make a big deal out of it. What’s the point of living? Besides, how many times did you even see that man? He’s dead, so what? It’s not a big deal.” An Jiu could not understand her reason for being sad. Mei Jiu retorted, “What do you know?! Although I did not spend much time with my father, he was still my biological father. Blood ties are important; how can I not care! If he were your father, would you still be talking like this?!” “I am trying to comfort you, can you not tell?” An Jiu was annoyed. She had hardly ever comforted anyone in her life. “If you were not useful, I would not even want to waste bullets shooting a coward like you! I do not know anything about blood relatives; I only remember that when I was twelve, the first person I killed was my father.” “You…why did you kill him?” Mei Jiu felt a chill run down her spine. Heavens, this ghost was so vicious even as a human, and now as a ghost… She shuddered, afraid to think any further. “He was a physician, a habitual domestic abuser, obsessed with drug research, and even secretly used my mother to experiment on his newly developed dangerous drugs. My mother died because of it, and he did not even face legal consequences! So I killed him.” Afterwards, An Jiu was imprisoned in a juvenile detention center. After six months, someone got her released and provided her with a comfortable life, even getting her into a competitive archery team. Those were some of the few happy times in her life since her mother’s death, but a life of utter darkness began from then on. The criminal organization targeted the violent genes in her blood, inherited from the man she called “Father.” Over time, as she took more and more lives, she gradually became numb to love and hate. She did not hate her father, nor did she feel any affection for him. An Jiu calmly recounted this harrowing past, but it terrified Mei Jiu, turning her lips white. An Jiu realized her attempts to comfort her seemed to have the opposite effect and became very dissatisfied. “Hey! Do not be nervous!” “You are not human!” Mei Jiu cried out in terror. An Jiu said, “I do not need you to remind me.” She was now merely a wisp of soul residing in someone else’s body; she could not truly be considered a human anymore. Mei Jiu stopped speaking, silently shrinking into the corner of the bed, burying her head between her legs, trembling all over. She finally endured until dinnertime. When Mei Jiu saw Mei Yanran, tears streamed down her face. An Jiu was speechless, afraid that saying another word would frighten the girl into fainting, so she could only silently savor the fragrance and warmth emanating from that woman’s embrace. This time, unlike when she held hands with Ah Shun and she felt repulsed, she actually felt a little comfortable, as if… this was the safest place in the world. “My child, do not be afraid.” Mei Yanran gently patted her back. “As long as your mother is here, I will never let you suffer.” “Mother,” Mei Jiu choked, wanting to tell Mei Yanran about the terrifying ghost residing within her body, yet worried about harming her mother, she could only hold back. Dinner consisted only of Mei Yanran, her daughter, and Ah Shun. Influenced by An Jiu, Mei Jiu began to eat and drink voraciously as soon as she sat down at the table, behaving like a country bumpkin who had never seen the world. In contrast, Ah Shun ate quietly and slowly, appearing more like a refined young lady. Startled, Mei Jiu momentarily forgot everything else. It was only after several glances from Ah Shun that she remembered her promise from that morning. After the meal, she found an opportunity to whisper it to Mei Yanran. Mei Yanran, a woman of experience, saw through Ah Shun’s cunning and disliked her. However, she knew the Mei family could not hide anything from her anyway; it would be exposed eventually, so why should she bear her daughter’s resentment? Therefore, she readily agreed. Relieved, Mei Jiu happily told Ah Shun. As dusk fell, Mei Jiu was exhausted. After the maid made her bed, she fell asleep immediately. She slept soundly through the night. The next day, just as dawn broke, Wen-Cui urged Mei Jiu to get up. “Go early so the Old Madam will not feel neglected. Besides, after seeing the Old Madam of Bixiang Residence, you still need to pay your respects to the Old Madam of Shayun Residence. This round trip will take until after noon.” Mei Jiu did not have the habit of sleeping in, so upon hearing Wen-Cui’s words, she quickly got out of bed and let the maidservants help her wash up. An Jiu looked at the transformed young girl in the mirror, almost dazzled! Her features were exquisitely beautiful; she wore a light blue dress, the wide collar unable to conceal her slender neck, the ribbons of her dress cascading down, the ends tied with a circular white jade ring, and her long black hair half-draped, half-tied, exuding a unique, clean elegance amidst her youthful innocence, like a crane gracefully gliding by the water. An Jiu could not help but acknowledge, “Gold and jade on the outside, tattered cotton inside.” Mei Jiu was startled. Wen-Cui did not miss Mei Jiu’s momentary panic and asked softly, “What’s wrong, Young Lady? Are you unhappy with your outfit?” “No, no,” Mei Jiu denied repeatedly. Wen-Cui did not press further, but she wondered why someone would be frightened by themselves. Or… be amazed by their own beauty? Mei Jiu froze, only slowly relaxing when she stepped into the sunlight: Ghosts were afraid of sunlight, were they not? Meanwhile, An Jiu was busy admiring the scenery in the courtyard, having no time to concern herself with the young girl’s thoughts. The Mei Mansion was large, filled with trees as far as the eye could see, with the corners of houses swaying in the breeze. It was the height of autumn, and withered leaves swirled down like butterflies. A gentle breeze passed, and a rain of fallen leaves began to trickle in the woods. “Is Mother not going?” Mei Jiu asked. An Jiu had not had enough of looking around when her gaze suddenly shifted away. She huffed a few times in dissatisfaction, startling Mei Jiu into a stumble. “Fourteenth Young Lady, be careful,” Wen-Cui said, supporting her. “If Lady Yan is not going, Fifteenth Young Lady will go with you. Let’s go to the ferry and wait for her.” “Ferry?” Mei Jiu was shocked. Her family even had a ferry! It was not far from Yuwei Residence to the ferry. Passing through a forest path, the view suddenly opened up before her. The morning sun had not yet risen, and the vast lake was shrouded in mist, water and sky merging into one. Through the veil of haze, verdant islands could be vaguely seen. A pine-wood ferry extended into the lake, with several small boats moored beside it. Ah Shun and her maid were already waiting at the ferry. She wore a light pink cross-collar ruqun, her phoenix eyes slightly raised; she was indeed a beauty.

chapters.title: Mei Ruxue
chapters.content: A gentle breeze lifted her hair and clothes. Ah Shun smiled sweetly. “Sister.” “Ah Shun.” Mei Jiu was overjoyed and was about to take her hand when she suddenly heard An Jiu cough loudly, so she awkwardly withdrew her hand. Ah Shun, unaware of what had happened, reached out and hooked her arm around Mei Jiu’s, whispering, “Sister, I am a little nervous.” An Jiu immediately snapped, “Stay away from this woman!” Only Mei Jiu could hear An Jiu’s voice, but their physical sensations were synchronized. An Jiu was not used to being so close to someone and instinctively wanted to throw Ah Shun over her shoulder. “Ah Shun.” Mei Jiu was very embarrassed, wanting to push Ah Shun away but unable to find an excuse. Mei Jiu did not offer any comfort, making the atmosphere slightly awkward. Wen-Cui pretended not to hear and smiled, “Young Ladies, please board the boat.” Ah Shun gave the absent-minded Mei Jiu a strange look and let her board the boat first. To prevent Ah Shun from getting any closer, Mei Jiu deliberately chose the narrowest spot at the bow of the boat, just wide enough for her alone. Once everyone was on board, the boat moved slowly forward in the water. Ah Shun was uneasy, wondering why Mei Jiu had suddenly become distant, and decided to break the awkward silence. She asked her maid, “Wen-Bi, I am not very familiar with the household customs. Is there any etiquette I should show to the Old Madam?” Mei Jiu looked at Wen-Bi. Her appearance was quite different from Wen-Cui’s; she had a thin, long face that was not particularly pretty, with somewhat heavy single eyelids. When she looked at people, her eyes were mostly white with less black than white. She did not smile much, but her voice was quite amiable. “Our Old Madam is very kind. She did not have many children or grandchildren, but now she has two granddaughters, which makes her very happy. Young Lady, you do not need to worry.” Wen-Cui chimed in, “Yes, our Old Madam is nothing like that one at Shayun Residence. She’s very kind!” “Are there two Old Madams in the family?” Ah Shun asked curiously. Wen-Cui explained, “The two Old Madams are sisters-in-law. Our Old Madam is the eldest daughter-in-law, and the Old Madam of Shayun Residence is the principal wife of the second branch. Both Old Masters have passed away.” An Jiu listened to their account and roughly understood the family’s situation. The Mei family was currently divided into two branches; the eldest branch had fewer members, while the second branch had many descendants. The small boat drifted along, reaching the shore in less than the time it takes to drink a cup of tea. The group disembarked one after another. Before them stretched a large pine forest, surrounded by evergreen trees, their verdant leaves glistening in the morning mist—a stark contrast to the withered autumn leaves elsewhere. A young girl in a smoky-colored dress stood at the small ferry crossing to greet them. “Sisters Wen-Bi and Wen-Cui are back!” she said, then smiled and bowed to Mei Jiu and Ah Shun. “This humble servant, Chun-Yi, greets both ladies.” Seeing Mei Jiu uncertain about what to say, Ah Shun said, “Miss Chun-Yi, there’s no need for such formalities.” An Jiu said disapprovingly, “Could you be any more clueless? What a waste of a presentable face!” These words were directed only at Mei Jiu. Standing in the morning light, Mei Jiu’s fear of An Jiu lessened somewhat. She said aggrievedly, “I am just a country girl; I do not know how to act like a refined young lady.” An Jiu recalled a memory: Mei Jiu had always lived in the countryside, but Mei Yanran had never treated her like an ordinary country girl. She had been taught music, chess, calligraphy, and painting; it was just that Mei Jiu had little contact with people, so she was somewhat shy. As An Jiu admired the scenery, she murmured, “What makes humans superior to other species is their advanced ability to disguise themselves. You’ve lived this long and still cannot even do the most basic disguise; you are clearly a defective product.” Mei Jiu did not understand some of the words, but because of their telepathic connection, she could roughly grasp the meaning. Unable to refute, she could only lower her eyes and look at her toes. “Look up!” An Jiu commanded. “What will it take to satisfy you?!” Mei Jiu thought this devil was being far too nosy! No one could hear their internal conversation, but Ah Shun, who had been watching Mei Jiu closely, clearly saw the fleeting anger on her face. “We are here,” Wen-Cui reminded her. Mei Jiu finally looked up. The architecture of Bixiang Residence differed from the ornate beams and painted rafters of the surrounding buildings. The combination of green walls, black tiles, and pine trees exuded a simple yet grand atmosphere, reminiscent of the Qin and Han dynasties. The buildings, nestled among the pines, with a babbling brook, created a tranquil and charming ambiance. Several people stopped outside. Chun-Yi quickly went in to report, then returned shortly to welcome them in. Mei Jiu’s heart was in her throat, her palms sweating profusely. This was absolutely inhuman torture for An Jiu. She could kill an entire squad with a single shot without her heart even racing, but now she was forced to experience this tension. What was more, An Jiu’s normal heart rate was 45 beats per minute, while Mei Jiu’s was over 90. An Jiu already had difficulty adapting, and now it had jumped from 45 to 120—it felt like her heart was about to burst! She wondered if Mei Jiu was about to die suddenly. Relying on Mei Jiu was futile; An Jiu quickly tried to control her body with her mind. Perhaps it was Mei Jiu’s subconscious attempt to escape, but she easily gained control of her entire body. The sudden sense of reality made her involuntarily jump for joy. “This is my granddaughter?” a woman’s voice came. An Jiu looked up and was first met with a pair of eyes as clear and bright as the sky, definitely not the eyes of an elderly person. Sure enough, the woman in the main seat, dressed in a dark brown jacket, was no more than forty years old. Her eyebrows were like willow leaves, her eyes long and narrow with slightly upturned corners, her nose delicate, and her lips cherry-red—a true beauty with an ancient charm. When she smiled, fine lines appeared at the corners of her eyes. “Come here quickly.” An Jiu obeyed and walked to her side, followed by Ah Shun. “Good child.” The woman grasped An Jiu’s wrist, subtly feeling her pulse. When she found nothing unusual, her smile faltered slightly, and she carefully examined An Jiu’s face. “Good child.” Meeting An Jiu’s gaze, she finally noticed something different. That cold, penetrating gaze was definitely not ordinary. “What’s your name?” “Mei Jiu,” An Jiu replied concisely and firmly. The woman frowned. “What kind of name is this? Such disrespect for my granddaughter!” She gazed at the pine forest outside the door, pondering for a long time. “Fallen plum blossoms lie scattered like snow beneath the steps, brushing them off only to find them still covering you. From this day forward… your name will be Mei Ruxue3, and this name will be recorded in the family genealogy.” “Yes, Grandmother,” An Jiu agreed obediently. A name was just a label; as long as it was not unbearable to hear, it was acceptable. Suddenly, Mei Jiu lost control of her body. In her panic, she heard the old lady change her name and protested even more fiercely. “Jiu is the name my mother gave me, meaning longevity and peace. It cannot be changed so easily!” An Jiu threatened coldly, “Shut up, or I will kill your mother. Do you want your name or your mother?” Mei Jiu immediately quieted down. “And you?” the old lady asked, looking at Ah Shun. Ah Shun was overjoyed and quickly replied, “Mei Shun.” “Hmph, not ‘Shun’? Even less auspicious,” The Old Madam was also dissatisfied, saying, “Let’s call her Mei Ruyan, meaning ‘flame.'” Wen-Cui praised, “White plum blossoms like snow, red plum blossoms like flames, Old Madam, you’ve chosen such a beautiful name!” The old lady smiled and said, “Not at all, not at all; far inferior to the second branch! Hmph, Mei Zhengjing is so frivolous; her talent for naming is something I cannot even dream of matching.” Several maids covered their mouths and chuckled in agreement. Wen-Cui playfully scolded, “Old Madam always knows how to make fun of people.” “Alright, I do not like crowds; go back now! Wen-Cui and Wen-Bi, you two help out and make arrangements, keep your eyes open, and pick out some good maids to serve them.” With that, the Old Madam, holding her spring dress, got up and left. She stopped just before reaching the door. “Ruyan, never forget the kindness of the Mei family.” Ah Shun’s heart skipped a beat; she knew her secret of not being Mei’s daughter had been exposed. She immediately knelt on the ground with a thud. “Yes, Ruyan swears to never forget.” An Jiu saw the Old Madam’s profile, backlit, with a faint smile, peaceful yet profound. She was so warm and friendly when speaking to people, yet her actions were cold, just like the impression she gave now. “Fourteenth Young Lady, Fifteenth Young Lady, this servant will accompany you to Shayun Residence,” Wen-Cui said. An Jiu nodded, feeling that something was a little off about the atmosphere. Mei Jiu struggled to control herself, but An Jiu coldly said, “Behave yourself!”

chapters.title: Making a Name for Oneself
chapters.content: Shayun Residence was also built on a small island in the lake. As the sunlight parted the morning mist, the red maples and yellow apricots could be seen across the lake, like flames on the water, casting long shadows in the azure water—a truly beautiful sight. The boat docked at the ferry crossing. Wen-Cui led the two through the apricot grove to a lush bamboo forest. It turned out that the island was surrounded by maple and apricot trees, enclosing the bamboo grove in the center. “Hey!” A girl of about fifteen or sixteen, with her hair in two buns, appeared on the stone steps, her almond-shaped eyes glaring at Wen-Cui. “Sister Wen-Cui, do not you know our Old Madam is impatient with people from Bixiang Residence?” Wen-Cui was not angry. She smiled and said, “Miss Man-Xiang, I am no longer with Bixiang Residence. Our Yan-niang has brought the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Young Ladies back to the mansion. I’ve come to guide the two young ladies.” As the saying goes, one does not hit a smiling face. Although Man-Xiang’s attitude was still unpleasant, she did not make things too difficult. “Sister Wen-Cui knows the Old Madam’s temper. You can wait here. You two young ladies, come with me.” She turned to leave, completely disregarding her two young ladies. “Wait,” Ah Shun suddenly called out to her. Man-Xiang stopped and turned back. “What is it, Young Lady?” Ah Shun lifted her skirt slightly and walked up the stone steps. Reaching Man-Xiang, she suddenly raised her hand and slapped her hard across the face. “A mere maid, how dare you show no respect! Is everyone at Shayun Residence so unruly?” From the moment she changed her name to Mei Ruyan, Ah Shun knew she had to cling to the coattails of the Old Madam of Bixiang Residence. The eldest branch of the family was weak, but she was nominally on their side. The second branch had a large number of descendants, so she could not expect the Old Madam of Shayun’s favor. Rather than struggling to survive, she decided to choose one side. She also knew that the head wife was the Old Madam’s daughter-in-law. Offending Shayun Residence would likely make her future difficult. However, she was different from Mei Jiu; Mei Jiu was a true member of the Mei family, while she was merely an imposter. Without fighting, how could she ever rise to the top? An Jiu watched this scene quietly, a barely perceptible smile playing on her lips. Sunlight filtered through, illuminating a flickering flame in her slightly upturned phoenix eyes. She felt this girl was perfectly suited to the name “Ruyan.” “You!” Man-Xiang covered her face, tears streaming down her cheeks. She glared fiercely at Mei Ruyan, then abandoned them and ran away. Wen-Cui sighed. “Fourteenth Young Lady, Fifteenth Young Lady, let’s go back.” “Why go back? We are not the ones who did anything wrong,” Mei Ruyan said. Wen-Cui leaned closer and whispered, “That Old Madam of Shayun Residence is fiercely protective of her children; there’s no reasoning with her. Her wrath is something no ordinary person can withstand.” Mei Ruyan raised an eyebrow. “You think she can kill me?” With that, she chased after Man-Xiang. Wen-Cui felt a surge of satisfaction, worried that Mei Ruyan might suffer alone, so she urged An Jiu, “Fourteenth Young Lady, let’s go see what’s going on. Just in case… we will have someone to look after us.” “Let’s go see,” An Jiu said. Why not watch the show? She was with Mei Ruyan; she only needed to follow along, doing nothing, and the credit would be hers. Even if someone else took the lead, she could still win over her grandmother. The two had just reached the entrance of the courtyard when they heard a commotion inside. An Jiu stood at the entrance and looked around. She saw about a dozen burly women surrounding Mei Ruyan. On the opposite side of the corridor, there was a couch with maids standing quietly on either side. An elderly woman, well past fifty, was gesturing as she arranged flowers in a vase. She wore a dark blue jacket with gold trim, her hair was completely white as frost, and her face was wrinkled with a few light brown age spots, but because she was very fair, she appeared very clean. Below the steps, Man-Xiang covered her face and glared angrily at Mei Ruyan. “Greetings, Great-Aunt,” Mei Ruyan said calmly in a bow. “Oh dear! What’s going on?” Wen-Cui quickly stepped forward, smiling as she gave the Second Old Madam a deep bow. “Wen-Cui greets you, Old Madam. What mistake has Fifteenth Young Lady made that warrants such a grand display?” The Second Old Madam seemed oblivious, engrossed in her flower arranging. An Jiu leaned against a ginkgo tree in the courtyard, calmly watching the spectacle. Several maids glanced at her frequently, but the Second Old Madam deliberately ignored the people from the main house, so they dared not speak up. After about half an hour, the Second Old Madam finally completed her masterpiece, a vase of vibrant colors, and the maids beside her rushed to offer their praise. “Oh dear, why are there two more people squatting in this courtyard?” The Second Old Madam seemed to have only just noticed Mei Ruyan and Wen-Cui. Maids served tea and massaged shoulders, and one whispered, “Old Madam, there’s someone else standing under the apricot tree over there.” The Old Madam turned her head in surprise and saw a little girl in a light green dress huddled against the tree trunk, looking timid. Having watched the commotion, An Jiu lowered her head and moved to the center of the courtyard. “Greetings, Great-Aunt.” The Old Madam picked up her teacup and prompted An Jiu, “Tell me, what did those two do wrong?” An Jiu glanced at Wen-Cui and Mei Ruyan and said earnestly, “I only saw one of them make a mistake.” The two girls’ hearts jumped. An Jiu had not been punished with them, and now she was staring at them expectantly—was she going to switch sides? An Jiu’s suggestive gaze led everyone to believe that the person she was referring to was either Wen-Cui or Mei Ruyan, since only Mei Ruyan had actually hit anyone. The Old Madam said gently, “Oh? Who made a mistake?” An Jiu pointed at Man-Xiang. “Her.” “Oh? Since Man-Xiang made a mistake, why did they take the initiative to apologize?” the second Old Madam asked, puzzled. An Jiu looked at the Second Old Madam very seriously and sincerely. “Because these old women are all very fierce, they are afraid of being beaten.” Seeing that her attempt to instigate infighting had failed, the Second Old Madam lost her patience and, too lazy to pretend any longer, slammed her teacup into the courtyard. “No one has ever dared to lay a hand on me! You two have no respect for your elders, bullying this old woman, and you think you can leave peacefully? Beat her!” “Wait! We sisters are only beating a servant; we’ve never bullied our great-aunt!” Mei Ruyan argued. Seeing that she herself could not escape being beaten, An Jiu added casually, “Yes, how can a lowly servant be worthy of being called our elder?” The veiled insult nearly made the Second Old Madam faint with anger, but if she lost her temper, would that not be admitting that she was a lowly servant? A surge of anger welled up inside her, and the Second Old Madam pressed her chest, trying to suppress her rage. “We sisters are all filial people. If Great-Aunt is truly enraged, what does it matter if she beats us to death for a mere maid as long as it helps her vent her anger?” Mei Ruyan was certain the Second Old Madam would not dare. The maidservant massaging the Second Old Madam’s shoulders whispered, “Old Madam, if things really escalate, would not that give the Bixiang Residence something to talk about? Would it not be better to make them apologize to Man-Xiang and humiliate her a bit?” The Second Madam thought about it and agreed. Making them bow down to a mere maidservant would be quite satisfying. “Fine, I will not stoop to your level. Just apologize to Man-Xiang and go back.” Mei Ruyan said, “Great-Aunt, just beat me to death! I’d rather die than bow down to a servant!” An Jiu added, her voice carefully controlled, “Do not be silly. Great-Aunt does not have Mei bones or skin. Even if you break or beat her, it will not hurt at all.” The Second Old Madam suddenly stood up, trembling with anger. She opened her mouth to say something, but suddenly rolled her eyes and fell backward. Chaos erupted in the courtyard. “The Old Madam has fainted from anger! Quickly, fetch the physician!” An Jiu craned her neck to look, then her hand was grabbed. She instinctively reached out to deliver a knee strike. “Ah Jiu!” Mei Ruyan exclaimed. Mei Jiu’s soul and body were much more in sync than An Jiu’s. Startled, she instantly regained control of her body, her movements abruptly halting as she stumbled forward. “The Second Old Madam is not well; she cannot take anger out on her. Quick, quick!” Wen-Cui swiftly caught her, urging the two to leave amidst the chaos. Within a single afternoon, nearly a thousand people in Meihua Lane knew that the newly returned Fourteenth Young Lady and Fifteenth Young Lady had caused the Second Old Madam to faint from anger. Arriving early and already being “famous”—a cause for celebration for some and sorrow for others!

chapters.title: Grandma Lang
chapters.content: “How could you speak so rudely?!” Mei Jiu mentally berated An Jiu. An Jiu said nonchalantly, “Judging by her appearance, I thought she was tough and resilient, but who knew she was so weak! Besides, she’s an enemy; the less we have to do with her, the better!” Mei Jiu corrected her, “She’s my great-aunt, not an enemy.” An Jiu was too lazy to argue with her. “I’ve been itching to kill someone lately, so tell me, are you going to die yourself or let that great-aunt die?” “I…” Mei Jiu gritted her teeth. “Kill me if you want, but do not harm my family!” An Jiu paused, then sensed Mei Jiu’s extreme tension, and she began to feel uncomfortable as well. She said fiercely, “I will not kill you, but you need to work on your courage; otherwise, I will kill you first and then your whole family!” “How can you be so unreasonable?” Mei Jiu was both afraid and unable to resist. It was precisely this small struggle that made An Jiu want to tease her. “How could I? You cannot insult my character. I can be very reasonable when I want to.” Mei Jiu felt a surge of anger. “Just talk properly, can you not?” “Ugh, it’s just a few words; do not get emotional!” An Jiu felt uncomfortable all over. Thinking about the current situation, she could not help but laugh self-deprecatingly. She felt like she was torturing herself for no reason and in a more sophisticated way. Mei Jiu’s eyes reddened, and she remained silent. Wen-Cui brought in tea and snacks. Seeing Mei Jiu sitting silently in the corner, her face slightly pale, she assumed she was afraid and comforted her. “Young Lady, do not worry about it. Apart from the Second Old Madam, everyone in the Second Branch is reasonable and will not blame you. The Second Old Madam has a weak heart, and the whole family caters to her wishes. She’s used to a life of ease and cannot stand the slightest displeasure now. It’s not your fault at all.” “Wen-Cui, thank you,” Mei Jiu said. Wen-Cui smiled, leaned closer, and whispered, “If the Third Madam knew, she would not make things difficult for you; in fact, she’d thank you!” “The Third Madam is the Second Old Madam’s daughter-in-law, is she not?” Mei Jiu asked, puzzled. “Yes, what mother-in-law and daughter-in-law in this world are truly of one mind? The Third Madam and the Second Old Madam are outwardly friendly but inwardly at odds.” Wen-Cui reached out to help her up. “Young Lady, you’ve had a long day; have some pastries to tide you over.” It was getting dark outside. In the center of Shayun Residence, the Second Old Madam, with a handkerchief covering her forehead, was complaining to a middle-aged man, “Third Son, I may not have the bones or blood of the Mei family, but I’ve been married into the Mei family for forty years, and everything I’ve said and done has been for their sake! A mere brat, still wet behind the ears, dares to call me an outsider!” The middle-aged man said, “Mother, you are making the Mei family’s young lady apologize to a servant? Where does that leave the Mei family’s reputation?” The Second Old Madam sat up abruptly from the bed, pointing at him. “You…I’ve raised such an ungrateful wretch! You are siding with an outsider!” “Stop it.” Seeing that the atmosphere had calmed down, the elegantly dressed woman stopped her husband. She sat down on the embroidered stool in front of the bed and took the Second Old Madam’s hand. “She was just disciplining a disrespectful junior behind closed doors; how did that involve the Mei family’s reputation?” “That’s right!” The Second Old Madam’s anger finally subsided a little. The Third Madam said, “It was all that inexperienced maid’s bad idea. A mere maid, daring to try to make her young lady bow down! She’s truly a wolf in sheep’s clothing! Luckily, Mother is sensible and did not agree. I think this maid cannot be kept anymore; get rid of her quickly, and I will pick out a better one for you.” The Second Old Madam’s face stiffened, realizing she’d fallen into another trap. Her eyes rolled back, and she fainted again. At the Yuwei Residence. Wen-Cui, while tidying the table, said, “The Third Madam is very cunning. If it were not for the Second Old Madam’s seniority, even a hundred of her would not be enough to deter her.” Mei Jiu had not expected so many intricacies. Unable to understand, she stopped thinking about it. “Wen-Cui, can I go sleep with Mother?” Before Wen-Cui could answer, An Jiu strongly objected, “No!” “Young Lady, please do not run around for now, but you can invite Lady Yan to Yuwei Residence.” Wen-Cui carried the tray out. An Jiu’s voice tightened. “How terrifying would it be to sleep next to someone!” “What’s wrong with that?” Mei Jiu asked, puzzled. “If someone sleeps next to you, they will be a corpse the next morning. Is that not terrifying?” An Jiu was not trying to scare Mei Jiu. She was the highest-bounty sniper on the wanted list, and being hunted by numerous experts had instilled in her the habit of never allowing a living thing where she slept. Mei Jiu shivered, her voice trembling with tears. “I will sleep alone.” Mei Yanran had come to see Mei Jiu before bed, said a few words, and then left. Strangely, there were no lights on in the room, and no maidservants were on night watch. Mei Jiu did not know the customs of ordinary wealthy families, so she was not surprised; it was just that the complete darkness terrified her. “An Jiu, are you asleep?” Mei Jiu asked tremulously, huddled under the covers. She coexisted with An Jiu. Although she could not access her memories or sense her emotions, she felt a strange sense of familiarity. Compared to the unknown dangers in the darkness, An Jiu was not the most frightening thing. An Jiu ignored her. “I can hear sounds from far away now. I am scared, but my heart is not beating as fast as before, and I do not seem particularly afraid,” Mei Jiu muttered to herself. During the day, her attention was scattered, so this feeling was not as pronounced. But in the quiet of the night, when her focus was sharp, she found she could even hear the howls of wolves in the wild. An Jiu sighed inwardly. So Mei Jiu had also inherited her ability. It seemed the ultimate victor was still uncertain! At least based on the current situation, Mei Jiu had the advantage; she was the original owner of this body and did not need to find a way to control it. Thinking this, An Jiu’s heart stirred. She coughed lightly twice and said in the gentlest voice she had ever used, “I am here.” “Can you talk? I am scared.” Mei Jiu could suddenly hear and sense so many things in the dead of night, and the once peaceful night suddenly became terrifying. “Are you not afraid of me anymore?” An Jiu asked. Mei Jiu did not answer. She was afraid, of course she was, but what she feared most right now were the sounds, like the soft rustling of falling leaves or perhaps the sound of people walking on tiptoe. “You do not need to be afraid of me. I was just looking for a place to stay and happened to find you.” An Jiu racked her brains, recalling some ghost stories she’d read before. “Not everyone is suitable for me to stay. The fact that you can take me in means we have a connection. You are doing a good deed; you will surely be blessed in the future.” Blessed! Hilarious! An Jiu thought playing the wolf in sheep’s clothing was really good. An Jiu knew very few ghost stories, but she thought it was enough to fool Mei Jiu’s intelligence. Sure enough, Mei Jiu was delighted. “I knew you were not a bad person.” “Good girl, you are right,” An Jiu readily affirmed. Of course, she was not a bad person, because she was a demon. “You should sleep first. With me here, no demons or monsters can get close.” An Jiu’s voice suddenly turned cold. “But I can protect you, and you have to promise not to tell anyone about my existence; otherwise… You know what will happen.” “Alright.” Mei Jiu readily agreed. With her company, Mei Jiu gradually relaxed and quickly fell asleep. An Jiu seized the opportunity to get out of bed and move around. She would not sit idly by and wait for her fate. If one person had to sacrifice another to achieve their goals, she would never be the victim! If the two could coexist, she would find a way to kill or expel Mei Jiu’s soul—because she was always alone and did not need any unnecessary appendages. She did not know how to seize the body, but first she needed to integrate with it. An Jiu could tell there were at least five people around the room, so she could not make any big movements. Since she had nothing else to do, An Jiu started by doing push-ups and sit-ups to exercise. But she discovered that this body was truly rotten! An Jiu lay on the floor, and her thin arms could not even hold a single push-up! She gritted her teeth and forced herself to do five. Too much of a good thing was bad; she needed to proceed gradually. An Jiu did not push herself. After the push-ups, she did twenty sit-ups. Afterward, she sat on the bed and practiced finger exercises, which not only helped her control her limbs but also improved her flexibility. After tossing and turning for most of the night, An Jiu finally closed her eyes reluctantly. Early morning. Mei Jiu woke up feeling as if her whole body was filled with lead; even her eyelids were incredibly heavy! “Young Lady, today we must go to the front courtyard to pay respects to Ah Lang and the clan elders,” Wen-Cui knocked on the door to remind her. “Come in.” Mei Jiu tried to sit up but could not. Wen-Cui pushed open the door and entered the room. Seeing Mei Jiu’s pale face and dark circles under her eyes, she was startled. “Young Lady, what’s wrong?” “I am not feeling well,” Mei Jiu said weakly. Wen-Cui checked her pulse but could not find anything wrong. Thinking her medical skills were inadequate, she said anxiously, “What should we do? We cannot delay seeing the clan elders! I will go fetch a physician.” She rushed out like a gust of wind before she finished speaking, showing how anxious she was. A short while later, Mei Jiu vaguely saw Wen-Cui leading a long-bearded old man in through the gauze curtain. The old man sat down by the bedside. Wen-Cui placed Mei Jiu’s wrist outside the bed curtains and covered it with a thin, icy silk cloth. The old man’s fingers rested on it, examining it for a moment. “The young lady is in good health, but perhaps she’s overworked and has not rested enough. Continue with the dietary supplements I prescribed the other day; she will recover completely in five days.” “But Physician Liu, the young lady is going to see Ah Lang and the clan elders today. Is there any way to help her get out of bed?” Wen-Cui asked. Physician Liu said, “She can get out of bed without medicine, though it will be tiring. Fourteenth Young Lady, please persevere.” “Thank you, Physician Liu.” Wen-Cui saw Physician Liu out. Upon returning, Wen-Cui pulled back the bed curtains. “Young Lady, today’s matter is extremely important! Please persevere.” “Yes.” Mei Jiu struggled to sit up. Wen-Cui helped her sit in front of the dressing mirror and began her daily grooming and dressing. Today, she was dressed in a simple, smoky-colored outfit, her hair styled in a simple bun without any adornment. “It’s a family rule that one should not dress extravagantly when meeting the clan elders,” she said. Mei Jiu smiled slightly. “It’s more comfortable this way.” “Yes,” Wen-Cui smiled, lightly dusting her face with powder to conceal the dark circles under her eyes.

chapters.title: Peach Blossoms Smiling Mo Sigui
chapters.content: Mei Jiu’s attire was quite different from yesterday’s. Not only was she no longer dressed in elaborate finery, but she had also added a belt, accentuating her curves! What was going on? Even Mei Jiu, unfamiliar with the customs of wealthy families, sensed something was amiss. “Wen-Cui, why am I dressed like this?” “It’s the custom,” Wen-Cui replied crisply. Mei Jiu, having been rebuffed, dared not ask further. Silence prevailed until they reached the entrance of Yuwei Residence. Only after Wen-Cui helped Mei Jiu into the carriage did she say, “If you are sleepy, Young Lady, take a nap. I will wake you when we arrive.” “Alright.” Mei Jiu felt relieved and leaned against the carriage wall, closing her eyes. After Mei Ruyan arrived, the carriage slowly began to move. The carriage ride was relatively smooth, and the gentle swaying quickly made Mei Jiu drowsy. Mei Ruyan asked Wen-Cui softly, “Is Sister not feeling well?” Wen-Cui shook her head and said softly, “She just did not sleep well last night.” Mei Jiu was rather timid, always appearing taciturn and weak in front of others. Yesterday, her sudden, sharp words, leaving Mei Ruyan quite puzzled, were a stark contrast. Now, seeing her back to her former self, Mei Ruyan felt strangely at ease. Perhaps this version of Mei Jiu was easier to fool. The carriage moved at a leisurely pace, stopping after about the time it takes to drink a cup of tea. Wen-Cui gently nudged Mei Jiu. “Young Lady, we’ve arrived.” “Hmm?” Mei Jiu opened her eyes. Wen-Cui took out a small bottle from her sleeve, uncorked it, and held it under Mei Jiu’s nose. The pungent smell made her sneeze, but a cool sensation rushed from her nose to her brain, instantly clearing her mind. The Mei Mansion occupied a large area, but there were no particularly exquisite buildings. Even the places where the head of the family and the elders resided were simple, with gray bricks and tiles. As soon as they got out of the carriage, they saw a tall, elegant young man in fine clothes standing under the eaves of the main hall. He looked about seventeen or eighteen years old, with the drooping, fiery red maple leaves reflecting off his fair face. His bright eyes sparkled, and he was clean-cut and dashing. An Jiu woke up just in time to see this scene and clicked her tongue in admiration, “What a handsome young man!” Mei Jiu frowned slightly, thinking to herself, “Can you say something more palatable?” An Jiu yawned. “Was what I said yesterday not palatable? That Old Madam was clearly so excited she fainted.” “It was because of you that she was so upset,” Mei Jiu reminded her. An Jiu said, “I said it yesterday; you did not need to emphasize it. I am not forgetful! Can you not tell it’s a joke?” Mei Jiu was displeased that she was joking about her own family. “What’s so funny?” “Then you really have no sense of humor,” An Jiu came to a conclusion, then, seeing the elegantly dressed young man walking towards them through Mei Jiu’s eyes, she automatically switched to “watching the show” mode. The young man, full of youthful vigor, stopped a step in front of Mei Jiu. His tall figure exuded a strong sense of pressure, and Mei Jiu’s breath almost stopped, only to suddenly quicken again after the young man gave her a bright smile. The forced, abnormally rapid heartbeat drove An Jiu almost mad. Even jumping from the thirtieth floor with a rope only one centimeter in diameter around her waist did not feel as intense as this! “Fourteenth Young Lady Ruxue,” the young man smiled, then looked at Mei Ruyan. “Fifteenth Young Lady Ruyan, I guessed right, did I not?” “And you are?” Mei Ruyan asked instead of answering. The young man said, “By all accounts, I am your cousin. My surname is Mo, my given name is Ran, and my courtesy name is Sigui.” Wen-Bi and Wen-Cui curtsied slightly. “Greetings, Young Master.” “Our young ladies do not marry outside the family, so where did this cousin come from?” Mei Jiu asked. Mo Sigui stared at Mei Jiu, his peach blossom eyes smiling. “There are always exceptions.” “Sedition.” An Jiu looked intently at Mo Sigui through Mei Jiu’s eyes. “Blatant seduction! This kind of boy is too flirtatious, too wanton!” Her words were very explicit. Mei Jiu’s cheeks flushed, and she lowered her eyes, not daring to look directly at Mo Sigui. She felt An Jiu was right; a man who flirted with her from the moment they met was very frivolous. For the first time, the two agreed. Mei Jiu was very happy, but then An Jiu sighed. “I like it.” She liked tormenting people like this! An Jiu was trying her best to play the kind and gentle wolf in sheep’s clothing, but fearing Mei Jiu would find her taste violent, she forcibly held back the last few words. She sighed with delight, but her emotions remained completely unmoved, startling Mei Jiu into involuntarily uttering, “Ah?” Mo Sigui asked in surprise, “Cousin?” “Ah, I…I…” Mei Jiu tried to say something, but her mind was a jumbled mess, and she said awkwardly, “It’s nothing, it’s nothing.” Mo Sigui understood. Most young women would feel a little shy upon first seeing him. Oh dear! It was all because he was too handsome; being naturally beautiful was truly a problem. Mo Sigui flicked open a folding fan from his sleeve with a “whoosh,” concealing his unrestrained laughter. Mei Ruyan watched the two of them exchange words, a slight smile playing on her lips, understanding the unspoken message. Mo Sigui composed himself, put away the fan, and adopted a serious expression, clearing his throat lightly. “The elders have not arrived yet. Please, cousins, sit in the side hall for a while.” It was rather strange for an outsider to take the initiative; Mei Ruyan glanced at Wen-Bi. Wen-Bi lowered her eyelids, pretending Mo Sigui was not present. “Young Master’s mother passed away long ago. He grew up in the Mei family and is just like our own son.” Mei Jiu secretly glanced at Mo Sigui’s face. Seeing his expressionless face, she thought to herself, “Being introduced like this to his face must be very uncomfortable, right?” An Jiu scoffed, “Mind your own business.” Mei Jiu thought she was jealous and quickly explained, “I…I have no feelings for him.” “What does that have to do with me?” An Jiu paused, suddenly remembering she could feel Mei Jiu’s body language. “No, it does! You are not allowed to have a relationship with him, or I will chop you two up!” From these vicious words, Mei Jiu was even more convinced she was jealous, so she understandingly assured her, “No, no.” An Jiu gave a satisfied “hmm.” After sitting in the side hall for a while, a servant came in to announce, “Ah Lang and the five elders will be arriving soon.” Mo Sigui stood up. “My two cousins, please go out and greet them.” The two agreed and followed him out of the side hall, standing on one side of the steps of the main hall to welcome the head of the family. A short while later, Mei Jiu saw a large group of people surrounding five elderly men with white hair and beards and a middle-aged man. All six were dressed in plain robes. The middle-aged man, holding a feather fan and wearing a turban, had a lean face and a serene, contented expression, exuding the air of a recluse. The elderly men all appeared to be over sixty, yet they walked with a brisk pace and remained robust. The middle-aged man walked up to Mei Jiu and the others, glanced at them indifferently, and without stopping, went straight into the house. Mo Sigui sighed softly. The last old man in the group raised his cane and tapped him on the head. “Why are you sighing at such a young age?” Mo Sigui, far from being deterred, grinned and said, “You are not lame, so why are you using a cane?” The old man glared at him resentfully. “You little brat! We will see what you are made of tomorrow!” “Bring it on!” Mo Sigui retorted, unfazed. Once everyone was inside, Mo Sigui noticed Mei Jiu’s pale face. “Do not be afraid; they are just a few strange old men.” Mei Jiu did not hear a word Mo Sigui said; her mind was filled with An Jiu’s voice: “Are you very tired? Want to sleep? Think about your soft bed, how comfortable it is to lie on it. Do you not feel like you cannot hold on any longer? Why not go to sleep first, and I will take over for a while? Such a big commotion is too scary…”

chapters.title: Heroic Effort
chapters.content: Mei Jiu, having survived a life-or-death escape, had only just recovered from exhaustion yesterday. Then, An Jiu forced her to exercise until she was half-dead. She desperately wanted to rest… Mei Ruyan, walking behind Mei Jiu, saw her sway and fall backward. She could not help but gasp and reach out to catch her. Mo Sigui, hearing the sound, turned to grab her. Mei Jiu’s closed eyes suddenly opened, revealing a pair of bright eyes reflecting the red maple leaves, slightly mocking. Taking advantage of his momentary daze, An Jiu casually grabbed his belt, using his clothes to conceal it, while her other hand snaked between his legs, grasping a handful of flesh. She used this leverage to lift herself up! The force was so great that her fingernails likely dug into his flesh, yet to an outsider it appeared as merely a grab of his belt. Mo Sigui cried out in pain, staring incredulously at his cousin, who had just been so shy. “Thank you.” An Jiu raised an eyebrow, then lowered her head to shave her nails. “Go on in.” Mo Sigui limped up the stairs, his clothes rubbing against the wound on his inner thigh, causing him to wince in pain. An Jiu knew that controlling Mei Jiu’s body now was pointless; she simply did not want to miss any opportunity for their souls to mesh. Entering the main hall, An Jiu saw that Mo Sigui was not too reserved, performing only standard courtesies, so she relaxed considerably, bowing in greeting as Mei Jiu usually did. The furnishings in the main hall appeared simple and unpretentious, but An Jiu recognized that even the armchairs were made of fine rosewood. The floorboards, at first glance, looked like wood, but upon closer inspection, they were actually bamboo. These bamboo pieces were somehow leveled, seamlessly joined, and polished to a high shine, resembling a single, continuous floorboard—truly breathtaking. Everywhere in the room seemed ordinary, yet it possessed an indescribable comfort, revealing meticulous attention to detail throughout. “No need for formalities,” the patriarch said gently. The three straightened up, and he continued, “Fourteenth Young Lady and Fifteenth Young Lady have just returned home. Today, they will meet the elders and, incidentally, formally become disciples. Sigui is already Elder Qi’s chosen disciple, and today he will perform the disciple-acceptance ceremony with the two children.” An Jiu thought to herself, “Were we not supposed to be included in the family genealogy? Why the disciple-acceptance ceremony? This family’s instructions are too vague! Adapting to circumstances is risky.” “Fourteenth Young Lady, Fifteenth Young Lady,” the patriarch called out. An Jiu and Mei Ruyan looked up. The patriarch’s lean face wore a faint smile as he casually waved his feather fan. “Although our Mei family is a merchant family, we’ve always valued education. Our Mei children are all accomplished in both literature and martial arts; there has never been a lazy, uneducated one. Moreover, only after being recognized by a certain elder and formally becoming a disciple are they qualified to have their names written in the family genealogy. Do you have any questions?” “No,” the two replied in unison. What questions could there be? Was it not obvious? This means that children with poor aptitude were not recognized by the family. In this unfamiliar place, where even the rules of the game were unclear, what would be the consequences of not being included in the family genealogy… An Jiu felt a slight sense of crisis. She was proficient in none of the arts—music, chess, calligraphy, painting, poetry, and prose. Should she awaken Mei Jiu’s talents? If Mei Jiu were to participate, naturally, nothing would be a problem. The family head ordered the tools for testing their skills in music, chess, calligraphy, and painting to be laid out. “You two choose two,” he said. Mei Ruyan said, “Sister is skilled in calligraphy and painting, so please give me the music and chess.” She sounded very helpful, but in reality, she was quite skilled in these arts. Raised in a brothel, she was best at these entertaining skills. An Jiu was also satisfied and readily agreed. One should not show off one’s lack of knowledge in music and chess, but writing a few characters with a brush was still possible; it was just a matter of beauty or ugliness. “Sister, please go first,” Mei Ruyan said. An Jiu briefly recalled how to hold a calligraphy brush. After the maid laid out the paper, she boldly wrote, with a sense of shameful heroism, the line, “The wind howls, the Yi River is cold; the hero departs, never to return!” The decisiveness and elegance of her brushstrokes delighted the patriarch and several elders. As soon as she finished writing, two elders could not help but step forward to examine it. “This… putting aside the poor handwriting, what’s with the layout!” One elder pointed to the horizontal lines of characters on the paper, then to the comma and exclamation mark in the middle. “What does this mean?!” An Jiu was displeased: “You old fool, if you can write anything, just make do! Why are you being so picky?” The other elder was also somewhat disappointed, but remembering her earlier brushstrokes, he still held a sliver of hope. “Do you know anything else?” “I know a lot,” An Jiu replied calmly. The old man was pleased, but An Jiu added, “My skill level is about the same as my calligraphy.” The old man’s face darkened, and he scolded, “Young lady, do not speak so casually!” “Yes,” An Jiu replied readily. The elder scratched his dwindling white hair. “Are you really Lady Yan’s child? She did not just pick her up to fool us, did she?” An Jiu remained silent. The others also came over to look, shaking their heads in disappointment before returning to their seats. The elder who had spoken to her earlier, however, did not show much disappointment.
