Having been reborn, she was fortunate enough to experience “Startling the String” and fortunate enough to meet Mei Yanran; that was enough.

chapters.title: To Try or Not to Try?
chapters.content: Neither the urge to kill nor the desire for a peaceful life was enough to sustain An Jiu’s will to live. An Jiu had always thought her emotional instability stemmed from mental health issues, but only now did she understand that humans were social animals. Besides their inherent fear of death and attachment to life, they needed emotions as a pillar. Without any emotional connection, nothing could fill that void. Before, she was a weapon devoid of emotion. Now, her deeply buried instincts were gradually awakening. The more she experienced emotion, the emptier she felt. This was something she could not steal. She did not know how to develop feelings for others, nor how to make others develop feelings for her. Whether in her past or present life, she had always walked alone, unchanged. Rather than saying she had lost the ability to interact with people, it was more accurate to say she had closed her heart, unwilling and afraid to approach anyone. A gust of wind blew, and the snow in front of Qiming Hall pattered softly onto the ground, startling the sparrows perched on the branches. An Jiu raised her hand, and the door opened at that moment. Mo Sigui’s peach blossom eyes were full of surprise, but upon seeing her unapproachable expression, he immediately became interested. “Oh, Fourteenth, you are back! I heard you returned early. How are you? Are you injured? Cousin has some good medicine here; it will prevent scarring.” “Is Elder Qi here?” An Jiu automatically ignored his rambling. “It’s cold outside, let’s come in and talk.” Mo Sigui stepped aside and led An Jiu into the pharmacy. The room was filled with the rich aroma of herbs. The medicine pot on the stove was bubbling away, its lid pushed open, spilling medicine everywhere. “You little rascal! Who knows where you’ve run off to be lazy again!” Mo Sigui quickly found a clean rag, wrapped the medicine pot, and carried it down. “Please, sit wherever you like!” Mo Sigui casually wiped the spilled medicine on the floor with a rag, saying to himself, “This is Ah Yuan’s medicine. I heard she was frightened and cried nonstop after waking up! My poor second cousin, gone at such a young age. The head of the family and his wife are burying their son, alas!” “Are you sad?” An Jiu asked. Mo Sigui was used to rambling on to himself and had not expected a response. Hearing An Jiu speak, he paused, slightly taken aback. “Among my peers in the Mei family, I only got along well with my eldest and second cousins,” Mo Sigui sighed. “Although I did not particularly like his always-serious lectures, I still cannot believe he’s suddenly gone. I always feel like he will come to me in a couple of days to get medicine for the two elders. As for sadness… perhaps it’s because physicians are used to life and death, and are more ruthless; surprisingly, I am not that heartbroken.” Mo Sigui was a chatterbox, especially when it came to things that interested him, always asking endless questions. Now that he’d finally caught An Jiu calm, he naturally would not let it go. “Where’s my adorable little cousin?” “Fourteenth Young Lady?” An Jiu asked. Mo Sigui rolled his eyes. “Yeah! You do not think I’m talking about you, do you?” “Do you want to see her?” An Jiu was not annoyed. “Elder Qi said that with two souls united, the stronger the spiritual power, the easier it is to damage. Can you suppress spiritual power?” Mo Sigui opened his mouth, then hesitated for a long time before speaking. “What…what are you going to do?” “Answer me.” An Jiu stared at him. Mo Sigui coughed lightly and said, “I understand. But I’ve never tried it before. After all, someone like you is extremely rare in the world. I should be grateful to have encountered even one.” “I will give you a chance to try. Kill me,” An Jiu said. Seeing her calm expression, Mo Sigui became even more curious. “You do not seem like a coward. What’s bothering you that you want to die?” An Jiu said, “Did you not want to see your adorable little cousin? Just achieve your goal; why ask so many questions?” “I am not that stupid. Whether this succeeds or not, Elder Zhi will be the first to punish me if he finds out!” Mo Sigui looked at the medicine pot. “The fire is too high; it will ruin the medicine’s effectiveness.” As he spoke, he did not pour out the medicine, but instead put it back on the stove to continue boiling. “For something like this, medicine alone will not do,” Mo Sigui explained to himself. “A little bit of medicine is enough; do you expect me to suffer through a heartbreak with an herbal decoction? There’s no such miraculous medicine in the world!” An Jiu stared at his face, flushed red in the firelight, and suddenly wanted to talk to him. “What’s it like living under someone else’s roof?” Mo Sigui looked up, grinning. “You really do not know how to talk. Who comes up here and immediately hits the nail on the head?” “Otherwise?” An Jiu asked, not ashamed to ask. “Nothing much. If it were someone else, would they have such a good temper? Only me.” Mo Sigui scratched his head and pouted. “You think I latched onto the Mei family? I am doing just fine in Bianjing; I am all set for myself. It was the Mei family who insisted on bringing me here.” He lived alone, with no one to care for him or ask about him. Although he was quite free, he was also very lonely. Mei Zhengjing picked up Mo Sigui, and the two hit it off immediately, so Mo Sigui willingly came to Mei Mansion. “It’s all that frivolous uncle’s fault! He tricked me into coming here and then dumped me with Elder Qi.” Mo Sigui leaned closer to An Jiu, lowering his voice. “Speaking of which, I should thank you. If it were not for your stunt, I might be in the same situation as my older cousin right now.” “But I have to clarify,” Mo Sigui quickly added. “I am not young at all.” “Do you have to let the whole world know you are not young? Or are you having feelings for your cousin?” An Jiu said disdainfully, “You beast.” “What’s wrong with liking a young woman?” Mo Sigui took out the fan with the “Red Apricot Over the Wall” design and added some air to the fire. “So clueless about romance,” Mo Sigui suddenly remembered. “You did not come here to see me from the beginning, did you?” “Have you always been so oblivious?” An Jiu said. “I only remembered you existed when I saw you open the door. I figured it would be easier to find you than Elder Qi.” Mo Sigui flung the fan away, angrily saying, “Is this how you ask for a favor?” “Are you forgetful? You already said you do not want to do it. What else do you want me to ask for?” An Jiu said. Mo Sigui closed the fan and tapped his forehead. “Even someone as calm as me has been angered by you. That shows how unlikable you are.” Seeing An Jiu got up to leave, he immediately rushed to the door to block him, his face turning into a grin. “You are so impatient. We were just joking. Look at you, turning around and leaving.” An Jiu was not emotional; she just felt that since he was not willing to do it, there was no point in staying any longer. “I agree to give it a try,” Mo Sigui said with a resolute expression. But An Jiu was certain this man had been eager to try from the start; he was just putting on airs. “You do not need to impress me. If you succeed, I will disappear. No one will owe you a favor. If you fail, I certainly will not.” “You are really no fun at all,” Mo Sigui said, leaning against the doorframe with his arms crossed, glancing out onto the veranda. “You have a bodyguard with you. How can we talk if I do not deal with him?” This explanation was more acceptable. An Jiu sat down again and explained the situation: “Mei Jiu is currently missing. I can sense she’s still there, but she’s not responding.”

chapters.title: An Jiu’s Kindness
chapters.content: “Let me take your pulse.” Mo Sigui’s eyes gleamed. Ever since he learned to use true qi to take pulses, he had been searching everywhere for people to experiment with. This method was a thousand times more precise than simple pulse taking, and he was eager to know how the pulse of someone with dual souls would differ from that of an ordinary person. Mo Sigui placed his fingers on An Jiu’s wrist, strands of true qi transforming into silken threads, slowly seeping in. He carefully examined the entire meridian system, but found nothing different from that of ordinary people. Undeterred, he examined it again and again. After the time it takes to drink two cups of tea, Mo Sigui finally discovered a subtle difference around the heart meridian. Some tiny fluctuations there were not as smooth as the rest of the meridian. He tried to approach it with his true qi, and those tiny fluctuations suddenly disappeared. Seeing sweat beading on Mo Sigui’s temples and his face growing increasingly pale, An Jiu asked, “Are you done yet?” Mo Sigui frowned slightly, without answering. The only sound in the room was the bubbling of the medicine pot. An Jiu felt a slight movement in the air around her, and suddenly a fair and strong hand gripped Mo Sigui’s wrist. An Jiu felt her internal energy rapidly dissipate. She looked up and saw Elder Qi’s face filled with rage. A moment later, as Mo Sigui opened his eyes, Elder Qi slapped him on the back of the head, roaring, “You brat! Do you want to die? Get out of the medicine hut! I only admit people who come in sideways, not out sideways!” Mo Sigui, used to being beaten, calmly smoothed his disheveled hair. “I am still alive and kicking.” “Alive and kicking!” The renowned physician, who had cultivated his health for decades, was now panting heavily with anger. “Tell me! How many times have I pulled you back from the edge of the cliff these past few days? If you do not behave, get out of here!” Elder Qi had just returned from gathering herbs in the back mountain when he found a guard unconscious on the beam in the corridor. Taking a few steps closer, he smelled a sedative mixed with a hallucinogenic drug, immediately guessing that it was Mo Sigui’s doing again! Elder Qi deeply regretted teaching Mo Sigui the method of pulse diagnosis using internal energy. Mo Sigui was highly talented and had a strong grasp of the subject, initially making Elder Qi very pleased. However, after only a few days, Elder Qi realized he was in deep trouble—this brat was trying it on everyone he met! He was treating internal energy like trash picked up off the street! It was important to understand that pulse diagnosis using internal energy was extremely taxing on both internal and mental strength. Occasional use could temper mental strength, which was beneficial in the long run, but excessive use in a short period would lead to depletion of internal energy and decline in mental strength, potentially even resulting in sudden death. Elder Qi tried reasoning with him and appealing to his emotions, and repeatedly warned Mo Sigui seriously, but to no avail, because he simply could not control his curiosity! Elder Qi slowly calmed his anger and warned him again. “You better shut up, or I will break your damn hands!” Mo Sigui leaned lazily against the medicine cabinet beside him, his chin resting on his folding fan, grinning. “I’ve been obedient. It’s been three hours since I last tried. There’s a special situation, you know.” “Three hours! That’s a long time!” Elder Qi kicked him away impatiently. Mo Sigui had been with Elder Qi for a long time and knew what he meant, so he quickly jumped up. He fawned over Elder Qi, vigorously wiping the stool with his sleeve, then fanned him with his folding fan, and reached out to help Elder Qi sit down. “Please sit down, please sit down.” “Sigh!” Elder Qi sighed helplessly. Elder Qi had a strange temper. But he was helpless against Mo Sigui. Sometimes, when he was really angry, he wanted to just kick him out, but thinking of Mo Sigui’s exceptional talent, he could not bear to. Imagine… Who else in this world could earn the title of “miracle physician” in Bianjing at the age of twelve or thirteen? Even if most people admired him because of his youth and gave him some credit, without genuine talent and skill, he would not deserve such a great reputation. Even Elder Qi admired Mo Sigui’s aptitude for medicine. His curiosity and focus on medicine were qualities Elder Qi appreciates, but this was also what made him a headache. “Is something wrong?” Elder Qi asked An Jiu. Before An Jiu could speak, Mo Sigui interjected, “She said the weaker one’s spiritual power is stagnant; she does not know if it disappeared or what.” An Jiu nodded. Elder Qi glared at him and asked, “What were the results of your pulse diagnosis?” “The other spiritual force has only weakened, but has not disappeared yet,” Mo Sigui added. “I am not entirely sure, but I am about 70-80% certain.” “I’ve never encountered two souls in one body before, but in the past few days I’ve read through ancient books and found a few fragmentary records,” Elder Qi said. “I’ve pondered this for a long time and believe this situation will not last long. Two tigers cannot share one mountain. If nothing unexpected happens, the strong will eventually devour the weak.” Elder Qi placed his fingers on An Jiu’s wrist, taking her pulse for a while, and slowly said, “Survival of the fittest, whether you like it or not.” “How is she now?” An Jiu asked. Elder Qi shook his head, his face expressionless. “Such matters are extremely mysterious; I cannot possibly understand them.” Knowing she would not get any answers, An Jiu stood up and said, “Thank you.” “Mm,” Elder Qi accepted readily. Seeing An Jiu about to leave, Mo Sigui jumped up. “Let me see you off!” “Sigui!” Elder Qi called out to him. “Do not worry, I will not kill myself,” Mo Sigui said, then went out of the house first. The sun was shining brightly outside, the icicles on the eaves reflecting golden light, the snow dazzlingly white. An Jiu squinted. “Since you are not the same person as Fourteenth, do you have a name?” Mo Sigui asked. An Jiu walked silently towards the door, only saying “An Jiu” when she was almost out. She acknowledged Mo Sigui because she had not given up on the idea of ​​self-destruction. Elder Qi was not very cooperative, but Mo Sigui seemed quite interested in the matter. “An?” Mo Sigui pondered, hands clasped. “You even have a name. Are you a wandering spirit? Did you do too many wicked things to be reincarnated? Should I find some monks to chant sutras for you?” “You can prepare that first.” An Jiu did not even glance at him, turning and leaving the room. “I think someone of your character is probably capable of many wicked deeds. When you are about to die, have hundreds of monks chant sutras for a hundred days, and you might end up like me.” “I am just trying to be kind; can you not appreciate it a little?” Mo Sigui was anxious for a while, but seeing no reaction, he scurried back, trying to smooth things over, “Fine, I am a kind-hearted person. Tell me, what good deeds have you done? I will have a high-ranking monk chant before Buddha from time to time; maybe it will help.” Some things were mysterious. An Jiu, erring on the side of caution, thought carefully, “I let the neighbor’s kid play with my favorite toy for three days.” Although she gave the kid a good beating when he broke the toy. “…” Mo Sigui’s eyes widened, and after a long pause, she said, “Is there anything bigger, more meaningful?” An Jiu pondered for a while before her furrowed brows relaxed. “When I was volunteering in the community, I helped an old lady feed her dog for a month.” “You…” Mo Sigui met her icy gaze. “That’s quite a great deed.” “Are you really unable to find out Mei Jiu’s condition?” An Jiu asked.

chapters.title: Accompanying You to Bianjing
chapters.content: The topic shifted abruptly, but fortunately, Mo Sigui was a quick-witted person. “As soon as my true energy touched her, she immediately dodged, so I could not probe her condition. But the fact that she reacted means she’s still conscious. Perhaps she’s deliberately avoiding me?” “Hmm.” An Jiu thought Mo Sigui’s words made sense. “Based on my interactions with Fourteenth, she’s completely different from you,” Mo Sigui said. “She’s kind and gentle by nature. She might be able to cope with ordinary setbacks, but killing is something not everyone can do.” He intended to be sarcastic, but An Jiu did not detect anything amiss. “I think so too.” Mo Sigui’s punch missed its mark, and he lost interest. “Have you considered that if you disappeared, Fourteenth probably would not survive more than two days in the Mei family? You might as well see it through, or rather, let nature take its course.” According to Elder Qi’s suggestion, letting nature take its course meant An Jiu would be the victor sooner or later. She murmured to herself, “As long as I live, I cannot avoid killing. The more people I kill, the further I get from the peace my heart seeks.” Though unwilling to admit it, she was indeed a madwoman. The more she killed, the colder her heart became, yet the more her blood boiled. There was a time when she could not control her killing intent, wanting to strangle any living thing she saw, even herself. In the snow, she exhaled mist, murmuring these words softly, the words dissipating in the wind. Yet, Mo Sigui perceived a hollow and pale life, without hope or despair, living in a daze, then killing. Mo Sigui patted her shoulder. “Do not be afraid; Cousin will take you to experience the beauty of this world.” An Jiu was slightly taken aback. “I am not the Fourteenth Young Lady.” “Ha, I was not talking to her either.” Mo Sigui fanned himself hard with his folding fan for a while, unable to dispel the pity he felt for An Jiu. He himself wondered how such a fierce and unlikable girl could inspire pity? An Jiu pursed her lips. She had not expected that her first time voluntarily revealing her true feelings would be to the person she hated most! And this shameless physician actually pitied her for her ruthless killing? “Ahem, go ask Elder Zhi. After my second cousin’s funeral, we will go to Bianjing together,” Mo Sigui said. “There are many fun places there.” “A trade. I will find a way to get you out, and you kill me.” An Jiu saw through his intentions at a glance. The Mei family’s rules. No one in the Mei family was allowed to enter or leave Mei Mansion at will. Since arriving here, Mo Sigui had rarely had the opportunity to go out. Although he enjoyed his secluded life, he occasionally missed the prosperity of Bianjing. Mo Sigui gritted his teeth, thinking to himself: stubborn, sharp-tongued, cold-faced and wicked, utterly ignorant! Having thoroughly vented his frustrations in his mind, he finally spoke. “Alright, deal.” “Since that’s the case,” An Jiu said casually as she walked towards Elder Zhi, “if you cannot kill me, I will take your life.” “Hey!” Mo Sigui had never intended to actually agree to her request. Hearing her say that, he hurriedly chased after her. “A physician saves lives. It’s bad luck if someone dies before I’ve even completed my apprenticeship! How about we wait a few years until I am fully trained?” An Jiu stopped and turned around. “Then let me know when you’ve completed your apprenticeship, and I will go ask Elder Zhi for help.” Mo Sigui persisted, trying to persuade her. “Bianjing is full of talented people, and there are several Taoist temples and Buddhist monasteries nearby. We can go and take a look; they understand the soul better than physicians.” Seeing that An Jiu was somewhat tempted, he quickly added fuel to the fire. “Besides, your stay in the mortal realm is a rare opportunity. Do you not want to go and see it? There’s no fighting and killing outside; it’s completely different from Mei Mansion.” He used his inner strength to scan the surroundings, making sure no one was around, then lowered his voice and said, “I know you are tired of fighting. Lady Yan felt the same way back then. If you could escape Mei Mansion as Lady Yan did, would you not be able to enjoy a peaceful and prosperous era?” An Jiu’s choice to self-destruct had many reasons, and what Mo Sigui said was only one of them. However, one sentence in particular resonated with An Jiu: he said there was no fighting and killing outside. An Jiu’s previous life was also relatively peaceful, without large-scale wars, but she had not had the opportunity to experience it. Although she was still following the old path, she was not a wanted criminal, and she had a family to rely on. She could relax and go out for a stroll—an opportunity she’d never had before. She made a concession. “Fine. But you still have to do your best to destroy me. I promise I will not kill you even if I fail. Besides, I am just a soul, not a human life.” “I did not expect you to be so talkative,” Mo Sigui said helplessly, looking at her. “But what kind of talk is this?” Who spoke of destroying oneself as effortlessly as discussing everyday matters? Meeting An Jiu’s calm gaze, Mo Sigui waved his folding fan haphazardly. “Fine, fine, I will do as you say.” Having reached an agreement, they headed towards Yongzhi Hall together. One had exhausted his inner strength; the other had almost none. In the blinding light of the snow, the two trudged forward, one step deep, the other shallow. The snow on the shooting range in front of Yongzhi Hall was smooth, leaving two long trails of footprints where they had walked. Mo Sigui chattered incessantly along the way, but suddenly fell silent upon entering Yongzhi Hall. The large courtyard was deserted. The two wandered around for a while, and Mo Sigui muttered under his breath, “I dislike Elder Zhi’s residence the most; it’s so big but lacks any human warmth.” “Fourteenth,” Elder Zhi’s voice suddenly came from the main hall. “Come in.” An Jiu entered the house, and Mo Sigui followed eagerly inside. There were no chairs in the main hall, only about ten futons. Elder Zhi knelt on the futon at the head of the table, his body hunched over. “Sit down.” Mo Sigui loved watching a spectacle, so he obediently knelt with An Jiu. “How did the trial go?” Elder Zhi asked. “Not bad,” An Jiu replied. Elder Zhi nodded, quite pleased. “I roughly understand what happened from Third. I heard you overpowered a Transcendent Realm archer.” An Jiu said, “It was all luck.” “Not arrogant or impatient, good,” Elder Zhi praised. Later, Mei Tingzhu and An Jiu separated. Only the members of the Konghe Army were present when An Jiu fired the arrow; Elder Zhi was unaware of this; otherwise, he would never have remained so calm. “Why have you come to see me?” Elder Zhi asked. An Jiu replied, “I am going to Bianjing.” Elder Zhi’s gaze swept over Mo Sigui. “What for?” “To take a look,” An Jiu said matter-of-factly. Mo Sigui was secretly anxious. This did not sound like a request at all. Would Elder Zhi take his anger out on him? “Very well. There are many hidden matters in this trial, and the major families will need time to investigate. We will send you juniors away from Mei Mansion as a precaution.” Elder Zhi’s quick agreement completely surprised Mo Sigui. Although they did not fully understand Elder Zhi’s meaning, they sensed a chilling undercurrent.

chapters.title: The Blue Arrow
chapters.content: “It’s not safe for my cousin to go out alone,” Mo Sigui said. Elder Zhi seemed not to understand him. “I will assign you guards. Qianshan…” He paused, staring at Mo Sigui with displeasure. “Where’s Qianshan?” Mu Qianshan was a seventh-level martial artist, skilled in hidden weapons. It was impossible for an ordinary person to take him down silently unless drugged. In the Mei Clan, only Elder Qi and Mo Sigui possessed this ability. Elder Qi obviously would not be so bored as to trouble a mere Shadow. Mo Sigui shrank his neck, stammering, “I saw… I saw him squatting on the roof beam, looking exhausted…” Elder Zhi was not particularly short-tempered, but in the entire Mei Clan, Mo Sigui feared him the most. He possessed a wise mind, a gaze that seemed to see through everything, and rarely considered emotions in his actions. Such a wise man was truly terrifying. Elder Zhi did not press the matter further, gently letting the topic pass. He then said to An Jiu, “After Tingjun’s burial, come to me to retrieve your entry token.” “Alright,” An Jiu replied. Silence followed for a moment. Then An Jiu said, “Elder, please have Mo Sigui come out with me.” “Do you two not have a grudge?” Elder Zhi’s calm face betrayed no emotion, as if he were asking casually. Mo Sigui chuckled, “We are all family, there’s no grudge that lasts overnight. A small misunderstanding was cleared up long ago.” “That’s good.” Elder Zhi got up to leave. Mo Sigui said, “Elder…” “Oh, right,” Elder Zhi interrupted him, instructing An Jiu, “Starting tomorrow, come here to practice. You do not need to go to the clan school.” With that, he turned and left. Mo Sigui kept giving An Jiu meaningful glances, his eyes almost twitching. An Jiu calmly replied, “I can unleash the ‘Startling the String’ technique.” Elder Zhi abruptly stopped, turned to look at An Jiu a few times, and suddenly grinned. “You may not understand, but I hate it most when people blatantly lie.” “What force do you think I used to suppress a Transcendent Realm expert?” An Jiu stood up and said, “I have no internal energy, but others do.” Elder Zhi’s eyes widened slightly. “Really?” “Since I dared to say it, it is true,” An Jiu said. Elder Zhi appeared calm, but his voice trembled uncontrollably. “Come here.” “If you promise I can go out with Mo Sigui, I will tell you the secret.” An Jiu remained standing. Elder Zhi’s expression darkened slightly. “You are blackmailing me.” “It’s a deal,” An Jiu corrected him. He revealed the secret of the ‘Startling the String’ technique for just this small request. Elder Zhi disapproved of An Jiu’s ruthless pursuit of her goal, but of course, he would not pass up an opportunity. “If you can successfully fire the arrow, I will agree.” “Alright,” An Jiu replied. “Then let’s go.” Elder Zhi turned and left. Mo Sigui was stunned for a moment before realizing what An Jiu had just said and quickly got up. Elder Zhi and An Jiu were heading towards the large shooting range outside. His inner strength was slowly gathering, so he gathered his energy and flew after them. Visibility was extremely high today. The wind was also light. Elder Zhi ordered someone to fetch a bow and arrows. An Jiu casually shot a few arrows at the target to familiarize herself with the bow and arrow. “Shoot a few more arrows and see,” Elder Zhi said, staring at the bullseye in the distance. An Jiu did as instructed and drew her bow. She was quiet and focused while preparing, almost every muscle in her body tense, yet at the moment of release, she seemed remarkably relaxed and casual. Elder Zhi remained silent, lost in thought. After a moment, he raised his hand and pressed it against An Jiu’s back. An Jiu felt a surge of icy internal energy enter her, her meridians instantly feeling as if icicles were being driven into them. The pain quickly subsided into numbness. Elder Zhi’s internal energy clashed with that of the Divine Martial Commander, like fire and ice. An Jiu’s meridians had already been damaged when they were forcibly widened before, making this experience even more unbearable. Mo Sigui saw her face turn pale instantly and reached out to grasp her pulse. “Elder, stop!” Mo Sigui exclaimed. “If this continues, her meridians will be ruined.” Elder Zhi’s eyes dimmed, a moment of hesitation passing through him, but he did not stop. Elder Zhi was a cold-blooded man. His special regard for An Jiu stemmed solely from his fanaticism for archery. He had pursued the pinnacle of archery for decades, and now, with the opportunity to witness the amazing feat of archery firsthand in his lifetime, how could he let it slip by? His disregard for An Jiu’s life was also due to his fervent passion for archery. An Jiu had already given up all hope; what did it matter if one of her meridians was destroyed? “Hey!” Mo Sigui released her hand, trying to persuade her, “What will Fourteenth do if your meridians are destroyed?” “Too late.” An Jiu’s meridians were already replenished with internal energy. She raised her bow, spreading two fingers to draw the string. Mo Sigui lowered his shoulders, looking at An Jiu’s exquisite profile. Her skin was fair and translucent in the snowy light, her eyes reflecting the snow like black glass. She was calm and cold. A blue light slowly emerged between her slender white fingers, just like the master on the cliff. A crane’s cry. The blue arrow flew three zhang before disappearing abruptly, the target twenty zhang away, swaying slightly. The world returned to calm. Elder Zhi released his grip, darted to the target, and raised his trembling hand to touch the arrow holes. But the moment his fingertip touched it, the entire target instantly turned to dust. He immediately went to check the large tree behind the target. “Ha!” Elder Zhi suddenly laughed. “Hahaha!” It turned out the target was too small to withstand the powerful internal force, so the remaining force pierced the tree, pulverizing the entire trunk. Elder Zhi slapped it, sending wood chips flying everywhere. Blood slowly seeped from An Jiu’s mouth and nose. Mo Sigui gripped her wrist again. An Jiu broke free, using her bow as a cane for support, and hastily wiped away the blood. “So this is not your body, and you do not care?” Mo Sigui checked her pulse again. This time, An Jiu did not resist, letting him take her pulse. “Do not move! I will go back to the medicine furnace to get the needles and be right back!” Mo Sigui lifted his robe and hurriedly ran off. An Jiu felt as if her entire body was being torn apart and stitched back together bit by bit; every inch of her body was wracked with excruciating pain. “How did you do that?” Elder Zhi had returned sometime earlier. The true power of the “Startling the String” technique was like this: It did not have any earth-shattering momentum, but its destructive power was terrifying. Once the arrow of pure internal energy struck its target, its power would explode within the target’s body! That was a tree; if it had been a person, one could imagine how their internal organs would have been torn apart. “Mental energy.” An Jiu opened her mouth, blood gushing out, which she wiped away with her sleeve. “I used my mental energy to distribute or condense my internal energy.” Elder Zhi was somewhat disappointed. He had grasped this principle more than a decade ago but had never been able to put it into practice. He was about to examine An Jiu’s injuries when he suddenly thought of something. “Perhaps it is similar to Elder Qi’s method of diagnosing pulses with true qi?”

chapters.title: I Quite Like You
chapters.content: Elder Zhi, as if possessed, focused his inner energy on his fingertips, completely oblivious to his surroundings. An Jiu lowered her eyes, seeing the red plum blossoms in front of her feet blooming more and more vibrantly, her vision blurring. Standing in the cold wind for an unknown amount of time, An Jiu swayed, feeling a pair of hands supporting her arms, and then everything went black, and she lost consciousness. She slept very soundly, without dreams, but felt very tired. An Jiu opened her heavy eyelids and saw Mo Sigui’s face, so thin it was almost unrecognizable; only his ever-bright peach blossom eyes remained as beautiful as ever. “Awake!” Mo Sigui’s eyes shone brightly, his voice filled with arrogance as he exclaimed, “You bastard, how could you ruin my lifelong reputation!” “What happened to me?” When An Jiu was unconscious, she thought she was going to die, but she never expected to open her eyes and still be alive. “What’s wrong?” Mo Sigui raised her voice, noticing her hoarseness, and turned to pour her a glass of water, feeding her with a small spoon. “You really do not know how to cherish yourself! And rightly so; it is pointless to talk to someone who’s contemplating suicide.” Most people who contemplated suicide could not bear the suffering of living and wanted to end it all, but who could be as ruthless to themselves as An Jiu? The pain of having one’s meridians destroyed was something Mo Sigui could not even bear to think about. “I really do not know why someone like you would want to destroy yourself!” Mo Sigui said irritably. “Is Mei Jiu unresponsive?” An Jiu asked. Mo Sigui slammed down the glass and plopped down on the stool by the window. “Maybe she is. You kept crying while you were unconscious, but you would not wake up.” “That’s her.” An Jiu had never shed a tear because of her injuries. “My meridians…” Mo Sigui released her spiritual power to check the surroundings, confirming no one was around. “With your meridians completely destroyed, you almost certainly will not have any internal energy left.” An Jiu’s expression remained indifferent. “In other words, the shocking event half a month ago might have been the last time you ever experienced it.” Mo Sigui tapped his palm absently with his folding fan. “A person’s internal energy corresponds to the five elements, and meridians have innate attributes. Your meridians belong to the fire element, and not long ago, they were forcibly widened by an internal energy of the ‘fire’ element. Although you were slightly injured that time, it was actually very beneficial to you. As long as you recover well, your internal energy will increase rapidly afterward. Elder Zhi’s internal energy is the most domineering type of the water element. Your entire meridian system was torn apart, and even your dantian was almost completely destroyed.” With meridians destroyed and no attributes remaining, how could she generate internal energy? An Jiu’s attention was completely elsewhere, only murmuring, “I’ve been unconscious for half a month.” Mo Sigui sighed helplessly, “Since you came to me, it means you do not want to hurt Fourteenth, but even if you get what you want, how is she supposed to live? You were too impulsive.” He rarely spoke so seriously, but An Jiu was unmoved. “How she lives is her business; I am not her mother. I have no responsibility to take care of her!” Mei Jiu could control her body but did not resist, so An Jiu felt no guilt. “I begged Elder Qi to keep this a secret. If Elder Zhi is deliberately testing me, he will not be able to hide it,” Mo Sigui smiled lazily, “but he probably does not have time to bother with you right now.” His robes were loose, and he leaned casually against the table. He possessed a unique, almost romantic air about him. Listening to his slightly hoarse voice was like feeling rough fingers gently stroking one’s skin, a tickle that went straight to the heart. “I saw it all long ago. In this family, besides the younger generation, only Elder Qi and my uncle still have any humanity left.” Mo Sigui was not included in the family register, and by all accounts, he should have been immediately sent away from Mei Mansion. It was Elder Qi who overruled everyone’s objections and insisted on keeping him by his side. Mo Sigui’s willingness to stay stemmed entirely from Elder Qi’s familial treatment of him. “Thank you,” An Jiu said. Mo Sigui flicked open his folding fan and chuckled. “No need for thanks. I suddenly realize I quite like you. I am never stingy with people I like.” An Jiu turned her head, quietly looking at him, waiting for him to continue. “You are like a block of wood; I do not have to worry about causing trouble by talking to you,” Mo Sigui said, his eyes crinkling. “Besides, you always seem to have some rare injuries or illnesses. As a physician, how could I not like that?” An Jiu was displeased. She hated being used as a guinea pig, but Mo Sigui seemed different from the physicians she’d encountered before. “You used to hate me not long ago,” An Jiu said, intrigued by this. Not long ago, An Jiu had also intensely disliked Mo Sigui, but now things seemed to have changed, though she did not know when. “Do not ask why. I always do things based on my whims.” Mo Sigui tossed his fan onto the table and pulled two tokens from his robes. “I guessed Elder Zhi would be in seclusion, so I got the tokens before he went into seclusion. At such a high price, this matter cannot fall through. Rest for a few more days, and then we will go to Bianjing.” Mo Sigui’s sudden enthusiasm for An Jiu had many reasons. In truth, he was the one who started this whole affair. Even though things had escalated beyond his expectations and it was not entirely his fault, he still felt a pang of guilt. Furthermore, as a physician constantly striving for the pinnacle of medical skill, he could not possibly ignore such a peculiar case as An Jiu’s. In addition to these identifiable reasons, there was also a touch of sympathy and pity that even he could not quite articulate. The following days were blessed with fine weather; the snow had melted completely. An Jiu basked in the sun by the medicine stove, reading books—a life she had never known before. Mei Ruyan came to see her every day. An Jiu watched as the young woman grew increasingly beautiful. Yao-Ye often whispered in her ear about Mei Ruyan’s infatuation with Master Mo, but she always kept to herself, and besides, she was already preoccupied with her own affairs, so she could not be bothered to interfere. In her spare time, however, she did think about many things. She discovered that Mo Sigui had been solely responsible for her injuries, while Elder Qi only occasionally came to check on her, never offering to diagnose or treat her. It seemed he had given up on treating her, leaving her to Mo Sigui for experiments. What caught her attention the most was that Elder Zhi’s internal energy was exactly the same as that of the master archer in the temple. If this was a coincidence, it was far too much. These things were enough for her to ponder for a while. After seven days, Mo Sigui, confirming that her injuries were no longer hindering her movement, prepared a carriage. The two of them, accompanied by a group of maids and servants, set off for Bianjing amidst the envy of onlookers. The carriage swayed gently. An Jiu initiated a conversation with Mo Sigui. “How many people have reached the mastery of water-based internal energy?” “Well… I think I can count them on one hand, fewer than twenty, but most are at the third rank. Second-rank, like Elder Zhi, is extremely rare,” Mo Sigui said doubtfully. “Why did you ask that?” An Jiu did not answer but instead asked, “Are there many people with internal energy attributes like Elder Zhi’s?”

chapters.title: Many Doubts
chapters.content: “There are quite a few, but those above the Transcendent Realm are extremely rare. In the entire world, only three can be named.” Mo Sigui then asked in confusion, “Why are you asking this?” An Jiu still did not answer, “Which three people?” Mo Sigui said, “Besides Elder Zhi, there’s Wei Yunshan, the former master of Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, and Cui Huling of the Cui Clan, but Cui Huling passed away three years ago.” “What kind of place is Piaomiao Mountain Mansion?” An Jiu asked. “Master Wei is a man of the martial world, seventy years old this year, a reclusive sage. He never married and had no children, but adopted two sons thirty years ago: Wei Chuzhi and Wei Yuzhi. Piaomiao Mansion was founded by the eldest son, who honors Wei Yunshan as its patriarch. This Piaomiao Mansion is a place that raises assassins; people pay them to do things,” Mo Sigui finished speaking, then said with dissatisfaction, “That’s not fair! I’ve said so much, but you have not revealed anything! It is not fair!” “Wait a minute,” An Jiu continued. “Was Master Wei as obsessed with archery as Elder Zhi?” Mo Sigui shook his head. “No, Master Wei’s weapon is an ancient zither.” He leaned back against the carriage wall, smiling. “It’s said that the zither was a keepsake from his fiancée, and he’s never parted with it for decades.” Cui Huling was dead, so that did not count. Then, could Wei Yunshan be that archery master? An Jiu did not know how the guqin was used as a weapon, but since it was made of strings like a bow, it was somewhat suspicious. “Could there be a hidden master of the Transcendent Realm?” An Jiu asked. Mo Sigui lowered his gaze, playing with the two round jade seeds, each the size of a quail egg, beneath the jade pendant. Hearing her question, he looked up and said, “Do you know why martial arts ranks are divided into two levels? Because after reaching the ninth level, you encounter a barrier. This is where your mental strength is most tested; if your mental state is not high enough, you cannot break through. The world is full of things that can influence and tempt people, and very few can comprehend them. Therefore, there are many ninth-level martial artists in this world, but few at the Transcendent Realm. The gap between the two is vast, and if even one appears, it is impossible to hide it.” He moved closer to An Jiu. “Are you done asking? Hurry up and tell me what happened; I am really suffocating!” An Jiu did not hesitate and simply explained the reason: “During the trial, I was ambushed by a group of mysterious people. I encountered a Transcendent Realm archery master. His internal energy, once solidified, was exactly the same as Elder Zhi’s.” Mo Sigui sat up straight. “That’s strange!” An Jiu would not joke about something like this. Mo Sigui had a bad feeling, as if he remembered something but could not quite grasp the key point. “This is not something I can interfere with,” Mo Sigui said, stopping himself from thinking about it. “After the Lantern Festival, Elder Qi and I will travel far and wide to find a highly skilled master to separate your soul. Elder Qi will take you with him then.” This was also one of the key reasons why Elder Qi agreed to help conceal An Jiu’s destroyed meridians. Mo Sigui blinked, her expression sly. “Since Elder Qi has already helped conceal it, he’s very likely to agree to take you with him. After all, if he leaves you in the Mei family, he might be exposed in a few days. How will he face Elder Zhi then? How will he face the family?” Elder Qi was determined to take this opportunity to take Mo Sigui away and pass on all his skills to him. If the family knew that An Jiu’s meridians were destroyed, they would never allow Elder Qi to go through the trouble of finding someone to help her separate her two souls. Elder Qi’s plan would then fall through. An Jiu stared at Mo Sigui, remaining silent. She was surprisingly unaccustomed to someone being so kind to her. Mo Sigui kicked her a few times. “Hey, hey, you cannot even say thank you. Why are you looking at me like that?” An Jiu said sternly, “Because I hate you.” “Why?” Mo Sigui knew An Jiu had always disliked him, but had they not gotten along well these past few days? “Do you not look in the mirror?” An Jiu closed her eyes. Mo Sigui paused, then said, crossing his legs, “Yes, I do. My handsome appearance would eclipse the heavens and earth, and my aura and charm would be awe-inspiring, making it impossible to look directly at me.” “Hmm,” An Jiu mumbled. “Beauty and intelligence—it is true that you cannot have your cake and eat it too.” Was this a roundabout way of saying he was stupid? “I am telling you…” Mo Sigui gritted his teeth and glared at her, “Do you dare say something nice?!” An Jiu’s breathing was even, as if she had fallen asleep! An Jiu’s meridians had gradually recovered, but she was still taking medication. Because Mei Jiu would cry incessantly from the pain after she fell asleep, preventing her body from resting and aiding in her recovery, Mo Sigui added a strong sedative to her medicine. However, despite his anger, Mo Sigui had not expected An Jiu to maintain such a sharp and alert mind just before falling into unconsciousness. Her quick reflexes were something most people could not keep up with, even when fully awake. Her earlier comment, “Do you not look in the mirror?” was clearly meant to imply that he was ugly and repulsive, which was why he had deliberately replied with such a long string of words to shut her up, but he still ended up being mocked. “Fine, that’s all the fun you have. I will let you off this time,” Mo Sigui muttered. He flicked open his folding fan, looking at the delicate, red apricot blossoms peeking out from behind the wall in the light. A faint smile slowly spread across his lips, and a rare tenderness appeared in his eyes. “Ningyu, I am here.” Mo Sigui’s fingers lightly traced the surface of the fan. “Who is Ningyu?” An Jiu suddenly asked. Mo Sigui was startled. “You were not asleep!” “Ningyu is your sweetheart?” An Jiu asked. “Looks like I will have to increase the dosage of the calming medicine next time,” Mo Sigui muttered, then continued, “Her name is Qiu Ningyu, and we were betrothed since childhood. Hey? I will not scold you for being such a nosy person!” An Jiu was not interested in other people’s private affairs; she was just curious what kind of person could make such a carefree guy so affectionate. This was not exactly a secret for Mo Sigui, and he wanted to confide in someone. “Ningyu’s father and my father were close friends and served in the same court…” Mo Sigui’s father, whose given name was Qing and courtesy name was Dengxian, had served as a supervisor in the Imperial Medical Bureau. Qiu Ningyu’s father, Qiu Jian, worked in the Imperial Guard; although his rank was not high, he had frequent access to the Emperor, making it a very desirable position. After three years of marriage without children, the Qiu couple asked Mo Sigui’s father to treat them. Six months later, Madam Qiu became pregnant, just as Madam Mo had given birth to a son. When the two ladies were eight months pregnant, Mo Dengxian determined the sex of the unborn child, and the Qiu couple decided to arrange a marriage. Qiu Jian was handsome and dashing, and Madam Qiu was one of the most beautiful women in Bianjing in her youth. Even if their daughter inherited all their flaws, she would not be too bad-looking. Furthermore, the two families had known each other for many years and were very familiar with each other. Mo Dengxian happily arranged the marriage. Mo Sigui said, “Ningyu is different from ordinary young ladies from wealthy families. She has a cheerful personality and has dressed as a boy to play with me since she was little.” Qiu Jian had finally gotten a daughter and doted on her, never scolding or disciplining her. He let the two children play together freely until Qiu Ningyu was thirteen years old before Madam Qiu confined her at home to learn needlework. “She’s a year younger than you; that’s not young,” An Jiu interjected after a while. She knew to some extent that women here married young, some even as young as eleven or twelve. Mo Sigui was almost twenty. Could that girl really wait this long? “Uncle Qiu passed away when Ningyu was fifteen, and she drowned three months later.” Mo Sigui’s eyes reddened. “But we searched everywhere and could not find her body. I just cannot believe she’s dead.” An Jiu turned her head to look at Mo Sigui. He tilted his head back for a moment, forcing back his tears, and smiled, saying, “I really wanted to propose as promised, but my entire family was wiped out; the ancestral hall was destroyed. If I married her, it would only make her a rootless, lonely soul. It is better to leave it as it is.” “I feel like I’ve been reborn. The world is no longer the same,” An Jiu said absentmindedly. “What do you mean?” Mo Sigui asked. An Jiu said, “When I came back from the trial, everything had changed. Even the rogue had become a devoted lover.” The kind and caring Elder Zhi had suddenly become cold and ruthless. Mei Jiu had disappeared, as if she had never existed. And the always carefree Mo Sigui… She roughly understood the changes in human relationships, but found them difficult to comprehend. Mo Sigui was immersed in the sadness of his memories when he heard An Jiu say this, and she could not help but feel a little angry. “I knew you could not expect anything good to come out of a dog’s mouth!”

chapters.title: Tokens of Love
chapters.content: An Jiu did not care about the mild insults at all. She woke up every time she wanted to look out the window, then went back to sleep. Mo Sigui wanted to chat with An Jiu, but she remained unresponsive despite his hoarseness. They set off early in the morning, hurrying as fast as they could, and finally entered the city before the gates closed. The Mei family owned several residences in Bianjing. While none were as spacious and luxurious as those in Meihua Lane, they were all complete with pavilions and terraces, and the scenery was excellent. The family arranged for them to stay in a small and exquisite residence. The main courtyard had a hall and a courtyard. The front courtyard was not large, but it had pine trees, bamboo groves, strange rocks, fragrant grass, and a small pond, creating a serene environment. The rear residences did not have the obvious multiple courtyards typical of northern residences, but were divided into four buildings, nestled among artificial hills and groves. Three were living quarters, and one particularly secluded courtyard served as a study. The snow-covered ground, unlike the lush greenery of summer, made the small, cramped space feel much warmer than the expansive buildings. After settling in, Mo Sigui came to find An Jiu. Because it was nearing the end of the year, shops were closing late, and the government had extended the curfew. “We came out with the steward. We only have three days to buy New Year’s goods; we cannot waste them.” Mo Sigui practically dragged An Jiu into the carriage. This small courtyard was located in a bustling area. An Jiu had barely settled into the carriage when she heard the lively sounds outside. Yao-Ye brought out a veil, but An Jiu refused to wear it. She could cover her face when committing murder and arson, but why should she have to cover it up just to go shopping? Yao-Ye earnestly advised, “On the streets, only poor women and maids do not cover their faces. You must wear a veil.” Even the most attractive courtesans in brothels would wear veils and cloaks when they went out. “Then I will go back and change into a maid’s outfit,” An Jiu frowned. Yao-Ye thought to herself that she had never thought her young lady was so stubborn before. How come she’d become such a different person since she came back? People usually became more and more menacing when they’d taken lives, but the changes in her young lady went far beyond that! “With your bearing… even in linen, you do not look like a maid. I beg you, please wear it,” Yao-Ye pleaded, looking at Mo Sigui with a distressed expression. Mo Sigui, with a look of gleeful anticipation, said, “If you do not want to wear it, then do not! It is not a big deal!” Yao-Ye’s face darkened. “Watch your words! Do not teach my young lady such bad things!” Mo Sigui closed her folding fan. “Later, we will go to a tailor shop and buy you a men’s suit that fits your size. Tomorrow, you will not need to wear a veil when you go out. Just bear with it for now.” “Alright,” An Jiu nodded. Yao-Ye was overjoyed. All his grudges against Mo Sigui vanished instantly. The group finally got out of the carriage. Shops lined both sides of the street, lanterns lit in front, and vendors lined the street, their pots steaming with hot vapor. An Jiu hesitated for a moment, then moved closer to a nearby stall. Mo Sigui followed, seeing the stall owner making candy, and said, “Boss, two portions, please.” The stall owner, seeing the group dressed so elegantly… His face lit up instantly, and he eagerly responded, “Oh, what kind of fillings would you like, My Lord and My Young Lady? We have peanuts, sesame seeds, walnuts…” Mo Sigui said. “One of each, please.” “Please wait a moment.” The stall owner took out several clean sheets of oil paper, neatly tied five small packets about the size of a fist, and handed them to Yao-Ye beside him. “Fifty coins in total.” Ten coins for a small packet, containing only about four or five pieces. Mo Sigui tossed in a small piece of silver. “The rest is your reward.” “Thank you, My Lord!” The stall owner happily pocketed the silver. An Jiu took a small packet from Yao-Ye, untied it, picked up a piece, and put it in her mouth. “My Young Lady, you must not,” Yao-Ye whispered, trying to stop her. “Let’s find a private room to eat slowly.” An Jiu ignored him. She continued stuffing candy into her mouth while moving closer to the stall next to her. Seeing Mo Sigui’s generous spending, the pastry vendor grinned when An Jiu turned around. “My Young Lady, would you like to try these mung bean pastries? Though they are simple, it is good to try something new.” “Two portions, please,” Mo Sigui said, leaning forward. “Alright!” In the blink of an eye, Yao-Ye had two more small bags in her hands. Because she needed to attend to An Jiu at all times, she handed the bags to the servant beside her. An Jiu popped the candies into her mouth one after another, visiting each stall. After walking about seven or eight zhang, the arms of the servant beside her were already full. Yao-Ye initially thought An Jiu was unfamiliar with these things, but after a while, she realized that her mistress was easily swayed; as long as the stall owner greeted her with a smile, she would rush over. She had the servant carry the things she did not like, and Yao-Ye carry the things she did like. Mo Sigui felt that An Jiu at this moment was practically like a five or six-year-old girl. “My Young Lady, there’s still tomorrow,” Yao-Ye gently advised. The group arrived at a restaurant. Mo Sigui glanced at the sky and said, “I have some business to attend to. You rest here for a while; I will be back in a couple of quarters.” An Jiu asked Yao-Ye, “Do we have money?” “Yes, plenty,” Yao-Ye replied. Hearing that they had money, An Jiu led Yao-Ye into the restaurant. A group of guards followed them in, leaving only the two men sent by Elder Qi with Mo Sigui. “Ungrateful wretch!” Mo Sigui patted his empty purse, heartbroken. He had just thought she was like a little girl; he was truly blind. Upstairs, in a private room by the window, several elegantly dressed young men watched An Jiu’s sweeping shopping spree unfold before their eyes. A young man in a long robe clicked his tongue. “Whose young lady is this? She’s a veritable female bandit!” “What nonsense! She paid!” a slightly older man chuckled. “Can you not see?” Another handsome young man in a blue brocade robe leaned against the window frame, his long, slender fingers holding a celadon wine cup, his eyes lowered as he looked down. The crowd followed his gaze and saw a slender plum blossom on the carriage emblem. “So it is the Mei family, no wonder,” one of them suddenly said, intrigued. “I’ve heard their daughters are all stunning beauties; why do we not go take a look?” He looked at the young man in the blue robe and said with a grin, “Brother Rongjian, do you still dare?” His words were met with a burst of laughter. Last time, during their outing, they made a bet that the loser would have to go to a mass grave. Hua Rongjian, true to his word, went into the graveyard, but the group waited and waited outside without seeing him emerge. Hua Rongjian was a direct descendant of the Hua family; if anything happened to him, they could not bear the responsibility! It was almost midnight, a time when, according to legend, the yin energy was at its strongest, so after discussing it, they hurriedly went inside to search. When they found Hua Rongjian, they saw him disheveled and laughed, accusing him of having an affair with a female ghost in the graveyard. “This time it really is a young lady! If Brother Rongjian can do it like last time, we will truly be convinced,” someone teased. Hua Rongjian put down his cup, stood up with a bright smile, and said, “You will see.” “Are you really going?” The older man pulled him back. “They are just teasing you. Why are you acting so recklessly?” “You’ve known me for a long time.” Hua Rongjian straightened his clothes, opened the door, and went out. The man followed him out, whispering, “Rongjian, is your family not currently negotiating a marriage with the Mei family? If this causes trouble, Prime Minister Hua might not forgive you!” Hua Rongjian was unconcerned. He grabbed a waiter, asked where the Mei family’s women were, and strode over. Over there, An Jiu had just entered the private room, and Yao-Ye was about to close the door when a hand pressed down on her. The two guards at the door did not even have time to stop him! “My name is Hua Rongjian, and I request an audience with Lady Mei,” he said. Hua Rongjian was a full head taller than Yao-Ye. Yao-Ye looked up, and a handsome face with an unrestrained smile was almost within reach. His teeth were white and even, his lips clean, his face fair yet possessing a heroic air, and his eyes, though somewhat frivolous, were not wicked, making it difficult to feel any ill will towards him. “Please, My Lord, show some respect,” Yao-Ye said. She did not need to ask An Jiu’s permission; what young man would come alone to visit a young woman of marriageable age? “I have something I wish to ask Lady Mei. If it is inconvenient to go inside, you can ask outside, but…” Hua Rongjian smiled. “The content might be detrimental to your lady’s reputation.” Yao-Ye’s mind raced slightly. “Whatever you wish to say, I can convey it to her. Please consider the reputation of both our families.” “I will go back and write a letter, then have a servant deliver it,” Hua Rongjian said. The room was not large, and An Jiu heard their conversation clearly. “Let him in!” “Young lady!” Yao-Ye stood guard at the doorway. “That’s an order,” An Jiu said calmly. Yao-Ye bit her lip, hesitated for a moment, then stepped aside. The Mei family’s children often died young, so they did not value chastity and reputation as much as ordinary families; even if some bad rumors spread, it would not matter much. Hua Rongjian entered the room and, through the crystal curtain, saw a slender woman drinking tea under the lamplight, with the Suzhou embroidery of bamboo rustling on the screen behind her. Seeing Hua Rongjian raise his hand to lift the curtain, Yao-Ye quickly stepped in front of him, gesturing for a chair in the outer room. “Please sit, Master Hua.” Hua Rongjian lowered his hand, turned, and sat down. “My Young Lady left me her jade pendant and handkerchief. Does she have feelings for me?” Yao-Ye was pouring tea when she heard this; her hand trembled, and scalding tea spilled onto the table. “My Lord, you cannot talk nonsense!” Jade pendants, handkerchiefs, and hairpins could all be considered tokens of love. If a man and woman exchanged these items without a betrothal ceremony, it was considered a secret transaction. An Jiu remembered that she had indeed robbed Hua Rongjian at the mass grave, taking his jade pendant, handkerchief, and dagger… However, Hua Rongjian’s purpose in appearing at the graveyard was suspicious, so she did not intend to admit it. “Do you recognize me?” “Yes, do not get it wrong,” Yao-Ye said urgently. “Fourteenth Young Lady,” Hua Rongjian immediately identified her. An Jiu was somewhat surprised. She had never revealed her birth order within the Mei family, yet this person had said it so readily, indicating a deep understanding of the Mei family and likely knowledge of their clandestine dealings. How should she respond in a meaningful way?

chapters.title: A Fight (1)
chapters.content: An Jiu put down her teacup. “You said I took your jade pendant? When and where?” “The mass grave,” Hua Rongjian said. So easily admitted it? “I…” An Jiu paused, a cold smile playing on her lips. Trying to trick me? Not so easy. “What would I be doing at the mass grave in the middle of the night? You’ve mistaken me for someone else.” Hua Rongjian smiled. “Since I recognized your identity, I am certain that the person I met that night was not someone else.” “Your rogue tactics are too low-level,” An Jiu commented casually. Hua Rongjian raised an eyebrow, stood up, and took a step forward, but Yao-Ye blocked his way. “The maids of the Mei family are different from those elsewhere.” Hua Rongjian took a few steps back, cupping his hands in salute. “I am sorry to have bothered you. Farewell.” Yao-Ye’s face paled slightly. In her haste, she had used all her power. “Wait,” An Jiu said. Hua Rongjian’s lips curled into a smile as he turned and asked, “Is there anything else, Young Lady Mei?” “How would the Emperor feel if he knew that Young Master Hua had gone to such lengths to inquire about the Konghe family?” An Jiu asked. After speaking, she suddenly realized that she seemed to have fallen into a trap. If Hua Rongjian was absolutely certain that Young Lady Mei was from the Konghe family, he would not have gone to the trouble of testing her today. Even so, An Jiu did not care much. She did not understand politics and was too lazy to care. Her current mindset was the same as Mo Sigui’s—acting according to her mood and whims. “Young Lady Mei has a straightforward personality, which I like,” Hua Rongjian said with a smile. “Would you be interested in hearing a story?” “Go ahead,” An Jiu said. “Bring a pot of tea.” Hua Rongjian casually sat back down. Yao-Ye was terrified. These two were talking about such a momentous matter as if it were a joke. She wanted to stop them, but hesitated, wanting to know what Hua Rongjian wanted to say. Hua Rongjian accepted the tea Yao-Ye brought. “Emperor Taizong, waking from his drunken stupor, donned a yellow robe at Chenqiao, and his army marched back to the capital. Emperor Gong of Zhou abdicated, changing the dynasty name to ‘Song’ and the era name to ‘Jianlong.’ The entire affair lasted only four days.” This was the “Chenqiao Mutiny.” An Jiu had heard a rough account from Mei Yanran and knew that this coup was not as simple as it appeared; in reality, the Konghe Army had secretly eliminated many opponents. “No coup d’état is ever completely bloodless.” Hua Rongjian spoke with his usual nonchalant air, yet his words were not the words of any spoiled brat. “If it were not for the achievements of the Konghe Army, would changing dynasties be so easy?” “Since ancient times, the rabbit has been killed after the hunt,” Hua Rongjian said. “The Konghe Army is too powerful now. Families occupying key positions within it will inevitably be attacked and may even face annihilation.” If the person listening to him today were the real Young Lady Mei, or someone who valued their life, it would certainly have an effect. However, Hua Rongjian did not know that the person he was facing now not only did not care about Young Lady Mei, but also did not care about her own life. “And then?” An Jiu genuinely listened as if it were a story. Hua Rongjian was secretly shocked by her reaction. Such composure at such a young age. He did not know if it was carefree or just too calm. He thought of the fleeting glimpse of her in the mass grave, and then of the reason he had decided to risk coming here today, and he calmed himself down. “Do you know what the commandments of the Konghe Army are?” Hua Rongjian asked. An Jiu replied, “No.” Hua Rongjian took a sip of tea, clearing his throat. “It’s loyalty and righteousness.” These two seemingly simple words caused An Jiu to pause, momentarily realizing the fundamental difference between her past and present lives. Although both involved killing, she had been a wanted criminal before, but now she served her country. At least she did not have to live a life hunted by the entire world. “Why are you telling me this?” An Jiu scoffed. “You want me to obey?” “Not at all. The reason I mention this is to tell you that the current Emperor is not worthy of such devotion from you.” Hua Rongjian’s words were firm and resolute. Yao-Ye gasped, immediately interjecting, “Young Master Hua, watch your words! Do not frighten my young lady! The Hua family has deep roots; they dare to say anything and talk about anyone. We are a humble family, no match for you. Please leave!” If it were not for the threat of exterminating nine generations of one’s family, Yao-Ye would never have spoken so rudely to the eldest son of the Hua family. In the Song Dynasty, there was a degree of freedom of speech, but regardless of the dynasty, such threats to imperial authority were forbidden. The crimes were clearly stated in the Song Code. “I’d heard Second Young Master Hua was a good-for-nothing philanderer, but that’s a misunderstanding.” An Jiu leaned forward slightly, elbows resting on her legs. “Turns out he’s a madman.” Yao-Ye sighed inwardly. Hua Rongjian’s words and actions were unrestrained and arrogant to the point of being lawless. He certainly seemed crazy, but he posed no real danger. Even if he said such things in front of the Mei family head, it would not matter. The Mei family was suspected by the Emperor; without concrete evidence, exposing Hua Rongjian would bring no benefit. “Given all this… you should think it over carefully. Do not join the Konghe Army. How about marrying me?” Hua Rongjian went around in circles before finally getting to the point. “Follow me, and I guarantee you a lifetime of wealth and honor.” Yao-Ye could not believe it. To utter such rebellious words for this was something no ordinary philanderer would do! It really was that guy. An Jiu had initially thought that even this guy she’d only met twice had changed his ways after she’d completed her trial! “Young Master Hua! Marriage is a major life event, a matter of parental consent and a matchmaker’s word!” Yao-Ye said coldly. “Will you leave on your own, or will I have someone invite you out?” Yao-Ye was flustered and worried, completely manipulated by his words. Even the most patient person would lose their temper, let alone Yao-Ye, who was known for her temper. Hua Rongjian glanced at her unhappily, then said earnestly to An Jiu, “If the young lady agrees, even such an ugly and irritable maidservant is tolerable to me.” With An Jiu’s sharp eyesight, she could clearly see through the crystal curtain that Hua Rongjian was quite handsome. Thinking of Mei Yanran’s wish, An Jiu said, “Alright, I will wait for you to come and propose.” Yao-Ye stared in disbelief. Things were starting to go downhill! “Since that’s the case, may I have a look at your face, my young lady?” Hua Rongjian explained. “Rumor has it that every woman in the Mei family is stunningly beautiful, but before I propose marriage, I must confirm it.” Yao-Ye was almost in despair. Her young lady would not listen to anything she said today, but out of a sense of responsibility, she still had to speak up and stop her. “My Young Lady! No!” “Why did you not state your demands before saying all this?” An Jiu said listlessly. “You only think about being picky after we’ve already agreed on the conditions? Too late, you fool! Let me tell you, since you are wasting my time, you have to find a way to marry me.” “Fool?!” Hua Rongjian’s forehead veins throbbed, and he raised his leg to rush inside. Yao-Ye’s mind was a mess, but she reacted quickly, grabbing him. However, Hua Rongjian’s strength was unexpected; he actually dragged Yao-Ye into the inner room along with him! The crystal curtains rattled loudly.

chapters.title: A Fight (2)
chapters.content: An Jiu slowly raised her eyes to look at him. Their eyes met, and Hua Rongjian froze. Her gaze, still cold yet subtly menacing, seemed somewhat out of place on her delicate, yet undeniably beautiful, face. The bamboo on the brocade screen rustled. She wore a light blue silk dress spread out on the couch, a white brocade jacket with a red plum blossom embroidered on the collar, her long neck and fair skin slightly exposed, her dark hair half-tied up, and her delicate face radiant. Hua Rongjian coughed lightly. “I… I am telling you, if you push me too far, I do not care about gender!” “Sure?” An Jiu’s lips curled into a smirk, the soft snort of laughter from her nose sharper than any harsh word. Hua Rongjian’s anger, which had just subsided, flared up again. He lunged forward, grabbed An Jiu by the collar, and lifted her. However, once the thought crossed his mind, he hesitated to strike. He’d done countless disgraceful things outside, but he’d never laid a hand on a woman. He had his reservations, but the person opposite him showed no mercy. A fist swung, landing a solid blow to his cheek. A man who hits a woman was shameless; a man who gets hit by a woman was a coward! Hua Rongjian was utterly enraged, forgetting why he’d come in. He grabbed An Jiu’s collar with one hand and pinned her right hand down with the other. An Jiu’s left hand held a dagger drawn, about to touch his ribs, when she suddenly stopped, gripping the hilt and striking heavily. Hua Rongjian grunted, releasing An Jiu’s collar and grabbing her other hand. “Young Lady!” Yao-Ye, holding a vase, wanted to help, but the two were locked in a fierce struggle on the couch, and she could not find a way to attack. She simply put down the vase and went to pull them apart. Hua Rongjian initially tried to restrain An Jiu on the defensive, but An Jiu, never one to be at a disadvantage, naturally struggled to break free! In this tug-of-war, neither side yielded an inch, yet both maintained a degree of composure. Neither side used their full strength. The moonlight outside was bright. Mo Sigui, considering the late hour, bought only a jug of wine, offered a simple libation to Qiu Ningyu by the river, and then returned to the tavern. He stepped into the lobby, sensing the strange atmosphere. He faintly heard a commotion on the second floor and grabbed a waiter. “What happened?” “It’s Second Young Master Hua getting into a fight! I heard it is a young woman inside! Oh, what a tragedy. I do not know how that young woman offended Second Young Master Hua.” The waiter, realizing he should not gossip, changed the subject with a smile. “Young master, do not worry. Encounters with disturbances are normal; it will not affect you.” Mo Sigui nodded. “Do you know which room Young Lady Mei is in?” “Young Lady Mei…” The waiter hesitated. Suddenly, his face showed surprise. “You are Master Mei?” “Yes.” Seeing his reaction, Mo Sigui had a bad feeling. “You’d better go see her quickly!” The waiter slapped his forehead. “She’s in the Emerald Bamboo private room. I completely forgot! That’s Young Lady Mei! I was just saying the woman who fought with Second Young Master Hua…” Before the waiter could finish, Mo Sigui, startled, rushed upstairs. Many people in the private rooms on the second floor, hesitant to approach due to the guards at the door and Hua Rongjian’s status, opened their doors and peered outside. The guards at the door, sweating profusely, clung to Mo Sigui like a lifeline. “My Lord, they’ve been fighting inside for a while, but My Young Lady will not let us in.” Since An Jiu had returned alive from the trials, these guards instinctively assumed she was skilled in martial arts. Even though Hua Rongjian was a man, he was still an ordinary person without internal energy and could not possibly gain the upper hand. They were worried their mistress might accidentally kill Hua’s son! Mo Sigui kicked open the door and strode inside. The room was a mess. Mo Sigui saw An Jiu pinning a man in a blue brocade robe against the wall, one leg against his abdomen, her right hand pressing down on his neck, and her left hand gripping the man’s hand. The man was not idle either; he had one hand around An Jiu’s neck while his other hand was wrestling with her. The two were still, their faces flushed with anger, while Yao-Ye was busy tying Hua Rongjian’s feet, having torn off cloth from a cushion on the couch. “Tsk tsk!” Mo Sigui strolled over, observing their disheveled state and slowly flicking his fan. “Truly an eye-opener.” A faint fragrance wafted with Mo Sigui’s fanning, and An Jiu, Hua Rongjian, and Yao-Ye gradually felt as if all their strength had been drained, collapsing to their knees. An Jiu had some resistance to this type of drug and was still able to move. Mo Sigui snapped his fan shut. “Lord Hua, forgive me.” His drug could render someone powerless without causing them to faint. Hua Rongjian asked, “Who are you?” “I am Fourteenth’s cousin,” Mo Sigui said. “I will give you the antidote. You can leave on your own. Today’s matter will be temporarily put on hold. Is that alright?” Hua Rongjian glanced at his torn clothes and readily agreed, “Alright.” Mo Sigui took out a handkerchief and waved it near his nose. After a moment, Hua Rongjian felt he could move again. He quickly glanced at An Jiu, whose face was dark with anger, bowed to Mo Sigui, and strode out. Hua Rongjian’s gang of lackies were already waiting outside. When they saw him emerge in disheveled clothes, they immediately started making a ruckus. One of them said, “I told you Rongjian could do it! Come on, a bet’s a bet; pay up!” “Did you place the bet for me?!” Hua Rongjian covered his bruised face. “I put in a lot of effort!” “Yes, yours is on my side…” The door opened a crack, and An Jiu heard the laughter coming from the corridor. Her face darkened even more. Mo Sigui turned and closed the window, tapping the table with his folding fan, and sneered, “Wow, the girl’s grown up; she’s really impressive!” For an experienced assassin to engage in such a low-level fight was truly shameful! An Jiu turned her face away, remaining silent. Mo Sigui looked around, picked up a seemingly intact stool, and sat down, leaning lazily against the table, curiously inquiring, “When did you and Second Young Master Hua start this feud?” He sighed inwardly; if her meridians had not been completely destroyed this time, An Jiu would not have needed to fight like this. “No enmity…” An Jiu hesitated, unable to recall why they had fought. “It’s Second Young Master Hua who’s gone too far, repeatedly harassing our lady!” Yao-Ye said indignantly. “No way?” Mo Sigui said. “Hua Rongjian is a dissolute philanderer. He keeps over a hundred courtesans at home and frequents brothels, yet he does not like having wives or concubines and therefore never touches respectable women.” Yao-Ye asked in surprise, “He said he wants to marry a wife; could it be true?”

chapters.title: Who Does Not Know Mo Sigui?
chapters.content: Mo Sigui was astonished. “Marry? You are not joking, are you? I’ve been away from Bianjing for years, and even Hua Rongjian wants to get married? Things have really changed!” Seeing An Jiu’s unpleasant expression, Yao-Ye did not dare say that her young lady had readily agreed! More than just changed, it was shocking! “A leopard cannot change its spots. There must be a conspiracy.” An Jiu thought that after her disappearance, it would be best to arrange a stable environment for Mei Jiu, but upon reflection, this Hua Rongjian was indeed a bit unreliable. There were many onlookers outside, and Mo Sigui felt it was not advisable to linger too long, so he told An Jiu to leave. Upon leaving the private room, they found the shopkeeper and accountant waiting at the door. “Young Master Mei, look at this loss…” The shopkeeper, with a forced smile, handed the account book to Mo Sigui. Before the money could even reach Mo Sigui, it was blocked by his folding fan. “Everyone in the restaurant saw it. It was Second Young Master Hua who bullied us, barging into our private room and smashing things. Is the manager afraid of offending powerful figures and specifically targeting us commoners? Are his father and brothers not supposed to be the most reasonable? Second Young Master Hua’s unreasonable behavior is entirely his father and brother’s fault for not teaching him properly; they should bear the responsibility.” The manager instantly broke out in a cold sweat. He knew that taking the debt to Prime Minister Hua or Hua Rongtian would immediately secure compensation, but those two would certainly not let Hua Rongjian off easily. If Hua Rongjian were to be disciplined at home, would he forgive him later? A rough calculation showed that the contents of this room were worth ten thousand taels of silver, but he was unwilling to accept it. “Young Master Mei, you cannot say that. You booked this private room, so naturally, we are asking you for compensation. What business is it of yours with Second Young Master Hua? After all, we did not even see who broke it, did we?” “Oh, alright then!” Mo Sigui made a move to take the bill. “Then we will not trouble the shopkeeper. I will take this bill and pay the money as promised. We will take this bill and ask His Majesty to ask the Hua family for the money.” The Mei family were imperial merchants; if they wanted to speak to the Emperor, it was not impossible. The shopkeeper’s hand trembled, and he quickly withdrew it. “This… how could we trouble His Majesty with such a small matter? I will go ask Second Young Master Hua myself.” His heart was bleeding. This money was probably going to be wasted. Second Young Master Hua was notoriously stingy; unless you were a beauty, you could not expect him to part with a single coin. With the matter resolved, Mo Sigui did not hesitate to offer kind words. “The shopkeeper is truly wise and understanding.” “Not at all.” The shopkeeper took out a handkerchief to wipe his sweat, but his expression had already regained its composure. He smiled and asked, “Young master, you are a man of great talent. May I ask your name?” Mo Sigui smiled faintly. “I am Mo Ran, courtesy name Sigui.” Mo Sigui nodded slightly in greeting and led An Jiu and the others away. The crowd watched their retreating figures, whispering amongst themselves: “His surname is Mo. He’s not the young master of the Mei family. The Mei family’s children all die young; I knew a young man of that age should be dead by now!” “Could it be another daughter about to marry out?” “Tch, ignorant. Years ago, a daughter of the Mei family married out, and his surname was Mo. That must be his offspring.” “Could it be Mo Dengxian, the Grand Instructor of the Imperial Medical Bureau?” “So it is the young Divine Physician Mo! The Mei family took him back supposedly to care for their orphaned children, but was the young Divine Physician Mo not doing just fine outside? If you ask me, it is better he had stayed outside. Going to Mei Mansion might have meant he’d be affected by the curse too.” “Exactly.” A collective sigh rippled through the crowd. An Jiu, with her keen hearing, said, “You are quite popular in Bianjing.” These words brought back memories for Mo Sigui. Back then, he was very young, the only surviving member of the Mo family, with only an old servant by his side. At first, he had to compete with beggars for a place to sleep in a dilapidated temple. The old servant was a close associate of Mo Dengxian and possessed some medical knowledge. Initially, he was able to earn money to support Mo Sigui, even managing to buy a remote, dilapidated thatched hut. However, his age made him increasingly frail. One harsh winter, he and Mo Sigui both caught a cold. Unable to gather herbs in the mountains and with limited medicine at home, he gave all his medicine to Mo Sigui, refusing to spend money on medicine for himself. Ultimately, he died of his illness. Mo Sigui was not yet ten years old that year. Born into a family of physicians, he had been immersed in medical training from a young age. A natural medical prodigy, he already knew the properties of thousands of herbs and possessed some medical knowledge and skills.
