Facing the madman head-on was tantamount to suicide. “We have to leave now,” Mo Sigui said. “It’s easy to get in, but hard to get out. The ambush has been going on for almost half an hour, and I’ve noticed their men are slowly gathering here. More and more are coming. We only have fewer than sixty people left. Try to stall them a bit and buy them time to escape.” This task was daunting. An Jiu asked Mei Jiu, “Are you going to run away or listen to him?” After asking, An Jiu felt she had made a fuss. Mei Jiu would definitely choose to stay; she could not tolerate so many lives being lost. Sure enough, Mei Jiu said, “In this situation, how can we just ignore it?” An Jiu had no attachment to the situation anyway. Since Mei Jiu chose to stay, she had no objections. “You said you could shoot a ‘Startling the String’?” An Jiu’s cold voice carried a hint of mockery. “But you still used an arrow. Is this what you call a ‘Startling the String’? Utterly laughable!” “If you do not believe me, I will show you!” The madman threw down the arrow and drew his bow empty-handed. Mo Sigui shrank back, trying to avoid being caught in the crossfire. An Jiu gently pushed open the broken window behind her with her bow, preparing to leap inside as soon as he released an arrow. There was a fire inside, and she could easily be burned, but it was better than being hit by the arrow. “Your spiritual power is scattered. If you can unleash a true ‘Startling the String’ with this attack, I will go out and be your target!” An Jiu knew that spiritual power was key to controlling the concentration of internal energy. She could not sense internal energy, but she was very sensitive to spiritual power. “Shut up!” the madman said irritably.

chapters.title: Farewell
chapters.content: An Jiu did indeed shut up, but her cold laugh drove the madman madder than any vicious word. The madman, enraged, loosened his bowstring, unleashing a torrent of internal energy. Having witnessed Elder Zhi’s unfocused, explosive bowstrings, An Jiu did not hesitate for a moment, leaping through the window into the house. Boom! The roof tiles were violently torn off, shattering into tiny fragments that rained down. Mo Sigui, standing below, was caught off guard and struck, his face covered in dust. Perhaps because the madman had been constantly firing arrows, his internal energy was somewhat depleted; this attack was weaker than An Jiu had anticipated. A dark figure landed beside the madman, pointing at Mo Sigui and shouting, “Shoot him!” The madman was used to acting without thinking, but he was not stupid. He noticed An Jiu cared about the boy, and upon hearing Cui Yichen’s words, he immediately realized their validity. He drew his bow empty-handed and aimed at Mo Sigui. An Jiu, peering through the broken window, saw the madman’s actions and her heart skipped a beat. “An Jiu, save my cousin!” In Mei Jiu’s heart, An Jiu was a ghost, and ghosts were more powerful than humans. An Jiu seemed not to hear her words, her mind still racing, yet she had already rushed out. Out of the corner of her eye, An Jiu saw the madman’s bow fully drawn, sensing he was about to release an arrow, and without a second thought, she leaped forward! The madman, still hoping to test his martial arts skills against An Jiu, did not intend to kill her yet. Seeing An Jiu’s movement, he shifted his position slightly. His finger loosened. A clear crane’s cry rang out, a burst of blue light erupted, and a powerful gust of wind cleaved through the flames, seemingly carrying a world-destroying force as it hurtled towards Mo Sigui. An Jiu lunged at Mo Sigui, the arrow grazing her back. She felt a sharp pain, her chest churning, and a metallic, sweet liquid gushing from her throat. The Madman’s arrow, not yet fully focused or practiced, carried immense force, even causing Mo Sigui to cough up blood. The arrow pierced through two black-clad men, disappearing into the banquet hall behind them. A moment of silence followed, then a deafening roar as the entire grand hall collapsed, the ground trembling as if an earthquake had struck. Everyone was stunned by this sight, almost forgetting the battle. The Madman, feeling incredibly powerful, was overjoyed. “Ha! Hahaha!” Cui Yichen had planned this all along, and having suffered a great loss at Chu Dingjiang’s hands because of An Jiu, he would not let this golden opportunity slip by! Taking advantage of the Madman’s elation, he flicked his wrist and launched a poisoned hidden weapon. An Jiu, severely shaken, struggled to concentrate, only sensing the approaching weapon but unable to move. Mei Jiu, hiding behind An Jiu’s mental energy, was also affected, but her situation was relatively better. Through An Jiu’s spiritual power, she truly sensed the approaching danger, but An Jiu was unconscious. She steeled her resolve and took control of her body. Just like in the past decade or so, so naturally, her sudden burst of spiritual power was more than ten times stronger than usual, but unfortunately, her severely injured body could not move freely. Mei Jiu gritted her teeth and crawled forward a few inches. Suddenly, she felt a chill on her back; something had pierced her. An Jiu had taken the brunt of the excruciating pain, leaving only numbness; Mei Jiu did not even feel the pain. Only her consciousness was slowly fading. Mei Jiu had a clear feeling that she was going to die. On the rooftop, the madman noticed Cui Yichen’s subtle movements, his initial elation turning to rage. He grabbed Cui Yichen by the collar. “How could you kill her?!” “She’s not dead!” Cui Yichen lied. “I was afraid she’d run away again, so I knocked her unconscious first!” “Is that so?” The madman released his grip, half-believing. …Mei Jiu collapsed onto the snow, her cheek pressed against the cold ground, fear gripping her heart. “An Jiu, An Jiu… I… I do not want to die…” Even in the perilous Mei family, even knowing she could not adapt to this life of slaughter, even in her cowardice, she had never considered giving up her life so easily. An Jiu’s spiritual power slowly gathered. “Idiot! Who told you to be such a hero! Do you not know that whoever controls the body will be injured!” Mei Jiu knew, but at the time, she did not know what she was thinking; she just did it. She felt An Jiu about to take over her body and quickly said, “No! We will both die… I beg you to do one thing for me; you cannot die.” “Speak.” An Jiu had witnessed countless deaths; she thought she was already numb, but now a strange sadness began to well up inside her. “An Jiu…” Mei Jiu’s voice was weak. “Leave the Mei family, find a village to settle down in, raise a flock of sheep, plant a few acres of grapes, and then… marry… marry… a… good family.” An Jiu was stunned. She thought Mei Jiu would say, “An Jiu, join the Konghe Army and help me rescue my mother,” but this idiot actually told her to live? “Bullshit! Do those things yourself!” An Jiu grabbed control of her body without a word. “When you used to curse me like that, it hurt me,” Mei Jiu’s voice was tinged with laughter, “but now it makes me happy.” An Jiu glanced at the still delirious Mo Sigui and forced herself to sit up. “Nonsense! I have no interest in playing the tragic card with you. Hold on, Elder Qi is over there!” “I do not want to die, but I know in my heart that without you, I would have died long ago. A coward like me cannot live like this…” Mei Jiu’s rambling voice grew weaker and weaker until it disappeared. An Jiu froze. She could not describe the feeling, but she knew Mei Jiu was truly gone. She was dead, in this chaotic night, unknown to anyone, not even leaving a body. In the initial physical struggle with Mei Jiu, An Jiu had been filled with unwavering confidence, but later lost the will to live. From beginning to end, she was the one in control. An Jiu had never considered defeat, much less anticipated this outcome. It seemed the hidden weapon was at work; An Jiu suddenly felt a tearing pain in her heart. She clutched her chest, stunned, her body losing its mental support, and collapsed. Mo Sigui regained consciousness and saw An Jiu fall. Suddenly remembering the moment An Jiu had rushed towards him, his heart clenched. “An Jiu!” All of this happened in an instant. Realizing Fourteenth Young Lady was dead, the madman turned to confront Cui Yichen, yelling, “Did you not say you knocked her out?! How did she die?!” “I misjudged!” Cui Yichen said. “Do not worry, grab Elder Qi! He can bring the dead back to life!” The madman’s anger turned to delight. He released Cui Yichen, patting him on the shoulder. “That’s right! Haha, Little Chen, you are so clever!” He turned and headed towards Elder Qi. Mo Sigui overheard their conversation, his heart filled with shock and anger. This was clearly a trap. Cui Yichen knew the madman valued An Jiu, so he attacked her first, then tricked the madman into capturing Elder Qi alive!

chapters.title: A Choice
chapters.content: “An Jiu,” Mo Sigui helped An Jiu up, fed her a pill of an antidote, then used acupressure to stop the bleeding. He anxiously looked up to see the battle situation on Elder Qi’s side. Mo Sigui’s internal organs were injured, and he did not have the strength to carry An Jiu. “Give her to me.” Cui Yichen appeared before them unnoticed. Thinking of An Jiu’s selfless rescue, Mo Sigui would rather die than hand her over. But he could not fight him head-on, so he had to buy time to think of a solution. “You have a grudge against her?” “Yes.” Cui Yichen had always been the pride of his family and rarely suffered setbacks. Last time, he had fallen into Chu Dingjiang’s trap because of kidnapping An Jiu, suffering heavy losses, and being severely punished by his master. He was always vengeful and would seek revenge on Chu Dingjiang sooner or later; An Jiu was just an afterthought. Mo Sigui never imagined that Cui Yichen would want to kill An Jiu over such a trivial matter. Cui Yichen glanced around. “If you delay any longer, the Mei family will be finished.” Mo Sigui and An Jiu were to the north, upwind. The wind was not strong, but it was enough to deliver a little poison! He discreetly uncorked a bottle with the hand supporting An Jiu, speaking to distract Cui Yichen. “When a person dies, the light goes out. She’s so young; what irreconcilable hatred could you possibly have to want to torture a corpse?” “Mo Sigui.” Cui Yichen recognized him and suddenly smiled. “You should worry about yourself.” Cui Yichen waved his hand lightly, and a dozen black-clad men surrounded him. He said calmly, “Take him alive.” If they could not protect Elder Qi, capturing Mo Sigui would be just as good. In fact, the Lord might be even happier. After all, according to the information obtained earlier, Elder Qi’s passion for medicine had waned in recent years, and he was quite sentimental. The Lord had tried several times to capture his son, who had joined the Konghe Army, but had failed. Someone like Mo Sigui should be easier to control. A refreshing fragrance of plum blossoms slowly filled the air. Those black-clad men, those with lower martial arts levels, began to feel weak all over. Their swords clattered to the ground. Cui Yichen also sensed something amiss. Where did the plum blossom fragrance come from amidst the blood and flames? He stepped back a short distance, raising his hand to cover his mouth and nose. The madman’s voice came from not far away: “Old man! Surrender obediently, and I will not hurt you!” Mo Sigui quickly glanced, a sharp pain shooting through his heart—Elder Qi was badly injured, almost soaked in blood, his white beard turned red, and his face was deathly pale. “I know you want to capture Elder Qi.” Mo Sigui’s eyes always seemed to carry a hint of flirtatiousness. “I will go with you. My medical skills are now no less than his, on the condition that Elder Qi leaves with her body.” “Your suggestion is good, but unfortunately, your behavior is not very friendly.” Cui Yichen glanced at the black-clad men who were falling one after another around him. Mo Sigui slightly raised his hand, and Cui Yichen immediately took a few steps back. Upon closer inspection, he realized it was just a porcelain bottle that had rolled to his feet. Mo Sigui’s lips curled into a smile, seemingly lazy yet mocking. “The antidote. Dare to try?” “Why would I not?” Cui Yichen raised an eyebrow. He bent down, picked up the antidote, and tossed it to one of the poisoned individuals. The person secretly thought, “Of course I dare! It is not me who’s poisoned!” Though he thought this, his actions were without hesitation. He took the antidote, pulled up his mask, poured out a pill, and swallowed it. Before he could observe the effects, a cold light flashed. The surrounding poisoned individuals offered no resistance. Master Mo easily broke through the encirclement and picked up Mo Sigui. “Take her with you.” Mo Sigui held An Jiu tightly. Master Mo glanced down at the curtain and scooped An Jiu up in one swift motion. “Sound Killer!” Cui Yichen was extremely wary of this intruder. He only dared to verbally advise, “You have no connection with the Mei family, why meddle in their business?” How could there be no connection? When no other place dared to take him in, the Mei family did, and he no longer needed to risk his life on missions or live a life of hiding. “An army is raised for a thousand days, used for one.” If not now, when? Headmaster Zhao and the others might be ruthless killers, but they all had a bottom line: “loyalty and righteousness.” If it were not for this virtue, the Mei family would not have gone to such lengths to recruit a few unrelated people. “A good dog does not block the way.” Master Mo turned his head, coldly glancing at Cui Yichen. Meeting the anger in his eyes, he said sarcastically, “Do not force me to act.” Cui Yichen gripped his sword hilt tightly, his teeth almost grinding to powder, but ultimately dared not make a move. “Sound Killer” was renowned for his prowess. Even as a novice with only sixth-tier strength, he could kill an eighth-tier expert. Later, he repeatedly took on all sorts of unbelievable jobs; Cui Yichen was no match for him, not even worth a flick of his sword. “My Lord,” Mei Ruyan rushed over. Master Mo handed An Jiu to her and then summoned a member of the Mei Clan’s shadow. “The enemy’s numbers are increasing. I will fight my way out of Mei Mansion. Take the Mei Clan’s token and enter Bianjing tonight.” The Mei Clan, serving the royal family, naturally enjoyed certain privileges. As founding heroes with a mission to protect the Emperor, during the reign of the founding Emperor, the Mei Clan, with their tokens, had the authority to bring a thousand troops into the city at any time. Later emperors felt this power was too great and considered revoking it, which provoked protests from various powerful Konghe families. After three Emperors, the matter was finally resolved. To appease the various families, this privilege was retained, but limited to a maximum of ten people. “Elder Qi has given me the token!” Mei Ruyan said. Mo Sigui stopped. An Jiu was on the verge of death and needed his help, while Elder Qi was being besieged and seemed on the verge of collapse… His mentor and his savior—how could he choose? Seeing Mo Sigui’s hesitation, Elder Qi roared, “Get lost!” Mo Sigui’s eyes welled up with tears, blurring his vision. He closed his eyes, turned, and followed Mei Ruyan away. After a few steps, he stopped again. “Fifteenth, take Fourteenth away first. I will catch up shortly!” Mei Ruyan nodded. “Alright.” Mo Sigui removed all the Jade Tears on Clothes that he was keeping, turned, and ran back. Elder Qi treated him like a son; he could not bear to watch his mentor and father figure be left alone in dire straits. Mo Sigui silently vowed, “I will do everything in my power to survive and save you, but, Fourteenth Young Lady Mei, I am sorry; I cannot choose you at this moment!” The siege had lasted nearly an hour, and the enemy’s numbers continued to grow. These men charged relentlessly, seemingly endless, until Master Mo’s plain white robes were finally stained with blood, like blooming red plum blossoms in the snow. They charged all the way to a small canyon at the exit of Mei Mansion. Seeing the increasing number of pursuers behind them, Master Mo said, “I will hold them off. You go first.” Dozens of pursuers remained, each a one-against-one threat, a near-certain death. “I will not go!” Mei Ruyan grabbed his sleeve, her gaze resolute. “We will die together!” “Live.” Master Mo turned his face away, slashing his sleeve with his sword. “If I live, we can meet again. If I die, avenge me.” Was this an acknowledgment of their feelings? Tears welled up in Mei Ruyan’s eyes. She reached out and hugged him. “Alright.”

chapters.title: Highway Robbery
chapters.content: “Go!” Master Mo used his inner strength to propel the two of them two zhang away. Mei Ruyan glanced back. Master Mo, covered in blood, stood like a monument at the narrow valley entrance, sword in hand, facing dozens of black-clad men. The sharp sword light guarded the exit impenetrably, creating an aura of one man holding off ten thousand! Mei Ruyan felt both proud and heartbroken. “From the highest heavens to the deepest hell, if you do not come looking for me, I will come looking for you!” She mobilized all her inner strength, carrying An Jiu on her back, and ran wildly. “Fifteenth Young Lady Mei!” Someone chased after her. Mei Ruyan recognized the voice, but she dared not stop. “Who is it?” “Ling-Xi,” the person announced. When Mei Zhengjing confronted the First Old Madam with his sword, Mei Ruyan had already fainted and was unaware of their betrayal. Mei Yanran had repeatedly warned her not to get close to the First Old Madam before leaving, but these were extraordinary times, and she could not worry about that now. Her only thought was to entrust An Jiu to someone else’s care before returning to find Master Mo. Mei Ruyan stopped. Ling-Xi, looking disheveled, said, “Come with me.” “Where to?” Mei Ruyan hesitated. “To see someone who can save us.” Ling-Xi felt slightly relieved that there were no pursuers for the time being. “The First Old Madam is seriously injured. I need someone to help. I will guarantee your life and a life of wealth and honor for the rest of your days.” Mei Ruyan, quick-witted, immediately understood Ling-Xi’s meaning. She was with an unconscious person; if she chose to help, she would have to abandon An Jiu. Seeing that Ling-Xi was preoccupied with her own problems and that entrusting An Jiu to her was impossible, she said, “Nanny Ling-Xi, the pursuers are close behind. It is best to leave quickly!” She immediately continued walking. Ling-Xi was stunned. She had been monitoring Mei Ruyan throughout her time in the Mei family. She knew Mei Ruyan very well and what kind of person she was, and she never expected to be refused! “Fifteenth Young Lady Mei! If you agree, once reinforcements arrive, we might be able to save Master Mo’s life!” Ling-Xi’s voice came from afar. Mei Ruyan abruptly stopped. “We are the Emperor’s spies planted in the Mei family. Reinforcements will arrive in no time. You just need to help me get through this moment, and I promise to send someone to rescue Master Mo.” Ling-Xi was certain that she would not refuse this time. Mei Ruyan paused for a few moments, then said coldly, “We cannot afford such wealth. Do not follow me anymore. No matter what you say, I will not agree! Nanny Ling-Xi, do not waste time; escaping is the priority.” She was not unmoved, but then she thought, if she got involved in this mess, she’d be controlled by the Mei family, her life and death in someone else’s hands, just like Master Mo was at Piaomiao Mansion. If Master Mo enjoyed this life of constant danger, he would not have hidden his elegance and secluded himself as a tutor at the Mei family’s school. She did not want to do what he disliked. Besides, Ling-Xi was just a maid. How high could her status be in the Konghe Army? Did she really believe whatever Ling-Xi said? No one would believe that! Mei Ruyan did not want to get entangled with Ling-Xi any longer. After adjusting her breathing, she quickly left. Ling-Xi was asking for help, and Mei Ruyan refused even at the cost of her life, so there was nothing she could do. Now she did not even have time to kill someone to vent her anger. Mei Ruyan started practicing martial arts late, and even with her exceptional diligence, she was only at the third level. She had run for less than half an hour carrying An Jiu before her inner strength was completely exhausted. She saw a patch of waist-high grass by the roadside, went over, and put An Jiu down. An Jiu lay beside her, panting heavily. Puffs of smoke escaped from her mouth and nose, then dissipated. The night was deep, the wilderness silent. Mei Ruyan sighed. “After all this time, it is you and me running away together again. Mei Jiu, I wonder if I owed you something in my past life or if you owed me something!” Unlike last time, Mei Ruyan genuinely wanted to save her this time. Mei Ruyan was a selfish and calculating person, but she also had a strong sense of gratitude and resentment. Mei Jiu, with her honest heart, was truly good to her. Besides, if she had not been taken in by the Mei family, she would not have met Master Mo. In a way, Mei Jiu had done her a favor. After resting briefly in the grass, Mei Ruyan stood up, looked around at the vast wilderness, and her nose tingled and her eyes suddenly blurred. Master Mo was a man who never showed any tenderness or compassion, yet being by his side brought a sense of security. Having grown accustomed to that feeling, now alone, Mei Ruyan felt utterly helpless. Mei Ruyan raised her hand and fiercely wiped her face, her cheeks burning from the silk. She told herself, “You are Ah Shun; you grew up in a lowly place like a brothel. How did you become a delicate woman?” Mei Ruyan used to hate this past, but now she was grateful for it. In the brothel, she learned the wickedness of human nature early on and learned how to navigate social situations, which allowed her to survive to this day. A gust of wind rustled through the dry, frosty grass. Mei Ruyan felt a chill run down her spine. She stiffened, then slowly turned her head. A figure cloaked in black stood silently in the grass. The withered grass swayed in the wind, but he remained motionless, like a statue, not even a wisp of his clothing fluttering. “Fourteenth Young Lady?” His deep voice came from beneath the cloak. Without even revealing his face, his imposing, dignified presence was enough to send chills down one’s spine. “Who are you?” Mei Ruyan heard her own voice tremble slightly. The man moved swiftly. Mei Ruyan did not see his movements clearly; she only saw a blur before An Jiu was in his arms. “Stop!” Seeing him turn to leave, Mei Ruyan quickly chased after him. “Are you friend or foe? Why did you take my sister away?” “Friend, not foe,” He calmly stated his name, “Chu Dingjiang.” The grass rustled, and Chu Dingjiang leaped up like a predatory eagle, disappearing into the night in a few bounds. Mei Ruyan frowned. Regardless of whether Chu Dingjiang’s words were true or false, she was powerless to resist. She had done her best to the utmost. Freed from her burdens, Mei Ruyan sat cross-legged and began to focus intently on regulating her inner energy. Half an hour later, she set off back to Mei Mansion. A few snowflakes drifted in the north wind, pattering softly against the withered grass. Mei Mansion had become a sea of ​​fire; the ambush had finally come to an end. In the cellar beneath the medicine hut, Mo Sigui clutched the bloody hole in Elder Qi’s chest with one hand, while the other frantically searched through his medicine chest. “Sigui, listen quietly to me for a few minutes,” Elder Qi said. A warm trickle of fluid seeped from between Mo Sigui’s fingers as he stubbornly searched for a hemostatic agent. “You brat! You want me to die with my eyes wide open in disbelief!” Elder Qi’s anger caused the blood in his wound to gush even more fiercely. Mo Sigui was also furious. “Speak your mind! I am listening! Do not delay me!” After his outburst, he slumped down and listened obediently to Elder Qi. “Beneath the outhouse at the northernmost part of the medicine furnace lies a medicine jar, containing twenty scrolls of books—my life’s work,” Elder Qi said, coughing twice. “I was preparing for today.” Mo Sigui’s forehead veins throbbed. “Could you not have hidden it somewhere else?” “Sigui…” Elder Qi looked at him, his cloudy eyes unfocused. “Your understanding of medicine far surpasses mine. Given time, you will surely become a legendary physician. I have nothing to say, only a word of advice: do not be too obsessed, and do not betray the word ‘love.'” Family, love, friendship—Elder Qi had missed too much. He did not want Mo Sigui to repeat his mistakes. “I’ve remembered,” Mo Sigui agreed, his mind preoccupied with the thought of abandoning An Jiu. “Hmm.” Elder Qi sighed deeply and closed his eyes. Mo Sigui’s tears fell uncontrollably. Elder Qi suddenly opened his eyes again, saying with concern, “Swear an oath.” “You, you…” Mo Sigui was startled, but seeing the expectation on his face, he did not waste any words and obediently clasped his hands. “I, Mo Ran, swear to heaven that I will never betray love or be unfaithful again. If I break this oath, may I die a horrible death!” Elder Qi’s mouth opened slightly, as if he wanted to say something, but his breathing stopped, and his pupils became unfocused. Mo Sigui reached out and covered his eyes, then found a clean cloth and silently wiped the bloodstains from his face. He was already overwhelmed with grief, but Elder Qi’s words had startled him, and now he could not describe his feelings. After everything was tidied up, Mo Sigui knelt beside Elder Qi, remained silent for a long time, and murmured in a hoarse voice, “Elder, I have done a small act of kindness.” Mo Sigui used the dagger he carried to dig a pit, buried Elder Qi, kowtowed nine times, picked up his medicine box, got up, and hurriedly left the cellar.

chapters.title: Chaos
chapters.content: All the attackers had retreated from Mei Mansion. The fire was still burning, and the air was thick with acrid smoke. The houses were ruined. Mo Sigui made his way to the stables, only to find the ground littered with horse carcasses. He had no choice but to pursue them on foot. Reaching the valley entrance, in the dim light of night, Mo Sigui saw a large fire burning at the entrance and a pile of black things blocking the road. He cautiously approached through the withered bushes, and only when he was about ten paces away did he realize it was a pile of corpses. Directly opposite the pile of corpses stood a tall figure leaning on a sword. His black hair was disheveled, and his clothes were soaked in blood, their original color unrecognizable. The flames were about to engulf his figure. “Master Mo!” Mo Sigui recognized his sword and rushed into the fire without hesitation. There was no response. Mo Sigui grasped his pulse, his fingers touching warm skin, but there was no pulse. With the fire around, the temperature was naturally very high. He might have just died, or he might have been dead for a long time! Mo Sigui’s heart sank. He let go and began frantically searching through the pile of corpses. An Jiu was traveling with Master Mo! He had to find her alive or dead. “Fourteenth Young Lady! Mei Jiu! An Jiu!” Mo Sigui muttered incoherently, then paused, suddenly remembering that he had placed a tracking incense on An Jiu when they parted. He reached for the small gourd hanging from his waist and released a dozen butterflies. This was a common tracking method in the martial arts world. The butterflies used were fed a poisonous incense, allowing them to survive the winter and fly purposefully. However, they were relatively slow, with an effective tracking range of only ten li. The butterflies circled the valley entrance once; eight or nine were burned to ashes, while the rest began to fly away. Mo Sigui was overjoyed and, clutching his medicine box, followed. After a few steps, he turned back and bowed to Master Mo. “I am sorry!” Mo Sigui only had a deep bond with Elder Qi at Mei Mansion, so even though he was worried about An Jiu, he would only leave after burying him properly, but for him, finding An Jiu was more important right now, as she might still be alive. He bowed and hurriedly chased after the butterfly. After walking for about a quarter of an hour, a person approached from the road, and the butterfly stopped flying. Mo Sigui recognized it as Mei Ruyan and rushed forward. Both of them felt a pang of sadness upon seeing each other. “Where’s Fourteen?” “Have you seen Master Mo?” The butterfly fluttered around Mei Ruyan, who was grabbing Mo Sigui and pressing him for answers. “Did you see Master Mo when you came out of the valley?” “Yes.” Mo Sigui paused, then said softly, “He’s dead.” “You…you say it again?” Mei Ruyan asked, tears streaming down her face. “Take it easy. His body is still at the valley entrance. If you hurry, you can see him one last time.” Seeing this, Mo Sigui thought it was a sign of their deep teacher-student bond, but now he could only offer a few perfunctory words of comfort. Mo Sigui was deeply concerned for An Jiu’s safety. He could not help but ask, “Where’s Fourteenth Young Lady?” “She was taken away by Chu Dingjiang,” Mei Ruyan said, staggering towards the plum blossoms. The butterfly followed her for about two zhang before returning. “Who is Chu Dingjiang? Where did he go?” Mo Sigui called out. Mei Ruyan ignored Mo Sigui, who could only watch her retreating figure. After a moment’s hesitation, he followed the butterfly. Although he had not used the tracking butterfly many times, he did not doubt his abilities. In the vast wilderness, several butterflies, scarred by the fire, fluttered and fell in the wind. Mo Sigui pressed on tirelessly, oblivious to the scabbing and reopening of his wounds, his only concern fixed on the last butterfly. The sky was beginning to lighten, as if stained with blood, a faint red hue. On a hillside, a house stood, a lamp in the corner still casting a faint glow. The entire house consisted of only three stone rooms and a dilapidated fence enclosing a courtyard. In the northeast corner stood a simple shed with a stove made of rubble and mud underneath. A man in tight-fitting clothes squatted before the stove, idly poking at the firewood in the firebox. Wisps of white steam rose from the pot, filling the air with the aroma of rice. When he felt the rice was almost cooked, he extinguished the fire and went inside. Without lighting a lamp, in the dim light, he walked precisely to the bedside and stood there with his arms crossed, seemingly lost in thought while gazing at the woman lying on the bed. He only stirred when there was a barely audible noise outside. “Commander, you need medicine,” someone said from outside the door. “Put it down,” the voice was hoarse. “Yes!” The man put down his bundle and continued, “Commander, you should hurry back. I’ve heard from the Council of the Konghe Army that someone has proposed punishing you, and even the Privy Council has intervened.” The man inside the room had eyes shrouded in darkness, unfathomable. “I understand. I have my own plans. Tell the brothers that as long as their loyalty to Chu remains unchanged, they should prioritize self-preservation. True loyalty lies in the heart, not in outward appearances.” The man who received the order understood. Chu Dingjiang was reminding them not to be stubborn; they must yield when necessary. “Yes! Take care, Commander.” The man lingered in the corridor for a moment, making sure Chu Dingjiang had no further instructions before leaving. Chu Dingjiang sat down on the edge of the bed, reaching under the covers to touch a slender wrist, his fingers gently resting on it. The pulse was weak; he could not feel a heartbeat, nor could he sense any meridians, as if the body was in a state of chaos. Chu Dingjiang was puzzled. She had only been injured and poisoned, so why was this happening? He remembered experiencing the same thing when he broke through to the ninth-tier, the Transcendent Realm. If one could endure it, life would emerge from the chaos, allowing one to reach another level. For most ninth-tier martial artists, this opportunity only came once in a lifetime. A failed first breakthrough would create even greater obstacles for the next. The human heart was strongest when it returned to its true nature, unshakable by anything external, yet also most fragile, tolerating no impurities. If there were inherent flaws, they were extremely difficult to remove in the chaos. At least, he had never heard of anyone successfully breaking through under these circumstances. Chu Dingjiang channeled his internal energy into An Jiu’s body, confirming that her internal energy was almost negligible, unless… her spiritual power was about to break through! Considering this possibility, Chu Dingjiang quietly withdrew, ate a quick meal, and went to practice in the woods next to the house. Day after day passed. An Jiu felt as if she had walked for an unknown amount of time in the darkness, her body utterly exhausted, as if filled with lead, each step leaving her drenched in sweat. Just as she was about to stop and rest, she suddenly heard a deep, mellow male voice say, “Why not just throw the person into the pond to drown?” An Jiu instinctively felt he was talking about her, and in her anger, a faint red light suddenly appeared before her eyes.

chapters.title: Dare to Offer Yourself in Return?
chapters.content: An Jiu opened her eyes. The light was a bit blinding, so she closed them to adjust. “Awake?” Chu Dingjiang was somewhat surprised. An Jiu turned her stiff neck and saw a black-clad man in close-fitting clothes sitting opposite her with an imposing presence. His back was straight, and his form-fitting clothes outlined his figure, vaguely revealing muscles brimming with immense power, like a leopard poised to pounce. “Chu Dingjiang?” An Jiu stared at the half-mask on his face. “Not bad eyesight.” He stood up and reached out to take her pulse. The warm fingers on An Jiu’s wrist felt like they were burning, and she involuntarily flinched, but Chu Dingjiang held her firmly. The pulse was normal, but there was no change in her internal energy, so he was certain that the previous signs of a breakthrough were a breakthrough in mental power, something that could not be detected by pulse diagnosis. “You were unconscious for half a month.” Chu Dingjiang released his grip. “You are finally better now.” “Did you save me?” An Jiu asked. “Thank you.” Chu Dingjiang said calmly, “I dare not take credit. It is all thanks to someone who treated your wounds beforehand and gave you the antidote; otherwise, even a celestial being could not have saved you.” An Jiu’s memory of the incident was somewhat fragmented, but she remembered that only Mo Sigui was by her side. The only person who could do such a thing for her was him. Thinking of this, An Jiu looked up at the man before her. “You saved me; how do you want me to repay you?” A smile appeared in Chu Dingjiang’s eyes. “How about repaying me with your body?” “I did not expect you to be so flirtatious beneath your seemingly serious exterior,” An Jiu said. “I am not joking.” Chu Dingjiang’s gaze shifted to her chest. “When I retrieved the hidden weapon in you, I saw your body. From this day forward, you are my wife. As for the wedding, I am serving in the Konghe Army and cannot give you a grand dowry. Only a pair of red candles and a wedding quilt are offered; I apologize for the inconvenience.” As a member of the Konghe Army, taking a wife without permission was a great risk for Chu Dingjiang; this was the limit of what he could offer. “Are you repaying a debt of gratitude?” An Jiu asked calmly. Chu Dingjiang frowned. “What are you talking about? I am simply doing what a true man should do!” “Then I will repay this debt in another way. You do not mind, do you?” An Jiu thought carefully and, considering her debt to Chu Dingjiang, added, “Although my views on sex are not very conservative, I am not inclined towards promiscuity, and you do not need to take responsibility for that.” Chu Dingjiang froze, his face suddenly flushing red. He awkwardly coughed a few times and looked away to compose himself. Having weathered countless storms and bloodshed, he was a man of experience and quickly regained his composure, calmly changing the subject. “There’s porridge. Want some?” “Yes,” An Jiu answered succinctly. Chu Dingjiang went out and soon returned with a bowl of plain porridge. He sat down by the bed and spooned the porridge to An Jiu’s lips. His movements were clumsy. He did not even help An Jiu sit up; it was clear he had never cared for anyone before, and An Jiu simply ate it from the spoon. For both of them, feeding and being fed were memories buried deep within their being. Although it seemed somewhat incongruous, a strange emotion flowed between them. After An Jiu finished the bowl of porridge, Chu Dingjiang said, “Want to go outside and sit?” An ordinary person would have found this strange—why go outside in the middle of the night when there was no sun? But strangely, An Jiu readily agreed to the suggestion. After half a month, An Jiu’s external wounds had healed, and she could move around a little without difficulty. An Jiu sat on the veranda, draped in a cloak, her hands gathered over her chest, squinting at the distant mountains in the night. Chu Dingjiang leaned against a pillar, arms crossed, his eyes fixed on the whorl of hair on An Jiu’s head. He sat quietly until the moon set. Chu Dingjiang said, “Let’s go back inside.” An Jiu did not move. “If someone told you before they died to live well, would you choose to follow their dying wish or avenge them?” Chu Dingjiang had not known An Jiu much, but he could see her coldness inside and out. He had not expected her to value someone so much. An Jiu looked up into his dark eyes. Chu Dingjiang paused for a moment, then said, “Life is full of meetings and partings, no longer than a hundred years and shorter than a moment. Just let things take their course.” An Jiu nodded in agreement. “Is the Commander of the Konghe Army very free?” Otherwise, why would Chu Dingjiang have been here taking care of her for half a month? “Of course not.” Chu Dingjiang smiled. “But I was demoted a long time ago.” An Jiu raised an eyebrow. This was an inquiry. It concerned the secrets of the Konghe Army, something Chu Dingjiang should not have told her, but he did not hide it. “So many people are trying to oust me. Recent events have caused heavy losses for the Konghe Army, giving them a convenient excuse.” He did not try to seize power now to avoid an unfavorable opportunity. “Was the Emperor the one who attacked the Lou and Mei families?” An Jiu did not know if she’d get an answer, but she asked anyway, curious about the ruthless mastermind behind it all. “If the Emperor wanted to act, he would not choose such drastic methods. Although the current Emperor is quite calculating, he seeks immortality and would not act too cruelly,” Chu Dingjiang said. “Currently, all the clues point to Yelu Huangwu of Liao, and I believe it is undoubtedly her.” An Jiu looked at him quietly. “What’s your mentality in telling me everything?” If he considered her one of his own just because he saw her body, that was absurd! There might be many such people in this era, but An Jiu’s intuition told her Chu Dingjiang was not. “It’s a long story.” Chu Dingjiang examined An Jiu and found her meridians completely destroyed. He initially thought it was because he had forcibly widened them, forcing her to use the Startling the String technique. Of course, her physical condition also played a role. There were many other subtle reasons, such as An Jiu’s personality being a good listener for him. As a master of the Transcendent Realm, he rarely found someone with comparable mental strength, let alone someone like An Jiu who only possessed mental strength but no internal energy. He could easily silence her like crushing an ant. An Jiu could not fathom his many complex thoughts. She judged that Chu Dingjiang meant no harm, so she did not press him further. “One last question,” the question An Jiu most wanted to know, “why did you save me?” A breeze stirred, the lamplight flickered, and light danced across their faces. After a few moments of silence, Chu Dingjiang spoke, “I did not know your meridians were destroyed beforehand.” “You should have thrown me into the pond and drowned me long ago.” Chu Dingjiang laughed, “Holding grudges and forgetting kindness is not a good habit; you have to change it.” … The sun rose slowly, the ice and snow melted, and all things revived. In a secluded tavern seventy miles outside Bianjing, a young man in a wide, earth-yellow robe sat by the window. On the table lay a silk handkerchief, upon which lay a butterfly with tattered wings. The table was laden with food and wine, yet it remained untouched. “Elder, my heart is tormented,” he murmured. The butterfly died three days after emerging from the plum blossoms. Mo Sigui had searched the entire area within a seventy-mile radius, but found no trace of her.

chapters.title: Ning in the North, Mo in the South
chapters.content: His heart ached, yet a sliver of hope remained. When Fourteenth Young Lady was struck by a hidden weapon, he had sealed her acupoints and administered the antidote. If Chu Dingjiang were skilled in healing, she likely would not have died. But did Chu Dingjiang actually know how to heal? Damn it! Who thought of using something as fragile as a butterfly to find someone! Smash! Mo Sigui slammed his fan on the table, shattering the remaining butterfly into dust. Mo Sigui gritted his teeth and vowed that he would find a way to use tigers and wolves as guides for tracking incense in the future! The guests in the hall all looked over, and the innkeeper timidly approached, “This, sir…” Mo Sigui prepared to pay, then felt in his sleeve, only to remember that the little silver he had left had been used to buy a piece of clothing and stay at an inn for the night; now he only had a few coins left… “This will cover the meal.” Mo Sigui tossed the folding fan to the innkeeper. The innkeeper was unaware of the fan’s true value, but the tassel—a round, jade seed the size of a quail egg—was incredibly valuable, enough to buy ten of his shops. “Take care, My Lord!” the innkeeper said, tucking the fan into his robes and seeing him off with great courtesy. As he reached the door, he brushed past a man and a woman. The man was tall and burly, with a dark complexion; the woman was slender with wheat-colored skin. Their appearance was quite different from that of the people around Bianjing. Even more striking was the menacing aura emanating from them. Their presence at the doorway instantly silenced the shop. “Who is the innkeeper?” the woman asked in perfect Mandarin. As she spoke, her gaze swept over Mo Sigui, catching only a glimpse of the back of his head. She sniffed lightly, as if detecting a faint medicinal scent. “It is this old man,” the innkeeper said with a smile, bowing to the two. “Would you like to eat or rest? We do not have rooms.” The innkeeper’s attention was diverted by the woman unfolding two portraits. “Have you seen these two people before?” Mo Sigui glanced at them, vaguely recognizing an old man and a young man in the portraits, and his heart skipped a beat. Could it be Elder Qi and him? He lowered his eyes, pretending to be nonchalant as he walked out. The innkeeper found the young man’s portrait somewhat familiar, but sensing the menacing nature of the two, he feared getting into trouble and said, “Our inn is in a remote location, and we do not have many customers all day. I have not seen these two in the portraits.” The woman put away the portraits and went inside, finding a seat by the window. “Tea, please.” The man also sat down. As he placed his sword beside him, he noticed powder on the corner of the table. “Innkeeper! Come wipe the table!” “Yes! Yes!” The innkeeper, having just brewed the tea, hurriedly grabbed a rag and ran over. The shop was usually quiet, run by the owner and his wife, with the wife as the cook. He was the only one working in the dining area, but now he was being bossed around by two people. He was about to wipe the dish when the woman stopped him. “Wait!” she said. The woman took a gourd from her waist and poured out a large centipede. The centipede crawled onto the table, followed the scent to the powder, and began to eat it. In a moment, its entire body turned crimson, almost swelling into a pupa. The innkeeper trembled, dropping the dishcloth without even realizing it. “I am asking you, who was sitting here before?” the woman said kindly. But the man’s long sword was already drawn, pressed against the innkeeper’s neck. “It was a young man. He had just left when you came in!” the innkeeper said, terrified. He dared not hide anything and quickly pulled out a folding fan from his robes. “Brave warrior, heroine, that young man even offered this as payment for his meal. This old man is blind and did not recognize him as the person you two are looking for. I did not mean to protect him; please, have mercy.” The woman took the folding fan and slowly unfolded it. Seeing a red apricot blossom on the fan, her eyes lit up. “Chase!” Before she finished speaking, she flashed and rushed out. The man sheathed his sword and hurriedly gave chase. “Ning Yi,” the man asked, “is it Mo Sigui?” The woman, called Ning Yi, released a centipede. Seeing it crawl north, she chased after it without hesitation. “It must be him! This time, we must meet him!” “Our lord values ​​you. If he also submits to our lord, would he not be your equal?” the man said. Ning Yi chuckled. “Equal? ​​This world is vast, but the pinnacle is as small as a needle’s point; there’s never been room for two number ones.” “Why not kill him?” the man suggested. “Killing him would make me unparalleled in the world?” Ning Yi chuckled. “No, killing him would only leave me feeling like I’ve forever had an insurmountable obstacle in my life.” Ning Yi’s real name was Ning Yanli, and he was only in his early twenties. From a young age, he was hailed as a medical genius, and seven or eight years ago, there was a saying, “Ning in the North, Mo in the South.” However, after Mo Sigui joined the Mei family, his reputation gradually faded, and “Ning in the North” disappeared from public view for unknown reasons. In the years that followed, these two medical prodigies were gradually forgotten by most people. The two tracked him for ten miles. Ning Yi saw the figure carrying a bundle ahead and blew out two flying needles. Mo Sigui sensed the noise behind him and quickly dodged. “Liu Hen, capture him alive!” Ning Yi ordered. Liu Hen obeyed, suddenly exerting his strength, shooting out like an arrow. A chain flew up and coiled around Mo Sigui like a serpent. He stumbled, almost falling to the ground. “Mo Sigui.” Ning Yi caught up, her voice laced with amusement. “I finally caught you!” Mo Sigui steadied himself, turned around, and said flippantly, “I do not remember getting into any romantic entanglements.” Ning Yanli met his pair of alluring eyes, which held a hint of a smile, and paused for a moment. “You are much more handsome than in the portrait.” Mo Sigui smiled noncommittally. “I’ve heard so much about you! My name is Ning Yanli. We do not know each other, but I am sure you’ve seen my masterpieces.” Ning Yanli quickly returned to the main topic. “The half-baked product?” Mo Sigui’s attitude became serious. “You used drugs to enhance those people’s skills!” “That’s right.” Ning Yanli flicked her wrist, releasing two poisoned flying needles. The poisoned needles sank into his thigh, and Mo Sigui groaned. She said, “This is a special gift I prepared for you. I hope you like it.” Mo Sigui forced a smile, enduring the pain spreading from his leg. “I will find you again in half a month.” Ning Yanli set a date for their next meeting, then glanced at Liu Hen. “Let’s go!” “Physician Ning.” Liu Hen had already gripped the hilt of his sword, wanting to kill Mo Sigui, but dared not act rashly. Ning Yanli did not turn her head. “If he dies by your sword, our bond will be severed from now on!” Liu Hen gritted his teeth, forcefully pulled back the iron chain, and followed Ning Yanli. Mo Sigui endured until the two figures disappeared from view. His body swayed slightly, and he reached out to steady himself on a withered branch beside him. “Such a potent poison.” Mo Sigui’s face was pale and bluish, but his eyes shone brightly, revealing a hint of excitement. As someone obsessed with medicine, he often tested medicines on himself because no one could better understand the subtle differences in the effects of medicine than he could. He readily accepted Ning Yanli’s provocation.

chapters.title: From Here
chapters.content: Mo Sigui, his slender fingers swiftly inserting silver needles into more than ten acupoints, first protecting vital points, then finding a secluded spot to analyze the toxicity. Based on his own reaction to the medicine, he could roughly determine the type of poison. As for the exact prescription, he would need to perform bloodletting and experiment with various methods. After most of the day had passed, Mo Sigui collapsed, exhausted, onto a pile of withered grass. Watching the golden crow about to fall, he suddenly thought of An Jiu. She had once, to keep her promise to him, endured the danger of damaging her meridians and forced herself to release Startling the String. He thought of the scene of her flying to save him that day, and then of his own difficult choice to help Elder Qi… He did not regret it. If he had to do it all over again, the result would be the same, but he felt a deep unease. Aside from his mentor-like and fatherly relationship with Elder Qi, he had always been the one doing favors for others. This was the first time he felt so indebted to someone. The mountain was shrouded in mist. Lights flickered on in the courtyard, and An Jiu sat on the threshold watching Chu Dingjiang cook. His cooking skills were limited, but everything he made tasted decent, enough to satisfy someone like An Jiu, who absolutely did not care for the taste in food. A soft crackling sound came from the stove, and the orange light cast a warm glow on Chu Dingjiang’s cold mask. “Where do you plan to go after you recover?” Before An Jiu could answer, he continued, “Let me make it clear beforehand: I am not responsible for protecting you.” “Protecting you…it’s been over a decade since I’ve been ‘protected,'” An Jiu thought to herself. Actually, Mei Jiu had protected her at the last moment, had she not? She gave a self-deprecating smile. Despite being an experienced assassin, she always needed such a frail person to shield her at crucial moments. Once it was her mother, and then it was Mei Jiu. “I want to join the Konghe Army,” An Jiu decided to find Mei Yanran. Ultimately, she did not want to owe Mei Jiu a lifetime of debt. “I want to remind you: with your meridians destroyed, purely external cultivation will be a disadvantage,” Chu Dingjiang said without further ado. “Hmm.” She had only herself to blame for this whole affair. There was nothing to complain about. Back then, she had so desperately wanted to separate from Mei Jiu. Mei Jiu was like a shackle, constantly binding and tormenting her; every second spent with her was agony. But now that they were finally separated, she felt an emptiness in her heart. Death came so suddenly, without any warning. “What are you thinking about?” Chu Dingjiang had somehow appeared beside her, tapping the ground lightly with his fire poker. An Jiu was startled. Her mental strength was strong, and her alertness was extremely high; she had actually been distracted just now—something that had never happened before! “Nothing,” An Jiu said. “I will return to the Konghe Army the day after tomorrow evening to report for duty.” Chu Dingjiang took a token from his robes and placed it in her hand. “This is the Divine Martial Token. Take it to the Bianjing Prefectural yamen, and someone will escort you to the Konghe Army.” “Thank you,” An Jiu said. In the twilight, her features were delicate, her skin pale. A pair of dark eyes stared at him without flinching. Chu Dingjiang turned his face away. “The work at the Konghe Academy is no easier than missions. Usually, we are divided into groups of ten, trained by a single master. Every two weeks, we draw lots for a sparring match. At first, it is just a simple duel, a point-to-point contest to determine a winner. Two months later, we are regrouped. Subsequent battles are life-or-death. The survivors have the option to choose between the Imperial Guards Team, the Divine Martial Team, the Divine Strategy Team, or the Dangerous Moon Team.” “You said you did not want to protect me; I thought you meant you did not care about me.” But he said these things. “Oh, then you misunderstood.” Chu Dingjiang did not consider himself a good person. But as a man, he could not just abandon a girl he’d just seen. He was currently too busy, but this was a small favor, and he’d done it. “My honest advice is, do not join the Imperial Guards Team.” “Why?” An Jiu asked, puzzled. Chu Dingjiang leaned closer to her, smiling, and said, “His Majesty believes in Taoism and believes that dual cultivation can improve one’s cultivation, especially for women who know martial arts. The Imperial Guards are responsible for protecting His Majesty closely for twelve hours a day… therefore… the women in the Imperial Guards also have this duty.” An Jiu nodded. “I understand.” Such a secret could not elicit the slightest reaction from her; Chu Dingjiang was very curious about what could possibly break her composure. “How high is the rank of the Divine Martial Commander of the Imperial Guards?” An Jiu asked. “A fourth-rank military officer.” Chu Dingjiang casually drew a simple diagram on the ground with a fire poker. “The headquarters of the Konghe Army is called the Konghe Bureau, headed by the Dark Commander, a principal second-rank official. Below him are two deputies, secondary second-rank officials, called Dark Deputy Commanders. Below them are four Dark Guards, principal third-rank officials. Below the Dark Guards are eight Dark Assistants, secondary third-rank officials. These people are the backbone of the Konghe Army…” The Konghe Army was divided into four branches: Imperial Guards, Divine Martial, Divine Strategy, and Dangerous Moon. The titles of the leaders were basically the same as those of the Konghe Army, except that they were prefixed with the names of their respective branches. They only had the authority to command troops, but not the authority to deploy troops or make decisions, and they did not receive the treatment that ordinary military officers should have. Therefore, Chu Dingjiang, as a fourth-rank official, was neither particularly low nor particularly high in status. “There is also a Supervisory Commission, headed by two Konghe Army Supervisory Censors, with subordinates being the Imperial Guards Commander, Divine Martial Commander, Divine Strategy Commander, and Dangerous Moon Commander,” Chu Dingjiang said. An Jiu suddenly realized, “So you were from the Supervisory Commission.” Being transferred from the Censorate was like releasing an eagle among a flock of cranes. Who would not be trembling with fear, worried about being pecked blind? It seemed Chu Dingjiang had actually managed to find allies among a group of outcasts—truly remarkable. “That’s right.” “Where have you been demoted to now?” An Jiu asked. Chu Dingjiang replied nonchalantly, “Divine Martial Commander, fifth rank.” It was a two-rank demotion, even lower than that of the Deputy Commander of the Divine Strategy Team. Thinking of that person, An Jiu recalled that fleeting glimpse of him, then remembered what he had said, and frowned. “Who is the Deputy Commander of the Divine Strategy Team?” “Gu Jinghong?” The Divine Strategy Team had two deputy commanders, but Chu Dingjiang had only guessed that An Jiu was referring to Gu Jinghong because he had previously served under the Mei family for a few days. “Not familiar, just a capable fellow.” Chu Dingjiang admired Gu Jinghong. He himself had become the Commander of the Divine Martial Army through six parts planning, two parts luck, and two parts skill, while Gu Jinghong had distinguished himself among the many members of the Konghe Army through meritorious service in carrying out missions, gradually rising to his current position. Chu Dingjiang sighed. “A steady and methodical approach is certainly good, but not everyone is a martial arts prodigy. Life is short, only a few decades; to achieve great things, one cannot afford to waste a moment.” “Assassinate those old men in the Konghe Army.” To repay Chu Dingjiang for saving her life, An Jiu sincerely offered this suggestion.

chapters.title: A Fierce Cousin
chapters.content: Because she had heard that there were very few masters at the Transcendent Realm in the world and that the martial arts of those leading armies were all at the Transcendent Realm, it meant that most of the high-ranking officials in the Konghe Army were less skilled than Chu Dingjiang. “What a brilliant idea!” Chu Dingjiang exclaimed. “Then I will assassinate the Prime Minister, and I will be second only to the Emperor!” An Jiu sensed the sarcasm and snorted. “You are clearly not cut out to be a high-ranking official! What high-ranking official does it personally? Just hire someone else to do it.” Chu Dingjiang laughed, pulled out a small piece of silver from his pocket, and said with boundless generosity, “Help me assassinate the Emperor’s favorite minister. After I take the throne, I will pay double!” “Alright!” An Jiu took it and stuffed it into her pocket. “I will assassinate the Emperor’s most favored eunuch for you, making sure it goes smoothly, so you can prepare to take the throne!” Sometimes the Emperor would send his favored eunuchs to serve as military supervisors or inspectors; they were no longer merely slaves but could also be considered ministers. “Haha!” Chu Dingjiang reached out to ruffle her hair, but An Jiu raised her hand to block him. Chu Dingjiang was slightly surprised. After all, he was at the Transcendent Realm while An Jiu had no internal energy. If he exerted his strength, An Jiu would not be able to block it. But her quick reaction was extremely rare; what a pity… “Go to sleep early!” He stood up and patted himself, dust scattering and landing all over An Jiu. An Jiu did not expect him to do something so childish and, for a moment, forgot to dodge. Watching him turn and go into the house, An Jiu slowly said, “The demotion must have been a huge blow to you, right?” “How so?” Chu Dingjiang turned back. An Jiu pointed to her head. “Your IQ has deteriorated.” “IQ?” Chu Dingjiang instinctively felt this was not a compliment, so he did not wait for her explanation. “Sleep as much as you can while you can; you will not have such carefree days later.” “Chu Dingjiang,” An Jiu called out, “how many people are left in the Mei family?” Seeing her calm expression, Chu Dingjiang answered truthfully, “Less than fifty in total. Only Mei Zhengjing, Mei Tingzhu, Mei Tingyuan, Mei Tingchun, and Mei Ruyan remain of the Mei bloodline. The two Old Madams are also unharmed.” Of the nearly one thousand people in Mei Mansion, only fifty remain. It seemed like a significant loss, but the Mei family’s direct descendants were already few in number. Mei Mansion only had a few hundred people, most of whom were servants. No one expected the enemy to have so many ninth-rank members. It was quite remarkable that the Mei family managed to preserve its main force of the younger generation amidst this unexpected attack. An Jiu lowered her eyes, hesitated for a moment, and said… “Then…among the survivors, is there anyone named Mo Sigui?” Chu Dingjiang could vaguely sense her tension. “Elder Qi and Mo Sigui are very famous in the Konghe Army, and they are also key figures protected by the army. Unfortunately, the shadow guards sent to them were killed, and we have temporarily lost contact with these two. However, we have not found any suspected bodies either. I have not received any news about Mei Clan for three days; he might still be alive.” As a low-ranking officer in the Divine Martial Capital, Chu Dingjiang only needed to receive missions and could no longer concern himself with every detail. “He will not die,” An Jiu murmured. Chu Dingjiang thought to himself that she and Mo Sigui must have a very deep relationship. Just as he was about to offer some words of comfort, he heard someone say, “Evil lives a thousand years. A scoundrel lives even longer.” “Having a cousin like you is truly Mo Sigui’s blessing!” Chu Dingjiang clicked his tongue. “You saved me, so you are my benefactor.” An Jiu, seemingly oblivious to his sarcasm, simply said, “If your fate were uncertain, I would certainly pray for you in the same way.” Chu Dingjiang’s lips twitched slightly. “You’ve gone to so much trouble!” “It’s nothing,” An Jiu replied. Chu Dingjiang felt that talking to this girl was a complete waste of time and emotions; sleeping would have been far more meaningful. Night fell. An Jiu and Chu Dingjiang always shared a room, but An Jiu slept in the bed. Chu Dingjiang would just find two stools to use. The weather was still chilly, but recently there had not been any heavy tasks, and he did not need to be on guard all the time, which was already a luxury. “You can sleep in the bed,” An Jiu said, putting on her cloak and pulling back the curtain. Chu Dingjiang turned his head and opened one eye. “Unable to sleep?” “Mmm.” An Jiu walked outside, feeling a sudden gust of wind beside her ear. She abruptly bent over, and as she stood up again, a punch was already thrown at the attacker. Chu Dingjiang grabbed her waist with one hand, and with the other, he swiftly pressed her pressure points, the fist stopping just half an inch in front of his nose. “Confiscating your dagger was a wise decision.” Chu Dingjiang carried her to the bed, dipped his hand in a sleeping potion, and covered An Jiu’s mouth and nose. Only after she closed her eyes did he release the pressure points. He turned around, and a sudden gust of wind unexpectedly swept in. “Unreasonable!” Chu Dingjiang’s good intentions were met with ingratitude. He spun around and grabbed her wrist, only to discover the dagger in her hand. He was instantly enraged; it seemed he had been raising a venomous snake these past few days! So he became even more ruthless. An Jiu launched a flying kick, and as Chu Dingjiang dodged, he leaned forward, pinning her firmly to the bed. Almost face-to-face, he clearly saw no murderous intent in her clear eyes. He instantly understood that An Jiu’s attack was not intended to harm him but was merely an outlet for her anger. He was right. Killing was the only way An Jiu could vent her anger, whether it was anger, hatred, or sorrow… Chu Dingjiang snatched the dagger from her hand and tossed it aside. He stood up, ripped off his cloak, revealing his agile figure, and dispelled all his protective internal energy. Looking down at her, he said, “Get up!” An Jiu’s mental energy erupted instantly, and she threw a punch. Chu Dingjiang felt an immense pressure, like a mountain, pressing down on him, rendering him immobile. In the instant his consciousness struggled, An Jiu’s fist had already landed solidly on his chest. He had underestimated her! Chu Dingjiang quickly broke free of the mental pressure and, like An Jiu, fought her using only mental energy, without any internal force. He had initially thought that he had only been suppressed by An Jiu’s mental energy due to momentary underestimation, but after ten moves, he was shocked to realize that her mental energy was far superior to his own! Without using internal force, he was actually at a disadvantage. After a while, Chu Dingjiang discovered that although An Jiu did not exude murderous intent, every move she made was a sure kill. During the trials at the ancient temple, he had already sensed that An Jiu was a troublesome opponent. But after dissipating his pride and joy in his inner strength, he truly discovered that she was more than just troublesome; she was utterly inhuman! When she attacked, her ferocity was like that of a predator determined to kill its prey, and a highly strategic one at that. Instantly, Chu Dingjiang’s fighting spirit was ignited. The two exchanged blows until, after a quarter of an hour, Chu Dingjiang’s physical advantage became apparent. However, An Jiu’s ability to maintain such a level of skill despite her severe injuries had already earned his respect. Seeing her face turn pale, Chu Dingjiang released his inner strength and stepped forward to restrain her. “Enough, that’s enough. Your wounds might reopen.” Feeling her release her strength, Chu Dingjiang helped her sit on the edge of the bed, and in the blink of an eye, he saw the mess in the room. The two looked like they had just been pulled out of the water. Chu Dingjiang said, “You are weak right now; rest for a while. I will go boil some water for you to wash up.” As soon as he said that, he almost bit his tongue off. Judging from her behavior just now, he really could not tell that she was weak.

chapters.title: Bandits
chapters.content: A fire was lit in the stove. Chu Dingjiang squatted in front of the stove, taking out the bottle of sleeping potion from his pocket. He had used a considerable dose to help An Jiu rest, but it was his first time using such a thing, and it had failed! The potion did not seem to have any effect on An Jiu at all. Chu Dingjiang could not help but wonder if it had lost its potency after being left out for so long. He poured a little into his palm and sniffed it. After only two sniffs, he felt dizzy and lightheaded. He immediately brushed the potion away, stepped out of the shed, and stood in an open space, closing his eyes to regulate his breathing. A dignified Commander of the Konghe Army, the Divine Martial Commander, would be a laughingstock if he had drugged himself! Fortunately, the amount inhaled was extremely small, and he recovered quickly. Chu Dingjiang opened his eyes, looking thoughtfully at the room where An Jiu was. After heating the water, he poured a basin of it into the room. “Just a quick wipe will do.” “Thanks,” An Jiu said. Chu Dingjiang hummed in agreement, exited the house, and closed the door behind him. He lightly leaped onto the roof, found a flat spot on the ridge, and sat down, gazing at the undulating mountains bathed in moonlight and mist. The mountains here were not very high or steep; from a distance, they appeared as a continuous, undulating expanse, like waves painted in ink. Listening to the rushing water inside the house and looking at the distant peaks, Chu Dingjiang could not help but recall that youthful body, already showing signs of curves, her body stained with blood—white and alluring, red and seductive… Thinking about it, he felt a warm current slowly gathering in his lower abdomen. Chu Dingjiang snapped back to reality, his cheeks flushing, and quickly tried to distract himself. When he rescued An Jiu this time, he did not know her meridians were completely destroyed. His original intention was to take her in, and later, when he discovered she was practically crippled, he had considered abandoning her. However, he had always believed… Those who win the hearts of the people could achieve great things. Even an ordinary person, if truly loyal, could sometimes play an unexpected role. With this mindset, he spent time rescuing her. His recent tasks had been quite light, and since he was idle anyway, he might as well do something. Sure enough, An Jiu did not disappoint. Even without internal energy, she was unlike any ordinary woman. No wonder she’s Mei Yanran’s daughter! Chu Dingjiang knew she had only recently returned to Mei Mansion, so she could not possibly be someone trained by the Mei family. After much thought, this was the only explanation. After sorting through his thoughts, Chu Dingjiang felt extremely remorseful for having such despicable thoughts. Sitting quietly for a while, he let out a sigh. Since he had intended to use her from the beginning, he should have maintained this mutually beneficial relationship. Although he had been forced to see her body to save her, she had clearly expressed her refusal, so he should not have harbored any other thoughts. Night returned its quietness. The next day, the two maintained their peaceful coexistence, as if nothing had happened, with only some bruises proving the fierce battle of the previous day. The following day, Chu Dingjiang returned to Bianjing to report for duty. Before leaving, he left a large bag of silver. Even though An Jiu did not know the local currency system or prices, she could guess it was a huge sum. Inside the bag was a note from Chu Dingjiang with just a few words: “Too much money, nowhere to spend it, please help me.” The signature was a powerful and imposing “Chu.” An Jiu’s lips curled into a smile. She understood the feeling of having too much money. She did not think Chu Dingjiang was joking. An Jiu had also had a lot of money before, but as one of the world’s most wanted criminals, she rarely had the opportunity to spend it. Holding this huge sum of money in her hand… It could have bought a large plot of land, but An Jiu felt utterly bored with life. Now, a slight bond had formed in her heart—to find Mei Yanran and Mo Sigui—so she used the money for travel expenses without a second thought. Those who did not want to die died, while those who did not want to live lived. Fate, truly, never went according to plan! After recuperating in the courtyard for five days, An Jiu set off towards Bianjing. Chu Dingjiang told her to keep heading east until she reached a place called Li Family Village, then turn north, saying nothing more. He intended to test the waters further. In this desolate mountainous region, unfamiliar with the terrain and lacking any road signs, even a highly experienced member of the Konghe Army would likely face considerable difficulties. However, An Jiu’s wilderness combat and survival skills were exceptional; she found the Li Family Village in just one day and one night. After observing the surrounding area for an hour, An Jiu entered the village, bought some men’s clothing, and found an inn to rest. The Song Dynasty had stricter regulations on women than the Tang Dynasty; none of the tailored clothes in the shops were made for women. An Jiu was relatively tall for a woman, but even that did nothing to make the men’s clothing fit her well. So, she altered it herself at the inn, tearing and tying it up, but it turned out quite neatly. The next day, she bought a horse, packed some provisions, and began her journey north. While buying pancakes, An Jiu asked the stall owner if she could find Bianjing. She estimated it would take three or four days by fast horse, plus time for rest and resupply, and that she could arrive in six days if all went well. However, fate was unkind. Just half an hour after leaving Zhao Family Village, she discovered that over thirty people were following her. These people had come from the middle of the road; they were not from the village. The earthy smell in the air and the damp wind suggested an impending rain. An Jiu, still recovering from a serious injury, was easily chilled by the rain. She hurried for seven or eight li and spotted rooftops faintly visible in the woods beside the road, so she spurred her horse towards them. The group of men following her saw this and reined in their horses. One of them said, “Brother, this young lady is acting strangely. Why is she heading into the woods?” Another man, with a high-pitched voice, chuckled lewdly. “Heh heh, I knew she was not from a respectable family. Who would wander around alone like that? She must be a prostitute. Look at her face, her figure… maybe she’s going into the woods to have some fun with us…” The leader said, “The scar on my arm is throbbing; it must be about to rain. This young lady seems quite experienced in travel; she might be from some martial arts sect. Let’s follow her and see what happens. If anything seems amiss, we will retreat immediately!” “Alright!” everyone agreed in unison. The rooftop looked close, but it was actually quite a distance away. Dark clouds slowly gathered in the sky, and by the time the group arrived, it had begun to drizzle. This was an abandoned local temple, often used by travelers on the main road to rest or seek shelter from the rain. Today, two people were resting inside: a scholar and a villager. Surprisingly, there was no woman in sight. The scholar held a book, his eyes fixed straight ahead, while the villager shrank back nervously. “Hey! You there, did you see a young woman come in?” the bandit leader asked the villager. Seeing the menacing look of the group, the villager quickly and honestly replied, “I did not see her.” “Strange!” One of them circled the temple, finding no hiding place. “Brother, the girl’s gone.” Slap! The bandit leader slapped him on the back of the head and glared at him fiercely. Scholars held a high social status these days. Seeing the scholar lodging alone in a dilapidated temple, yet dressed in brand-new, clean robes of fine fabric, he clearly came from a scholarly family, perhaps even a scholar who had passed the imperial examinations. Why he was lodging in a dilapidated temple was hard to say. In any case, the bandit leader did not want to provoke such a person. Seeing the rain outside intensifying, someone volunteered to scout the surrounding area. After a moment, the man returned, leading a horse. “Brother, the horse’s still here!” How fast could a young woman run? She could not have gone far without the horse. A woman of that beauty could be sold for thousands of taels of gold in Bianjing! They’d always been doing small-scale “business”; they could not possibly steal that much in a lifetime. Men died for wealth; birds died for food. The bandit leader hesitated for a moment, but ultimately could not resist the temptation of the enormous sum. “Chase!” The bandits, upon receiving the order, all rushed out. Two hours later, as dusk settled and the rain continued unabated, the villager paced anxiously around the entrance, then gritted his teeth and braved the rain to leave. Inside the temple, the scholar untied a bundle of firewood and piled it together. He gathered fallen leaves under the eaves to start a fire. As he gathered leaves in a corner, he suddenly felt a warm sensation on his fingers. He froze, his wrist suddenly gripped tightly. He struggled, and from the pile of leaves emerged a beautiful face. “Hey,” the beauty calmly asked, “How far is the nearest village or town?” The scholar replied blankly, “Ten li.” An Jiu frowned. Ten li was not far, but what if they ran into those people…? An Jiu could sense that the bandits were at most second or third-level martial artists, but there were too many of them, and her own condition was not much better, so she dared not be careless. Someone’s here! An Jiu could sense a large group approaching from afar; presumably, those who had failed to catch her had returned! “If these men ask where a woman is, point towards the Li Family Village!” An Jiu drew her dagger and pressed it against his neck. “If you do not do as I say, you will face the consequences.” With that, she picked up her bundle and straw hat, used a pillar for support, and climbed onto the roof beam. The scholar, still dazed, clutched a handful of leaves, not yet recovered from his amazement. The bandits, rushing through the rainy night, reached the temple gate. Seeing the scholar’s distraught state, the bandit leader’s mind raced. “My Lord, have you seen a young woman?” The scholar was startled, turned around, and, seeing them, remembered An Jiu’s instructions. He quickly pointed in the direction of Li Family Village. “Ha!” The bandit leader chuckled enigmatically, his eyes darting around. The scholar had acted perfectly the first time they arrived, but now he seemed flustered—very suspicious. They thoroughly searched the area within a two-li radius, but found no trace of her. She must still be in the temple! “Our young lady ran away on her own. If you know her whereabouts, My Lord, please tell us the truth,” the bandit leader said, bowing to the scholar. He then added, “But if you insist on not telling us, please forgive us, brothers, for offending you.” As he spoke, several men had already reached the corridor.

chapters.title: Tracking
chapters.content: An Jiu considered carefully. When her mental power erupted, it could even subdue a master like Chu Dingjiang at the Transcendent Realm; a mere second or third-tier martial artist should be no problem. She knew very well that once she started killing, her emotions were easily out of control. Although she remained relatively calm during the attack on the Mei family, she had a history of mental illness; who knew when it would flare up again? Even if she could never become someone like Mei Jiu, An Jiu did not want to continue being a killing machine. “Do not be ungrateful!” As An Jiu spoke, a surge of mental power suddenly swept over everyone present. “I do not want to start killing, but you keep forcing me. Those who do not want to die, get out of here now!” The overwhelming killing intent felt like a giant hand gripping their bodies, ready to crush them at any moment. The crowd turned pale, their bodies went limp, and they fell from their horses, not even daring to entertain the thought of escape. An Jiu withdrew her mental power. The bandit leader, gritting his teeth and forcing himself to stay upright, suddenly collapsed from his horse with a thud, kneeling on the ground. “Thank you for sparing my life, senior!” he cried. After kowtowing several times, he scrambled away, some of the fallen men failing to mount their horses several times before giving up and galloping away, abandoning their mounts in the process. An Jiu had not expected her mental intimidation to be so effective. If she had known, why bother playing hide-and-seek? This mental power seemed incapable of causing any real harm, but it was enough to scare people. As she thought this, she suddenly sensed a gaze. Looking down, she saw the scholar looking up at her. The scholar’s face was somewhat pale, but he did not appear fearful or panicked like the bandits. “This…” the scholar hesitated, choosing his words carefully. “Young lady, may I ask who you are?” An Jiu grew wary, subtly gripping her dagger. “You are not a scholar.” “A scholar?” He looked infatuated yet did not forget his manners, bowing respectfully. “My name is Wei Yuzhi.” “Wei Yuzhi… Wei Yuzhi…” An Jiu felt the name sounded familiar. She searched her memory for the name. That’s it! Mo Sigui had once told her about Piaomiao Mountain mansion. The mansion lord was named Wei Chuzhi, and he had a younger brother named Wei Yuzhi! “Piaomiao Mountain mansion?” In An Jiu’s mind, such a place was like the organization she used to belong to, all involved in illicit murder.
