Her back was tense, constantly on guard that they would try to take back the Plum Blossom Fist manual if they got the jade pendant. However, no one followed her until she reached the gate. Inside the hall, Mei Tingyuan rushed over and grabbed the jade, tears streaming down her face, a suppressed sob escaping her throat. “Ah Yuan,” Mei Tingzhu hugged her, closing her eyes and gently stroking her back. Mei Tingyuan suddenly burst into tears. Mei Zhengjing turned his face away, gripping the armrest of his chair tightly. After Mei Tingyuan finished crying, she remembered to ask, “Sixth Uncle, Fourteenth Young Lady is eager to sever ties with us; why are you still so good to her?” “She’s not simple,” Mei Zhengjing said, gazing at the bright moonlight outside the door. “She was able to sneak in here silently, without any of us noticing. She’s no ordinary person. That martial arts manual…” He looked at Mei Tingzhu; this niece had always been very clever, and he did not need to explain many things to her. “I kept the last copy,” Mei Tingzhu said. Mei Zhengjing nodded. Giving this scroll to An Jiu again would be a favor; even if she was not moved, at least she’d do something for the Mei family in return. “Uncle, what’s in the building? Could it help us rebuild the Mei family?” Mei Tingzhu asked. Mei Zhengjing sighed, “Yes, it is. Not only does it contain the vast wealth accumulated by the Mei family over the past century, but also contains a secret scroll recording the forces the Mei family has secretly cultivated.” Hearing this, Mei Tingyuan could not help but say, “Fortunately, Fourteenth Young Lady did not have any selfish motives!” “Even if she did, she would not be able to get in. I’ve been going back and forth through that secret passage since I was a child, and now it takes me several days to figure it out.” Mei Zhengjing recalled the past, a hint of a smile appearing in his eyes. “I was away from home for several years, and you all thought I had gone traveling again. Actually, I was trapped inside for several years. There are dense forests, fruits, and wild animals and birds; food is not a problem. However, if you are unlucky, you might be trapped there for life.” “Eldest brother also went traveling; could he have gone there too…” Mei Tingyuan thought of Mei Tingjun, her face turning pale and her eyes filled with pain. In the temple, Mei Tingjun was shot by a blue-fire crossbow while trying to push her away, turning into a pool of flesh and blood. This scene, Mei Tingyuan would never forget in her lifetime. In the dead of night, it would all be vividly clear in her mind; even many details she had forgotten at the time would become increasingly clear. Time blurred many things, but also made some things more profound. The moon sank in the west. An Jiu wandered through the city. Just before dawn, He Cai came to tell her that the mission was complete. She could rest for a few more days and practice her Plum Blossom Fist. An Jiu sighed inwardly. “Sister?” An Jiu was about to quicken her pace when a familiar voice sounded behind her.

chapters.title: Indifference
chapters.content: An Jiu turned around and saw a person emerge from the shadows. She wore a gray-black outfit, but the person had the handsome features of a young man. “It really is Sister!” she exclaimed excitedly. “Mei Ruyan,” An Jiu said, uttering her name. Mei Ruyan paused. Mei Jiu usually called her “Sister” or “Ah Shun,” rarely using this name. “Why are you being so distant, Sister?” Mei Ruyan approached, her expression hurt. She said sadly, “I did not receive a reply from Lord Chu in Yangzhou, so I risked following him to Bianjing. I guessed Sister might return to the Mei family, so I’ve been waiting nearby for over a month.” She removed her mask, revealing a radiant face. In An Jiu’s eyes, Mei Ruyan’s beauty was distinctly Eastern; her slender eyes could be both sharp and alluring. But equally, in An Jiu’s eyes, this face was deceptive. “If you wanted to use a fool, I am sorry; that fool is no longer here.” Mei Ruyan’s expression froze, and then she asked, “What did you say, sister?” “Stop pretending,” An Jiu said calmly. “Wei Yuzhi is as cunning as a ghost, and his mental power can manipulate external objects. How did you manage to escape from him?” “His physical constitution was weak to begin with. After using his manipulation abilities once, he needed a long recovery period, which allowed me to escape.” Mei Ruyan was so anxious that tears were almost streaming down her face. “Sister, you have to believe me. I ran away to save you because I thought I could rely on you in the future. If you ignore me, I will be dead sooner or later once Wei Yuzhi recovers!” In her desperation, she drew her sword and held it to her neck. “Since I am going to die sooner or later anyway, I might as well end it now! It will save me from living in constant fear.” A smile slowly crept onto An Jiu’s face; she was incredibly beautiful, but in the moonlight, she was as cold as frost. “From today onwards, I’ve changed my opinion of you. You are nothing special.” An Jiu was somewhat disappointed. She used to think that Mei Ruyan, growing up in harsh conditions, was like a flower on a cliff—though perhaps too worldly and cunning, she possessed a resilient beauty, far superior to Mei Jiu, that delicate little flower nurtured under someone’s wings. But now she felt that Mei Jiu was not bad either, at least far superior to the woman threatening suicide with a sword in front of her. Mei Ruyan lowered her sword. Watching An Jiu’s retreating figure, she called out, “Why are you so sure I have ill intentions?” “Because I do not care about you at all.” An Jiu did not turn around, throwing out this irrelevant answer. Because she did not care, she ignored her life and death. Mei Ruyan stood frozen. This was not the Mei Jiu she knew! Even if a person changed, they would not be so drastically transformed, would they? An Jiu moved through the city like an arrow. She returned to the Konghe Army in no time. She first went to Mo Sigui’s courtyard and threw the Plum Blossom Fist manual in front of him. “Check if anything’s missing?” Mo Sigui was intently trimming his nails, not having time to look up. “I am not surnamed Mei; how would I know what a manual looks like?” “You can recognize other martial arts manuals. How come you cannot recognize this one?” An Jiu sat opposite him, staring straight at him. “Have you gone blind lately?” “Ouch!” Mo Sigui’s fingers ached from filing them, and he glared at her fiercely. “Is this how you ask for a favor?” They stared at each other for a long time before An Jiu finally pouted. Just as she was about to say a few kind words to coax him, he raised his hand to stop her. “I understand your feelings perfectly, but there’s no need for words. Even a fool could see through it; a dog’s mouth will never produce ivory.” “I can,” An Jiu said. Mo Sigui was greatly surprised. He picked up the two scrolls on the table, his mood brightening. “You can actually make fun of yourself! I thought you only knew how to say hurtful things to irritate others.” An Jiu leaned closer to read with him, replying, “I just think you often make a lot of sense.” Slap! Mo Sigui slammed the scroll on the table. “I am not reading anymore!” An Jiu quickly checked the scroll, and seeing it was not broken, said, “The psychologist said that people who frequently cannot control their emotions are prone to mental illness. You often get angry for no reason; you’d better be careful.” “For no reason?” Mo Sigui raised his voice, then deflated, picking up the manual again. “I am almost driven to my wits’ end by you! I want to tell you something serious—An Jiu, be careful I do not poison you one day!” “You will not,” An Jiu said confidently, “because you are interested in the injuries on my body.” “…” Mo Sigui felt like he was being manipulated and tossed around. This feeling was so intense and sudden that he was speechless with “surprise.” Seeing that he was not moving, An Jiu urged, “Look quickly!” Mo Sigui silently flipped through the pages, moving very fast. When he reached the last page of the second volume, he suddenly grinned, rolled up his sleeves, and said, “Come on, let me guess, you must have put in a lot of effort to get this, right? But you still got tricked. This book is incomplete; there should be at least two more fist techniques at the end. Wow, what a turn of fortune! I’ve finally gotten my chance!” “I knew it,” An Jiu echoed Mo Sigui’s words, touching the scroll and saying, “It did take a lot of effort. The jade pendant the former patriarch gave me before he died—I painstakingly preserved it for so long, and then I just gave it to them? I hesitated for a whole day.” Mo Sigui’s smile faltered. “They gave me the manual so easily and did not even try to take it back, so I figured they must have withheld some of the content,” An Jiu continued, her slender, pale fingers tapping lightly on the table. “I will need a few more years to practice the later parts, right? I am thinking, if the Mei family does not give me the rest of the manual, or if their demands are too unreasonable, I should be able to snatch it. At the very least, I can steal it, right?” Mo Sigui said with a mocking smile, “I did not realize you were so capable. My apologies.” His mockery was so exaggerated that it was hard for An Jiu to ignore it. “This is a very serious matter…” Mo Sigui grabbed a nail file. “Take Da Jiu and Xiao Yue to play somewhere else. Do not disturb me while I am doing my important business.” An Jiu thought to herself, what kind of important business was filing nails! But then she noticed him lightly brushing the nail polish dust he’d scribbled down into a paper packet with a brush. “What are you collecting this for?” “To make medicine, of course,” Mo Sigui chuckled as if he’d thought of something amusing. “This is for your medicine! Feeling uneasy?” “I’d eat your finger even if you chopped it off.” An Jiu’s gaze lingered on his finger. This time, it was Mo Sigui who felt uneasy. He pocketed the packet. “Go away, go do what you are supposed to do!” An Jiu returned to her room to carefully study the Plum Blossom Fist. The way the Plum Blossom Fist generates power was very different from the Meridian-Severing Palm. The Meridian-Severing Palm’s force was fierce and violent, severing meridians while also damaging flesh, almost crippling the opponent. Plum Blossom Fist, however, was like “hitting a cow through a mountain,” containing a power that was both soft and strong. According to the manual, if one mastered Plum Blossom Fist to perfection, one could injure internal organs without leaving a trace on the skin.

chapters.title: Battlefield
chapters.content: An Jiu had been engrossed in studying the martial arts manual for several days, just beginning to grasp its basics, when she suddenly received a mission from above—to go to the battlefield and assist the Song army! This time, the entire team was being deployed under Gao Dazhuang’s leadership. Such a long-distance mission would take at least three to five months round-trip, making it impossible for He Cai and the others to accompany her. Upon receiving the news, He Cai immediately relayed it to Chu Dingjiang. On An Jiu’s side, except for Lou Mingyue, whose mission was still unfinished, the others had already set off overnight. They rode swiftly through the night. By sunrise, they were already dozens of li away from Bianjing. The further north they went, the more chilly the early spring became. Bianjing had long since shed its heavy winter coats, while here, the withered leaves were still covered with a thick layer of frost in the early morning. Gao Dazhuang tied up his horse and grumbled, “I must have been tricked into this mission!” Li Qingzhi, a man of strong character, immediately retorted, “That’s good! Going to the battlefield to lend a hand is much better than killing unidentified people all day!” “What do you know?” Gao Dazhuang pointed a delicate finger at his broad chest. “You have not seen how incompetent our Song army is; you cannot possibly understand!” Hearing this, Sui Yuntong said, “Lord Gao, could it be that you are…” Gao Dazhuang’s voice sounded effeminate, inevitably reminding people of a eunuch, but no one dared to ask. To An Jiu’s surprise, Gao Dazhuang was not angry. Instead, he sighed softly, “I personally witnessed those incompetent fools deserting in the face of battle; truly despicable.” An Jiu suddenly interjected, “I thought that eunuchs as military supervisors were the key to ruining the Song army.” “…” A gentle spring breeze swept by, and the scene fell silent. Gao Dazhuang suddenly erupted, one hand on his hip, the other pointing at her, “What do you know?! A eunuch may lack a leg, but he’s not brainless! Do not think that just because Lord Chu is protecting you, you can arbitrarily label people!” An Jiu looked at him calmly. “I will not bother with a disabled person like you.” Gao Dazhuang did not care about anything else, but he clearly understood the word “disabled,” and immediately rolled up his sleeves, ready to fight, “You little dwarf, you little blockhead! You tell me clearly, who’s disabled!” “My Lord, please calm down.” Sui Yuntong reached out to block his grabbing hand. “Young Lady Mei is straightforward and did not mean to slander or insult. My Lord is magnanimous; please forgive Young Lady Mei this time. Everything should be based on the mission!” Internal strife before even reaching their destination was punishable in the Konghe Army. Upon being reminded, Gao Dazhuang, considering all the potential concerns, found a way to back down and waved his hand, saying, “Fine! Anyway, I am not a eunuch!” The others thought to themselves, “I do not see anything about you that does not resemble a eunuch,” and were simply exasperated. Why were you getting so worked up about not being a eunuch? “My Lord, could you elaborate on the battlefield?” Before joining the Konghe Army, Li Qingzhi’s greatest wish was to serve in the military, and he was filled with fervent hope of leading an army to defeat the Liao Kingdom. Therefore, he was particularly keen on this mission. Gao Dazhuang saw that everyone seemed interested. He cleared his throat. “Eight years ago, I was in the Konghe Army, and I was also sent to the battlefield to assist the Song army. I was only sixteen or seventeen then, just like you, a big, simple-minded guy, full of enthusiasm and fearless in my actions. I was much more dedicated than when I took on other missions! I remember we risked our lives to infiltrate the enemy camp and gather a lot of crucial information. At that time, the Song generals were also full of confidence, but when the Liao cavalry approached with overwhelming force in the first battle, haha, our soldiers were so scared that their balls went limp. There was even a deserter. Once they started, they fled in a chaotic swarm. I was standing halfway up the slope, and the scene was truly spectacular! Before the cavalry even reached them, the Song soldiers were already trampled to death by their own men. After the Song army withdrew, only Liao soldiers and a eunuch remained on the vast battlefield.”  Recalling that scene, Gao Dazhuang still sighed with emotion. “I heard the eunuch shout, ‘Long live the Emperor!’ and then he grabbed his sword and charged alone towards the Liao army! I was utterly shocked.” Later, the eunuch was killed by a hail of arrows, but the Liao army showed him great respect, not disturbing his body.” Gao Dazhuang personally wrapped the body and buried him. “That eunuch was castrated at six or seven and raised deep in the palace. He has little worldly experience; he only knows a few characters and how to read people’s faces. How could he possibly be a military supervisor!” Gao Dazhuang sighed. “However, he was considered good. He did not understand and would not give orders recklessly. We all pretended he did not exist, and nobody respected him. Unexpectedly, in the end, he was the most loyal and resolute.” The crowd fell silent. For over ten years, the Song army had rarely reported victories against the Liao army. Being able to barely hold the border and prevent the Liao army from advancing unimpeded was already considered extremely good news! This situation was far from optimistic for those of them who had gone to the battlefield. After a long silence, Li Qingzhi could not help but ask, “What’s the situation on the battlefield lately?” “The Liao army is burning, killing, and looting. After a long winter, the Liao Kingdom is short of supplies and can only ask the Song Dynasty for help,” Sui Yuntong replied. Sun Dixian asked, “I heard the Liao Emperor is dying; is that true?” “Probably. Liao Emperors have always had short lifespans,” Sui Yuntong replied. “Pshaw! With so much burning, killing, and looting, how could he not die young!” Gao Dazhuang shrieked. The crowd remained silent. As dawn broke, the group continued along a side path, their initial enthusiasm and ease gone. An Jiu was not new to large-scale warfare, and she carried a lingering sense of unease. At this moment, she told herself to move forward, even if faced with similar situations, to avoid repeating past mistakes. Often, one’s mindset would determine the success or failure of a task. The group marched hastily, and the next day, Lou Mingyue caught up after completing her mission. Half a month later, they finally reached Hejian Prefecture, the largest city in the northern part of the Song Dynasty. The Shadow Guards dispatched by the Konghe Army were under the command of the Grand General, but also subject to the orders of the Supervising Officer. If the Supervising Officer questioned the Grand General’s orders, they were not obligated to carry them out. This was a rather absurd rule, but they had no choice but to comply. Upon arriving at Hejian Prefecture, Gao Dazhuang led the group to pay their respects to the legendary military supervisor. This time, the supervisor was not a eunuch but a civil official. The moonlight, like silver, streamed into the hall. The lamplight flickered in the wind. The middle-aged man with a fair complexion and a handsome beard, seated at the head of the table, gently set down his teacup. “Since you have been sent by the court, you will remain here temporarily, ready to be dispatched at any time.” “No need,” Gao Dazhuang refused bluntly. “We are here on His Majesty’s orders to receive our duties, not to enjoy ourselves. If you have any orders, My Lord, simply cough three times in the courtyard, and we will be ready to serve.”

chapters.title: The General
chapters.content: The supervising officer’s face darkened. He’d been doing well in the capital, but being suddenly relegated to this menial supervisor post was already frustrating enough. Now, even a lowly Shadow operative dared to show him attitude—this was intolerable! “Quite the temper!” The supervising officer slammed his hand on the table, the teacup rattling and spilling tea. “You’d better understand this clearly: who’s on whose orders?” Gao Dazhuang swayed, grabbing the officer’s collar and lifting him. He said menacingly, “We are all men who live on the edge, our lives hanging by a thread. We are here on His Majesty’s orders to offer our meager assistance in this battle, not to watch you show off! You’d better stay put, or we will skin you alive before we even kill any Liao soldiers!” The others remained motionless, as if they had not heard or seen anything. The supervising officer’s face turned ashen with rage, but Gao Dazhuang’s bloodthirsty aura prevented him from uttering a single word in rebuttal. Seeing this, Gao Dazhuang was even more disdainful, tossing him onto a chair with a look of disgust. “Farewell.” Hearing his words, the others quickly slipped out, disappearing into the moonlight in the blink of an eye. The supervising officer stared intently at the empty doorway, his teeth grinding, his expression gloomy; whether from fear or anger, it was hard to tell. The group stopped in the shadows a hundred paces away from the supervising officer’s residence, each finding a place to settle down—some hidden in trees, some on rooftops, some in dark alleys… Everything returned to calm, except for Gao Dazhuang’s muttering to himself from the alley, “Tsk, why bother arguing with that supervising officer? I should have just slept in that mansion.” He also wanted to stay in a better environment, but seeing the supervising officer’s airs made him unable to control his anger. Did those scholars even know how to fight? The Song Dynasty would perish sooner or later at the hands of these cowardly yet arrogant fools! Seeing these ignorant fools putting on airs gave Gao Dazhuang a headache. However, the supervising officer still had direct command over him, and if someone was intent on revenge and trying to trip him up, there was nothing he could do. Now, realizing the situation was irreversible, why did he make things difficult for himself? Gao Dazhuang felt that his impulsiveness was suicidal! He did not know that his earlier display of “heroism” had successfully salvaged his “dead eunuch” image. An Jiu and the others, who had initially been reluctant to accept him as their leader, now tacitly accepted his position. Even though Gao Dazhuang’s actions were irrational, he was right. They were people who risked their lives; being able to live a little more freely was a kind of consolation. “Are you not going to see the General?” Li Qingzhi asked. Gao Dazhuang, silent in the alley, replied after a moment, “I have not received any orders.” The Konghe Shadows had to strictly follow orders from above; matters like these, without instructions, could not be decided on their own. An Jiu paused, then asked, “Who is this supervisor?” Gao Dazhuang, still holding a grudge, had not intended to respond, but he could not help but speak his mind. “His name is Zhao Ling. He passed the imperial examination seven or eight years ago, but his ranking was not high, and he’s not well-known in the capital. He’s just related to the royal family. He’s good at scheming, so his official career has been smooth. For some reason, he was recommended as a supervisor. What does someone like that know about warfare?” His anger flared again as he spoke. They could not go see the army commander. Hearing Gao Dazhuang’s words, everyone felt a deep sense of powerlessness. A scholar who had never experienced war only knew how to scheme in the court. Did he really understand warfare? As members of the Konghe Shadows, none of them valued their lives too much, but the thought of possibly dying under meaningless orders felt both pathetic and laughable. Silence. The second day, awaiting orders, had just begun when three soft coughs came from Supervisor Zhao Ling’s courtyard. “Everyone, go over there. Sui Yuntong and I will appear together. The rest of you, wait around the courtyard,” Gao Dazhuang said. A series of dark figures darted about, arriving at the supervisor’s quarters in the blink of an eye. Gao Dazhuang and Sui Yuntong landed silently two zhang away from Zhao Ling like ghosts. Zhao Ling had just been threatened by Gao Dazhuang two days ago, and feeling somewhat embarrassed, he waited a while. When Gao Dazhuang did not speak, he coughed a few times and said in a deep voice, “These past two days, Liao cavalry have been wantonly burning, killing, and looting in border villages. I want to know the distribution of the Liao troops. You have three days to give me an answer.” “Yes,” Gao Dazhuang acknowledged the order and waited quietly. Zhao Ling said, “That’s all.” Gao Dazhuang and Sui Yuntong flashed out. The rest of the group gathered around. “You all heard it too. This mission will be carried out by Lou Mingyue, Li Qingzhi, and Qiu Yuntong,” Gao Dazhuang said. “Yes!” the three replied in unison. After they left, Gao Dazhuang happened to see An Jiu and said irritably, “If your lightness skill was not so terrible, I would not want to keep you hanging around in front of me for even a second!” An Jiu said calmly, “If you really hate someone, you do not need to waste your breath.” Gao Dazhuang was stunned. Thinking carefully, he realized that his dislike for An Jiu stemmed from some trivial matters and an inexplicable feeling, not from deep-seated hatred. That’s why he vented his emotions on her. Most people would find it difficult to remain calm when faced with insults, yet she saw right through him, demonstrating either exceptional composure or extraordinary insight. The wind in the north was still quite sharp, and the nights were much colder than in Bianjing. They huddled around the courtyard eating dry rations, while the supervising officer, Zhao Ling, had a late-night snack prepared—six dishes, a soup, and some wine. This difference fueled the resentment among the group. Only An Jiu seemed oblivious, eating her dry rations heartily. Gao Dazhuang took a big bite of his dry bread, glared at An Jiu, and said, “Useless!” An Jiu finished her bread, wiped her mouth, and said coldly, “Is it more impressive to just drool over other people’s food?” Gao Dazhuang gritted his teeth in hatred. “Incompetent, and not only are you alluring, but you also have an unpleasant way of speaking. You are only alive because of your good fortune in your past life. If you do not use it wisely, heaven might just take you away!” “Thank you for your concern,” An Jiu said, tying her face towel around her neck, her tone indifferent. “As a token of my appreciation, I will kindly remind you that heaven might be interested in androgynous creatures.” This was easy to understand; it simply meant he was neither male nor female. Gao Dazhuang’s face instantly turned ashen, and the dry bread in his hand turned to dust in an instant. “Please calm down, My Lord,” Sui Yuntong said quickly. Gao Dazhuang snorted, “A wretch like her, so utterly despicable, does not need my help! If you want to plead for her, you’d better burn incense and pray to Heaven!” Sui Yuntong handed him the dried bread. “Please have some, My Lord.” Gao Dazhuang was about to take it when An Jiu said coolly, “Such a promising person, eating dried bread?” “No! I will stay here and keep watch. Go get any orders, and I will make arrangements when I get back!” Gao Dazhuang said through gritted teeth, then turned and disappeared into a cluster of houses. Sui Yuntong sighed, “Young Lady Mei, you should not have offended him like this.” “He will not do anything.” An Jiu had a keen intuition; although Gao Dazhuang acted coy, he was not a petty person, as could be seen from his recounting of the Liao-Song war. Seeing that Sui Yuntong was still worried, An Jiu said, “I feel his personality is somewhat similar to Li Qingzhi’s.” “Similar?” Sui Yuntong was slightly surprised. What could a burly, bold man and a timid, sarcastic person have in common? Now that An Jiu brought it up, Sui Yuntong suddenly remembered Gao Dazhuang’s words when he recounted his experiences. That kind of temperament certainly did not seem like that of a petty person. Thinking of this, Sui Yuntong could not help but glance at An Jiu again, realizing that he did not understand this woman in front of him at all, who always seemed to speak without thinking. Halfway through the military supervisor’s late-night snack, a general in armor strode in with his men. This man was about thirty-five years old, tall and imposing. His chiseled face was half-hidden by a beard, and he had a deep scar on his cheek. His hair was haphazardly tied in a bun on his head. Although his armor was relatively clean, it still looked somewhat dirty and disheveled. What caught An Jiu and his companions’ attention was the murderous aura emanating from this military officer, an aura only achievable through mountains of corpses. He stood there, exuding an imposing presence without even needing to utter a sound, capable of intimidating ordinary people. Someone went in to report, and Zhao Ling quickly came out to greet him, reeking of alcohol.

chapters.title: The Beauty Trap
chapters.content: The military officer frowned, wanting to say something, but held back, giving him a slight bow. “Supervisor Zhao.” The position of Supervisor in the army held a delicate status. In terms of rank, it naturally could not surpass the Grand General, but the word “Supervisor” implied oversight. He monitored the entire military operation on behalf of the Emperor, essentially acting as the Emperor’s eyes and ears, wielding immense authority, and naturally, no one dared to neglect him. Zhao Ling returned the bow. “What important matter brings the Grand General here so late at night?” As he spoke, he made no attempt to invite him in to sit down. As Supervisor, Zhao Ling should have been with the Grand General in the central camp, but he insisted on staying in Hejian Prefecture. The Grand General, fearing that someone unfamiliar with warfare would be a hindrance, agreed. Now, having come to see him personally and received this cold reception, the Grand General’s attendants were visibly angry. “That’s right. I submitted a memorial half a month ago stating that the grain supplies were insufficient, but I do not know why there has been no response until now.” The General, suppressing his anger, asked calmly. “Could Supervisor Zhao inquire about this matter?” “Are the grain supplies not enough to last for two months? What’s the rush? Is the General afraid that His Majesty is not taking this seriously?” Supervisor Zhao, still harboring resentment from Gao Dazhuang’s words, spoke with particular sharpness. The Privy Council was primarily responsible for managing this matter, not the Emperor alone. Zhao Ling’s words were simply stirring up trouble. The general’s deputy, unable to contain himself any longer, coldly said, “It will take at least half a month to transport the supplies to Hejian Prefecture. Moreover, the Liao cavalry is elusive and might try to steal the supplies. We have not heard a word yet. If we run out of food, will Supervisor Zhao be left to guard the border alone, eating and drinking his fill?” “You!” Supervisor Zhao roared, “General, you should really discipline your subordinates!” The general turned and said, “Go back and receive your punishment!” “Yes, My Lord!” The deputy turned and left decisively. Then, the general acted as if nothing had happened. With a calm demeanor, he said, “His Majesty and the Privy Council are extremely busy; they may have overlooked something. Supervisor, please bring it up. After all, if the border cannot be defended because of this, your future will be ruined.” “Alright,” Zhao Ling clearly saw that the General was putting on an act with his deputy, but he took it to heart. He did not want to jeopardize his promising future. “I will submit a memorial tonight.” “Thank you!” The General bowed and turned to leave. Zhao Ling then said, “Look at my memory! General, you’ve been in such a hurry. Have you eaten? I’ve only just eaten now. Would you like to share a bite?” “No need. Just remember to submit your memorial, Supervisor Zhao.” The General suddenly remembered something. “I heard His Majesty sent Shadow to assist in the battle. Have they arrived yet?” Supervisor Zhao exclaimed in surprise, “General, what are you saying? Shadow is responsible for protecting His Majesty and the capital. Why would he be assisting in the border battle?” The few people in the shadows who heard this could not help but want to jump out and beat Zhao Ling up. The General said nothing more and strode away. An Jiu dispersed her mental energy. She vaguely heard the general’s voice from afar, “Damn it! I’ve risked my life here, and even getting a bite to eat requires me to be subservient, suffering this humiliation every day. I will not live long if I do not die on the battlefield!” With a loud crash, something collapsed. It turned out this general was not just bad-tempered but also had a fiery temper. “Why did you keep it from the general?” Sun Dixian whispered. Sui Yuntong sighed. “That was General Ling. Of all the military generals over the years, General Ling has the best record. It is thanks to him that we were able to defend against the Liao army. The entire Song Dynasty has a million soldiers, and he commands over 300,000. Do you not think His Majesty should be wary of him?” General Ling’s name was Ling Ziyue. He was literate, joined the army in his teens, and was quite intelligent, a man of both literary and martial talents. He was a magnanimous man, and in his twenty-odd years in the army, most of his soldiers, from commoner to lieutenant general, remained loyal to him. For such a man, rebellion would be incredibly easy. Moreover, throughout history, those who sit alone at the pinnacle of power were often suspicious, and few could truly be open-minded and practice the principle of “not using those you suspect, and not suspecting those you use.” “Ahem!” Zhao Ling coughed a few times, covering his mouth, while standing in the courtyard. None of them wanted to go out, but they could not refuse to obey orders. Finally, An Jiu and Sui Yuntong climbed over the wall and appeared before Zhao Ling. “Did the General say anything after he went out?” Zhao Ling asked. It was such a trivial matter! An Jiu remained silent, but Sui Yuntong said, “The General said that the Liao army might attack at any moment, and we must return to the camp as soon as possible.” Zhao Ling nodded. “That’s all; you may leave.” The two said yes and left together. After asking about this matter, Zhao Ling did not summon them again. The group watched the moon and the sun cast their shadows on the ground, rising in the east and setting in the west twice. Lou Mingyue and her two companions returned, bringing back much information about the Liao army. However, Zhao Ling did not immediately inform the general; instead, he hatched a plan to seize the credit. So he summoned Shadow again. This time, Gao Dazhuang went in alone. “I see there are several women among you,” Zhao Ling said. Gao Dazhuang agreed. “Call them out,” Zhao Ling said. Gao Dazhuang hesitated for a moment, then said, “The three of you come out.” Lou Mingyue, Sun Dixian, and An Jiu appeared in the room one after another. Zhao Ling carefully examined the three women’s figures. “Remove your masks.” “Ha,” Gao Dazhuang scoffed. “The only person in this world who could say such a thing to them is His Majesty. Is Supervisor Zhao plotting a rebellion?” Zhao Ling’s expression changed several times, but he ultimately did not get angry. He explained politely, “This gentleman misunderstands. I simply want to see their faces. I’ve heard quite a bit about Xiao Cheng of the Liao Dynasty; he’s fond of beautiful women. I’d like to ask one of them to approach him and see if we can get any useful information from him.” The Liao Dynasty previously practiced “governing the Khitans with the Liao system and treating the Han people with the Han system.” Therefore, the central government was divided into two major systems: the Northern Officials and the Southern Officials. The Northern Officials managed Khitan affairs, while the Southern Officials managed Han affairs. Later, the two institutions merged, with one person holding the position of “Chief Privy Councilor.” Xiao Cheng was the Chief Privy Councilor of the Liao Dynasty, a powerful minister with immense influence. “Has this matter been approved by the Grand General?” Gao Dazhuang asked. “I do not believe you do not know His Majesty’s intentions. Do not mention the Grand General again. You only need to obey my orders.” Zhao Ling displayed his official authority, and before Gao Dazhuang could reply, he pointed at An Jiu. “Her. It is her.” “She will not do,” Gao Dazhuang objected. Since he had to obey, Gao Dazhuang relented. He pointed to Lou Mingyue and Sun Dixian. “Choose one from among them.” Lou Mingyue had the highest martial arts skills and could protect herself, while Sun Dixian was shrewd and adept at flattery and winning people over. Both were also quite beautiful. Even if Sun Dixian was slightly less skilled, there was always the art of disguise.

chapters.title: Gao Dazhuang’s Past
chapters.content: Gao Dazhuang deeply felt that sending someone like Fourteenth Young Lady, who was utterly lacking in every way except for her appearance, to carry out the mission was like sending a lamb to the slaughter. Zhao Ling said, “Xiao Cheng has a particular fondness for women from Jiangnan. This one is petite, and her features are the most beautiful; she’s the most suitable.” Gao Dazhuang said, “Forgive my bluntness…” “Hmph,” Zhao Ling snorted, thinking to himself, “Have you not been blunt enough already!” “We’ve been sent to assist in the battle, to plant spies in Xiao Cheng’s residence. We will not be of much use in the war in the short term, so I refuse your orders.” Gao Dazhuang’s words were indeed very direct. For a moment, An Jiu and the other two could not help but look at him. Gao Dazhuang seemed to have become much tougher after arriving in Hejian Prefecture; even his effeminate manner could be ignored. “You dare refuse orders!” Zhao Ling, repeatedly thwarted, turned ashen-faced and glared at him. “I will report this to the Emperor!” “Hmph, go ahead and try.” Gao Dazhuang clicked his tongue, a murderous aura emanating from him, his eyes gleaming with bloodthirsty excitement. “I can also report to the Emperor that you harbor treasonous intentions. Want to take a gamble? Will the Emperor believe you or me?” “You!” Zhao Ling’s hair stood on end. The current Emperor was extremely suspicious. Even a loyal minister like Ling Ziyue, who showed no signs of rebellion, was feared. If someone were to report him to the Emperor, what would become of him? Zhao Ling shuddered at the thought. If Zhao Ling were an upright and honest person like Ling Ziyue, without any wrongdoing, he could speak with righteous indignation. However, Zhao Ling had engaged in many underhanded tactics to climb the ranks. Even though these had nothing to do with treason, once a person had a guilty conscience, they became weaker in their inner conflict. In truth, Gao Dazhuang had fooled Zhao Ling. Zhao Ling was unaware that the Emperor had already begun to crack down on the Konghe Army, and he was even more ignorant of the army’s internal affairs. Someone of Gao Dazhuang’s rank would not even have the right to submit a memorial, let alone an audience with the Emperor. “If the Lord has any further serious orders, then summon us,” Gao Dazhuang said, swaying as he left. An Jiu followed behind him, watching his swaying figure, even more alluring than the three women, and raised an eyebrow slightly. Lou Mingyue, always fond of straightforward people, had no objection to Gao Dazhuang’s actions. At least among these people, Sun Dixian was relatively rational. Once outside the courtyard, she said softly, “The Lord is playing with fire.” The Shadow’s duty was to obey orders unconditionally, and Gao Dazhuang not only refused to carry out the mission but also showed disrespect to his superiors. Zhao Ling had not grasped the situation. If he understood that he was in a position of overwhelming power, Gao Dazhuang would be in danger. “I used to be in the top ten of the Konghe List,” Gao Dazhuang said, gently smoothing his eyebrows with a finger, glancing sideways at them. “Do you know why I was kicked out of the Konghe Army?” Everyone was hearing this for the first time and stared at him in astonishment. “Because I crippled the Dark Capital Commander,” Gao Dazhuang sneered. “Do you know why I was not killed even though I committed a capital crime?” The Dark Capital Commander! That was the third-in-command of the Konghe Army… An Jiu suddenly said. “The saying ‘Evil lives on for a thousand years’ is very true. The more repulsive a species is, the more tenacious its vitality.” Like cockroaches and flies. Gao Dazhuang glared at her. The others suppressed their laughter, but seeing An Jiu’s serious gaze, they could not help themselves anymore. Sun Dixian adjusted her mindset and flattered him, “My Lord, you are truly amazing. Please teach us, alright?” Gao Dazhuang gave her a “teachable” look. Rubbing his aching back, he slowly said, “Because I am utterly loyal to His Majesty. If His Majesty says the sky is red, I will never say it is blue. If His Majesty sentences me to castration, I will cut off my own manhood without anyone lifting a finger.” Gao Dazhuang was once one of the top assassins who could meet the Emperor directly, but he was kicked out of the Konghe Army for making a mistake. However, instead of being reassigned elsewhere, he was transferred to the Konghe Institute, which trained trusted secret guards for the Emperor, showing that the Emperor still trusted him. “I never thought I’d come back like this, only to be put in this predicament,” Gao Dazhuang said, pointing at several people with his finger. “The way to survive in the Konghe Army is to be utterly loyal; otherwise, it is all about your own ability.” An Jiu’s impression of Gao Dazhuang kept changing; by now, she had actually developed a slight liking for this dead eunuch. “Your Excellency initially agreed with the supervisor’s plan; why did you change your mind later?” Sun Dixian’s gaze quickly swept over An Jiu. It was only when Zhao Ling pointed to An Jiu that he flatly refused. Sun Dixian had not seen An Jiu do anything to please anyone, so she was puzzled as to why everyone was protecting her. Gao Dazhuang chuckled twice and waved his hand. “At first, I only thought Fourteenth Young Lady was a good-for-nothing. Throw her into the river, and she would not be able to stop the flow or build a dam. But then I thought about it carefully, and you are not much better! The only one who fits the bill has a mind full of hatred. If she goes to Liao, she might be even worse than the two of you! It is a real pity for any of you to die like this. It would be better to throw you onto the battlefield to kill a few Liao soldiers.” The little bit of feeling of being protected that the three of them had had instantly vanished. “Besides, the ‘beauty trap’ is something you people who’ve practiced martial arts for over a decade do not need to do. There are plenty of cunning, venomous beauties in Dangerous Moon; you could throw one anywhere, and she’d stir up a storm.” Gao Dazhuang pointed at An Jiu and Lou Mingyue. “With your faces that look like you are owed two taels of silver, you are not cut out for it. Sun Dixian’s personality, however, is quite suitable.” Sun Dixian was a little smug at this assessment, but Gao Dazhuang immediately added, “However, her ugliness is a major flaw.” Sun Dixian’s face stiffened. She thought to herself that her earlier compliment had been wasted and gave a light snort, “Your Excellency speaks like Fourteenth Young Lady.” Although she was still far from being skilled at using a beauty trap, and although she certainly could not compare to Lou Mingyue and An Jiu, she was at least considered pretty. An Jiu, despite being criticized, did not utter a single word in response. Gao Dazhuang was somewhat puzzled and glanced at the silent An Jiu. An Jiu noticed his gaze and said calmly, “I only speak the truth; I never take pleasure in mocking people.” She could poison an entire village with her words, so why this expression of distancing herself from him? Gao Dazhuang’s face darkened, thinking to himself, “Who wants to associate with a shorty like you?” Sui Yuntong, Li Qingzhi, and Qiu Yuntong, who were nearby, also heard their conversation and secretly grinned. After laughing, they felt even more respect for Gao Dazhuang. Back at the Konghe Academy, no one had seen the instructors make a move; they never dreamed that this seemingly unremarkable effeminate man was so surprisingly skilled.

chapters.title: Femininity
chapters.content: After staking out the area for two days, Gao Dazhuang ordered Lou Mingyue to remain on standby, while the others went out in shifts to gather intelligence. They had not received orders, but they could not afford to be unaware of the battle situation. The Liao people were mostly nomadic tribes on horseback. This time, as in previous years, they were launching attacks with small cavalry units, each no more than five hundred men, burning, killing, and looting wherever they went. In recent years, dozens of nearby villages had already suffered. The Song army still lacked an effective way to deal with these cavalry units, often only able to handle the aftermath when they arrived. Moreover, each cavalryman was capable of taking on ten men and was exceptionally fierce. Even five thousand Song soldiers might not be able to stop five hundred of them. Therefore, every time they dealt with this tactic by the Liao army, the Song army was exhausted, and the feeling of being toyed with dampened the morale of the soldiers. Sui Yuntong believed that this winter was much longer than usual, and the Liao would not be satisfied with small-scale looting; they would at least try to capture several large cities to somewhat alleviate their resource shortages. General Ling Ziyue also suspected this, which was why he petitioned the Emperor to send the Konghe Shadows to assist in the battle. He was wholeheartedly concerned for the Song Dynasty, yet he knew that making such a request would only increase the Emperor’s suspicions. But why would he do this if he was not forced to? Over the years, he had trained many scouts, but these men were originally just farmers with no martial arts background, limiting their effectiveness. The Liao Kingdom, on the other hand, was investing heavily in its army of skilled warriors, making its cavalry so unstoppable. “Sigh! Let’s hold out for the Song Dynasty for as many years as we can,” Ling Ziyue sighed, standing in the wind, gazing at the distant, beginning-green grasslands. The adjutant following behind said, “But General, we’ve submitted five or six memorials urging for provisions, and we have not heard anything about them. We submitted a memorial requesting the Konghe Shadows long ago, but there’s still no sign of them!” “The Konghe Army has arrived,” Ling Ziyue said. The adjutant was surprised. He quickly looked around. “Where?” “At Zhao Ling’s place.” Ling Ziyue gripped the hilt of his sword, his brow furrowed, his voice weary. “It seems they are under Zhao Ling’s command. If we can control Zhao Ling, we can make those people work for us.” As a loyal general, he had guarded the border for over a decade, returning home only twice. Being treated like this by his ruler, it was impossible not to be hurt. But he had long since seen through it all; he was seen as a mountain between the Liao and Song dynasties, a mountain the Liao army would have to climb over his dead body to cross. The lieutenant understood the unspoken meaning, his eyes reddening. “My mother told me to study hard, but I did not listen. Now I realize that if you do not pass the imperial examinations, you are a useless person for life. Even if you sacrifice your life for your country, you will still be looked down upon.” “Hahaha!” Ling Ziyue laughed wildly. He patted his lieutenant’s shoulder heavily, causing him to stumble a couple of steps. “You are almost thirty, and you still talk like a brat. What future do you have?” He turned and went back to the camp, the lieutenant following, rubbing his shoulder. “All that pedantic stuff—who can fight the Liao cavalry?” Ling Ziyue joked. “The Song Dynasty should send ten thousand teachers to Liao to instruct. When I die, their kids will all be pedantic, Confucian scholars, spouting platitudes, unable to even climb a horse. Then the Song Dynasty can truly rest easy!” “General, that’s a great idea!” Mocking scholars was one of their greatest hobbies, and the lieutenant said gleefully, “So, studying really is useful!” “Of course!” Ling Ziyue laughed. An Jiu peeked out from behind a bush, watching the two figures enter the camp. Her eyesight allowed her to see the gray hairs already on Ling Ziyue’s head, even though he was still in his prime. So the Song Dynasty had people like that, too! However, before him lay the formidable Liao army, and behind him, the Song Emperor and his officials remained wary. An Jiu had never witnessed the interaction between civil and military officials, but she often heard scholars use terms like “warrior” and “vulgar,” their words dripping with undisguised contempt. This suggested that the military held a low status in the Song Dynasty. She stood there for a long time, yearning to approach this tough man who, despite his dire situation, could laugh so heartily, but ultimately suppressed the impulse. She infiltrated the camp under the cover of night and observed Ling Ziyue’s tent for an entire day. Ling Ziyue, a seasoned general, though his mental strength was inferior to An Jiu’s, instinctively sensed someone watching him. He remained calm, ordering the camp’s defenses tightened and carefully checking the confidential documents. Only after finding no signs of tampering did he breathe a sigh of relief. As night fell, he dismissed his men and stood in his tent, asking, “Is this the Shadow of the Konghe Army?” An Jiu heard this from afar, pursed her lips slightly, and remained silent. “If you are one of us, show yourself. If not, do not blame this general for being impolite!” Ling Ziyue’s mental strength was considerable; when it suddenly erupted, even An Jiu felt a tremor in her heart. Admiration aside, An Jiu never bought into threats. Ling Ziyue seemed to sense the person secretly watching him for a fleeting moment, but it vanished in an instant, along with the feeling of being watched. Ling Ziyue became increasingly certain that the other party was the Shadow of the Konghe Army, but he could not figure out their intentions. Were they here to assist in the battle or to monitor him? For the next two days, nothing unusual happened in the camp. On the fourth day, someone threw a crumpled piece of paper into the tent. Ling Ziyue was looking at the map when, before he could react, the person had vanished again. He hesitated for a moment, then picked up the crumpled paper and unfolded it. On it, several lines of writing were scribbled in a distorted manner: “Xijin Prefecture, 150,000 Liao troops.” At the end of the note was a lifelike crane seal. Ling Ziyue had seen it long ago; it was part of the Shadow Token of the Konghe Army! Receiving this news gave him a jolt, but out of caution, he simultaneously sent people to verify the information and urgently deployed troops for battle. Xijin Prefecture was not far from Hejian Prefecture. The Liao Kingdom’s secret gathering of 150,000 troops there meant a major operation was imminent. An Jiu left the camp and returned to Zhao Ling’s residence in Hejian Prefecture to meet the others. “Did it arrive?” Gao Dazhuang asked. “Yes.” An Jiu paused slightly. “He sent people to verify and began deployment.” “That’s good.” Gao Dazhuang yawned. “I thought coming here would mean facing death, but it turns out there’s nothing to do.” “It’s not that there’s nothing to do; it is that you refused orders,” An Jiu reminded him. Gao Dazhuang glanced at her sideways. “You look like you’d love to be a spy?” “I do not have the talent for that with my kind of sour face that looks like someone owes me two taels of silver,” An Jiu said, leaning against the wall, her voice coming softly from the shadows. “I am not even as feminine as you are.”

chapters.title: Rangers
chapters.content: Li Qingzhi could not help but burst out laughing. “What are you laughing at?!” Gao Dazhuang’s voice became shrill. No one spoke again. An Jiu climbed onto the roof and lay on the ridge, watching the stars hang low over the vast plain. The northern night wind was biting. At midnight, an unusual tremor came from the ground, startling all the hidden shadows! They all landed on the ground, listening intently. Gao Dazhuang frowned and immediately said, “Fourteenth Young Lady, quickly go and inform General Ling!” “Yes!” An Jiu flashed towards the army camp. They had gathered a lot of information these past few days and knew that Ling Ziyue had not deployed any cavalry nearby, nor did he have any plans to mobilize cavalry in the next two days. Besides, such a neat and powerful tremor did not seem like that of the Song cavalry. An Jiu arrived at the camp as quickly as possible. The soldiers on the watchtower only saw a fleeting shadow in the darkness, and when they looked again, there was no one there. An Jiu headed straight for Ling Ziyue’s tent. He was still awake, gathering his generals to prepare defenses against a Liao army surprise attack. An Jiu suddenly appeared in the tent. The generals immediately went on alert, their killing intent erupting, only to be extinguished by An Jiu’s overwhelming mental power. “There are cavalry in Hejian Prefecture, numbering over ten thousand,” An Jiu said in a deep voice. “They are not Song cavalry, are they?” The men looked at the mysterious woman before them. A white crane was embroidered in silver thread on the hem of her black robe. Her tight-fitting clothes accentuated her beautiful, slender figure. Compared to these rough men, she appeared thin and small. On her back was a long, black cloth bundle almost as big as she was; its shape did not resemble swords or knives, but rather a bow and crossbow. Incredibly, such a terrifying aura emanated from that small frame. Ling Ziyue was the first to recover. He glanced at An Jiu’s attire but, without asking her identity, immediately raised his voice. “Charge!” A roar jolted everyone awake. They glanced at An Jiu with lingering fear, then grabbed their armor from the table and strode out. Ling Ziyue made rapid arrangements as he went. With each command, the entire camp seemed to awaken suddenly. An Jiu hesitated for a moment, then followed behind Ling Ziyue. After everyone had departed, Ling Ziyue noticed the shadowy figure beside him. “Thank you.” An Jiu was silent for a moment before saying, “We should have sent you the message sooner.” Ling Ziyue smiled silently. Offering even a little help was already good enough; he never asked anything of others. “Actually, we have already disobeyed orders,” An Jiu emphasized, intending to tell him not to reveal the Shadow’s assistance. Ling Ziyue understood her meaning and nodded. Watching the army hurriedly leave the camp, he asked, “It is said that the Konghe Army obeys orders without question. Why did you disobey?” “We share the same fate,” An Jiu said. Ling Ziyue did not understand. He suspected that the Konghe Army, like himself, was also struggling. He said, “I thought you’d talk about protecting the country.” “I have no home.” An Jiu had never felt such lofty sentiments before. She acted solely on instinct, and her willingness to help Ling Ziyue stemmed entirely from her admiration of him. As for what Gao Dazhuang thought, she had no idea. According to Ling Ziyue’s analysis, Hejian Prefecture had a large garrison, and its walls were strong and high, making it difficult to conquer in a short time. Moreover, it was close to Ling Ziyue’s camp, facilitating support. Therefore, the Liao army’s target was most likely not Hejian Prefecture. If the Liao army were to move a large force, he could not possibly be completely unaware of it; the most likely scenario was that the Liao had gathered all their cavalry. Furthermore, a siege would not be carried out by cavalry alone; they must have other plans. Ling Ziyue ordered the camp to strengthen its defenses, focusing on safeguarding the remaining meager supplies. “I should go back and report,” An Jiu informed him, and without waiting for Ling Ziyue’s reply, she quickly left. Her speed was slightly slower than that of those skilled in light-footed martial arts, but her superior mental strength allowed her to conceal her presence completely. Midway, An Jiu stumbled upon a group of Liao cavalrymen and encountered the deputy general sent by Ling Ziyue. Observing from the shadows for a while, she realized it was not a chance encounter but a premeditated Liao ambush. The Liao cavalrymen, their faces completely obscured by armor, were significantly larger and more imposing than the Song soldiers. Their swordplay was fierce, and their combat prowess was extremely formidable. Compared to the Song soldiers, they seemed like a different species, slaughtering them with the aura of someone at the top of the food chain! Watching the Song soldiers’ blood splatter in their panic, An Jiu frowned. She hesitated for a moment, then drew her Dragon-Subduing Bow, nocked a white-feathered arrow, and aimed at a cavalryman who was using a spear to impale a Song soldier. Her aura seemed to merge with the darkness. Whoosh! The bowstring hummed, and the arrow streaked across the night sky like a meteor, heading straight for the man’s neck. An Jiu had observed that the rangers were clad in thick armor, with only a small gap where their helmets met their bodies. The rangers were engrossed in the battle, and by the time they realized the arrows were coming and tried to dodge, it was too late! The arrows pierced their carotid arteries, and blood gushed out like a torrential downpour. One of the rangers shouted in Khitan, and immediately, more than ten riders charged towards An Jiu. An Jiu simultaneously nocked four arrows, pulling the bow back with all her might, drawing it three-quarters of the way to a semi-full shape for the first time. The bow seemed unable to withstand the weight, creaking as if it were about to snap. An Jiu released her grip, and the four arrows instantly embedded themselves in the rangers’ mounts. The four horses neighed in pain, propelled forward several dozen chi before collapsing to the ground, sliding another six or seven chi before crashing into several trees as thick as bowls. The other horses, startled, suddenly slowed and turned to run in another direction. Taking advantage of the chaos, An Jiu swiftly fired several arrows, each one hitting its mark. The cavalry leader, amidst the fighting, noticed this and whistled sharply, seemingly out of nowhere. One of the cavalrymen suddenly leaped from his horse, disengaging from the battle, and in the blink of an eye, was less than ten paces away from An Jiu. An Jiu was startled. She lowered her Dragon-Subduing Bow, gripped her dagger, completely concealed her presence, and dodged several paces to the left. The battlefield was noisy, and the man did not notice An Jiu’s movement until he reached her previous spot, only to find her gone. An Jiu stared intently at the man. He was dressed like the other Liao cavalrymen, but not burly. He was tall and thin, his face completely covered by a metal helmet, revealing only a pair of dark eyes. This was a skilled warrior whom the Liao had placed among their cavalry. An Jiu judged him to be around level eight or nine, capable of taking on thousands of ordinary soldiers single-handedly! The Liao Kingdom placed such skilled fighters in its army, while the Song Dynasty’s experts were either imperial guards or the Emperor’s personal possessions. How could they possibly compete? The man remained vigilant while carefully searching for An Jiu’s whereabouts. However, the difference in their mental strength was too great; he could not find An Jiu. He also guessed that his opponent’s martial arts were superior, so he became even more cautious.

chapters.title: A Master of the Song Dynasty
chapters.content: The moonlight filtered through the grove, casting cold, white beams onto the cavalryman’s armor, making it appear eerily cold. An Jiu, hidden in the shadows, watched the light spots on the cavalryman’s body shift and change as he moved forward. When they were less than five zhang apart, An Jiu raised her arm and pulled the trigger of his crossbow. The man reacted with lightning speed, dodging to the right the instant he heard the sound. The crossbow bolt grazed his right arm, sparks flying as it struck her armor. An Jiu gave him no time to breathe, firing four arrows in quick succession, each half a chi apart and at varying heights, blocking his path. The cavalryman, seeing this, leaped onto a nearby tree, but before he could rise halfway, the four arrows were already upon him, one striking him squarely in the thigh! He grunted, knowing his opponent was skilled with a crossbow. Maintaining this distance would keep him at a disadvantage; he had to get close! Thinking this, he gritted his teeth, slashing away the obstructing arrows with his sword, and darted away like lightning. The force of his movement caused blood to gush from his leg wound, leaving a trail of blood. An Jiu had underestimated the ranger’s speed. She retreated hastily, drawing her twin swords from her back. A sinister smile appeared in the ranger’s eyes. His heavy sword gleamed with a blood-red hue in the dappled moonlight. Even before the blade reached her, An Jiu felt a powerful gust of wind. The sword was powerful and bold, wielded like a tiger. The wind from the blade, infused with a biting aura, could also be deadly. An Jiu was a fraction too slow to dodge, and a bead of blood, the size of a bean, welled up on her left cheek, sliding down like a tear of blood. Swords clashed heavily, sparks flying. Cracks appeared on An Jiu’s twin swords, seemingly on the verge of shattering. The light was dim, but by the faint glimmer of light, An Jiu glimpsed the cracks in her sword. Her opponent’s blade remained unscathed. An Jiu abruptly stomped her foot, unleashing a burst of power and launching a desperate counterattack. The ranger was both pleased and suspicious. He was pleased because the martial arts of external cultivators were mostly based on fierce and domineering techniques, and women were inherently weaker than men in this path. He was suspicious because he did not know how his opponent was concealing her aura; if her mental strength was extremely high, she would become very troublesome. In that moment of distraction, An Jiu’s twin swords snapped. She leaned back, the blade grazing her nose. An Jiu drew a dagger from her leg and leaped three zhang away. The two faced each other, blades drawn. The sounds of fighting outside gradually subsided, and An Jiu had a bad feeling—the Song army had been defeated and was retreating! She had to find a way to escape quickly! A thought flashed through An Jiu’s mind. She raised her hand and fired seven or eight arrows at the cavalryman. In the instant he dodged, An Jiu spun and disappeared into the darkness. She concealed her presence and retreated rapidly. A sharp whistle sounded behind her. Immediately afterwards, An Jiu sensed six more experts relentlessly pursuing her. Although these six were not as skilled as the cavalryman, their speed was astonishing. An Jiu’s speed was inherently inferior to that of an internal cultivator, and the distance between them was closing rapidly. The enemy had not yet found her trail. But with this encirclement maneuver, they would soon discover her. If there was no chance to escape, she might as well launch a counterattack! An Jiu abruptly stopped, minimizing her presence. Following her mental senses, she drew her Dragon-Subduing Bow and fired several arrows in the direction she sensed. The sound of arrows clashing against weapons echoed through the woods, along with screams of agony. They had not expected their fleeing prey to suddenly stop and counterattack, much less that someone could hit their target without them even seeing them! One of them roared in Khitan, and the remaining five suddenly doubled their speed. In almost two breaths, they appeared before the tree where An Jiu was hiding, forming a semi-circle around her. An Jiu leaped down from the other side of the tree and slowly emerged from behind it. After a brief standoff, the five men, wielding large swords, charged forward. An Jiu stood motionless against the powerful wind and energy. When they were only a few steps away, her mental energy suddenly erupted. The impact and pressure were like a mountain crashing down from the sky. Caught off guard by such a powerful mental attack, their minds went blank, leaving only the piercing sound in their ears! This was a mental attack technique that An Jiu had observed for a long time. Although it was the first time she had used it, the effect was clearly similar to what she had imagined. An Jiu drew her twin swords from her sides and immediately charged forward. The swords were coated with poison she had obtained from Mo Sigui; the moment they touched the skin, a smell of corroding and burning flesh emanated. An Jiu watched helplessly as a ranger’s armor turned into a hollow shell before her eyes, falling to the ground as a lifeless pile. In a short instant, she had killed three with her sword. The remaining two, freed from their predicament, took a few steps back in fear upon seeing the scene before them. An Jiu regretted not using her limited poison on her arrows. “The Song army has retreated, and you are surrounded by our men. You’d better surrender obediently,” one of them said in broken Chinese. Martial artists of the fourth rank and above were not everywhere. Even if the Liao Kingdom deployed all its martial artists to the army, there would not be many. An Jiu was not intimidated by these words; instead, they stirred a strange emotion within her. She coldly retorted, “Running wild on someone else’s territory, daring to speak so arrogantly!” Before her words even finished, she had already shot forward like an arrow. Her mental power merged with the two swords in her hands, making her appear as a giant sword slashing down from the sky. Before the sword even struck, her mental power had already cleaved a trench in the ground. The two men froze, feeling blood welling up from their skulls, washing over their faces. A short distance away, the Liao cavalry was approaching in this direction. From afar, they saw a large number of birds suddenly take flight from the forest, soaring into the night sky. The leaves, stirred by some unknown force, rose densely, almost obscuring the moon. No one gave the order, yet all the cavalrymen stopped in their tracks, watching this strange phenomenon with astonishment. The cavalry leader frowned, muttering, “So this is what the Song Dynasty’s experts are like…” Leaves fell in the forest. An Jiu coughed up blood, using her broken sword to steady herself. She glanced at the several corpses amidst the carnage, confirming they were all dead, before pulling out a medicine bottle from her robes. She took a pill, wiped the blood from her mouth, covered her face with her handkerchief again, and hurriedly left. After her reforging, the damage from the mental energy’s impact on her body had healed by seventy or eighty percent. Combined with the medicine Mo Sigui had given her, she was now almost completely recovered. Even An Jiu had not expected to suddenly unleash such powerful mental energy! Even her reforged body could not withstand it… Why was that?

chapters.title: Medicine
chapters.content: An Jiu ignored the Song army’s advance or retreat and rushed back to Hejian Prefecture to reunite with Gao Dazhuang and the others. At this time, the city walls of Hejian Prefecture were brightly lit, clearly preparing for battle. An Jiu sneaked into the city and, before even seeing the supervisor’s residence, sensed the presence of Gao Dazhuang and the others! An Jiu was startled. Previously, she could only discern the presence of a few individuals from a distance, like Chu Dingjiang, but not like this! It seemed her mental strength was exceptionally sharp now; despite her serious injuries, her mental awareness was clearer than ever. Without time to think, An Jiu headed straight for the others. Gao Dazhuang sensed An Jiu’s arrival and smelled the strong stench of blood and lingering killing intent. “Who did you fight?” “The Liao army.” An Jiu swallowed the blood that welled up in her throat. Acting without orders was a taboo of the Konghe Army. Sui Yuntong was about to plead for mercy when Gao Dazhuang asked, “Did you win or lose?” “I killed a few Liao martial artists. From my personal perspective, I won,” An Jiu replied. Gao Dazhuang chuckled twice, satisfied. “Well done.” An Jiu continued, “But I only exchanged five blows with one Liao martial artist before the Song army was defeated and retreated.” Gao Dazhuang snorted coldly. “Sure enough, a few hot-blooded men cannot save such a bunch of cowards!” “Cough! Cough! Cough!” Three coughs echoed from the supervisor’s residence. Gao Dazhuang rolled his eyes and lightly leaped into the courtyard. Zhao Ling asked with a grim face, “Is the Liao army going to attack the city?” Gao Dazhuang, too lazy to explain, simply replied with a word, “No!” Zhao Ling’s expression visibly relaxed. “What happened when the defending general came to report that Liao troops had entered the city?” “I do not know,” Gao Dazhuang said. Zhao Ling’s face darkened further, and he said coldly, “Go investigate! You are not going to refuse even this order, are you?” “Yes!” Gao Dazhuang replied, without moving. Zhao Ling waved his hand impatiently. “Nothing else; go.” He had initially thought that the court sending a few of the Konghe Army’s secret guards was a great thing. Regardless of whether it was beneficial to the war, at least his life would be more secure. But now it seemed that was not the case at all! These shadows were arrogant and did not take him seriously at all, and he really could not do anything about them. After all, the Emperor had not given him the authority to directly command the shadows. Ostensibly, they were supposed to be his assistants, but in reality, they were cooperating… Gao Dazhuang returned. “Find a place to sleep.” “Are you not going to tell him?” Sui Yuntong asked. They had gathered a lot of information these past few days, and based on that, they could guess the Liao army’s intentions in this surprise attack. Gao Dazhuang did not seem to intend to tell Zhao Ling any of this. “What use would it be for him to know all this for?” Gao Dazhuang said indifferently. “If he lived in the main camp, he’d know the situation by now. Why would we need to tell him?” “My Lord, are you not going a bit too far?” Sun Dixian asked worriedly. After all, the supervisor’s authority was considerable. If Zhao Ling were truly pushed to the limit, they probably would not have a good time either. Sun Dixian generally did not easily offend people, especially superiors. “Useless trash, I have no interest in serving him.” Gao Dazhuang flattered whomever he felt like. He knew Zhao Ling’s background from the beginning, but he was not too opposed to him. After all, this was the consistent rule of the Song Dynasty. But Zhao Ling was abusing his official power—this was unacceptable! Gao Dazhuang had dealt with many civil officials before and understood their nature very well. If they were obeyed blindly from the start, they would take it for granted and have the Shadow Guard handle every trivial matter. Therefore, it was necessary to warn them in advance that the Shadow Guard of the Konghe Army was not someone anyone could order around at will! No one spoke again; each lost in their own thoughts, they found suitable places to rest. An Jiu curled up on a beam in the corridor, closing her eyes to regulate her breathing. After taking the pills specially prepared by Mo Sigui, the damage to her body caused by the mental energy quickly healed. After about two hours, the pain was no longer as intense as before, and she clearly felt that her senses had become clearer. An Jiu took out the small bottle containing the pills, opened it, and sniffed it. The first thing she smelled was a strong medicinal odor. Just as she was about to seal it, she suddenly noticed a faint, almost imperceptible, scent of blood. The smell was extremely faint, but An Jiu was always very sensitive to the smell of blood. An Jiu sniffed carefully, and the scent of blood became clearer and clearer. Recalling that after her body was rebuilt, Mo Sigui had given her similar pills, much larger than the ones in the bottle. At that time, she had just come out of a medicinal bath, and her senses had not fully recovered, so she had not noticed the bloody smell. Now… she was certain that the rapid healing of her wounds and the change in her mental strength were closely related to this pill. Thinking about the changes in her seven orifices, An Jiu’s heart skipped a beat, as if she had grasped something, but the feeling was fleeting and never became clearer. An Jiu put away the medicine bottle and secretly practiced the Plum Blossom Fist. The east began to lighten. The distant rumble of war drums could be faintly heard. The people hiding in the corner were awakened. Zhao Ling also woke up from his sleep. The lights in the room were on. He hurriedly dressed and ran to the main hall. “Someone, come here!” The guard entered the room. “Sir!” “What happened?” Zhao Ling asked. The man said, “I do not know, but judging from the direction, it seems the Liao army launched a surprise attack on our camp.” “What?” Zhao Ling was shocked. Having spent many years in officialdom, while not quite at the level of completely concealing his emotions, he was at least not easily flustered. “The Liao army dares to attack our camp?” The man slightly raised his eyes, not daring to answer, thinking that this was expected. The Liao Kingdom harbored wolfish ambitions, raiding the border for years; a large army pressing in was only a matter of time. Zhao Ling, however, was thinking, “Was Ling Ziyue not hailed as a divine general of the Song Dynasty? His years of guarding the border had deterred the Liao army from making any rash moves—was that not impressive?” “You may leave,” Zhao Ling said, slowly calming himself. “Yes!” The guard bowed and withdrew. An Jiu, in the corridor, heard the entire conversation clearly. Zhao Ling coughed three times. A pebble struck a pillar near An Jiu with a loud crack. An Jiu knew Gao Dazhuang was telling her to go in, so she lightly jumped down and slipped into the house. An Jiu’s murderous aura had not completely dissipated. She had several wounds on her body, and because of her black clothes, the bloodstains were not visible, but a faint smell of blood wafted through the air. Zhao Ling glanced at her a few more times. “What happened?” “An encounter with Liao army martial arts instructors,” An Jiu answered truthfully. Zhao Ling paused. “Where did you encounter the Liao army?” Huh? Did she let something slip? An Jiu frowned, trying to figure out how to cover it up. She could not very well tell Zhao Ling the truth—that they were secretly helping Ling Ziyue… Seeing her silence, Zhao Ling pressed, “They were not sent to assassinate me, were they?” Great! He’d actually found a reason for her. An Jiu’s brow relaxed, and she nodded solemnly.

chapters.title: An Jiu’s Care
chapters.content: Zhao Ling thought to himself that these Shadows were indeed useful; he should still cultivate good relationships. Thinking this, he felt a desire to get closer to her. He hesitated for a moment, his gaze finally settling on An Jiu’s jade-like forehead and eyes. Seeing the scars under her eyes, he said with pity, “You are such a beautiful woman; why did you choose this path?” An Jiu was usually not very talkative with strangers, but she wanted to offer her opinion on his question. After a few pauses, she summarized what she wanted to say: “Faced with a powerful enemy, if one cannot stand up, who will?” If one interpreted this slightly differently, it would be incredibly crude! But Zhao Ling held back. He had to seize this opportunity to win over the Konghe Army and prevent the relationship from deteriorating further. He forced a faint smile. “Young lady, your words are straightforward; you must be a person of strong character. However, you may have misunderstood something. We have never been weak in the face of the Liao invasion.” “Ha.” An Jiu showed no smile. After gaining a deeper understanding of the Song Dynasty’s situation, she felt it was an extremely serious matter. So, to ensure Zhao Ling fully understood her meaning, she used an analogy. “It seems we have different understandings of weakness. Faced with rape where there is still room for resistance, some people shout ‘No!’ while enjoying it, demonstrating through their actions that their education is insufficient to combat the animalistic desires within their nature. We do not shout, saving our energy for fighting.” Zhao Ling clenched his teeth, his beard trembling slightly. Seeing his expression, An Jiu wondered if she had been too harsh. So, she said in what she thought was a very tactful way, “I cannot bring myself to just obediently submit, which is why I am still in this line of work.” Hmm, that was a great explanation, very considerate of his feelings. An Jiu felt herself becoming more and more normal and that she would soon be out of the ranks of the mentally ill. She felt a slight excitement. Her bright, dark eyes stared intently at Zhao Ling. “You…” Zhao Ling’s voice trembled. “You…you get out.” An Jiu’s gaze calmed. This reaction was not what she expected… “Yes.” An Jiu leaped onto the roof beam, glancing down to see Zhao Ling panting as he poured himself a glass of water. An Jiu was not good at communicating, but she could clearly tell if the other person was happy or angry. After a moment’s thought, she kindly added, “If you do not want to resist, My Lord, we can protect you. No need to be too grateful. Just do not turn around and hate us for interfering with your enjoyment.” Pfft! Zhao Ling sprayed water all over the table, some even coming out of his nostrils, choking him and making his eyes water. He frantically pulled out a handkerchief to wipe himself. An Jiu paused, hearing Gao Dazhuang’s laughter coming from afar. She frowned, and before Zhao Ling could finish cleaning up, she rushed over. “What are you laughing at?” An Jiu landed on a nearby tree. Gao Dazhuang laughed until tears streamed down his face, slumping against a horizontal branch and gasping for breath. “Mei…Fourteenth Young Lady…you said it so well. The Great Song is proud of you.” “My intuition tells me you are mocking me,” An Jiu said, not falling for it. “Really,” Gao Dazhuang wiped away his tears and told her earnestly, “I finally think you are a rather likable little dwarf.” “I will grow taller,” An Jiu calmly told him this fact. An Jiu was half European and half American in her previous life. She was already over 1.7 meters tall at sixteen or seventeen, and now she was about 1.6 meters tall. Although shorter than in her previous life, it was not a big problem for a girl still developing! “Then we will talk about it after you grow taller,” Gao Dazhuang secretly decided. In the future, dealing with people like Zhao Ling should be handled by the Fourteenth Young Lady! As the two were talking, Lou Mingyue returned. “It was the Liao army attacking the camp. They were after the supplies and equipment,” she said, revealing the information she had just gathered. “This time, the Liao army deployed many skilled fighters; even I was almost overtaken. Although General Ling has made preparations, I think the Liao army will still be able to escape unscathed.” Sui Yuntong analyzed, “They are taking this risk to pave the way for the Liao army’s imminent arrival. I checked a couple of days ago, and there’s not much grain left in the Hejian Prefecture granaries.” The Song Dynasty had a million soldiers. Such a large force would be extremely taxing even without war, let alone now, when the war was at its most intense.
