An Jiu clicked her tongue expressionlessly. “Poor horse.” Chu Dingjiang smiled, “He is Xiao Zhenning, a fierce general from Empress Dowager Xiao’s maternal clan.” An Jiu saw the towering Xiao Zhenning speak, and the Liao general beside him fell silent. Having fought for many years, he understood Ling Ziyue better than anyone. “Blue-fire crossbows!” An Jiu whispered. Chu Dingjiang’s expression also sharpened. He looked towards Xiao Zhenning’s direction, and sure enough, there were ten black-clad men with crossbows, their weapons aimed at Ling Ziyue! Xiao Zhenning’s expression was also grim. He would much rather defeat Ling Ziyue with his own strength than face this situation, but he had been given top-secret weapons and orders to kill Ling Ziyue, and he had to obey. Death was imminent. Ling Ziyue saw it too, but if he turned and fled now, his commander would escape, and the Song army would be defeated. The short stalemate felt like decades to Ling Ziyue. Faced with this situation, Chu Dingjiang’s expression was unusually heavy. He stared at the blue-fire crossbows, his dark eyes deep, as if waiting for something. Ling Ziyue wore the same expression, fine beads of sweat already forming at his temples.

chapters.title: Turning the Tide
chapters.content: An Jiu took down the Dragon-Subduing Bow, but instead of taking an arrow, she glanced at Chu Dingjiang. Chu Dingjiang immediately understood her meaning and placed his hand on her back. The bowstring was drawn back, and as a red light appeared at An Jiu’s fingertips, the Dragon-Subduing Bow seemed to emit a low, satisfying hum. At the same time, Chu Dingjiang felt his inner energy surge forth like a floodgate being opened. A red-glowing arrow of inner energy took shape, and An Jiu aimed at the crossbow hole of a crossbow a hundred feet away. Dust filled the air, severely limiting visibility. As she aimed, the Dragon-Subduing Bow seemed unsatisfied, continuously drawing out Chu Dingjiang’s inner energy. This energy circulated within An Jiu’s body, eventually converging at her fingertips. The initially ethereal arrow grew darker and darker, from light red to deep red, then to dark red, finally forming a clearly shaped black arrow, seemingly solidified! Gao Dazhuang watched this scene in astonishment. If An Jiu had noticed the arrow’s shape at this moment, she would have been even more astonished than Gao Dazhuang, for the solidified arrow was none other than the Killing Feather Arrow! After the Killing Feather Arrow appeared, the Dragon-Subduing Bow continued to absorb internal energy, and soon, wisps of red light, like burning flames, swirled around the black arrow. After circulating her true qi twice within her body, An Jiu felt her vision become clearer. At this moment, her mind was filled with the low hum of the Dragon-Subduing Bow; everything in the world seemed to fade into nothingness, except for the hole of a crossbow in the distance, which was crystal clear, as if magnified infinitely before her eyes. The dazzling red light shooting into the sky attracted the attention of the Liao army’s rear. Xiao Zhenning’s eyes darkened, and he suddenly turned his horse around. Just then, a clear crane’s cry pierced the heavens, and a streak of red light, like a hurricane, sent sand and stones flying across the ground. Dust, stirred up by the true qi, surged to both sides like waves cleaved by a sword. The sky in the middle was crystal clear. The two armies locked in fierce combat suddenly felt an intense heat. For a fleeting moment, they thought a golden crow had fallen; wherever the light passed, countless cranes cried out, their usual elegant forms suddenly filled with terrifying killing intent. The arrows approached the blue-fire crossbows in the blink of an eye. Before the crossbowmen could react, their crossbows began to shatter silently upon contact with the red light. It seemed like ten thousand years, but in reality, only a moment. Boom! A deafening roar ripped through the chaos, and the ball of light exploded a hundred feet away. After a brief pause, the force of this energy, a mixture of masterful skill and the power of over a dozen blue-fire crossbows, surged outwards with earth-shattering power. No one would forget this scene. Where the light struck, flesh and blood flew everywhere, but in the blink of an eye, not a drop of blood remained; instead, plumes of black smoke billowed, emitting a foul, acrid smell. Ling Ziyue roared, his voice thick with inner strength, “Retreat!” However, his voice was drowned out by the deafening roar. For a moment, both the Liao and Song armies could only flee blindly, driven by instinct. An Jiu stared wide-eyed at the scene before her. Her eyes reflected the ball of light, astonishingly bright, and her blood seemed to boil! This destructive power was in no way inferior to advanced firearms! Chu Dingjiang coughed up blood and fell from the tree. An Jiu froze. Her mind was a blur. The destructive urge that had been fueled within her gradually dissipated as Chu Dingjiang fell. A moment of clarity returned to her mind, and without thinking, she lunged down to grab him. “Chu Dingjiang!” A hint of fear lingered in her voice. A faint smile appeared on Chu Dingjiang’s pale face. An Jiu watched helplessly as his tall body crashed heavily into the dust, raising a cloud of dust, as if she heard something shatter within her own heart. In an instant, it felt as if he had fallen into an ice cave. The restlessness stirred by the killing was instantly forced back, her mind became crystal clear, and a long-absent sense of panic returned to her heart. “Chu Dingjiang!” An Jiu, having just landed, rushed over to help him up, placing her hand on his neck pulse. Finding it still beating, she breathed a sigh of relief. Chu Dingjiang, seeing her terrified expression, turned his head and coughed up blood, his voice hoarse. “I will not die.” “Mm.” An Jiu crouched down, grabbing his arm. “I will carry you away.” Chu Dingjiang silently leaned against her small back, his eyes burning. How long ago had he dreamed of someone standing by him in times of crisis? Even if they could not offer much help, at least he would not feel alone. And now, his dream had finally come true. The petite woman before him could carry just as much as he could. An Jiu was not particularly tall or muscular, but her explosive power and endurance were astonishing. Carrying the large Chu Dingjiang on her back, she ran straight into the camp without even breaking a sweat. “Chu Dingjiang, how are you?” An Jiu placed Chu Dingjiang on Ling Ziyue’s couch. Seeing him about to fall asleep, she anxiously slapped his face hard. “Should we call a physician?” “An Xiao Jiu, count how many times you slapped me today!” Chu Dingjiang said through gritted teeth. An Jiu thought to herself, “He can still hold a grudge, so his condition is not too bad.” Chu Dingjiang, after appreciating her rare display of panic, comforted her, “I am fine. My inner energy was drained too quickly and violently; I am a little weak right now and need to rest and recuperate. Do not disturb me.” “Alright, then I will guard you.” An Jiu picked up the Dragon-Subduing Bow and stood at the door. Chu Dingjiang looked at her, covered in dust but holding the Dragon-Subduing Bow with a serious expression, and his gaze softened even more. Chu Dingjiang was not a gentle person at heart. He was adept at disguising himself, sometimes appearing forthright and generous, sometimes considerate and attentive, sometimes cold and taciturn… He was a strategist, displaying different faces to different people, but in reality, his heart was cold and ruthless. He had never understood what An Jiu meant to him. At first, she was merely a pet he intended to keep for amusement and to alleviate his loneliness, but his feelings seemed to be gradually spiraling out of control. Just now, he clearly saw An Jiu throw herself down without hesitation, touching the deepest softness in his heart. For him, it did not matter whether she fell from a tree or a cliff; what mattered was that someone had selflessly accompanied him. Chu Dingjiang closed his eyes to regulate his breathing. About half an hour later, the army returned to camp. The crossbows exploded, causing several thousand casualties on both the Liao and Song armies. The closest enemy forces were almost entirely Liao soldiers. Since no bodies could be found, a rough estimate suggested approximately five or six hundred dead, with several thousand more Liao and Song soldiers also caught in the crossfire, suffering varying degrees of injury. Xiao Zhenning assumed the Song forces used weapons similar to their crossbows, but lacking information on their numbers, he dared not launch another attack and hastily retreated. Ling Ziyue returned to find An Jiu standing like a statue at the door. He paused for a moment, then clasped his hands in a deep salute. An Jiu did not exchange pleasantries, saying directly, “May I borrow your place to heal my wounds?” Ling Ziyue readily agreed, “How are your injuries? Would you like a military physician to come and examine you?” An Jiu shook her head. “General, the men from the Armory have arrived!” someone reported.

chapters.title: Weapon Master
chapters.content: “Let them come over.” Ling Ziyue assumed the court would send at least ten people. However, the soldiers only brought three people. The one on the left looked to be about fifteen or sixteen years old, dressed as a boy, carrying a huge bundle in her arms. Her bright, almond-shaped eyes darted around nervously like a startled deer, making it seem as if a slight noise might send her running away. Ling Ziyue immediately recognized her as a woman! The person beside her was a real man with captivating eyes, exuding charm. Behind him, a child with a topknot, resembling a bean sprout, was struggling to carry a large wooden box and a bamboo basket on his back. The box looked extremely heavy, swaying with each step, a stark contrast to the elegant man in front, who walked empty-handed. Ling Ziyue saw the man with captivating eyes smiling at what was behind him and knew he knew the woman behind him. He had witnessed An Jiu’s incredible archery skills and believed the Konghe Army was indeed not to be underestimated. He would not look down on these two men because of their appearance, especially since they both possessed disguise skills, and their current appearance might not be their true selves. However, Ling Ziyue was overthinking it. A man as proud of his good looks as Mo Sigui would not use such things to cover his face unless absolutely necessary! Ling Ziyue’s blood-stained armor had not been cleaned yet, and his murderous aura was still palpable. Mo Sigui sighed inwardly, “What a fierce general!” He bowed politely. “I am Mo Sigui; greetings, General.” “Master Mo, you must be tired from your journey,” Ling Ziyue said, bowing back. “Let’s not delay; let’s go into the tent and talk in detail.” He assumed the other two children were attendants. Mo Sigui knew he had misunderstood and stepped aside to let Lou Xiaowu go first. “This is a weapons expert sent by the court; I am merely a physician.” Upon hearing this, even the soldier leading the way could not help but widen his eyes in surprise. Lou Xiaowu sidled closer to Mo Sigui, glancing cautiously at Ling Ziyue, and muttered, “Do not be like this. We did not want to come either.” Seeing the awkward atmosphere, Mo Sigui said, “This child is naive and inexperienced; please forgive her, General.” When Lou Xiaowu was raised away from home, she was just a girl from a modest family. Although her education differed from that of ordinary young ladies, her activities were confined to a small courtyard. Later, after returning to the Lou family, where all the women lived, they mostly went out at night, always veiled. This was the first time she had ever been to a military camp full of rough men in broad daylight. Ling Ziyue snapped out of his daze, his shock vanishing. He respectfully clasped his hands in a fist salute to Lou Xiaowu. Remembering that his main tent was occupied, he gestured for the two to enter the supervisor’s tent, saying, “Please follow me, both of you.” Mo Sigui was busy flirtatiously looking at An Jiu, but Lou Xiaowu tugged at him. “Brother Mo, let’s go!” The group entered the supervisor’s tent one after the other. Zhao Ling was listlessly sipping tea when he suddenly felt the light dim. Looking up, he saw Ling Ziyue and several men in plain clothes enter. Without bothering to ask questions, he stood up and said, “Congratulations on your triumphant return, General!” In front of outsiders, Ling Ziyue still gave Zhao Ling some face. “The supervising officer has also worked hard in the rear.” He paused, then introduced them. “This is the weapon expert sent by the court, and this is Physician Mo.” Ling Ziyue had spent most of his time at the border and had never heard of Mo Sigui’s reputation. However, since he was a physician sent by the court, his medical skills must be excellent, deserving of the title “Divine Physician.” Zhao Ling’s reaction to Lou Xiaowu was far more exaggerated than Ling Ziyue’s. “This…this…” Lou Xiaowu’s face clearly showed her displeasure. As the head of the Lou family, she was carefree and could do whatever she wanted. Even if she stayed indoors researching weapons for ten days or half a month, no one would bother her. Then, inexplicably, she was banished here. Everyone treated her like a circus monkey, making her extremely uncomfortable. “Please sit down,” Ling Ziyue said. Zhao Ling hesitated for a moment but finally remembered to offer Ling Ziyue his seat. “General, please sit.” Everyone took their seats. “May I ask how everyone is addressed?” Ling Ziyue asked, looking at Lou Xiaowu. “My name is…” Smack! Lou Xiaowu had barely opened her mouth when Mo Sigui flicked her forehead, her lips pouting, looking at Mo Sigui with teary eyes. This girl had gone mad from being cooped up in her room all day. She would definitely reveal her name and background honestly! Mo Sigui answered for her, “General, just call her Xiaowu.” “Then I apologize for my intrusion,” Ling Ziyue said politely, though he was not one to mince words, since she was a woman. He continued, “Xiaowu must already know about the Liao Kingdom’s crossbows.” Lou Xiaowu’s almond-shaped eyes welled with tears. She nodded, placed the large bundle she was carrying on the table, and untied it. Inside, everyone saw a large pile of miscellaneous parts and tools, all mixed in a chaotic mess, indistinguishable from one another. Ling Ziyue looked at her aggrieved little face and then at the bundle, feeling a slight unease. As he was thinking this, he saw Lou Xiaowu quickly pick out some loose parts and assemble them without hesitation. Everyone only saw a pair of white hands moving like butterflies; in just a few breaths, a complete crossbow appeared before their eyes. She carefully placed a specially made arrow inside and set it on the table. “I obtained one before, took it apart, and spent months studying it to make a new one. However, the materials used to make the arrow were medicinal stones, some of which are quite rare, so I only made one…” Ling Ziyue’s hawk-like eyes lit up. He stood up and picked up the crossbow. “Is this as powerful as the crossbows used by the Liao army?” Lou Xiaowu nodded, her voice leaving no room for doubt. “Of course, and even more so.” Her demeanor and tone were completely different from her earlier timid appearance; this was absolute confidence in her area of ​​expertise. Ling Ziyue naturally sensed her change. His heart, which had just been pounding, slowly calmed down. He lowered his eyes to carefully examine the crossbow in his hand. This crossbow was not made of wood, but of something that was neither iron nor copper, and it felt cold to the touch. The arrow was made of the same material; the shaft was thicker than ordinary crossbow bolts, and the arrowhead was not sharp, but rather shaped like a very sharp needle. “Why was it made this way?” Ling Ziyue asked. “This makes it easier to launch the crossbow and reduces friction during flight.” Lou Xiaowu stopped him as he reached for the arrowhead. “This arrow is not for shooting; it explodes upon contact with the target during its rapid advance.” “I see.” Ling Ziyue examined it again before placing the crossbow back on the table. “The Liao Kingdom has already used over a dozen blue-fire crossbows, all of which were destroyed by a single arrow from a Shadow. However, according to our investigation, the Liao Kingdom has over twenty hidden in Xijin Prefecture alone. We do not know if there are any elsewhere. My request for weapons experts from the court is mainly to dismantle and destroy this type of weapon.” Hearing Lou Xiaowu’s explanation, Ling Ziyue knew that it was impossible to manufacture a large number of blue-fire crossbows in a short time. Moreover, for those accustomed to using cold weapons, the sudden appearance of such a powerful weapon was difficult to accept. If both sides used such weapons, the casualties would increase a hundredfold or even a thousandfold.

chapters.title: Calamity
chapters.content: Given the current situation, Ling Ziyue still strove to destroy the enemy’s blue-fire crossbows, hoping to escape this unfair battle. The Liao army was already stronger than the Song army. If the blue-fire crossbows could not be destroyed, Ling Ziyue would truly sigh, “Heaven has doomed the Song!” “Disassembling the weapons is no problem, but the problem is…” Lou Xiaowu shifted her bottom shyly. “My martial arts are not very good, and there’s something even more important…” Ling Ziyue listened attentively. “I am not getting enough to eat.” Lou Xiaowu’s voice was barely audible, her face flushed from the roots of her ears to her cheeks. Mo Sigui glared; this sounded like he was the one inflicting pain! Ling Ziyue smiled. As long as Lou Xiaowu had real skills, nothing else mattered. “I will have the cook prepare a whole roasted lamb right away. Last month, I intercepted two Liao nomadic herds and got quite a few lambs; they are very tender.” Lou Xiaowu swallowed, nodding with a greedy look despite her reserved demeanor. Ling Ziyue arranged accommodations for the two men and then went to his own tent. He needed to take good care of the mysterious expert; no one else could have infiltrated the Liao army undetected, and the disarming of the blue-fire crossbows still depended on his abilities. Ling Ziyue’s impression of Chu Dingjiang could be summed up in a word—mysterious. He was clad in a black robe, and his voice suggested he was young, at most in his prime, but speaking with him felt like talking to a highly respected elder. Back in his tent, Ling Ziyue saw An Jiu still standing inside the door, bow in hand, and asked in a low voice, “How is that Shadow’s injury?” Chu Dingjiang said he was fine but had not yet come out. Knowing An Jiu’s way of thinking, she would not suspect Chu Dingjiang was lying to comfort her; she would only think, “He needs time to recover.” “That’s good.” Ling Ziyue did not mention asking for help for the time being and turned to instruct his subordinates to prepare a large meal. This emergency retreat by the Liao Kingdom relied entirely on the deterrent effect of Chu Dingjiang and An Jiu’s arrow. Although Ling Ziyue breathed a sigh of relief, he felt no joy at the victory. He temporarily moved to another tent, carefully considering the words of the mysterious figure. Perhaps it was because he cared too much that the Emperor was now wary of him. But even if time could turn back, he could not guarantee that he could keep the Emperor from becoming suspicious. The figure was right about one thing: since he was acting with the country and its people in mind, he should not be too concerned about his personal reputation. Sometimes, he did not need to care so much about the court’s or the Emperor’s thoughts. Under the court’s oppression, he had been so submissive and humiliated, yet the court had not shown him much respect or trust! As long as he could defend the border, he had to be domineering when necessary and cunning when required, not blindly loyal. How many more years could Ling Ziyue defend the Song Dynasty? So be it. His conscience would judge his merits and demerits. He only hoped that his conscience was clear before Heaven and Earth. Ling Ziyue tossed and turned until midnight, then got up, threw on his clothes, and wrote a memorial. The gist of it was: The border troops were running out of supplies. They had to count every grain of rice at each meal, and the soldiers were starving and could not take it anymore. If supplies were not provided soon, they might as well all resign and return to their fields! Anyone who wanted to guard the border could come. He quit! After writing it, the pent-up anger he had been holding in suddenly dissipated. He read it over and over again, then gritted his teeth. He summoned a messenger and ordered it to be sent to Bianjing by express courier. In reality, Ling Ziyue was not exaggerating; he was now meticulously calculating every meal, fearing there would not be enough to last until the imperial supplies arrived. The imperial court was slow, but he could not wait until he was literally counting every grain of rice before trying to urge them on! After sending the memorial, Ling Ziyue thought of his trusted generals who had died tragically and of the numerous battles, large and small, he had fought on the border over the years. He could not sleep anymore, so he threw on his clothes and went out for some fresh air. He stood outside the tent for a while. As he was about to return, he saw a figure standing like a statue, bow in hand, at the entrance of the main tent. He paused, then walked over. “Please rest, young lady. I will send someone to relieve you.” Ling Ziyue wondered, “Is there no one else among the guards? Why is she the only one on guard?” An Jiu pursed her lips tightly and shook her head. She planned to keep watch for another hour. If Chu Dingjiang still had not made a move, she would go and call Mo Sigui to check. “Just come to me if anything happens.” Countless generals around Ling Ziyue had died in battle. Even the hardest-hearted man would be moved. Being able to do something for his comrades was a luxury for him. “Young lady, your arrow was a stunning feat, turning the tide of battle. I, Ling Ziyue, am filled with admiration.” Even now, recalling that arrow, Ling Ziyue still remembered the shockwave that made his blood boil, as if his internal organs were about to shatter. “I thank you again, young lady, and all the Shadow Warriors.” Both the crossbow bolt and the arrow fired by An Jiu far exceeded Ling Ziyue’s expectations. He considered himself a well-traveled and knowledgeable man, yet the warriors of both nations repeatedly shattered his perceptions. It was as if divine soldiers had descended from the heavens; Ling Ziyue clearly felt his own insignificance and weakness. This was also one of the reasons he had the courage to coerce the court. He was not very strong to begin with; if he were to be timid and hesitant, how could his meager strength withstand a powerful enemy and protect the Song Dynasty? An Jiu could not guess Ling Ziyue’s thoughts, but she could clearly sense his emotions. After a moment of silence, just as Ling Ziyue sighed and prepared to turn back, An Jiu said, “I rarely admire anyone in my life, but General, I admire you.” Ling Ziyue stopped and turned around. “I do not deserve your admiration.” An Jiu met his gaze, noticing that the general’s aura had weakened somewhat since their first meeting. Displeased, she coldly said, “In terms of martial arts, General, you are only at the eighth or ninth level. There are plenty of those in the Konghe Army. But we are all ghosts who cannot see the light of day. General, you are the blazing sun. If you cannot illuminate the Song Dynasty, you should disappear as soon as possible and not give people false hope.” These words were very blunt. Ling Ziyue understood the underlying meaning but disagreed with her view. “Only with hope and anticipation can there be a future. I will do my utmost to bring a ray of dawn to the people of the Song Dynasty, even if it is false.” There would always be people drawn to this ray of dawn and would relentlessly strive forward. If more and more such people gathered, it was not impossible to turn hope into reality. “It’s like being in the desert, about to starve to death, when someone tells you there’s food ten li ahead. You will fight with all your might to get it.” Speaking to An Jiu, Ling Ziyue cast aside his momentary self-doubt, realizing how silly his earlier thought was. He laughed, “Maybe after ten li, there’s another ten li. As long as we keep the thought of food ahead, we can go further. Maybe we will really find a chance to survive along the way.” An Jiu fell into thought. Ling Ziyue’s explanation was simple and easy to understand; she agreed. She was just wondering why she had not thought of it herself. “This year, the Liao army breached two border cities of the Song Dynasty, abducting over 70,000 Song people, more than half of whom were women and children. And grain, gold, and silver…” Ling Ziyue sighed, wanting to say more, but ultimately remained silent. The Liao Kingdom was divided into the Northern and Southern Courts, with the Southern Court primarily governing the Han Chinese. The Liao Kingdom’s climate was harsh, and its domestic food production could not sustain a large population. Every year, many people perished during the long winter. The one or two cities on this border were simply not worth diverting manpower to fight the Song army. The Liao Kingdom had always been eyeing the prosperous lands south of the Yellow River. Ling Ziyue heard footsteps and turned to see Mo Sigui, dressed in a long robe, leisurely approaching, seemingly satisfied with his meal. Two plump, half-grown tigers followed him, one of which excitedly swished its fat tail and lunged at An Jiu. The tiger tugged at her trouser leg, rolling around. She bent down and scooped it up with one hand. The tiger immediately stopped its struggle, lying comfortably in her arms, its eyes half-closed, even letting out a large yawn. “General Ling,” Mo Sigui bowed. Ling Ziyue returned the bow and said, “I have other matters to attend to. If you two need anything, please send someone to let me know.” “Of course, of course,” Mo Sigui replied without hesitation. After Ling Ziyue left, Mo Sigui rushed excitedly to An Jiu’s side, peering into the tent. “I heard Chu Dingjiang is injured? How is he? When will he die?” An Jiu slowly turned her head, her dark eyes calmly fixed on him. “He will die a moment before you.” “That’s ruthless!” Mo Sigui exclaimed, but he was quite pleased. “The extra moment I live is thanks to my good character.” An Jiu coldly sneered, “Evil lives a thousand years; good people do not live long. When it comes to character, you have to find someone who lives longer. You are slapping yourself in the face like that and trying to glorify yourself; I will not admire you, I will just think you are brain-dead.” After saying that, An Jiu, thinking that Mo Sigui might need to save Chu Dingjiang later, paused and sincerely offered him a suggestion, “If you want to change the situation, you still have to let Chu Dingjiang outlive you.”

chapters.title: Hidden Enemy
chapters.content: “Ha!” Mo Sigui chuckled, a half-smile playing on his lips. “Ah Jiu, you are really laying your heart bare for a game. Do you dare dig any deeper into your cunning?” An Jiu stared at him silently, inwardly wondering, “Was it really that obvious?” “Fine, I’ve resigned myself to it anyway.” Mo Sigui suddenly leaned closer to her and whispered, “How’s our little Yuyu doing now?” “She’s doing well,” An Jiu pondered. Mo Sigui waited expectantly, but she seemed lost in thought and did not say anything more. “Tell me more! Like, is she eating well? Is she dressed well…?” “She eats dry rations and wears this black outfit.” An Jiu scoffed at him. “Do you not already know? Why waste my breath!” “Sigh!” Mo Sigui sighed a few times, abruptly changing the subject, and reached out to take her wrist to feel her pulse. After a moment of silence, he solemnly grasped An Jiu’s other wrist. After a pause, he said, “Have you been seriously injured again recently?” An Jiu nodded, thinking to herself that Mo Sigui was indeed quite skilled. “Once, I encountered the Liao army alone and suddenly used my mental power, which caused me to vomit blood.” “No wonder! Otherwise, with the pills I’ve prepared this time, plus your gradual practice of Plum Blossom Fist, you should have recovered long ago.” Mo Sigui took out another small bottle from his pocket. “I suppose you are running low on pills. Continue taking them, two at a time, to help you recover.” An Jiu uncorked the bottle and sniffed it gently. Sure enough, she smelled a faint bloody odor again. “What kind of medicine is this? Why does it smell like blood?” “I cut my finger while clipping my nails,” Mo Sigui lied without batting an eye. An Jiu knew that Mo Sigui’s pills were concentrated. Such a large pot of ingredients could not possibly produce such a strong smell from just a little blood, especially since it was definitely raw blood, never boiled. “You did not just cut your finger; you chopped it off!” An Jiu frowned. “Are you hiding something from me?” Mo Sigui shook his head decisively. “You are overthinking it.” He then changed the subject. “I’ve noticed your mental state is much better; your madness seems to be healing.” If An Jiu was determined to pursue something, she would not be so easily fooled. Seeing her stern face and unblinking eyes, Mo Sigui waved his hand. “Fine! I will tell you, it is Gu Jinghong’s blood.” “Why?” An Jiu could not understand. When did Gu Jinghong donate blood to her? And why? “Because…because…you are beautiful…” Mo Sigui could not think of a reason either. He said impatiently, “You are asking me? Who am I supposed to ask? Just thinking about Gu Jinghong makes me furious! Anyway, do not stop your medication; do not give up treatment for any reason! I cannot take any more blows!” Mo Sigui had gone to great lengths to give Gu Jinghong a chance to live and had paid a considerable price, but he still died. Mo Sigui was truly unwilling to accept it. “He gave you blood. Did he not say anything?” An Jiu asked, still unwilling to give up. Mo Sigui was about to answer no, but then suddenly remembered, “He really did say something. Did you drink and chat with him? He said it was his way of thanking you. Sigh!” Mo Sigui said regretfully. “I actually really enjoy talking to people about their troubles.” Hearing this, An Jiu felt a burning sensation in her hand as she held the medicine bottle. “Gu Jinghong… how did he die?” “Anyway, he did not die from bloodletting. He could not think straight.” Mo Sigui had just finished saying that he enjoyed talking to people about their troubles. When asked to elaborate, he immediately became impatient again. “Do not think about such nonsense. You should just stay as silly and single-minded as before! Why be so sentimental?” “You seem very agitated today,” An Jiu said, looking into his eyes. “You were rejected by Lou Mingyue again, were you not? Or did she simply ignore you?” “Fine.” Caught off guard, Mo Sigui squatted down against the tent, looking dejected. “My heart is filled with medicine; I rarely think about marriage and children. Since hearing of Ningyu’s passing, I’ve completely given up on that idea. Seeing her again this time, I thought it would be nice to spend this life with her, but unfortunately, she does not share that sentiment. I… I am tired.” He had sacrificed so much time and energy to follow Lou Mingyue? He chased after her, yet was anxious about wasting time. Three to five months would be fine, but if it continued, his heart would surely be exhausted. “Unable to grasp it, unable to let it go,” Mo Sigui sighed deeply. “You each have your own things to do; you’ve taken different paths. Why force yourselves to stay together?” An Jiu could not understand. If it were someone else, they might answer because of feelings. But for Mo Sigui, besides feelings, there was also a sense of responsibility towards Lou Mingyue. They were childhood sweethearts; he had long considered her family. Watching a loved one walk down a path of no return, unable to pull her back, unable even to be there for her—it was agonizing. “Ah Jiu, what do you think I should choose?” Mo Sigui pulled the little tiger from the ground, cuddling it and smoothing its fur. “I’ve always been alone, only responsible for myself,” An Jiu finished speaking, then thought of Mei Yanran and Mei Jiu. “Maybe now I have something to hold onto, but I always act on my gut feeling. If I feel it is right, I do it.” Mo Sigui suddenly felt that being single-minded was not so bad; at least he would not be confused, always knowing which direction he was heading. Neither of them spoke. The surroundings were quiet, save for the crackling of the torches. Mo Sigui was enjoying the tranquility of the night when An Jiu’s murderous aura suddenly erupted. The two tiger cubs, who were being petted, snapped at him as if their tails had been stepped on, baring their teeth and becoming wary. He followed her cold gaze; everything seemed normal, with a squad of soldiers on night watch passing by with torches. But An Jiu did not relax at all. She had just seen a figure flash by in the flickering firelight, and for a moment, she had sensed the person’s presence. At this moment, few could hide around An Jiu, not even the Madman who had once been a master of martial arts. This time, she could not even discern the other person’s martial arts level, let alone accurately sense their aura! Mo Sigui did not ask, but simply stroked the tigers’ backs intermittently. Thinking of Chu Dingjiang, who was still healing, An Jiu immediately turned and went back into the tent. Mo Sigui also got up and followed her in. He did not see any suspicious figures, but he felt inexplicably uneasy, as if a thorn was in his side. Seeing Chu Dingjiang sitting cross-legged on the couch, An Jiu felt a sense of relief, but she dared not relax for a moment, slowly extending her mental energy outwards. Even if this did not find the hidden enemy, it would at least have a deterrent effect, preventing the other party from making a move easily.

chapters.title: Kidnapping
chapters.content: An Jiu spent the entire night on guard. She showed Chu Dingjiang’s injuries to Mo Sigui, and only after confirming he was out of danger did she feel relieved enough to continue her vigil. Mo Sigui also spent the night lounging in the main tent. At dawn, he took the two tigers to eat, while An Jiu ate some dry rations in the tent. The sun was setting. The afternoon sunlight streamed through the open tent flap onto the floor. Chu Dingjiang let out a long breath, opened his eyes, and saw An Jiu sitting beside the couch, bow in hand. A smile appeared in his eyes, and he reached out to stroke her hair. “Are you tired?” Chu Dingjiang thought, An Jiu was, after all, a woman; she needed to be pampered. Unfortunately, she shook her head, spoiling the mood, and said, “Someone infiltrated the camp last night.” Chu Dingjiang, who had been thinking of continuing their tender moments, had to temporarily abandon his romantic thoughts upon hearing this. “What happened?” An Jiu said, “I do not know their intentions. What worries me most is that I cannot ascertain their strength or even accurately track their movements.” Chu Dingjiang pondered for a moment, “Perhaps that person, like you, only possesses mental power and no martial arts.” An Jiu’s eyelids twitched, recalling the feeling of facing Wei Yuzhi face-to-face before. “Indeed.” “However, according to intelligence, Wei Yuzhi has disappeared. Last time he used his mental power and suffered a backlash, he probably will not recover so quickly.” Chu Dingjiang spoke for a long time with a dry mouth, but the young woman did not pour him a cup of water. Helpless, he got up, went to the table, poured himself a cup, and gulped it down before saying, “There are many cases like yours, but I’ve never heard of anyone whose mental power is comparable to yours.” “Could it be a Liao spy?” An Jiu asked. Chu Dingjiang said, “The Liao Kingdom is ambitious and would use any force to attack the Song Dynasty. If they had such talent, they would have used him long ago, not waited until now!” “That’s…” An Jiu had thought the same thing, but she could not think of any other explanation. “Like this Liao cavalry, most of them are not real Liao cavalry but martial artists who came for the bounty to take Ling Ziyue’s head,” Chu Dingjiang quickly figured it out. “Perhaps the talent has always been there, but he did not obey the Liao Kingdom’s orders. Now, something here has attracted him, so he accepted the Liao Kingdom’s command.” “Is it still after Ling Ziyue?” Although that person lingered near the general’s tent last night, An Jiu vaguely felt that he was not after Ling Ziyue. Chu Dingjiang laughed, “You really think I can predict the future? The opponent only showed themselves once; I have not even seen them yet. Anything you say is just guesswork.” Hearing him say that, An Jiu stopped dwelling on the matter and instead asked, “How is your injury recovery?” Chu Dingjiang’s gaze fell on the Dragon-Subduing Bow she was holding. “Once, when I was healing you, I sensed a suction force in your meridians. I did not expect this object to amplify that force. Fortunately, I left some restrictions within my body; otherwise, this would have been truly dangerous.” An Jiu pulled off the black cloth covering the Dragon-Subduing Bow, revealing its jet-black body. “This bow is indeed strange; it seems to be getting lighter and lighter. I wonder if it is related to your internal energy.” The once dark bow now gleamed coldly in the bright sunlight, and when held up to the light, the inside of the bow faintly glowed red, as if it had been forged by a fierce fire. Chu Dingjiang reached out to take the Dragon-Subduing Bow, but then heard hurried footsteps. “Ah Jiu!” Mo Sigui rushed in, followed closely by two tigers. He gasped, “I know why that person came last night! After lunch, I took Da Jiu and Xiao Yue for a walk in the camp, but when we returned, we found that the medicine boy and medicine chest were gone.” Gu Jinghong’s blood! An Jiu instantly understood his meaning. “The person is definitely still in the camp. Quickly inform General Ling,” An Jiu said immediately. Even with her level of mental power, compared to internal cultivators, her heavy body was a disadvantage. Although there were few martial artists in the military camp, everyone was very vigilant. In broad daylight, this person might be able to come and go alone, but it would be impossible for him to move freely with someone. Mo Sigui said, “I’ve already told Xiaowu to tell him only that someone infiltrated the camp, stole my medicine chest, and kidnapped my medicine boy. As for the rest, it is best not to let too many people know.” A common man was innocent, but possessing a treasure was a crime. The heart’s blood of a medicine person was extremely precious, and the outside world had long circulated rumors about its miraculous power, saying that it could not only bring the dead back to life and heal the wounded, but that consuming large quantities could even lead to ascension to immortality! Mo Sigui knew this was impossible, of course, but others did not. If the Emperor found out, he’d probably try to snatch it too. Mo Sigui had not accepted Gu Jinghong’s offered blood out of greed. Raising a medicine person was a heinous crime, and the more powerful and influential someone was, the more they had to keep it a secret. Besides, if others knew about such a valuable item, it would surely lead to a frenzy of looting, wasting years of effort and money. So even without the blood, the person could only suffer in silence, secretly sending people to steal it. Mo Sigui did not say it outright, but Chu Dingjiang guessed from their conversation, “Your future probably will not be easy.” “This time you have to protect me,” Mo Sigui said, chin raised. “If it were not for treating your dear Da Jiu, I would not have ended up being targeted.” Chu Dingjiang knew Mo Sigui’s willingness to take the risk was not entirely out of friendship but mostly out of curiosity about the medicine person’s properties, but he did not expose him. “Alright.”

chapters.title: Love or Ruthlessness
chapters.content: “Where’s the medicine?” An Jiu was still more concerned about this question. Mo Sigui flicked a stray hair from his forehead, proudly raising his chin. “How could anyone steal what’s in my possession!” “In that case, you should stay with us for now. That person will definitely come again,” An Jiu said. Mo Sigui, however, showed no sign of tension. “It’s alright. There are some pills made with Gu Jinghong’s blood in the medicine chest. Even if my master came back to life, he would not be able to tell the difference from his own heart’s blood. Only after taking them for a period of time and observing their effects can we be certain.” “Your medicine boy…” Chu Dingjiang wanted to say that the medicine boy was likely dead, but he did not say it outright. He had only intended to test Mo Sigui and was not sure about the matter. “A medicine boy assigned to the Konghe Army; whether he lives or dies depends on his own abilities.” His words implied that he did not care about the child’s life at all. Chu Dingjiang confirmed, “Really, no need to save him?” Mo Sigui hesitated for a moment, then said, “If you have time, lend a hand; if not, forget it.” He was unwilling to beg Chu Dingjiang for a mere apprentice medicine boy, owing him a favor. “Whether I have time or not is up to you,” Chu Dingjiang said, then did not ask any more questions. An Jiu, seeing Mo Sigui’s calm and almost heartless expression, concluded that he was truly so heartless. In fact, even Mo Sigui himself thought so, and he fell asleep quickly after nightfall, sleeping soundly, lost in dreams all night. He returned to the cellar in Mei Mansion. Elder Qi, covered in blood, lay before him, his aged voice ringing in his ears, each word clear and distinct. “Sigui, do not betray the word ‘love’.” “Do not betray the word ‘love’…” “Love…” Mo Sigui repeated this word over and over, his vision blurring. Once more, he saw the many trivial things about learning medicine with Elder Qi. Mo Sigui always remembered the medical teachings he received most clearly, yet these events seemed never to have been etched into his memory. However, in his dream, they were clearer than ever before. Dreams were long, but they always came to an end. In the dawn light, Elder Qi, leaning on his cane, smiled at him, his eyes filled with affection, expectation, and deep worry. “Since you are dead, rest in peace. Do not worry about anything…” Mo Sigui muttered, waking up in the blinding light. In his hazy state, he actually saw someone standing before him, the strong light shining into the tent from behind, obscuring their face. After his eyes adjusted for a moment, he could see clearly that the person before him was An Jiu. She asked curiously, “You cried.” Mo Sigui raised his hand to touch his face, and indeed, it was covered in tears. He paused for a few moments, then offered a less-than-perfect excuse: “It must be because the sun was too strong.” “Chu Dingjiang said that the Liao Kingdom is eager for Gu Jinghong’s heart’s blood. Regardless of whether the medicine in the medicine chest is genuine or not, they will use that medicine boy to threaten you. He tells you not to worry.” An Jiu became even more curious. “You really care about that medicine boy? You even cried secretly. You have not cried for Lou Mingyue.” “Stop making that exaggerated face!” Mo Sigui scoffed. “I’ve consulted quite a few psychologists, and I know a little about this,” An Jiu analyzed seriously. “If you suppress yourself like this, you will soon become depressed.” Mo Sigui glared. “Do you want me to vent like you and end up becoming a lunatic?!” Whoosh! An arrow pierced the air. It landed with a thud on the bed in front of Mo Sigui. Chu Dingjiang walked in, holding the Dragon-Subduing Bow. Although he did not speak, his eyes were full of threat. “See, you admit you’ve been suppressing your feelings,” An Jiu calmly concluded, ignoring the tense atmosphere. Mo Sigui’s face turned ashen. He abruptly stood up, glaring at the two people before him and gritting his teeth. “You two are a match made in heaven!” Equally annoying! Mo Sigui threw on his clothes and shoes and rushed out. An Jiu, oblivious to the tension, said, “You are safer with us.” “I’d be more comfortable anywhere than here!” Mo Sigui said, fastening his belt as he ran. He arrived at Lou Xiaowu’s tent. She was putting sulfur, saltpeter, and other substances into a sealed tube and firing a crossbow bolt from a distance. Boom! A loud explosion followed, and the tent filled with smoke. Mo Sigui hurriedly fled. A moment later, Lou Xiaowu emerged from the thick smoke, her face blackened, making the whites of her eyes stand out starkly. She blinked a few times, then wiped away tears with her sleeve. “Brother Mo, you got up very late today.” She exhaled a puff of smoke as she spoke. Sigh! If this were before, Mo Sigui really would not want to acknowledge Lou Xiaowu, but compared to those two annoying people, she was clearly much more endearing. People’s bottom lines were indeed gradually lowered under adversity… Mo Sigui was in a very bad mood. “Inspired by the blue-fire crossbow, I am seeing if I can make some other weapons.” Lou Xiaowu knew the power of the blue-fire crossbow well and was even more enthusiastic about it. Having witnessed its destructive power, researching swords, bows, and crossbows just did not interest her at all. She rubbed her chubby little face vigorously, sighing sadly, “If only I had a furnace for smelting iron!” Chu Dingjiang walked over. “What do you need a furnace for?” “I want to try making the crossbow smaller, the kind you can hold in your palm.” Lou Xiaowu had an innocent, baby-faced appearance; even when thinking about such profound questions, she remained naive. An Jiu peeked out from behind Chu Dingjiang. “I think your idea is excellent.” Chu Dingjiang’s tall figure completely obscured An Jiu’s silhouette. Neither Mo Sigui nor Lou Xiaowu had noticed her before, so her sudden voice startled them. Lou Xiaowu quickly recovered. “Fourteenth’s here too!” Encouraged, she instantly felt An Jiu’s image had improved tenfold. Mo Sigui turned his head away, deciding to avoid the annoyance. An Jiu walked over. “Perhaps I can help you.” Was what Lou Xiaowu had just been thinking about not firearms? An Jiu could not speak for other things, but she was thoroughly familiar with the structure and performance of all kinds of firearms. With the help of someone skilled in weaponry, perhaps she really had a chance to build one! “You guys are busy,” Chu Dingjiang said, turning his head. “Physician Mo, let’s talk.” “I have nothing to say to you,” Mo Sigui snorted. “If it is not necessary, I do not want to say anything more,” Chu Dingjiang said. Mo Sigui glanced at him but saw Chu Dingjiang turn and walk towards the back of the camp. He paused for a moment, then followed, saying as he walked, “If you dare hit me again, I will fight you to the death!” Chu Dingjiang did not turn his head. “Do not worry, I do not want to always lower myself.” “Tch!” Upon reaching an open area, Chu Dingjiang spread his mental energy around to confirm that no one was around before speaking again. “With me nearby, that person who covets the heart’s blood will be even more cautious. It will not be easy to capture him. I will pretend to leave for the next few days.”

chapters.title: Keeping the Appointment
chapters.content: “But the problem is, will your enticement not put me in danger?” Mo Sigui said, hands clasped. Chu Dingjiang raised an eyebrow. “Do you not think that person will come to kill you if we do not use this method? Do you not know how big a mess you’ve made?” Seeing Mo Sigui about to retort, Chu Dingjiang interrupted him. “Do not use our Xiao Jiu as an excuse. With your ruthless nature, only caring about medicine, you only care about your own interest, not who the patient is! I do not need to cover for you this time.” Having said that, how could Mo Sigui not understand? He hated owing favors, so he frowned. “What do you want? You’d better make it clear first. I can owe money and my life, but I do not owe favors! If anyone owes anyone anything, it is someone else owing me.” “Help me heal the scars on my face,” Chu Dingjiang said. “Just that simple?” Mo Sigui did not believe it. “Everyone is selfish. Someone else’s life might not be worth a hair on your head, let alone your face.” Chu Dingjiang had long understood Mo Sigui’s character. If he tried to coax him now, Mo Sigui would become suspicious. Instead, he would say something truthful and unpleasant to gain Mo Sigui’s trust. Mo Sigui did not deny it. “Fine, since that’s what you think, I will gladly accept it.” “How is Ah Jiu’s condition?” Chu Dingjiang asked. “What kind of illness?” Mo Sigui raised his peach blossom eyes slightly and smiled. “She has more than one or two ailments.” Chu Dingjiang said, “All of them.” “Why should I tell you?” Mo Sigui had finally found Chu Dingjiang’s weakness and was not about to give up easily. Chu Dingjiang smiled, quite nonchalantly, “I do not necessarily need to know right now.” But Mo Sigui understood the subtext: he could not resort to force now because of their cooperative relationship, but things might change after this. His face darkened slightly. He snorted and turned to leave, just as he saw Lou Xiaowu and An Jiu rushing over. Lou Xiaowu held a piece of paper in her hand. “Brother Mo, someone sent a message through an arrow.” Mo Sigui stepped forward, took the paper, glanced at it, and then turned to hand it to Chu Dingjiang. The letter demanded that Mo Sigui go alone to the appointed place, or else the medicine boy would be killed. “Hmph! Do you think I am that easy to threaten?” Mo Sigui said angrily, his tone veiled. “I will take a whole group with me and see if he will even blink after killing someone!” Chu Dingjiang used his inner force to shatter the letter, the paper scraps flying like snowflakes in the wind. “Why are you not saying anything?” Mo Sigui asked him. “My deal with you does not include the lives of others,” Chu Dingjiang said. Mo Sigui remained silent. The group returned to their respective tents. An Jiu, very enthusiastic about making firearms, went with Lou Xiaowu. Chu Dingjiang initially planned to go too, but then remembered that Ling Ziyue might need to see him, so he returned to his main tent. A short while later, Ling Ziyue indeed arrived. “How is the brave warrior’s injury?” he asked. Chu Dingjiang replied, “It’s nothing serious.” After a few casual pleasantries, Ling Ziyue revealed his purpose: “Recently, someone secretly infiltrated the camp and abducted the Divine Physician’s apprentice and medicine chest. Does this mean this person can freely enter and leave the camp?” “More or less.” Chu Dingjiang knew that the person might not truly be able to come and go as they pleased, but it was already a significant threat to the Song army; no wonder Ling Ziyue was anxious. “For him, there are no secrets here anymore.” Ling Ziyue’s expression was grave. “The Liao army will likely soon find out that the Song army lacks blue-fire crossbows.” Once the Liao army confirmed this, they would soon launch an even more ferocious attack. This was something Chu Dingjiang had anticipated. “General, you should prepare accordingly.” “What worries me is that the Liao army still has more than a dozen blue-fire crossbows.” Ling Ziyue clasped his hands in a deep salute. “Could I humbly request that you, for the sake of the people of the Song Dynasty, lend me a hand?” Chu Dingjiang quietly accepted his salute but did not definitively say anything. “I will do my best.” “Thank you very much!” Ling Ziyue cupped his hands, paused for a moment, and awkwardly coughed a few times. “I wonder… when will you be able to set off?” He was referring to taking Lou Xiaowu into the enemy camp to dismantle the crossbows. “If there are no unforeseen circumstances, we can take men to deal with the crossbows tomorrow evening,” Chu Dingjiang said. The kidnappers’ letter stipulated a time of midnight tonight. Chu Dingjiang was used to giving himself some time to deal with unforeseen circumstances. Besides, he did not need to explain his whereabouts to anyone. His willingness to tell Ling Ziyue was a sign of respect for his heroic character. “Your Excellency is very righteous,” Ling Ziyue stood up. “Then I will not disturb you any longer.” Chu Dingjiang said, “General, please return to your main tent tonight. This is a military camp; it is already inappropriate for me to have taken over.” Without waiting for Ling Ziyue’s reply, he vanished from the tent in a flash. Ling Ziyue stood with his hands behind his back, his brows furrowed in thought. After a while, he strode to the desk, picked up a pen, and wrote a memorial, suggesting that a portion of the Konghe Army be incorporated into the military camp. Ling Ziyue knew very well that once this memorial was presented to the Emperor, the fragile trust between him and the Emperor would shatter instantly. However, he could not care less. He had experienced countless battles, large and small, and had stood on the brink of death countless times. Just surviving this long was a blessing. Since he had long since become indifferent to life and death, why bother hiding anything? The Emperor would not appreciate this sentiment; it was better to risk everything and do something concrete for his country and its people. He completed the entire memorial in one go, reading it over and over again. After sealing it, he called for someone to deliver it to Bianjing. Having done all this, Ling Ziyue picked up his brush and wrote a letter: My Lady… After writing these two words, the brush paused in mid-air, ink dripping and spreading across the paper. The Ling family had three generations of renowned generals. Ling Ziyue’s grandfather had been a valiant general under the Taizu Emperor, leading troops against the Liao Kingdom even in his late sixties. His father had been wounded by an arrow in a major battle against the Liao, and after returning, the wound festered, and he died. Ling Ziyue joined the army at a young age and married at twenty. His wife was the daughter of a traveling merchant from the border region, without a distinguished family background. They enjoyed several years of loving companionship after their marriage. Later, when Ling’s mother fell critically ill, Ling Ziyue took his wife and children back to Bianjing for her funeral. At the time, the court was short of military officers for the border defense. Therefore, after Ling’s mother’s death, the Emperor posthumously conferred the title of Founding General on Ling Ziyue’s deceased grandfather and the title of Guardian General on his deceased father. Ling Ziyue was appointed General and sent to lead troops to the border, while his wife and children were detained in Bianjing to observe mourning for the Founding General, Guardian General, and their wives. This mourning lasted for many years. Ling Ziyue felt deeply sorry for his wife and children, owing them too much and wanting to say too much. How could a mere piece of paper contain it all? “My Lady, I am well now…” He still wrote a letter home as usual, only this time it was longer. He thought that even if his own life was hanging by a thread, he had to do his best to ensure the safety of his wife and children. If he could not, he could only repay all his debts in the next life. There was no need to exaggerate and make them anxious now. The moon was high in the sky. Torchlights were lit in the camp. Mo Sigui and the others left the camp together, heading towards the location agreed upon in the letter. As they sped along, An Jiu, filled with doubt, glanced at Chu Dingjiang, only to see a smile in his eyes. “Did Mo Sigui not say he did not care about the life or death of the medicine boy?” An Jiu asked in a low voice. “Saying one thing and meaning another,” Chu Dingjiang did not deliberately avoid the subject. “You can tell from his feelings for Lou Mingyue. His apparent indifference is actually a sign of deep affection. In the end, he’s the only one suffering. Lou Mingyue is determined to go down this path to the bitter end, unlike him, who is in such a difficult position.” These words struck Mo Sigui like a thunderbolt, a wake-up call. The most agonizing thing in life was the agonizing decision-making process at a crossroads. Having chosen one path, you always wonder which one would have been better. To be able to stick to one path to the end requires not only courage but also talent. Mo Sigui was far inferior to Lou Mingyue in this regard. “Ah Jiu, I will go with Mo Sigui. You hide in the shadows and wait for my signal to attack,” Chu Dingjiang instructed. “If I draw my sword, you can seize the opportunity to fire your arrow.” An Jiu thought he was shrewd and naturally had no objection to his arrangement. When they were almost at their destination, An Jiu and the others parted ways, finding a high point nearby for cover. There was a gentle slope here, which could block part of the view and provided many escape routes. The wind rustled through the waist-high grass, making the wilderness seem even more silent. After waiting for about the time it takes to drink two cups of tea, something seemed to move across the grass. Chu Dingjiang and Mo Sigui could only see the grass shaking violently, as if a wild beast was among them. An Jiu, who was lying in ambush on high ground, could clearly see that it was a person.

chapters.title: Change
chapters.content: Ten feet away from Mo Sigui, the movement ceased. A person straightened up in the grass. When An Jiu saw his face, her eyes widened slightly—it was Wei Yunshan! Actually, she had considered this possibility before, but when it became a reality, she could not help but be a little surprised. Wei Yunshan stared at Mo Sigui. “Hand over the Ghost Shadow Heart Blood.” “Did you not steal it?” Mo Sigui said sternly. “I refined all the blood into pills. Since you already have it, why did you kidnap my medicine boy?” “Hahaha! A child’s trick, you think you can fool this old man?” Wei Yunshan acted like a seasoned martial arts master, showing no remorse for stealing. “Since you are willing to risk your life for a mere medicine boy, I will value you a little. Hand over the medicine obediently, and I will not make things difficult for you.” He clapped his hands, and twenty dark figures rushed towards them. One of them carried an unconscious boy—Mo Sigui’s medicine boy. “Wei Yunshan.” Chu Dingjiang, who had been silent until now, spoke first, revealing his identity. Wei Yunshan’s expression hardened slightly. “These days, not many people recognize me. Who are you?” There were only a handful of Transcendent Realm experts in the world, and portraits of them exist in the Konghe Army. Chu Dingjiang had seen them countless times. Wei Yunshan was thinner than in the portraits, but his general features were still there. He was merely testing the waters. “Rumor has it that Wei Yunshan is a reclusive master, free from worldly desires. So he’s a traitor!” Mo Sigui felt a surge of contempt. “I have no country, no home; I only know that that blood can cure all my ailments.” Wei Yunshan had lost his patience. “In two quarters of an hour, if you do not give my order, your medicine boy will be beheaded!” “Old fool,” Mo Sigui sneered. “Do you think a medicine boy can control anyone? I came here today to see who’s so blind as to try and steal from me!” Wei Yunshan noticed the close relationship between Lou Xiaowu and Mo Sigui. He had originally intended to capture her, but Ling Ziyue’s guard was too strict. Leaving the camp alone was already difficult enough; alerting the enemy would make it even more impossible. So he captured the medicine boy instead. He had not intended to use the medicine boy to threaten Mo Sigui, but he thought the boy might know something. Unexpectedly, he had indeed gained something. “The medicine boy is nothing,” Wei Yunshan said, taking a scroll from his sleeve. “Then what about your master’s manuscript?” From the medicine boy, Wei Yunshan had learned that Mo Sigui cherished this manuscript greatly. Mo Sigui’s expression darkened further. He had only kept the manuscript on a whim; even if it were destroyed today, it would only mean losing a small part of his memory. But he could not bear to see anyone use it to threaten him. Seeing the change in his expression, Wei Yunshan was even more certain that he had found his weakness. “Senior Wei must have already presented those medicines from the medicine chest to your master, believing them to be genuine.” Chu Dingjiang suddenly interjected. “You are certain they are fake, yet you’ve deceived your superiors, harboring the intention of keeping the real medicine for yourself!” He looked at the black-clad men behind Wei Yunshan. “After he gets the medicine, will he keep you to report back?” The black-clad men, who had been like statues, made subtle movements. Seeing this, Chu Dingjiang took out a small bottle from his robes, poured out a pill, and held it between his fingers. “This is made from the medicine person’s heart’s blood. Does anyone want to test it?” A medicine person’s heart’s blood was limited. One pill was already quite potent; any martial artist would want to possess it. After a few moments of silence, one of the twenty burly men stepped forward. “Hand this over for me to examine.” Chu Dingjiang’s gaze shifted slightly. No one objected to this man taking the lead. However, Chu Dingjiang clearly saw a slight reaction from a few people the moment he stepped forward. A slight smile played on his lips behind the mask as he channeled his inner energy into the pill, flicking it with two fingers and tossing it towards the man. The man caught it; the pill was intact. Even before bringing it to his nose, the rich aroma of medicine mixed with the stench of blood instantly cleared his senses. “Elder Wei, how do you explain this?” the man demanded, holding the pill. Mo Sigui realized from the man’s words that Wei Yunshan was indeed deceiving his superiors! He could not help but glance at Chu Dingjiang, wondering how he knew. “Do not listen to his deceitful words!” Wei Yunshan sensed something was wrong. He frantically tried to devise a countermeasure while tensing his entire body, ready for a desperate fight. “These words at the last minute are nothing more than an attempt to throw us into chaos. Do not fall for it!” Though he said this, suspicion had been sown. “Return the Divine Physician’s manuscript and the apprentice, and you can have all the medicine,” Chu Dingjiang said. An Jiu noticed the medicine bottle in his hand and was somewhat surprised. When had he taken it? “You are willing to do a losing deal?” Wei Yunshan asked, unconvinced. Chu Dingjiang said, “If I am not mistaken, the medicine person was raised by the Liao Emperor. If we submit, we cannot withstand the full force of the Liao kingdom. Even if we get rid of you all today, other experts will come in a few days. This thing is good, but it is too hot to handle. We might as well exchange it for something more practical. Anyway, we’ve already gained some advantage, so why not retreat while we are ahead? What do you say, senior?” This explanation made perfect sense, but precisely because it made so much sense, Wei Yunshan felt something was off, yet he could not pinpoint anything suspicious. He paused for a moment, then raised his hand and said, “Release him.” The burly man behind him, holding the boy, threw him over. Neither Chu Dingjiang nor Mo Sigui caught him; the medicine boy landed heavily on the ground. Mo Sigui lowered his eyes to carefully observe his complexion. Seeing nothing amiss, he temporarily ignored him and simply nodded to Chu Dingjiang. Chu Dingjiang then raised his hand. “There are too many of you for us to deny it. Throw the manuscript over first, and I will serve the medicine immediately.” Wei Yunshan knew Chu Dingjiang was at the Transcendent Realm, but confident he could handle it, he simply tossed the manuscript over. Mo Sigui could tell the difference between real and fake manuscripts even with his eyes closed. After only a cursory glance, he grabbed the medicine boy and stuffed the manuscript into his pocket. Chu Dingjiang waved his hand. The group tensed up, but seeing that he had not thrown it, they were immediately annoyed. An Jiu, hiding in the shadows, saw this gesture and knew he was telling her to retreat. So she quietly retreated, circled the gentle slope, and prepared to meet Chu Dingjiang. Just as Wei Yunshan was about to erupt in anger, Chu Dingjiang suddenly threw out the medicine bottle. He was overjoyed, but to his surprise, the medicine bottle was not thrown to him but rather to a burly black-clad man on the far side.

chapters.title: The Pursuit
chapters.content: The burly black-clad man paused for a moment upon receiving the medicine bottle. When Wei Yunshan approached, he involuntarily took a half-step back. “Give me the medicine.” Wei Yunshan gritted his teeth in hatred for Chu Dingjiang. “Elder Wei, the medicine here will be given to our master anyway, so there’s no need to trouble you.” The leader of the black-clad men spoke up. Wei Yunshan’s mind raced. He suspected the medicine bottle might be a trap, but what if it was genuine? Whether the medicine was embezzled by a few scoundrels or sent to that person in Liao, it would be difficult for him to get it back! Therefore, even if there was only a 10% chance it was genuine, Wei Yunshan was unwilling to let it go. Fighting twenty men alone, though difficult, was much easier than snatching it from that person. “That kid is very cunning. I need to verify the authenticity of the medicine,” Wei Yunshan said, unwilling to give up. The leader of the black-clad men reached out. The burly black-clad man holding the medicine hesitated almost imperceptibly but still handed over the medicine bottle. The black-clad leader uncorked the bottle. Before even looking at it, he was greeted by a rich medicinal aroma, many times stronger than the single pill from before. He glanced at it and could see the pill through the narrow opening. A pill mixed with heart’s blood, it possessed a unique fragrance and color; its scent could clear the mind and senses, making it difficult to counterfeit. Someone coveted the divine medicine. After confirming this, the black-clad leader immediately stuffed the bottle into his robes. Wei Yunshan’s eyes sharpened, and his mental power erupted instantly, manipulating the weapons at the waists of over twenty men like an invisible thousand hands. … Meanwhile, Chu Dingjiang and the others calmly returned to their camp. Before Mo Sigui could catch his breath, he hurriedly questioned Chu Dingjiang and An Jiu, “You really handed over the things?!” An Jiu looked at Chu Dingjiang, reluctant to admit her oversight, but still said, “I did not even know when he took the medicine bottle.” As she spoke, she felt in her pocket and pulled out the small bottle Mo Sigui had given her the first time. She was taken aback; the bottle felt heavy, not empty. She clearly remembered there were only a few pills left. An Jiu immediately opened it and found it was full! “I poured all the pills into this bottle. The other bottle had a stronger medicinal smell, making it easier to fool people,” Chu Dingjiang said. “Wei Yunshan is facing off against twenty martial artists. Regardless of who wins or loses, the winner will still come to snatch the medicine, right?” Mo Sigui said discontentedly. “Since you are playing mind games, why leave a loose end?” “There is a loose end.” Chu Dingjiang mentally calculated the time. “I will go back and deal with it.” “I will go with you.” An Jiu grabbed his arm. “Wei Yunshan can manipulate external objects with his mental power, a thousand times stronger than Wei Yuzhi.” Last time at Piaomiao Mountain mansion, An Jiu casually tossed a feathered arrow to Wei Yunshan, perhaps believing that mental power was only for bursts and could not be sustained. Even with a sharp blade, it would not be able to saw through the cage. But this old man far exceeded her expectations. Her mental power could not even manipulate external objects yet, and she could already hold her own against eighth or ninth-level martial artists. Wei Yunshan must be terrifying. Chu Dingjiang patted her hand, intending to refuse, but seeing her gaze, he changed his mind. “Alright.” An Jiu tossed the medicine bottle to Mo Sigui. “Keep it safe.” Mo Sigui watched the two leave, hesitated for a moment, then stuffed the bottle into his pocket. Chu Dingjiang returned with An Jiu. Over there. The battle was nearing its end. Wei Yunshan had single-handedly killed twenty martial artists ranging from fifth to ninth rank, but was also seriously injured. His white beard was stained with blood. Trembling, he slumped into the grass, clutching the medicine bottle, looking as if he had aged ten years. After catching his breath, he uncorked the bottle, poured out a reddish-brown pill, sniffed it carefully, a smile appearing on his face, and put it in his mouth. The pill melted instantly in his mouth, flowing down his esophagus. Wei Yunshan sat cross-legged and circulated his internal energy. After only one cycle, he felt his injuries had healed by seventy or eighty percent, and he was overjoyed. “This place is not safe to stay in for long.” Wei Yunshan got up and headed southeast. He walked for a while, then realized someone seemed to be following him. Turning around, he saw only a thin mist shrouding the moonlight, the surrounding fields a vast expanse of white. After a brief pause, Wei Yunshan resumed his journey. Chu Dingjiang and An Jiu followed behind, and when they realized they could no longer pinpoint Wei Yunshan’s presence, they suddenly increased their speed. Excessive use of mental energy was extremely exhausting, like spending several sleepless nights thinking. Wei Yunshan was currently in this state. He had been fighting beyond his limits, constantly on guard against being followed, and was already utterly exhausted. He only realized this when Chu Dingjiang and An Jiu closed to within thirty chi. He had reigned supreme in the martial world for so many years; even being betrayed by his adopted son had never left him in such a sorry state. Wei Yunshan knew that Chu Dingjiang was a master at the Transcendent Realm. Although his foundation was not very solid, he was not someone he could easily deal with at his current level. He had to find a way to avoid him. Unfortunately, things did not go as planned. Chu Dingjiang’s lightness skill far exceeded his expectations. In the blink of an eye, he was within ten zhang. At such a short distance, if they were to face each other again, he would likely die quickly. Wei Yunshan was forced to stop. Chu Dingjiang gave him no chance to catch his breath, setting An Jiu down before leaping forward with a sword attack. After An Jiu stopped, she immediately drew her Dragon-Subduing Bow and released an arrow with mental energy. The invisible arrow was faster than Chu Dingjiang. Wei Yunshan was skilled in mental energy, and when An Jiu’s arrow was within three chi, he sensed a great threat. This double threat actually stimulated his even stronger potential. His figure instantly vanished from his original spot, reappearing ten zhang away, so fast that even An Jiu, with her keen eyesight, could only see a blur. Chu Dingjiang did not press the attack again. “It’s you, you little brat!” Wei Yunshan recognized An Jiu’s bow, remembering how he had spent over a month using his mental energy to control the arrowheads to grind the cage, nearly dying from exhaustion. “I was not mistaken,” An Jiu said. Wei Yunshan assumed she was praising him for escaping with a mere arrow and could not help but scoff arrogantly. However, she continued, “You really are no good.” A subtle shift occurred in the tense atmosphere. “Killing the two of you will not be easy,” Wei Yunshan said. “I can share the medicine with you in half.” Chu Dingjiang said, “Since I can have all of it, why should I only take half?” “So, you are deliberately trying to make things difficult for me?” Wei Yunshan’s tone was calm, but inwardly he was furious and alarmed. If Chu Dingjiang really fought to the death for the medicine, he had almost no chance of winning. What to do? Abandoning the medicine was worse than letting him die. Wei Yunshan sighed, “I never imagined that I, who has defeated countless masters in my life, would be defeated twice by such unexpected means.” The first time was by Wei Yuzhi, and the second time was today. Chu Dingjiang’s brilliance lay in the fact that his schemes were laid bare, yet he had no choice but to fall for them. “At least let me die knowing why,” Wei Yunshan said unwillingly. “I did not even distinguish the authenticity of the entire bottle of medicine; how do you know I’d fall for their trap?” “You are willing to risk your life for the Liao people, so you are probably determined to get this medicine,” Chu Dingjiang said calmly. The consumption of mental energy was not like internal energy; it was not something that could be recovered from quickly. “I see a desire in your eyes that should not belong to someone at the Transcendent Realm.” Generally, those who had reached the Transcendent Realm in mental energy were not easily swayed by emotions. Mental energy was different from internal energy. Martial arts skills could be disrupted by intense emotional fluctuations, leading to qi deviation, but they would not weaken. However, mental energy fluctuated with emotional changes. This was why martial artists must cultivate their minds first. “Why do you want this item? To restore your internal energy?” Chu Dingjiang asked. Wei Yunshan said, “I overused my mental energy, causing me to faint. When I woke up, my body had already been strengthened by drugs.” Wei Yunshan raised his hand, his sleeve slipping down to reveal a strong, powerful arm in the moonlight, its vibrant life force no less than that of someone his age. “I understand medicine, and I know that if this continues, I will explode and die within three months.” Chu Dingjiang’s brow furrowed slightly. His understanding of Wei Yunshan came entirely from the records of the Konghe Army and the legends of the martial world. Both accounts were consistent, describing Wei Yunshan as a detached person, yet this old man before him was extremely attached to life, a man with intense desires. Chu Dingjiang thought for a long time, his mind made up, and a murderous aura instantly arose around him. He transformed into a black shadow, swirling with cold light as he attacked Wei Yunshan. Wei Yunshan appeared relaxed throughout, but in reality, he was constantly on guard. Upon the attack, instead of fleeing, he raised his sword to meet it.

chapters.title: Fallen
chapters.content: The two clashed, their weapons locked in a deafening roar that seemed to shift the wind, ripples spreading across the grass around them. Wei Yunshan gritted his teeth, swallowing back the blood that welled in his throat. If he had not been so consumed by killing those twenty experts, his killing intent still burning, his fighting spirit undiminished, he might have had a chance. But now, the taut string had loosened, leaving only exhaustion. His mental energy was severely depleted, and the anxiety he felt while fleeing had rendered him powerless. What did it mean to be the mantis stalking the cicada, unaware of the oriole behind? Wei Yunshan finally understood. What frustrated him most was that he knew all along there was an oriole lurking behind him, yet he had no other choice. He also realized that Chu Dingjiang not only wanted to retrieve the medicine but also to silence them. And he, Wei Yunshan, had become prey hunted by a ferocious beast. The two had already exchanged four blows. A trickle of blood slowly flowed from Wei Yunshan’s mouth. He released his grip, spitting out the blood, his voice hoarse. “I possess a martial arts manual that will be of great use to that girl. If you release me, I will give you the manual. As for the medicine, we will split it in half; how about it?” An Jiu lacked internal energy; if she could better utilize her mental power, it would be a good path, better than pure external cultivation. Chu Dingjiang was somewhat tempted. Seeing his hesitation, Wei Yunshan immediately pulled out a medicine bottle, poured all the pills inside into his mouth, and swallowed them forcefully. “Hahaha!” he laughed maniacally. “Even if you kill me, it is useless!” Chu Dingjiang looked at him, a slow smile playing on his lips. As Wei Yunshan laughed, he suddenly felt a burning pain down his esophagus. The pain quickly spread to his abdomen, gradually feeling as if his internal organs were being crushed, causing large beads of cold sweat to appear on his forehead, his face turning pale. This medicine… only the few pills on top were real! Wei Yunshan laughed bitterly. If he had not eaten one, if he had not been truly driven to the brink… how could he have made such a foolish move! However, it was too late for him to realize this now. “I’ve been cautious my whole life, arrogantly confident in my intelligence, only to find myself utterly foolish!” Wei Yunshan’s face contorted in rage as his body turned to dust and dissipated into the mist. Wei Yunshan was always slow to realize things. Even after being imprisoned for so many years, he had not figured things out. After being schemed against by Wei Yuzhi to such an extent, his first instinct after escaping was to seek out Wei Yuzhi. Then, falling into the trap once more, he finally saw that the sickly young man was not a rabbit but a ferocious wolf. An Jiu watched coldly, finally understanding why Wei Yunshan had been so thoroughly outmaneuvered. Wei Yunshan’s stupidity truly astonished her. He seemed like a very shrewd person, having used various methods to deceive her at Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, almost succeeding. This immediately made An Jiu realize the danger. Was her IQ even lower? Seeing her grave expression, Chu Dingjiang asked, “What’s wrong?” “Chu Dingjiang, did you expect him to take that medicine?” An Jiu wanted to dissect his brain to see if it was structurally different. “It’s always better to be safe than sorry.” Chu Dingjiang pinched her cheek. “What are you thinking about?” “Wei Yunshan almost fooled me.” An Jiu had always considered herself not exceptionally intelligent but not bad either, so she was very troubled by this. “Am I really that stupid?” More stupid than Mei Jiu? “Some people are cunning but narrow-minded; they will not achieve anything great.” Chu Dingjiang comforted her. “You are different from him.” An Jiu breathed a sigh of relief. “Even this little thing makes you so worried?” Chu Dingjiang walked over and picked up the medicine bottle that had fallen into the grass.
