He put it in his pocket. “I heard that Wei Yunshan lost all his internal energy due to the schemes of his two adopted sons and was trapped in a cage. This time, Wei Yuzhi is probably involved too.” An Jiu frowned deeply, sighing deeply. “How tragic!” Chu Dingjiang reached out and pulled her close, gently patting her shoulder without speaking. The surroundings were shrouded in mist, the air thick with the smell of burning. Shortly after they left, a group of black-clad men arrived. They searched the area, and one of them said, “There’s no trace here.” “Judging from the signs of a struggle over there, it must have been Wei Yunshan’s doing,” another added. “Go back and report that Wei Yunshan is suspected of embezzling the divine medicine.” “Let’s go!” The group disappeared into the wilderness. … Late at night. The gates of Zhending Prefecture were not yet open. The guards on the city wall saw a group of people approaching the gate and immediately shouted, “Who goes there!” The group paused, and a man on horseback approached. “We are here to escort the imperial army’s provisions!” The man placed the token and documents into a bamboo basket in front of the city wall. “Strange, I have not heard of any military provisions passing through Zhending Prefecture,” the city wall commander muttered, ordering someone to pull up the basket. The garrison commander, having carefully verified the documents and tokens to be genuine, shouted, “Let them pass!” The supply convoy immediately proceeded. The commander looked down from the city wall, his gaze sweeping over the large carts of grain. Out of the corner of his eye, he noticed a soldier’s armor seemed several cun too small. Looking at the other soldiers, most appeared similarly small. His heart sank. After a moment’s hesitation, he shouted, “Immediately stop the supply convoy from entering the city!” Having shouted this, he ordered his adjutant down from the city wall. Most of the guards below the city wall had already been felled. At that moment, a deafening battle cry echoed from afar. “Liao army!” roared the men on the city wall. The commander yelled, “Prepare the crossbows!” A dense mass of Liao cavalry closed in on them in the blink of an eye, arrows raining down from the city wall. Liao cavalrymen fell continuously, but the city gates were wide open. The cavalrymen charged towards the gates recklessly, and within moments, a large number of cavalrymen poured into the city. Instantly, a great uproar erupted within the city. At Hebei Camp. “Report—!” The urgent cry startled everyone awake. The soldier, carrying a red flag, rode into the camp, dismounting just before reaching the main tent. The guards caught his weapon and let him in. The soldier knelt on one knee. “Reporting to the General, Zhending Prefecture has fallen!” Ling Ziyue abruptly stood up. Zhending Prefecture was the capital of Hebei West Circuit, with garrisons in the surrounding counties. How could the Liao army have breached it?! “Guards!” Ling Ziyue reacted immediately, “Summon all generals!” The firelight in the camp suddenly intensified. Chu Dingjiang and An Jiu sensed something was wrong as soon as they returned. Gao Dazhuang, noticing their return, said before Chu Dingjiang could ask, “The Liao army has captured Zhending Prefecture.” Chu Dingjiang’s heart skipped a beat. “What happened?” “The Liao army found the imperial grain transport convoy and followed it all the way into the city,” Gao Dazhuang said through gritted teeth. The border garrison was not limited to Ling Ziyue’s unit. Usually, provisions from the imperial court would first stop in Zhending Prefecture, be distributed, and then sent to the various garrisons. However, this time the provisions were transported separately to the Hebei camp, which, in principle, should not have gone through Zhending Prefecture.

chapters.title: Punishment
chapters.content: Therefore, either the Liao army was posing as a supply convoy, or they had genuinely intercepted the Song army’s supplies. Comparatively, the former was better. “Xiao Zhenning lost ten crossbows but did not get any benefits from General Ling, so naturally, he will try to get something back elsewhere.” Chu Dingjiang had seen countless wars of annihilation, large and small, and did not take this matter to heart. His composure also calmed Gao Dazhuang, who observed the development of the battle. At dawn, news finally arrived from the Yongning army. As Chu Dingjiang had predicted, the Liao army entered the city and swiftly burned, killed, and looted, retreating rapidly before the surrounding defenders could react. They abducted five thousand people, along with a large amount of gold, silver, and jade. Those abducted were mostly young women and children. The enraged Yongning army pursued them into Liao territory, defeating the Liao army and rescuing the abducted to return them to their owners. Upon hearing this news, several members of the Konghe Army exclaimed with delight, “This is truly gratifying!” General Yongning, Liu Yun, was the most capable military commander besides Ling Ziyue. This battle ignited the Song army’s confidence. Ling Ziyue and Liu Yun jointly submitted a memorial requesting permission to attack the Liao Kingdom. Although generals in the field were not always bound by imperial orders, the Song Dynasty had been on the defensive for years. The two generals wanted to seize this opportunity to deliver a heavy blow to the Liao army. Such a large-scale operation required the Emperor’s approval! However, this fervent enthusiasm took a turn for the worse when it reached Bianjing. The Emperor, finally relieved of his pent-up anger after the victory, was in high spirits and summoned his ministers to discuss a counterattack. However, the court officials were divided into three factions. One faction advocated defense and strongly opposed Ling Ziyue and Liu Yun’s approach, not only disagreeing with the war but also subtly implying that Ling Ziyue and Liu Yun were colluding. Not only the Hebei West Circuit, but the entire north was under the control of these two. One faction advocated for action, believing that the Song Dynasty, as a superior nation, could not always tolerate and yield; it was time to show its power. Another faction maintained a neutral stance. The Emperor’s initial enthusiasm, dampened by a sudden setback, gradually cooled, and his paranoia returned. At this time, someone impeached Liu Yun. Firstly, for neglecting defenses, allowing the Liao army to plunder Zhending Prefecture; secondly, for leading a large army into Liao territory without authorization and abandoning his post. Others defended him, arguing that the Yongning Army’s primary duty was to guard the Zhending Prefecture area and that Liu Yun’s pursuit of the Liao army after its plunder was simply fulfilling his duty. In the study, it was so quiet you could hear a pin drop. Incense smoke curled from the burner. A middle-aged man in a yellow robe sat with his hands clasped and eyes closed before his desk. A memorial lay open on the table—the one Ling Ziyue had requested for grain supplies. A moment later… He slowly opened his eyes, raised his hand to the memorial, and tapped his fingers lightly. “Go and summon the Grand Tutor, the Grand Commandant, the Chancellor, and the Privy Councilor.” “Yes,” the eunuch bowed and withdrew. A short while later, the four ministers arrived. “Sit,” the Emperor said. “Thank you for the seats, Your Majesty.” The four bowed and took their seats. The Emperor said, “Take General Ling’s memorials to the four ministers.” “Yes,” the eunuch went to retrieve the memorials from the table and handed them to the Grand Tutor, who sat at the head of the left. After the four had read them in turn, the Emperor finally spoke, “What do you four ministers think of General Ling’s and General Liu’s joint attack on the Liao Kingdom?” One was a memorial urging for grain supplies; the other was about attacking the Liao Kingdom—fundamentally unrelated matters. What did putting them together mean? These men were all shrewd old men; until they had fully grasped the situation, they remained silent. Seeing no one answer, the Emperor called upon Hua. “Prime Minister Hua, you speak first.” Hua rose and said, “The Great Song is a celestial empire; whether or not to fight is entirely up to Your Majesty’s decision. I will obey Your Majesty’s will.” In truth, he did not control the military; he was merely offering his opinion. Besides, the Emperor had summoned them today not simply to discuss whether or not to fight, but also clearly showed his dissatisfaction with Ling Ziyue. Prime Minister Hua was well aware that he was also on the suspect list, and it was best to avoid giving his opinion in such matters. The Emperor remained unmoved, saying, “Sit down and speak. What’s the tension?” The Emperor was generally unpredictable, but his composure was exceptional; he rarely showed his emotions. The Grand Commandant leaned slightly forward, then suddenly changed the subject. “Your Majesty, General Liu has won a battle, but it was due to his own negligence. We cannot ignore this simply because of his military achievements. I believe he should be punished.” The Emperor was silent for a moment, then asked, “Grand Commandant, what do you think he should be punished for?” Hearing the tone, everyone immediately understood that the Emperor wanted to deal with an internal problem first. This internal problem was not Liu Yun, but Ling Ziyue. There was no immediate replacement for Ling Ziyue, so the punishment of Liu Yun was merely a warning to others. Prime Minister Hua thought that the Emperor trusted Liu Yun relatively much and that he was the only suitable replacement for Ling Ziyue; the Emperor probably did not really intend to punish him… “This…” The Grand Commandant had not decided yet. The Grand Tutor said, “I believe that General Liu’s victory has boosted the morale of the border troops. He should not be punished lightly, lest it dampen their spirits.” The Emperor frowned slightly. The Grand Tutor abruptly changed the subject. “However, as the Grand Commandant said, General Liu has made a mistake. Your Majesty should summon him back to the capital, reprimand him in person, and punish him by withholding his salary.” “Absolutely not!” the Privy Councilor exclaimed. “Your Majesty, the border defense cannot be without its generals for even a moment. This is a critical time of war; you absolutely cannot summon General Liu back to court!” The room fell silent. “This cannot be done, that cannot be done; truly, even I am helpless when a general is in the field!” the Emperor sighed. “You may all return. Think it over carefully, and come up with a solution for me tomorrow!” The four men rose, bowed, and withdrew one after another. The study fell silent again. The Emperor took out a secret letter, read it for a while, and even dismissed his personal eunuchs. “Come out.” As soon as the Emperor finished speaking, two black-clad men descended from the rafters. “I’ve heard that the Konghe Army has done a great deal for General Ling this time,” the Emperor said, coldly looking at the gaunt black-clad man at the head. “Your Majesty, please forgive me.” He immediately knelt on one knee. “The Konghe Army is loyal to Your Majesty and to the Great Song Dynasty. Their efforts were also in service of Your Majesty.” The other black-clad man behind him also knelt. “Rise. I was merely asking casually.” The Emperor stroked the secret letter and said, “Recall them and incorporate them into the newly established Dragon Martial Guards. From now on, they will directly obey my orders. The existing Dragon Martial Guards will be renamed the Konghe Guard.” “Yes!” the black-clad man acknowledged the order. “General Ling suggested incorporating the Konghe Army into the army. What do you think?” the Emperor suddenly asked. If they could be incorporated into the army, their clandestine lives would end. Even if they died on the battlefield, at least they could live like human beings! The black-clad man kept his eyes downcast, unable to see the Emperor’s expression, but he knew his mood was definitely not good.

chapters.title: Making an Example
chapters.content: The allure of regaining sight was immense! Yet he could not show the slightest desire. “The Konghe Army swears to be loyal only to His Majesty and obey only His Majesty’s decrees!” His resounding words eased the Emperor’s brow, and a smile finally appeared on his face. “Go, immediately recall the Konghe Army from Hebei.” “Yes!” The black-clad man bowed and vanished. The Emperor fell into deep thought. A full hour passed before he spoke. “Someone, come here.” A eunuch entered with hurried, light steps, bowing. “This servant is here.” “Prepare the hot spring bath,” the Emperor said. This was to clear his mind and seek enlightenment. The eunuch, accustomed to this, had already ordered everything prepared. He came out to have someone prepare and serve him, stood at the door for the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, then turned back into the room, respectfully saying, “Your Majesty, the bath is ready.” The Emperor rose and moved to the Yuquan Palace. After a fragrant bath, the Emperor changed into a loose white silk robe and sat in the pavilion, his hair disheveled. A eunuch brought in a tray with an exquisite box made of gilded and jade-inlaid golden nanmu wood, its surface carved with lifelike images of immortals flying in the sun. “Your Majesty,” the eunuch said, “this is a golden elixir newly delivered by the Immortal yesterday.” He opened the box, revealing six pills radiating a warm, golden glow, hidden beneath the black silk. The Emperor picked one up and placed it in his mouth. The eunuch closed the box, put it away, and stood by, hands at his sides. Seeing the Emperor begin to sweat, he softly asked, “Your Majesty, would you like to practice dual cultivation today?” “Hmm,” the Emperor hummed through his nose. The eunuch gestured for someone to immediately summon Consort Yu. If the Emperor had not specified his dual cultivation partner beforehand, he would not have bothered choosing anyone at this time. Everything was arranged by the eunuchs. Consorts desiring sons would bribe the eunuchs to conceive a child. Otherwise, those high-ranking concubines would not be willing to make love in the pavilion in broad daylight. The eunuchs were also adept at striking a balance. They would not arrange for the concubines to do it every time. On occasional instances, the Emperor would not blame them, because compared to those female Shadows who treated it like torture, the beauties in the harem were more sophisticated and knew how to please. Cranes strolled in the courtyard, a gentle breeze rippled across the lotus pond, and half-open white lotuses stood gracefully among the green canopies, partially obscuring the middle-aged man in white in the pavilion. At first glance, he truly appeared somewhat ethereal. A short while later, a woman in flowing white robes came, parting the flowers and willows, and bowed gracefully at the foot of the pavilion. “Your Majesty.” The Emperor slightly opened his eyes. A sudden gust of wind lifted the ribbons on her arms, causing her black hair to flutter. Her beautiful face was pure and shy; for a moment, he seemed to see a fairy. Consort Yu slightly raised her eyes, not missing the amazement in his eyes. So, emboldened, she quietly removed her shoes and walked barefoot into the pavilion. Her snow-white feet were faintly visible beneath her white gauze skirt, unadorned and alluring. Seeing this, the eunuch ordered the white gauze covering the pavilion to be lowered, then sent everyone to the distant corridor to await orders, while he himself remained at the foot of the steps outside the pavilion, ready to act at any moment. From noon until sunset, the ordeal lasted for over two hours. The eunuch secretly wiped his sweat, wondering if it was the extraordinary efficacy of the elixir presented by the Immortal or if Consort Yu’s beauty was simply intoxicating! But Consort Yu had prepared for so long and came so many times; if she still could not conceive, it would truly be bad luck, and he could not arrange for her to come again… The Emperor’s harem was never short of beauties, but Consort Yu’s looks could not compare to the Imperial Concubine or the other delicate beauties, and therefore, she was usually not favored. However, to the eunuch’s surprise, although Consort Yu still had no children, she managed a remarkable turnaround thanks to her newfound beauty and unexpectedly gained the Emperor’s favor! The Imperial Concubine, upon learning this, was furious but powerless. She could only order people to research Taoist scriptures and rack her brains to dress up as a fairy. Within the palace, intrigue and scheming for the Emperor’s favor played out constantly, all vying to become immortals. Meanwhile, on the border, Ling Ziyue and Liu Yun waited anxiously for over half a month, only to receive an imperial edict reprimanding Liu Yun for negligence and dereliction of duty! Liu Yun’s reprimand caused an uproar even among the people of Zhending Prefecture. But what Liu Yun cared about most was not the reprimand itself but the impending deduction of a year’s salary! Since the family had not divided the property, Liu Yun had four brothers, an elderly grandmother still alive, two sons, a daughter, and several grandchildren. His family was large and prosperous, and while they maintained a respectable appearance, they lived a frugal life in private. He knew all this. Normally, while in the army, he ate only military rations, his undergarments patched and mended repeatedly. When his family sent him clothes, he would write that he was wearing armor and that the court also provided such undergarments. Even if new clothes were made, he had no chance to wear them; every six months, he would have some smaller garments made and sent. Military generals leading troops in the field, with frequent border wars, had no other way to earn money. Liu Yun was an honest official, never accepting bribes or extorting money from the people. He supported his large family in the capital solely on his salary and estates! Although he was not completely destitute, this year’s salary deduction would truly be a financial blow to his entire family. The Emperor was making an example of him; Ling Ziyue knew this all too well, and his initial enthusiasm cooled considerably. If he had not agreed to join forces with Liu Yun to attack Liao, perhaps the Emperor would not have punished him. Ling Ziyue’s family was smaller, and his salary was higher than Liu Yun’s. However, given the current situation, he feared that offering assistance would only cause Liu Yun unnecessary trouble, so he decided against it. Seven or eight days passed, and Ling Ziyue noticed that the Konghe Army had disappeared. On the table lay the blue-fire crossbow made by Lou Xiaowu. It was obvious they had been summoned back by the Emperor. His sudden change in attitude had pushed the Emperor to his limit, but what could he do? He was still serving as a general, was he not? Military rations arrived several times faster than when he had to beg and plead! Only then did Ling Ziyue fully understand Chu Dingjiang’s meaning. In the current state of the Song Dynasty, protecting the country and being loyal to the Emperor could not coexist. If he were to blindly remain loyal, the purpose of defending the borders would be minimal. The Liao Kingdom had been invading annually, and he was not without opportunities to launch offensives. However, the court was afraid of being defeated and would not allow him to send troops, fearing further reparations after a defeat. Now that the Emperor could not touch him, he could abandon his reputation and do something practical for the Song Dynasty and its people. Doing so might lead to a tragic end, and his disloyalty might be etched in history, but his burning ambition could no longer tolerate waiting for the Liao people to come and burn, kill, and plunder every year! In the darkness. A group of black-clad men rode to the post station for a short rest. After changing horses, everyone stood in the courtyard. Lou Xiaowu complained, “We said we did not want to come, but they forced us. We came and were sent back without doing anything… Is this not just playing with us?” “Lord Chu, is it really all right not to dismantle the other dozen or so blue-fire crossbows?” Gao Dazhuang asked. “If General Ling is determined, not even a dozen or a hundred crossbows could stop him,” Chu Dingjiang said, confident in Ling Ziyue. Before leaving, he had left the crossbows in the camp. He only had a basic understanding of weaponry, but after watching Lou Xiaowu handle them, he roughly knew their structure and weaknesses. He assumed Ling Ziyue knew them too, so why worry about finding a solution? Everything in this world was wondrous, like a giant game of Weiqi. Strengths and weaknesses depended on the times and circumstances. No piece could become invincible without reason; even the strongest position had its weaknesses. It waxed and waned. Chu Dingjiang smiled. Sometimes, the Daoist saying made a lot of sense. He came to his senses and saw An Jiu squatting on the ground, tossing the tiger named Da Jiu. The two tigers were not growing fast, but they were very sturdy. Their silly, cute faces never became more imposing despite their size. Sometimes, their arrogance even paled in comparison to that of a cat. An Jiu thought to herself that Mo Sigui’s medicine must have made them stupid. She resolved to eat more and take less medicine from now on. Otherwise, being “physically strong but mentally disabled” would be really bad. “My Lord, after we return to the capital, will we still be doing our old work?” Li Qingzhi was very unwilling. He did not want to go back to his old life, different from his time in the military camp. If one day he could don armor and fight on the battlefield, even dying in battle would be exhilarating. “What’s wrong with doing our old work?” Gao Dazhuang said irritably. Li Qingzhi hung his head and squeezed out a word: “Frustrated.” “What kind of life is not frustrating? Did you not see Liu Yun being fined even after winning a battle? Did you not see Ling Ziyue having to act like a grandson to get military rations!” Gao Dazhuang tapped his head hard with his orchid-like fingers. “You should be content!” No one spoke again. After eating their rations and resting for half an hour, they continued their journey. When they left Bianjing, it was a cool night with misty spray; upon their return, it was a warm, damp, rainy night. The group returned to the Konghe Army, whereupon someone immediately led them into the palace. After Gu Jinghong’s death, the rebuilt Dragon Martial Guards personnel were secretly summoned to the palace. Unlike the other Shadow Guard units, the Dragon Martial Guards were positioned closer to the Emperor to protect him. An Jiu felt conflicted when she learned she had been assigned to the Dragon Martial Guards. She would soon see Mei Yanran, but she was not overly excited, as she was not prepared to face Mei Yanran or handle their relationship… “Go in and behave properly. The Emperor is inside!” the black-clad man leading the way whispered a warning. Only then did the group realize their journey was to meet the Emperor. They had rushed back, disheveled and exhausted, and hastily entered the main hall. An Jiu saw a middle-aged man on the throne drinking tea. He had a neatly trimmed beard and a lean face. He was not as imposing as she had imagined; instead, his expression was gentle and approachable. “Long live the Emperor!” Gao Dazhuang led the way, kneeling. The others followed suit, shouting “Long live the Emperor!” and kneeling as well. The Emperor paused, slowly setting down his teacup. “Gao Yuanxin?” Gao Yuanxin was Gao Dazhuang’s later name, and few people called him that. Gao Dazhuang bowed his head and said, “Yes, Your Majesty.” “You’ve returned,” The Emperor smiled, stepping down from the throne and helping him up. “You were already remarkable in the Konghe Army, and this time you’ve truly impressed everyone at the border. I am very pleased.”

chapters.title: Appearance
chapters.content: “Serving Your Majesty, I will naturally give my all.” Gao Dazhuang’s words implied that he was taking all the credit for himself. Li Qingzhi and the others were immediately dissatisfied. Without their life-and-death struggles, how could they have achieved such remarkable success? The Emperor glanced at the group, then said to Gao Dazhuang, “From now on, you will remain by my side. The others will continue to obey your orders.” “Your subordinate obeys.” Gao Dazhuang did not speak further but simply pulled off his mask, allowing the Emperor to see his face clearly. This was customary; the Emperor could not be unaware of the appearance of his close guards. Sui Yuntong, Li Qingzhi, Qiu Yuntong, and Sun Dixian also revealed their true faces one after another. Lou Mingyue hesitated for a moment, then removed her veil. The rush through the rainy night had left her disheveled; strands of her dark hair still clung to her forehead, threatening to fall with raindrops. Her sharply angled eyebrows added to her beauty, yet she also possessed a heroic air. Gao Dazhuang remained calm. He was not worried, because although Lou Mingyue was stunningly beautiful, she was not the Emperor’s type, unless the Emperor’s taste suddenly changed. Over there, when An Jiu removed her veil, Gao Dazhuang’s gaze could not help but flicker. Seeing that she still wore a human skin mask, he felt slightly relieved, hoping the girl was not too honest and would remove the mask. The Emperor looked around and nodded slightly. “Withdraw.” Gao Dazhuang breathed a barely perceptible sigh of relief and immediately led the way away. The Emperor returned to his seat, looking at the documents laid out before him, and suddenly said, “Halt!” Gao Dazhuang stopped abruptly, turned, and bowed. “Your Majesty.” The Emperor spread out the documents for several people, his cold gaze sweeping over them, lingering between An Jiu and Sui Yuntong, finally settling on An Jiu. “How dare you not show your true face to the Emperor!” The documents stated three men and three women, plus Gao Dazhuang, who was neither male nor female. However, there were now four men and two women. Clearly, one was a woman disguised as a man. Gao Dazhuang glanced at An Jiu, feigning surprise, and knelt with a thud. “Your Majesty, please calm down! This child is meeting you for the first time; she’s ignorant.” He then lowered his head and whispered a reprimand, “Quickly remove the mask!” Several people slowly knelt. An Jiu took out a bottle of oil from her bosom, applied it to the edge of the mask, and after two breaths, removed the human skin mask. Below the mask was an exquisitely beautiful face. The face was small and delicate, its paleness, due to the long period of covering, giving it a slightly sickly-white appearance. When her eyes were lowered, she possessed a captivating charm; any more color would be too gaudy and any less too pale. The Emperor stared at this face for several breaths before recovering. “Mei family?” “Yes,” An Jiu replied. Over the years, more than one woman from the Mei family had accompanied the Emperor. Their appearances were all so captivating. A few days ago, a woman from the Imperial Guard was betrothed to Hua Rongtian, and the Emperor was still somewhat reluctant to part with her. Now, another one had been added… “Your Majesty, Fourteenth Young Lady is an exceptional archer. In this border battle, she turned the tide, reversing the tide of war and forcing the Liao army to retreat.” Gao Dazhuang did not need to look at the Emperor’s expression to know what he was thinking. “The Mei family has just suffered a severe injury. Fourteenth Young Lady was distracted and unintentionally offended you. I implore Your Majesty to punish her leniently.” The Emperor, hearing his obvious favoritism, could not help but laugh. “Gao Yuanxin, you still cannot handle things properly.” His gaze lingered on An Jiu’s face for a few moments. “Leave.” Most men liked beautiful women, but the Emperor was more obsessed with seeking immortality and enlightenment. Beautiful women were merely embellishments. He sensed resistance, but he would not force her into bed. Besides, the records stated that Fourteenth Young Lady was purely an external cultivator, lacking internal strength, which was of no benefit to cultivation. As for mere beauty, there were plenty in the harem. Several people withdrew, and a black-clad man floated down from the roof beam, appearing before them and handing a bundle to Gao Dazhuang. “The commander has ordered that starting tomorrow, you, Lord Gao, will have to disguise yourself as a eunuch. Do a good job, and soon Huang Bandang will take you as his apprentice.” Huang Bandang was the Emperor’s personal eunuch. His surname was Huang, and he had served the Emperor since childhood, practically a playmate. The Emperor privately called him Bandang. Serving the Emperor from childhood was an honor for a eunuch, and he liked being called Huang Bandang, so most people with a little official rank addressed him that way. Gao Dazhuang felt a bitter taste in his mouth, and the bundle in his hands felt incredibly heavy. Without his manhood, he was bound to end up like this sooner or later! At least this was a pretty high starting point! Gao Dazhuang mocked himself inwardly. “Yes,” he replied. The black-clad man said, “I am Xuan Liu. If you need anything in the future, come find me.” He tossed a map of the palace to several men. “The red dots are places His Majesty frequents. The purple dotted lines mark your assigned areas. Whenever His Majesty enters your assigned area, you must absolutely guarantee his safety! But do not look at what you should not look at, and do not listen to what you should not listen to! The black dots are the living quarters of the Dragon Martial Guards. As for the shift schedule, you can discuss it yourselves and report back to me. If there are any oversights on any day, the top officials will hold the responsible personnel accountable!” “Yes!” the men replied in unison. Xuan Liu handed them a bell. “The rules for choosing living quarters are the same as in the Konghe Army.” Gao Dazhuang glanced at it enviously. He had never found the bell so adorable! As the saying goes, if you were going to play a part, you had to go all the way. He was playing a eunuch, and from now on, he would have to live with eunuchs, never again enjoying time alone. Having received the map, they went to find their living quarters, at least to change their soaking wet clothes. An Jiu was the first to arrive. The Dragon Martial Guards’ living quarters were in a courtyard within the Cold Palace, a neat, square layout with many rooms but no clear hierarchy; they were all roughly the same size and simply furnished—a bed, a table—reminding An Jiu of her former dormitory within the organization. A fence surrounded the courtyard, but it was overgrown with weeds. An Jiu looked around and found all the rooms empty, realizing this was reserved for their group. She chose a room with an east-facing window and hung a bell on the door. As soon as An Jiu pushed open the door, she heard singing coming from not far away. Having spent time in a mental hospital, she could sense the neuroticism hidden beneath the beautiful singing; the singer was definitely not normal. After a short while, the singing abruptly stopped halfway through, and the woman shouted joyfully, “Your Majesty! Your Majesty!” An Jiu hummed the tune she had just heard and looked around the room. The furniture in the room was all new, seemingly freshly cleaned, and not very dusty. A box sat by the bedside, filled with clothes and shoes. A moment later, Lou Mingyue and the others entered the courtyard. After choosing their rooms, Sui Yuntong called everyone out to discuss the shift arrangements. “I, Fourteenth Young Lady, and Li Qingzhi will go together; Second Young Lady Lou, Qiu Yuntong, and Sun Dixian will go together,” Sui Yuntong said, knowing this group never voiced their opinions, and took it upon himself to divide the rooms. “Does anyone have any objections?”

chapters.title: The Uncle’s Counterattack
chapters.content: As expected, no one objected, and the shift work was happily decided. Watching everyone carefreely retreat to their rooms, Sui Yuntong resigned herself to her role as a maid and went to inform Xuan Liu of the assignment list. The treatment as a guard in the palace was truly excellent. Shifts were twelve hours long, and when not on duty, they had free time. Even leaving the palace was no problem with Gao Dazhuang’s permission! Due to their meritorious service at the border, the Emperor granted them a half-month rest. After half a month, Lou Mingyue’s team went on duty first, while An Jiu’s team rested in their quarters. There were even fewer people in the quarters, so Sui Yuntong encouraged An Jiu and Li Qingzhi to go out for a stroll. Li Qingzhi was eager to go, and An Jiu thought it would be nice to go out, so they immediately agreed. The three of them went to find Gao Dazhuang. Gao Dazhuang was assigned to Gushe Palace, a place bestowed upon Consort Yu by the Emperor. Here, he was merely a lowly eunuch. In the palace, all eunuchs started as “junior eunuchs,” and those with merit would be promoted to “eunuch palace attendants.” Consort Yu was to move into Gushe Palace soon, and the palace was still in the process of being hastily prepared. People were coming and going, and all the eunuchs looked almost identical. An Jiu and her two companions finally managed to find Gao Dazhuang. This was the first time they had seen Gao Dazhuang’s face. He was not as strikingly handsome as they had imagined; instead, he was quite refined, appearing to be only sixteen or seventeen years old. The three crouched in the shadows. Li Qingzhi whispered, “My Lord, are you wearing a mask?” An Jiu thought to herself, “He’s already so old; can he not at least disguise himself?” Gao Dazhuang’s ears twitched slightly. Hearing Li Qingzhi’s words, he grabbed a broom and swept haphazardly, avoiding people to a secluded spot. “Come out.” The three climbed over the wall and landed in front of him. “What is it?” he asked. Seeing Gao Dazhuang working so hard, Sui Yuntong knew he was definitely upset and was carefully considering how to speak. Li Qingzhi then said, “My Lord, we need to go out for a bit.” Gao Dazhuang raised his narrow eyes. “Go out for what?” “Go for a stroll!” “Go buy some things.” Li Qingzhi and Sui Yuntong said simultaneously. Sui Yuntong turned his face away. Seeing this, Li Qingzhi realized he had misspoke and quickly tried to salvage the situation: “Yes, yes, we are going out to buy some things and take a stroll.” “Get back here, all of you!” Gao Dazhuang roared in a low voice, throwing his broom heavily to the ground. “He’s really getting worse with age!” The last sentence was unclear whether he was referring to himself or the three of them. “I will not forget to bring you something good to eat,” An Jiu said simply. Gao Dazhuang, hands on his hips, was panting heavily with anger. “Do I really owe you a bite to eat?!” “Of course, the lord has plenty to eat and drink,” Sui Yuntong interrupted An Jiu, seeing she was about to speak again. “Fourteenth Young Lady means that we’d like to offer you some food from our trip.” Gao Dazhuang felt a little better, calming down before saying, “I want fried noodles from Ximen Liao Shi, no scallions. Extra chili.” He pulled a small, finger-sized stamp from his pocket. “Hold out your hands!” The three of them unfastened their hand guards and opened their palms. Gao Dazhuang stamped one on each palm. “Keep them safe; do not let them fade. Otherwise, do not blame me if you cannot get back in.” “Can you not think of a more reliable way?” An Jiu said disdainfully. “You only know how to make things convenient for yourself!” The Dragon Martial Guards was not just one team; each team had different passes. These were all determined by the leader and reported to their superiors. Gao Dazhuang picked up a broom and started hitting An Jiu. “Gao Dazhuang!” a shrill voice cried out from the front hall, filled with anger. Gao Dazhuang froze, suppressing all his arrogance. He glared fiercely at An Jiu, then grabbed the broom and scurried to the front hall. Three onlookers, always eager for a good show, followed him. They saw a eunuch repeatedly slapping Gao Dazhuang with a whisk. “You little brat! You’ve been slacking off in the blink of an eye! Who gave you the audacity? Who gave you the audacity? Today you will lick the entire ground of Gushe Palace clean, even if you have to!” Gao Dazhuang, true to form, looked timid and cowered, head bowed as the eunuch whipped him. “My Lord has it tough,” Li Qingzhi sighed. “We must bring him two bowls of noodles.” The three slipped away, went back to change clothes, disguised themselves slightly, and, relying on the red mark on their palms, successfully left the palace. Once outside, the three parted ways to attend to their own business. An Jiu had just reached Yu Street when she recognized a familiar presence. Looking up, she saw a young man sitting in a teahouse, dressed in a dark blue, wide-sleeved robe. One arm rested on the windowsill, the slightly taut silk outlining his broad shoulders and arm. His slender fingers held a blue-and-white porcelain cup, wisps of steam rising from its rim, mingling with the morning light and softening the sharp lines of his handsome face. He looked down at her, a smile playing on his lips. An Jiu hesitated for a moment, then strode into the teahouse, appearing before him in an instant. He set down his teacup and smiled. “Do you not recognize me?” “Chu Dingjiang,” An Jiu said softly. Chu Dingjiang’s smile deepened. “Come and sit down.” An Jiu finally believed he had once been a noble young master. He was indeed very polite, but his every move was unlike the restrained and weak manners of Song Dynasty scholars; instead, he possessed a noble air mixed with a free and unrestrained spirit, attracting many sidelong glances. “Have not had breakfast yet?” Chu Dingjiang called over an attendant and then ordered her a basket of steamed buns, several side dishes, and a bowl of congee. Once breakfast was served, Chu Dingjiang picked up chopsticks and handed them to her. An Jiu raised her hand, not to take the chopsticks, but instead reached out and pinched his cheek, pulling hard. Looking at the red mark on his face, she muttered, “It’s really true?” Mo Sigui’s medical skills were truly impressive; such a large scar had been smoothed out so quickly. Chu Dingjiang shoved the chopsticks into her hand. “So surprised?” “Yes, it feels like I’ve become a different person.” An Jiu picked up a steamed bun and stuffed it into her mouth. “How did you know I would come out today?” Chu Dingjiang smiled inscrutably. An Jiu suddenly understood. “It’s Sui Yuntong.” An Jiu did not know when Chu Dingjiang had managed to win over Sui Yuntong, making him willing to work for him. His methods were truly discreet and efficient. “Hmm,” Chu Dingjiang said, “Eat.” His actions were the same as before; only his clothes had changed, the scars and beard were gone, and his entire demeanor had undergone a complete transformation. An Jiu, sitting opposite him, felt a sense of unreality. After breakfast, the two went out for a stroll together. An Jiu was still dressed as a boy, in a drab gray outfit, walking beside Chu Dingjiang like his servant. “Ah Jiu, go change your clothes; let’s go to the outskirts,” Chu Dingjiang said. Chu Dingjiang was handsome, tall and strong, with a unique air about him. He already attracted attention on the street, and with her dressed as a servant walking beside him, everyone turned to look. An Jiu was not used to being the center of attention, so she said, “Alright.” However, she did not understand why they needed to change clothes specifically for going to the outskirts, so she leaned closer to him and whispered, “Are we being followed?” Chu Dingjiang, seeing her serious expression, found it amusing and nodded solemnly. The two quickened their pace and entered a clothing store. Chu Dingjiang, feigning profundity, glanced around the storeroom and selected a moon-white women’s dress for her to change into. The shopkeeper gave them a strange look, but Chu Dingjiang pretended not to notice, tossing a sum of silver on the table. “Find someone to style her hair like a woman; this is the payment.” The shopkeeper took the money, his mind filled with all sorts of ulterior motives, all things shady. He gave Chu Dingjiang an “I understand” look and went to the back to call his wife to style the young man’s hair, now dressed as a woman. An Jiu’s features were already rather gentle, and with the women’s clothing and hairstyle, she was passable. After getting dressed, the two secretly slipped out of the shop through the back door and rented a carriage to leave the city. “Why did you not change?” An Jiu had been suspicious for a while. She had been carefully checking with her mental energy but had not found anyone following her or felt any threat. Chu Dingjiang took out a small bottle of oil and gently wiped her face before removing the mask. “You lied to me,” An Jiu said coldly. Chu Dingjiang had only meant it as a joke, but seeing her genuine anger, he could only say, “Do not be angry. I was just teasing you because I found you amusing. It is my fault; you can punish me as you see fit.” His quick admission of wrongdoing put An Jiu in a dilemma. Continuing to keep a cold face seemed petty, but letting it go felt like swallowing her anger. “I will write down the bill first, and I will think about it,” An Jiu said sternly. The carriage traveled out of the city and stopped at a pear orchard. At this time of year, the pear blossoms were long gone, and most of the pears were still green, offering nothing interesting. Passing through the pear orchard, a vast expanse of wildflowers came into view—white, yellow, and purple. Beside a shimmering stream stood a thatched cottage, its path completely hidden by wildflowers, as if it had been uninhabited for a long time. An Jiu’s mood instantly lifted. The world was vast, and there was no one else around. Chu Dingjiang put his arm around her waist, leaping across the flowers, his ribbons billowing in the air, and the two of them landed lightly in front of the cottage, like celestial beings. “I prepared some things last night,” Chu Dingjiang said, pushing open the door and carrying two baskets out of the cottage. He loosened his belt, rolled up his sleeves to reveal his strong arms, and smiled at An Jiu. “A suckling pig was slaughtered this morning; it will make a good roast for lunch.” An Jiu looked at him, somewhat dazed, feeling as if today’s beauty was a fragile dream. She had harbored some fantasies about a beautiful life, filled with blue skies and white clouds, wildflowers, fruits and peaches, horses and sheep, but she had never imagined having a man. But everything she saw now made her think that having a man would not be so bad; after all, Chu Dingjiang and her father were completely different kinds of people. “What are you standing there for? Come here!” Chu Dingjiang held a slaughtered piglet in his hand, his robes tied up, looking very casual. An Jiu regained a sense of familiarity. She ran over, a slight smile on her face. “You are better off this slovenly way. That kind of effeminate dressing does not suit you.” “…”

chapters.title: Romantic Killer
chapters.content: Chu Dingjiang shook his head helplessly, securing the suckling pig to the iron fork. Having prepared everything, Chu Dingjiang saw her idly standing there and ordered, “Take those vegetables and mushrooms to wash.” An Jiu shook her head, holding out her palm with the stamp on it to him. “If I lose it, I will not be able to go back.” Chu Dingjiang glanced at it and laughed, “Gao Dazhuang certainly knows how to make things difficult for people.” Gao Dazhuang only had a small stamp, very easy to hide, but it was a real hassle for these travelers. Even a little sweat would blur the stamp, making it very difficult to protect. Chu Dingjiang brushed a thin layer of oil on the suckling pig, lit a fire, and then took a basket of mushrooms to wash. When he returned, he saw An Jiu lying in the grass, hands clasped, acting like a big shot. An Jiu grinned when she saw him wet. As Chu Dingjiang approached, she said regretfully, “Actually, I quite like playing in the water too.” It sounded like he was always playing! Chu Dingjiang’s hands were still wet, and he took the opportunity to vigorously shake them at her. She did not even flinch, which completely killed his interest in teasing her. He took a cleaned pheasant from the basket, mixed chestnuts and mushrooms with seasonings, and then stuffed it all in. He then sewed up the belly before putting it in a ceramic pot to cook. While both sides were still raw, he washed some wild vegetables, boiled a pot of water, scalded them briefly, drained them, added seasonings, and drizzled a few drops of sesame oil. The aroma wafted through the air, and An Jiu, who was sunbathing with her eyes closed, sniffed the smell and came closer, grabbing a few pieces and stuffing them into her mouth. Chu Dingjiang did not stop her. He got up to turn over the roast suckling pig, but when he turned back, almost the entire plate of mixed wild vegetables was already in An Jiu’s mouth. Seeing her cheeks bulging, he pointed to the small clump of wild vegetables on the plate. “I’ve been busy all morning, and this is all you leave me?” Compared to Chu Dingjiang’s physique, An Jiu felt this was indeed too little. “Then I will pick some more for you.” An Jiu had just spotted some of this vegetable in the grass. “Go on, protect your precious little treasure!” Chu Dingjiang teased her. So An Jiu raised one hand and buried her head in the grass, picking wild vegetables. Watching her huddled in a ball, Chu Dingjiang felt a surge of pride, like watching his daughter grow up, and a feeling of tenderness welled up within him. In his previous life, he would never have dreamed that he would one day indulge a woman like this. The Hua clan of the Warring States period was a large family, with dozens of cousins ​​alone. Everyone wanted to rise in the ranks, everyone had to shoulder family responsibilities, and true kinship was rare. He grew up in this environment into a schemer, his mind filled with calculations, never taking the time to enjoy family affection. Even his marriage was an exchange of interests. It was not until many years of forced seclusion that he felt the need for warmth in his life. In this world, to be able to care for someone and to be cared for by someone was a kind of happiness, a source of peace. Chu Dingjiang snapped out of his reverie, smiling as he turned the roast suckling pig. Soon, An Jiu handed him a handful of wild vegetables. Chu Dingjiang took them and washed them. He quickly rinsed and tossed them, the tender vegetables releasing a refreshing aroma. An Jiu stared at them intently for a few moments, then turned to look at the roast suckling pig. Chu Dingjiang loved watching her feign profundity while making silly gestures. He grinned mischievously, took a large bite of the wild vegetables, and deliberately sighed with enjoyment. “Wild vegetables are the most refreshing thing to eat in this weather.” An Jiu pouted. She reached out to poke the roast suckling pig with her finger. Chu Dingjiang lightly tapped her finger with his chopsticks. “Your hands are covered in mud; are you still going to eat it later?” An Jiu silently turned away to ruffle the wildflowers beside her. An Jiu preferred solitude to being with others, so Chu Dingjiang did not disturb her. He enjoyed company but did not necessarily need much conversation. By the time she had finished wreaking havoc on a patch of wildflowers, the suckling pig was half-cooked. Chu Dingjiang brushed honey onto it. This was a method he had learned while traveling; others used it to roast chicken and lamb, but he did not like it, finding the sweet and salty taste strange. However, after trying it a few times, he discovered that while he could not accept the sweet and salty flavor of lamb, it went quite well with suckling pig. Chu Dingjiang was usually very casual, seemingly unconcerned with anything, but when he did, he was no less particular than those literary figures. For example, when eating wild game, he would set up a low couch on the ground, lay down a woolen felt mat, and place a small table on top of it. Even the tableware was exquisite, high-quality white porcelain, crystal clear and delicate like jade, almost translucent in the sunlight, with some pieces decorated with elegant orchids. Besides this, he also brought two jars of wine. Seeing her staring at the porcelain, Chu Dingjiang said, “This is Yue ware white porcelain from the Tang Dynasty. Once, I accidentally discovered an ancient kiln with two sealed kilns. When I opened them, I found two kilns of perfectly preserved porcelain of superior quality. I sold them all to a porcelain shop, keeping only this set for myself.” Although he was not particularly interested in financial management, he needed money for everything from realizing his ambitions to the mundane details of food, clothing, and shelter, and he would never let a free money-making opportunity slip by. When the meat was almost cooked, Chu Dingjiang pulled An Jiu to the river to wash her hands. An Jiu turned her head, staring intently at the handsome face reflected in the shimmering water, her eyes unblinking, seemingly lost in thought. Wild ducks fluttered up, the sun shone brightly, and a gentle breeze swept across the water and grass, scattering ripples and petals. The stream reflected the handsome man and the beautiful woman. The atmosphere was incredibly romantic. Chu Dingjiang scooped water while smiling gently at her, his back to the sun, his gaze deep and captivating. Chu Dingjiang’s charm lay not in his handsome appearance but in his refined character, like fine aged wine, and the profound wisdom gained through life’s experiences. His gentle smile was enough to captivate any woman. An Jiu’s usually resolute and cold gaze gradually melted, as if bathed in sunlight, and a soft smile appeared on her face. Chu Dingjiang took her hand and slowly drew closer. “Chu Dingjiang,” An Jiu whispered. “Hmm?” Chu Dingjiang’s voice was deep, slightly husky, carrying an indescribable allure. He tilted his head, lowering his eyes. Just as his lips were about to touch hers, he heard her sigh, a rare moment of emotion. “You are just like my mother… except… for that flirtatious laugh.” Even Chu Dingjiang, who was usually unfazed by the collapse of Mount Tai, nearly coughed up a mouthful of blood. He took a deep breath, bit her, and angrily grabbed her hand. “Go eat the meat!” An Jiu was still immersed in the touching moment when he carefully washed her hands, something her mother often did when she was a child. The two returned to the bedside. An Jiu sat cross-legged, watching Chu Dingjiang cut the meat. Hmm… her lips were slightly pursed, her chin tense, as if she was angry. Chu Dingjiang had already noticed her scrutinizing him. He thought that, considering his hard work in serving her, she should at least offer a few words of comfort, so he deliberately kept a straight face. After waiting a while, An Jiu did speak, but what she said was, “If you shave your beard, it will be easier for you to show your expressions. Is that not bad for a politician? It is better to have a beard.” After saying that, An Jiu felt, to herself, that her advice was very pertinent.

chapters.title: Chop Up These Brats
chapters.content: Chu Dingjiang had planned this outing for two or three days, not even entrusting a single wild vegetable to anyone else. He’d never planned anything like this, doing everything himself! He sighed. He’d somewhat anticipated this situation; it was not too bad. At least An Jiu trusted and relied on him, and for now, that was enough. “It’s inconvenient to cover my face with a beard,” he said calmly. An Jiu nodded, accepting his explanation. Not getting the expected reaction, Chu Dingjiang could only find an excuse for her in his mind: not caring about appearance was a fine virtue. He did not want to continue discussing the beard, so he cut two pieces of meat and put them in her bowl. The perfectly marbled suckling pig was roasted until sizzling, its skin golden brown, emitting an enticing aroma. An Jiu’s attention was indeed diverted. She quickly picked up a piece and put it in her mouth. The crispy, fragrant crust, seasoned with salt and pepper and a hint of honey, was delicious, while the tender, juicy meat underneath melted in her mouth. The lean parts still had a bit of chewiness, and each bite left a lingering aftertaste that whetted her appetite even more. An Jiu ate several pieces in a row without finding it greasy at all. Seeing her eyes light up, Chu Dingjiang sighed, thinking that deep down she was still a child, like a boy he had once met who possessed a photographic memory, was incredibly knowledgeable, and was a sensation. Yet this prodigy was completely ignorant of basic agricultural knowledge, and after the family he relied on fell into ruin, only two or three months later, when people remembered him again, they discovered that this boy had starved to death. An Jiu was not quite like that, but her interpersonal skills were truly unbearable to watch. Chu Dingjiang placed the earthenware pot on the table. An Jiu chewed on the meat while staring at the chicken soup. In the earthenware pot was only a single, naked white chicken, its broth seemingly bland. But Chu Dingjiang used long chopsticks to turn the chicken over, and with a dagger, he cut open the line on its belly, releasing a rich aroma. An Jiu swallowed the meat in her mouth and eagerly picked up a chestnut. Chu Dingjiang handed her a bowl of soup. “Your cooking is quite good,” An Jiu praised, taking a moment from her busy routine. Chu Dingjiang immediately perked up. “So many years focusing on one thing. If I had not figured it out, I might as well have died sooner.” During his years on the run, the thing he pondered most every day was how to make delicious dishes with limited ingredients. Those memories were too painful to recall! While Chu Dingjiang was lost in somber recollections, An Jiu remained unaffected, devouring a pot of mushrooms and two large chicken legs in a flash. Shortly after lunch, the sunlight had turned golden-red. The two lay on the grass, watching the clouds glow red in the evening light, the grass rustling softly in the breeze. As dusk fell, Chu Dingjiang escorted An Jiu back to the palace gate. Two rows of palace lanterns hung on the battlements, illuminating the area before the city as bright as day. An Jiu had taken six or seven steps when she heard Chu Dingjiang say behind her, “Ah Jiu, Mei Yanran lives in the courtyard next to yours. Find her, and I will arrange for you to leave.” She stopped and turned back, seeing him in the dim light, wearing a black cloak, the large hood obscuring most of his face. He had reverted to his most common appearance. “Will you come with us?” An Jiu remembered him saying they would live in seclusion together, and after today, a glimmer of hope stirred within her. “Yes. I need to arrange everything. Perhaps I will be two or three months later than you,” Chu Dingjiang’s voice came from under the hood. “Go back.” An Jiu nodded and also put on her black cloak. Concealing her face, she darted swiftly towards the city wall, passing through a hidden side gate. Back in her quarters, An Jiu saw Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi sitting on the courtyard steps. Upon seeing her return, they both rose to greet her. “Did you buy fried noodles?” Li Qingzhi asked hurriedly. An Jiu hesitated for a moment, then shook her head. Li Qingzhi and Sui Yuntong exchanged glances. “We did not buy any…” Sui Yuntong sighed. “One of you said you’d bring him something delicious, and the other said you’d buy two bowls. I thought someone would buy some.” “I was having so much fun shopping that I only remembered it when I came back. I thought you were always so thoughtful, you’d definitely buy some, so I did not go out again,” Li Qingzhi had explained this many times already. He asked An Jiu, “Were you not the one who first suggested bringing him something delicious? Even if Yuntong did not buy it, you should have!” “That…” She’d forgotten about it as soon as she left the city gates! “I bought some fine tea; take it to the Lord,” Sui Yuntong said, then asked the two, “What did you buy? Take it all as a gift.” Li Qingzhi immediately drew a short knife from his waist. “Take this precious sword too.” The two looked at An Jiu. “I…” An Jiu felt in her pocket and pulled out a Yue-kiln white porcelain cup. She thought it was very beautiful, so she took one with her, before returning, to use for tea. Sui Yuntong did not say anything else, taking the cup. “Fine tea deserves a fine cup; it is perfect. Come with me.” The two reluctantly followed Sui Yuntong to the eunuchs’ quarters in Gushe Palace. It was rest time. The eunuchs quickly washed up and climbed onto their communal beds. After about the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, the courtyard quieted down. One eunuch remained in the courtyard, carrying water. Another emerged from the outhouse, yawning and grumbling, “Do not make any noise; we are all trying to sleep!” The water-carrying eunuch did not reply, but he moved even more quietly. The three crouching in the shadows watched Gao Dazhuang carry water, sighing inwardly. They could guess he’d been punished for “slacking off” that morning. Actually, he’d only been gone for a moment; this treatment was just an old man disciplining a newcomer. Gao Dazhuang had already spotted them. After filling two vats of water, he listened intently, confirming everyone inside was asleep, and then quietly slipped to the base of the wall. As soon as the three appeared, Gao Dazhuang impatiently shouted, “Where’s the noodles? I have not eaten all day! Hurry!” The three: “…” They stared at each other, Gao Dazhuang’s expression gradually darkening. Sui Yuntong hurriedly pulled out tea leaves, a teacup, and a waist knife. “My Lord, would you like to make yourself a cup of tea first?” “I…” Gao Dazhuang grabbed the waist knife and drew it, growling, “I will chop you bunch of blind bastards! Can you not see what kind of life your grandfather leads?!” Having such unreliable subordinates was a recipe for disaster! Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi dodged, but An Jiu did not dodge, instead holding out an object to him. Gao Dazhuang’s blade paused. Seeing the large oil-paper package in her hand, his expression softened. He tossed the waist knife aside, caught the package, and snorted, “I knew you would not dare…” An Jiu turned and ran. Seeing this, Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi immediately gave chase. When Gao Dazhuang received the oil paper package, he felt its weight was off. Seeing their reaction, he realized he’d been tricked!

chapters.title: Mother and Daughter
chapters.content: Gao Dazhuang did not chase after them. He opened the oil-paper package and saw a small bunch of wildflowers inside. He trembled with anger. The three of them rushed back to their quarters. Sui Yuntong finally had a moment to ask, “What did you give him?” “A bunch of small white flowers,” An Jiu thought to herself. “I should have picked some wild vegetables; at least he’d have something to eat.” “Who gives someone white flowers? Are you trying to infuriate him?” Sui Yuntong sighed. An Jiu was unconvinced. She had only picked the white flowers because they were pretty; there were many yellow and red ones over there that she had not picked. Of the three, Li Qingzhi was the most conscientious. He frowned, asking anxiously, “My Lord will not really go hungry, will he? The palace has the imperial kitchen; at least he can get something to eat, right?” Sui Yuntong shook his head. “Every area of ​​the palace is guarded by secret guards. The imperial kitchen is probably quite well-staffed. Speaking of which, have you not figured out My Lord’s character yet?” Li Qingzhi’s eyes widened, his face showing utter bewilderment. “My Lord sometimes acts out of line, but always in a perfectly timed way, never giving anyone a handle to use against him. This time, His Majesty ordered him to impersonate a eunuch. In my opinion, he would not secretly run away from Gushe Palace,” Sui Yuntong said. An Jiu lacked a clear sense of right and wrong. Hearing Sui Yuntong’s words, she gradually felt a pang of guilt. For people like them, going hungry for three to five days without food, let alone a day, would still inspire them to kill. However, An Jiu had promised to bring him food, but then broke her promise; that was wrong of her. However, the die was cast, and further contemplation was pointless. After a thorough self-examination, An Jiu quickly put the matter aside, as she noticed the people in the neighboring courtyard had returned… An Jiu stood there for a moment, then turned and left the courtyard. Li Qingzhi and Sui Yuntong exchanged a glance and went back to their rooms. Although An Jiu was not ready to face Mei Yanran, the Konghe Army was not openly present, and now that they were so close, it was best to make contact first. Having made up her mind, she did not hesitate any longer and gently knocked on the door. There was no response from inside. An Jiu pushed the door open and went in. She did not want to clash with the people in the courtyard, so she first introduced herself and explained her purpose, “Fourteenth Young Lady of the Dragon Martial Guards, here to find a member of the Mei clan.” As soon as she finished speaking, a slender figure emerged from a room. “Who are you?” The person’s voice trembled, filled with disbelief. An Jiu hesitated for a moment, then whispered, “Mother.” The moment she uttered the word, Mei Yanran appeared before her, removing her veil to reveal a gaunt face. The Mei Yanran that An Jiu remembered was a gentle, serene woman, untouched by the hardships of her years away from home. Yet, having only recently joined the Konghe Army, a chilling aura had already appeared between her brows. This aura, however, slowly dissipated upon seeing An Jiu. An Jiu removed her hood and called out again, “Mother.” This time, her voice was much more resolute. Mei Jiu’s physical appearance had changed, and coupled with An Jiu’s distinct temperament, she seemed utterly unfamiliar to Mei Yanran at first glance. But after all, she was a piece of her own flesh and blood. The blood ties remained unbroken. She paused for a moment, then reached out and embraced An Jiu. “Jiu’er, how much suffering have you endured!” She believed her gentle and kind daughter had been forced into this state within the Konghe Army. Though hard to imagine, it was the only explanation. “Mother, let’s talk in my room.” An Jiu trusted her group of people. Mei Yanran nodded and took her hand as they went out. Her hands clasped together, An Jiu tensed uncomfortably, but a glance at Mei Yanran’s profile eased her tension. Upon entering the courtyard, Sui Yuntong was the first to peek out. “Who is it?” As assassins, they were extremely wary of strangers. “My mother,” An Jiu introduced briefly. Sui Yuntong, surprisingly, greeted her with a bow, like a scholar. “I did not know you were Lady Mei. I am so sorry for the intrusion.” He knew that the Mei family’s daughters never married outside the family, hence addressing Mei Yanran as Lady Mei. Mei Yanran was slightly surprised. Sui Yuntong’s manners would be normal outside, but here they felt out of place; she had never seen anything like it during her time with the Konghe Army. “No need for formalities,” Mei Yanran said calmly, despite her surprise. Sui Yuntong bowed again and returned inside. An Jiu led Mei Yanran into her room, and after they sat down, she was momentarily at a loss for words. Mei Yanran, however, held her hand and scrutinized her closely. An Jiu, impersonating Mei Yanran, felt insecure under such direct scrutiny and could only lower her eyes and remain silent. Her appearance was delicate, and this demeanor made her seem like she had suffered a grievance but refused to speak, causing Mei Yanran a dull ache in her heart. She pulled her close, choking back tears. “My child!” An Jiu leaned against her chest, pondering what topic to use as a starting point. She thought and thought, but could not come up with anything. Once Mei Yanran had calmed down, she initiated the conversation, “I heard that the Mei family suffered a calamity. How did you escape? And how did you end up here?” This was a poor choice! An Jiu was self-aware enough to know that her ability to deceive might frighten a naive girl like Mei Jiu, but it would not work on Mei Yanran. For some reason, a name naturally popped into An Jiu’s mind at that moment: “It was Cousin Mo who saved me.” Such a ridiculous excuse would be exposed sooner or later! But there was no way to tell Mei Yanran immediately, “Your daughter is dead, but she’s been resurrected, and I just happened to be in her body too.” That would be too much information, and An Jiu was not sure if Mei Yanran would be so shocked and angry that she’d draw her sword and kill her. She had to appease the situation for now. “I wanted to join the Konghe Army to find you, so I went to the Konghe Courtyard first. I did not expect to get close to the Dragon Martial Guards so quickly. It is because I helped the Song army in battle at the border that I gained the Emperor’s attention,” An Jiu tried to downplay the situation, barely managing to make it sound plausible. “Also, there’s an official in the Konghe Army who has been helping me.” Mei Yanran stroked her hair. “My child, your kindness is rewarded.” The mother and daughter’s conversation was inevitably overheard by others in the courtyard, who were immediately filled with emotion. Fourteenth Young Lady was kind-hearted? Truly, everything in a mother’s eyes was precious! Since Chu Dingjiang was mentioned, An Jiu picked up a pen and paper and wrote down her departure from the Konghe Army, including Chu Dingjiang’s assistance, as it would be difficult for her to completely break free from the organization on her own. After reading it, Mei Yanran was very suspicious. Why would a high-ranking official in the Konghe Army, who was not related to them, help them? It was impossible for someone to do a favor without expecting anything in return! She was worried that her daughter had been deceived, so she wrote: “We will discuss this later.” Then she crumpled the paper, put it in a teacup, and poured water into it. “Have you seen Elder Zhi?” An Jiu was slightly taken aback. “Is he in the palace?”

chapters.title: The Crown Prince
chapters.content: “Yes, he’s now a lecturer at the Zishan Hall,” Mei Yanran said. The Zishan Hall was where princes studied, and the lecturers were responsible for instructing and supervising the Crown Prince or other princes. Elder Zhi was a talented scholar in his youth, having achieved the highest rank in the imperial examinations and earning the Emperor’s high praise. The Mei family held considerable power in the Imperial Guard and were also wealthy locals, so the Emperor was naturally reluctant to promote him to a high position. Now that the Mei family had fallen from grace, it was not surprising that he was able to take up an official post. “I’ve never seen him before.” An Jiu had finally managed to get here from the Imperial Guard, half due to her own abilities and half due to luck. She had no time to pay attention to anything else, especially since she was not particularly interested in Elder Zhi’s affairs. Mei Yanran did not continue, only taking her hand and sighing, “Jiu’er, I almost do not recognize you anymore.” An Jiu remained silent, thinking that it was already quite good that she recognized her. “It’s my fault for not taking good care of you.” Mei Yanran’s feelings were a mix of emotions, including guilt, heartache, and a touch of relief. “You are a strong child.” Every few days, Mei Yanran would go to Elder Zhi to inquire about her daughter. She had thought that after the Mei family’s downfall, Mei Jiu might not survive, but the reality was quite the opposite! Now, her daughter stood before her, unharmed, though her demeanor had become somewhat cold and aloof, giving her a sense of unfamiliarity. However, in a place like the Konghe Army, which was designed to toughen people up, how could one survive without hardening one’s heart? Thinking of this, Mei Yanran cast aside all other thoughts, leaving only heartache. The two women spoke for a while, then went to rest. Mei Yanran stayed. Although An Jiu was not used to it, she did not ask her to leave. As dusk fell, there was a gentle knock on the door. Sui Yuntong whispered, “Let’s go.” It was time for her shift. An Jiu quickly packed her clothes, slung the Dragon-Subduing Bow over her shoulder, and saw Mei Yanran also putting on her robe. She said, “I am leaving.” Without waiting for Mei Yanran’s reply, he hurriedly left. Mei Yanran swallowed back the words that were on the tip of her tongue. The Emperor was cautious about his own safety, so the commander assigned them to the East Palace. The Crown Prince would spend two hours in the Zishan Hall in the morning, and after lunch, he would study state affairs with his tutor and others in the East Palace. Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi took good care of An Jiu, letting her be in charge of the inner chambers to avoid the wind and sun. An Jiu readily complied, lying on the rafters of the East Palace study and sleeping soundly. Whenever the Crown Prince moved, she would follow, essentially acting as his personal bodyguard. After idly sleeping all day, An Jiu woke up and squatted on the rafters to observe the Crown Prince. It was said the Crown Prince was nineteen this year, but he looked much younger. His fair, delicate face suggested he was only fifteen or sixteen, with refined features and fine, downy eyebrows. When reading, his brow was furrowed, as if he were deeply concerned for the country and its people. In reality, he often drifted off into thought. An Jiu secretly yawned. The next Emperor did not seem so promising! The Emperor had only three sons, leaving him with limited choices. Seeing this, An Jiu suddenly understood why Emperors wanted many sons—statistically, this greatly increases the chances of having a bright child. The Crown Prince finally made it to dinner. After seeing off the officials from the Eastern Palace, he slumped onto his mat and let out a long sigh. A eunuch bowed and entered. “Your Highness, would you like to bathe?” “I need to rest,” the Crown Prince said lazily. The eunuch said softly, “This servant will massage Your Highness’s shoulders.” The Crown Prince closed his eyes and hummed in agreement. The eunuch knelt behind the Crown Prince, his shoulder massages practiced and skillful. The Crown Prince dozed off comfortably, soon collapsing onto the eunuch’s lap. The eunuch’s slender, white hands then massaged down the Crown Prince’s shoulders to his chest and then down to his groin… In no time, the Crown Prince had an erection. Wait, something was not right! An Jiu looked closely at the eunuch and realized he was actually a woman! The Crown Prince suddenly rolled over, pinning the woman to the ground. The woman’s eunuch hat fell off, revealing a head of black, silky hair spread across the mat, exposing a delicate and pretty face. The Crown Prince leaned down and kissed her lips, both of them breathless from the kiss. An Jiu estimated the girl was only fourteen or fifteen years old; with the two teenagers rolling around on the ground, doing this and that, the scene was both innocent and exciting. Seeing the prince’s practiced ease, he was clearly a seasoned veteran. In no time, the girl was crying and begging for mercy. An Jiu suddenly remembered yesterday by the stream when Chu Dingjiang had brought his lips close to hers… Her eyes widened slightly as she understood Chu Dingjiang’s intentions. Indeed, who in this world would be kind to someone for no reason? An Jiu did not resist being close to Chu Dingjiang. Looking at the arousing scene below, she was certain her instincts were still there. If she saw Chu Dingjiang again, she would not mind doing it again, but beyond that, she did not want to think about it anymore. She never wanted a husband, nor children, and she certainly did not want her children to face a terrifying father. An Jiu’s mind wandered for a while, and then the two of them finished. Like cats who had stolen food, they did not dare call for service. After cleaning themselves up, they went to the bathhouse together. An Jiu was in charge of everything inside, so she had to go with them. Young people were indeed full of energy; these two got excited halfway through their bath and spent the entire half hour making a ruckus inside. An Jiu had never seen such a long, explicit scene in her two lifetimes combined. She’d had her fill—she’d been on duty for twelve hours, and the Crown Prince had been with her four or five times, each time with a different woman. So much so that when she returned to her quarters, her mind was filled with images of white, swaying buttocks. Fortunately, she had strong willpower and had received professional anti-brainwashing training. She quickly put these thoughts aside and began thinking about how to get Mei Yanran to leave with her. An Jiu could understand Mei Yanran’s concerns. Even she, someone who did not know Chu Dingjiang well, sometimes wondered if his friendliness towards her had ulterior motives. She had not quite figured it out before, but today, thanks to the Crown Prince, it finally became clear. Days in the palace passed by, both boring and fleeting. Before An Jiu knew it, half a month had gone by. She realized the Crown Prince was simply a lustful creature; he neglected his studies and political affairs, spending all his energy on women every night. If the Song Dynasty were to fall into his hands, it would be better to hand it over to the Liao Dynasty. In the living quarters, Sui Yuntong was tilling the ground to plant vegetables. An Jiu squatted on the veranda, basking in the sun, and asked him, “What kind of people are the other two princes?” Sui Yuntong, while scattering seeds into the holes, replied, “It’s said the Second Prince is fond of martial arts and dislikes Taoism. He has been reprimanded by the Emperor several times for offending Taoist masters, so the Emperor does not like him much. The Third Prince is skilled in both literature and martial arts, but due to the prevailing social trends, he prefers literature and calligraphy.” “Do they both have many women?” An Jiu asked.

chapters.title: Dangerous Moon Assassins
chapters.content: “Yes, which powerful noble does not have three wives and four concubines? Especially a prince? But the Third Prince is young, so he probably has fewer women serving him.” Sui Yuntong stopped what he was doing and looked at An Jiu. “Why are you suddenly interested in these things?” “Nothing.” An Jiu did not mention that she watched live performances every day, but she was just a little curious. “Who’s in charge of guarding the room on Lou Mingyue’s team?” Hearing her question, Sui Yuntong could roughly guess what had happened and smiled, “I do not know, but I guess it is Sun Dixian.” Seeing the question in her eyes, Sui Yuntong explained, “The affair between Qiu Yunzhu and Sun Dixian is obvious. Qiu Yunzhu will definitely take care of Sun Dixian and arrange for her to stay indoors. In this way, he can spend time with Young Lady Lou, whom he has been longing for. Why not?” An Jiu gave him a deep look. “I did not expect you to be so gossipy.” “Gossipy?” Sui Yuntong asked. An Jiu thought for a moment, then told him, “I suppose it means being well-informed.” Sui Yuntong smiled and said modestly, “Not at all. Actually, the most nosy one among us is Lord Gao. Do not let his low-key demeanor fool you—he’s got a lot of information stashed away!” Just as the two were speaking with all seriousness, Li Qingzhi returned. Unable to bear the guilt in his heart, he had managed to get some food today and brought it over to Gao Dazhuang. Li Qingzhi had half his face covered, with streaks of blood running down his forehead, as if a rain of needles were falling outside. “Did the Lord hit you with his broom?” Sui Yuntong tutted, pulling some ointment from his bosom and tossing it to him. “Go rub some on right away.” Li Qingzhi took the bottle and examined it closely. “That’s unusual. You are actually willing to use Master Mo’s medicine on me?” Sui Yuntong had gone to great lengths to beg for two bottles of medicine from Mo Sigui, and she usually could not bear to use them. “Well, that’s because you took a beating for the two of us,” Sui Yuntong said. An Jiu pulled out a few bottles from her person and tossed them to him. “Here, this is for you too!” Li Qingzhi knew An Jiu and Mo Sigui were close friends, and that all the medicine An Jiu used was made by him. He was overjoyed, taking the medicine and showing it off to Sui Yuntong. Sui Yuntong sighed, “I should have just gone and gotten beaten up!” Although he said this, there was no jealousy in his tone; it was just a casual joke. He then continued planting his vegetables. It was almost noon when Sui Yuntong washed his hands and went to cook. They were a hidden presence in the palace, and no one prepared meals for them every day. The Konghe Army would send someone to deliver food once a month, so they had to solve their own food problems. Thus, they took turns cooking. But ever since Sui Yuntong ate the food cooked by An Jiu and Li Qingzhi, he had taken the initiative to cook, not out of altruism, but purely for self-preservation. The two of them were happy to have their meals taken care of. Li Qingzhi sat down next to An Jiu, basking in the sun. After a while, he sighed, “The peaceful days here, compared to the borderlands, feel like a dream. If His Majesty could see it for himself, he probably would not be content with his peaceful life of cultivation!” An Jiu listened to Li Qingzhi’s worries about the country and its people. She thought to herself that if she were in the Crown Prince’s quarters, she’d probably feel like the sky was falling. After all, if this generation was incompetent, there was always hope for the next, but unfortunately, the next generation might be even less capable. Just as Li Qingzhi worried, while the palace was bathed in sunshine under a clear blue sky, war had broken out on the borders. The Liao army was like madmen, rampaging through the borderlands, burning, killing, and looting; sixty percent of the cities had been raided. The court had issued a clear order forbidding border residents from migrating inland. They could not come in, and the borders were difficult to defend effectively, making the areas bordering the Liao Kingdom in Hedong, Hebei West Road, and Hebei East Road feel like hell on earth. Everywhere was a mountain of corpses and a sea of ​​blood; nine out of ten houses were empty. The border troops were on high alert, barely having time to bathe.
