After half a month, everyone looked as if they had crawled out of a pool of blood. Ling Ziyue stood atop the city wall, hands behind his back, gazing into the distance. Everywhere he looked, there were corpses. A few days ago, a fierce battle had taken place here. The two women who had stayed by his side had tried to kill the Liao army leader, but their attempt failed, and they were captured alive by the Liao army. Ling Ziyue did not know who they were, but he saw that the assassination attempt was a ruse; their real purpose was to be captured alive and taken prisoner. Recalling the resolute look in the two women’s eyes, Ling Ziyue could not help but sigh deeply. Even women had such spirit; the Song Dynasty lacked it. In the Liao capital’s main camp, a snow-white tiger skin was spread on the head seat. Xiao Zhenning, dressed in Khitan civilian clothes, leaned back in his chair, drinking tea. His tiger-like eyes looked thoughtfully at the two women bound hand and foot below. “General, these two are Ling Ziyue’s women, are they not?” a general asked. The other generals, who were enjoying their meal, immediately slowed down and looked towards the head of the table. “What do you think?” Xiao Zhenning asked the women below. Soldiers stepped forward and untied the strips binding their lips and tongues. One of the women stared coldly at him and spat, “One day, my husband will lead his army straight into your capital!” This was their direct admission of their relationship with Ling Ziyue. Xiao Zhenning suddenly laughed, “The one in the Northern Court should be very happy to see Ling Ziyue’s women! Men! Tie these two up and send them to the King of the Northern Court.” “Xiao Zhenning, you beast, we will haunt you even in death!” Seeing them about to bite their tongues, the soldiers immediately grabbed their jaws, but one soldier was a step too late. Blood gushed from one of the women’s mouths, and she died shortly after. The other woman’s jaw was dislocated; her eyes were bloodshot, and she stared at Xiao Zhenning with venomous hatred. Now, Xiao Zhenning truly believed they were Ling Ziyue’s women. He’d heard that women in the Song Dynasty valued chastity highly; if they were merely assassins, they would not have committed suicide so easily. After all, if they had been a little later, both would be corpses! The woman dragged away was not Ling Ziyue’s woman, but the resentment in her eyes was genuine. She was Dangerous Moon, the last survivor after being sent to Liao. They had been in Liao for six months, killing two Liao ministers before losing two themselves. But during the assassination attempt on the Northern King Yelu Jinglie, only two remained. Their reason for joining Ling Ziyue was not to escape, but to return in another form. They had a certain understanding of the character of several important Liao ministers and had anticipated that admitting to being Ling Ziyue’s women would lead to them being sent back to Yelu Jinglie. Among the group, she was not the strongest in martial arts, but only her appearance remained undetected. Even if Yelu Jinglie suspected her, it did not matter, as long as Ling Ziyue admitted it. They placed a letter on Ling Ziyue’s desk; he would definitely cooperate. As long as she survived by Yelu Jinglie’s side, she would surely have her chance to strike!

chapters.title: A Return to Life
chapters.content: Once the Dangerous Moon received a mission, they relentlessly pursued their target to the death. Even if they could not complete the mission, they must risk their lives to leave a scar on their target. This was Dangerous Moon, a peculiar force within the Song Dynasty court. They were not necessarily highly skilled in martial arts, but they were carefully selected individuals from the Konghe Army. The conditions for joining Dangerous Moon were the following: first, one must be extreme and stubborn; second, one must be ruthless; and third, one must possess sufficient strength to sustain one’s ruthlessness, such as hatred. Therefore, most assassins in Dangerous Moon had tragic backgrounds or experiences, and most were women. It was not that women were more extreme and ruthless than men, but rather that women faced greater hardships in this world. Once they lost the protection of their families, they were like rootless, withered leaves, mostly destined to fall into the dust and be trampled upon. Because of this, they often had no way out, making the Konghe Army’s brainwashing even more effective. This brainwashing was similar to the psychological intervention An Jiu had undergone, extinguishing all hope and driving them to unleash their most extreme and ruthless sides in despair. Meanwhile, an event related to Dangerous Moon was unfolding within the Konghe Army, causing considerable turmoil. —After a monotonous and tedious two weeks in the palace, Lou Mingyue actually volunteered to join Dangerous Moon! When she made this request, not only An Jiu and the others, but even Gao Dazhuang was stunned speechless for a long time. Dangerous Moon, to put it nicely, was a group of righteous warriors willing to shed their blood for the Song Dynasty; to put it bluntly, they were a bunch of human punching bags used to fill holes. Although the Konghe Army was a hidden organization, it was still divided into different ranks. Someone like Lou Mingyue, from a noble family and with an excellent foundation, would absolutely not want to join Dangerous Moon. Members of Dangerous Moon were difficult to recruit and train; it was a case of every member who died being one less, with supply far exceeding demand. It was unlikely anyone would refuse. Before the official reply had even been approved, An Jiu, upon hearing the news, immediately requested to leave the palace. This time, Gao Dazhuang merely rolled his eyes at her a few times but did not actually stop her. An Jiu easily entered the Konghe Army camp using her identification stamp and found Mo Sigui. Lanterns were lit in the courtyard, and the bells hanging in the corner of the house jingled crisply. Mo Sigui was feeding two tigers. Upon seeing An Jiu, he crossed his arms and stood up. He smiled and said, “Oh, is this not the lord from the Dragon Martial Guards?” The Dragon Martial Guards were now officially established; it was no longer a secret. Seeing his beaming face, An Jiu, unusually, did not give him a harsh rebuke. She silently picked up Da Jiu, who had run to her, and carefully stroked its fur. “Hey, something’s not right!” Mo Sigui stepped forward, examined her closely, and said smugly. “Should you not tease me a bit? I have not been teased in so long; I feel really uncomfortable.” His utterly servile expression instantly extinguished any sympathy An Jiu felt for him. “Lou Mingyue is joining Dangerous Moon.” Mo Sigui’s smile froze on his face. After a long pause, he forced a smile, his voice dropping eight octaves. “Really? That’s good. She perfectly fits Dangerous Moon’s criteria.” “I’d rather you cry; this expression is distressing,” An Jiu said. Mo Sigui slowly composed himself, bending down to pick up Xiao Yue, who was nestled at his feet. He sat on the steps of the veranda, remaining silent for a long time. An Jiu wanted to offer some words of comfort, but seeing his demeanor, she felt any words would be too weak, so she simply sat quietly beside him. Mo Sigui stared calmly at the swaying bell in the corner of the room and said with difficulty, “Have a drink with me.” After Gu Jinghong, it was now Mo Sigui. An Jiu felt she had become a trusted older sister, so she nodded professionally. Mo Sigui had a servant boy bring over two jars of wine, and the two began drinking from them. An Jiu was afraid of drinking too much and causing trouble, so she did not drink freely. “Drink!” Mo Sigui, noticing her lack of enthusiasm, snapped, “Is my relationship with you less important than Gu Jinghong’s face?! Drink up, or you are disrespecting me!” An Jiu was an honest person and gulped down several large mouthfuls. Mo Sigui laughed immediately, patting her shoulder. “Loyal to me, a true brother!” “Just drinking is not a solution,” An Jiu said, grabbing the mouth of his jar. “Did you think I came to tell you this to make you sad?” Mo Sigui shook his head with a smile. “You do not understand her. She’s always been stubborn. Although she’s aloof now, she’s even more stubborn than before. Not even the King of Heaven could change her mind!” His smile was ordinary, but An Jiu saw bitterness in it. After saying that, he gulped down a large amount of wine, spilling a lot, soaking his clothes without noticing. After finishing one jar, he snatched the jar from An Jiu. But sometimes, even when one wanted to get drunk, one could not. He finished two jars of wine, half-drunk and half-spilled, but Mo Sigui’s eyes grew brighter, and his thoughts were clearer than ever before! After staring blankly for two or three hours, Mo Sigui finally sighed. He went inside, sat at his desk for a while, ground ink, picked up a brush, and wrote a line. An Jiu stood beside him, seeing the powerful characters written on the paper: “If alive, return to me; if dead, I will long for you forever.” After the ink dried, Mo Sigui folded the letter and placed it in an envelope, handing it to An Jiu without sealing it. “Please tell her I am grateful to her. If she is ever injured, come to me. The only thing I can do for her is to save her life before she avenges her family.” An Jiu had promised not to interfere in their affairs and had never said a word. This was the first and last time she would break her promise. She put the letter away and looked at Mo Sigui carefully. His expression was calm, but slightly weary, as if a heavy burden had suddenly been lifted, yet he also seemed suddenly weathered. “Are you alright?” An Jiu asked. Mo Sigui took a medicine bottle from the shelf behind him and handed it to her. “Give this to Lord Gao. I appreciate his kindness in letting you out to deliver the message. This is a Resurrection Pill. It will not bring him back to life, but it can keep him alive and buy him time to seek medical help. I am giving him a second chance at life.” An Jiu took the bottle and put it in her bosom. Before leaving, she finally spoke her mind: “Those who walk different paths cannot make plans together. It is better for you and her to have come to this point than to be entangled and tormented.” As the saying goes, bystanders saw things more clearly. Although An Jiu did not quite understand why they were so conflicted, it was like day and night, merely a brief intersection of dawn and dusk. When An Jiu returned to the palace, the sky was already bright. She did not go back to her quarters but went straight to the Crown Prince’s palace to find Lou Mingyue, gave her Mo Sigui’s letter, and relayed his words verbatim. Lou Mingyue read the letter, her expression complex. After hearing An Jiu’s words, her eyes welled up with tears. She turned her head away. An Jiu then quietly left to find Gao Dazhuang.

chapters.title: Exposing the Truth
chapters.content: These past few days, Consort Yu had been staying at Gushe Palace, keeping Gao Dazhuang extremely busy. The Emperor also frequently visited. After taking the Golden Elixir, he had Consort Yu disguise herself as a fairy and engage in sexual intercourse with her, as if he had already ascended to immortality. After witnessing the Crown Prince’s jubilation, and then unfortunately witnessing his father’s jubilation as well, An Jiu was struck by the decadence and depravity everywhere she looked. A growing aversion to the palace began to creep into her heart. She suddenly understood why Lou Mingyue had joined the Dangerous Moon Team. Lou Mingyue joined the Konghe Army with the intention of leveraging its power and resources to strengthen herself. However, as a Dragon Martial Guard in the palace, she would likely never have the opportunity for revenge or to hone her skills. Assassins only honed their skills through constant missions; a life of leisure would dull their blades. In the Gushe Palace’s sleeping quarters, a passionate lovemaking was taking place. A group of maids and eunuchs stood outside the tent, listening to the blush-inducing sounds. Six bodyguards surrounded the Emperor. Although they would have difficulty detecting An Jiu, any movement by Gao Dazhuang could easily lead to misunderstandings. Therefore, after watching the “performance” for a while, An Jiu returned to her quarters. Before even entering the room, she sensed Mei Yanran’s arrival. She pushed open the door and called out, “Mother.” Mei Yanran responded, remaining seated in her round-backed chair. Watching An Jiu reach for water, she whispered, “You are not Jiu’er.” An Jiu stopped and turned to look at her. It was too sudden! She had only met Mei Yanran once before being exposed, and before that, Mei Yanran had not shown any unusual behavior. Now that she had been discovered, An Jiu did not intend to hide it any longer. She calmly said, “She’s still alive. I borrowed her body to come find you in her place; consider it repaying a debt.” In the dim light, Mei Yanran’s clenched hand trembled slightly. Was it the shocking news or anger and worry? Silence. “How could you tell I was not Mei Jiu?” An Jiu asked. After all, it was still the same body, and the two had very little contact. When An Jiu was with her, she was almost like a statue, barely moving and speaking. “What mother would mistake her own child?” Mei Yanran looked at her figure, almost hidden in the darkness, her tone elusive. “People change, but habits do not change overnight. For example, she calls me ‘Mother,’ and she habitually raises her pinky finger when pouring water.” Mei Yanran had been too emotional when she first met An Jiu, so she had overlooked many details. But after spending one night with An Jiu, she noticed that her sleeping habits were completely different from her own daughter’s, so she observed her more closely. The bond between mother and daughter was not just about blood ties; it also included a connection of the heart. “Is she… alright?” Mei Yanran asked hesitantly. After hearing An Jiu’s words, she was terrified, fearing that Mei Jiu was experiencing some unimaginable hardship. “She’s fine. She’s even married,” An Jiu said. “Really?” Mei Yanran seemed to snap out of her daze, her eyes brightening. “She’s married? Who did she marry? How is she doing?” For a mother, nothing was more important than her daughter’s safety and happiness. Even though the events of the past were hard for her to accept, hearing good news about Mei Jiu had put her mind at ease. “Yes. She married Hua Rongtian.” Having said that, An Jiu took the opportunity to persuade her to leave. “If you stay here, she will not be able to live in peace. Why not leave with me? You can go with her or come with me.” An Jiu felt a pang of disappointment. She wanted to make up for everything she owed her mother through Mei Yanran, but perhaps that was impossible now. Mei Yanran looked at her for a long time before saying, “Roll up your left sleeve.” An Jiu was taken aback, then realized that Mei Yanran still did not quite believe her, probably wanting to see the markings on this body. She unfastened her gauntlet and rolled up her sleeve to her shoulder. Mei Yanran stood up and walked to her side, noticing a tiny red mole, as small as a pinhead, on the back of her upper arm near her armpit. Even an imposter would not be this meticulously crafted! Mei Yanran closed her eyes briefly, her gaze towards An Jiu becoming much more complex. This was her daughter, and yet not. “You can leave?” Mei Yanran asked. An Jiu confidently scoffed, “Do not worry, I am not Mei Jiu. The plan is very thorough.” Seemingly good news? But Mei Yanran was not particularly happy, as if her daughter were incompetent. However, she did not let this small amount of emotion show; her expression and tone remained unchanged. “I’ve ingested a deadly poison and need to collect the antidote every so often.” An Jiu frowned. “Why have we not taken the poison?” “Have not taken the poison?” Mei Yanran was surprised, but then she thought that perhaps it was due to the different roles within the Dragon Martial Guards; her responsibility was close protection of the Emperor, so naturally, she was under closer scrutiny. Thinking of all this, she stopped pondering the question and continued, “Your cousin Mo…” She habitually mistook An Jiu for Mei Jiu, pausing slightly before continuing, “If we knew Sigui’s whereabouts, he might be able to help me cure the poison, but have you considered that if we leave, all the Mei family members remaining in the Konghe Army will suffer collateral damage?” “You still have attachment to the Mei family?” This was truly bad news for An Jiu. Mei Yanran was speechless. She had forgotten again that the person before her had no feelings for the Mei family and was not Mei Jiu. “It’s not attachment, but for the family that gave birth to me and raised me, I cannot let so many blood relatives die because of me,” Mei Yanran said. This was a problem… An Jiu had not considered. An Jiu’s biggest concern was how to find Mei Yanran and then how to leave; as for family, that was completely outside her concept. “Let me think about it.” An Jiu was somewhat overwhelmed. Asking her to use her destructive intellect to save them was a bit too much of a stretch! In her view, destroying a family single-handedly was a hundred times easier than preserving one. “What was your original plan?” Mei Yanran was also eager to go out and see Mei Jiu. An Jiu pulled a map from her bosom. “I’ve prepared seven routes. Leaving Bianjing safely should not be a problem.” Mei Yanran: “…” So the so-called meticulous plan just meant how to quickly pack up and leave? Stirring up the Emperor’s hornet’s nest—she’d be hunted down for life! An Jiu thought for a moment. Since she was going to be hunted down anyway, why not, “Eliminate the future threat first?” Mei Yanran’s eyelids twitched; she understood that An Jiu wanted to kill the Emperor. “Then we will have to replan,” An Jiu muttered. Seeing her seriousness, Mei Yanran quickly stopped her. “No!” “Keeping an Emperor like this around is a disaster.” After saying that, An Jiu realized that the Emperor’s reign was a disaster; without him, the Song Dynasty would likely fall into war even more easily. A country could not be without a ruler for a day, especially with a powerful enemy at its side. Seeing that she seemed to understand, Mei Yanran breathed a sigh of relief. “Let’s take our time to plan.”

chapters.title: An Jiu’s Excitement
chapters.content: The phrase “let’s discuss it further” left An Jiu speechless. She wondered if she should try to kidnap Mei Yanran. But then she thought better of it. Had she not been hunted down enough in her past life? She did not need to completely avoid repeating the same mistakes in this life, but at least she should not needlessly incur hatred! After thinking it over, An Jiu glanced at Mei Yanran and noticed a fleeting hint of wariness and distance in her eyes. She was slightly hurt but quickly recovered. For a wandering ghost who had somehow possessed her daughter’s body, not killing her was already showing mercy. Mei Yanran saw her smile and did not know what to say next, because no matter what she said, she would not completely believe it. After standing there for a few moments, Mei Yanran slipped out of the house. An Jiu poured water but stopped just before it reached her lips. She emptied the kettle and went to the kitchen to boil water again. Her mother was good, but unfortunately, she was not her own! Mei Yanran’s reaction was something she had to be wary of. An Jiu boiled water while thinking. So many changes had occurred around her in such a short time. Everyone else had made their own choices, but she had not. She drifted along; wherever fate pushed her, she floated there, never finding a direction, never even considering the meaning of her existence. Even Mei Jiu knew she was aiming for marriage and children, while An Jiu was just a killing machine. She obeyed orders; everything she thought and did was related to her mission. It was not that she lacked intelligence, but she had long forgotten how to think and choose for herself. An Jiu had never thought of pursuing her ambitions, much less marrying and having children… So, where was her path? An Jiu’s face was reflected in the warm glow of the fire in the stove, and a self-deprecating smile appeared on her face. She was a rat that only knew how to follow the swarm of rats, occasionally looking down on those who passed by—you foolish humans! Actually, the most pathetic and laughable one was herself. The water in the pot was boiling. An Jiu scooped some out with a ladle and carried it to the courtyard, intending to drink it directly from the ladle. The moonlight was like water as she stood beside the vegetable garden that Sui Yuntong had cultivated. She saw that the recently sown seeds had already sprouted tender green shoots. “You cannot water them with hot water!” Sui Yuntong saw her carrying a ladle of hot water to the edge of the garden and staring at the seedlings, so he rushed out of the house to stop her. An Jiu, one hand on her hip and the other holding the hot water, calmly turned to look at Sui Yuntong rushing towards her and said, “Do you have a dream?” Sui Yuntong’s movements suddenly stopped. He shook his hand, which was numb from the force of the impact, and looked at her strangely, thinking, “Is she having another episode?” So he carefully answered, afraid of saying anything that might offend her, “Yes.” “What kind of dream?” An Jiu asked with interest. Sui Yuntong glanced at the hot water in her hand, worried she might spill it on the ground or onto him. His muscles tensed slightly. “Picking chrysanthemums by the eastern fence, I leisurely gaze at the southern mountains. I want to find a place with beautiful mountains and clear waters, marry a simple, honest girl, and live a peaceful life.” At this moment, he felt no sense of leisure or ease. “Hmm,” An Jiu thought for a moment. “I do know a simple, honest girl.” Sui Yuntong was half nervous, half puzzled. “She’s already married, but unfortunately, her marriage is not ideal. How about I introduce her to you?” The simple, honest girl in An Jiu’s mind was Mei Jiu. Sui Yuntong did not respond to that. He could not help but ask, “What are you doing with that hot water?” “Drinking!” An Jiu looked at him with an expression of utter disbelief. “Oh, is that so?” Sui Yuntong relaxed, then continued his sentence. “I am still not in control of my own life; how could I possibly have the fortune to marry?” “Whether it is fortune or not is hard to say. She just loves to cry.” An Jiu brought the water ladle to her lips. She took a sip. “Do you like this type?” Sui Yuntong was speechless. Was this some kind of matchmaker? Not only was she mentioning a married woman, but she was also picking on the worst aspects. Seeing An Jiu waiting earnestly for an answer, Sui Yuntong could only chuckle. “I like the feistier kind.” Upon hearing this, An Jiu gave up. Mei Jiu rarely uttered harsh words, but she remembered Sui Yuntong’s words. Sui Yuntong was completely unaware that his words today would lead to his “tragedy” for the rest of his life; he simply thought it was just flattering a lunatic. “I am going back to my room,” Sui Yuntong said. An Jiu hummed in agreement, then fell into deep thought. Her conversation with Sui Yuntong had suddenly sparked an idea. Since she could not find a direction, she might as well help others! Helping others fulfill their dreams was a good path! It could also be considered making amends for the killings she had committed. An Jiu was a woman of action; she did what she thought of. After finishing her drink, she went to Li Qingzhi’s room. Li Qingzhi was practicing his martial arts upside down from the roof beam when he saw An Jiu enter and jumped down. In the dark room, he could vaguely see a glint in An Jiu’s eyes. “Do you have a dream?” Li Qingzhi was taken aback. His first reaction was the same as Sui Yuntong’s: this girl had gone mad again. “Sit down,” Li Qingzhi said outwardly and thought to himself. “I really cannot let this madness happen outside. This is the palace; you could lose your head at any moment.” So, with a sense of responsibility, he decided to try to keep her occupied with conversation. “Yes, I admire General Ling. A man with ability should protect his country. Sigh, what kind of world is this now?” An Jiu nodded repeatedly. “Your idea is good.” Li Qingzhi was even more puzzled. When did she start saying such nice things? It was practically unheard of! He could not help but want to drag Sui Yuntong over to listen. “It’s alright; you continue practicing.” An Jiu waved her hand and strode out of the room, using her momentum to find Gao Dazhuang and give him the medicine Mo Sigui had brought. Li Qingzhi hurried to Sui Yuntong’s room. “Can we just not follow her? Last time at the border, all that commotion was handled by Lord Chu, but he’s not here this time!” Sui Yuntong hesitated. “Her mental strength is high; if we follow her, we will definitely be discovered.” “If things escalate, we will both be punished,” Li Qingzhi said. Sui Yuntong nodded. “Alright, we will follow from a distance.” The two of them flashed off, chasing after the direction An Jiu had left, but they had already lost her presence. The key areas of the palace were guarded by the Dragon Martial Guards. They were not familiar with the other teams, and wandering around would cause unnecessary trouble. Sui Yuntong pondered for a moment. “Go inform Lord Gao.” By sheer luck, when the two of them arrived, they bumped into An Jiu and Gao Dazhuang talking. Of course, she asked the same question. Normally, Gao Dazhuang’s piercing gaze would have been enough to kill her, but having received Mo Sigui’s generous gift, he was in an exceptionally good mood. So he merely rolled his eyes and grumbled, “You woke Grandpa up in the middle of the night just for this? Do you not know how busy Grandpa is usually? You are so inconsiderate!” Gao Dazhuang’s good mood was not just for today; he was not one to suffer in silence. A few days ago, fueled by pent-up anger, he had taken advantage of the dark of night to catch several eunuchs who often caused him trouble and give them a sound beating. Only then had his anger subsided somewhat. An Jiu, her blood boiling with excitement, completely oblivious to the cold shoulder, eagerly guessed, “If you dream of your little penis growing back, that’s a bit difficult. I wonder if Mo Sigui can make it happen.” Gao Dazhuang’s face turned green. He took off his shoes and started hitting An Jiu, yelling, “You little dwarf, you little blockhead, you lunatic! You have time to worry about my little penis? Why not call Physician Mo to cure your ailment!” An Jiu dodged incredibly fast, disappearing in a flash. Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi, fearing collateral damage, quickly and quietly retreated. Although An Jiu suffered a setback, her mood remained high. Regardless of whether her approach was correct, at least she had figured out a non-lethal objective. Suddenly, she felt fulfilled; this feeling was wonderful! Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi crept into their respective rooms, pretending they had not gone out all night. The next day, when it was her turn to be on duty, Sui Yuntong specifically pulled An Jiu outside to stand guard with him so that An Jiu would not be alone in the room and might run off to ask the Crown Prince if he had any dreams. An Jiu was still immersed in joy when Li Qingzhi, who had been personally protecting the Crown Prince four times, became depressed. Judging from his expression, An Jiu knew he must have witnessed the Crown Prince’s dissolute behavior! In the past two weeks, during her shifts, the Crown Prince had only missed two days without seeking out women, which meant he was probably “exercising” at least twenty-five days a month. It was not surprising that Li Qingzhi had caught him four times. The Crown Prince… was even more promiscuous than his father in this regard! The Emperor, being a Taoist, usually paid more attention to health and would not seek out someone for dual cultivation every day. “Looking at this Crown Prince, I really have no desire to serve him at all,” Li Qingzhi muttered, squatting by Sui Yuntong’s field ridge. While weeding, Sui Yuntong said, “Be careful what you say.” An Jiu said, “There’s no one else within ten zhang.” “How about we pledge allegiance to another master?” Li Qingzhi asked. Sui Yuntong considered the feasibility of this suggestion, then suddenly thought of something strange and lowered his voice, “I remember seeing in the records of the Konghe Army that the Dragon Martial Guards used to have a rule about taking poison. Why do we not have that?” “That team does,” An Jiu said, pointing to the neighboring courtyard. All three fell silent. After a while, Sui Yuntong beckoned to the two. Li Qingzhi and An Jiu leaned closer, and he whispered, “Could it be that Lord Gao withheld it…?” It was indeed possible! The Emperor trusted Gao Dazhuang greatly, and his unwavering loyalty had likely left a deep impression on the commander of the Konghe Army. The poison was most likely withheld before it reached him; otherwise, there was no reason why everyone else had taken it while they remained unharmed. If this were the case, then Gao Dazhuang must have ulterior motives! Sui Yuntong glanced at Li Qingzhi. “You cannot say such discouraging things anymore, lest you cause unnecessary trouble.” The Konghe Army members were people who never saw the light of day. Aside from missions, they usually minded their own business. But wherever there were people, there was conflict, and this place was no exception. There would always be those who crave power and engage in open and covert struggles. “I will go ask him once Lord Gao’s anger has subsided in the next few days,” Sui Yuntong said. An Jiu said, “What if it is not him?”

chapters.title: Meeting
chapters.content: What if Gao Dazhuang had not withheld the poison? If they questioned him, would it not expose that they had not taken the poison? Gao Dazhuang was so loyal; perhaps he’d made up for it? Thinking about it carefully, they really could not just speak up. The three discussed for a long time without coming up with a solution, so they went back to rest. After entering the room, An Jiu found a letter on the table. She saw a tiny “Chu” character written in the corner and opened it. Chu Dingjiang had already arranged for a replacement, instructing her to leave the palace in three days. Besides Mei Yanran, Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi would also be leaving with her. It turned out that Chu Dingjiang had not only taken Sui Yuntong under his wing but also Li Qingzhi. Of this group, Lou Mingyue was the most skilled in martial arts, and Qiu Yuntong was adept at using poison. Why did Chu Dingjiang specifically choose two people with mediocre abilities? An Jiu lit a lamp and burned the letter as she pondered this. Sighing, she wondered if Mei Yanran could leave with her in three days. Knock knock! Someone knocked on the door. An Jiu opened the door and saw Mei Yanran standing outside. “I’ve decided to go with you, but before that, I need to see Jiu’er,” Mei Yanran explained. Actually, she had already arrived at the Hua residence today, but there were many guards there, and she could not guarantee she would not alert them. She had considered writing a letter to invite Mei Jiu out, but she had some concerns, so to be on the safe side, she returned to find An Jiu. “Alright,” An Jiu said, “Wait a moment; I will go get the travel permit.” “No need.” Mei Yanran took out a token and tossed it to her. “This works too.” An Jiu caught the token and left the palace with her. When they left the palace, it was just beginning to get light. After changing into casual clothes, the two found a teahouse for breakfast. Mei Yanran had little appetite. Watching An Jiu, wearing a human skin mask, stuffing steamed buns into her mouth, she felt a pang of sadness. The teahouse was not crowded yet. Mei Yanran asked, “What did you do before?” An Jiu swallowed a large mouthful of steamed bun, then drank some soup to settle her throat. “The same as now.” The Konghe Army was full of female Shadows, and perhaps because An Jiu was now in Mei Yanran’s daughter’s body, it touched her somewhat. “What about your parents?” “They died long ago.” An Jiu sensed her weakened hostility and thought to herself that she finally understood where Mei Jiu’s personality came from. Although Mei Yanran was intelligent, like Mei Jiu, she would let her guard down for some inexplicable reason. “And you?” Mei Yanran asked. An Jiu wondered what she wanted to ask. After a moment’s hesitation, she said softly, “Died while on a mission.” The teahouse filled up quickly, and soon it was almost full, so Mei Yanran did not ask any more questions. An Jiu quickly finished a steamed bun, then drank her soup, glanced at the sky outside the window, and said, “Let’s go.” Mei Yanran thought An Jiu would have some way to get Mei Jiu to come out, but instead, she knocked directly on the front door. She told the gatekeeper, “We are looking for your Madam.” The Hua family only had two mistresses: the Grand Madam and the First Madam. Hua Rongtian held a high-ranking official position. His wife also had an imperial title, so to avoid confusion, everyone respectfully addressed the Prime Minister Hua’s wife as the Grand Madam. The gatekeeper, seeing that the two women were not dressed particularly well but possessed a certain air of authority, did not dare to be negligent. “You two have come at an inopportune time; our Madam is ill. She has not been receiving guests lately.” “We are from the Mei family. We heard she was ill and rushed over to see her,” An Jiu said. The gatekeeper glanced behind them, thinking to himself, “Coming to see the sick empty-handed? That’s a first!” However, the eldest son had instructed that the First Madam’s guests should not be neglected, so he said, “Please wait a moment; I will go and report.” Mei Yanran asked curiously, “Could it be that she is still a member of the Mei family?” “Yes, it was an imperial marriage,” An Jiu said. Mei Yanran then remembered that she had heard some time ago that the Emperor had bestowed a marriage upon the Hua family, but she had been away on missions and did not know the details. After about the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, the main gate opened again, and the gatekeeper said, “Please come in, both of you.” Mei Yanran’s hands, which were tucked into her sleeves, clenched tightly. Her palms were already damp as she walked from the main gate to the second gate. Mei Jiu was already waiting at the second gate, her face pale. It seemed she was truly ill, not just making excuses. Mei Jiu saw An Jiu wearing a human skin mask from afar and was slightly taken aback. “It’s me,” An Jiu said as she approached. She finally smiled, quickly approaching, tears welling in her eyes. “You’ve finally come to see me.” Mei Yanran looked at the unfamiliar, elegantly dressed woman, every smile, every gesture reminding her of Mei Jiu, and her own eyes immediately welled up with tears. Mei Jiu wanted to pull An Jiu closer, but considering An Jiu’s current male attire, she awkwardly withdrew her outstretched hands. Her gaze swept over Mei Yanran, paused slightly, and then she looked at An Jiu questioningly. Although Mei Yanran was still dressed as a woman, she wore a human skin mask, and Mei Jiu did not recognize her at first. An Jiu, fearing she might lose her composure in front of others, said, “Let’s go inside and talk.” Mei Jiu nodded, constantly glancing at Mei Yanran as she walked. She tripped on the steps, but fortunately, her maidservant caught her quickly enough to prevent her from falling. Once inside, Mei Jiu dismissed all the maidservants. Mei Jiu then looked closely at Mei Yanran. Their eyes met, and Mei Yanran’s voice choked. After a long pause, she tentatively called out, “Mother?” She could recognize her?! An Jiu glanced at Mei Yanran, thinking that even if her deceased mother was not completely unrecognizable, she probably would not recognize her standing before her now. Her mother’s emaciated appearance had left a deep imprint on her mind, to the point that her mother’s original features were blurred. “You two talk; I am going for a walk,” An Jiu said, turning to leave. Stepping out from behind the curtain, she heard Mei Yanran sigh, “Jiu’er.” This was followed by Mei Jiu’s sobs. The sun was shining brightly outside. An Jiu squatted on the steps, and a maidservant approached, saying, “Young master, why not sit in the pavilion over there?” “No, stay away from me,” An Jiu said coldly. The chilling voice made the maidservant’s hair stand on end, and she quickly retreated three feet away. The maid was a fourth-level martial artist, either an agent of the Emperor or Hua Rongtian. An Jiu turned to look at her. “Step back ten zhang.” The maid felt the oppressive aura emanating from An Jiu but bit her lip and stood motionless. An Jiu’s mental power suddenly erupted, pressing forward. The maid felt a buzzing in her head, her body going blank, and she collapsed to the ground. An Jiu got up, personally dragged her away, and threw her into the garden, then gave her another sharp slap on the back of the neck. “The one on the roof, do you want me to do it, or will you leave on your own?” An Jiu called out. The voices of Mei Yanran and Mei Jiu inside the house paused. After the person quietly retreated, An Jiu said to the person inside, “Continue, I will wait outside.” Interrupted, the mother and daughter inside stopped crying and began to talk about what had happened since they last met. Mei Jiu’s appearance was quite different from before. Mei Yanran initially found it awkward, but the noses of the Mei family members all looked very similar—small and high-bridged. Upon closer inspection, there was also a resemblance between her eyebrows and her original features. Combined with her expression when speaking, the overall impression became three or four parts similar to her former self. Mei Yanran simply attributed it to her daughter’s appearance maturing during her absence. An Jiu sat on the railing of the veranda, arms crossed, basking in the sun. Sensing a third or fourth-level martial artist approaching, she looked up. A young man in a blue robe entered. He carried a scroll, his handsome face radiant like the moon. His smile was still incredibly bright, but compared to before, he carried a more somber air. Hua Rongjian’s smile deepened when he saw the human skin mask on An Jiu’s face. “I did not expect you’d still be using it.” At this time, Hua Rongtian should be at court or in his official residence. An Jiu immediately asked, “What are you doing here? You would not even spare your own sister-in-law, would you?” Hua Rongjian was taken aback. “Is that what you think of me? All my deep affection and waiting for you for so long has been for nothing.” An Jiu did not believe him. “Really! As soon as I heard the gatekeeper say that someone from the Mei family was coming, I guessed it was you.” Hua Rongjian peeked out. “Why are you outside?” “None of your business,” An Jiu said. Hua Rongjian did not take it seriously and plopped down next to An Jiu. “What about what I told you last time? What have you thought about?” An Jiu thought for a moment, knowing what he meant. “I do not fancy you. Do you not think you’ve escaped a disaster?” Hua Rongjian chuckled. “Just kidding, do not take it seriously.” “Have you ever said anything serious?” An Jiu squinted at the pomegranates hanging heavily on the trees in the courtyard. Hua Rongjian unrolled the scroll and nudged her with his elbow. “This is a love token painted for us by Physician Mo.” An Jiu glanced at it sideways. “He painted it for you; what does it have to do with me?” “This one is female!” Hua Rongjian pointed to one of the females. An Jiu remained silent, looking at him as if he were an idiot. Hua Rongjian put down the scroll, his smile fading, his eyes filled with loneliness and bitterness. He might not really want to marry her; it was just that there were too few people around him whom he could confide in. He kept telling himself to live a good life and forget the mystery of his origins, but he could not help but notice it. He had not deliberately investigated, but after paying attention, something just did not feel right. “Fourteenth Young Lady,” Hua Rongjian slowly rolled up the scroll, “come have a drink with me.” An Jiu was full of questions. Her recent behavior seemed off! Why were people always confiding in her? Was Chu Dingjiang’s “confidant uncle” persona contagious? “Just drinking,” Hua Rongjian said. His eagerness to confide was obvious, and An Jiu did not doubt it. “Let’s see this afternoon.” Hua Rongjian finally smiled again. “Alright, as a reward, I will tell you that my elder brother will definitely be back at noon today.” Mei Jiu was sent by the Emperor, and Hua Rongtian would definitely be wary. Their sudden arrival today seemed likely to cause Mei Jiu some trouble! “How are your elder brother and sister-in-law getting along?” An Jiu asked. “Respectful to each other? That’s how it appears on the surface.” Hua Rongjian leaned closer to her and whispered, “But I heard they have not consummated their marriage yet.” Looking at his beaming face, An Jiu could not help but comment, “Sleazy.” “It was all said by the maids at home; I just overheard it!” Hua Rongjian said discontentedly. “You get the benefit, but do not forget to mock me!”

chapters.title: An Ordinary Man
chapters.content: “That Chunxin?” An Jiu remembered how heartbroken he was last time he cried. “It’s Chunmeng!” Hua Rongjian glanced back into the room. “There are not many people left in the Mei family, are there? Who’s inside?” An Jiu seemed not to hear him. “Would your elder brother harm your sister-in-law?” She remembered that Hua Rongtian’s first wife was an informant sent by the Emperor, and in the end, she devoted herself to him, refusing to do anything to harm him, even at the cost of her life. If a specially trained shadow was like that, An Jiu had reason to worry that Mei Jiu would become the second. “My elder brother is not that kind of person.” Hua Rongjian was quite confident about this. “After his first wife passed away, he was depressed for a long time. People say the Hua family produces devoted lovers, just like my father, who has only loved my mother all these years, and my younger brother, who always remembers his childhood sweetheart.” Hua Rongjun had a marriage agreement when he was young. At that time, the Hua family was not as powerful as it was today, so a marriage alliance with the Crown Prince’s tutor’s family was not a problem. The Crown Prince’s tutor rose through the ranks from Jiangning Prefecture, gaining considerable prestige and numerous students. Although he had never held real power, his connections were formidable. Hua Rongjun was well past marriageable age, yet Prime Minister Hua hesitated to allow him to marry. Hua Rongjian said, “My brother’s childhood sweetheart is the Crown Prince’s tutor’s granddaughter, and the tutor was also my father’s teacher…” The relationship was already quite close; how could the Emperor tolerate such a marriage alliance? Therefore, unless the Hua family fell, Hua Rongjun’s marriage would inevitably fall apart. An Jiu was not interested in this. She thought, “If Prime Minister Hua were truly so devoted, you would not exist!” An Jiu felt inexplicably uncomfortable and fell silent. After half an hour, Mei Yanran finally emerged. An Jiu saw her red eyes and did not ask anything. “Let’s go.” “Hey, we agreed to go drinking!” Hua Rongjian said, displeased. An Jiu hesitated. Mei Yanran said, “If you need anything, feel free to do as you please. Do not worry about me.” “Alright!” An Jiu sighed. The three of them left the mansion together. Hua Rongjian and An Jiu boarded the carriage, while Mei Yanran returned to the palace alone. The carriage took them to the slums. Hua Rongjian leaned against the window, no longer the lively person he usually was. After a while, the carriage stopped in front of a house. Hua Rongjian did not get out, peering through the bamboo curtain at the tightly closed gate, his brows gradually furrowing. This was Lu Danzhi’s residence. An Jiu had been here with him once before. Lu Danzhi’s death had changed Hua Rongjian’s life. He probably did not like coming here! An Jiu said, “I know a quiet place.” Hua Rongjian raised an eyebrow. “Let’s go then.” An Jiu knocked on the carriage wall and told the coachman where to go. “Once, I was wandering around and found a pretty good wonton place here,” An Jiu explained. “A decent wonton stall over here?” Hua Rongjian was skeptical. In such a poor place, let alone wontons, even meat broth was a luxury! Hua Rongjian loved to wander around. The coachman was familiar with the city’s streets and alleys, and in about the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, they arrived at the crossroads of the river. The carriage could not go any further, so An Jiu dragged Hua Rongjian out and walked towards Wu Lingyuan’s wonton jars. Even before they reached the location, a rich aroma wafted out. Hua Rongjian looked incredulous. An Jiu, smelling the aroma, was also somewhat surprised. Last time, Wu Lingyuan had used lard to impersonate pork, and the wontons in the clear broth had been sitting there for who knew how long. How could things have changed so much in such a short time! Turning a corner, An Jiu saw a man in a greyish-white robe lying on the riverbank under the shade of willows. His face was covered with a copy of the Great Compassion Mantra, and he held a fishing rod, looking relaxed and content. The stall still had the same tattered table and chairs, with steam rising from the pot on the charcoal stove beside it. Wu Lingyuan heard footsteps, his ears twitched slightly, and he removed the Buddhist scripture from his face with his thin, slender hand, smiling as he asked, “Is it my benefactor?” An Jiu sat down on the stool behind him and hummed in agreement. Wu Lingyuan got up and secured his fishing rod. “I prepared some for my benefactor long ago,” Hua Rongjian, seeing his handsome appearance but his lifeless eyes, roughly guessed his predicament. “Do you have any wine?” Wu Lingyuan shook his head. “I can have someone fetch a pot. Please wait a moment.” An Jiu held out her hand to Hua Rongjian. “Give me the money.” Hua Rongjian took out his purse and pulled out the few loose silver coins he had, placing them in her hand. An Jiu tried to give them to Wu Lingyuan. “How can I accept money from my benefactor?” Wu Lingyuan quickly refused. “Anyway, it is not my money. The man next to me is so deplorable that he has only money left. You do not need to save for him,” An Jiu said. Wu Lingyuan smiled. “Then I will have to accept your kind words.” Hua Rongjian unconsciously relaxed at his gentle smile, watching Wu Lingyuan leave, and said, “That man is no ordinary person.” An Jiu went to the stove, lifted the pot lid, and steam mingled with the aroma of chicken, rising and hitting her face. “Compared to you, how can he be considered ordinary?” “I invited you here to talk and relieve my boredom, not to have you annoy me,” Hua Rongjian said, displeased. “If you want to hear something nice, you can pay someone to flatter you. I only have the truth here.” An Jiu ladled a bowl of chicken soup and handed it to Hua Rongjian. Seeing her still serving him soup while scolding him, Hua Rongjian felt a warmth in his heart. He took the bowl, drank a couple of sips, and praised, “Not bad, quite delicious. This chicken is a pheasant.” After he drank most of the bowl, seeing An Jiu had not drunk any, he asked, “Why are you not drinking?” An Jiu was silent for a moment, and seeing that he was alright, she ladled a bowl for herself as well. “When you are out and about, you have to be careful.” Especially in places she had been. Hua Rongjian’s face darkened instantly. “Fourteenth Young Lady, you really are… really…” He could not find the words to describe her! After finishing their soup and chatting for a while, Wu Lingyuan returned, carrying two jars of wine. “Have some wontons to tide you over before you drink?” he said. The soup had whetted their appetites, and Hua Rongjian agreed. Wu Lingyuan washed his hands and began rolling out wonton wrappers. Despite his blindness, he worked quickly, wrapping twenty or thirty in no time. Seeing no one around, Hua Rongjian asked, “Do you have any business here?” Wu Lingyuan replied, “Yes, quite a few boats dock here in the mornings. I am busy for about an hour a day.” “No one causes trouble?” Hua Rongjian asked. Wu Lingyuan put the wontons into the pot. “The people here are kind and honest. I often teach the children to read. They often bring me food, and no one causes trouble.” Those local thugs did not come to this poor place either. He prepared a portion for An Jiu every day; if An Jiu did not come, he let the neighbors take it. Two steaming bowls of wontons were served. An Jiu took a bite and was surprised to find that Wu Lingyuan’s cooking was truly excellent. The wontons were fresh and delicious, the outer skin smooth and refreshing, and the meat inside not greasy but chewy. Hua Rongjian finished one bowl and asked for another. His initial worries vanished instantly, and even the wine became a post-meal enjoyment. After the meal, Hua Rongjian inquired further about Wu Lingyuan’s background. It turned out that Wu Lingyuan was a nobleman from the Tang Dynasty. When the Tang Dynasty fell, his family moved south. Wu Lingyuan was on his way to the capital to take the imperial examinations, but unfortunately contracted an eye ailment and could not return. His parents had long since passed away, so he planned to spend the rest of his life here. Hua Rongjian sighed, “I will find a physician to examine you tomorrow.” After saying that, he turned to An Jiu and asked, “Where’s Physician Mo?” “He’s currently troubled by love,” An Jiu said. Hua Rongjian asked with interest, “Which love?” “He has many?” An Jiu raised an eyebrow. “How would I know? Otherwise, why would I be asking you?” Hua Rongjian scoffed. Anyone who did not know Mo Sigui thought he was a miracle physician who saved lives. Those who knew him casually thought he was indifferent and cold in matters of the heart. Only someone like An Jiu knew what the real Mo Sigui was like. “He’s infatuated with a woman, but that woman does not like him,” An Jiu said. Hua Rongjian looked at her with disdain. “Boring.” However, he believed that stripping away the exciting details, what An Jiu said was undoubtedly the truth. Having lost interest, Hua Rongjian dragged Wu Lingyuan fishing. An Jiu sat on a stool. Looking at Hua Rongjian’s back, she noticed he had grown taller and thinner. Hua Rongjian was a very cheerful person; his smile was like warm sunshine. Such a person should not have become so gloomy. Thinking this, she suddenly felt some resentment towards Chu Dingjiang’s actions back then, but then she felt this feeling was inexplicable. She herself had countless lives on her hands; what right did she have to criticize Chu Dingjiang? The two stayed at the wonton stall until sunset before strolling away along the riverbank with two jars of wine. “How about we have a fight?” Hua Rongjian suddenly said. “Heh.” An Jiu squinted at the golden-red sky. “You should just drown your sorrows in alcohol. If a real fight breaks out, I reckon someone will find the bodies of the two Hua sons drowned in the river tomorrow.” “…” Hua Rongjian sat down by the riverbank, opened the jar, and gulped it down. An Jiu sat down beside him. “Lu Danzhi said I am not actually twenty-six.” Hua Rongjian wiped the wine from his lips, propped himself up on the jar, and turned to look at her. “I had amnesia when I was little, supposedly due to illness, but considering all the circumstances, I cannot help but suspect that the real Hua Rongjian died for some reason, and then I was used to take his place.” An Jiu fell silent. The truth was pretty much what he suspected, but he would probably never guess that it was the real Hua Rongjian who orchestrated it. She knew the truth, but she could not tell Hua Rongjian. Seeing him like this, she could not say a word. “But I look a lot like my older brother and younger brother, and my parents treat me very well.” Hua Rongjian doubted his mother. She spoiled him too much, unlike how she was strict with his older and younger brothers. If he had not been pampered like this from a young age, perhaps he would not have wasted his life as he had before. “Mothers usually love their youngest child more, do they not? Why does my mother spoil me so much?” Grand Madam Hua also loved Hua Rongjun, but unlike with him, she often disciplined him. Before Lu Danzhi spoke, he only felt that his mother loved him more than his two brothers, but now it seemed that was not the case. “Am I being very unfilial? To doubt my mother?” Hua Rongjian looked at her, his eyes shimmering as if about to overflow with tears.

chapters.title: Falling into the Water
chapters.content: An Jiu avoided his gaze. “It’s rare to be confused.” Thinking about it now, she suddenly understood the helplessness contained in those words; perhaps only someone who had lived clearly could say such a thing. Night fell, and occasionally boats passed by on the water, their lights reflected in the water like starlight. Seeing him half-drunk, An Jiu asked, “If the truth is as you suspect, what do you plan to do?” Hua Rongjian lay on the altar. “I just want to know why, yet I am afraid to know.” “Perhaps… Prime Minister Hua had you with another woman, and the real Hua Rongjian unfortunately died young, so he took you back to raise,” An Jiu said. “The things being hidden might not be that serious.” Hua Rongjian looked up at An Jiu’s profile. She wore a human skin mask; her features were delicate, her eyes were lowered, and her long eyelashes cast shadows beneath them. “What you said… is possible.” Hua Rongjian sighed and smiled. “Perhaps I am overthinking it.” Lu Danzhi told him because he was afraid he was living in a daze. As a friend, it was natural to worry about his safety. If Lu Danzhi had not died, he might never have revealed this. Thinking of Lu Danzhi, Hua Rongjian sighed, “The Cui family line was completely extinguished because of a woman!” “Yelu Huangwu?” An Jiu asked. Hua Rongjian nodded. “If Cui Yichen had not known Yelu Huangwu, she would not have known about the Cui family, the Cui family would not have fallen, Cui Yichen would not have gone mad, and Danzhi would not have died… This woman, she really has some impressive methods.” An Jiu said, “Not only the Cui family, but the Mei and Lou families were also destroyed in an instant, were they not?” “Khitan men are jackals, and women are venomous snakes,” Hua Rongjian said. “How could the Song Dynasty, with its abundance of Confucian scholars, possibly defeat such enemies?” “It seems you are not content to be a fool.” An Jiu looked at him with newfound respect. Hua Rongjian glared at her. “This young master has never been a fool!” “I used the wrong words,” An Jiu thought carefully for a moment. “Was it a pretty face but no substance?” Hua Rongjian reached out to flick her, and An Jiu instinctively blocked him with her hand. He was holding a wine jar in one hand, his center of gravity swaying, his body staggering. “Quick, Fourteenth Young Lady, grab me!” Splash! An Jiu watched helplessly as he fell into the water, the wine jar still in his hand. At first, the empty jar floated on the water for a couple of breaths, but after being filled with water, it quickly sank. Hua Rongjian thrashed to the riverbank. Grabbing onto the grass on the bank, he leaped out of the water, creating a splash like a torrential downpour. An Jiu, still holding the wine jar in one hand, quickly pulled an oilcloth umbrella from behind her with the other, opened it, and looked back at Hua Rongjian, who had fallen not far behind her. Hua Rongjian, with his cool and arrogant demeanor, noticed the water splashing against her umbrella. An Jiu’s calm gaze swept over his body through the cascading water. He looked down and saw his silk robes, soaked and clinging to his skin, revealing his figure. Even his nipples and the bulge in his crotch were clearly visible. Even fine clothing had its drawbacks! “Why are you carrying an umbrella on such a sunny day?” Hua Rongjian exclaimed, annoyed and embarrassed. “When you are out and about, you always have to be prepared.” An Jiu used to not carry an umbrella; the umbrella in her hand was actually a weapon, its edges inlaid with sharp blades. The ribs were also detachable weapons, and pressing a mechanism on the handle could even fire poison needles. This was Lou Xiaowu’s prized creation among her hidden weapons. Originally an ordinary oilcloth umbrella, inspired by An Jiu, Lou Xiaowu modified it into a folding umbrella, folding it to only a foot long. Lou Xiaowu was overjoyed. She gave it to her as a thank-you gift. An Jiu quite liked it; it was a good self-defense tool when it was not convenient to carry the Dragon-Subduing Bow. She just had not expected to use it for the first time under these circumstances. She carried many weapons, which would easily be exposed if her clothes got wet; she would not use this unless absolutely necessary. “Talking to you all day has only made me feel worse!” Hua Rongjian took off his outer robe and wrung it out. An Jiu closed the umbrella and put it in the bag behind her. Hua Rongjian’s attention was drawn to the umbrella. “Huh, you have one of these umbrellas, too.” “You’ve seen it before?” An Jiu asked curiously; there should only be one in the entire Song Dynasty! “Yes, I have twenty or thirty at home.” Hua Rongjian wrung out his clothes as he sat down on the grass beside her. “Recently, a shop opened in the capital that specializes in selling these strange and unusual things, and these folding umbrellas are the most popular.” If they were selling so well, Lou Xiaowu, as an expert in this area, should not be unaware of them. “When did they start selling these umbrellas in the capital?” “About ten days ago,” Hua Rongjian said with a smile. “That shop also takes on various private jobs, mainly custom-made cheat codes for students preparing for the imperial examinations, such as hiding questions in the umbrella handle—small creations that only cost two taels of silver.” “The shopkeeper’s surname is not Lou, is it?” An Jiu thought Lou Xiaowu did not seem like the type to have this kind of mind. “No,” Hua Rongjian said, “His surname is Zhu.” Zhu Pianxian? The name flashed through An Jiu’s mind. Seeing her apparent interest, Hua Rongjian said, “She’s a very interesting young widow.” An Jiu glared. “You do not even spare young widows?” Sheng Changying’s face would turn bright red every time he saw Zhu Pianxian; anyone with eyes could see he was interested in her. An Jiu had a good impression of Sheng Changying, always thinking it extremely difficult for someone as rigid as him to be moved by love. Before Hua Rongjian could answer, An Jiu earnestly advised, “You are a womanizer who does not discriminate between men and women, young and old; you can leave this one for someone else to mess with!” “No wonder I’ve never been able to mess with you,” Hua Rongjian laughed. “Physician Mo said there are four kinds of people in this world: men, women, eunuchs, and Fourteenth Young Lady. It is true.” An Jiu snorted. “He never says anything nice.” “Your words sound like a thief crying, ‘Stop thief!'” Hua Rongjian said. “You saw through me.” An Jiu stood up, looking down at him. “A fool’s world must be simple, right? You only have trouble because you suddenly became a little more intelligent. Keep being a fool; do not try to become more intelligent.” She shoved the wine jar into his arms and turned to leave. Hua Rongjian did not chase after her. He watched her walk about ten paces away, then called out, “Fourteenth Young Lady! You bastard!” An Jiu stopped and turned back, looking at him expressionlessly. “Great! You did not realize this was comforting, which means you are still a happy fool. I am happy for you!” “Pshaw! Who said I did not realize it? But this gentleman is not happy about it!” Hua Rongjian roared. “Is that so? That’s because you have not found the right way to be happy.” An Jiu tossed out a sentence and vanished into the night. Hua Rongjian looked at the vast night and suddenly laughed, tilting his head back and gulping down a mouthful of wine. A servant from the Hua family rushed over upon hearing the commotion. Seeing his clothes soaked to the bone, he quickly unfolded his cloak. “Young Master, you’ve fallen into the water?” “Yes, how refreshing!” Hua Rongjian smiled. The servant’s eyes welled with tears. “Young Master has not smiled like this in so long.”

chapters.title: Wonderful Ideas Tower
chapters.content: Hua Rongjian flicked the servant’s forehead, tossed the wine jar into the river, and strolled along the riverbank with his hands behind his back. After leaving, An Jiu did not rush back to the palace but wandered the streets alone for a while. The lanterns were just coming on. The Song Dynasty had a curfew, but shops on two streets were allowed to close at midnight. These two streets were mostly lined with official and private brothels; other shops benefited from their influence. The private brothels that could operate on this street all had powerful backers, and the girls inside were bought from poor families. An Jiu watched the brightly dressed girls standing upstairs, sweetly greeting customers, her thoughts drifting away. When she first arrived, this body of hers had escaped from a brothel and was still being pursued. Now, almost three years had passed since she arrived, and her hands were stained with blood, but she could clearly feel that her life was different from before. In her long-closed world, she was finally no longer alone. Even walking alone on the street now, she felt much more fulfilled, no longer feeling that sense of being abandoned by the world. Dark clouds obscured the moon, and within half an hour, rain began to fall in drizzles. Many people on the street opened their folding umbrellas. An Jiu, who had already quickened her pace, slowed down upon seeing this and strolled in the rain with her own umbrella. Although there were many folding umbrellas, the one in her hand was the most dangerous. With the umbrella providing cover, An Jiu felt more at ease. She noticed a bustling crowd in front of a shop not far ahead and curiously went to investigate. It turned out that the shopkeeper, seeing the rain, had placed portable folding umbrellas under the eaves for sale at the same price as usual. It seemed they were not trying to make a quick buck from the rain but genuinely offering convenience. An Jiu looked up and saw the signboard read “Zhu’s Wonderful Ideas Tower.” A slight smile appeared on her lips as she closed her umbrella and went into the shop. The shopkeeper, with his keen eye, noticed that the folding umbrella in An Jiu’s hand was more exquisite than the ones sold in the shop. Guessing he was a friend of the shopkeeper, the attendant’s smile grew even more ingratiating. “What would you like to buy, My Lord?” An Jiu did not waste any more words. “I am looking for Zhu Pianxian.” Seeing his cold expression, the attendant dared not engage in further conversation and hurriedly said, “Please sit here and wait a moment. I will have someone inform her right away.” An Jiu did not sit down as instructed, standing straight in the middle of the room, radiating a faint yet palpable aura of coldness. Water droplets from his umbrella dripped onto the wooden floor, but no one dared to approach him. A moment later, a voluptuous woman came out to greet him. Zhu Pianxian had first seen An Jiu wearing this human skin mask, so she recognized him immediately and approached him familiarly. “Good brother, what brings you to see your sister? Look how damp you are! Come with me to the back for a cup of tea.” An Jiu followed her into the backyard without a word. She finally spoke, “Staying on this street, you’ve picked up the habits of those girls.” Look at what she just said; anyone who did not know better would think she’d wandered into the wrong place! Zhu Pianxian spat. “We have not seen each other in ages, and now that we meet, there’s no need for pleasantries. I am just not cut from the start!” Upon hearing this, An Jiu could not help but look at her more closely. She was not like this before; she always acted coy and sweet, calling herself “this humble servant” at every turn. Zhu Pianxian was utterly astonished to see An Jiu. Forgetting even her pretense, she quickly tried to recover, half-covering her mouth and nose with her sleeve, and said in a coquettish voice, “This humble servant was simply too excited to see an old friend.” Since she wanted to exchange pleasantries, An Jiu readily obliged, saying, “You’ve gained weight.” Zhu Pianxian’s eye twitched, and without bothering to cover her face, she touched her chubby cheeks anxiously, asking, “Where have I gained weight?” An Jiu raised her hand and slowly and deliberately tapped her face, neck, chest, and waist. “The good thing is, you’ve gained weight in the right places too.” The literati of the Song Dynasty did not appreciate a woman as plump as Zhu Pianxian. They believed that a woman’s figure should be as slender as an orchid, her face as pure and elegant as a pear blossom, and her temperament as ethereal as a lotus. “With you around, I feel like life is not beautiful anymore!” Zhu Pianxian flung her wide sleeves; Chu Dingjiang was not watching, and she was too lazy to pretend in front of An Jiu. An Jiu had a favorable impression of people like Zhu Pianxian. Although Zhu was sometimes hypocritical and pretentious, she was generally a straightforward and proactive person. “Lord Chu asked me to come out and make money for him and others. The thought of all that hard-earned money going into other people’s pockets makes my heart ache,” Zhu Pianxian began to ramble on, probably seeing An Jiu’s silence. “But thinking about it, doing some business is much more interesting than being locked up there, especially since someone can afford to invest the capital to buy this building in the capital.” Zhu Pianxian was not interested in ordinary small businesses, but she did not have any grand ambitions; she just felt a great sense of accomplishment from making large sums of money. The room was filled with a rich fragrance, exuding an air of opulence. An Jiu’s aesthetic sense was average, but she could not say the same for Zhu Pianxian’s. Zhu Pianxian invited her to sit down and had tea served. “What brings you here?” To be honest, Chu Dingjiang brought Zhu Pianxian to the capital mainly to keep An Jiu company. She assumed An Jiu had come to visit her, which explained her initial tone. Zhu Pianxian was a woman with a particularly self-deprecating spirit and was very easygoing. Regardless of societal opinions, she acted however she pleased in private. She might put on a show of politeness, but it was rather perfunctory. “Just taking a stroll.” The room was filled with fragrant aromas, and An Jiu could not even drink a sip of tea. “Tell me, how did you persuade Lou Xiaowu to collaborate with you?” In her previous life, Lou Xiaowu would have been a pure academic genius, wishing all worldly affairs were irrelevant to her, focusing solely on her research. She’d even consider eating a waste of time; how could she possibly want to go out and do business to make money? “It’s difficult to say, yet easy in fact,” Zhu Pianxian said calmly, sipping her tea. “Her spending on those things was considerable; the Lou family’s savings were not enough for her extravagant spending. After cooperating with me, she only needs to open her mouth, and I will have my people find it for her from all corners of the country. I handle all the trivial matters for her. I am not some exploitative merchant; why would she not be happy?” Zhu Pianxian was indeed very shrewd. She treated Lou Xiaowu with more devotion than a deity, even thinking of things that were delicious and time-saving, and she did not ask for things very often. Besides those custom-made ingenious mechanisms, she could find every possible way to make money from ordinary gadgets, intending to only bother Lou Xiaowu when she felt she had almost run out of profit to squeeze out. Furthermore, Zhu Pianxian’s demands were often tricky and ingenious, which Lou Xiaowu found very challenging. Sometimes, when a customer wanted something, but Lou Xiaowu did not find it interesting, Zhu Pianxian would provoke her with words. Lou Xiaowu’s emotional intelligence was even lower than An Jiu’s; she was clearly destined to be completely outmatched. She’d only been working with Zhu Pianxian for half a month, yet she already felt she could not live without her. In short, since Zhu Pianxian joined her, Lou Xiaowu’s appetite had returned, her life was carefree, and she worked with even more enthusiasm. Upon learning of Zhu Pianxian’s capabilities, An Jiu thought to herself that her judgment was indeed excellent. Zhu Pianxian put down her teacup, leaned forward slightly, and looked serious. An Jiu thought she was about to say something very important, but instead, she heard her say, “Have I really gained weight?” An Jiu paused slightly, nodded firmly, and then, fearing Zhu Pianxian would not believe her, described it in detail, “Your features were already small, and your face was big. Before, you could barely look like a Tang Dynasty beauty, but now your face is a whole size bigger than before. It looks like a pile of flesh has squeezed your eyes, nose, and mouth together.” Zhu Pianxian stared at her blankly. An Jiu, adding insult to injury, said, “Look, you used to have a double chin; now you have a triple chin…” “Xiaowu is much more likable than you!” Zhu Pianxian rolled her eyes, leaning back worriedly. Sheng Changying was a typical scholar; he probably did not like fat people! After thinking about that, Zhu Pianxian glanced at An Jiu again. An Jiu and Lou Xiaowu were similar types—both specialized in one area, practically idiots in everything else. However, they were on completely different paths. Even when Lou Xiaowu was angry, she would only glare with her big, almond-shaped eyes. This one was much more troublesome! Zhu Pianxian really did not know how to deal with An Jiu. If she flattered her, An Jiu would not say anything nice; if she did not, it seemed she could not afford to offend her. “Are you not quite close to Mo Sigui?” An Jiu asked, seeing her bitter and resentful expression. “Why not ask him to prescribe some diet pills for you?” Zhu Pianxian’s eyes lit up, overjoyed. “Oh my, it is rare to see someone so likable!”

chapters.title: Heartbroken
chapters.content: An Jiu truly did not understand what made her so happy that she could not even remember things that did not require much thought. But then An Jiu remembered something else. Mo Sigui was in the Konghe Army, and Zhu Pianxian should not be able to come and go freely there. Chu Dingjiang certainly would not ask him for help over such a trivial matter. “Mo Sigui is out, too?” “Yes! He went back to Mei Mansion, did you not know?” Zhu Pianxian said. An Jiu shook her head. “Ten days ago, he suddenly resigned from his post at court, saying he wanted to return to Mei Mansion to devote himself to medical research. I do not know why. I went to see him once; he buried himself in a pile of medicinal herbs, not even lifting his eyelids.” Zhu Pianxian sighed; she was surrounded by people like this, even Sheng Changying was the same. Thinking of Sheng Changying, Zhu Pianxian felt a pang of heartache. “Others are engrossed in their work because they are absorbed in it, but Changying forces himself. If he does not do a lot every day, he cannot even sleep soundly, afraid of falling behind and having to live a hard life.” “You two have already progressed to sleeping together?” An Jiu completely missed the point. After asking, she felt she was becoming increasingly sophisticated, even possessing such a high-level attitude towards life as gossip, and secretly applauded herself. “No!” Zhu Pianxian was, after all, a native of the Song Dynasty. Even in the most open-minded places, she was not this open. An Jiu’s question was so explicit that her face, like a steamed bun, flushed red instantly. An Jiu, however, stared at her intently, adopting a very devout and serious posture, waiting for an answer. She was so embarrassed that she wanted to bury An Jiu with silver. Everyone knew Sheng Changying was not sleeping well, and An Jiu did not believe Zhu Pianxian at all when she said they had not slept together. She pondered for a moment, then said very considerately, “Do not worry, I am tight-lipped. Even psychological hypnosis cannot get a single word out of me.” This infuriated Zhu Pianxian. Pointing tremblingly at the doorway, she took a long breath before finally managing to say, “Grandma, you should go see Physician Mo. He’s been very unhappy lately.” Hearing this, An Jiu’s confidence suddenly surged. She felt she would definitely adapt to a normal life more and more, so she nodded to Zhu Pianxian and left with a light, cheerful step. Zhu Pianxian clutched her chest, panting heavily. Once she finally calmed down, she quickly instructed her maid, “Next time you see that person, just say I went out on business.” An Jiu dashed out of the city like the wind, not even needing a horse, and walked on foot under her umbrella to the plum blossom grove. Mei Mansion had been cleaned up; the entrance no longer bore the desolation of the fire that had ravaged it years ago. An Jiu pondered that Mo Sigui was the precious darling of the Konghe Army. They certainly would not trust him to come out alone, so she concealed her presence, using her mental power to hide herself, and entered smoothly. Mei Mansion was vast. An Jiu had a gut feeling he would be in his old thatched hut. She followed the clues and, sure enough, saw a window open, letting out a dim light. An Jiu stood holding an umbrella, gazing into the rain. The Konghe Army’s hidden guards quickly spotted her, but Mo Sigui was unaware of their presence, so they dared not rashly intercept her. They could only remain on guard, ready to rush out at any moment if An Jiu intended to harm Mo Sigui. As An Jiu was still figuring out how to get in, a small tiger leaped out from under the door, darting to her feet in the rain. Then, the door creaked open, and Mo Sigui stood at the doorway, hands at his sides. “Come in, or stand there like a tree stump in the rain?” An Jiu took Da Jiu in her arms and strode to the porch, where she closed her umbrella. In the dim light, she looked at Mo Sigui; he still had that carefree, nonchalant expression, as if nothing had happened with Lou Mingyue. However, he had become terribly thin. An Jiu had just learned the art of small talk from Zhu Pianxian, and now it came in handy. “I just saw Zhu Pianxian; she’s gained a lot of weight. If you could have some of that, you would not be so thin and unsightly.” Mo Sigui took a deep breath and turned to go inside. An Jiu followed. Mo Sigui raised his chin, his mood somewhat gloomy, and said, “There’s tea on the table. Pour yourself some if you are not afraid of being poisoned.” She put Da Jiu down, poured herself a glass of water, and thought to herself that Mo Sigui probably felt the same way—that small talk was not important. Mo Sigui leaned back on the couch, watching An Jiu watch as he held a long pipe, puffing out clouds of smoke. “If you are here to comfort me, you do not need to. I am very happy.” An Jiu was not sure. Did they even have tobacco these days? Was he addicted to opium? Had he really fallen so low? Mo Sigui did not speak, his face blurred by the smoke. His thin face made his peach blossom eyes stand out even more, revealing a deep, captivating charm amidst his former dashing appearance. Although his face was not as handsome as before, it was even more alluring. However, An Jiu could not see any joy in him. The smoke drifted over, and An Jiu smelled a strong medicinal odor, realizing he was not smoking tobacco or drugs. Mo Sigui, observing her expression, said, “I am not so easily defeated that I need to numb myself with hibiscus ointment.” Pipes and hibiscus ointment had existed for a long time, supposedly introduced during the Tang Dynasty when all nations paid tribute. A small number of people had used them, but it was unclear whether they still did. Mo Sigui noticed this stuff while browsing records; he discovered it seemed to have medicinal uses and even collected some poppy seeds, planning to plant them the following year. As for the pipe, it was because he’d been having trouble sleeping lately, staying up for seven or eight days straight. Not wanting to appear cowardly, he’d been taking medication. He had not actually fainted, but the direct consequence was severe insomnia. Even when his body was utterly exhausted, lying in bed with his eyes closed, his thoughts would not settle. However, a strange pride prevented him from brewing a bowl of sleeping pills, so he thought of inhaling the smoke to treat his insomnia. Initially, he burned it in an incense burner, but everyone else in the courtyard slept soundly, while he alone tossed and turned in bed, his eyes bloodshot. Then, while fiddling with poppies, he remembered the pipe, and a flash of inspiration struck him—using this method of inhaling the smoke finally solved his insomnia. An Jiu asked curiously, “Heartbreak can be treated with medicine?” Mo Sigui narrowed his eyes, a wisp of smoke escaping his lips as he spoke. “Would you lose a piece of flesh if you did not poke at someone’s sore spot?” “Sorry,” An Jiu said. The herbs had burned out. Mo Sigui tapped them on the table, cleaning out the residue. “It’s nothing. Maybe poking at it will numb the feeling?” He was saying this, and he was saying that too. An Jiu simply shut up. “Why did you come to see me in the middle of the night?” Mo Sigui yawned, his gaze slightly hazy as he looked at An Jiu. Why did everyone seem to think there had to be a reason for meeting? An Jiu patiently explained, “I just suddenly felt like coming.” Mo Sigui yawned again and held out his hand to her. An Jiu instinctively offered her wrist. Mo Sigui’s cool fingers took hold and released after a moment, but did not let it fall. An Jiu then instinctively offered her her other wrist as well. After checking her pulse for a while, he mumbled, “Not bad. How’s your Plum Blossom Fist practice going lately?” Was this just small talk? An Jiu thought everyone’s progress might be different, so she answered seriously, “I’ve been busy with missions, so I have not had much time to practice and have not seen any results yet.” “You are not making any progress! You are not taking it easy on yourself, and all my medicine is going down the wrong path! I hate bastards like you who do not follow medical advice.” Mo Sigui leaned back in his chair, closed his heavy eyelids, and said slowly, “The medicine you are taking now contains Gu Jinghong’s lifeblood.
