A prime minister and a powerful general, if they joined forces, would surely make the Song Dynasty collapse. Prime Minister Hua wanted to speak up for Ling Ziyue, but he was burdened by many concerns. The memorial had been written three days ago, but he had not yet submitted it. He quickly calmed down from his initial shock and anger, regaining his usual composure and wisdom. “You’ve repeatedly advised me to retire; your purpose was not to protect the Hua family, was it?” Even if he retired, the Hua family’s power and influence would not suddenly disappear, and the Emperor might not necessarily let him go. However, doing this would at least preserve a portion of the Hua family’s bloodline and strength. But once Prime Minister Hua retired and Ling Ziyue died, the precarious state of the Song Dynasty would become undeniably apparent. What Chu Dingjiang had done was detrimental to the Song Dynasty. Prime Minister Hua had to think more deeply. “You must feel you are in a bind now?” Chu Dingjiang tapped his fingers lightly on the memorial, speaking calmly. “The Song Dynasty lacks nothing, except a good Emperor.” Prime Minister Hua’s brow twitched, and he subconsciously glanced out the window. After a moment of silence, Prime Minister Hua frowned. “What do you mean?” He truly felt trapped; suddenly giving up now would be detrimental to the country. If he stubbornly persisted, he would eventually suffer the same fate as Ling Ziyue. He originally thought he would die first, but unexpectedly, Ling Ziyue fell first. How could the usually composed and patient Ling Ziyue suddenly act so recklessly? Prime Minister Hua gave Chu Dingjiang a deep, thoughtful look. Knowing his doubts, Chu Dingjiang changed the subject. “Do you think the scholars of the Song Dynasty lack backbone?” Prime Minister Hua pondered for a moment, “What scholars lack is not backbone, but courage.” “Scholars do not lack backbone, nor do they lack courage.” To understand the current state of Confucianism, Chu Dingjiang often read the works of highly respected Confucian scholars of his time. “They appear weak because the slap has not landed squarely on their faces yet! Influenced by Confucian thought, they are destined to retreat step by step, only revealing their stubborn and unyielding spirit when there is nowhere left to retreat.” Therefore, they would say, “This is intolerable!” “I will stop here.” Chu Dingjiang paused, stood up, and said, “I hope you will reconsider.” Seeing him about to leave, Prime Minister Hua’s tone became urgent: “I want to know why you left the Hua family back then.” “Because I did not want to again be bound to the Hua family for the rest of my life.” Chu Dingjiang slipped out of the room. Prime Minister Hua noticed the use of the word “again,” a thought flashing through his mind, but he quickly dismissed it. Confucius did not speak of strange phenomena, physical prowess, disorder, or spirits; Prime Minister Hua was also a Confucian. He carefully considered Chu Dingjiang’s words and put himself in his shoes—it was indeed true! If he were just an ordinary scholar, and iron cavalry were about to trample him into the mud, he would certainly fight back. But before the fire reached his eyebrows, he would feel he had time to calmly devise a countermeasure. To make the Song people feel a real sense of crisis and anger, his sudden voluntary retirement alone was not enough; it also needed to be coupled with… Ling Ziyue’s blood and the Song Dynasty’s crushing defeat. If Ling Ziyue lived, he might have secured peace on the border, but if he died unjustly, given the Song people’s mentality, most would not dare blame the Emperor entirely but would instead unleash their anger on the Liao Dynasty, though they would inevitably harbor resentment and hatred towards the Emperor. The Song Dynasty’s most urgent task was to ignite the Song people’s fighting spirit and, secondly, to enthrone a new Emperor. Prime Minister Hua only needed to add fuel to the fire, carefully maneuvering his actions. He would submit a memorial in defense of Ling Ziyue, then be implicated and dismissed from his post, thus avoiding the storm. He would return to power when the Song Dynasty desperately needed someone to shoulder the responsibility… If a drastic measure was not taken before a new one was established, even if Ling Ziyue captured Xijin Prefecture today and held it firmly, the Liao people would surely launch a counterattack after his death. Even a rabbit would bite when cornered, let alone a mad wolf! To entrust the safety of the entire nation to one person was truly worrying. It would be better to kill this pillar of the nation, splattering his blood on the faces of the Song people, letting them watch helplessly as the sky collapsed. If they did not rise up in resistance, they would only await their death… “What a treacherous and vicious plan!” Prime Minister Hua sighed. Prime Minister Hua had considered installing a new Emperor, but the Zhao family simply did not have a suitable candidate. The Crown Prince was out of the question; Prime Minister Hua had been relentlessly seeking fault with him, looking for an opportune moment to impeach him. His numerous transgressions were simply unbearable. Next was the Second Prince; he was martial, with a strong and unyielding personality, but he neglected his studies and acted impulsively. The Third Prince was too young; if he were to ascend the throne, the Song Dynasty would be thrown into chaos, so he could not be relied upon for the time being. Choosing the tallest among the short, only the Second Prince was a viable option… Prime Minister Hua never imagined that his predicament would be so easily resolved by Chu Dingjiang. No, he resolved not only the Hua family’s deadlock but also the Song Dynasty’s! It was said that the Northern King of Liao had captured Ling Ziyue’s woman and had been constantly humiliating him in an attempt to provoke him. Ling Ziyue’s misstep must be due to Liao’s interference. And in this game, the Liao, the Song Dynasty, and even Ling Ziyue and himself were all pawns in Chu Dingjiang’s hands. The person behind the Liao Kingdom’s scheme was no slouch either. Prime Minister Hua sensed the tension, a battle of wits between experts. After pondering for a while, he walked to his desk, picked up the memorial, and gently stroked it. Really, to scheme and murder a righteous and courageous general like this…? Night began to fall. Some shops on the street maintained the lingering atmosphere of the Emperor’s decree of universal celebration, their lanterns lined up, bright as day. Chu Dingjiang saw a peony lantern displayed at a stall not far ahead. He walked over, reached out, and picked it up, recalling the playful antics of An Jiu and Hua Rongjian by the river that day. “Fish I desire; bear’s paw I also desire. What should I do?” Hua Rongjian murmured, lighting the lantern, tossing down a coin, and setting it down on the riverbank. This plan, once started, could turn the world upside down. He felt his long-dormant blood begin to boil again, finally rediscovering the youthful vigor he once possessed. That day, he saw An Jiu and Hua Rongjian together. Although he was displeased, he did not think it was a big deal. “Fight!” Chu Dingjiang’s voice was not loud, but it was firm and powerful, revealing a fierce courage and determination that would not back down even if the sky were to fall and the earth were to shatter.

chapters.title: A Cry for Help
chapters.content: At the Mei Mansion. An unexpected guest arrived. Li Qingzhi sat beside Sui Yuntong, head bowed, filled with shame. When he returned today, he had not expected to be followed by someone, and he had unknowingly led them to the island. This person was none other than Gao Dazhuang! Having served as a eunuch for some time, his behavior had become increasingly effeminate; even the way he held his teacup was enough to give one goosebumps. “Ahem.” He cleared his throat and said to Mo Sigui, “My subordinates…” Mo Sigui exhaled a smoke ring, interrupting him. “Take them all away so I do not have to see them.” “My Lord, now that we are out, we do not plan to go back.” A hint of murderous intent emanated from Li Qingzhi. “Hmph.” Gao Dazhuang sneered twice, fiddling with his fingers. “Do you think everyone else is as stupid as you? If I wanted to take you all back, would I dare to come to the island alone?” He pointed at An Jiu. “You are an ungrateful wretch, a waste of the few Gu pills Grandpa gave you.” An Jiu narrowed her eyes. “Are you determined to walk the path of no return as a eunuch?” Gao Dazhuang quickly withdrew his hand, rolled his eyes, and ignored her. “My Lord, please speak plainly. If we can help, it will be a way of repaying your kindness,” Sui Yuntong said. “Finally, someone who understands.” Gao Dazhuang glanced at the others. “Talking to people like you is exhausting.” He took a sip of tea and shifted to a more comfortable position. “I did not follow the rules and use the Gu poison; I intended to recruit you all under the Second Prince’s command in the future. Who would have thought you’d be so capable, escaping like that? Forced relationships do not work, so I will not force you. I’ve come here to ask for your help with a small matter.” “Please speak, My Lord,” Sui Yuntong said. “Many officials in court have petitioned for General Ling’s punishment. The winds are blowing in one direction, and there are many treacherous officials around the Emperor. General Ling is likely in a bad situation this time,” Gao Dazhuang said. “The Second Prince wants to save General Ling. If he cannot succeed, he hopes you can help him break him out of prison.” Li Qingzhi was almost about to nod immediately, but Sui Yuntong spoke faster. “We can only do our best.” Meaning, he would not risk his life. “Yuntong,” Li Qingzhi said, slightly annoyed, “General Ling is loyal to the Emperor and loves his country. How can we not risk our lives to save him after he’s been wronged?” “No one is stopping you from risking your life,” Sui Yuntong said. Although he seemed ruthless, he had a vague feeling that something was amiss. He would not make any promises before he figured it out. “What about you?” Li Qingzhi asked An Jiu. An Jiu paused, then said, “I will play it by ear.” “You’ve all witnessed General Ling’s battles! Such a hero, is it so difficult to lend a helping hand in times of crisis?” Li Qingzhi’s greatest wish in life was to become a man as upright and indomitable as Ling Ziyue, but fate had driven him down that path. Everyone fell silent. Mo Sigui leaned back in his chair, tilting his head back and exhaling smoke rings that rippled like water before him. “It’s good that you are willing to help,” Gao Dazhuang said, standing up. “I am going back now. I will keep it a secret for as long as I can. You all take care of yourselves.” Sui Yuntong saw him to the door. Li Qingzhi hesitated for a moment, then followed him out. An Jiu and Mo Sigui seemed frozen in their chairs. They did not move. After the two returned, Mo Sigui tapped his burnt-out pipe. “Do not bother me with your trivial matters anymore!” Because Mo Sigui had arrived on the island first, the group implicitly considered him their leader. Today, when Gao Dazhuang arrived, they pulled him out to entertain the guests. “Physician Mo, how can this be trivial?! The Song Dynasty’s fate rests on the shoulders of General Ling,” Li Qingzhi said, displeased. Mo Sigui, already standing and strolling to the door, turned back upon hearing this. “I do not care about these things! But I see it clearly: a nation’s fate resting on one person’s shoulders is not necessarily a good thing.” In times of crisis, if one person could stand against the tide and others only needed to hide behind him, unaware of the perilous situation, they would become increasingly naive and cowardly. This was easy to understand; at least An Jiu understood, just as Mei Yanran understood Mei Jiu. Actually, if Ling Ziyue could hold the border, it would be a good thing, but who could guarantee that this person would remain standing forever? The Song Dynasty’s current predicament was beyond the ability of one or two people to turn the tide. “To be put in a life-or-death situation is to be reborn,” Sui Yuntong sighed deeply. “It’s a cruel irony that someone has to die because of this. Would the Divine Physician be interested in guessing whether the jackal devoured the weak lion or the lion killed the jackal?” “Sigui!” Sheng Changying’s voice was urgent, accompanied by rapid footsteps. As soon as he appeared, he said, “Young Lady Lou has fainted at the ferry.” Everyone snapped out of their daze, only to see a blurry figure; Mo Sigui had already vanished. They quickly followed. When An Jiu arrived at the ferry, Mo Sigui was kneeling on the ground, holding Lou Mingyue’s head. Upon closer inspection, it was clear he was pressing his fingers against the wound between Lou Mingyue’s shoulders and neck. The wound was extremely deep, gaping outwards, seemingly a severed artery. However, due to the prolonged bleeding, the pressure had lessened, and the blood did not spurt out, but rather trickled from Mo Sigui’s fingers, flowing into the lake and staining a large area red. The surrounding Dream Flowers absorbed the blood, growing wildly at a visible rate. In a short time, the buds had unfolded, their alluring red surpassing even the fresh blood. “Mingyue, do not sleep!” Mo Sigui growled. An Jiu rarely saw him so distraught, his thin, haggard face dotted with blood. Mo Sigui slowly channeled his true qi into her to ensure she would not faint during this time. Lou Mingyue’s eyelashes were blurred with blood. She struggled to open her eyes, her throat bobbing, her chapped lips trembling, but she could not utter a single word. “Ah Jiu, get my silver needles out,” Mo Sigui said. Knowing that she often received treatment from him and that he liked to keep silver needles tucked into his robes, An Jiu took them out and went to support Lou Mingyue’s head. Mo Sigui freed one hand and swiftly inserted silver needles into the area near the wound. The bleeding stopped quickly. Mo Sigui picked her up and hurried back into the house. Sheng Changying had already prepared everything. “This water was boiled half an hour ago; it has gotten a little cold. I am having Pianxian boil it again.” “Alright.” Mo Sigui quickly cut away the clothing around Lou Mingyue’s wound with scissors, then grabbed a basin of water and used a cloth to clean the blood around the wound. He then washed the wound directly with his prepared medicinal solution. Everyone except An Jiu left. Mo Sigui, his face grim, carefully tended to the cut flesh, beads of sweat forming on his forehead. An Jiu wiped his forehead clean with a cloth. “You can go out now; I can manage on my own,” Mo Sigui said. An Jiu did not waste any words, put down her things, and turned to leave. Outside, some people were standing, and some were sitting. Xiao Yue, who had been lying on the ground, suddenly got up. Seeing An Jiu come out, Li Qingzhi asked, “How is she? The Divine Physician does not look too good.” “She’s probably alright,” An Jiu said, unsure if Lou Mingyue had any other injuries. Sui Yuntong nodded. “The Divine Physician’s complexion is bad, probably because the injured person is Second Young Lady Lou.” If it were anyone else, even if they were bleeding almost to death, he would probably calmly administer acupuncture without being disturbed. “To injure Second Young Lady Lou to this extent, the other party is no ordinary person. Qingzhi, come with me to check around the island, just in case,” Sui Yuntong said. “Alright,” Li Qingzhi replied. Zhu Pianxian boiled hot water and brought it in; Xiao Yue followed. Only Sheng Changying and An Jiu remained outside. He stared blankly for a moment, then suddenly asked, “Has Ah Jiu seen Lord Chu?” “Once, why?” An Jiu asked. “General Ling has always been calm and patient; a sudden change always has a reason. I’ve roughly estimated that he had already changed before you left the Hebei camp. I think…” Sheng Changying hesitated, starting to speak. “Think what?” An Jiu already had a suspicion. “Is this related to Chu Dingjiang?” Sheng Changying looked at her and nodded. “Perhaps only he can save General Ling, and he…” He was the least likely person to save Ling Ziyue. An Jiu said, “You are telling me all this so I can persuade him?” “Yes.” Sheng Changying still looked very sleepy, with faint dark circles around his narrow, fox-like eyes, but he was much better than before, indicating that Zhu Pianxian had been taking good care of him recently. “I also admire General Ling,” An Jiu said, then changed the subject, “but I will not persuade Chu Dingjiang. If he wants Ling Ziyue dead, there must be a reason why Ling Ziyue must die.” “If I am not mistaken, he probably wants Ling Ziyue’s death to incite the Song people to resist the imperial power and the Liao Kingdom. An Jiu, do you know how dangerous that is?” Sheng Changying sighed. “One wrong move and the whole game is lost!” Conservatives all shared Sheng Changying’s thoughts. “Why is Headmaster Sheng meddling in these matters? Is Ling Ziyue a relative of yours?” An Jiu asked, puzzled. Sheng Changying knew a lot, but he always kept to himself, only concerned with his own little domain at the Konghe Institute, never caring about anything else. A strong smell of medicine permeated the room. Sheng Changying glanced around. “I was just moved. I simply believe that those who are willing to sacrifice themselves for their country should not die for anything else. If you do not want to follow my advice, just pretend I did not say anything.” Sheng Changying himself could not be patriotic, but that did not stop him from supporting these people. An Jiu looked at the doors and windows, her lips slightly pursed. “Also, before leaving the Konghe Army, I saw news that the new Emperor of Liao had only recently ascended the throne and was seriously ill. Without this heart’s blood, he would not live more than five years. They are determined to seize it. You must be careful,” Sheng Changying said. “Mm,” An Jiu replied. Seeing that she was lost in thought, Sheng Changying did not disturb her. He leaned against a pillar, closed his eyes, and rested. After a while, beads of sweat appeared on his forehead. He was used to being busy, always using this method to survive. Now that he was idle, he felt a bit anxious, always feeling uneasy.

chapters.title: The Final Verdict
chapters.content: About two hours later, Mo Sigui emerged, covered in blood and pale-faced. Standing on the veranda, he silently placed a pill in his pipe, lit it, and took a few puffs. Seeing his appearance, An Jiu guessed he was mostly alright but still asked to confirm, “Are you alright?” “I am fine,” Mo Sigui replied. Upon hearing this, Sheng Changying got up and left. An Jiu was about to turn around when she heard Mo Sigui say, “Ah Jiu, talk to me for a while.” An Jiu stopped. But both remained silent. After standing there for a while, Mo Sigui spoke first, saying, “I am fine; go back and rest.” Mo Sigui and Lou Mingyue were both stubbornly pursuing their chosen paths. Only if one of them compromised could their paths intersect. Unfortunately, Lou Mingyue was someone who would go all the way. Although Mo Sigui had wavered slightly, An Jiu did not believe she could persuade him to abandon his pursuit of medicine for a woman. For some people destined not to be together, too much interaction only added to their pain. An Jiu did not think too deeply about it. She simply felt that if he could not have her, it was better to let go. So she did not try to persuade him, but she did not leave either. Mo Sigui smoked his pipe, one pill after another, until the medicine in the pipe burned out. He put in another pill, and when it reached the eighth, An Jiu reached out and pressed down on the pipe. “Do not worry about me, you…” Bang! Before Mo Sigui could finish speaking, An Jiu chopped him unconscious. “Nothing else works as fast as this.” An Jiu grabbed his collar and dragged him into the room. Seeing Lou Mingyue lying on the bed, she hesitated for a moment, then carried him to the bed and laid him next to Lou Mingyue. After doing all this, An Jiu went back to her room to rest. Lying fully clothed on the couch, she closed her eyes, and an image inexplicably appeared in her mind: lanterns gleaming, red silk hanging everywhere. Chu Dingjiang solemnly proclaimed his intention to marry her. The scene haunted her, consuming her. Clearly, she had not thought anything of it at the time. Until late at night, An Jiu rose and went to the courtyard. Moonlight filtered through the thin, gauze-like mist, casting a hazy glow. She looked up, staring blankly at the almost full moon, secretly regretting that she should not have knocked Mo Sigui unconscious… The capital was moonless, and heavy snow fell, threatening to engulf the buildings. A brief commotion erupted in the Liao palace before silence returned. In a side hall, Yelu Huangwu clutched a water cup tightly; it was no longer steaming, but her face was somber, and none of the servants dared to replace it. After about the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, a eunuch hurried in, bowing to her. “Your Highness, His Majesty is well. Physician Ning said she needs to adjust the prescription and sent me to report this.” Yelu Huangwu snorted. The eunuch, her meaning unclear, stood for a few moments before saying, “His Majesty still needs someone to attend to him. This servant will take his leave now.” “Go,” Yelu Huangwu said. A short while later, Ning Yanli, dressed in green, hurried in. “Master,” she bowed. Yelu Huangwu dismissed the others in the room and asked in a low voice, “How is my brother’s condition?” “Not good.” Ning Yanli never uttered polite words to Yelu Huangwu. She said directly, “This was originally the perfect opportunity to obtain the heart’s blood, but unfortunately, the divine medicine has been lost. There’s no better way at the moment; I can only try my best to delay for at least one or two years, at most seven or eight.” “One or two years,” Yelu Huangwu frowned. “Even if my brother could wait, the heart’s blood would probably be gone long before.” Ning Yanli said, “The heart’s blood is extremely potent; one cannot take too much each day. Since it has not been lost for long, there must still be a large amount remaining.” Yelu Huangwu snorted coldly, “Wei Yunshan has been imprisoned for so many years, yet he has not become a single bit smarter. He died before even achieving his goal, and Wei Yuzhi is becoming increasingly incompetent!” Ning Yanli did not dare to reply. After a while, she heard her say again, “It’s urgent. It seems I must go and retrieve the medicine myself this time.” “Master, actually…” Ning Yanli hesitated, then leaned down and lowered her voice, “You do not necessarily have to push someone else to the throne; that heart’s blood is also of great use to you.” Slap! Yelu Huangwu raised her hand, and Ning Yanli received a solid slap, a red handprint quickly appearing on her face. She immediately knelt. “Ningzi, you’ve followed me for so many years, and now you are becoming increasingly presumptuous.” Yelu Huangwu’s voice was calm, but her slightly lowered phoenix eyes held a cold light, like a sharp sword suddenly drawn. “There are some things I do not want to hear a second time!” “Yes, Your Highness, I admit my guilt,” Ning Yanli replied immediately. Yelu Huangwu stood up and straightened her sleeves. “You will stay in the palace to serve the Emperor until he recovers.” Ning Yanli remained prostrate on the ground. “Yes, Your Highness, I obey.” Only after hearing the footsteps fade away did Ning Yanli dare to raise her head. Yelu Huangwu knew martial arts; her slap was merciless, and half of her face quickly swelled up. After kneeling for a while, she took out some ointment from her medicine box and applied it to her burning face. After applying the medicine, Ning Yanli lowered her hands, looked up, forced back her tears, and a stubborn look appeared on her face. The little dignity she had left could only be cautiously revealed in this solitary moment. She had served Yelu Huangwu for many years, yet she had never truly understood what this woman, roughly her own age, was thinking. Yelu Huangwu had devoted herself wholeheartedly to the Liao Kingdom, exhausting all her resources and schemes. Ning Yanli refused to believe that she had never coveted the throne. The Khitan had a long-standing tradition of women holding power, and there were many precedents in Liao history, among whom Yelu Huangwu’s mother, Empress Dowager Xiao, was a prime example. She had been imprisoned for so many years, enduring so much, secretly and cautiously plotting to help her brother return and inherit the throne, finally restoring his former glory and allowing him to stand openly in the Liao palace once more. However, no one knew whether this was a beginning or an end. Winter spread, and soon even the entire territory of the Song Dynasty was plunged into winter. The “General Ling’s treason case” had concluded—some letters, half-destroyed, were found in Ling Ziyue’s camp, and a large quantity of gold and silver jewelry was discovered in the cellar of his Bianjing home, much of it being gifts of the Song Dynasty to the Liao Dynasty. The cellar contained vegetables and cured meat for the New Year. Frequent opening of the cellar was detrimental to food preservation, and with no shortage of fresh ingredients, the Ling family would not have gone to the cellar unnecessarily. They could not explain how a cellar full of winter vegetables had mysteriously turned into gold and silver jewelry! They were utterly speechless. In fact, these discoveries had been made a month earlier, but the Emperor delayed for over twenty days. He did not want to kill Ling Ziyue easily, as there was no civil official who could truly rival Prime Minister Hua. Although the Song Dynasty traditionally valued civil officials over military ones, Ling Ziyue, at least, commanded a large army and could counterbalance Prime Minister Hua. Besides treason, the Emperor was most concerned about whether Ling Ziyue had secretly allied with Prime Minister Hua. However, with no results in sight, the calls for his execution grew increasingly fierce among the officials.

chapters.title: Go or Not
chapters.content: Ling Ziyue’s correspondence with the Liao Kingdom, whether intended as rebellion or treason, was a capital offense punishable by the extermination of his entire clan. While plays often depicted the extermination of nine generations of a family, in reality, such acts were rare. Even with Ling Ziyue’s “serious crime,” he was ultimately sentenced to the complete confiscation of his family’s property. All the male members of his clan were enslaved, and all the women were forced into prostitution. Having spent half his life fighting to protect his country, he ended up with his family destroyed, a truly tragic end. Military families clearly possessed far more backbone than ordinary families. Despite the brutal confiscation of their property, few cried out in despair, not even the youngest children. Ling Ziyue’s execution was scheduled for the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. Gao Dazhuang secretly smuggled weapons into Mei Mansion half a month in advance, requesting An Jiu and others to assist him. Gao Dazhuang laid down his swords and left. The group sat in a circle in the hall, silently staring at the weapons piled on the table. After a long silence, Sui Yuntong asked, “Are you going or not?” “General Ling is loyal and brave, a virtuous minister of the Song Dynasty. I will go,” Mei Yanran declared first. She had come to terms with things a little better now, no longer clinging to the mother-daughter bond with Mei Jiu. She even felt some regret, believing that her excessive interference in her daughter’s life had led to her tragic end. Seeing Sui Yuntong looking at him, Li Qingzhi immediately added, “No need to ask me; I will definitely go!” “We are not going,” Zhu Pianxian said, including Sheng Changying. He did not know martial arts and could not be of much help. Sui Yuntong nodded. “What about Fourteenth?” An Jiu, sitting with her arms crossed, slightly raised her eyes upon hearing this. “I will go.” It was rare to meet someone she found agreeable. Now that they were unjustly accused, lending a hand would not be difficult. After all, they were already prisoners after escaping the Konghe Army. Gao Dazhuang could hide it for a while, but not forever; exposure was inevitable. “It’s truly outrageous! The entire court, civil and military officials alike, cannot tolerate General Ling,” Li Qingzhi sighed. “If General Ling truly intended to betray the country, would he have waited until today? Do they not realize that with General Ling’s death, their good days are over!” “Actually, General Ling might not be without fault,” Sui Yuntong said. “What?” Li Qingzhi’s eyes widened, as if he would not rest until Sui Yuntong gave a reason. Sui Yuntong said, “His mistake was in his lack of understanding of politics and the state of affairs in the Song Dynasty.” Li Qingzhi scoffed, “The state of affairs in the Song Dynasty is weak; even a blind man could see that!” “The court’s withholding of funds and provisions is not entirely due to neglect of the border war; it is probably because they need to quickly gather the necessary supplies,” Sui Yuntong smiled. “General Ling thought the national treasury was full and was preparing for a protracted war of attrition with the Liao Dynasty, but that’s unrealistic.” “The Song Dynasty is actually that poor?” Li Qingzhi exclaimed in surprise. Zhu Pianxian interjected, “Of course, the Song Dynasty is not poor; what’s poor is the national treasury. The Song Dynasty has been plagued by redundant soldiers and officials for a long time. Each official’s monthly salary, land ownership, clothing expenses, horse and saddle allowances, charcoal costs, ice money… all add up to a considerable sum. The Song Dynasty has always loved rewarding officials with titles and promotions. There are countless people holding sinecure positions and receiving paychecks, ultimately enriching the officials and impoverishing the court.” The prosperity of Bianjing was arguably unparalleled in the world. Officials, nobles, merchants—wealthy people were everywhere, but apart from the merchants, most were either supported by the court or exploited the common people. Beneath this magnificent structure, the framework was rotten and could collapse at any moment. “But if the general were to fall, the Liao Kingdom would inevitably retaliate,” Li Qingzhi said worriedly. “They will not,” Sheng Changying summarized from the recent news. “It’s said that the new Emperor of Liao recently narrowly escaped death. Liao was also bogged down in production this spring and summer due to General Ling’s influence, making this winter extremely difficult. The Northern King is ambitious, and Liao will not choose this juncture for a large-scale counterattack against Song.” Ling Ziyue’s death would certainly have an impact, but Song had other generals; the entire army would not suddenly be paralyzed just because one person was missing. Besides, the Emperor had wanted to replace Ling Ziyue for a long time; there must have been arrangements made beforehand. “But this cannot be blamed on General Ling!” Li Qingzhi could not help but cry foul for Ling Ziyue. “Soldiers only need to know how to protect their country. The Song’s overstaffed army and officials have led to an empty treasury; it is the court’s fault. Even if General Ling was not aware of this, it is not unreasonable!” If Ling Ziyue knew the situation, perhaps he could temporarily suppress his thoughts of counterattacking Liao. Mei Yanran sighed, “It’s all for the best now! General Ling’s successful capture of Xijin Prefecture was a heavy blow to the Liao Kingdom, and the Song people have at least seen that reclaiming the Sixteen Prefectures of Yanyun is not an unattainable dream.” It was precisely because Ling Ziyue possessed this ability that the Second Prince was willing to go to any lengths to rescue him. For him personally, this may not be a bad outcome. “Let’s scout the terrain near Caishikou these next few days. Ideally, we should have a rescue plan within five days,” Sui Yuntong said. An Jiu said, “We are not the main force in this rescue. Gao Dazhuang has not revealed any information. We will just provide assistance when necessary.” They did not know the specifics of the Second Prince’s faction’s rescue plan and had no way to coordinate. If they inadvertently disrupt their plans, it would be disastrous. “But I still find something strange,” Sui Yuntong said. “We were able to escape from the deep palace, so we must have had external help. Lord Gao should not know our background, so why does he trust us so much?” The Second Prince’s plan to secretly rescue a disgraced official—would he easily reveal such a significant matter? “Could there be some conspiracy?” Sheng Changying had worked with Gao Dazhuang in the Imperial Guard for many years and knew his character well; he was no saint. An Jiu suddenly asked, “Do you have a way to contact Chu Dingjiang?” She had known Chu Dingjiang for so long, but only now did she realize that he had always been the one to initiate contact. “We knew how to contact him when we were in the palace, but not now,” Sui Yuntong sighed. “If Lord Chu were here, things might be clearer.” While everyone was talking in the hall, the atmosphere in Mo Sigui’s bedroom was extremely strange. Lou Mingyue’s injuries had not fully healed; her face was thin and pale, her cheeks sunken, her cheekbones prominent, and her two sharp eyebrows slanted upwards, adding a cold and ruthless edge to her otherwise heroic appearance. “Thank you this time,” Lou Mingyue finally spoke to Mo Sigui. Mo Sigui kept puffing on his medicinal cigarette, his entire body enveloped in thick smoke, his figure and face somewhat blurred. “I made a promise, and I will not break it. If you ever suffer any pain in the future, you can come to me.” Lou Mingyue remained silent, stroking the sword at her waist. A moment of silence followed. Lou Mingyue’s lips moved slightly, as if she wanted to say something but ultimately could not utter a word. Someone once said that one should look forward, not backward. Lou Mingyue had tried to forget her hatred, but she couldn’t.

chapters.title: The Word “Love”
chapters.content: Mo Sigui did not wish to walk the path of revenge with her, but he had too many things left undone. Call it cowardice, call it selfishness, but his life and time would not be wasted on revenge. There were only a handful of people in this world who understood him, and Lou Mingyue was one of them. They could have been a perfect couple, but alas, he could not let go of his medical profession, and she could not let go of her hatred. “Tomorrow…” Mo Sigui interrupted Lou Mingyue. “You leave after three days. A gentleman takes revenge even after ten years. Can you not even wait three days?” “I understand,” Lou Mingyue did not refute. The pipe was out of embers. Mo Sigui tapped it on the table. “I remember when we were little, you were even more mischievous than the boys. Stealing birds and catching fish—you were always the one leading the charge, and I was always the one to cover for you when you got into trouble.” Lou Mingyue did not know why he suddenly brought this up. Hearing this, a pang of pain shot through her heart, and her eyes welled up with tears. She quickly lowered her gaze, concealing the rare glimmer of emotion she felt. Mo Sigui said slowly, “If you wanted to cry, you’d just open your mouth and wail; if you wanted to laugh, you’d laugh your heart out. I always thought you were a very easygoing person.” Lou Mingyue held back her tears, her eyes slightly bloodshot. “Since you know I am not like that, why say such things?” “Then may I ask, how did you get injured this time?” Mo Sigui put down his pipe and looked at her. “To assassinate Yelu Huangwu.” Lou Mingyue pursed her lips, a hint of resentment showing in her stubborn expression. Mo Sigui said, “I’ve heard that all members of the Yelu clan suffer from a disease that limits their lifespan to middle age. Yelu Huangwu is already nearing her end. You’d be better off assassinating Ning Yanli sooner.” “You do not understand.” Lou Mingyue stood up, walked to the window, and opened it. A sky full of stars, veiled by a thin mist, came into view. “How happy and carefree I was in my childhood. Now, it is ten times more painful. Although the Ning couple were not my biological parents, they were not indifferent to me. Because of the Liao Kingdom’s schemes, my family was destroyed, and my father risked his life to save me…” Lou Mingyue’s words suddenly choked, her brows furrowing tightly. No matter how hard she tried to hold back, tears still streamed down her face. She still remembered her father’s arrows. He carried her for many li, and when pursuers caught up, he hastily threw her into the river. “I left you a letter,” he had said, “located in the artificial cave you always hide in. If you survive, my child, take it and read it. Do not seek revenge for your parents.” These few words revealed his unwavering fatherly love. Whenever she was angry, she would hide in that cave for days, without even her personal maid. Only the kitchen maid knew, often bringing her food, but it turned out… She floated and sank in the river, witnessing her father’s gruesome death at the hands of two black-clad men. Back then, Lou Mingyue was well protected by the Ning couple. She had never seen a dead person before, let alone witnessed her father, with whom she had lived day and night, die before her eyes. The shock was devastating. Every time she thought of that scene, she felt that even tearing those two black-clad men to pieces would not be enough to quell her hatred. Lou Mingyue’s biological mother was a cold and wise woman, very strict with her. But it was not hard to see a deep love for her daughter. To Lou Mingyue, she was both a mother and a teacher. She was even somewhat like a close friend. And yet, she had been forced to burn her own mother alive! She could not forget the sight of her mother’s slightly open eyes in the flames. Even though it might have been an unconscious movement, in her dreams it was interpreted in countless ways: questioning, resentment, confusion, pain… waking her up in terror every night. Twice her family was destroyed, yet Lou Mingyue did not break down. Instead, she grew even stronger, all because of this burning hatred! She stood by the window, letting the night wind dry her tears. Mo Sigui stepped forward and embraced her from behind. This was the first time in ten years they had been so close. “Ningyu,” Mo Sigui’s voice was hoarse. Looking at her lonely back, he felt an urge to die with her, but in the end, he only said, “You do not need to sever ties with me. Though I cannot be with you through life and death, I want to be your support.” Lou Mingyue felt the warmth from behind and did not push him away. Sometimes she felt a pang of resentment, but upon calming down, she realized he owed her nothing. Why should she expect him to abandon his lifelong pursuit for some unrelated hatred? If she could let go, she could be with him, living a carefree life amidst nature. Unfortunately, as long as her enemy lived, she could not sleep or eat in peace! Compared to her lifelong ideals and deep-seated hatred, Lou Mingyue’s feelings for Mo Sigui seemed insignificant. It was not a passionate, irreplaceable love, but rather an unbreakable bond. Childhood sweethearts, their bond was more complex, perhaps containing a mixture of familial affection and romantic love. A jumble of thoughts churned in her mind. As the storm subsided, Lou Mingyue said, “Thank you.” Outside the window, starlight streamed down from the night sky, cascading into the lake and shimmering on the water, mirroring the emotions in their hearts at that moment. The night was still, the candlelight dim. The next day, as dawn approached, An Jiu went to scout the terrain of Caishikou, while the others busied themselves with preparations. The weapons Gao Dazhuang brought were clearly insufficient. Regardless of whether the rescue attempt succeeded or not, they could not return, so there was much to prepare. An Jiu returned to the island before noon. Just as the small boat docked, a deafening roar erupted, and a flock of startled birds took flight, soaring into the sky. Immediately afterward, thick smoke billowed from the forest. The islanders temporarily abandoned their tasks and rushed to Lou Xiaowu’s courtyard. An Jiu was the last to arrive. She had barely stepped across the threshold when a dark figure lunged at him, revealing a set of pearly white teeth. “Fourteenth, Fourteenth, did you see that?” “Quick, put out the fire!” Sui Yuntong hurriedly pulled An Jiu. The surrounding trees were charred black. What had started as a few scattered flames had ignited and spread rapidly without their noticing. Autumn and winter were dry seasons, making fires more likely, especially with the thick layer of dead leaves on the ground! An Jiu, while rolling up her sleeves to fetch water, asked Lou Xiaowu, “What happened?” “I was making bullets, but I have not finished them yet. However, I accidentally created a kind of fire bomb. How about that? Pretty powerful, right?” Lou Xiaowu said proudly. Mo Sigui raised his pipe and hit her on the back of the head, yelling, “Put out the fire! I will deal with you later!” Lou Xiaowu’s almond-shaped eyes, clearer and brighter than ever on her dark face, seemed to speak volumes, filled with grievance. Reluctantly, she picked up a ladle to pour water, only to be hit again by Mo Sigui. “Are you watering flowers? Get me a bigger bucket!” Mo Sigui had gone to great lengths to defend the island, and he was not about to give up easily. The Dream Flowers, as the first line of defense, had already bloomed; the Poison Orchids, as the second line, were just beginning to grow, and the herbs used to isolate the poisonous gas were still tender buds. If the fire spread, all the work he had put in months of effort would be destroyed. Lou Xiaowu pouted and went to fetch water to put out the fire. After working for half an hour, she finally managed to stop the fire before it spread to the herb garden. Lou Xiaowu then quietly approached An Jiu, gently poked her with her finger, and asked with bright, sparkling eyes, “How is it?”

chapters.title: Parting Words
chapters.content: “Very good,” An Jiu commented objectively. Lou Xiaowu’s eyes immediately crinkled with laughter. After the initial excitement, fatigue set in. Lou Xiaowu rubbed her eyes and nestled into Mei Yanran’s arms, falling asleep. Li Qingzhi sighed, “With such a fine weapon, how can we not drive the Liao people out of the Sixteen Prefectures of Yan and Yun?” An Jiu sat on a large rock by the stream, watching Mei Yanran carefully wipe Lou Xiaowu’s smudged face with a damp handkerchief. Mo Sigui sat down beside her. “Envious?” An Jiu looked away, ignoring him. “The third medicinal bath is in five years. Remember to come find me.” Mo Sigui took a medicine bottle from his pocket and placed it in her hand. “These are the remaining pills. The heart’s blood medicine is extremely effective, especially after an injury. You absolutely cannot use too much, otherwise it will do more harm than good.” “Alright.” An Jiu carefully put the medicine away. Gu Jinghong streaked across the night sky like a shooting star, dazzlingly bright, and vanished without a trace. An Jiu was not particularly grateful to him, but she felt a strange sense of shared misfortune. “After we part, I do not know when we will see each other again. Is there anything you want to say to me?” Mo Sigui was unusually sentimental. An Jiu hesitated, then said earnestly, “After I leave, do not bully Da Jiu.” “Get as far away as you can! I do not know you!” Mo Sigui shoved her. An Jiu grinned. “Silly.” Mo Sigui put down his cigarette, picked up the holder, and mumbled, “How can I argue with a fool?” “Mo Sigui, I am indeed a little worried about you,” An Jiu said. Mo Sigui was inevitably touched, pausing to look at her. An Jiu asked cautiously, “Your insomnia is so severe. Will you not live more than five years?” “What the hell!” Mo Sigui jumped up, pointing the cigarette at her nose. “You are insulting my medical skills!” The tense atmosphere, ready to explode at any moment, made one worry that their friendship was over. However, Mo Sigui and An Jiu locked eyes for a moment but ultimately could not bring themselves to lash out. He could only angrily turn and leave, muttering as he went, “I am going to write to Chu Dingjiang and get this bastard out of here as soon as possible. Every extra moment makes my life unbearable…” An Jiu got up and followed him back to their lodgings. Lou Mingyue was carrying a bundle of firewood, placing it under the eaves of the kitchen. The two stopped simultaneously. Lou Mingyue nodded to her. An Jiu clasped her hands in a respectful bow. Silence fell between them. After a few moments, An Jiu silently turned and left. She and Lou Mingyue were on different paths, and although they walked the same road, she still yearned for light and hoped to one day live a normal life. Therefore, she felt some resistance towards Lou Mingyue, who had plunged headlong into a dead end. Lou Mingyue was quite self-aware and no longer yearned for friends or shared her deep-seated hatred. One person, buried deep in her heart, was enough to sustain her through the rest of her life. The next day. Before dawn, Lou Mingyue, as usual, chopped a bundle of firewood and placed it in the kitchen, then boiled a pot of water. The firelight illuminated her increasingly full face. The water in the pot boiled, steam rising, and she extinguished the fire in the stove. She took her sword and went out. The doors and windows of the main hall were tightly closed, but Lou Mingyue noticed Mo Sigui’s unusual behavior. She stopped and looked over, her gaze softening. It was as if she could see his face through the latticed window. Mo Sigui saw Lou Mingyue’s figure through the crack in the door and raised his hand to the latch, hesitant. The two stood separated by the door for a long time until there was movement from Mei Yanran’s room, and then Lou Mingyue turned and quickly left. Mo Sigui sighed softly, his hand falling to his side, and murmured, “Mo Ran, Mo Ran, you do not even dare to see her off gracefully!” Hearing this, and seeing the steam rising from the kitchen, Mei Yanran guessed that Lou Mingyue had left and could not help but sigh as well, “Life is so difficult; a temporary farewell is nothing!” Mo Sigui paused for a moment, then turned to the medicine storeroom to select the herbs he needed for the day. He had recorded many difficult and complicated cases during his medical practice, and now he had almost solved most of them. Studying medicine in isolation was not advisable; in a while, he would travel around, searching for various cases and rare herbs, so he spent most of his time practicing his martial arts during this period. Those with wind meridians were truly blessed; their internal energy cultivation was ten or a hundred times easier than that of others. But the world was often fair; those born with wind meridians were susceptible to evil influences. The so-called “evil energy” did not refer to ghosts or spirits but rather was a medical term meaning someone was more susceptible to external influences and prone to illness than the average person. Furthermore, Mo Sigui always used himself as a guinea pig for medicine, so ordinary drugs were no longer effective against him. If he were to contract a serious illness, it might be incurable, so An Jiu’s concerns were not unfounded. For him personally, prevention was key. Life on the island returned to its leisurely and peaceful state, while the outside world was in turmoil due to the Ling Ziyue case. Many scholars concerned with current affairs jointly petitioned the court to thoroughly investigate the case, given Ling Ziyue’s crucial importance to the Song Dynasty. However, these requests were all rejected. The court’s reply was that the case was clear-cut, the evidence conclusive, and there was no need to waste time reinvestigating. As the year drew to a close, despite the gravity of Ling Ziyue’s life-or-death situation, it did not stop families from preparing for the New Year. As long as the sky did not collapse, life had to go on. Amidst the turmoil, the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month arrived quickly. That day, snow fell in Bianjing. The heavy snow poured down, seemingly burying the heavens and earth. Those sentenced to beheading were all scheduled for autumn and winter. Firstly, autumn and winter had a somber, deathly atmosphere; secondly, the autumn harvest was over, allowing the people to gather and witness the executions, serving as a deterrent to crime; and thirdly, the colder weather in autumn and winter made corpses easier to dispose of, preventing outbreaks of plague. Ling Ziyue happened to be “caught” at this time. For such a serious crime, the Emperor could not possibly postpone his punishment until next year. The execution ground was already packed with people, and An Jiu and her group were already lying in ambush in various places. Wearing a human skin mask, she sat in a private room of a teahouse twenty chi away, observing from the window. It was still early, and the site was heavily guarded. The executioner had not arrived yet, and the prisoner had not been brought in, but An Jiu could already sense the undercurrents. There were over two hundred martial artists of ranks four to nine around her! And their numbers seemed to be increasing! “The Second Prince would not be so extravagant, would he?” An Jiu wondered. At the end of the day, soldiers began clearing the road, followed by the executioner and the prison cart. Unlike ordinary executions, straw mats were hung around the execution platform, and even the prison cart was covered with a straw curtain. This was to prevent any attempt to break in. Those who attempted to intercept the prisoner would not dare reveal their whereabouts easily, thus buying time for the execution. The prison cart stopped before the execution platform. Just as two soldiers were about to lift the straw curtain, a feathered arrow suddenly pierced the snow, approaching with a sharp sound—its target was Ling Ziyue inside the cart!

chapters.title: Escape
chapters.content: At the same time, a dozen or so people leaped out of the crowd and rushed towards the prison cart, their speed reaching the arrowheads. Fearing being caught in the crossfire, the civilians immediately began to flee. The scene suddenly descended into chaos. The executioner, seated at the head of the table, was terrified and abruptly stood up. “Keep a close eye on the prisoners!” Ling Ziyue was a wanted criminal. If he were to die a gruesome death on the spot, that would be one thing, but if he were rescued, his head would likely be lost! Even more terrifying was that if his political enemies impeached him for colluding with a rebel, his family might also… Thinking of this, a bead of cold sweat slid down his temple. He beckoned to his trusted guard beside him and whispered, “Take men and resist. If the situation turns bad, execute Ling Ziyue on the spot! Go quickly!” “Yes!” The guard obeyed and led a dozen or so men into the fray. An Jiu, gripping the Dragon-Subduing Bow, stood up. Turning around, he suddenly recognized a familiar sight and could not help but look up at the roof beam. A tall figure, shrouded in a black cloak, revealed only a long, dark beard. “Get on,” he said in a low voice, tossing down a rope. An Jiu reached out without hesitation and grabbed it. She was easily lifted. “What happened?” An Jiu asked in a low voice. Chu Dingjiang knew she was asking about the chaos at the execution ground, but he did not answer. He simply held her close, moving silently like a ghost across the roof beams, leaving the house and heading straight for the southern suburbs. Snow was falling heavily outside, making the road almost invisible. An Jiu faintly heard a huge roar erupt from the crowd behind her, interspersed with cries for Ling Ziyue’s innocence. The two landed safely in the desolate area. Only then did Chu Dingjiang say, “It’s just a struggle between princes.” “A struggle between princes?” An Jiu could not think of any princes involved. The Third Prince was too young; he should not be involved in this. The Crown Prince… could someone with that kind of character really do anything worthwhile? “The Second Prince secretly plotted to rescue Ling Ziyue, but somehow the Crown Prince found out. So the Crown Prince used a clever ruse, throwing the Second Prince’s men into disarray and exposing them prematurely,” Chu Dingjiang said. An Jiu gasped, truly surprised by the Crown Prince’s deep cunning. “Was that General Ling in the prison cart?” “It should have been,” Chu Dingjiang said, seeing her interest, and decided to explain clearly. “When the Crown Prince suggested using straw mats to cover General Ling and preserve his last shred of dignity in court, I sensed something was wrong. So I had someone replace General Ling. Then I sent more men to assist the executioners, to prevent a raid on the execution ground.” In short, the loyal and patriotic war god of the Song Dynasty must be executed in full view of everyone. As for other things, Chu Dingjiang would not let Ling Ziyue be easily sacrificed until he had squeezed every last drop of usefulness out of him. “The fact that Ling Ziyue was switched will be exposed sooner or later, so you should flee south with him to hide near Jiaozhi. I will come find you after I’ve dealt with things here.” Chu Dingjiang pulled a bundle from under his cloak and stuffed it into An Jiu’s arms. “Go, General Ling is near Changting. I’ve already sent someone to inform Sui Yuntong and the others. After you meet up, leave immediately.” “Alright.” An Jiu ran a dozen paces with the bundle, then suddenly stopped. She could no longer sense Chu Dingjiang’s presence, but still turned back for a glance. In the vast snow, he stood alone, a black cloak covering him from head to toe. His silent aura blended into the snow, like a monument that had stood for a thousand years. Just like when they first met. The swirling snow seemed to be blocked by something invisible, unable to fall on him. An Jiu ran back through the snow, bumping straight into his chest. An Jiu did not see it, but just as she was about to bump into him, he suddenly withdrew his protective aura, and the heavy snow, now unobstructed, fell heavily onto his broad shoulders. The snow pattered underfoot as Chu Dingjiang pulled off his hood. An Jiu rubbed her sore cheek, looking up but only seeing his chin, and frowned slightly. She was about to take two steps back when Chu Dingjiang embraced her. “I came back because I have something to say,” An Jiu said, her face buried in his chest, her voice muffled. “I understand,” Chu Dingjiang said with a slight smile. “No need to say it aloud.” It was not that he really knew what An Jiu wanted to say, but he guessed that she probably would not say anything romantic, so he’d rather let her imagine it herself. “I want to say it because I think it is very profound, very affectionate,” An Jiu insisted. Chu Dingjiang nodded helplessly. “A few days ago, I saw Mo Sigui write a sentence to Lou Mingyue,” An Jiu said. Hearing that it was written by Mo Sigui, Chu Dingjiang had an even worse premonition. “If you live, return; if you die, I will long for you forever.” An Jiu felt a little smug. “How about it? Does it not fit this scene perfectly?” “…” Chu Dingjiang rubbed the back of her head. “Do not worry, I usually do not die.” He understood the lingering sentiment and what An Jiu wanted to express, but it really did not sound very pleasant! Therefore, understanding was indeed the best way to communicate with An Jiu. “Then I am leaving.” An Jiu smiled at him and quickly darted away, disappearing several dozen chi away. An Jiu did not know light-footed fighting skills. Although her running movements were swift, they were not as light and graceful as walking on water; at first glance, she looked more like a fox running through the snow. Chu Dingjiang watched her go with a smile, his inner energy gradually filling up, once again separating him from the heavy snow. The snow fell heavily, already accumulating a thin layer on the ground in the suburbs. An Jiu arrived near the pavilion and spotted several people and horses in the distance. Sui Yuntong and his companions, with their exceptional lightness skills, had arrived even before her. Ling Ziyue, whom she had not seen in a long time, was among them. Thick clothing wrapped around his lean frame, but the indomitable, unstoppable aura he possessed at the border was gone. “Let’s go,” Sui Yuntong said. The group mounted their horses and galloped along the official road through the snow. After traveling several li, the snow had completely dried up. It was overcast, but no snow had fallen. After riding for two days and one night, they finally rested at a dilapidated temple. Sui Yuntong lit a fire and roasted the dry rations they had brought over it, finally getting a warm meal. Li Qingzhi placed a piece of bread in Ling Ziyue’s hand. Seeing his gloomy expression and reluctance to eat, he offered words of comfort: “General, as long as you are alive, you can always fight again. Do not ruin your health.” Ling Ziyue nodded and took a bite of the bread, but his expression showed no improvement. Just as Li Qingzhi was about to persuade him again, Sui Yuntong stopped him. For someone like Li Qingzhi, who lived alone in the shadows, any price was worth paying to fight openly on the battlefield. However, only when one truly reached that point did one realize that things were not as simple as imagined. Ling Ziyue survived alone, but his wife and children were all given a cup of poison and imprisoned. The Emperor, in his “gratitude,” spared him a complete corpse. His body remained, but his heart was dead! Ling Ziyue now did not even have the strength to hate. Sui Yuntong gazed at Ling Ziyue’s gaunt profile, sighing inwardly. Although his attack on Xijin Prefecture had been too hasty, it could not be denied that only he in the entire Song Dynasty could have accomplished it, and perhaps no one else would be able to for the next fifty years. In Bianjing, the turmoil of the execution ground storm had long since subsided. The execution platform at Caishikou was soaked in blood, proclaiming to everyone that General Ling, hailed as the God of War, was gone. The splattered blood that day seemed to have been poured onto everyone’s faces, burning them with unbearable pain. Rumors spread from somewhere that Ling Ziyue had been framed, the accounts detailed and seemingly credible. These rumors, like a fire thrown into a boiling oil pan, ignited rapidly. In an instant, public outrage surged, especially among the scholars, who joined together to submit a petition. They had done similar things before Ling Ziyue’s execution, but then, due to prejudice against military men, their emotions were far less intense than they were now. In a Song Dynasty rife with complacency and decadence, Ling Ziyue was truly an anomaly. In his youth, he had studied under a master and participated in the imperial examinations; though he had not passed, he was still a scholar. This resurfacing of his past further stirred the sympathy of the literati. While this was causing a great uproar, the court was also worried about two other matters—the Liao army, upon receiving news of Ling Ziyue’s execution, immediately launched a major attack! Furthermore, apart from a snowfall on the day of Ling Ziyue’s execution, there had been very little snowfall this winter, which would likely affect next year’s harvest. This year was destined to be turbulent. Winter seemed to fly by in its hectic pace. As soon as the branches began to sprout tender green leaves, Mo Sigui packed his bags and, with two tigers, began his itinerant physician’s journey. On the island, only Zhu Pianxian, Sheng Changying, and Lou Xiaowu remained. An Jiu and her group arrived in Jiaozhi in mid-second month, and at this time, the court issued a secret order to arrest Ling Ziyue. Near Jiaozhi, there were also heavy Song troops stationed, but the area was mostly dense forest and swamp, making it easy to hide. An Jiu had considerable experience in jungle survival and would not starve to death. However, Ling Ziyue grew increasingly despondent in the dark, sunless jungle. After nearly a month of trekking through the dense forest, they finally found a small clearing and saw the long-awaited sunlight. An Jiu, seemingly oblivious to her surroundings, took off her outer garment and hung it on a withered tree. She wore a vest-like top, revealing her fair arms. She was no longer as frail as before; her figure was agile, her every movement decisive and swift. Although not physically imposing, it was easy to discern her hidden explosive power and her almost abnormal control over her body. “General Ling,” An Jiu said, walking towards Ling Ziyue with her water pouch. She gulped down a mouthful as she went, then handed him the rest. Ling Ziyue took it and tilted his head back to drink. “The most indispensable thing for survival here is willpower,” An Jiu said, squatting down beside him, her dark eyes fixed on him. “In your current state, you will not last three months.” Ling Ziyue remained silent, his lips pursed. An Jiu dropped a bombshell, saying, “Your life is still long, at least longer than the current Emperor’s. You might still have a chance to regain your military power.” The others all looked over, each with their own thoughts. Mei Yanran stared at An Jiu’s pale arm with a complicated expression, wishing she could wrap her in a coat, but after a long while, she made no move. “Yes, General, you must pull yourself together!” Li Qingzhi echoed. It was Sui Yuntong who could somewhat discern Ling Ziyue’s thoughts. “General, you have always been true to your nature, and you know what kind of court the Song Dynasty is, yet you still remained loyal, for the sake of the country, not for any particular person or court. Now that you have been unjustly accused and suffered injustice, has your patriotism changed?”

chapters.title: Yelu Quancang
chapters.content: Ling Ziyue’s expression shifted, and he gulped down several mouthfuls of water. “You are right!” He could not let a minor setback deter him. He had previously disregarded life and death even when he had attachments; now, with no attachments, there was no reason to give up. Seeing Ling Ziyue’s renewed spirit, Mei Yanran admired his unwavering resolve yet also felt that those who possessed great love were often almost heartless. An Jiu, however, found his performance satisfactory; it was worth all the protection he had received. “Staying cooped up in the jungle is not a solution. Let’s get out of here as soon as the storm passes,” Sui Yuntong said. Everyone agreed. They were not simply trying to survive; it was better to learn about the outside world sooner. At the Liao Kingdom, in Shangjing. Snow piled high on the palace rooftops. Yelu Huangwu stood outside the palace. She stood on the steps, clad in a black fur coat, only the dark purple cuffs of her skirt visible, gazing absently at the icicles hanging from the eaves. “Long time no see, A-Wu,” a clear, gentle voice rang out. Yelu Huangwu snapped out of her reverie and turned to see a handsome man in a dark red robe gracefully approaching. He was tall and slender, wearing a raccoon-colored fox-fur hat that accentuated his ethereal bearing. This man was none other than Yelu Jinglie, the Northern King of the Liao Kingdom. “Uncle,” Yelu Huangwu greeted with a faint smile, a rare hint of girlishness in her expression. Yelu Jinglie, his usual stern demeanor vanishing, reached out and patted her head, laughing. “It’s been over a decade since I last saw you! You’ve grown into such a beautiful young woman; the warriors of the Liao Kingdom must be fighting tooth and nail for you!” The two were actually eight or nine years apart in age, but Yelu Jinglie was remarkably well-preserved; anyone who did not know them would surely mistake them for siblings. “Uncle, you still love to tease people,” Yelu Huangwu said with a smile. “Eleven years have passed since we last met. The fact that you recognized me at a glance shows that you are the one who cares about me the most in the entire Liao Dynasty.” She was demoted at fifteen for privately building an army. Officially, she was sent to guard Empress Dowager Xiao’s tomb, but in reality, she was under house arrest. “Even if many more eleven-year periods passed, I would still recognize my niece at a glance,” Yelu Jinglie sighed. “A-Wu resembles the Empress Dowager, especially after so many years of filial piety; her demeanor has become increasingly similar.” Empress Dowager Xiao had once held great power in the Liao Dynasty; Yelu Jinglie’s words were clearly intended to put her in a difficult position. Yelu Huangwu understood perfectly well and smiled faintly. “I do not want to suffer like my mother all my life. I am fortunate to have inherited some of her beauty; I will be content if I can find a good husband in the future.” “Haha! A-Wu, what ambition!” Yelu Jinglie laughed heartily. At present, everything seemed harmonious. In reality, a fierce competition was brewing beneath the surface. Ten years ago, the two had already clashed secretly several times. At that time, Yelu Huangwu was still young, and although talented, she did not yet hold much power in the Liao Kingdom. Therefore, there was not much conflict between them. Now, however, things were different. Yelu Jinglie had long coveted the throne, and Yelu Huangwu had become the current Emperor’s right-hand man. If they were to clash again, it certainly would not be a minor skirmish like before. “What were you looking at just now, A-Wu?” Yelu Jinglie asked. “Icicles.” The icicles on the eaves reflected a dazzling light. Yelu Huangwu said cheerfully, “I heard that the Southern Song only had one snowfall all winter, on the day Ling Ziyue was beheaded, and not a drop of rain fell in the spring. Truly, Heaven blesses our Great Liao!” “Yes! Heaven blesses Great Liao!” Yelu Jinglie felt a hidden worry. The new Emperor had ascended the throne, but his position was not yet secure. Currently, most tribes were still on his side. But once they achieved an unprecedented victory in the attack on the Song, the domestic situation would be unpredictable! Seizing the throne again would be even more difficult. Just then… A eunuch hurried over and bowed, saying, “Princess, Your Highness, the Emperor requests your presence.” The two nodded slightly and followed the eunuch up the steps into the hall. A faint medicinal scent filled the room. A man draped in a black cloak stood by the window, feeding a hawk. “Greetings, Your Majesty,” the two said in unison, bowing. “No need for formalities,” the man replied without looking up, continuing to feed the hawk. This was Yelu Jinglie’s first time meeting the new Emperor so closely. He could not help but steal glances at him out of the corner of his eye. The man was very tall, though slightly thin, with a sickly pale face, and his downcast eyes bore a striking resemblance to his own! After feeding the hawk, the Emperor returned to his seat. “Sit,” he said. “Thank you, Your Majesty.” The two chose seats to sit on either side of each other. After the eunuchs served tea, Yelu Jinglie rose again. “I have come to inquire, Your Majesty, about the arrangements for the tribal chiefs’ coming to pay homage in the spring.” “As in previous years, thank you for your trouble, Uncle,” the Emperor replied. The new Emperor of Liao was named Yelu Quancang. He had been adopted by a wise man in search of longevity since childhood. Yelu Jinglie barely remembered what his nephew looked like back then, and there was no affection between them whatsoever. He was currently more curious about Yelu Quancang. Yelu Quancang leaned against the armrest, his robes flowing, his dark hair half-disheveled. At first glance, he seemed more otherworldly than Yelu Jinglie. However, upon closer inspection, his sharply defined face, with its brows like blades and deep phoenix eyes, exuded a majestic and cold aura, unable to conceal his imperial presence. Yelu Jinglie’s heart skipped a beat, and he quickly bowed. “It is my duty; how dare I complain of hardship?” “Uncle, if you are not busy, why not sit in the side hall and wait for me to have lunch together?” the Emperor said. The Emperor inviting him to lunch was something Yelu Jinglie would only do if the tribes collectively rebelled; otherwise, how could he refuse? “Thank you, Your Majesty.” “Uncle, take care.” Yelu Huangwu rose to see him off. Seeing that he had left, Yelu Quancang spoke first, “Take Guihu to assist in the attack on Song, and be sure to capture Zhending Prefecture in one fell swoop.” “But the medicine…” Yelu Huangwu was already prepared to personally go to Song to seize the medicine. “Leave it to Wei Yuzhi; he is not incompetent,” Yelu Quancang said. Unsure whether he was acting out of caution, Yelu Huangwu did not press the matter. “Yes, but the Ghost Tiger’s strength is far less than before, and their assistance may be limited. It would be best if we could find a way to get the various tribes to contribute.” After she was imprisoned, the Ghost Tiger disbanded and went into hiding. Their strength had not diminished but rather grown, even surpassing the royal guards, Ghost Shadow. However, she chose to conceal their power. “Hmm,” Yelu Quancang responded indifferently, his words neither believing nor disbelieving. Yelu Huangwu, recalling her uncle being invited to a meal, understood. The Emperor likely had this in mind. Even if her uncle had not come today, he would have summoned him anyway. The Emperor’s cunning and shrewdness far surpassed hers. With such an Emperor, the Liao Dynasty’s conquest of the Song Dynasty was imminent. Unfortunately… If she could not reclaim the heart’s blood and the Emperor died, the throne would likely fall to Yelu Jinglie. At that point, her days would be numbered! Yelu Jinglie was defeated by the low status of his maternal clan, but he had the advantage of longevity. As the saying goes, “A new Emperor brings a new court,” and frequent changes in the dynasty were extremely detrimental. Short-lived emperors reigned for only a few years, dying before they could accomplish anything significant. If this continued, the country would decline year by year. Both officials and the people yearned for a long-lived monarch. Late in the fourth month. The Liao Kingdom was like a pack of wolves starving after a winter’s hunger. Fortunately, the court had anticipated this and had recalled Wu Zhuo, stationed in Jiaozhi, to defend the city. Wu Zhuo had previously served as a general against the Liao and had a considerable record. While leading a large army to resist would not guarantee victory, he would certainly not allow the Liao army to easily approach Bianjing. However, Yelu Huangwu secretly sent Guihu, posing as a member of the Song Dynasty’s Konghe Army, to deliver an oral message to Xu Yun, ordering him to lead troops to block the Liao cavalry. Xu Yun believed it to be true. After deploying defenses at Xijin Prefecture, he personally led 10,000 elite troops to assist Wu Zhuo in resisting the enemy! The following day, the Liao Ghost Tiger Army infiltrated Xijin Prefecture, coordinating with 3,000 Liao soldiers to retake the prefecture, annihilating Xu Yun’s 70,000-strong army. Meanwhile, the Song Dynasty’s northern region suffered from prolonged drought, and a plague was quietly spreading. The devastating news reached Bianjing like snowflakes. The Emperor, who had always been engrossed in cultivating immortality, seemed struck by lightning and finally began to govern diligently. However, resolving these numerous issues was no easy task. Only now did he truly understand the importance of Ling Ziyue. The Liao and Song dynasties finally sat down at the negotiating table again. This time, the situation was far from optimistic; the Song Dynasty’s territory might shrink further south. Just a short while ago, the entire nation was immersed in the immense joy of capturing Xijin Prefecture, but in the blink of an eye, the situation deteriorated rapidly. It seemed they could not even hold their borders—a fall from grace as if from heaven to hell! If there was any good news amidst this dramatic disaster, it was that the Song Dynasty, after suffering such a heavy blow, was finally showing signs of awakening. Defending the country was of paramount importance. Humans were easily influenced by their atmosphere; even a scholar, normally powerless, could impulsively take up arms and fight. As Chu Dingjiang said, “Confucianism had undergone transformations and was no longer what it once was, but its spirit had never disappeared.” At the edge of the jungle bordering Jiaozhi in the southernmost part of the Song Dynasty, five people emerged one after another. The group found a hunter nearby to wash and rest, taking more than two hours to become recognizable. After a brief disguise, they headed towards Yongzhou. Although they mostly traveled along small paths, they still managed to gather considerable information along the way. “It’s over.” Ling Ziyue felt utterly weak. “What do you mean?” Li Qingzhi asked hastily. Sui Yuntong said, “General Wu should not be that incompetent! If Zhending Prefecture had not fallen, why would His Majesty have ordered General Xu to abandon Xijin and rush to Zhending Prefecture to resist the Liao army? It is most likely that General Xu fell for a Liao trick! This plan could both recapture Xijin and bring down General Xu.” At the time, the situation was urgent, and Xu Yun had no doubt about Wu Zhuo’s abilities. He had hesitated before sending troops, but ultimately, considering Wu Zhuo’s urgent dispatch to Zhending Prefecture by the court, he could not rule out the possibility that he was overwhelmed in the short term. However, regardless of the circumstances, Xu Yun was undeniably responsible for this major blunder! Even if the country was in peril and needed capable men, how could he explain the lives of those 70,000 soldiers? His abilities would inevitably be questioned. “Given General Xu’s character, he will most likely commit suicide.” Ling Ziyue knew Xu Yun too well. He was very cautious in his actions, and with his own example as a warning, he might sacrifice himself to protect his family. The two great generals of the Song Dynasty were one with too many concerns and the other with too few concerns.

chapters.title: Breaking the Promise
chapters.content: Upon arriving in Yongzhou, the group suddenly had access to more information, gaining a clearer understanding of many situations. Currently, negotiations between Liao and Song were underway, making it impossible to punish Xu Yun for the time being. He was prioritizing the overall situation, stationing troops in Hejian to hinder the Liao army. Although Liao appeared to have achieved an overwhelming victory, the situation within Liao was far from optimistic, making a prolonged war unwise. They had made two preparations: if a settlement could be reached, all the better; if not, they were not afraid to sustain the war through conflict. Meanwhile, the Song court was filled with fervor, with even wealthy merchants and gentry donating money and grain to the court, willingly obeying its orders and transporting food and medicinal herbs northward for disaster relief. Under such circumstances, even if the Liao army attacked, they might not be without a fighting chance. The bargaining chips of both sides were not significantly different. The envoys from both countries remained deadlocked at the negotiating table for half a month, without reaching a conclusion. The Liao Kingdom was willing to withdraw its troops, but on the condition that its territory be redrawn, with the Qiong River as the boundary, and all areas, including Zhengding Prefecture and Hejian Prefecture, would belong to the Liao Kingdom. This was the final concession made by the Liao Kingdom after half a month of negotiations. As a result, the Liao Kingdom’s territory moved several dozen li closer to the border. “Fight! I refuse to believe that the Song Dynasty’s million-strong army cannot stop the Liao army!” The restaurant was in an uproar, with someone slamming their fist on the table in anger. “The history of the Sixteen Prefectures of Yan and Yun must not be repeated!” An Jiu occupied a corner table, eating while listening to the commotion in the main hall. As soon as the man finished speaking, voices of agreement arose around him; surprisingly, the vast majority of people supported war. If even in such a remote place, such was the situation. One could imagine the situation in the north. Someone else said, “But it is said that all three routes in Hebei are suffering from severe drought; even without war, the people are destitute. If war really breaks out, the consequences… are unpredictable.” These words… Immediately, someone objected, “That does not mean we can cede territory from both routes! There’s precedent for this. Since the time of Emperor Taizu, there has been an attempt to recover the Sixteen Prefectures of Yan and Yun, but what was the result? After several generations, not only have we failed to recover our lost lands, but we are even being forced to cede more! If we are going to fight, we should fight to the death! Unless the Liao people can slaughter all the people of our Great Song, we will not give up a cun of land!” Another person said, “It’s not like there’s no chance. General Ling was able to capture Xijin Prefecture in one fell swoop, which shows that this matter is very promising. As long as the mountains remain, there’s no shortage of firewood. It is better than inappropriate bravado!” The people in the hall argued fiercely over these two viewpoints, and in the end, the pro-war side won. “Should we fight this battle or not?” Li Qingzhi asked quietly. Sui Yuntong said, “Whether we fight or not is up to the court. What’s the point of thinking about it?” An Jiu, however, felt that this battle would not happen. She did not understand politics, but she often carried out missions. When facing a formidable target, she would never easily rush in to assassinate them, but rather lie in wait in the shadows for the best opportunity to strike a fatal blow. The same principle applied between nations. Therefore, she believed the Liao Kingdom would continue to concede, and the negotiations would not drag on too long, given the Liao army’s significant losses abroad. Every extra day would cause them anxiety. As An Jiu predicted, on the twenty-fourth day, both sides finally reached an agreement— Since the Treaty of Chanyuan, the Song Dynasty would pay the Liao Kingdom an annual tribute of 100,000 taels of silver. Starting this year, this would be increased to 250,000 taels, along with various grains, artifacts, and beautiful women.
