Furthermore, Hejian Prefecture would be the boundary; the land north of Hejian Prefecture would be open to Liao grazing… All of the above was formally signed in a treaty, with the Song Dynasty acknowledging its vassalage and paying tribute. The treaty took over a month to reach Yongzhou after its signing. The bustling public suddenly fell silent; the entire Song Dynasty experienced a brief period of silence. No one discussed it, no one objected, and no one rejoiced; everyone seemed stunned. However, in reality, this was already a relatively good outcome. Previously, the Song Dynasty treated the Liao Dynasty as a vassal state, paying annual tribute, which was essentially the same as submission. Now, this was merely a formality, and the tribute had increased; the Song Dynasty could afford 150,000 taels of silver. However, for most scholars, ceding territory was preferable to accepting “submission and tribute.” Submission meant the Song Dynasty was no longer an equal state to the Liao but an enslaved one. This humiliation was even more unbearable than paying reparations to other states! Besides paying annual tribute to the Liao, the Song Dynasty also had to pay 50,000 taels of silver to the Western Xia, nominally to appease a vassal state, but essentially it was the same. After a brief shock, a sense of grief and indignation spread. Scholars began to express dissatisfaction with the reality, secretly criticizing it. Satirical folk songs circulated widely, but the court used force to suppress them, temporarily silencing these dissenting voices. In the middle of the sixth month, an imperial edict recalled Xu Yun. Although Xu Yun was a valiant general, his overly cautious nature as a subject, coupled with his overshadowing of Ling Ziyue in Hebei, had diminished his reputation. The loss of 70,000 soldiers further strained his image, leaving few in the court or even among the common people willing to plead for his life. Xu Yun was ordered back to court and immediately submitted a 2,000-word memorial of apology. He then took his sword and committed suicide at the palace gate to prove his innocence. When the ministers arrived, they found only his body lying in a pool of blood. In the end, Xu Yun had merely fallen into a trap, leading to the defeat. While victory and defeat were common in war, the consequences of his failure were far too severe. The Liao Kingdom’s scheme, eliminating two Song generals in exchange for Song’s submission, was a resounding victory. At this point, some could not help but think that if Ling Ziyue had not been stopped from continuing his attack on Liao and if he had not died, they might still have ended up at the negotiating table, but the outcome would likely have been completely different. The current Emperor was now filled with regret. Fortunately, due to the recent low temperatures, the plague in the three routes of Hebei was contained before it could spread widely, much to the relief of the entire court. Following this incident, the Emperor suddenly fell ill. Many court officials who had not previously taken sides began secretly choosing other allies, and a tense atmosphere of impending conflict arose between the Crown Prince and the Second Prince. With one court matter after another, the pursuit of Ling Ziyue and his associates was temporarily suspended, especially after the Emperor’s illness; no one mentioned the matter again. Chu Dingjiang, unable to leave immediately, sent a messenger to Yongzhou to deliver a message. An Jiu left Bianjing in winter, and when she returned, it was another winter, and again, it was snowing heavily. She saw Chu Dingjiang in the snow, draped in a black cloak, and was slightly dazed, as if she had only turned a corner in the blink of an eye. An Jiu walked step by step through the snow to him, smiling. “I am back.” Chu Dingjiang did not speak, but reached out and pulled her into his arms. After a moment, he released her. “You all go back to Mei Mansion to find Sheng Changying.” “Alright.” Sui Yuntong led the others away, leaving An Jiu behind. “I knew you would break your promise.” An Jiu raised her hand to brush his hood away. “We agreed on a year’s notice. If we did not come back, you still could not leave!”

chapters.title: From Here
chapters.content: A smile appeared in Chu Dingjiang’s eyes. “I originally thought you were just a beautiful woman on the other side of the water, but I never imagined you would become my confidante.” An Jiu had always thought that words like “beautiful woman” and “confidante” were far removed from her own life. Hearing Chu Dingjiang’s words now, it felt like he was talking about someone else, leaving her with little feeling. “Ah Jiu, I cannot back down now,” Chu Dingjiang said. An Jiu looked at the misty breath he exhaled. “I know. If you want to stay, why should I not accompany you? I am just curious; why did you suddenly change your mind?” Chu Dingjiang did not seem to be the kind of person who acted on a whim. “That day, seeing you and Hua Rongjian releasing lanterns by the river, I suddenly had an epiphany.” Chu Dingjiang touched her cold cheek. “Human hearts, power, or peace and tranquility… if one does not strive and fight in this world, even what is easily obtained may turn into a fleeting dream. Moreover, the emptiness in one’s heart is truly hard to fill if one is mediocre. Ah Jiu, with you by my side in this life, I can live life to the fullest, and I will have no regrets, no matter the outcome.” At this moment, a woman would usually be very moved and would inevitably explain that she had no affair with other men, but An Jiu’s blunt honesty tore apart the tenderness. “I never had any goals to begin with. Following you seemed like a good choice.” Chu Dingjiang sighed helplessly. “When will you understand love?” An Jiu suddenly remembered Zhu Pianxian’s methods of seducing Sheng Changying. She was a pragmatist; once she decided to act, she immediately pointed her index finger. Because she was so focused on what she was doing, there was not a trace of tenderness or affection in her expression. Chu Dingjiang did not guess the profound meaning behind it, so he asked, “What are you doing?” An Jiu, seemingly lost in thought, almost reflexively grabbed his hand, placed her index finger against his, and grinned brightly. “That’s how we communicate where I am from.” “Communicate?” Chu Dingjiang looked at their intertwined fingertips. “What does that mean?” “It’s so we know what each other is thinking.” An Jiu insisted that this was their hometown’s way of expressing affection. People unconsciously raise their voices when they lie. Her overly forceful tone made her seem suspicious, but Chu Dingjiang did not call her out on it; instead, he found it amusing. “The ten fingers are connected to the heart, so that makes sense. Now, do you know what I am thinking?” An Jiu reluctantly withdrew her hand. “You are thinking: An Jiu, you idiot!” “Hmm?” Chu Dingjiang raised an eyebrow. “It actually worked?” He grabbed her hand, their index fingers touching again. Chu Dingjiang said enigmatically, “You are thinking now. Being able to guess my thoughts is because you are smart.” An Jiu’s eyes widened. She had indeed been secretly chuckling to herself: Old man, I guessed it all thanks to my exceptional intelligence! “Huh?” An Jiu was surprised for a moment but quickly realized that he guessed it because of his intelligence… and she had reason to suspect that Chu Dingjiang had been playing her tricks all along; after all, playing mind games was his forte. Thinking of this, An Jiu rolled her eyes at him. “Hmph!” One moment it was the warmth of spring; the next it was the dead of winter. They said children change their minds quickly, and An Jiu was no exception. “Are you acquainted with Madam Hua?” Chu Dingjiang asked, trying to find a topic she might be interested in. An Jiu indeed put aside her prejudice against him. “Something happened to her?” “Not really,” Chu Dingjiang said. “I heard that she’s been ordered to assassinate Hua Rongtian within six months.” An Jiu had almost forgotten that Mei Jiu had joined the Konghe Army! Assassinating Hua Rongtian was something Mei Jiu absolutely could not do. “What will happen if she disobeys?” “You forgot? The Konghe Army has a tradition of using Gu poison to control people. Madam Hua is prone to betraying her master on missions, and there are precedents for this. Once is not enough; she’s been poisoned multiple times,” Chu Dingjiang said. Previously, a Dangerous Moon assassin fell in love with Hua Rongjian but ultimately could not bring herself to do it, not only exposing herself but also revealing the Emperor’s intentions against the Hua family. But now the conflict between the Emperor and the Hua family was out in the open, and An Jiu was very puzzled. “If Mei Jiu makes a move, will the Emperor and the Hua family not completely break off relations?” Chu Dingjiang analyzed for her, “The Emperor is seriously ill and has to plan for the future. The Konghe Army has discovered that Hua Rongjian has been in close contact with the Second Prince, showing signs of wanting to pledge allegiance. If the Emperor were to pass away, the Song Dynasty would likely experience a civil war over the throne, and the Song Dynasty could not withstand such turmoil.” “But that Crown Prince is really not good.” An Jiu’s mind was filled with images of white, swaying flesh when she thought of the Crown Prince. Chu Dingjiang smiled. “Do not be fooled by his seemingly absurd behavior; he’s ten times more cunning than the Second Prince.” An Jiu ignored Mei Jiu and asked him, “So what’s your plan… You do not intend to support the Crown Prince, do you?” Chu Dingjiang smiled without answering. An Jiu tugged at his robe. “Really?” “I’d like to go to the Second Prince’s residence for a while,” Chu Dingjiang said. “Did you not say he was not as cunning as the Crown Prince?” An Jiu privately thought that being an Emperor meant being unfathomable.

chapters.title: Whose White Flower Has Just Grown (1)
chapters.content: “The current Emperor is quite shrewd, but is he a wise ruler? Character and talent are the most important.” Chu Dingjiang had been observing the Second Prince for some time. He was brave but not impulsive, sometimes lacking in strategy, but when his advisors offered various suggestions, he remained unfazed and could choose the one most suitable for the current situation. The Second Prince’s birth mother, Lady Li, was from a military family. Her appearance was not particularly outstanding, and because of her overly resolute nature, she lacked the gentle beauty of ordinary women. Furthermore, she lacked talent, so the Emperor always disliked her. Before Lady Li’s family declined, the Emperor reluctantly tolerated her, but once the Li family finally relinquished their military power, he would not even look at her, resulting in the Second Prince having little contact with his father during his childhood. Under Lady Li’s influence, the Second Prince developed a greater fondness for martial arts. Chu Dingjiang recounted all this to An Jiu, saying, “I’ve also learned about Lady Li; she’s truly an extraordinary woman. In the harem, she does not vie for favor, nor does she compromise herself to please the Emperor. Her actions are remarkably composed. With such a character, her child, if carefully raised, will surely be quite good.” If Lady Li wanted to gain favor, she could easily have molded her son into the kind of person the Emperor liked, but she didn’t. The Emperor did not like Lady Li, and she probably did not think much of the Emperor either. “If the skin is gone, where will the hair attach?” Chu Dingjiang sighed. “I thought I could be indifferent to everything, but seeing the Song Dynasty in turmoil, I cannot help but want to wade into the muddy waters.” An Jiu thought for a moment and said, “We are still young. If we spent our lives hidden in the mountains, it would be a bit monotonous. Why not wade into the muddy waters first and then wash ourselves clean and come back to herd sheep when the water clears?” Chu Dingjiang was very pleased to hear this and held her hand tightly. “My Ah Jiu is so understanding.” An Jiu honestly said, “Actually, we are so close; you do not need to be hypocritical. I just had not noticed.” “…” The two walked silently through the snow until they reached the plum blossoms. As dusk fell, the lanterns in Bianjing City were lit, casting a warm orange glow on the snow. The wind and snow were fierce, and the streets were almost deserted. At the Hua Mansion, a group of people walked quickly along the veranda. Two maids in light green jackets and skirts led a woman in a red dress, carrying lanterns. Four maids in brown jackets and skirts followed behind. No one spoke, only the rustling of clothes. As they approached a bend, the woman in the red dress saw a group of people approaching from the opposite direction. Prime Minister Hua was extremely busy with state affairs, and his evening meals were irregular, as were those of Hua Rongtian. The Prime Minister’s wife disliked noise, and since her two daughters-in-law were sent by the Emperor, she did not want to have much interaction with them. Therefore, for convenience, everyone usually ate in their own courtyards, only gathering as a family a few times a month. “Stop, wait for sister-in-law,” the woman in red said, stopping. Mei Ruyan had only seen this sister-in-law five or six times since marrying into the Hua family, and had not had a chance to speak to her. Hearing that she was not only a secret guard of the Konghe Army but also a member of the Mei family, and that someone who could interact with Hua Rongtian was certainly not a simple character, Mei Ruyan wanted to learn more. Seeing the other person stop, Mei Jiu slowed her pace. Ever since she learned that Hua Rongjian had married Mei Ruyan, she had tried her best to avoid meeting her. Fortunately, she usually preferred to stay indoors, so she did not need to deliberately avoid her. Now, seeing Mei Ruyan stop, Mei Jiu hesitated, but it was inevitable that they would meet again. The two met at the bend in the road. Mei Ruyan bowed slightly. “Sister-in-law.” Mei Jiu returned the bow slightly. “Sister-in-law.” They could not help but look at each other. Mei Jiu saw a familiar face yet felt a sense of unfamiliarity. Mei Ruyan wore a red, wide-sleeved satin jacket embroidered with slender white plum blossoms in silver thread, bright yet with a touch of fresh elegance. She was more alluring than before, but her eyes held a hint of coldness, no longer displaying the bright smile she used to give to everyone. Fate was fickle. Years ago, when Mei Ruyan desperately tried to shed the image of a courtesan, her words and demeanor always carried a hint of worldliness. Now, however, she had come to terms with it and finally possessed a refined air. Mei Jiu, on the other hand, wore a dark purple jacket and skirt, with a cloak over it. Her face was fair, and her eyes were like autumn water; her nose and cheeks were red from the cold, giving her a healthy glow. This was the first time Mei Ruyan had closely observed Mei Jiu’s current appearance. Indeed, she lived up to the Mei family’s reputation for producing beauties—a captivating beauty with a touch of innocence, the kind of woman men would want to protect at first sight. What surprised Mei Ruyan even more was that this woman exuded not a trace of murderous intent. “It’s too cold outside, let’s hurry,” Mei Jiu said, suppressing her emotions. “Please go first, sister-in-law,” Mei Ruyan said. Mei Jiu did not say much, only nodded slightly, and stepped through the archway. Her eyes narrowed slightly to shield herself from the wind and snow, and the corners of her lips curled up almost imperceptibly. When Mei Jiu saw Mei Ruyan deliberately waiting for her, she felt quite uneasy. However, she was no longer the naive girl living under her mother’s wing, and her response revealed nothing. At that moment, she suddenly felt incredibly relieved. She thought to herself, “So this is what it feels like to deceive others. No wonder so many people are obsessed with scheming.”

chapters.title: Whose White Flower Has Just Grown (2)
chapters.content: The Hua family’s dinner was unusually quiet. After dinner, Prime Minister Hua and Hua Rongtian left early due to their respective official duties, while Hua Rongjian and Hua Rongjun stayed to talk with the Old Madam. Mei Jiu had long heard of the two brothers’ reputations, but upon seeing them in person, she felt that the rumors were not entirely true. Hua Rongjun was not as cheerful as she had imagined; despite his young age, he had a melancholy air about him. Hua Rongjian, on the other hand, was more talkative but not as unreliable as the rumors suggested. “Second Sister-in-law does not look well; she should go out more,” the usually taciturn Hua Rongjun suddenly interjected. The Old Madam disagreed. “A young lady should be quiet, take care of her health, and give Second Brother a healthy baby boy soon!” It was generally believed that women who practice martial arts were physically strong, but too much of a good thing could be bad; those women with high martial arts skills were actually less likely to conceive. Mei Ruyan glanced at Hua Rongjian, and seeing his reluctance to speak, rose and said, “Mother is right. Thank you for your concern, brother-in-law.” “You must also remember this,” the Old Madam said, looking at Mei Jiu. Mei Jiu had been married into the Hua family for over a year, and every day she would pay her respects to the Old Madam morning and evening, rain or shine, regardless of whether the Old Madam saw her or not. If she were an ordinary daughter-in-law, it would not be a problem, but Mei Jiu was someone sent by the Emperor, and such attentiveness inevitably made people suspect ulterior motives. To prevent Mei Jiu from harming Hua Rongtian, the Old Madam secretly sent people to monitor her, but each time the guards reported back, she was either embroidering, writing, painting, playing the zither, or reading and playing Weiqi. Looking at the embroidery and calligraphy the guards retrieved from her, they discovered that she was actually a woman of great talent, completely unlike the assassins of the Konghe Army! The Old Madam did not know much about the Konghe Army; ninety percent of her knowledge of female assassins came from her previous eldest daughter-in-law. Hua Rongtian’s first wife was no fool either. However, since she devoted most of her energy to martial arts training, her knowledge of music, Weiqi, calligraphy, and painting was only superficial. She was far from achieving the level of skill Mei Jiu possessed. These things could not be innate, especially calligraphy. It would take over a decade of practice to write like that. How could a female assassin spend all her time on such things? The Old Madam was puzzled. “Your daughter-in-law will heed Mother’s teachings,” Mei Jiu said, rising. The Old Madam, seeing her every move as that of a sheltered young lady, found it even more unbelievable. She said to Hua Rongjian and Hua Rongjun, “You two go ahead with your work. I will speak with the eldest and second sons’ wives.” The two brothers looked slightly surprised, pausing for a moment before getting up to leave. A maidservant brought tea. The Old Madam waved for all the maids to leave, leaving only an old woman and a personal maidservant by her side. “We both know perfectly well how you two married into this family. I do not want to waste my breath explaining,” the Old Madam said. The Old Madam was usually obedient to her husband and son, giving the impression of a woman lacking independent thought, but at this moment, her authority was oppressive. “Being confined to this courtyard is not as liberating as walking in the dark, experiencing the freedom of death,” she said. Her words carried a deeper meaning. Mei Jiu replied, “Like duckweed born of water, yet rootless and adrift, if given a handful of earth, I would gladly be crushed into dust.” She meant that being in the Konghe Army was a matter of necessity, and if someone could give her peace, she would be willing to die in that peace. She met the Old Madam’s scrutiny with a resolute gaze. She was usually charming and delicate, but now all her vulnerability was hidden. After her rebirth, Mei Jiu had pondered many things. For example, her pitiful yet feigned strength could soften Hua Rongtian’s gaze, but it would only provoke disdain from other women. This insight came from An Jiu; if she had not so openly expressed her disdain, Mei Jiu would not be so keenly observing the subtle reactions of those around her. Mei Jiu was inherently a woman of an extremely delicate and sensitive nature, and having spent so much time with her maids, she had already grasped eight or nine tenths of their thoughts. After Mei Jiu stated her position, Mei Ruyan immediately followed. “My heart is with my sister.” She did not call her sister-in-law, but rather “sister,” intending to make the Old Madam understand that they were both women of the Mei family, bound together in the same boat. However, Mei Ruyan preferred freedom. “Very good.” The Old Madam’s expression relaxed slightly. “I only want to tell you that I am merely a mother, I neither understand nor concern myself with politics, but anyone who dares to harm my son, I will exact revenge a hundredfold.” The two women agreed verbally, but in their hearts, they thought, “The one who most wants to harm your son is the Emperor!” However, although the Old Madam’s attitude was relaxed, she thought to herself, “These two women are more difficult to deal with than the previous one!” Ordinary female assassins did not have so many schemes in their minds. Even if they were somewhat cunning, how could they compare to the Old Madam, a master of inner courtyard intrigue? Despite her current situation—no mother-in-law, no sisters-in-law, and a weak daughter-in-law—she had once lived with her mother-in-law and sisters-in-law and had her share of squabbles. The three women spoke for a while before the Old Madam dismissed them. The snow outside had subsided. Mei Ruyan, holding an umbrella, walked alongside Mei Jiu, trying to ingratiate herself. “Are you from the eldest branch of the family, sister?” Hearing Mei Ruyan’s affectionate address of “sister,” Mei Jiu felt a moment of disorientation, suddenly understanding many things. Before, she had not met many people, and among the group of girls confined together, Mei Ruyan was the kindest to her. Therefore, she naturally considered Mei Ruyan her best sister. Now, she was no longer herself, yet Mei Ruyan’s address of “sister” remained unchanged… “You should still call me sister-in-law,” Mei Jiu said with a smile. “We must be careful about our relationship.” “Sister-in-law is right,” Mei Ruyan replied, her smile deepening. Whether it was the Mei Ruyan of the past or the Mei Ruyan of the present, she always possessed this affable quality. Even strangers or those with whom she harbored resentment found it difficult to remain cold. Mei Jiu thought that perhaps only An Jiu in this world could do that. Thinking of An Jiu, Mei Jiu remembered that An Jiu had once told her about Mei Ruyan’s allegiance to Wei Yuzhi. Even who Wei Yuzhi was, it was An Jiu who had explained it to her. That was irrelevant. What mattered was that she knew Mei Ruyan had allied herself with the Liao Kingdom and joined the Konghe Army. Whatever the reasons behind it, she could take precautions in advance. Seeing that Mei Jiu’s answer was irrelevant, Mei Ruyan knew she was not interested in establishing a connection, so she did not press the issue. The two parted ways at the archway, heading to their respective rooms. Thick cotton was sewn into the curtains to block the cold. A stove burned inside, making it warm as spring. Upon entering, one could immediately feel the heavy dampness on their clothes. Mei Jiu, attended by her maids, changed her clothes behind a screen, dismissed everyone in the room, and sat on the couch with a book in her hand. Most of the maids were there to monitor her, so she preferred to be alone most of the time. “What you said to your mother-in-law was so sentimental and fake; it gave me goosebumps,” a woman’s voice suddenly spoke in the quiet room. The words were disdainful, but the tone clearly implied, “Well done!” Mei Jiu looked up in surprise and saw a slender figure sitting down in the chair opposite her.

chapters.title: The Uncle’s Shattered Dignity
chapters.content: “An Jiu.” In the warm orange light, Mei Jiu smiled radiantly, her bright eyes as gentle and clear as ever. However, An Jiu knew she was no longer the innocent little rabbit she once was. “It’s been a while since I last saw you; you’ve changed beyond recognition.” Her words were neither praise nor criticism, but a slight feeling stirred within her. Mei Jiu smiled serenely. “And it is not just me, An Jiu. Seeing you like this now, I am very happy for you.” An Jiu was slightly taken aback. Although the two had previously coexisted as one, Mei Jiu had never sensed her emotions. Now, she was becoming more and more like a “person.” “I heard you received orders to assassinate Hua Rongtian.” That was why An Jiu rushed over overnight. Mei Jiu’s expression darkened. “This is fate, is it not?” “So you are planning to wait to die?” An Jiu frowned, staring intently at her, both wanting her to act against Hua Rongtian and not wanting her to. The original Mei Jiu would never have harmed Hua Rongtian, but now, An Jiu was uncertain. “How could I?” Mei Jiu suddenly smiled, meeting her gaze. Her composure and determination were dazzling. “Even ants cling to life; I, blessed by Heaven, how dare I take my own life?” An Jiu felt ashamed of herself for recognizing the situation so quickly; she had remained lost, only able to follow in others’ footsteps. “I would never kill my husband.” Mei Jiu’s expression seemed calm, but the tight grip on her book betrayed her inner emotions. “Though everything is dark now, I believe that as long as I keep going, there will always be a light at the end of the tunnel.” An Jiu’s slightly anxious heart relaxed. Mei Jiu was still largely as kind as before. “You’ve taken a liking to Hua Rongtian? You slept with him?” Mei Jiu blushed. She spat, “When will you ever be more subtle?” “Do not try to change the subject,” An Jiu said seriously. Mei Jiu shook her head helplessly. Her cheeks were flushed, and her eyes were brimming. “He and I have never…never consummated our marriage.” “Huh, is Hua Rongtian perhaps ill?” An Jiu asked suspiciously. “A girl like you easily arouses a man’s desire to trample and ravage.” Mei Jiu’s face instantly turned purple, so ashamed she wanted to disappear into a hole. An Jiu did not realize how strange her words were. Seeing Mei Jiu’s reaction, she added, “Look, you are just like that…” “Do not say anything,” Mei Jiu quickly interrupted. “Did you not come to help me?” An Jiu shook her head, calmly telling her, “You are overthinking it. I just came to see you.” “…” Mei Jiu had finally calmed down a bit, but An Jiu had rendered her speechless. For a long while, An Jiu remained silent, simply looking at her, as if she truly had come to “see” her. Mei Jiu felt somewhat embarrassed by her undisguised gaze. “How is my mother?” “Without you as a burden, she’s doing very well,” An Jiu said. Mei Jiu swallowed back many questions that were on the tip of her tongue and could only stammer, “That’s good then.” “I think you’ve misunderstood. First of all, Mei Yanran is now my mother. Although I get along very badly with her, and she does not want to talk to me, that’s an unchangeable fact. Secondly, I personally proved something very important to myself.” An Jiu began to delve into the depths of life, and this seriousness infected Mei Jiu. “What is it?” “A pig is a pig, even if it becomes a little smarter. It is still just a smarter pig,” An Jiu concluded. “You are not here to help in times of need; you are here to kick someone when they are down!” Although Mei Jiu said this, she had a feeling in her heart that An Jiu would not really stand idly by. An Jiu had always been like this to Mei Jiu. If Mei Jiu were poisoned and on the verge of death, she would definitely say, “Your face is blue now; you look especially ugly,” or “Do you have any last words?” But even if she said that, she would still try her best to save her. Some people were still annoying even when they were helping others. “Actually, I went back to Mei Mansion before coming here. Sheng Changying has a way to contact Mo Sigui. He’s in Daming Prefecture, not far from here. At his speed, he should be back in ten days at the latest.” An Jiu leaned against the armrest, one hand supporting her chin. “Besides, the antidote is very complicated. I do not know if you can hold on until then.” Luckily, Mei Jiu had a good temper; if it were Hua Rongjian, she would definitely have argued with her. “I am leaving.” An Jiu stood up. “Next time they give you the antidote, it would be best to leave some for Mo Sigui to analyze the poison.” “Alright.” Mei Jiu also stood up, about to ask her to stay, when she suddenly heard footsteps outside the door. Her heart tightened, and she turned to look. A lantern was lit in the courtyard, casting a faint shadow on the door. The person stopped at the door. Mei Jiu recognized it as Hua Rongtian and quickly turned back to tell An Jiu to leave through the back window, but found that she was already gone from inside. With a creak, the door was pushed open. Seeing Mei Jiu staring blankly at the center of the room, Hua Rongtian quickly scanned the room out of the corner of his eye but found nothing amiss. Mei Jiu tried hard to suppress her emotions and turned around, saying, “Why has my husband come?” Hua Rongtian never used to come here after nightfall, so his sudden appearance today made her somewhat uneasy. “They are gone?” Hua Rongtian said calmly. Hua Rongtian knew that members of the Konghe Army frequently came, so Mei Jiu did not hide anything. “Yes.” He did not press further. A silence fell over the room. Mei Jiu said, “They wanted me to assassinate you.” Hua Rongtian’s gaze darkened slightly. “Why tell me?” “Because you are my husband.” Mei Jiu slowly sat down on the edge of the couch. She had felt guilty in front of Hua Rongtian before, but now, as she spoke the truth, she suddenly felt at ease, a faint smile unconsciously appearing on her face. “I heard about you back in Mei Mansion. You went to propose then… I never imagined I would actually marry you. It is a blessing from heaven, but unfortunately, we are destined to be apart.” Her clear eyes gradually filled with mist, gathering into tears, sliding down her cheeks to the corners of her slightly upturned lips, blurring that faint smile with a poignant yet resolute quality. Hua Rongtian felt a dull ache in his heart. The suppressed grief and anger, with nowhere to vent, made his entire body tense. He had tasted this feeling once before, when he did not know his wife was an assassin. He had poured almost all his emotions into loving her. This time, he thought he had always guarded his heart tightly, without a trace of emotion, yet this woman had somehow entered his heart. And the weight she held in his heart surprised him. Only then did he realize that all the excuses he had made for coming today were, in reality, simply to see her. He wanted to see her shy smile with downcast eyes, to see her like a little rabbit struggling to suppress her excitement when she was happy, to see her eyes sparkling when she discussed poetry and literature, to see her frowning in deep thought while playing Weiqi… So, he already missed her this much. “Tenth Young Lady…” Hua Rongtian’s voice was low and hoarse. She wanted to tell Hua Rongtian that she was not Mei Ruhan. Nor was she the assassin from the Konghe Army who had impersonated Mei Ruyan to marry into the family; she was Mei Jiu. However, after a moment of silence, she replied, “Husband.” Mei Jiu had not forgotten that Hua Rongtian was not only her husband but also a brilliant politician. Hua Rongtian paused, regaining his usual calm and wisdom. Remembering what Mei Jiu had just said, a vague idea flashed through his mind. “Fourteenth Young Lady…” Hua Rongtian suddenly remembered proposing marriage at Mei Mansion that year. Mei Jiu’s expression changed slightly. Although her words had almost revealed her identity, how many people in this world would think of using a corpse to reincarnate? Had she underestimated Hua Rongtian…? Hua Rongtian had only been testing her casually, but seeing her reaction, he could not help but be surprised. “You are actually Fourteenth Young Lady?” There were many reasons why he had proposed to the Fourteenth Young Lady back then, the two most important being that the Mei family desperately needed her mother and, secondly, she had grown up away from home and would not have a strong sense of belonging to the Mei family. Of course, these were secondary considerations. Their main purpose was to test whether this Mei family was indeed from the Konghe Army and to gauge the Emperor’s attitude. The Emperor and the Hua family’s current open and blatant confrontation was closely related to this matter. Hua Rongtian could not understand many things. Fourteenth Young Lady should only be seventeen or eighteen years old this year, while the woman before him looked to be over twenty, yet her every move did not resemble that of an assassin who had trained in the Konghe Army for many years. Moreover, why would the Emperor have thought of using the Fourteenth Young Lady as a substitute? Seeing Hua Rongtian deep in thought, Mei Jiu realized he had not considered the possibility of resurrection. His bold guess stemmed from his previous lack of knowledge about the female assassin serving the Emperor, nor about Mei Jiu herself. Their eyes met, and Mei Jiu looked away. A cold wind carrying snow swept in from outside, rustling the scrolls on the bed. Not long after leaving the city, An Jiu spotted a tall, striking figure in the snowy twilight. “Chu Dingjiang!” An Jiu called out, running towards him. She moved with lightning speed. Chu Dingjiang felt she would bump into him, which was a pity… “When running at high speed, try not to stop suddenly,” Chu Dingjiang offered a plausible reason. “It can easily injure your internal organs.” An Jiu thought it made sense and readily agreed, “Alright.” “As it is today, you can just run into me; it will not hurt me,” Chu Dingjiang said. An Jiu glanced at him, seeing his deep and serious expression, and nodded, then asked, “Did you wait here for me for something?” “I guessed you’d definitely go to see Madam Hua, and I was worried about your safety alone,” Chu Dingjiang offered another reason that left no room for doubt. “The Liao Kingdom will absolutely not give up on the medicine person’s heart’s blood.” “Hmm,” An Jiu agreed. If Wei Yuzhi came looking for her again, she might not be as lucky as last time. “You need to practice your skills more diligently, and do not run around aimlessly. Just let me know if anything happens. Instead of wasting time playing with lanterns, you should practice more forms of martial arts,” Chu Dingjiang admonished her with a kind, uncle-like face. An Jiu pondered for a while, “After my meticulous analysis and rigorous reasoning, are you jealous?” “Hahaha!” Chu Dingjiang ruffled her hair. “You do not understand a man’s heart. I would not take such a small thing to heart.” “Really?” An Jiu was suspicious, but remembering his usual magnanimity, she thought she was overthinking it. Previously, Chu Dingjiang had largely adopted a hands-off approach towards An Jiu. Even when she was not immediately receptive, he was not impatient. Now, after much consideration, he decided he could not continue like this. He had many things to do in the future and could not always be by An Jiu’s side. If talented and handsome young men were to flock to her, it was hard to guarantee that An Jiu would not fall for one of them. Therefore, it was safer to win her heart first. This was Chu Dingjiang’s first time doing something like this, but he felt that conquering a city was a piece of cake, and winning a woman’s heart was definitely not a problem. The key was to proceed cautiously. He did not use his protective aura. By the time they returned to the island, the fine snow had already frozen into patches on his outer robe. “Come in and warm yourself by the fire,” An Jiu said. Chu Dingjiang followed her into the house without ceremony. An Jiu borrowed a stove from Sui Yuntong. When she returned to the house, she saw that Chu Dingjiang had taken off his thin undergarment, revealing the clearly defined outline of his strong physique. “Why not use your inner energy for protection?” An Jiu asked curiously, placing the stove in front of him. “It requires internal energy,” Chu Dingjiang replied calmly. Actually, for someone of his cultivation level, that amount of inner energy was negligible; otherwise, why would he use it so casually? An Jiu, after all, had no internal energy and did not understand such things. But clearly, An Jiu was not easily fooled. “Then why do you usually use it to shield yourself from snow and rain?” Chu Dingjiang pondered for a moment. “Do you not think it is quite imposing?” “…” An Jiu stared at him speechlessly, feeling like she’d just met him for the first time. “Take off your clothes and roast yourself,” Chu Dingjiang suggested. An Jiu quickly stripped off her clothes, leaving only a vest, and swayed around the stove with her bare arms. Chu Dingjiang had been celibate for so many years, and back then, he had not felt any affection for An Jiu. Just looking at her body was enough to make him unable to shake off his thoughts, almost giving him a nosebleed. Now, this scene was truly unbearable. She let her long hair down, the damp strands clinging to her arms, making them appear even whiter and more lustrous. Her top was tucked into her trousers, her slender waist seemingly impossible to encircle, and her buttocks, encased in thick trousers, appeared even more shapely… Chu Dingjiang felt a sudden, sharp urge rise within him. An Jiu, oblivious to his reaction, deftly untied her own trousers, revealing her undergarment and two long, slender, white legs. Her body, rejuvenated twice, was like solidified cream, her fair skin radiating a warm glow. Chu Dingjiang felt an unbearable throbbing pain and lowered his head, no longer looking. “Oh, the charcoal’s almost burned out.” An Jiu approached, poking at the embers with tongs. A pair of small, delicate feet came into Chu Dingjiang’s view. From the cold, her ten plump, round toes were a pale pink, and the newly healed wounds on the sides of her feet were a light red, possessing a cruel yet alluring beauty within their cuteness. He hurriedly looked up, only to see An Jiu walking barefoot to the wall, bending over, and searching for something. Her shorts were loose, revealing her round, plump buttocks. Chu Dingjiang could feel his own erection, something about to burst forth. Based on his past life’s experience, he knew what was about to happen. He grabbed his coat hanging at the side, but it was too late. It was over! He looked down at his wet crotch, hearing the sound of his manly dignity shattering into pieces. “A few more pieces,” An Jiu said, pulling a bag of charcoal from a pile of junk. Turning around, Chu Dingjiang was already gone.

chapters.title: A Lifetime’s Promise
chapters.content: Chu Dingjiang was always elusive, so An Jiu did not pay much attention. She lowered her head and used the tongs to put charcoal into the stove. The charcoal was slightly damp, and smoke soon began to rise, but thankfully, it was usable. An Jiu squinted, and through the mist, she saw Chu Dingjiang push open the door again, his lower body covered in snow. “What happened?” she asked. Chu Dingjiang brushed the snow off himself, calmly taking off his trousers and placing them beside the stove. “Nothing.” An Jiu was suspicious but did not press further. The snow on his trousers melted by the fire, quickly becoming damp patches, and then steam rose from them. Chu Dingjiang unfolded a blanket and wrapped it around An Jiu. “Are you not cold?” “I can handle this chill,” An Jiu said, wrapped in the blanket except for her small face, letting out a comfortable sigh. “If only we had some roasted sweet potatoes.” Chu Dingjiang had already recovered and smiled. “I will bring some over for you next time.” An Jiu nodded and ordered without hesitation, “Also, roasted chestnuts and roasted lamb.” “Alright,” Chu Dingjiang replied gently. “Come on, let’s wrap ourselves up together,” An Jiu invited him, opening the blanket further. Chu Dingjiang hesitated. If he went over, things could easily get out of control again, and the situation would be too awkward! After what had just happened, he began to doubt himself. An Jiu was not opposed to having sex with him, but the key question was, would he ruin his sexual prowess by holding back for so long? He was once a noble young master, with countless women eager to seduce him. Therefore, he inevitably harbored a condescending arrogance towards matters of the heart. An Jiu, being indifferent to romantic love, always seemed to provoke him. Now, having let go of that arrogance, he suddenly felt a surge of insecurity. Chu Dingjiang did not doubt his self-control, because he was certain he had none in front of An Jiu! Since that was the case, he might as well accept it readily; at worst, it would just be embarrassing. A jumble of thoughts flashed through his mind. Having made his decision, he got up and sat down beside An Jiu. Under the covers, their bodies pressed close together, the temperature steadily rising, quickly becoming as hot as a furnace. Chu Dingjiang’s breathing became heavy, and his lower body quietly rose again. An Jiu felt parched and got up to pour two glasses of cold water. “Chu Dingjiang, Mo Sigui told me you practice the ‘Virgin Boy’s fighting skills.'” An Jiu sipped water, her slightly narrowed eyes reflecting the firelight. They were glistening, as if about to overflow with moisture. “Mmm.” Chu Dingjiang’s voice was low and husky, making one’s eardrums itch, an itch that went straight to the heart. “What happens if you have relations with a woman?” An Jiu asked. If you had relations with a woman, you would never reach the peak. When Chu Dingjiang chose to practice this martial art, he knew it would be torture. If he did not understand matters of the heart, it would not be so bad, but he not only understood; he had even tried it. Fortunately, he had never been very interested in it. Plus, he had strong self-control and knew how to deliberately avoid women, so he had never made a mistake. The reason he chose to practice this martial art was that it was the most powerful and easiest to level up among all martial arts. It did not require high innate conditions; all that was needed was a strong physique and abundant masculinity. The pinnacle of martial arts was a tremendous temptation for most men, but Chu Dingjiang did not take it to heart. “This skill is extremely fierce. It is easy to reach a certain level, but reaching the peak comes with enormous risks. One wrong move and you will explode and die.” Chu Dingjiang possessed a superior physique and excellent comprehension and had also absorbed the internal energy of another master. His martial arts were progressing rapidly, and he felt he was approaching a critical point. What kind of critical point it was was hard to say. It could be a breakthrough to the first rank of the Transcendent Realm, or it could be a sign of his physical limits. Chu Dingjiang did not say these things, only that “I chose to practice this martial art back then because I entered the Konghe Army alone. The road ahead was unpredictable, and I needed to quickly gain the ability to protect myself. My ambition was not in this.” An Jiu turned to look at him. Their eyes met, their faces were so close, their breaths could be heard, and for a moment, nothing happened; time seemed to stand still. After an unknown amount of time, An Jiu suddenly leaned in, her lips landing on his. Chu Dingjiang’s breath hitched. He raised his hand and pressed the back of her head, responding with a torrent of kisses. Her body, encased in the blankets, was burning hot. Chu Dingjiang felt a burning, throbbing pain in his lower body, desire clamoring like a caged beast about to break free, repeatedly assaulting his self-control. An Jiu reached out and wrapped her arms around his neck, where veins bulged, pressing her body against his. The blankets slipped to the floor. Chu Dingjiang’s strong arm gripped her slender waist. He abruptly stood up and strode towards the bed. An Jiu had not felt anything when she initiated the encounter, but now her heart felt like it was going to jump out of her chest. An unprecedented stimulation, yet the feeling was undeniably intense. Chu Dingjiang’s kisses and caresses were rough, and An Jiu, infected by his passion, responded with equal roughness. If what was once a tiny flame had now ignited into a raging fire. However, Chu Dingjiang’s movements gradually slowed and softened, his rough fingers gliding over An Jiu’s silky skin, making her shiver with ticklishness. This was a completely different feeling from before. The previous intensity had released her inner desire, but now it was only reigniting it. An Jiu gripped Chu Dingjiang’s broad shoulders tightly, feeling in her half-dazed state that a tremendous explosive force seemed to be suppressed within him. Large drops of sweat fell on her face, tickling her, but he continued to tease her at a leisurely pace. An Jiu’s legs moved slightly, touching that burning hot thing. “Do not move!” Chu Dingjiang’s voice was low, but his tone was almost a roar. An Jiu sensed his discomfort and, unusually obedient, lay upright, her wet eyes fixed on him. Chu Dingjiang gazed into her eyes, his heart stirred with passion, and he could no longer resist. He sighed, avoiding her gaze, and lowered his head to gently kiss her earlobe, moving down to her neck and chest. “Chu Dingjiang…” An Jiu felt something was off, and her trembling voice startled even herself. “Mmm.” Chu Dingjiang gently stroked her hair with his large hand, soothingly saying, “Do not be afraid, do not be afraid…” A light kiss landed on her stomach, and she could not help but tremble, not even noticing the soft moans escaping her lips, like kitten paws gently scratching at Chu Dingjiang’s heart. The bed was in disarray, clothes scattered, and the flickering firelight enveloped the two of them. “Ah Jiu, I do not want this to be just a fleeting affair,” Chu Dingjiang softly murmured. Ah Jiu, I cannot promise you wealth and glory; I cannot promise you a lifetime of peace; I cannot promise you a beautiful world, but I wish to have only you in this life. Just the two of us; if we cannot grow old together, then we will be together until death.

chapters.title: The Uncle’s Downhill Path
chapters.content: Despite Chu Dingjiang’s extremely gentle movements, An Jiu still felt a tearing pain. This feeling was more unbearable than ever before because it was not just physical pain but also a strange psychological sensation that made the whole process long and agonizing. An Jiu opened her mouth and bit Chu Dingjiang’s shoulder. Chu Dingjiang’s attention was entirely elsewhere, and he did not feel a trace of pain. When the two were finally intimately connected, Chu Dingjiang felt as if he had just emerged from water. All his restraint was focused on the process, so the first time ended quickly, but a second round soon followed. An Jiu went from being the active one to being passive and then gradually became active again; her passionate abandon amazed and satisfied Chu Dingjiang. A night of fiery passion. The next day, the snow stopped. Outside, the sky was hazy. Chu Dingjiang opened his eyes, heard the even, long breaths beside him, and could not help but smile slightly, pulling the person in his arms even tighter. An Jiu opened one eye, saw Chu Dingjiang’s silhouette, then closed it again, suddenly noticing that Chu Dingjiang’s manhood was rapidly growing. She immediately opened her eyes. “I want to see!” This surprised An Jiu greatly. Although she understood matters between men and women, this was the first time she had witnessed it firsthand. She was very interested and had forced Chu Dingjiang to “perform” for her several times last night. “I will not watch, or do not blame me for being ungentlemanly,” Chu Dingjiang said sternly. But this tactic was completely ineffective on An Jiu; she buried her face in the covers. Chu Dingjiang, helpless, could only forcefully pull her out. “I have something to ask you.” “Speak.” An Jiu stopped speaking. “You are clearly a first-timer. Yet you act so skillfully. You must have secretly read quite a few erotic books before?” Chu Dingjiang teased her. The so-called erotic books, of course, referred to… erotic novels. “No,” An Jiu said, proudly raising her chin. “It’s animal instinct. It relies on basic talent.” An Jiu had long forgotten where she learned this kind of knowledge, but she had not deliberately looked up any information. Besides, she was not subject to many constraints, and even though her movements were clumsy, her lack of awkwardness made her seem knowledgeable. This proved that sometimes understanding was one thing, but the state of mind was crucial. As she spoke, An Jiu suddenly remembered something. “You were so fast the first few times that I could not even tell the speed. Clearly, it is a congenital deficiency. You will not kill me to cover it up, will you?” Probably only she in the whole world could make such a joke! Chu Dingjiang thought helplessly. After confirming that he was alright, Chu Dingjiang stopped caring about these unimportant jokes and even smiled, saying, “Then please help me a lot in the future.” An Jiu patted his shoulder and said seriously, “Do not worry, I will not tell anyone.” Reassured, Chu Dingjiang could not help but chuckle at her serious expression. He finally understood that what initially attracted him to An Jiu was her passionate and unrestrained nature, which resembled that of a woman from the Warring States period! Now, he could no longer clearly discern the reason; he only felt a sense of peace and contentment holding her. Only now did Chu Dingjiang feel truly alive. After last night, Chu Dingjiang could now easily control his desires. When he habitually circulated his internal energy, he discovered he had fallen from the peak of the second rank of the Transcendent Realm to the early stage of the second rank. He calmly accepted this reality, anticipating that he might continue to fall. Based on the current situation, almost all Transcendent Realm experts in the world were dead or wounded. It could be said that those who could fight him to a draw were extremely rare. In addition, he had secretly cultivated some power over the years, which was more than enough to protect himself. What concerned Chu Dingjiang was the Liao Kingdom’s obsession with the heart’s blood of the medicine person. He had secretly dealt with many ghost figures, but these ghost figures seemed endless, appearing wave after wave. It was clear that the Liao Kingdom had mobilized almost all of its ghost figures to obtain the blood. “The Liao Kingdom’s ghost figures have recently appeared around Bianjing. Do not go out frequently recently,” Chu Dingjiang advised. An Jiu listened to his strong, steady heartbeat and simply nodded. Chu Dingjiang, lost in thought, reached out and gently stroked her hair. Silence fell for them, but both enjoyed the quiet tranquility. In this era, marriage was the most important event in a woman’s life, akin to a second reincarnation. Chu Dingjiang felt guilty for not even giving An Jiu a proper wedding, so he decided to stay on the island with her, detached from worldly affairs. Outside, it was freezing cold, but inside, it was warm and cozy. Chu Dingjiang, dressed in a wide-sleeved robe, his hair half down, leaned against the couch reading, his carefree demeanor clashing with the restrained decor around him. An Jiu, meanwhile, sat cross-legged to one side, meticulously repairing her collection of small toys, even more engrossed than Chu Dingjiang himself. “Playing with things is a waste of time.” Chu Dingjiang put down his book. “If you have free time, practice your skills or read books. Is that not more useful than playing these games?” An Jiu casually hummed in agreement, not even looking up. Chu Dingjiang lightly tapped her head with the scroll. “Look up.” An Jiu frowned, staring at him with a bitter and resentful expression. “It’s not that I do not want you to play, but with a formidable enemy at hand, can you not be a little more careful about your life?” Chu Dingjiang casually grabbed a cloth bag and stuffed his things inside. “Go practice your skills.” “I’ve already practiced for four hours,” An Jiu said unhappily. “How many hours did you practice before?” Chu Dingjiang asked. “How long ago?” “In your past life.” “That’s about seven or eight hours.” “What was the last thing that happened to you in your past life?” Chu Dingjiang asked. An Jiu was reluctant to speak, but still admitted, “I got my head blown off.” Chu Dingjiang quickly understood what “head blown off” meant. “See? This is what happens when you are not skilled enough. You used to spend seven or eight hours, and this happened, and now you dare to spend only four?” “Tch,” An Jiu scoffed without hesitation. “The pot calling the kettle black. Did you not always try to outsmart others? At least I could make up for it with hard work, but your intelligence is what it is. You lost at the starting line, and with age, everything declines. Struggling is useless. I am going to practice! I advise you not to waste your time.” “You little brat!” Chu Dingjiang flashed, his robes fluttering, appearing opposite her in an instant. An Jiu naturally would not surrender. The two started fighting in the room. Bang! Bang! Bang! “Fourteenth! Fourteenth!” A girl’s clear voice interrupted their struggle. An Jiu stopped fighting, disheveled, and went to open the door. Lou Xiaowu burst in, grinning. “I heard you are back! Come to my place; I finally finished making that pistol you mentioned!” As she spoke, she grabbed An Jiu’s hand and pulled her outside, completely unaware that someone else was still inside. A year had passed, and Lou Xiaowu had grown taller and more beautiful. Only her large, almond-shaped eyes remained unchanged. Her lively, chattering manner made it seem as if they had only been apart for two or three days.

chapters.title: Senior
chapters.content: “Shall we go take a look together?” An Jiu turned to Chu Dingjiang and asked. Lou Xiaowu then noticed a handsome man sitting opposite her and greeted him shyly, “Senior, I am from the Lou family, my name is Xiaowu.” Chu Dingjiang nodded slightly. Most of the men Lou Xiaowu knew were refined and elegant. Seeing such a rugged man, she could not help but feel a little nervous. She leaned closer to An Jiu and whispered, “I did not expect your father to be so young.” An Jiu sensed that Chu Dingjiang’s mood immediately soured. Although the Mei and Lou families had intermarried in the past, they had not had any contact for many years. Lou Xiaowu did not know much about the Mei family and did not know that Mei Jiu’s father had passed away more than ten years ago. “Senior, would you like to go take a look together?” An Jiu asked, a smile playing on her lips. Chu Dingjiang stood up and calmly said, “Let’s go.” Lou Xiaowu looked up at Chu Dingjiang and exclaimed, “Senior, you are so tall!” Then she turned to An Jiu and said, “Fourteen, you are nothing like your parents! I am almost taller than you!” An Jiu did not explain for Chu Dingjiang and pulled Lou Xiaowu out the door. Lou Xiaowu chattered incessantly about the pistol, completely ignoring the displeased look on the face of the great man behind them. Soon, the three arrived at a dilapidated dwelling. An Jiu looked around and found that not only was the house in ruins, but the surrounding area within ten feet was completely barren, with only some scorched tree trunks remaining. Lou Xiaowu led An Jiu into the last remaining stone house and warmly greeted them, “Please sit wherever you like!” The tables and chairs were covered in a thick layer of dust, and the air was thick with the smell of sulfur and gunpowder. A corner was piled with scraps of iron, and Lou Xiaowu quickly found some parts and assembled them into a gun about ten feet long. “This one’s a bit bigger than you said, but it is the best I’ve gotten after repeated adjustments,” Lou Xiaowu said with a hint of regret but quickly became excited again. “Let’s try it outside.” The light inside suddenly dimmed. The two looked up simultaneously and saw Chu Dingjiang enter, his tall frame almost completely blocking the small doorway. “Senior…” Lou Xiaowu wanted to ask him not to block her way, but seeing the light shining in from behind him, making his face appear gloomy, she shrank back and nudged An Jiu with her elbow. “Senior, please do not block the way,” An Jiu said for her. Chu Dingjiang gave An Jiu a deep look and stepped aside. The two went outside and stood in the open space by the door to test the pistol. Chu Dingjiang leaned against the doorframe with his arms crossed, looking at An Jiu’s profile. He had felt a slight displeasure earlier because An Jiu seemed unwilling to admit what had happened that night, and in the days they had spent together, she had not shown any shyness or anything unusual, leaving him unable to fathom her thoughts. The blinding sunlight illuminated An Jiu’s focused and beautiful face. Chu Dingjiang suddenly smiled. He realized he was too caught up in the moment, easily swayed by emotions. In truth, An Jiu was always direct and sharp in her words and actions; there was nothing to overthink. Bang! A gunshot rang out, startling birds foraging in the snow. It seemed to cause no damage, but with Chu Dingjiang’s mental power, he could roughly sense the damage the bullet had inflicted on the trees a hundred paces away. An Jiu watched the wisp of smoke rising from the muzzle and slowly exhaled. “Not bad.” However, her expectations were still too high. The gun Lou Xiaowu had created had excellent range and accuracy, but it also had many flaws. For example, due to the materials of the bullets and the barrel, it generated a lot of heat during firing, meaning the gun could not be used for rapid, continuous firing; otherwise, the gun might explode. But for the Song Dynasty, this pistol was already very advanced. “How much does a pistol cost?” Chu Dingjiang suddenly asked. “This…” Lou Xiaowu scratched her head. “I do not know, you will have to ask Sister Zhu.” All the materials were provided by Zhu Pianxian; Lou Xiaowu never questioned them. An Jiu asked, “You want to use it in the army?” Chu Dingjiang shook his head. “However, I think General Ling would be very interested in it.” Ling Ziyue was so close to Bianjing, yet it felt like an eternity. Confined to the island, all his pain was magnified, eroding his will day after day. He needed to find something to keep him busy, to forget his feelings. “Let’s have a contest?” An Jiu suggested. “What kind of contest?” Lou Xiaowu asked. An Jiu brandished the gun in her hand; it still had three bullets left. One for each of them to see who could shoot down more birds. Lou Xiaowu could make guns, but she was not necessarily a skilled gunslinger. Judging from her several tests, even ten bullets would not be enough to hit a single bird. “Alright!” Chu Dingjiang walked over. “I need to prepare first.” An Jiu shoved the gun into his hand, turned, and darted into the house. Lou Xiaowu, not daring to face Chu Dingjiang alone, quickly followed. “Fourteenth, wait for me!” The two fiddled around inside for a while before emerging. Chu Dingjiang took out the bullets, examined them, and then put them back in. At this moment, the startled birds landed in twos and threes on the nearby snow. “When do we start?” Chu Dingjiang was quite confident in his aim. “When all the birds gather,” An Jiu’s eyes gleamed, as if a plate of roasted birds was already laid out before her.

chapters.title: Sparrows
chapters.content: An Jiu and Lou Xiaowu each held a pistol. After splitting the three bullets in their magazines, the three stood quietly in the snow, waiting for the startled birds to return. Sheng Changying, who was gathering firewood in the woods, peeked out but did not disturb them. “Let’s scatter some millet,” Chu Dingjiang suggested. Lou Xiaowu and An Jiu nodded repeatedly, but neither moved. Chu Dingjiang reluctantly went back to the kitchen, grabbed two handfuls of millet, and scattered them on the snow. With food, more and more birds gathered. When there were about forty or fifty, An Jiu whispered, “Let’s begin.” It was Chu Dingjiang’s first time using a pistol, and he did not know the proper way to hold it, but he held the gun with one hand, his posture as upright as a pine tree, his movements casual yet focused—truly dashing. Although Lou Xiaowu had experimented countless times, her accuracy was still unsatisfactory. She had even thought her gun was not precise enough, but after watching An Jiu shoot, she was relieved; thankfully, the problem was with her, not the gun. Birds would definitely be startled by the gunshot, so the first person to fire had a significant advantage. “I will count to three, and we’ll fire together,” An Jiu said. The other two agreed. “One.” “Two.” “Three.” Boom! All sounds were drowned out by a deafening explosion. A crater was blasted out ten feet ahead. Lou Xiaowu glared at An Jiu and yelled, “Fourteenth, you are so mean! When did you secretly take that thunderclap grenade?!” This thing looked like a hand grenade. An Jiu had only glanced at it in the house and knew how to use it. She had grabbed one when she went back to get the gun. Her idea was simple: a hand grenade would surely kill more birds… Maybe enough for a game. She chose to detonate it about six or seven feet to the left of where the birds were gathered. Many birds were either killed by the lingering force of the sound or stunned by the noise, scattering across the ground. An Jiu quickly gathered a pile and brought them back. She held them out to Chu Dingjiang, saying, “We will eat this for lunch.” “Alright.” Chu Dingjiang swept the birds into his sleeve. “Cooking is easy, but someone’s come looking for trouble. You’d better think carefully before you act.” An Jiu slowly released her mental energy, sensing someone rushing towards her. “It’s Sister Zhu!” Lou Xiaowu happily greeted her. In the blink of an eye, Chu Dingjiang had vanished. Zhu Pianxian moved swiftly, appearing before Lou Xiaowu in an instant, and forcefully tapped her head. She said with exasperation, “You actually used a gun to shoot sparrows?” “Yes, but a gun is not as powerful as a thunderclap bomb; one shot and a whole bunch explodes!” Lou Xiaowu proudly raised her head. Zhu Pianxian clutched her chest, her face contorted with grief and indignation as she questioned the two. “Do you know how much these things cost? You actually used them to hunt sparrows! Do you even know how many sparrows a single bullet can buy?” An Jiu and Lou Xiaowu looked utterly bewildered. “What a spendthrift! What a spendthrift!” Zhu Pianxian felt a sharp pain in her heart, liver, spleen, lungs, and kidneys. Because bullets were so small, the components inside must be extremely delicate, making the materials crucial. Following Lou Xiaowu’s instructions, Zhu Pianxian had a blacksmith repeatedly forge the bullets, a considerable effort that cost eight or nine thousand taels of silver in total! Eight or nine thousand was nothing to Zhu Pianxian; what pained her was spending eight or nine thousand taels on sparrows! Lou Xiaowu cautiously asked, “That sounds very expensive?” “Expensive!” Zhu Pianxian gritted her teeth. “Extremely expensive!” Lou Xiaowu glanced at the instigator, then chivalrously took the blame for her. “How about I make some small things to sell…” Zhu Pianxian’s breath hitched, then she forced a smile, her heart pounding with excitement. She was about to nod, feigning reluctance, when An Jiu said, “I did it, it has nothing to do with her.” Damn it! Zhu Pianxian could not help but curse inwardly. Lou Xiaowu looked at An Jiu with teary eyes, her face saying, “You are such a good person.” “Name a number; I will go earn it for you,” An Jiu said. “Um…” Zhu Pianxian’s mind raced, then she slowly held up a hand. “Fifty thousand taels.” “Alright.” An Jiu was not familiar with the prices in the Song Dynasty, but she remembered that research was incredibly expensive, often costing tens of millions. Fifty thousand taels did not seem like much. Zhu Pianxian could not help but be overjoyed. These two idiots really did not know the market! And An Jiu seemed completely unaware that a large portion of Chu Dingjiang’s assets were now under her name. In less than two years, Zhu Pianxian had increased Chu Dingjiang’s original wealth more than tenfold, reaching a total of 300,000 taels of silver. While this amount was not much in Bianjing, a city teeming with wealthy merchants, her speed of earning money was among the best in the land. An Jiu had so much money, all earned by Zhu Pianxian herself. Scamming 50,000 taels from her offered no sense of accomplishment; besides, it was better to learn how to fish than to catch fish. Zhu Pianxian loved money, but she loved the enjoyment of making it even more. While swindling 50,000 taels from An Jiu was certainly fun, she was still preoccupied with finding an opportunity to talk to Lou Xiaowu and have her make something to sell. At lunch. A large bowl of roasted sparrows appeared on the table. The sparrows, plucked and gutted, were stuffed with seasonings and wrapped in yellow mud and straw. About the size of a goose egg, each one, when peeled open, instantly filled the entire room with aroma. Except for Mei Yanran, who remained somewhat composed, everyone else devoured the food. Chu Dingjiang calmly peeled the mud off the sparrows, but instead of eating any, he neatly arranged them in An Jiu’s bowl. This gesture saddened Lou Xiaowu, who thought with envy, “If only my father were still alive.” After the meal, everyone returned to their rooms to rest, while Chu Dingjiang went to the ferry alone. The Dream Flowers bloomed profusely and alluringly in the snow, a thick fog shrouding the sea of ​​flowers. Chu Dingjiang casually broke off an inconspicuous withered branch from the nearby herb garden. As he carried the branch through the Dream Flowers, the fog seemed to melt away, gently receding a foot. At the ferry, Chu Dingjiang found a carrier pigeon, bent down, took a note from the letterbox on its leg, read it, and threw it into the river. He then carried the pigeon back to An Jiu’s room. An Jiu was wiping the Dragon-Subduing Bow when she looked up at him. “Where did these pigeons come from?” Chu Dingjiang sat down, placed the pigeons on the small table, and after a moment of silence, said, “I have to leave for a few days.” An Jiu paused. “What happened?” “The Emperor is seriously ill, and the Crown Prince is overseeing the state,” Chu Dingjiang said succinctly. The Crown Prince had long considered the Second Prince a thorn in his side. With the Emperor’s condition uncertain, although he dared not immediately attack the Second Prince, he would inevitably seize the opportunity to eliminate his rivals. Seeing her silence, Chu Dingjiang said, “After I leave, you must practice your martial arts diligently. Do not just play around all the time. You should spend your time reading.” An Jiu frowned. “Why should I read?” Chu Dingjiang did not answer but only asked, “What are the words written on the plaque above the door?” “…” “Qingfeng Ningle.” Chu Dingjiang tapped the plaque a few times, then said seriously, “What if I write a letter and you cannot understand it?” “I recognize these words.” An Jiu indicated that it was not her problem at all. “How dare they hang it on the door with something written like that?”

chapters.title: Return
chapters.content: Although An Jiu stubbornly refused to admit it this time, she was clearly a little guilty. Chu Dingjiang did not expose her, only smiling as he reached out and embraced her. A single oil lamp cast a soft, warm glow, the room dimly lit, creating an exceptionally ambiguous atmosphere… The next day. Before dawn, Chu Dingjiang got up. An Jiu, still in bed, one smooth arm draped over the edge, opened her eyes slightly at the sound. In the dim light, Chu Dingjiang bent down and tucked her arm under the covers. He had just woken up, his voice slightly hoarse, a faint smile in his eyes. “Awake?” Chu Dingjiang was always gentle with An Jiu, but this was the first time she had truly felt his tenderness. So intoxicating. “I am leaving,” Chu Dingjiang said. An Jiu grabbed his fingers. Chu Dingjiang paused, his eyes questioning, then returned her hand and grasped hers. They held hands silently for a moment, then simultaneously released them. Chu Dingjiang lowered his head and gently kissed her cheek before turning to leave. The door opened and closed, a gust of cold wind blowing in, dispelling An Jiu’s last vestiges of sleepiness. She sat up, wrapped in the covers, suddenly finding the room unusually empty and silent. Given Chu Dingjiang’s cultivation level, when he did not deliberately exude murderous intent, his presence was less noticeable than that of ordinary people. He sat in the room reading or playing Weiqi, not interacting with her much. An Jiu had previously thought that his presence or absence made little difference, but she had not expected the difference to be so stark. It had taken her twenty years to get used to loneliness, while Chu Dingjiang had broken that habit in just ten days. An Jiu lay motionless on the covers, her heart churning with a mixture of anticipation and fear. In this intense struggle, she seemed to see a faint glimmer of light. It was hope. An Jiu seemed to understand her mother a little bit, why her father had done such cruel things to her, yet she had been able to tolerate it time and again. However, the more An Jiu understood, the more terrified she became. She feared she would fall into a man’s web like her mother and feared she would be nothing more than a sacrifice. As dawn broke, a strange song drifted from somewhere on the island. Sui Yuntong felt a chill run down his spine. The voice was all too familiar—it was Fourteenth Young Lady! “Come with me quickly,” Sui Yuntong said, knocking on Li Qingzhi’s door. “Something’s probably happened!” “You mean Fourteenth Young Lady?” Li Qingzhi yawned dismissively. “What could possibly happen to her on the island?” An Jiu had lost control once at the border. Li Qingzhi was recovering from his injuries then and had not personally experienced that horrific “disaster,” but Sui Yuntong knew all too well. “I am not afraid of her getting into trouble; I am afraid she will tear the island apart!” Sui Yuntong said and rushed off. An Jiu’s voice came from the woods next to Lou Xiaowu’s residence. If she were simply cutting down trees, that would be fine, but if she got something strange from Lou Xiaowu, she could easily sink the island. Seeing that Sui Yuntong was truly anxious, Li Qingzhi, without even bothering to put on his coat, strode after him. When Sui Yuntong reached the woods, An Jiu was still wailing, but before he could find anyone, the wailing stopped abruptly. He thought to himself, “Damn it, she’s deliberately hiding!” The others did not have Chu Dingjiang’s ability to find her with their mental powers. “Did you not find her?” Li Qingzhi rushed over. Sui Yuntong nodded, “She’s nearby, hiding from us.” Li Qingzhi knew An Jiu probably had some mental issues, so he said, “Should I go get the others to help search?” “Alright,” Sui Yuntong added, “let two people watch over Young Lady Lou first…” “Awooo!” Lou Xiaowu suddenly howled. “I will go check.” Li Qingzhi used his light-footed skill and rushed over. Upon hearing Lou Xiaowu’s alarming cry, Zhu Pianxian rushed over without even applying powder. “Xiaowu!” Zhu Pianxian had barely entered when Lou Xiaowu bumped into her. “What happened?” Lou Xiaowu took a few steps back, holding a gun and excitedly telling her, “This gun has been modified! The friction is significantly reduced, and the bullet’s velocity is increased, but the gun did not explode. It must have been modified by Fourteenth! She’s a genius, hahaha!” With that, she rushed out the door and ran towards An Jiu’s Qingfeng Ningle Residence. Without Chu Dingjiang, the anchor of stability, the island was in complete chaos. Meanwhile, the lake outside the island was calm, almost without a ripple. A slender man boarded a small boat with two enormous tigers. The boat was too small; the two tigers squeezed onto it, almost sinking it, but the small boat glided effortlessly across the lake. The man stood with his hands behind his back at the bow of the boat, gazing at a misty expanse on the lake. “Tsk tsk, the Dream Flower is truly beautiful; no wonder I planted it myself.” The man and two tigers quickly reached the ferry. Mo Sigui straightened his clothes, carefully examining the water, inwardly praising it. He then took out his folding fan and slowly made his way to his long-missed residence, happily imagining the joyful expressions on An Jiu and the others’ faces when they saw him. Upon arriving at his residence, he was astonished to find the courtyard completely empty. Mo Sigui walked around, muttering, “It’s still the firewood I chopped before leaving.”

chapters.title: Alone Again Naturally
chapters.content: Mo Sigui glanced at the excited Da Jiu. “Let’s go find her!” Da Jiu seemed to understand, its four plump paws flailing happily as it darted off, Mo Sigui and Xiao Yue close behind. When the man and the two tigers arrived in the forest, Sui Yuntong and the others were searching everywhere. Seeing Mo Sigui return, they were overjoyed. “Divine Physician Mo!” Mo Sigui was quite satisfied with his reaction, giving him a rare warm welcome: “Young Master Sui, it has been a long time.” Sui Yuntong was more skilled in martial arts than literature; addressing him as “Young Master” was not an exaggeration. “I do not deserve such praise,” Sui Yuntong said politely, then changed the subject. “Divine Physician, you are a lifesaver! We’ve searched everywhere for Fourteenth Young Lady without success; surely your tracking tigers can find her!” “Has she had another attack?” Mo Sigui asked. Sui Yuntong nodded. “This morning I heard her singing in the forest…” As they spoke, Da Jiu had already cleared away the pile of stones, revealing a stone door large enough for one person to enter. Li Qingzhi opened the stone door and peered inside. “It should be a wine cellar.” “Not fresh at all,” Mo Sigui scoffed. “You went into a wine cellar last time, too!” “Mo Sigui, tell them all to leave.” An Jiu’s voice came from below, sounding urgent. “I am afraid I might hurt someone.” “Let’s go, let’s go!” Mo Sigui planned to pull Da Jiu and Xiao Yue away with the others. “Mo Sigui, come down,” An Jiu said. Mo Sigui was somewhat smug, thinking that An Jiu, in her madness, was unrecognizable to even her own family, yet she kept him here, showing how important he was to her. “Fourteenth, what if you hurt Physician Mo?” Sui Yuntong knew An Jiu was still lucid now, but might be in a bad mood later. “I’ve rid the people of a scourge. I’ve finally done a good deed,” An Jiu said. Mo Sigui felt a little embarrassed and jumped into the wine cellar. “I am saving the world from suffering! Which eye of yours sees the harm?” he grumbled as he walked. He rushed through the narrow tunnel into the wine cellar. It was unusually cold inside, filled with the rich aroma of aged wine. The light was dim. Mo Sigui vaguely saw an oil lamp on the wall, so he fumbled for a tinderbox and lit it. The dim light slowly flickered to life. Mo Sigui turned around and saw dozens of large, dark wine jars piled against the wall. An Jiu was huddled in a corner, hugging a jar almost as big as herself, her face flushed and her eyes bloodshot. She looked utterly disheveled, causing Mo Sigui to swallow back his sarcastic remarks. “What’s wrong with you?” He knew it probably was not anything terrible. An Jiu was someone who could handle any situation; even the greatest difficulties could not drive her crazy unless something had touched a nerve, causing her heart to falter. An Jiu looked at him, her face full of distress. “Mo Sigui, I think I’ve fallen for a man.” “Huh? Which unlucky man?” Mo Sigui thought for a moment. “Is it Chu Dingjiang?” An Jiu nodded, impatiently pushing away Da Jiu, who was snuggling against her. “He deserves it,” Mo Sigui said. “What should we do?” An Jiu asked. “Whatever we can do, it is not a big deal. I’ve become quite indifferent to matters of the heart. I will give you some serious advice later,” Mo Sigui leaned closer. “How far have you two gotten?” An Jiu said. “We slept together.” “You moved so fast!” Mo Sigui suddenly felt a little hurt, thinking about how he and Lou Mingyue were childhood sweethearts, yet they had never even kissed. “People like you deserve to be troubled by love.” An Jiu took a big gulp of wine, and Da Jiu curiously licked the liquid spilling from the jar, tilting his head in a daze. “Oh, in a little while from now, If I’m not feeling any less sour, I promised myself, To treat myself, And visit a nearby tower, And climbing to the top, Will throw myself off…” An Jiu suddenly howled, startling everyone. She screamed in an unfamiliar language. Although Mo Sigui could not understand it, he was certain she was completely off-key; there could not be such an awful song. “In an effort to, Make it clear to whoever, What it’s like when you’re shattered, Left standing in the lurch, at a church…” “What are you even singing?” Mo Sigui could not help but interrupt her; it was just too awful. An Jiu howled, tears welling in her eyes, “In a little while, if I feel a little better, I promise myself to visit a nearby town, climb to the top, and then release myself, trying to show someone what it is like when someone breaks down…” “Is that what the song means?” Mo Sigui could not help but interrupt her again. An Jiu nodded. “You did not write this song yourself, did you? It sounds exactly like you,” Mo Sigui said. An Jiu sobbed, “You think so too? I feel like I am that mammoth, sob sob… a stupid mammoth…” She felt an increasing sense of resonance. “To think that only yesterday, I was cheerful, bright and gay, Looking forward to, Well, who wouldn’t do, The role I was about to play…” To think that only yesterday I was cheerful, bright and gay Looking forward to Well, who wouldn’t do The role I was about to play But as if to knock me down Reality came around And without so much As a mere touch Cut me into little pieces Leaving me to doubt Talk about God in His mercy Oh, if He really does exist Why did He desert me In my hour of need? I truly am indeed Alone again, naturally It seems to me that there are more hearts broken in the world That can’t be mended Left unattended What do we do? What do we do?
