Now looking back over the years And whatever else that appears I remember I cried When my father died Never wishing to hide the tears… An Jiu sniffled as she sang this, explaining to Mo Sigui, “I did not cry when my father died.” Mo Sigui had not understood a word she was singing and found her statement utterly abrupt. The rest of the lyrics were roughly, “After my father passed away, I stayed by my mother’s side, encouraging and comforting her until she passed away.” “Was that not a happy time? I wanted to comfort and encourage her, too,” An Jiu asked him. Mo Sigui frowned, enduring her breathtaking singing, enduring her occasional sudden pauses at the height of her voice, pausing to pour out her feelings, and finally could not resist taking out his pipe and lighting it. The wine cellar soon filled with smoke. This was a sleeping pill he had just acquired this year; it was potent. Sometimes, when he stayed overnight in a small village, he would smoke for half an hour, plunging the entire village into a deep sleep. An Jiu, who had been on edge, quickly relaxed under the influence of the sleeping pills and slowly fell asleep. Mo Sigui yawned, grabbed An Jiu by the collar, and dragged her out of the wine cellar. “What is love in this world that makes people willing to die for it?” Mo Sigui carried her back to Qingfeng Ningle, threw her onto the couch, and said with his hands on his hips, “If I had known Chu Dingjiang was not a good person, I could only have fooled a fool like you.” He assumed Chu Dingjiang had been unfaithful and abandoned An Jiu. “I will avenge you!” Mo Sigui said indignantly, but his eyelids grew heavier and heavier. “I’d better wake up first…” He staggered back to his room and fell asleep immediately. He slept soundly. When Mo Sigui woke up again, it was the middle of the night. He put on his clothes and went to the veranda. The chill was biting. He looked at the starry sky, took out his pipe, and lit it. But the more he smoked, the more awake he became. “Hmm, it has only been three months, and it is already not working…” Mo Sigui frowned and exhaled a string of smoke rings.  In case you are wondering about this song, it is this one. Such an oldies song hahaha! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gU3ubk8u7dA

chapters.title: Professional Finishing Touch
chapters.content: Three months seemed like a curse; each time the prescription was modified, it only lasted about three months, after which its effect on him diminished. Mo Sigui touched the jade pendant at his waist, sighing slightly. His insomnia seemed to be getting worse. After smoking a puff of medicinal smoke, he felt dazed and exhausted, yet his thoughts would not stop, even with his eyes closed. An Jiu, on the other hand, slept soundly until dawn, without even a dream. The next morning, before she even got out of bed, she found Mo Sigui standing in front of her door. Thinking something was wrong, she quickly dressed and went to open it. Mo Sigui turned around at the sound of her voice. “I have insomnia again.” “It’s obvious.” An Jiu looked at his thin, pale face with dark circles under his eyes. “Why?” “Probably because it has been a long time since anyone talked to me about personal matters.” Mo Sigui tapped his palm absently with his fan. “You just said you’d become indifferent to feelings,” An Jiu said. “Can you please not expose others so easily?” Mo Sigui frowned. An Jiu was silent for a few moments. “You miss Lou Mingyue?” This topic was clearly a bad one. Mo Sigui, like a cat whose tail had been stepped on, almost jumped up. “How could that be? I’ve always been so carefree; how could I be that kind of person?” Coming to talk to An Jiu was obviously a terrible decision. She never listened to people’s feelings and was always quick to expose them. “Is that not right? You called out Ningyu’s name in your dream yesterday, and when you went out for a smoke, you touched this…” An Jiu pointed to the jade pendant hanging at his waist. “Gathered, it becomes a pendant; separated, it becomes a ring.” This was the token of love between Qiu Ningyu and Mo Sigui, originally a jade pendant. When Qiu Ningyu “died,” Mo Sigui buried the other half in a cenotaph. Perhaps from that moment on, it was destined that they would never be together in this life. An Jiu, however, knew nothing of this, only noticing the crescent shape that seemed about to fall. She guessed it was related to Lou Mingyue, but guessing correctly was pure luck. Mo Sigui clutched the jade pendant tightly. “Let’s change the subject.” “What do you want to say?” An Jiu readily agreed. Mo Sigui’s expression relaxed slightly. “No need to say anything. Let’s go drink. I did not expect the Second Old Madam had stored so much wine for so long; we are lucky.” The two went to the wine cellar one after the other. Da Jiu and Xiao Yue were still fast asleep in the wine cellar. Mo Sigui picked out a jar and sat cross-legged on the open ground. An Jiu also casually grabbed a jar and took a sip. She sighed, “If Chu Dingjiang were here, that would be great.” Mo Sigui looked at her strangely. “Even you, a woman, can suffer from lovesickness; why does Mingyue not suffer from it?” An Jiu was lost in her own imagination, not considering the meaning behind his words at all. She clicked her tongue and said, “Then there would be so many snacks to go with the wine.” “Never mind what I said,” Mo Sigui said, feeling frustrated. An Jiu then said, “You ask why Lou Mingyue did not suffer from lovesickness? It is simple, she does not like you at all!” Mo Sigui clutched his chest, indignantly saying, “You really know how to stab someone in the back!” An Jiu looked at him and said, “Besides, even when you were still somewhat presentable, she did not even look at you, and now she’s even more…” Mo Sigui almost vomited blood. “You dare to add insult to injury! You cannot be satisfied until you see others riddled with wounds, can you? With your character, it would be an injustice if you did not go crazy.” Seeing that he was truly angry, An Jiu stopped talking. The two drank in silence for a long time. An Jiu then carefully added, “I always like to tell the truth.” What she meant was, “I was not tactful. Please forgive me.” Mo Sigui did not speak, drinking sip after sip. After a long while… She said, “I am just destined for this. So many people fawn over me, but when it comes to confiding in someone, I find myself instinctively drawn to you.” Because An Jiu was genuine and straightforward, one could see right through her, unlike others who hid countless schemes and hidden agendas. It was precisely because of this honesty that her words were often so inappropriate and unpleasant. Most of the time, the truth was not necessarily beautiful. “Unrequited love,” Mo Sigui sighed. “I wonder if it is because I cannot have her that I am always so preoccupied.” “If you get her, you will not be so preoccupied?” An Jiu asked. Mo Sigui wiped the wine from his lips. “Is that not how people are? When they do not have something, they crave it, feeling nothing in the world can compare. But once they get it, time wears it down, and it is nothing special.” An Jiu thought about his words carefully and found them very true. “When I first got a mission, I felt incredibly excited. Every day, even while eating, sleeping, and going to the bathroom, I was thinking about how to kill the target. But after actually completing it, I realized it was not really that interesting, and I forgot about it after a while.” Mo Sigui looked at her speechless. An Jiu humbly asked, “Is that not right? Then what counts as ‘getting’ something?” “Like you and Chu Dingjiang, you’ve both gotten something, right?” Mo Sigui could not resist trying to experience the feeling of stabbing someone in the back. But the person being “stabbed” seemed completely oblivious, even nodding in agreement. “So, does that mean we will find each other boring after a while?” “Men’s hearts usually change faster,” Mo Sigui said. An Jiu breathed a sigh of relief. “That’s good.” She was genuinely relieved, but a vague unease lingered in her heart, slowly turning into a sharp, needle-like pain. It was not particularly painful, but it made her heart tighten. Mo Sigui drank silently, not wanting to speak to her anymore. After spending the morning in the wine cellar, Sui Yuntong came to call them for lunch. Mo Sigui was sprawled out on a wine jar, asleep, and An Jiu was already slightly tipsy. An Jiu had not eaten breakfast and had drunk a lot of strong liquor, making her stomach burn. So she left the wine cellar. “It’s rare for Mo Sigui to fall asleep like this; do not wake him.” “Alright.” Sui Yuntong probably guessed that Mo Sigui had this “hidden ailment” and then asked An Jiu, “Are you alright?” “I am fine,” An Jiu replied. Mei Yanran was a good cook, and An Jiu loved her food. She used to think that children with mothers definitely had a better life. But today, facing a table full of food, the first thought that came to mind was that Chu Dingjiang’s cooking was still better. An Jiu stared blankly at her rice bowl, this being the second time she’d thought of him. Mei Yanran watched her for a long time, then could not help but ask softly, “What’s wrong?” “Why are you not eating?” Zhu Pianxian, noticing An Jiu’s absent-mindedness, casually placed a piece of dried bamboo shoot on her plate. “Eat quickly, eat your fill so you can go make money!” She could not stand seeing people idly daydreaming; it was such a waste of time. “Fourteenth misses her father,” Lou Xiaowu pouted. “I miss my father, too.” “Do not join in!” Zhu Pianxian knew Lou Xiaowu had never met her father. “Eat more rice, consider it feeding you for your father.” Mei Yanran glanced at An Jiu, then lowered her head and ate silently. An Jiu said to Sheng Changying, “I will come see you later.” She quickly shoveled down a bowl of rice, put down her chopsticks, and got up to leave. “Hey! What do you want with him?” Zhu Pianxian could not help but ask.

chapters.title: Bounty List
chapters.content: An Jiu did not answer. After dinner, Zhu Pianxian and Mei Yanran cleared the table. Sheng Changying found an opportunity to say to Zhu Pianxian, “I am going to take a look.” Zhu Pianxian smiled slightly, “Go quickly, it must be something important.” As she spoke, she saw him out. Zhu Pianxian retreated into the house, peeking out from behind the door. “He really left, huh? Cannot even understand polite words! Idiot!” “Go if you want; I will clean up here,” Mei Yanran said. Zhu Pianxian then remembered there was someone else in the house. She quickly stood up straight, straightened her clothes, and coughed twice. “Aunt Mei…” “Go ahead,” Mei Yanran smiled. Zhu Pianxian hesitated for a moment, then dashed out. Over there, An Jiu was already waiting in front of Sheng Changying’s usual small study. “Headmaster Sheng.” Although Sheng Changying was no longer the master treasurer, An Jiu still habitually used this title. Sheng Changying nodded in greeting. “What brings you here?” Looking at his serious expression, An Jiu could not help but recall the shy way she had glimpsed him in front of Zhu Pianxian that day, and a smile unconsciously appeared on her face. Sheng Changying was slightly surprised. “I wanted to ask where I can find work, like at Piaomiao Mountain Mansion.” An Jiu needed to earn money, but besides killing, she had virtually no other skills, so to earn the full 50,000 taels, she would have to return to her profession. Sheng Changying pondered for a moment. “I remember there’s a bounty board in the west of Bianjing City. It is usually used by the government to issue orders, but every night it becomes a place for bounty hunters to find work. It is tacitly approved by the court, and sometimes the court even assigns some work there.” An Jiu nodded. “How exactly does it work?” “Every night before midnight, midnight is the time to grab the list. Everyone chooses the list they are interested in, and when the night watchman strikes midnight, they can try to grab it based on their skills. After getting the list, wait in front of it, and someone will come to meet you.” Sheng Changying guessed her purpose and said, “I will draw the location of the list for you.” “Thank you,” An Jiu said. The two entered the house one after the other. There was nowhere to hide in front of the house, so Zhu Pianxian had to hide behind a rockery about twenty zhang away. The distance was too great to hear their conversation, but she could see An Jiu smiling faintly through the cracks, while Zhu Pianxian pressed herself against the rockery, so impatient she was almost scratching the stone raw. As soon as she saw the two enter the house, she dashed to the window. An Jiu had already noticed Zhu Pianxian’s presence. Seeing her so anxious, she could not help but tease her. “Headmaster Sheng, I’ve noticed you are getting more and more handsome.” This was true. Sheng Changying used to look very haggard, always appearing as if he had not slept at all. Now, while he was not necessarily more energetic, he looked much healthier and naturally more handsome, especially his long, narrow, fox-like eyes. His flirtatious demeanor was different from Mo Sigui’s. It seemed as if he always harbored a mischievous glint in his eye, and his languid pose was quite alluring. Anyone who did not know Sheng Changying would definitely think he was a womanizer and a wicked man. Sheng Changying did not remember An Jiu being the type to say such things. However, he quickly understood, glancing out the window. His voice carried a hint of amusement. “You flatter me.” This time, it was An Jiu’s turn to be surprised. She had always thought Sheng Changying was an honest and simple person. Truly… appearances mattered! Since he was willing to cooperate, that was even better. An Jiu was not stupid; she knew Zhu Pianxian was used to swindling money. The things she’d used might not even be worth a third of fifty thousand taels. She just did not like haggling. She would not let go of an opportunity for revenge. “Let’s go out for dinner sometime,” An Jiu said. “Dinner?” Sheng Changying lowered his head to draw, his dark hair falling over his shoulders, his eyes slightly curved. “Alright.” An Jiu’s ears twitched slightly, hearing the faint scratching sound outside, and she added fuel to the fire: “Just the two of us, how about tonight?” “There’s a good roast goose place on Pan Tower Street,” Sheng Changying said, essentially agreeing. Zhu Pianxian finally could not resist coming in, a flawless smile on her face. “What roast goose are you talking about?” “Nothing,” An Jiu said before Sheng Changying could answer. Zhu Pianxian looked at Sheng Changying with a resentful expression. “I suddenly have a craving for roast goose from Pan Tower Street for dinner tonight!” Sheng Changying, who could still muster a bit of mischief behind her back, seemed to have lost all his sense of reason the moment he saw Zhu Pianxian. He quickly said, “Then I will go with you tonight. If you are too tired, just wait for me to bring it back.” An Jiu silently rolled her eyes. She really did not know if it was genuine or just an act! “I have not been out in a long time either; let’s go together.” Zhu Pianxian was not about to give anyone else a chance. Sheng Changying readily agreed. “Is the drawing finished?” An Jiu was too lazy to play along with the two of them. She had originally intended to tease Zhu Pianxian, but unexpectedly, she had become the catalyst for their clingy relationship. She strongly suspected that Sheng Changying’s intentions were exactly that from the beginning. Sure enough, they were in cahoots, a den of snakes! “It’s finished.” Sheng Changying handed the drawing to An Jiu. Zhu Pianxian leaned forward. “What’s that drawing?” An Jiu casually folded the painting in half, turned to Sheng Changying, and said, “Thanks, I owe you another favor.” “It was nothing, no need to mention it,” Sheng Changying said. An Jiu pocketed the drawing and walked out. After taking a few steps, she suddenly remembered seeing Zhu Pianxian’s expression change several times before she came out. A smile played on her lips, and she quietly returned, silently climbing onto the roof beam. Inside the room, Zhu Pianxian sobbed, her face hidden behind a handkerchief. “Have you grown tired of me?” “No, no,” Sheng Changying said, wiping away her tears with a tender voice. “Having Pianxian as my wife in this life, I will never betray you.” Zhu Pianxian blushed slightly and spat, “Who said I was going to marry you?” “Pianxian…” Sheng Changying grasped her hand and sighed, “If you do not marry me, I am afraid I will grow old alone.” “Nonsense,” Zhu Pianxian gently covered his mouth. An Jiu pouted, disgusted. She just could not understand. Was teasing really that fun? Would it not have been better to have everything go smoothly? Why did they have to create trouble, have a crying fit, and then have to be comforted? However, she could also see that in Sheng Changying and Zhu Pianxian’s relationship, Zhu Pianxian had initially taken the lead, but now the balance was more even. Should she stir up some trouble and tease Chu Dingjiang sometime? An Jiu’s heart skipped a beat. This was the third time she’d thought about him! Realizing this, she lost interest in watching others’ sweet nothings and quickly left, returning to her room to prepare the weapons she needed for the evening. She donned a tight-fitting outfit, packed her weapons and medicine, wrapped the Dragon-Subduing Bow in hemp cloth, and slung it over her shoulder. Her gear was complete. After dinner, she informed Mo Sigui and then boarded a boat to leave the island. Returning to her profession, An Jiu’s mood was quite different from before. She felt more concerned and more worried. Logically, this was not conducive to assassination, but she felt more relaxed than ever before.

chapters.title: Domineering Ranking Takeover
chapters.content: The Bounty List was once just a martial arts organization whose bounty hunters included many wanted criminals. However, due to the sudden rise of the Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, the Bounty List suffered a huge blow, and coupled with a government crackdown, it was once on the verge of extinction. Later, the government’s attention was diverted by the Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, allowing the Bounty List to survive. However, due to the severe damage it suffered and the lack of leadership, it had been practically extinct for many years. In fact, the Bounty List’s resurgence was a recent phenomenon, occurring only in the last year or two. Someone had been recruiting many martial arts assassins with large sums of money and issuing numerous high-bounty missions, gradually attracting the attention of more reclusive bounty hunters. Although Sheng Changying was no longer with the Konghe Institute, he understood the institute’s communication methods and could often intercept messages. Since he had nothing to do all day and enjoyed intercepting messages, he had not become oblivious to the news while living on the island; on the contrary, he was even more knowledgeable about martial arts news. An Jiu, holding the map given to her by Sheng Changying, found her destination without any difficulty. This place was a bustling market during the day, so the government always posted notices on the most conspicuous wall, a practice that had remained unchanged for over a decade. An Jiu, her face covered by a black cloth, hid in an alley. This street was not a night market; after dark, few pedestrians remained, and at night it became even quieter, save for the eerie sound of the wind whistling through the alleyways. Around midnight, a masked figure carrying a scroll of notices landed in front of the wall. An Jiu could sense the unusual activity around her without using her mental power. After the figure finished posting the notices and left, people began to appear one after another. An Jiu also left her hiding place. Although there were clearly thirty-odd people standing on the street, it was eerily quiet, as if no one was there at all. An ordinary person would surely think they had encountered a ghost. When they saw the black silk scroll pasted on the wall, some bounty hunters who were there for the first time that day exclaimed in surprise, “There’s a black notice!” Bounty lists were divided into three levels: white, red, and black. White lists were for private grudges and vendettas. Prices were generally under 20,000 taels of silver. Red lists may involve officials, wealthy merchants, or notorious bandits; they were highly dangerous and expensive, around 150,000 taels of silver. Black lists only listed prices, without details of the mission; anyone with the courage and ability could claim one, and the prices were in gold. Because the bounty list was only re-established less than two years ago, there were very few martial artists above the eighth rank among those vying for it, so even red lists were rarely posted, let alone black lists. “This black list has been posted for over two months. Someone took it down three days ago,” another person whispered. “It’s been posted again today; that person must be dead.” Among the bounty hunters, An Jiu appeared particularly thin and small, buried in the crowd, craning her neck to see the contents of the list. Five white silk scrolls and one black silk scroll hung on the wall, each with brief information about the target and the price. The prices ranged from two hundred taels to one hundred and fifty thousand taels, all for figures who wreaked havoc in the region. The prices on the white silk ranged from two hundred to ten thousand taels. The black silk listed one hundred and fifty thousand taels but did not specify the target. Sheng Changying had not elaborated on these details, but An Jiu, observing the reactions of the others, knew this black list was definitely an extremely dangerous mission. An Jiu did not want to risk her life. She was interested in the six thousand tael one, targeting a bandit leader with martial arts skills around the seventh level. She slowly released her mental energy. The surrounding bounty hunters were mostly at the sixth or seventh level of martial arts. There were many other ways to kill; it would not be a direct confrontation. They could all be competitors for this target. According to the rules, after reading the notice, everyone consciously retreated ten chi, waiting for the midnight watch. The moonlight was silvery, and the atmosphere was tense like a drawn bowstring in the deathly silence. Time passed slowly, and soon everyone caught a faint sound coming from afar. Bang! Bang! Bang! At the sound of the night watchman’s gong, the bounty hunters, who had been as still as statues, moved with lightning speed. An Jiu did not rush forward; she stood still, her eyes fixed on the notice she desired. Several others beside her remained motionless, just like her. Going forward now would inevitably mean fighting with the crowd, wasting time and energy. It was better to wait until the competition had subsided. The others were scrambling because this competition also had a time limit. The night watchman had traveled from two li away, stopping frequently along the way, which would take about the time it takes to brew two cups of tea. The bounty hunters’ movements could not be seen by the night watchman. In other words, obtaining the notice within two cups of tea was valid; after that, competing for it would be meaningless. Some of the bounty hunters who remained stationary were there to try their luck, while others were confident in their skills. An Jiu listened to the night watchman’s gong while watching the fight unfold before her. The fight quickly split into five groups. A burly man wearing a bamboo hat snatched the 6,000 taels of silver mission from the notice board, and six others were fighting him, also trying to take the notice. An Jiu observed that although they were fighting, none of them were going for the kill. She guessed this might be the rule for grabbing the notice. This discovery was very disadvantageous for her! Without the goal of killing her target, she did not know how to fight. While she was struggling with this, the people around her moved. One of them, a seventh-level expert, charged straight at the 6,000 taels of silver scroll, knocking down each opponent with a single move. His speed was astonishing, clearly that of a seasoned veteran. An Jiu noticed that the night watchman had already traveled more than halfway—in the blink of an eye! Forget it, thinking too much was useless! If she was not confident in her strength alone, then… An Jiu charged forward, and in the blink of an eye, the scroll was in the hands of the seventh-level expert. “A mere external cultivator like you wants to try grabbing the notice?” The man chuckled softly, clearly underestimating his opponent. An Jiu’s mental energy surged forward with her movements, instantly striking the man who had been immobilized, unable to retaliate! An Jiu snatched the notice, tucked it into her robes, and retreated more than ten steps in an instant. This time, her mental energy was highly concentrated, comparable to her usual powerful mental attacks, without dissipating outward. Therefore, to those unaware of the situation, the scene appeared as follows: a large, seventh-level martial artist had his notice snatched in one move and was simply surrendering it without moving. The seventh-level martial artist’s mind went blank for a few moments. When he recovered, his eyes widened in shock. Knowing his limitations, he did not try to snatch it again, his tone becoming extremely respectful: “I apologize for my earlier rudeness, senior.” He believed that someone with such terrifying mental energy was definitely not a young girl. An Jiu did not waste any more words and turned to leave. Some of the people she had previously knocked down, who were about to try to snatch it again, hesitated upon hearing these words. “Since you possess such skill, why not go for the Black List?” a seventh-level martial artist asked. The entire hall fell silent, all eyes turning to An Jiu. Just now, everyone was focused on vying for the rankings and had not noticed anything amiss. Only now, hearing this, did they realize something was wrong. The petite woman who had left alone was like air; if they had not seen her back, they would not have detected her presence at all. This seemed to be… a Transcendent Realm expert.

chapters.title: Do Not Force Me
chapters.content: An Jiu found a place to hide, waiting for the bounty hunters to come and fetch her. The night watchman’s footsteps grew closer; the outcome was decided, and the crowd ceased their entanglement, quietly retreating. Around midnight, a person wearing a silver mask arrived at the bottom of the list, glanced at the black list, took it down, and then waited with their hands behind their back. Seeing someone move forward, An Jiu knew it was the bounty hunters and followed. The person took all the lists, finally looking at An Jiu and saying, “With your strength, there are few rivals in the entire Song Dynasty. Why did you not take the black list?” It was that same question again. The other four also looked at her. After all, experts at the Transcendent Realm were extremely rare in this world; establishing a connection and receiving some guidance would undoubtedly be immensely beneficial. “Can I not take the white list?” An Jiu countered with a question. Her clear voice stunned everyone present and those hidden nearby. This was clearly an extremely young woman! The man in the silver mask composed himself. “Of course.” An Jiu fell silent. Since accepting the challenge was effective, what else was there to explain? The temperament of highly skilled individuals was often eccentric; this rule was not without reason. If someone dedicated their entire life’s energy to one thing, becoming indifferent to everything else, it was difficult for them to be normal. Knowing it was not wise to press further, the masked man said, “Please follow me.” The people who had accepted the challenge automatically stopped, waiting for An Jiu to leave first. In the martial world, strength was paramount, especially for someone as powerful as An Jiu, who was so far removed from their level! The group followed the masked man to a simple hut. The hut was very clean, with shelves on the walls displaying numerous scrolls. A long table stood in the center, with six chairs around it. “The information on today’s targets is all here. You may take as much as you like and leave before dawn.” The masked man paused. He continued, “The longest delivery period for the White List is four months. Before that, as long as you complete the task, you can bring the goods to the place listed and contact the person who posted the notice that day. The reward and interest will be paid.” His gaze shifted slightly. “If you have no further questions, I will take my leave.” He paused for a moment. Seeing everyone heading to the bookshelves on all sides, he immediately left. An Jiu found information about the target on the list on the bookshelf. This person was named Liu Chi, also known as Big Liu. It was said that he started his journey in the martial world at the age of thirteen, becoming an outer disciple of Wudang. Later, he was expelled from the sect for spying, and from then on, he ruled the mountain for twenty-nine years, now a local tyrant in the Funiu Mountain range. Big Liu’s stronghold was built on Taiping Peak in the Funiu Mountain range, called Weihu Village. It had about three hundred people, but most were novice martial artists, some even without any martial arts skills, only possessing brute force. A complete rabble. Taiping Peak? The document only listed the name of the mountain, but there was no map. The room was silent. The other four people, holding the documents, kept glancing at An Jiu’s movements. Seeing her focused, they could not help but wonder. For a master like her, taking the head of a mere small mountain stronghold leader should be a piece of cake. Why was she looking at it so carefully? An Jiu had always felt her strength was weak. All martial artists in the world possessed internal energy, while she didn’t. She could only compensate for her lack with hard work. Little did she know that with her current strength, she had already entered the ranks of top masters in the martial world. Unless attacked by three or four eighth or ninth-level martial artists, she would not be defeated unless something unexpected happened. After finishing reading all the documents, An Jiu quickly went out, circled the city twice, shook off a few pursuers, and then returned to Mei Mansion to prepare her travel supplies. During the trial at the Konghe Academy, she had been to Funiu Mountain once, so she was somewhat familiar with the route. However, the Funiu Mountain range was continuous; who knew where the small Taiping Peak was? Sheng Changying… An Jiu thought of him again. Everyone on the island was asleep, except for one person. An Jiu went to Sheng Changying’s place and saw someone strolling over, pipe in mouth, puffing out smoke. “Why are you running into a man’s room in the middle of the night instead of sleeping?” “Why are you blocking a woman’s way in the middle of the night?” An Jiu retorted. Mo Sigui exhaled a smoke ring, somewhat annoyed. “Do you think I want to stay up in the middle of the night and block the way?!” “Get out of the way; I have important business.” An Jiu walked past him. Mo Sigui flashed and reappeared in front of her. “Talk to me for a while.” An Jiu was somewhat surprised by his rapid progress, but considering his special physical constitution, she figured it was just a passing phase. “I am busy. Do you not have two tigers? Talk to them.” “One’s a complete idiot, and the other’s covered in pockmarks. I’ve had enough!” Mo Sigui had confided in those two tigers before, but all he ever got was Da Jiu’s blank, vacant face, and Xiao Yue completely ignoring him. Mo Sigui finished his cigarette and tapped it against a tree trunk beside him. “What brings you here? Want to have some fun? Want me to join you?” An Jiu looked at him and suddenly laughed. “Interesting, very interesting.” “You…do not do that; it is creepy,” Mo Sigui shuddered. “I think I need to think about this carefully.” “I am going to Funiu Mountain. There are plenty of precious herbs there,” An Jiu said. “What do you think?” Funiu Mountain had a suitable climate for growing various herbs. Mo Sigui had been there countless times and knew it very well. “What are you going to Funiu Mountain for?” “Do you know about Taiping Peak in Funiu Mountain?” An Jiu asked. Mo Sigui thought for a moment. “That’s the territory of Weihu Village?” An Jiu was overjoyed; it was like a godsend. But then she thought of Mei Jiu’s Gu poison. “Has the antidote for Mei Jiu been prepared?” “You think antidotes are as easy as homemade food? You cannot just prepare one whenever you want!” Mo Sigui scoffed. “How much longer?” She considered completing the task after Mo Sigui cured Mei Jiu’s poison. “It’s better not to mention it! Once it is brought up, I am wide awake again!” Mo Sigui sighed deeply. The sleeping pills, whose formula he’d modified three months ago, had no effect on him, and coupled with the constant struggle with the antidote, he was in a state of heightened excitement. If this continued, he’d collapse soon. An Jiu seemed oblivious to his complaints, pressing, “How much longer exactly?” “I do not know; it depends on my mood.” Mo Sigui turned and walked away. An Jiu followed. “What kind of mood will allow you to prepare it quickly?” “A good mood,” An Jiu thought seriously for a moment. “How about I sing you a song?” This was her most prized talent. Mo Sigui quickly said, “Please don’t! I am afraid I will commit suicide after listening to this.” An Jiu automatically assumed that the previous long songs were too sad. “Do not worry, I will sing something cheerful this time.” “Do not force me.” Mo Sigui looked at her with despair. “If you force me again, I will kill myself!”

chapters.title: Buy One Get One Free
chapters.content: An Jiu fell into deep thought, finding it hard to accept the fact. “Is my singing really that bad?” Mo Sigui nodded without hesitation. “Why do I think I am alright?” An Jiu asked. “Because you are not an ordinary person!” Mo Sigui thought to himself. “The antidote will not be ready until next month at the earliest, and I cannot guarantee it will cure the Gu.” Mo Sigui changed the subject. Every Gu poison was different. Based on the small amount of antidote Mei Jiu left behind, Mo Sigui first concocted the same medicine to guess what kind of Gu she had been infected with and then considered how to cure it. This antidote could only provide temporary relief; it could not completely determine the composition of the Gu poison. This was a huge challenge for any physician. An Jiu was silent for a moment. “I thought you were omnipotent in medicine.” Mo Sigui pursed his lips and turned his face away. “Provocation does not work on me.” Whether it worked or not could be seen from his reaction. An Jiu did not argue with him. “Even in the worst-case scenario, there’s an antidote to alleviate the poison in her body,” Mo Sigui said. Curing a poisonous curse was difficult, but Mo Sigui was confident he could concoct the same medicine as the original antidote. “Actually, curing a poisonous curse is very risky.” Mo Sigui found a stone bench, sat down, put another ball of medicine into his pipe, lit it with a tinderbox, took a few puffs, and continued, “If I make a mistake with one of the ingredients, it could cause Mei Jiu to be poisoned by the curse itself. My aunt’s curse was easily cured because you gave me the original Gu, allowing me to treat the symptoms correctly.” “Then Mei Jiu’s original Gu…” An Jiu thought that if the Emperor personally kept those original Gu, she should be able to obtain them. Mo Sigui saw her thoughts and exhaled a puff of smoke. “Do not think about it. You cannot get the original Gu. Someone with Mei Jiu’s special status might be given a specially made poison.” “Who made the Gu?” An Jiu asked. “The Emperor uses Gu to control his close guards. Is he not afraid the person wielding the Gu will betray him? I’ve heard the Emperor is a very suspicious man.” Mo Sigui’s expression hardened. “You mean…” The one who used Gu was the Emperor?! Mo Sigui thought carefully. “You are right. Asking Sheng Changying might yield some clues.” “I was just about to go find him, let’s go together,” An Jiu said. The two arrived at Sheng Changying’s door, and without knocking, they pried open the latch and silently stood before Sheng Changying’s bed. “Put out your cigarette,” An Jiu frowned, glancing at Mo Sigui. His cigarette was not ordinary. It was a powerful sleeping pill capable of incapacitating an entire village! “Who is it?” Sheng Changying suddenly sat up. Since he had more and more free time, his sleep quality had deteriorated significantly. Plus, growing up in a place like the Konghe Academy, he was quite alert even in his sleep. “It’s Mo Sigui and me,” An Jiu said. Sheng Changying’s mind cleared slightly. Recognizing An Jiu’s voice, he wiped away a bead of cold sweat, got out of bed, and put on his shoes. “You’ve come in the middle of the night; is there something important?” “Yes, we wanted to ask you. Does the Emperor know anything about Gu poison?” An Jiu said. Sheng Changying lit the oil lamp. Almost without recalling, “I do not know if the current Emperor knows Gu poison, but during Emperor Taizong’s reign, there was a favored concubine from Miao territory. I heard she was the daughter of a tribal chief. The tribe was called Ju, descendants of Chi You. Despite the changing dynasties, this tribe has always maintained its most primitive form. Their tribe understands witchcraft, and for generations, a high shaman has assisted the chief in protecting the tribe. Since ancient times, witchcraft and Gu poison have been inseparable. That Miao concubine was very likely proficient in Gu poison.” “So many years have passed; even if many Gu poisons were left behind, they would have been used up long ago. Presumably, Emperor Taizong learned the art of Gu poison and passed it on to his descendants,” Mo Sigui guessed. Sheng Changying said, “Whether Emperor Taizong knew witchcraft or not is unknown, but Emperor Zhenzong was the son of that Miao consort, so it is not surprising that he understood witchcraft.” “Eh? Emperor Zhenzong was not born to Lady Li?” Mo Sigui asked, slightly surprised. Sheng Changying said, “That Miao consort was Emperor Taizong’s Lady Li.” “So that’s how it is!” Mo Sigui sighed. The entire Song Dynasty believed that Lady Li was Han Chinese and of illustrious birth, but it turned out that Emperor Taizong had deceived everyone. The inside story was complicated, and they did not want to delve into it; they already knew what they needed to know. Now that it was confirmed, An Jiu said, “I will infiltrate the palace to find the original Gu.” Mo Sigui glanced at her, remaining silent for a long time. Seeing his reaction, An Jiu asked, “Do you have a problem with that?” “You almost died last time removing the Gu poison from your aunt. Are you going again?” Mo Sigui said. “Speaking of debts of life, have you not paid them off enough?” When he first met An Jiu, Mo Sigui thought she was a cold-blooded killer. Later, he discovered that beneath her cold exterior lay a childish and neurotic madwoman. And slowly, he actually saw what was hidden deep within her… her loyalty, passion, and kindness. An Jiu never thought about paying off debts; she simply did not want to stand idly by and watch their lives depend on it. If she did her best, she should not be consumed by regret, right? “If you are not absolutely certain, I will definitely go,” An Jiu said resolutely. Mo Sigui’s peach blossom eyes, hidden beneath dark circles, curved slightly. “If I ever find myself in dire straits, will you help me like this?” “I cannot help you then,” An Jiu said, glancing at his dark circles. “Your dire straits are only two: Lou Mingyue dies, or you yourself die from severe insomnia.” If Mo Sigui truly faced difficulties, she certainly would not stand idly by. However, Lou Mingyue was single-mindedly focused on revenge, sinking deeper and deeper into this swamp, much like herself in the past. The difference was that she had fallen into it for various reasons, while Lou Mingyue possessed a clear, even calm, mind. An Jiu did not want to expend any effort for such a person. “The Divine Physician’s spirits have indeed been low lately; he should take good care of himself,” Sheng Changying said, seeing a reflection of himself in Mo Sigui. So this was how listless he had always been! “Mm,” Mo Sigui responded listlessly, feeling that the medicinal cigarettes he’d smoked for most of the night were finally having some effect. His eyes drooping, he said, “I am going to sleep.” An Jiu followed him out. The two walked along the corridor. Mo Sigui, who had been silent the whole way, suddenly said at the fork in the road, “No need to retrieve the original Gu.” An Jiu paused slightly. “Why?” Mo Sigui yawned and said lazily, “I will definitely undo this Gu.” His nonchalant attitude did not reveal determination but rather an air of confidence. An Jiu believed him but could not help asking, “Are you not just testing how to undo the Gu?” “What do you take me for? I know how to repay kindness!” Mo Sigui said unhappily. “Mei Jiu almost died for me back then. Heaven has given me a chance to repay it; how could I treat it lightly?” “It’s not that I do not believe you,” An Jiu said, “If we follow your calculations, you owe Mei Jiu a life, and you also saved her mother; you’ve already repaid that life.” These were the words Mo Sigui had just said to An Jiu. Mo Sigui was momentarily speechless, then snorted, “I got a buy-one-get-one-free deal; what’s it to you!”

chapters.title: Longing and Illness
chapters.content: In the darkness before dawn. A slender figure darted into a small alley in Pan Tower Street and snapped her fingers twice. “You brought the things?” A deep male voice came from the shadows. “This subordinate has failed in her duty.” The speaker was a woman. “What? You’ve been here so long and have not even gotten a single memorial?” The man’s voice held displeasure, but he did not lash out at her. “With your abilities, why could you not get a memorial?” The woman said, “Hua Rongjian is not as incompetent as the rumors say. He trapped me in the mansion, and even tonight I only managed to escape with great difficulty.” She raised her head, the dim light illuminating half of her face, revealing slightly upturned phoenix eyes and red lips—it was Mei Ruyan. The man was silent for a few moments, then continued, “Once this is done, find a chance to leave the Hua family. The top officials will be targeting the Hua family soon, so they asked me to warn you.” “Understood.” Mei Ruyan’s expression was complex, but it quickly returned to normal. “I will do it as soon as possible.” “Mm,” The man responded. In the blink of an eye, only the sound of the wind and Mei Ruyan remained in the alley. She stood motionless for a long time, her back to the alley entrance, her mind flooded with memories and chaotic thoughts. Sometimes she doubted whether she had chosen the right path, whether continuing down this road was a path of light or one of no return. Until the very end, no one knew… Mei Ruyan sighed, her figure disappearing like a phantom into the alley, the mist instantly dissipating into the air. Dawn. A new day dawned in Mei Mansion. Everyone had their own tasks to attend to. Ling Ziyue and Lou Xiaowu were studying pistols and thunderclap grenades; Mei Yanran was busy preparing three meals a day; Sui Yuntong had cultivated six mu of land; Li Qingzhi was diligently studying military strategy; Mo Sigui was locked in his room concocting antidotes; Zhu Pianxian’s abacus clicked away; Sheng Changying was intently waiting at the ferry crossing, preparing to intercept the carrier pigeons from the Konghe Institute… Only An Jiu felt the days dragging on, bored out of her mind. The medicine pots on the stove in the pharmacy steamed, filling the room with a strong medicinal aroma. Mo Sigui squatted in front of the stone mortar, pounding medicine. After finishing her practice, she sat in Mo Sigui’s room, meticulously polishing the Dragon-Subduing Bow. “Sigh,” An Jiu sighed. She had always longed for a peaceful and leisurely life, but now that she was living it, she found it too bland. She and Chu Dingjiang were indeed the same kind of people, unable to bear a life as tranquil as still water… Huh? She was thinking of him again! An Jiu rubbed her forehead for a while, then asked Mo Sigui, “I am lovesick; do you have any medicine?” Mo Sigui did not even look up, replying, “If I had medicine, would I be in this state?” An Jiu pointed out calmly, “You finally admit your insomnia is because of Lou Mingyue.” “Hmm.” Mo Sigui was racking his brains for a prescription when he heard her words, and his thoughts suddenly stopped. He stared blankly for a long time before slowly frowning, then jumped up and grabbed An Jiu, saying irritably, “Get out, get out!” An Jiu was practically dragged out of the room. Looking at the closed door, An Jiu was silent for a moment. This time, she was truly bored! She wandered around but could not stop thinking about Chu Dingjiang! Watching Mei Yanran cook, she thought Chu Dingjiang’s cooking would be even better; seeing Sui Yuntong farming, she wondered what Chu Dingjiang’s farming would be like; seeing Li Qingzhi studying military strategy, she thought Chu Dingjiang would know the most about these things… This state continued until the third day. An Jiu was torn between enduring the hardship or going to find Chu Dingjiang when he unexpectedly returned. At that time, An Jiu was at the ferry crossing with Da Jiu and Xiao Yue, watching Sheng Changying intercept carrier pigeons. She sat on a bare tree branch, staring motionlessly at the sky. Da Jiu was even more focused than her, his mouth agape, drooling occasionally, while Xiao Yue lay on the ground with half-closed eyes, appearing detached from worldly affairs. Only when the sound of water came from the ferry crossing did An Jiu shift her gaze. Through the hazy mist, a familiar, tall figure slowly became clear. He was still wearing a black cloak, obscuring most of his face, revealing only his beard. In that instant, An Jiu felt everything stop. Chu Dingjiang saw a woman in a light blue jacket and skirt perched in a tree. Looking up at the sky, she resembled a bird perched on a withered branch. When she turned to look at him, her clear, bright eyes seemed to reflect his image. Chu Dingjiang walked to the tree, brushed off his hood, and looked up at the person he had been longing for, smiling. “Ah Jiu.” An Jiu grinned and jumped down from the branch, which was two zhang high. Chu Dingjiang reached out and caught her steadily. “What are you looking at?” Chu Dingjiang asked. “Watching Headmaster Sheng catch birds.” An Jiu looked up at him. “Did you come back for something?” Chu Dingjiang nodded. “Yes, there’s something very important that I have to do.” An Jiu ran through the thought many times in her mind. Perhaps he wanted Lou Xiaowu’s Thunderclap bombs? Or perhaps he wanted to recruit some strong men to serve the Second Prince? It seemed possible, yet also unlikely… “What is it?” she asked directly. Chu Dingjiang smiled and said, “To see you.” An Jiu froze, her thoughts interrupted, and it took her a long time to react. “You thought of me, too?”

chapters.title: Advisor
chapters.content: “Also?” Chu Dingjiang instantly grasped the key point. Just as An Jiu had never expected Chu Dingjiang to think of her, Chu Dingjiang had not dared to hope either, so An Jiu’s reaction was a pleasant surprise to him. “I…” An Jiu stopped mid-sentence. “What’s wrong?” Chu Dingjiang encouraged her with his eyes to continue. An Jiu, thinking about her changes in the past few days, felt uneasy and changed the subject. “I took on a job these past few days.” Chu Dingjiang was slightly disappointed but still followed her lead and asked, “What kind of job?” “There’s a bounty list in Bianjing. I took on a white one there. The target is a bandit leader, six thousand taels of silver,” An Jiu said. Chu Dingjiang had heard of bounty lists. White lists had the lowest danger level. Although An Jiu did not have internal energy, in the battle at Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, she could fight several eighth or ninth-level experts single-handedly without being at a disadvantage. Even taking on a red list would not be a big problem. He just did not understand, “Why did you suddenly think of taking up the bounty list?” “Last time I used a thunderbolt grenade to blow up birds, Zhu Pianxian said it was worth 50,000 taels of silver. I did not have any other way to make money, so I inquired about this list,” An Jiu said excitedly. “I am also free to do something, so killing bandits is like ridding the people of a scourge.” In the past, she killed people indiscriminately, some even high-ranking officials with considerable achievements. Her feelings now were completely different. “Since you like it, just do it. Prepare carefully beforehand, and do not underestimate them. There are countless examples of people who have failed miserably!” Chu Dingjiang said this, but in his heart, he was thinking that he had to have a serious “talk” with Zhu Pianxian later. “Hmm.” An Jiu nodded, then asked, “Have you met the Second Prince? How was it?” Unconsciously, she had gradually integrated into the Song Dynasty. Seeing the Emperor and Crown Prince’s private debauchery and licentiousness, she could not help but worry about the future of the country. It was not that she was patriotic but rather worried that without the foundation, the people would not survive. Having experienced localized wars and upheavals, she knew that regime change was no simple matter. “As expected. Given the current situation of the Song Dynasty, if he were to rule the country, he might do better than the Crown Prince. However, he is still lacking in refinement, and hastily inheriting the throne would be unwise.” Seeing her interest, Chu Dingjiang explained in detail, “His lack of favor from a young age, coupled with his mother’s influence, has made him strong-willed and resolute and quite shrewd but also overly ambitious.” “Overly ambitious?” An Jiu did not quite understand. “He’s too conceited, believing his talents far surpass his father and brothers. Furthermore, he has not faced significant setbacks in recent years, inevitably leading to underestimation of his opponents and a lack of patience.” Chu Dingjiang thought for a moment and said, “He’s still too young; his thinking is naive.” “Are you not being too demanding?” An Jiu felt that it was already remarkable for a teenager to have the maturity of someone in their twenties, but Chu Dingjiang seemed quite dissatisfied. “He’s destined to be Emperor, so naturally we cannot judge him by ordinary standards,” Chu Dingjiang said, squeezing her hand. “Besides, everything is urgent. Fortunately, the Crown Prince’s methods regarding Ling Ziyue have finally brought him to his senses.” The Crown Prince saw through the Second Prince’s attempt to save Ling Ziyue, so he feigned an attack, prematurely exposing everything he had planned. As a result, he not only failed to save Ling Ziyue but also suffered a loss of strength. Fortunately, Chu Dingjiang secretly helped erase all traces; otherwise, this move might have ruined him. “Are you now his advisor?” An Jiu asked.

chapters.title: Tracking
chapters.content: Chu Dingjiang shook his head slightly. “I observe that the Second Prince is stubborn. If I were to serve as his advisor, he might not be able to follow my every word. Therefore, I will remain hidden in the shadows, guiding him at crucial moments.” If he were to become the Second Prince’s subordinate, he would have to treat him with utmost respect in everything, never overstepping his bounds. If the Second Prince made a wrong decision and Chu Dingjiang could not effectively stop it, even with a thousand schemes, it would be difficult to guarantee a successful turnaround every time. In comparison, maintaining secrecy was far more advantageous. People were prone to doubt and fear of the unknown. Chu Dingjiang’s decision to rescue the Second Prince in his most perilous moment and then gradually build his standing in his heart was far more prudent than joining the Prince’s inner circle from the outset. An Jiu, unaware of his true intentions, said, “If you do this, would it not be even easier for him to discard you once he’s ascended the throne?” “You used the right words,” Chu Dingjiang chuckled. “It’s truly remarkable!” He paused, then said, “Do not worry, I have my own plans. If nothing unexpected happens, we can even go herding sheep together in the future.” An Jiu looked at his face, clearly very young, yet his eyes held a world-weary look, and her heart softened. “What can I do for you?” “Take good care of yourself,” Chu Dingjiang said. Chu Dingjiang had experienced the countless wars of the Warring States period, the gradual annexation and destruction, and the suffering of countless people ravaged by war. But he had never underestimated the internal power struggles within the imperial court; for a strategist, they could be even more dangerous than plotting against other nations. Even having lived two lives, he dared not say he would ultimately retire unscathed. “Ah Jiu, following me is destined to be fraught with danger…” An Jiu interrupted him, “Even without you, my life is not much better. You go ahead and do your work; I have things to do, too.” These words were blunt, but Chu Dingjiang was used to it and simply smiled, “As long as you live, that’s more important than anything else.” “That’s not necessarily true,” An Jiu said, looking at him. “You never promised me you would survive, and I cannot promise you either.” In the past, snipers comparable to An Jiu’s skill were extremely rare. She had long stood at the top, and even though she was wanted by various countries, she always believed she could survive. Yet, in the end, she still died in a sniping mission that was not particularly dangerous. The most unpredictable thing in life was death. Even those doing honest work could not guarantee they would not suddenly fall ill and die one day. Chu Dingjiang smiled helplessly, but instead of making a promise, he reached out and hugged her, sighing softly, “Ah Jiu, I missed you.” An Jiu’s lingering longing was instantly rekindled, yet for some reason, she could not express it as naturally as he did. Her lips parted slightly, then tightened again after a long pause. The two embraced under the tree for a long time before Chu Dingjiang finally released her, leading her to the small boat. “Look what I brought you.” Two baskets were placed on the boat, filled with a slaughtered suckling pig and chestnuts. Da Jiu had been squatting at the ferry landing, swallowing hard, its eyes fixed on the baskets. Seeing Chu Dingjiang and An Jiu approach, its tail swept across the ground, causing the Dream Flower petals it touched to release even more mist. Chu Dingjiang turned his head and saw An Jiu also intently staring at the suckling pig. He happily picked up the basket. “Let’s go; let’s roast some meat.” Ignored, Sheng Changying stood among the Dream Blossom flowers, holding a tree branch, his cheeks slightly flushed. Looking at the vast, misty lake, he thought to himself that Chu Dingjiang was indeed unrestrained, and An Jiu was no less so. The two of them could embrace so openly in broad daylight; it was truly…enviable. As night fell, the mist in the plum blossom garden grew even thicker. A man dressed in a wide blue robe stood on the lakeshore, gazing at the distant water. Behind him stood seven or eight black-clad men. These men were not burly giants but rather varied in height and build, seemingly of different shapes and sizes. However, the murderous aura they exuded was chilling; just standing there silently gave one a suffocating feeling of facing death. “Master Wei, what should we do?” one of the black-clad men broke the silence. After a long silence, Wei Yuzhi finally spoke, “Wait.” The man frowned. “Please enlighten me, My Lord.” “You are all masters among masters, but even if you all attacked together, I am afraid you could not withstand that person.” Wei Yuzhi’s eyes were dark, like a still, deep well. “Do you not know how much effort I expended to conceal your auras?” “Could it be a Transcendent Realm expert?” The man’s tone suddenly became serious. “Yes, now, apart from a eunuch in the palace, no one in the Great Song can rival him.” Wei Yuzhi’s hand, hidden in his sleeve, twitched slightly. “Unless Ghost Tigers and I fight to the death together.” If it were a Transcendent Realm expert, Wei Yuzhi would not be so alarmist. Ghost Tiger suppressed his impatience and said sincerely, “But the medicine person’s heart’s blood has been in someone else’s hands for quite some time. If we do not act quickly, I am afraid…” “I’ve already found a way to reveal the secret of the heart’s blood to the Emperor of the Great Song. To reclaim the blood this time, we still need his help!” Wei Yuzhi’s fingers paused in his sleeve, his hands clasped together, his eyes growing colder and darker. “I heard that the Transcendent Realm expert is also a high-ranking official in the Konghe Army.”

chapters.title: Love
chapters.content: “So what?” Ghost Tiger asked doubtfully. Even if they were high-ranking officials of the Konghe Army, what did that have to do with the Song Emperor knowing the miraculous uses of the heart’s blood? It was truly perplexing. Wei Yuzhi did not explain, but instead said, “These people are all extraordinary, and the island is heavily fortified. We only have a 20% chance of success if we attack and seize it. The art of war dictates that if your forces are ten times the enemy’s, surround them; if five times, attack them; if twice, divide them.” Wei Yuzhi emphasized the phrase “if twice, divide them.” If your forces were twice the enemy’s, you should disperse them to concentrate your superior forces and eliminate them. “We only want the heart’s blood; we do not need to provoke anyone else,” Wei Yuzhi said expressionlessly. “The heart’s blood is most likely in the hands of Fourteenth Young Lady and Mo Sigui. We just need to lure them out for a siege.” “How do we lure them out?” Ghost Tiger asked. Wei Yuzhi’s eyes reflected the shimmering light of the lake, concealing the gloom in his heart. As the mastermind behind everything within the Song Dynasty, Wei Yuzhi was shrewd, and his schemes had never failed. Since the “Ming mansion” of Piaomiao Mountain Mansion was breached by the Konghe Army, the newly enthroned Emperor of Liao had reclaimed the power of the “Hidden mansion.” Was he really so impatient to discard the useful tool after the usefulness was over? Wei Yuzhi understood the new Emperor’s nature; he was not short-sighted. It was not time to discard the useful tool yet. However, no matter how hard he fought or how much he poured his heart and soul into the relationship, it ultimately could not compare to a woman with whom he shared blood. This was something he found hard to accept. Wei Yuzhi gritted his teeth. A lake breeze swept by, and his body swayed slightly. The Ghost Tiger closest to him darted forward and supported his back. “Are you alright, My Lord?” “Yes,” Wei Yuzhi forced himself to remain calm. “Stay in the plum grove nearby. Mo Sigui will definitely leave the island to gather herbs. According to our spies in the city, Fourteenth Young Lady was recently seen near Pan Tower Street. I predict she will reappear soon. Fourteenth Young Lady’s mental power has reached a transcendent level. You all stay within the formation and do not follow her out on your own, or you will bear the consequences.” “Yes,” all the Ghost Tigers responded in unison. These Ghost Tigers were Yelu Huangwu’s right-hand men. They were sent to assist Wei Yuzhi in seizing the heart’s blood, but they did not unconditionally obey orders, which greatly hampered Wei Yuzhi. Wei Yuzhi already had an illness, and he was severely injured by An Jiu during her kidnapping. His health had deteriorated further, and he had to recuperate for quite some time before he could barely handle things. Victory and defeat were common occurrences in warfare; strategists inevitably made mistakes and suffered setbacks. Wei Yuzhi poured his heart and soul into the Liao Kingdom, hoping to rise to the highest ranks of officialdom and be remembered in history. Unfortunately, since the new Emperor ascended the throne, his situation not only failed to improve but also became even more precarious. At one point, he suddenly felt utterly exhausted. Wei Yuzhi’s repeated defeats at An Jiu’s hands were not entirely due to her superior abilities but rather because he had never truly and earnestly plotted against her. He found playing games with her rather amusing. It was not until he received a personal letter from the Emperor, rebuking him for letting personal feelings interfere with national affairs, that he realized he had fallen into a dangerous game. As intelligent as he was, he knew his feelings for her would be fruitless, or at least lead to disastrous consequences. He told An Jiu he had “once loved her,” but truly forgetting and letting go was never so easy. In the dead of night, he often dreamt of finding that beauty amidst a pile of withered leaves… like a gift from heaven. It was the first time in his life he had felt his heart flutter for a woman. Now, to be with Fourteenth Young Lady, he could only bind her and imprison her in a secluded room. But for a strategist skilled in manipulating people’s hearts, merely possessing a shell was utterly tasteless. Wei Yuzhi sighed. That Fourteenth Young Lady, so stubborn… unyielding. “You all keep watch. I am going back to rest,” Wei Yuzhi said, turning and leaving. Several Ghost Tigers turned back to watch his retreating figure. In the night, his clothes fluttered in the wind, outlining his slender, bamboo-like frame, a mixture of desolation and wretchedness. “Is Master Wei planning to kill us here?” one of the Ghost Tigers suddenly asked. After all, two tigers could not share one mountain. Wei Yuzhi and Yelu Huangwu were both shrewd strategists, and one of them would inevitably occupy the position second only to the Emperor. Comparatively, Yelu Huangwu’s strength surpasses Wei Yuzhi’s, and his desire to weaken his rival was understandable. After all, Wei Yuzhi had never hidden his aversion to them. “No,” said the man who had been speaking with Wei Yuzhi. “This matter concerns the Emperor. If anything happens to him, our Highness’s situation will be precarious, and he will suffer an even worse fate.” The Ghost Tigers fell silent, agreeing that this made perfect sense. They had been lying low for so many years, finally witnessing Yelu Huangwu’s resurgence. It was time for them to reign supreme, and their excitement had not yet subsided. Some people in this world were eager to die, yet unwilling to die lightly. That kind of fervor was beyond the comprehension of ordinary people. The Ghost Tigers were like that. Under Yelu Huangwu, they had only one word in their hearts—loyalty!

chapters.title: What Is There To Be Smug About?
chapters.content: On the island, An Jiu finished a sumptuous dinner to her heart’s content. She and Chu Dingjiang then took Da Jiu for a walk in the garden. The two of them and the tiger were bathed in a golden-red hue by the setting sun. A thin mist lingered among the flowers, and ice crystals clung to the bare branches, reflecting the orange sunlight and shimmering in the sunlight, creating an otherworldly scene. An Jiu let out a satisfied burp and asked Chu Dingjiang, “When are you leaving?” “Tomorrow morning,” he replied. If it were not for the Emperor’s illness and the tense situation, perhaps he could have stayed longer. “When I arrived, I felt like someone was following me, but I could not spot anyone.” Chu Dingjiang had been thinking about this. Logically, even if his power had diminished somewhat, few people in the entire Song Dynasty could escape his mental energy, unless… “Wei Yuzhi.” He suddenly remembered that this person was proficient in formations and could block mental energy by altering the environment. “It’s possible he tracked me here.” An Jiu pouted and sat down on a rock. “I told you to eliminate this threat early, but you insisted that destroying the Liao Kingdom required him. I am used to eliminating all visible threats. If I get the chance next time, I will strike. Anyway, even if I do not bother him, he will bother me.” Chu Dingjiang pondered. He was used to considering the big picture, and for the greater good, there would always be sacrifices. This time, however, he had not considered that Wei Yuzhi might be a threat to An Jiu, or perhaps he had known but had not taken it seriously. “This time, I am sorry,” Chu Dingjiang murmured, unsure whether he was speaking to An Jiu or to himself. An Jiu was slightly taken aback. “What did you do wrong?” She thought for a moment, then narrowed her eyes and said, “You slept with another woman?” “Nonsense!” Chu Dingjiang flicked her smooth head with his finger. “I was talking about stopping you from killing Wei Yuzhi.” An Jiu regained her languid demeanor. She waved her hand. “There’s no need to apologize.” Chu Dingjiang felt deeply gratified. She truly lived up to his expectations of the woman he had chosen; she was very understanding. He was pondering how to encourage and praise her when he heard her say, “I’ve never had any expectations of men in this regard, so you do not need to feel too much pressure.” “…” The words Chu Dingjiang had prepared were swallowed back. An Jiu’s requirements for men were very low. As long as they were not sadistic like her father or stabbed her in the back, they were already passing grade. “I’d rather bear this pressure,” Chu Dingjiang sighed, bringing the topic back. “I will go check over there. Do not go out for now. What about that bounty list?” “It’s inside,” An Jiu said. Chu Dingjiang said, “Give it to me in a bit; I will have someone take care of it for you.” An Jiu rested her chin on her knees, looking up at him. “No, I am bored with nothing to do.” Chu Dingjiang suggested, “You could learn accounting from Madam Zhu. It is not really appropriate to entrust all our property to an outsider.” “Hmm. That makes sense.” An Jiu smiled. She was not concerned about the property issue; she just liked that he said, “we.” That intimacy touched a hidden softness in her heart. “I am going off the island to take a look,” Chu Dingjiang said. He turned around. But An Jiu grabbed his hand. “They will not run away.” Ice crystals like stars and thin mist like gauze. In the fading light, An Jiu tilted her head. Strands of hair fell across her forehead, her eyes clear. Her face was like jade, captivating Chu Dingjiang. A person’s temperament could completely change them. An Jiu’s appearance had matured, showing no trace of Mei Jiu, but rather increasingly resembling her appearance from her previous life. “Ah Jiu.” Chu Dingjiang returned the grip on her hand. The lake stretched out in a misty haze. Plum blossoms bloomed fiercely in the darkness on the opposite shore. Wei Yuzhi hurriedly returned, gathering the Ghost Tigers and taking them away. He did not know the true extent of Chu Dingjiang’s skill, but he was certain that Chu Dingjiang’s mental power was above his own, at the first level of the Transcendent Realm—a realm he did not understand. Therefore, he could not be sure if the formation he had set up would be foolproof. If Chu Dingjiang discovered it, the loss of the Ghost Tigers would be a minor matter; exposing their whereabouts and incurring the new Emperor’s displeasure would be disastrous! The Ghost Tigers were quite resentful of Wei Yuzhi’s last-minute change of plans, but he did not care about their feelings; as long as they complied, that was enough. “After we leave Mei Mansion, how do we capture Mo Sigui and Fourteenth Young Lady?” the Ghost Tiger leader asked. “It cannot be rushed; I have my own plan,” Wei Yuzhi said. “If you do not explain clearly, My Lord, we are afraid we cannot obey.” The Ghost Tiger leader slowed his pace, and the others stopped as well. Wei Yuzhi knew he needed to be patient, but his health was poor, and he felt as if he were about to burn out, making it difficult for him to remain calm. His face was ashen, his dark eyes cold. “Could it be that Her Highness the Princess sent you all here to supervise me?” Wei Yuzhi’s displeasure was written all over his face. Although the Ghost Tigers were not afraid, they dared not easily shatter the thin veneer of harmony between the princess and this man. “The princess sent us to assist the master, but…” The Ghost Tiger leader’s tone shifted, becoming sharp and almost sarcastic. “The master has repeatedly failed, suffering heavy losses. We, Ghost Tigers, are not afraid of death, but we will never sacrifice ourselves in vain.” This was a blatant questioning of his abilities. Wei Yuzhi was furious, but suddenly a calm settled in his heart. He sneered, “As long as you do not go to your deaths, you will not have sacrificed yourselves in vain!” With that, he turned and left. The Ghost Tigers paused for a moment, then followed their leader. The clouds thickened, and as night fell, not a single star could be seen. Fine snow began to fall. The Dream Blossom was gradually covered by snow, and the mist surrounding the island dissipated. The Dream Blossom originated in swamps, but through human cultivation, it was able to bloom in icy conditions. However, the cold always suppressed its vitality; although it could bloom year-round, winter was its weakest season, especially on snowy days. Chu Dingjiang stayed in An Jiu’s house for over two hours before leaving. He could not rest easy without checking on it. Reaching the ferry, he suddenly felt something was amiss. Looking around, he realized the mist had thinned. The Dream Blossom was covered by a thin layer of snow, its petals drooping, as if it were about to wither and die. Chu Dingjiang immediately turned back, heading towards Mo Sigui’s residence. Mo Sigui’s house was filled with hidden weapons and poisons. Chu Dingjiang did not sneak in; instead, he kicked the door open. A thick cloud of smoke billowed towards them, but Chu Dingjiang, prepared, leaped back seven or eight zhang. A moment later, a thin, tall young man with a pipe dangling from his neck emerged from the smoke. He squinted his almond-shaped eyes, which were hidden by dark circles, exhaled a puff of smoke, and said leisurely, “Oh, so it is Lord Chu who’s got such a fiery temper!” “Easy,” Chu Dingjiang replied with nonchalant sarcasm. “Compared to the still-unripe Physician Mo, I admit I am no match.” Mo Sigui clicked his tongue. “When I was enjoying my first taste of meat, I reckon Lord Chu was still masturbating.” “Is that so? I misunderstood you, Divine Physician. My apologies,” Chu Dingjiang chuckled. “However, some things have no set time. I’d rather wait until the day lovers are finally united.” Mo Sigui suddenly threw his pipe at Chu Dingjiang. “What the hell is there to be so smug about? I am going to sleep!” Chu Dingjiang did not catch the pipe but dodged it. “Wait, I need to talk to you.”

chapters.title: Loyalty and Righteousness
chapters.content: “You’ve come to me for something, so it is definitely not good news,” Mo Sigui said, but still turned around. “Speak.” “The fog on the island is thinning. Is there no way to compensate for Dream Flower’s weakness?” Chu Dingjiang gradually felt that keeping Wei Yuzhi was a mistake. Even though this person could change the situation in Liao, he was constantly worried that An Jiu would be plotted against. Mo Sigui walked down the steps, picked up his pipe, and walked towards the pavilion. “What, are the Dream Flowers going to die?” Chu Dingjiang followed. “They will not die, but if someone attacks now, the poison gas will have little effect.” Lanterns hung from the four corners of the pavilion, and the evergreen trees around it cast dappled shadows on the ground. The light and shadow swayed when the wind blew, making it appear hazy and tranquil. Mo Sigui lay on the rocking chair in the pavilion, carefully wiping his pipe with a handkerchief, and said casually, “It seems you are always asking me for favors.” “Not asking,” Chu Dingjiang said, sitting down on the stone bench, looking at him seriously. “You’ve also been dragged into the conflict by Gu Jinghong. Do you think you can stay out of it?” Mo Sigui wiped his pipe, his mouth gradually becoming dry, and he kept wanting to smoke that medicinal pipe. He smiled bitterly to himself; every medicine had its side effects, and he was now addicted to the medicinal pipe, not much different from smoking hibiscus ointment! Seeing the slight change in his expression, Chu Dingjiang’s grip on the pipe tightened and loosened; he roughly guessed what he was thinking, so he poured a cup of cold water and pushed it in front of him. Mo Sigui smacked his lips, picked up the teacup, and raised an eyebrow at him. “You are not thinking of poisoning me, are you?” “Do you think I need to use poison?” Chu Dingjiang countered. Killing someone was just a matter of a swift stroke, much faster than using poison. Mo Sigui took a sip of water. The icy cold stung his mouth, and he frowned, pausing for a moment. “Speaking of Gu Jinghong, I always feel like it was a dream.” That person came and went. He swept through the world in a flash, leaving only a fleeting shadow—truly a fleeting glimpse of a fleeting beauty. “It’s already a stretch that the Dream Flowers can bloom in all four seasons. I do not have the ability to modify them. I am a physician, not a gardener.” Mo Sigui sipped the water, gradually adjusting to the temperature, and finally found it quite comfortable. “We need to strengthen our defenses. We can only start from other aspects. I planted a ring of Blood Orchids next to the Dream Flowers, which bloom in winter. Unfortunately, these plants grow slowly; half of them are still just buds.” Chu Dingjiang lowered his eyes, staring at the pipe in Mo Sigui’s hand. “Could we use a similar smoke medicine to the Dream Flowers?” “Preparing the medicine is not difficult, but you must understand that ordinary smoke will not just linger around the flowers like Dream Flowers’ mist, and once released, it dissipates quickly,” Mo Sigui said. “I know, otherwise I would not have asked you.” Chu Dingjiang’s tone was full of “I really do not want to get close to you unless absolutely necessary.” Mo Sigui, holding a glass of water, leaned back lazily in his chair, swaying gently. Hearing this, he tilted his head and smiled. “Thank you for thinking so highly of me, but do you not think you are being too tense? Your woman is already being kind by not actively killing to silence witnesses.” Chu Dingjiang said. “I suspect Wei Yuzhi is nearby. It would be best to address the lack of security. Just tell me what medicinal herbs you need…” “Really?” Mo Sigui interrupted him, her eyes shining. “I will handle it accordingly.” Chu Dingjiang added what he had not finished saying. If he did not take this opportunity to make a huge profit, he would not be Mo Sigui. Even if Chu Dingjiang was worried about An Jiu, he was not stupid. He could roughly judge what medicinal herbs were needed and what weren’t, and he would not let himself be slaughtered. “Deal.” Mo Sigui knew Chu Dingjiang was going easy on him, deliberately letting him off the hook, so he accepted it without hesitation. Mo Sigui understood Chu Dingjiang’s mindset. If it were not for An Jiu, given his cunning and the various unpleasant aspects of their relationship, why would he suffer such a loss? “You’ve had it tough, too; consider this an act of charity,” Mo Sigui said, feigning innocence despite his gain. Chu Dingjiang did not take it to heart and got up to leave. “You want to get involved in this mess?” Mo Sigui suddenly asked. Chu Dingjiang reached the stone steps, stopped, and turned back. “Yes.” He knew without being told that Mo Sigui was referring to the succession struggle. “Everyone has their own path,” Mo Sigui said, stroking his pipe, his tone somewhat melancholic. In truth, he felt Lou Mingyue was a stranger, cold and aloof, while in his memory, he still remembered the simple, somewhat boyish Qiu Ningyu. Time was cruel, etching a completely different image onto a person. If Lou Mingyue and Qiu Ningyu shared any similarity, it was—stubbornness. Mo Sigui closed his eyes and slowly said, “When Ningyu was little, she thought the jujube and osmanthus cake made by a certain pastry shop was delicious, so she always ate it there for over four years and never bought it anywhere else. Later, the pastry shop went out of business, and she tried every means to find out where the shop owner had gone, but to no avail. From then on, she stopped eating jujube and osmanthus cake, thinking that no one in the world could make it as good as that shop owner. In fact, she had never eaten jujube and osmanthus cake from any other shop. I told her that if the shop made good pastries, it would not have gone out of business, but she stubbornly insisted on her own opinion. Is she not like a stubborn donkey?” After a moment, no one answered. Mo Sigui assumed Chu Dingjiang had left, but after a long pause, he suddenly heard him say, “Perhaps it has little to do with the osmanthus cake. She’s just sentimental and loyal. She does not eat it because she does not want to be reminded of the shop?” Mo Sigui was taken aback. Thinking carefully, the shop was only about half a zhang wide. The owner was an old soldier from the battlefield, lame in his right leg, with a dark face but a kind and gentle smile. He lived alone behind the shop, keeping many cats and dogs. Every time Qiu Ningyu visited, she would chat with him for an hour or two, always about the border war. Yes, sentimental and loyal. Mo Sigui suddenly understood. Lou Mingyue was not stubborn; she was just too sentimental. Some things were hard to let go of! If she felt this way about a casually met pastry shop owner, how much more so after experiencing the tragic deaths of the Qiu couple and her own mother? She must be in excruciating pain… His eyes stung, and he instinctively squeezed them shut. The moon shone brightly. At the border between Liao, Song, and Western Xia, a sharp north wind howled. A dilapidated inn was nestled at the foot of Heishan. The rotten wood on the door plaque creaked in the gale. The inn’s dozen or so rooms were all occupied. A figure flashed in the backyard. The horses stirred briefly but quickly quieted down. A woman lay panting heavily in a pile of hay in the corner of the stable. Her black, tight-fitting clothes clung to her body, clearly soaked through. Soon, dark red liquid seeped into the hay, staining a large patch and emitting a strong, pungent smell of blood. The woman pulled down her veil, revealing a beautiful yet fiercely handsome face. Her brows furrowed. She roughly tore open her clothes, revealing a bloodied and mangled shoulder. She pulled a dagger from her ankle and gritted her teeth, digging into the bloody hole in her shoulder. A moment later, an arrow and pieces of flesh fell onto the hay.
