She immediately sprinkled a large amount of wound medicine on it and then tightly wrapped it with strips of cloth. Having done all this, she was drenched in sweat, utterly exhausted, and covered in numerous large and small sword and knife wounds, too weak to tend to them. Lying on the hay for a while, she forced herself to hastily treat the other larger wounds, seizing the time to rest. In her half-awake state, she clutched the empty medicine bottle tightly in her hand, as if this would be the only way to survive. This was medicine given to her by Mo Sigui. She had always had great faith in him; besides, he was her only reason for living. Holding this medicine bottle was like holding Mo Sigui’s hand; with him, she knew she would not die… Due to the significant blood loss and the hurried journey, her body was utterly exhausted. She had originally planned to remain vigilant and rest for only an hour before leaving, but she unknowingly drifted into a deep sleep. In her dream, she did not see her father’s tragic death by the river, the turbulent waters, or her mother’s half-closed eyes in the fire. Instead, she saw only a boy with almond-shaped eyes, standing in front of Liu’s pastry shop, the warm spring sunlight bathing him. He leaned against the wall, smiling as he watched her squatting at the edge of the house, playing with a few cats, occasionally uttering a few sarcastic remarks. It was beautiful. “There’s blood on the ground!” A sudden scream abruptly cut through the silence. Lou Mingyue abruptly opened her eyes, finding herself still lying on the haystack. The morning light filtering through the window shone softly and comfortably on her face, but she dared not hesitate. She rolled over and climbed onto the roof beam, using her mental power to investigate the outside world.

chapters.title: Xiao Yue Goes Mad
chapters.content: The inn was located in a very remote area, and there were no martial artists in the tavern. Lou Mingyue breathed a slight sigh of relief and slipped out through the narrow ventilation window, disappearing in the blink of an eye. However, she was severely injured and could not hold on for long. She barely managed to find a patch of withered, waist-high grass and plunged into it. Looking at the sky, slightly yellowed by the rising sun, a faint mist escaped Lou Mingyue’s lips, her pale face somewhat hazy. Every sunrise was a new beginning, so even with setbacks, hope should have remained in her heart. But she sank deeper and deeper into the swamp of despair day after day. At these times, Lou Mingyue would have the thought of retreating, returning to Mo Sigui’s side, and accompanying him to the pinnacle of medical cultivation. She used to be playful and carefree, disdainful of such things, but now she found them especially precious. Perhaps that was how people were; what was within reach was often taken for granted, while what was unattainable was considered a treasure. Lou Mingyue recuperated on Plum Blossom Island for a few days. She considered staying, but the torment of hatred plagued her. The thought of her enemy still alive and well kept her awake at night. If she didn’t seek revenge, she feared she would eventually be driven mad by her suppressed hatred. Lou Mingyue joined the Dangerous Moon Team of the Konghe Army and was directly assigned the mission to assassinate Yelu Huangwu. This was her fourth assassination attempt. Her first attempt took place en route. She had been lying in wait for months, but unfortunately, she was stopped by a sudden attack from Ghost Tiger when she was still twenty chi from the carriage, nearly losing her life. The second assassination attempt took place at a private gathering. Yelu Huangwu was extremely busy, either at the princess’s residence or in the palace, rarely having such a perfect opportunity. With her enemy within reach, Lou Mingyue couldn’t resist acting. However, due to a lack of careful planning, it also ended in failure. This time, she was only a dozen chi away from Yelu Huangwu. The third assassination attempt was the most devastating. Yelu Huangwu left Shangjing to personally command the Liao army against Ling Ziyue’s fierce attack on the Liao border, escorted only by twenty riders. Lou Mingyue and six other members of the Dangerous Moon team set up an ambush, their choice of location and timing extremely successful. In that battle, sixteen of the enemy died, while all but Lou Mingyue perished. She alone killed ten powerful Ghost Tigers. After her companions were all killed, she closed the distance to within ten zhang of Yelu Huangwu. By this time, she was already severely wounded and should have retreated quickly, but separated by several Ghost Tigers, she stared intently at Yelu Huangwu. All the grief and hatred in her heart suddenly surged like a tsunami. In that instant, she unleashed a power almost approaching the pinnacle of perfection, her longsword swirling like a dragon. A thunderous strike, she successfully killed the remaining Ghost Tigers even in dire straits. Yelu Huangwu was so close; even if they were to die together, the thought filled her with immense satisfaction. Alas. Just as the last Ghost Tiger fell, she suddenly felt dizzy. Through her blurred vision, she saw the ugly woman beside Yelu Huangwu raise her crossbow and fire at her. As she fell, Lou Mingyue was almost swallowed by despair. Her revenge was unavenged; she couldn’t die. She absolutely couldn’t die! Through her hazy vision, she vaguely heard Yelu Huangwu’s cold voice: “To fight ten against one, such a rare talent, yet unable to be of use to me.” It sounded like praise, regret, and extreme anger. “There are women like this in the world; it’s truly lamentable,” the ugly woman said softly. Perhaps these words touched Yelu Huangwu. She paused, then said, “Send someone to collect the bodies of the fallen Ghost Tigers. This woman faced death without fear; her sword aura could shake the heavens and earth. Let her rest in peace.” “Yes,” the ugly woman replied. Lou Mingyue, in a daze, thought it seemed the ugly woman had deliberately spared her life… Suddenly, she felt a breath near her ear and heard the ugly woman say in a barely audible voice, “Go find Mo Sigui, or you will surely die.” As the sound of hooves faded into the distance, her consciousness gradually returned. The itching and pain from the crossbow wound became increasingly clear and spread rapidly throughout her body. Based on her experience, she knew she had been poisoned, so she hastily treated the wound and rushed back to the Song Dynasty to find Mo Sigui. Originally, she had planned to never have anything to do with him again in this life, but the regret and despair she felt when she was on the verge of death were too profound; she couldn’t die. Later, Lou Mingyue learned that the ugly woman beside Yelu Huangwu was named Ning Yanli, a famous physician in the Liao Dynasty, who was merely being used to challenge Mo Sigui. In a way, Mo Sigui had indirectly saved her. And this time, it was Lou Mingyue’s fourth attempt to assassinate Yelu Huangwu. At such close range, she could almost see her own reflection in Yelu Huangwu’s calm, dark eyes. Even though the result was still failure, each time she closed the distance, a glimmer of hope blossomed in the abyss of hatred and despair. —One day, she would avenge herself. Only by killing her enemy could she quell her hatred, comfort the spirits of her parents and mother, and give an explanation to the innocent Qiu and Lou clansmen who had perished so tragically. Perhaps only then could she live freely. Lou Mingyue felt as if she had been frozen in an ice cave for days and nights; she could no longer feel her limbs, nor even the cold. She silently prayed, “Mo Sigui, protect me so I can get through this ordeal.” No matter what misfortunes she had suffered, Mo Sigui was always the purest and most beautiful part of her life, a warm, small lamp in the long, dark night. If possible, she also wanted to cross this endless darkness and reach his side to draw warmth. The withered grass rustled, and icicles from the branches fell onto Lou Mingyue’s face, lingering for a long time. The sun rose as usual. On the island amidst the plum blossoms, chaos reigned. Mo Sigui had slept in the pavilion the night before, only to be awakened early this morning by strange noises. He rushed over and saw Xiao Yue running and bumping around in the woods like a headless fly, her head bleeding profusely. Her once azure eyes were now bloodshot, and she was howling in pain, her nose wrinkled. Mo Sigui’s heart sank, and he abruptly stopped. Xiao Yue was a tracking tiger specifically prepared for Lou Mingyue. Both she and Lou Mingyue possessed a parasitic Gu within them. This substance normally had no effect on the body; the Gu existed as long as the host existed, and the Gu died when the host died. If one were on the verge of death, the other would also sense the threat of death and begin to struggle. At this time, the host would suffer immense pain as the Gu writhes within its body and would also experience the feeling of impending death. The only reason Xiao Yue has suddenly gone mad can be this! Xiao Yue spotted Mo Sigui and immediately rushed over, cowering and trembling against the tree roots in front of him, her eyes filled with terror, and she whimpered softly. Through Xiao Yue, Mo Sigui seemed to see Lou Mingyue’s current appearance. His mind went blank, his limbs went weak, and his heart turned ice-cold.

chapters.title: Trapped
chapters.content: Mo Sigui quickly applied acupuncture to Xiao Yue to calm it down, then returned to his residence to pack his medicine box. “Ah Jiu!” Mo Sigui knocked urgently on the door, carrying his medicine box. The door creaked open, revealing An Jiu’s calm face. “What happened?” Mo Sigui took out a medicine bottle and handed it to her. “This is my cousin’s medicine. Take this for now to ease the situation. I’ll remove the curse when I return.” Aside from treating patients or preparing medicine, Mo Sigui was usually lazy and rarely so anxious. An Jiu subconsciously asked, “Did something happen to Lou Mingyue?” Mo Sigui was startled, his mind suddenly clearing, but his expression remained troubled. “Yes.” “Then go.” An Jiu pocketed the medicine bottle. “I’ll take it to Mei Jiu.” Mo Sigui patted her shoulder, wanting to say something, but ultimately felt that anything he said would be superfluous, so he turned and hurriedly left with Xiao Yue. “Mo Sigui,” An Jiu called out to him. “Wei Yuzhi might be nearby. Be careful.” “I know.” Mo Sigui didn’t turn around; his figure disappeared into the mist. An Jiu stood at the door for a while, noticing Mei Yanran’s presence nearby. She paused, then decided to pretend she hadn’t noticed. “I’ll go take her medicine,” Mei Yanran said, emerging from behind the artificial hill. She was in charge of everyone’s meals on the island, so she got up early. She happened to overhear Mo Sigui and An Jiu’s conversation and, hearing them mention Mei Jiu, couldn’t help but stop. “Aren’t you unable to go out?” Mei Yanran asked, unsure of her meaning. An Jiu was never one to back down from trouble. She roughly knew Wei Yuzhi’s current situation in Liao. Therefore, she didn’t have much power at her disposal. If they really encountered each other, she might not be the one to be slaughtered! However, since Mei Yanran was going, she wouldn’t deliberately stop her. So she took out the medicine bottle and tossed it over. “Thank you.” Mei Yanran took the medicine bottle, a smile that reached her eyes appearing on her face. An Jiu paused for a few moments, then said, “You’re welcome.” Having spent more time together, Mei Yanran had come to understand An Jiu’s personality somewhat. Although she didn’t know what An Jiu had been through, Mei Yanran felt she was a pitiful child, and her initial resistance gradually melted away. Mei Jiu’s current predicament was ultimately due to her own failure as a mother and had little to do with An Jiu. The two looked at each other, both wanting to say more, but remained silent for a long time. Though only seven or eight chi apart, it felt like an abyss. A cold wind blew past, creating an awkward atmosphere. “I’ll go cook first,” Mei Yanran spoke first. She was quite sociable, but facing An Jiu, she didn’t know where to begin a conversation. She had no choice but to temporarily abandon the idea of ​​communication. An Jiu nodded, watching her leave. Mo Sigui left Mei Mansion, riding his tiger northward, the wind whistling past his ears. His brows were furrowed, his thoughts seemingly scattered by the wind; one moment, he thought of the lively and cheerful Qiu Ningyu, the next of the aloof and cold Lou Mingyue; the two images gradually merged into one. In truth, he knew very well that Lou Mingyue was likely far from Bianjing, and by the time he arrived, it would probably be too late. But even if it was just to collect the body, he had to do it himself. The thin layer of snow on the road reflected the sunlight, blinding him. Winter in Bianjing had dissipated with the melting of the last snowfall, and in just a few days, the mountains and fields were already draped in a tender green. Rumors circulated that the Emperor had recovered and begun to attend to state affairs, but only a few key ministers knew that the Emperor’s condition had deteriorated rapidly, and he was only kept alive by medicine. The Konghe Army had been stationed in Mei Mansion for the past few days. They had come to “invite” Mo Sigui. A thick fog hung in the air, and everyone on the island gazed out from the ferry. Through the thin mist, they could vaguely make out figures on the other side. Sheng Changying said, “I think they’re planning to land on the island.” “Should we fight or not?” An Jiu asked. Only An Jiu, Ling Ziyue, Lou Xiaowu, Sheng Changying, Sui Yuntong, Li Qingzhi, and the medicine boy remained on the island. Mei Yanran had gone to the Hua residence to deliver medicine the day before, and perhaps because the Konghe Army was stationed on the lakeshore, she couldn’t return for the time being. Zhu Pianxian had gone to Bianjing to check the accounts as usual, a trip that would take five or six days. Lou Xiaowu’s eyes sparkled as she said, “Let’s fight! I recently made a kind of water mine; it’ll be perfect for testing its power!” Ling Ziyue glanced at her, and she immediately shrank back, weakly saying, “Am I wrong…?” “We only have seven people…” Ling Ziyue didn’t continue. Of the remaining seven, two were practically useless fighters—Sheng Changying and the medicine boy. These two wouldn’t be considered combat power; they would definitely be a hindrance. Besides, while Ling Ziyue’s martial arts were decent, he was better suited for leading troops in battle. Against assassins whose profession was killing, he wouldn’t be able to utilize his strengths. The remaining Sui Yuntong, Li Qingzhi, and Lou Xiaowu were of average ability within the Konghe Army, and there was also An Jiu, whose strength was an unknown quantity… Was this combination really reliable against dozens of assassins ranked on the Konghe List? An Jiu leaned against a thick ginkgo tree with her arms crossed. She casually interjected, “There are eight of us…” The others followed her gaze to the fat tiger yawning against a tree root. Da Jiu, its jaws agape, was halfway through its yawn when it noticed their stares and paused, then warily retracted its claws, wondering how they knew it had hidden a packet of poisonous plant seeds under its belly. Da Jiu fed on poisonous creatures. Mo Sigui hadn’t prepared anything when he left, casually tossing it a small packet of poisonous plant seeds. It thought that if Mo Sigui didn’t return this year, it would have to rely on these seeds to survive the winter. Yes, absolutely no mistakes! The fat tiger’s gaze hardened, displaying a rather fierce air. The others, unaware of the true situation, felt a slight sense of relief; at least this tiger, covered in venom, was a tiny bit stronger than Sheng Changying’s fighting power. Fortunately, the Dream Flowers were more vibrant than a few days ago, and the island’s fog had reformed, proving quite effective. “They’re here,” Sui Yuntong said. The splashing sound in the lake grew closer. The Konghe Army, aware that the fog surrounding the island was not simple, stopped outside the fog and began to call out, “Is anyone on the island?” The voice was infused with internal energy; though not loud, it was extremely penetrating, as if the speaker were standing right in front of them. No one answered. Everyone wondered if they were admitting someone was there or pretending. Sui Yuntong, acting on his own initiative, ordered the young medicine boy to answer. Because of their mental power, the Konghe Army, with its many experts, would surely sense that there were people on the island and more than one. “My master has gone out to consult physicians and won’t return for several months,” the young medicine boy’s clear voice replied. “Where has Physician Mo gone to consult physicians?” the man asked. The young medicine boy replied, “I don’t know; the physician left in a hurry.” The man added, “The Emperor ordered us to wait until we reached the physician to retrieve a medicine and then allowed us to come to the island to get it and leave.” If that were true, there would be no need to mobilize so many people at once; perhaps they planned to attack by force if the deception failed. The others were unaware of the matter of the heart’s blood, only assuming that the Emperor was dying and had come specifically to summon Mo Sigui. However, given the current situation, that was clearly not the case. “I think this is Wei Yuzhi’s scheme,” An Jiu said, preparing to confess the matter of the heart’s blood to everyone. Ling Ziyue, seeing her expression, said, “Let’s talk inside.” They feared the Konghe Army would overhear them here. Everyone nodded, leaving the young medicine boy to deal with the others. With the poisonous gas of the Dream Flower surrounding them, they wouldn’t be able to get over for a while. The group sat down in the dining hall. An Jiu said, “Gu Jinghong is a medicine person kept by the Liao royal family, specifically for prolonging the Liao Emperor’s life. However, he resented his fate and left his most precious heart’s blood with Mo Sigui. Wei Yuzhi’s lingering spirit is haunted by this. If it’s to save the Emperor’s life, do you think we should give the medicine to them?” An Jiu didn’t want to waste Gu Jinghong’s blood to save that lust-blinded Emperor, but since everyone was currently surrounded, she still sought everyone’s opinion. Sui Yuntong didn’t answer directly, but instead asked, “What does this have to do with the Konghe Army?” An Jiu said, “I know the Liao Kingdom has planted a spy within the Konghe Army. If it weren’t for him leaking the information, how would the Emperor know about the heart’s blood?” “If that’s true, then even if we hand it over, it will still fall into Wei Yuzhi’s hands.” While others might not know the wonders of the heart’s blood, Sheng Changying knew better than anyone, so she could foresee that Wei Yuzhi would go to any lengths for it. “If he didn’t have a high-ranking spy within the Konghe Army, he would never have used this tactic so easily. What if we were all loyal to the Emperor and handed over the medicine upon hearing of his illness? Wouldn’t his plan have failed? So he must be confident that once we hand over the medicine, it will definitely fall into the hands of his spy.” Wei Yuzhi’s willingness to expose such a deeply entrenched spy to obtain this item showed that the new Liao Emperor didn’t have many years left to live. “We absolutely cannot hand it over,” Li Qingzhi was the first to speak. Ling Ziyue didn’t speak, but clearly agreed with him. Although they were unwilling to pledge allegiance to the current Emperor, they remained loyal to the Song Dynasty. They would be overjoyed if the enemy Emperor were to die early. “Yes, it would be best if all the Liao dogs were wiped out!” Lou Xiaowu said hatefully. If it weren’t for that Liao woman, the Lou clan wouldn’t have perished within days. Her hatred was no less than Lou Mingyue’s, which was why she accepted the responsibility of reviving the Lou clan without hesitation when Lou Mingyue entrusted her with it. Lou Xiaowu’s growing obsession with military research was largely due to this. Her martial arts skills were lacking; if she were to assassinate Yelu Huangwu, she would likely be hacked to pieces before even getting a hundred chi away. Therefore, she hoped to develop useful weapons for the Song army, using this overwhelming military strength to destroy the Liao Dynasty. Every time Lou Xiaowu thought about the enemy possessing the terrifyingly powerful blue-fire crossbow, she felt highly motivated. Her immediate goal was to develop a weapon capable of instantly destroying the blue-fire crossbow.

chapters.title: Chu Dingjiang’s Choice
chapters.content: “Then prepare for battle.” An Jiu took out a bottle of medicine and placed it on the table. “These are pills made from that blood. I used them to repair my damaged meridians. Even healthy people will benefit greatly from them. Everyone, please share them.” They were all besieged because of this medicine. An Jiu was a very honest and fair person. Since they were going to fight the enemy together, she did not want to keep it all to herself. Faced with such temptation, everyone fell silent. After a while, Sui Yuntong said, “I do not want it.” If An Jiu had not saved his life during the attack on Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, he would be dead by now. He had no chance to repay her kindness, but he absolutely could not take advantage of the situation and accept this pill. “I do not want it either.” Li Qingzhi had also been saved by An Jiu back then. Of those present, only Ling Ziyue was unfamiliar with the effects of the medicine person’s blood. Therefore, to ensure fairness, Sheng Changying explained before he could speak, “Legend has it that this blood can bring the dead back to life and heal the wounded; it is a divine medicine.” Ling Ziyue smiled and shook his head. “If this medicine could save the Song Dynasty, I would snatch it even if it were not given to me. But… I am already disheartened. This medicine probably cannot save me, so I do not want it.” Sheng Changying smiled. “I will not waste such a miraculous medicine.” He was born with a crippled meridian; unless he was reborn in the womb, even drinking all of Gu Jinghong’s blood would not help him. “I do not need it.” Lou Xiaowu had never been interested in improving her martial arts skills. She believed that the weapons she created would eventually be indestructible, becoming her most prized means of defense and attack. The people outside were racking their brains to seize the medicine. If they knew that these people had this attitude towards the readily available medicine, they would probably vomit blood. An Jiu did not pretend to refuse either. She put away the medicine bottle. “This medicine can save lives. You all do not want it now, but I still promise you can come and get it anytime you need it.” Her words were earnest, and no one refused. “If a fight breaks out, what are our chances of winning?” Li Qingzhi asked. “The chances of winning… are definitely there,” Sheng Changying pondered for a long time, then slowly curled one index finger. Li Qingzhi said disappointedly, “Only ten percent!” “Less than ten percent.” Sui Yuntong interpreted his meaning more accurately. Sheng Changying nodded. Even if the Konghe Army was loosely organized, it was still an organization with nearly a hundred years of history. This time, it was to save the Emperor’s life, so they would definitely deploy a large number of experts. If it were not for the island’s defenses and Lou Xiaowu’s weapons, they would probably be completely annihilated. “Are they not going to come to the island? Why not hide the medicine? Let them come up; if they cannot find it, they will naturally assume it was taken by the Divine Physician,” Li Qingzhi suggested. Sui Yuntong said, “Do you think they will give up just because they cannot find us? We will be tied up and interrogated anyway. If we find out they are deserters from the Konghe Army, our fate will be even worse, and we might even implicate Lord Chu!” “I almost forgot…” Li Qingzhi scratched his head. There were not just deserters from the Konghe Army here, but also a general who should already be dead and the current head of the Lou family! If others discovered that Lou Xiaowu was mixed up with a group of traitors, then… Everyone in the Lou family within the Konghe Army would suffer! At that time, even more people might die, and the Konghe Army, having lost a major pillar, would face collapse. “Wei Yuzhi’s plan is truly meticulous and vicious,” Sheng Changying sighed. Sheng Changying had served in the Konghe Academy and knew countless secrets, so he was naturally familiar with the name “Wei Yuzhi.” Wei Yuzhi managed most of the affairs of the Piaomiao Mountain Mansion. All the plans were implemented by him. It could be said that the Piaomiao Mountain Mansion’s rapid rise to a pivotal position in the Song Dynasty’s martial arts world was due to him. The vast majority of the credit went to him. “This man is indeed a menace.” An Jiu believed Chu Dingjiang’s words. If Wei Yuzhi were to return to Liao and clash with Yelu Huangwu, even if one side won, they would pay a heavy price. Could one person change the fate of a nation? The answer was yes. Some people’s wisdom could indeed turn the tide. An Jiu did not think it was anything special. The food chain was a cycle; there were no truly apex predators. Even if Wei Yuzhi was powerful, he’s still just a life. As an assassin, An Jiu knew very well how fragile human life was. Time was of the essence. The group gathered together to make a rough plan, then went to prepare. Da Jiu sensed danger and hurriedly ran to a secluded spot to dig a hole, burying his grass seeds, carefully patting them down with his fat paws, and finally urinating around them. “Miss Ah Jiu! Those people are coming ashore!” The medicine boy came running, his face pale. As An Jiu wrapped her sword around herself, she asked, “What happened? The Dream Flower did not work?” The young medicine boy, having endured much torment from Mo Sigui, was nearly scared to death, but his speech was still clear. “Several people entered the mist and got trapped. They knew that even masked people could not pass through directly, so they sent people to dive in from underwater.” “Do not worry; it will be fine for now. The Dream Flower blooms underwater too,” An Jiu said. She had observed it quietly. The Dream Flower loved water and grew wildly by the water’s edge, but it only spread towards the lake surface, not towards the islands. Moreover, all the Dream Flower stamens faced the water’s surface, some even blowing into the water. Many fish that strayed into the flowers become lost, floating like drunkards, eventually dying. Da Jiu’s favorite thing to do was run to the water’s edge to catch these dead fish to eat, because they contained toxins. An Jiu deduced from this that the Dream Flower was also poisonous in the water. The young apprentice’s expression relaxed slightly. “That’s good.” “Find a place to hide.” An Jiu finished packing and finally slung the Dragon-Subduing Bow over her shoulder. The apprentice nodded quickly. “I am best at this.” He then took off running. An Jiu watched his rabbit-like retreating figure and smiled. An Jiu had experienced countless such desperate situations and was already able to face them calmly. She took a pill, and as it slowly dissolved in her body, her mind became clear. Since taking Gu Jinghong’s heart’s blood, An Jiu felt as if she had inherited his innate ability to have seven orifices of clarity. Although she could not use mind-reading, illusion, or bewitching techniques like him, she had achieved near-perfect control over her mental energy. She no longer experienced the explosive bursts of mental energy she used to have. After being scolded by Mo Sigui several times, she had strictly followed the physician’s orders during the medication period. She carefully suppressed her mental energy, as if she had not used her mental power for a lifetime! An Jiu stroked the Dragon-Subduing Bow. The bow, its dark surface tinged with a faint red glow, seemed to hum softly, yearning to be drawn again. The others on the island gradually gathered, and An Jiu pulled herself together. “Let’s negotiate with the Konghe Army first!” Sheng Changying said. This was a good option, but the key was who would negotiate. Everyone here was keeping their identities secret. “I will do it,” Sui Yuntong said. “I am just an unknown nobody from the Konghe Academy; the risk of my identity being exposed is small.” Everyone looked at An Jiu, hoping she would make the decision. This whole affair stemmed from her and Mo Sigui, and everyone was willing to live and die with her. They had entrusted their lives to her. At this time, it was most dangerous for everyone to have their own agendas, and everyone clearly understood this. “Alright,” An Jiu immediately decided. Only she, Sui Yuntong, and Li Qingzhi were relatively safe from being exposed. She and Li Qingzhi had never been good at this kind of thing, so letting Sui Yuntong handle it was the most suitable option. Having made up his mind, Sui Yuntong called out, “Who over there can make decisions? Please come out and speak.” After a moment or two of silence, someone answered through the mist, “What is it?” “It’s best if you all do not try to dive underwater anymore. It is a hundred times more dangerous underwater than above,” Sui Yuntong said casually. He had just heard An Jiu say that the Dream Flower was poisonous underwater. But whether the poison had become stronger or weaker, he did not know. He finished speaking without waiting for a reply and continued, “After passing this obstacle, there are several more layers, all filled with poisons carefully cultivated by the Divine Physician. Do not blame me for not warning you beforehand!” Silence fell on the other side. Sui Yuntong pretended not to know the other person’s identity or the Emperor’s condition. He continued, “Since you are seeking medicine, you can wait for the Divine Physician to return on the other side!” The other person remained silent for a long time, then suddenly spoke. “His Majesty’s condition is critical; he urgently needs this medicine! I fear we will not be able to wait for the Divine Physician to return.” Sui Yuntong frowned. He was now certain that the person Wei Yuzhi had planted in the Konghe Army held a very high position; otherwise, he would not have so easily released this news while the Crown Prince and the Second Prince were busy preparing to seize the throne. Wei Yuzhi was simultaneously having Mei Mansion besieged and instigating a power struggle for the Song Dynasty’s throne! This scheme was far more insidious and far-reaching than they had imagined. Ling Ziyue pursed his lips tightly, feeling as if the mighty Song Dynasty was a small, drifting boat in the hands of a strategist, vulnerable to being torn apart by a giant wave at any moment. All his previous efforts seemed so insignificant, so laughable. This feeling of despair and powerlessness came so suddenly and violently, occupying his entire mind, making him oblivious to the danger before him. For him, fighting the Konghe Army did not ignite the same bloodlust he felt when killing the Liao people. Internal strife, what was this? A bitter smile appeared on Ling Ziyue’s lips. “If the medicine you speak of is so important, why would the Divine Physician carelessly leave it on the island?” Sui Yuntong made a last-ditch effort. In Bianjing City. The Crown Prince and the Second Prince quickly received the news from Mei Mansion. The Crown Prince preemptively attacked the Second Prince, listing various pieces of evidence suggesting his ambition to usurp the throne. Even though the Second Prince did indeed harbor such intentions, he had acted cautiously and had not left any obvious incriminating evidence. Most of the so-called evidence presented by the Crown Prince was fabricated. But now, the veracity of the evidence did not matter. An Jiu, trapped on the island, must have found it hard to believe that the little rascal who daydreamed in class and buried his head in a woman’s breasts the moment his teacher left had once again driven the Second Prince to a dead end with such swift and decisive action. As dusk fell, in a dark alley outside the Second Prince’s residence, a figure stood silently like a monument. Beside him, someone bowed slightly and reported, “After two probing attempts, the Konghe Army has temporarily encamped on the lakeshore and begun inspecting the island’s defenses for weaknesses.” The tall figure nodded slightly. “Understood. Go back. Report back immediately if there are any developments.” “Yes!” The man vanished. Chu Dingjiang looked up, the dim moonlight illuminating his sharply defined face. He sighed, a mist of smoke dissipating from his lips. Fate was forcing him to choose again: the Second Prince or An Jiu… A choice between two equally desirable but mutually exclusive options.

chapters.title: Strike
chapters.content: The night sky grew increasingly dark with gathering clouds. The sound of orderly footsteps echoed through the streets and alleys, torchlight flickered, and a military general led several thousand men to surround the Second Prince’s residence. The general dismounted and gestured for his subordinate to knock on the door. The Second Prince’s gate was tightly shut, and although the gate was surrounded by men, it was eerily quiet, save for the faint crackling of the burning torches. The soldier stepped forward and knocked on the vermilion door with the brass handle, the dull thud echoing. No one answered. The general gestured for the soldier to continue knocking. For a long time, still no one answered; the courtyard was deathly silent. “Second Prince!” the general called out. “I have been ordered to summon the Second Prince to the palace for questioning!” After a pause, he called out again, “I have been ordered to summon the Second Prince to the palace for questioning!” Still no response. Just as the general was about to order his men to ram the door, a faint light appeared inside. A short while later, the side door opened, and a sleepy-eyed man peeked out. Seeing the soldiers standing before him, he was startled, and instantly his eyes widened, his sleepiness dissipating. “My Lord,” he said, “His Highness went outside the city tonight and is not in the residence.” The general seemed not to hear him. “I am ordered to search the Second Prince’s residence and request that he come to the palace for questioning. Will you open the door yourself, or will I force it open?” Seeing the unfriendly nature of the visitor, the gatekeeper’s expression darkened. He stood on the stone steps, sleeves rolled up, looking down at him arrogantly. “I do not care what rank you hold,” he said. “Trespassing is a serious crime, especially in the residence of the Second Prince! Without the Emperor’s decree, do not even think about opening the door.” “I will explain myself when I see the Second Prince!” The general waved his hand. “Break it open!” The gatekeeper, realizing it was serious, scrambled back inside, the side door not even closed before being pushed open by the swarm of soldiers. The gatekeeper darted towards the main courtyard like a rabbit. The main gate opened. The general led his men in. Several black-clad men had appeared in the courtyard, blocking their path. These black-clad men stood silently, like ghosts. Their murderous aura intimidated the soldiers, who dared not advance for a long time. “Cheng Jiang, how dare you trespass into the Prince’s residence!” A low shout came from the shadows, and one of the black-clad men slowly stepped out. In the firelight, Cheng Jiang immediately noticed the silver crane embroidered on the hem of his robe, his eyes widening in surprise. “The Konghe Army?” The man replied, “Indeed. We are the Konghe Army, ordered by His Majesty to protect the Second Prince. Without His Majesty’s decree, if you wish to search the residence and take the Second Prince away today, you will have to step over our dead bodies!” Cheng Jiang knew that the Konghe Army’s experts could often fight a hundred men single-handedly, so he patiently explained, “Without His Majesty’s decree, even if I had the greatest courage, I would not dare trespass into the Prince’s residence. I hope you understand.” “The Konghe Secret Order,” the man said, holding out his hand. The Konghe Secret Order could mobilize the Konghe Army. Only those who possessed this order could command them; otherwise, even an imperial decree would be useless. “Since that’s the case, do not blame me!” Cheng Jiang said coldly. “If even one person dies in the Second Prince’s residence today, even if the Second Prince is not guilty of treason, he will be condemned by the world tomorrow! Since you are here to protect the Second Prince, you might as well think carefully about what I am saying.” The Konghe Army replied emotionlessly. “We do not care; our duty is only to protect the Second Prince’s safety.” In the study in the backyard. A young man in magnificent robes sat upright in a round-backed chair. His brows were furrowed, and he kept fiddling with the jade pendant in his hand. Six advisors sat on either side of him. The room remained silent for a long time before one of them advised, “Your Highness, we do not know if the Northern Camp can reach you in time. You should leave the residence quickly!” The young man slightly raised his eyes, his voice hoarse. “I will not leave.” Seeing that the advisors were about to persuade him again, he said, “It’s not out of stubbornness, but because I do not want to be a stray dog. You all know the Crown Prince’s methods; once I leave my current power, I will be wiped out. The outcome is tonight.” “Your Highness!” a voice whispered from the doorway. “What is it?” the young man asked. The man hurriedly reported, “The Konghe Army is blocking Cheng Jiang in the front courtyard.” The young man was slightly surprised, clearly not expecting the Konghe Army to come to his aid. He thought carefully; a mysterious person had been secretly guiding him, telling him a few nights ago that the Emperor was nearing his end and urging him to prepare, offering some strategic suggestions. Of course, he would not completely believe it. He secretly sent people to investigate and discussed the mysterious person’s plan with his advisors, discovering that if the Emperor was indeed nearing his end, the method suggested by the mysterious person was the safest. Unfortunately, his spies in the palace could not find out the Emperor’s condition, so he could only make some adjustments discreetly, just in case. The Second Prince knew that the Crown Prince certainly could not find out either; otherwise, he would not have remained inactive for so long. Until today, when he heard that the Konghe Army had launched a large-scale siege of Mei Mansion, attempting to seize medicine from Mo Sigui. Even as the Emperor’s own sons, they were unaware that the Konghe Army was no longer the last line of defense loyal only to the Emperor and the Song Dynasty. It had long since degenerated, its foundations shaken several times, eroded by external forces, and experienced more than one internal power struggle. Therefore, when a large contingent of the Konghe Army went to seize the medicine, the Crown Prince and the Second Prince were almost certain that the Emperor’s condition was truly critical. Although the Second Prince had always found the mysterious man’s advice brilliant, he could never fully trust someone who never even showed his face and thus would not adopt all his methods, this time being no different. The mysterious man, however, seemed to have anticipated this and had made remedial preparations well in advance. Only then did the Second Prince believe that this man was truly loyal to him. Having gained such a strategist who excelled in power, strategy, and martial arts, he felt an uncontrollable excitement. Thinking this, the Second Prince’s eyes shone brightly, further solidifying his resolve. “Wait, wait until the Northern Camp arrives!” In the pitch-black night, Chu Dingjiang sat on the roof of his study, listening to the sounds below, his gaze fixed on the front courtyard. To confirm the Emperor’s condition, Chu Dingjiang had fought the eunuch, a master of martial arts. Their skills were evenly matched, and after a brief exchange lasting half a cup of tea, both had sustained minor internal injuries. He had finally confirmed that the Emperor was truly terminal. However, he had painstakingly gained the Second Prince’s trust, investing countless efforts for this day. He was on the verge of becoming the most outstanding “chess player” in the world simply by helping the Second Prince overcome his crisis, but now he faced a choice. Although a strategist should not have any worries about the future, being caught in this dilemma still infuriated Chu Dingjiang. This was not merely a simple choice; it was a blatant indication that his plan was not yet comprehensive enough. This time, Wei Yuzhi had revealed his trump card, completely dismantling and dividing the Konghe Army. Chu Dingjiang had anticipated this day, which was why he had Zhu Pianxian go out to do business beforehand. He had also gathered considerable influence, and once separated, Zhu would need money to support him. Most of these people followed Chu Dingjiang not for wealth and status but rather hoping to retire and live ordinary lives after completing this final mission. Chu Dingjiang naturally wanted to prepare a way out for them. This group only accounted for one-fifth of the total number of the Konghe Army. On one side were a large number of highly skilled Konghe Army soldiers, and on the other side was a large army. Dealing with either side individually would be difficult; it was impossible to spare strength to serve both. Chu Dingjiang gazed at the flickering firelight, lost in thought. He needed to make arrangements as soon as possible while there was still time. The plum blossoms in the night air exuded a delicate fragrance. The mist on the lake was even thicker than during the day, completely obscuring the island. A hundred Konghe Army soldiers stood guard on the shore, awaiting orders. More than twenty Konghe Army soldiers slowly advanced towards the island in boats using nets woven from medicinal herbs. Having roamed the martial world for years, the assassins of the Konghe Army were numerous and knowledgeable, and with their specialized intelligence department, they quickly learned that the flowers growing around the island were Dream Flowers. Dealing with this hallucinogenic poisonous flower was tricky but not without solutions; they had already prepared countermeasures. Initially, herbs blocked most of the poisonous gas, but the twenty-odd Konghe Army soldiers dared not relax their guard, carefully navigating the boat to avoid the Dream Flower blossoms. The deeper they went, the more relaxed they felt, an unprecedented sense of comfort enveloping them. Some even began to yawn, and many wore contented smiles as drowsiness crept in. The poison of the Dream Flower was peculiar. Those poisoned initially felt relaxed and comfortable, falling asleep. The poison then began to paralyze the central nervous system, causing hallucinations. Even if they did not turn on each other, they would eventually die from paralysis. Sheng Changying, observing from a high vantage point, breathed a slight sigh of relief. It seemed this Dream Flower had been specially cultivated; its poison could not be countered by ordinary herbs. The islanders took turns resting. Ling Ziyue and Sheng Changying kept watch first, while the rest rested on the first floor. The night passed. No one breached the first line of defense, and the Konghe Army remained silent all day. An Jiu sat on the rooftop, gazing at the sky, fiddling with an arrow. Sui Yuntong prepared dinner and called from the open space below, “Fourteenth, come down for dinner.” An Jiu, pressing against the roof ridge, gracefully leaped down a pillar. “Look!” Lou Xiaowu, holding a bowl of rice, pointed to the sky with her chopsticks. Everyone looked up and saw large birds circling overhead. Upon closer inspection, each “bird” had a person beneath it! “This is an ancient mechanical art,” Lou Xiaowu said, throwing down her bowl and rushing into the house. She grabbed a gun, shoved it into An Jiu’s hand, and urged, “Ah Jiu, shoot them down.” An Jiu gripped the gun, glanced at Ling Ziyue, and chambered a round. Lou Xiaowu, hands on her hips, a few grains of rice clinging to her chubby cheeks, said with satisfaction, “Luckily, we are smart. We are not afraid of anything that flies in the sky, runs on the ground, or swims in the water.” An Jiu held her gun, not pulling the trigger for a long time, waiting for these people to get within range. As the “bird” circled closer and closer, everyone held their breath, not urging her on. Just as the “bird” was about to land, two loud thuds rang out. The “big bird” swayed a few times in the sky, then plummeted to the ground like a kite with a broken string, blood raining down.

chapters.title: Hunter or Prey?
chapters.content: Lou Xiaowu’s gun magazine could only hold ten bullets and could not fire continuously. With limited ammunition, no one could guarantee a hit like An Jiu. The number of “big birds” in the sky was increasing, and one person could not handle it alone. The others had already gripped their sword hilts, ready to join the fight as soon as someone landed. Strangely, the later “big birds,” seeing their comrades shot down, continued to circle overhead. A few breaths later, a white powder mixed with specks of rain fell from the sky, quickly enveloping the entire island. An Jiu took a pill of Hundred Poisons Antidote and pulled up her mask. The island had little else, but the Hundred Poisons Antidote was plentiful. While it could neutralize most poisons, it had little effect on this kind of drug. Sheng Changying was the first to collapse. An Jiu frowned, grabbed him by the back of his collar, and tossed him onto Da Jiu’s back. “Take him to a safe place!” Da Jiu and An Jiu shared a certain degree of telepathy, and Da Jiu roughly understood her meaning. It then carried Sheng Changying and dashed into the forest. It ran to the spot where grass seeds were buried, dug away the withered leaves and soil, dragged Sheng Changying into the pit, and carefully covered him up. Sheng Changying struggled desperately, but Da Jiu swatted him with its paw, rendering him immobile. After Da Jiu left, Sheng Changying struggled to lift his head, finally managing to shake off the loose soil, revealing his nose and mouth, barely able to breathe. Night fell, and a heavy drizzle and fine rain, like a curtain, shimmered with golden light under the lanterns, creating a scene resembling a golden brocade. An Jiu drew her Dragon-Subduing Bow, nocked an arrow, and her mental power surged like a tide, locking onto the positions of the Konghe Army overhead. Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh! Arrows pierced the mist relentlessly, but it was not An Jiu who fired first; it was the Konghe Army above who launched the preemptive barrage. An Jiu released her grip, and the arrow flew like a whirlwind, like thunder. With unstoppable force, it sliced ​​through the mist, colliding with another arrow in mid-air, splitting it in two without diminishing its momentum, and embedding itself directly into the body of a Konghe Army member piloting a “giant bird.” Below, An Jiu immediately dodged the barrage after firing her arrow. Several people inside the house watched the crossbow bolts clattering into the ground outside. Li Qingzhi said, “Looks like they will be landing soon.” In the mist of arrows, Da Jiu, eyes wide, huddled in a grotto, its ears twitching. An arrow landed in front of it, startling it into a sharp pull. “These arrows can generally only fire ten arrows in succession. Even if you carry replacement arrows, there will definitely be time to reload.” An Jiu had spent some time with the Konghe Army and knew their weapons inside and out. She could tell what kind of crossbow they used just by looking at the arrows. “Let’s take this opportunity to occupy a more defensive position.” The Konghe Army rarely conducted such large-scale operations. This time, they were determined to capture the heart’s blood. At this rate, a large number of Konghe Army soldiers would fall on the island in less time than it takes to drink a cup of tea. If they did not surrender, they had no choice but to occupy advantageous positions first. “He has a secret medicine storehouse. Let’s go there first!” An Jiu suggested. Others did not know about Mo Sigui’s medicine storehouse, but An Jiu did. It was not in some secret room but in a small building halfway up a mountain beside a waterfall. “That’s it!” Sui Yuntong said. Just then, the rain of arrows outside indeed subsided a bit. In the fog, only An Jiu could confirm the route. The group rushed out together, and led by An Jiu, they headed towards the medicine storehouse. An Jiu ran while using her mental energy to scan her surroundings for anyone. Avoiding enemies along the way, she soon heard the gurgling sound of flowing water. It was a small waterfall, no more than three feet wide. The current was gentle, and the clear water splashed into the pool below, creating a white spray. Li Qingzhi’s tall frame swayed precariously, but An Jiu caught him and pulled him onto her back. Being carried by such a petite woman was difficult for Li Qingzhi to accept, and he struggled. “Do not move!” An Jiu coldly stopped him. “Save your energy!” Sui Yuntong’s face also paled. “Qingzhi, this is a matter of life and death; do not worry about trivial matters!” Li Qingzhi resignedly pursed his lips, letting An Jiu carry him halfway up the mountain. Ling Ziyue, walking ahead, kicked open the door. The medicine boy hiding inside turned pale, only breathing a sigh of relief upon recognizing him. “What’s wrong with that medicine?” The medicine boy was the only one among them who knew anything about medicine; the others were completely ignorant. If it were just a regular sleeping potion, Hundred Poisons Antidote would not be unable to withstand it. But if it was not a sleeping potion, why did she not feel anything? Her body could resist sleeping potions, but it was not immune to all poisons. “This, I do not know either.” The medicine boy had already noticed the change outside and crawled out from the corner to find the medicine. Because he was often forced by Mo Sigui to personally test medicines, he also had a certain resistance to them, and his body had not shown any abnormalities for the time being. “However, I smelled the scent of Dream Flower mixed in. This medicine might very well destroy Dream Flower, preventing the mist from lingering!” “Would that not also make it inconvenient for the Konghe Army to move around?” Lou Xiaowu lay on the couch, drowsy. Just as the medicine boy was about to speak, a series of deafening roars came from outside, one after another, like thunder shaking the heavens. Even the house built halfway up the mountain was affected, and dust fell from the beams. Lou Xiaowu suddenly laughed, coughing from the dust. “We…cough cough…the firecrackers we made sounded really good.” An Jiu guessed that once the Konghe Army landed on the island, they would definitely look for Mo Sigui’s pharmacy and residence immediately, so during preparations, she had Lou Xiaowu bury many specially modified thunderbolts around Mo Sigui’s pharmacy, their function being equivalent to landmines. The young apprentice was stunned by the loud noise for a while before recovering, “After the Dream Flower was damaged, the poison gas will dissipate quickly.” He dragged a box from the corner, took out the bottles and jars inside, and frowned as he examined them for a long time. “My Lord must have medicine here to cure your poison, but…I cannot find it.” Mo Sigui never had the habit of labeling medicines; he could easily identify the formula by smell. “I was not poisoned; could it be that Gu Jinghong’s heart’s blood worked?” An Jiu took out a medicine bottle. “In any case, taking this stuff is more beneficial than harmful, better than waiting to die.” As she spoke, she gave each person a pill. Lou Xiaowu swallowed the pill. Ling Ziyue held a small pill, smiled helplessly, and swallowed it. Just two hours ago, he had refused the medicine; he had not expected to have to use it so soon. They were the only few capable fighters on the island, and every extra person meant a greater chance of survival. After taking the medicine, the group sat cross-legged and circulated their internal energy. After about half a cup of tea’s time, their complexions improved slightly, and An Jiu, seeing this, felt somewhat relieved. The rain outside grew heavier, pounding against the wooden house with a dull thud. When An Jiu released her full mental energy, it could almost cover the entire island. She knew clearly that dozens of experts from the Konghe Army were already on the island. She had once defeated Piaomiao Mountain Mansion with fewer than ten people, but she had to admit that without Chu Dingjiang, the outcome would have been completely different. An Jiu leaned against the doorframe, silent, her fingers constantly stroking the Tang sword at her side. If they could get an antidote soon, they could fight their way to the ferry to the north and escape by boat. Whether they could leave was still uncertain… The heavy rain outside seemed to cheer on the Konghe Army, quickly dispersing the fog and leaving only a hazy mist. An Jiu suddenly remembered that Da Jiu had taken Sheng Changying to hide and had not returned yet. Thinking of being hunted again, she felt a surge of anger. Her hand, which had been stroking the hilt of her sword, paused and tightened suddenly. She put on her cloak. “You all rest here. I will be right back.” This place was easy to defend and difficult to attack, and with the various potent poisons developed by Mo Sigui and Sui Yuntong and the others having considerable combat experience, An Jiu was not worried. “Where are you going?” The young apprentice, seeing everyone else resting while he was the only one awake, thought that if someone attacked now, the entire army would be wiped out! “Do not worry, the Konghe Army is resting temporarily. No one will come for a while.” An Jiu closed the door, opened the umbrella specially made by Lou Xiaowu, and slowly walked down the mountain. The raindrops fell on the umbrella with muffled thuds. An Jiu’s gaze, calm yet laced with murderous intent, concealed a predatory glint. She was a hunter, not prey fleeing in panic! Continuing this passive path would be no different from her past life. Her advantage lay in her powerful mental strength, easily concealing her location—suitable not only for escaping but also for assassination! Since she was cornered, she might as well stop and fight her way back! Three members of the Konghe Army were approaching from five hundred paces ahead, two at the fifth rank and one at the seventh. An Jiu’s lips, hidden beneath her veil, tightened slightly. She stood still, waiting for the three to approach. The Konghe Army had suffered heavy losses in the recent explosion, and the main force was regrouping. Several squads had been dispatched to search the surrounding area, and this three-man squad was one of them. They knew there were about six or seven people on the island, and their martial arts levels were not very high, so they focused most of their attention on guarding against landmines and poison. An Jiu stood on a horizontal branch, holding an umbrella and watching the three men until they reached the foot of the tree. The three moved with lightning speed, their footsteps barely making a sound as they trod on the decaying leaves. The raindrops that gathered and dripped from An Jiu’s umbrella seemed to be falling more rapidly than elsewhere. The other three, equally alert, noticed the unusual sound of the raindrops on the leaves and looked up, but they were slower than An Jiu. As a string of raindrops slid down the edge of the umbrella, An Jiu abruptly closed it and leaped down, drawing her Tang sword from one hand while pressing a button on the umbrella handle with the other to launch a hidden weapon. Two clusters of silver needles, as thin as cow’s hair, instantly pierced the thigh of the seventh-level expert. He struggled for a moment, then collapsed to his knees. Everything seemed to slow down. Before the raindrops falling from the umbrella even touched the ground, An Jiu’s sword tip was already at the neck of one of the fifth-level martial artists. A thin line of blood instantly appeared on that pale neck. But her sword did not stop; she spun around, blocking another martial artist’s sword. Her hand suddenly loosened, the Tang sword falling to the ground. She moved like the wind, flashing past the opponent’s armpit, her hand, gloved in a rough black glove, grabbing the opponent’s neck and crushing the internal cartilage with a sudden burst of strength. Plop. The raindrops from the umbrella fell onto the withered leaves, mingling with the blood. Three people killed in an instant. The sweet, metallic scent of blood mixed with dampness spread through the air. An Jiu smelled this aroma and suddenly felt excited.

chapters.title: Battle in the Forest (1)
chapters.content: An Jiu slowly exhaled, bent down to pick up her Tang sword, and wiped it clean on the clothes of a nearby corpse. If she had a sniper rifle or a silencer, sniping would be much easier for her. Although the arrows fired from the Dragon-Subduing Bow were faster and more powerful than those from ordinary bows, a sixth- or seventh-level martial artist could still dodge them unless they used their mental power. When An Jiu slowly expanded her mental power, the impact on her meridians was negligible, but the impact of a concentrated attack was dozens of times greater. Now she could control her mental power better, but she could not guarantee absolute safety, so she did not plan to use it to kill unless absolutely necessary. The other group also consisted of three people: an eighth-level, a fifth-level, and a fourth-level individual. An Jiu swung her crossbow and lightly leaped onto a ginkgo tree. The rainy night was pitch black, and An Jiu’s figure was like ink on an inkstone, almost indistinguishable. Even with her excellent eyesight, An Jiu could not clearly see her target under such conditions, so she simply closed her eyes. Without visual interference, her mental perception suddenly became clear. Gradually, An Jiu felt as if she were sinking into the deep sea, surrounded by deathly silence—no sound, no light; she could not even feel herself. The three people to her left were getting closer and closer; their intrusion was like a pebble thrown into this dead sea, ripples spreading outwards. An Jiu’s grip on the Tang sword slowly tightened. At this moment, An Jiu’s world contained nothing but the three prey who had invaded her territory! She crouched down, her muscles tense. They were here! The three people under the tree were on guard. The eighth-level expert among them heard a slight gust of wind overhead and instinctively drew his sword to block, but the light was too dim; he could see almost nothing. When they tried to use their mental power, they found they could not sense anything at all! Just as they hesitated, they heard two muffled groans beside them. The eighth-level martial artist was shocked. Without thinking, he instinctively drew his sword to block. He was an assassin with countless deadly kills under his belt, and even in this situation, he managed to barely withstand An Jiu’s fierce attack. Clang! The two forces clashed, locked in a stalemate for a moment, then separated. In that instant, the eighth-level martial artist saw a pair of cold, dark eyes reflected in the opponent’s shadowy sword light. A chill ran down his spine; it felt as if death itself stood behind him, ready to crush him with a single squeeze. Emerging from his heightened sense of danger, the eighth-level martial artist immediately retreated. However, An Jiu’s sword was like a leech and faster than his retreat! The snow shimmered slightly, reflecting the rain curtain before him. The eighth-level martial artist knew he could not escape. With a determined heart, he gripped his sword with one hand to parry and grabbed the signal flare at his waist with the other. An Jiu swung her umbrella sharply, and sharp blades sprang from its ribs, slicing through the rain. The eighth-level martial artist felt a gust of wind; he could not see what it was, but guessed it was not something he could defeat with a single sword strike, so he hastily retreated. Just when the thing opposite him slowed down and was no longer able to catch him, a sudden chill ran down his back. A sharp blade pierced his chest, and something cold and wet appeared on his neck. The eighth-level martial artist heard a chilling cracking sound from his neck before realizing it was a hand! With his last bit of consciousness and strength, he made one last move—pulling the plug from the signal flare. With a piercing shriek, a bright orb of light grazed the eighth-level martial artist’s body and shot into the sky, instantly charring half of his body. The orb exploded above the forest, bursting into a crimson display.

chapters.title: Battle in the Forest (2)
chapters.content: An Jiu abandoned the corpse and quickly left the scene. The blood-red signal flare abruptly alerted the Konghe Army, who were gathering and resting. “Heaven Branch Class A reinforcements!” the Konghe Army’s Dark Guard of the Capital shouted. The red signal flare indicated an attack by a powerful figure—a desperate situation. The figures of six ninth-level experts from Class A disappeared into the darkness, while the rest of the Konghe Army silently gathered, awaiting further instructions. The Capital’s Dark Guard did not issue any further orders. Shortly afterward, the assassins from Heavenly Class A returned. “My Lord, the entire Mao and Xu teams of the Earth Branch are dead! The signal was made by the Mao team leader.” One assassin succinctly explained the situation, then added, “Of the six, the Xu team leader died from a hidden weapon, and the other two members were killed—one with a sword to the throat, the other with a broken neck; the Mao team leader also had his neck broken, and the other two had their throats slit with a sword.” Another assassin added, “It seems there were no more than three attackers.” Hidden weapons, a sword to the throat, a broken neck—the attacks were swift and decisive, instantly killing six experienced Konghe Army assassins. They could not believe it could be the work of the same person. “Such a master exists on the island!” The Capital’s Dark Guard was slightly surprised. “Increase the number of men in each group to ten and continue the search.” “My Lord, perhaps I should not question orders, but at this point, I cannot help myself,” the leader of the Heaven Branch Class A group asked. “If it is truly to save His Majesty, we would gladly die for him, but is it really the duty of the Konghe Army to spread the news of His Majesty’s serious illness so widely?” If he were already dead, what use was that peerless medicine? If the Konghe Army was truly only after the medicine, no one in the world would dare to challenge the entire Konghe Army so boldly. Their vehement resistance clearly indicated there was more to the story. The Capital’s Dark Guard was well aware of the problem with the order, but what right did he have to question it? “If you know you should not ask, then don’t!” he shouted. The team leader of Class A coldly replied, “My Lord, we may kill, but we are not fools!” The Capital’s Dark Guard angrily retorted, “Am I a fool?! But I have to accept this order! Because His Majesty is truly dying! Do you understand what our fate will be if His Majesty passes away?!” A new Emperor brings a new court. Whether it was the Crown Prince or the Second Prince, they all had their own personal guards. When any of them ascends the throne, their trusted guards would replace the original Konghe Army. These former guards would have to undergo a radical reform; those who obeyed would live, and those who resisted would die. The reforms within the Konghe Army would be different from those of the previous dynasty. They carried the same bloody and ruthless style, where life and death hang by a thread. Those in the upper echelons had been infected with a poison; the new Emperor would use them to purge the lower ranks first, and these very guards would be the first to suffer! Everyone present fell silent. Those unfamiliar with assassins would likely perceive them as a bunch of reckless idiots, but only they themselves understood that the more they kill, the more they cherish their lives, because they understood how fragile life is. Death was like a lamp going out; life was gone. Nothing remains. The team leader of Class A remained silent for a moment, then asked, “Is this medicine guaranteed to save His Majesty?” “Eighty or ninety percent certain,” said the Capital’s Dark Guard. “After all, few have personally witnessed the efficacy of the medicine person’s blood. However, it is recorded in the Chronicles of the Konghe, which is relatively reliable.” He paused, then added, “This medicine person was meticulously raised by the Liao royal family with immense resources. The efficacy of his blood is incomparable to that of ordinary medicine persons.” Having received this result, the assassins, however unwilling, could only follow the Capital’s Dark Guard’s instructions, working in groups of ten to search the island. The Capital’s Dark Guard pulled a box from his pocket. He hesitated for a moment, then handed it to the team leader of Class A. “The insect in this box can smell the blood of a medicine person. Take it…” He had been suspicious when he first accepted the box. It was an insect with a sensitive sense of smell, not uncommon in the martial world but troublesome to use. The insect had to be fed food infused with the scent it needed to track for a period of time before it would become interested. How could the Liao Kingdom’s medicine-training army possibly possess such an insect…? The Capital’s Dark Guard had already guessed that either the Dark Commander or one of the Deputy Dark Commanders was a Liao spy. These two were the top two commanders of the Konghe Army, and the Dark Commander could not find any clues. He decided that once he found the medicine, he would personally deliver it to the palace. The night rain pattered. The forest was shrouded in impenetrable darkness. An Jiu squatted on a tree, recalling the battle that had just taken place. The initial meditative state she entered was incredibly profound, as if she had woven a net with her mental energy. Once the prey entered this net’s area, it could no longer use its own mental energy… This hunting experience was exquisite. An Jiu was still savoring the afterglow of the experience, closing her eyes and slowly dispersing her mental energy. Darkness enveloped her once more. The surrounding mental fluctuations rippled outwards like chaotic waves, clashing and surging. An Jiu frowned, her temples throbbing. She endured for a moment, and when she opened her eyes again, everything was blood red. Twenty martial artists of varying ranks simultaneously stormed into An Jiu’s net. It was as if the prey was too heavy, causing the net to break. In the instant it snapped, she felt as if a needle had pierced her temples, and her eyes stung. Just as An Jiu’s head was spinning with pain, a crossbow bolt pierced the darkness and reached her. An Jiu leaned back, hanging upside down from a tree, the bolt almost grazing her nose. A dozen or so people approached silently, the glint of their swords flashing in the snow. Several more, carrying umbrellas and lanterns, followed, illuminating the scene clearly, revealing An Jiu’s figure. Her petite, slender figure was clad in a sharp, close-fitting outfit; only her bloodshot eyes were visible, a truly terrifying sight. Surrounded by over twenty men, An Jiu felt a mixture of fear and barely suppressed excitement. The weapon in the box began to stir. The team leader of Class A, his heart pounding, spoke up. “We’ve searched high and low, and here it is, without any effort at all. Hand over the medicine person’s blood, or we will be forced to fight.” “It’s Gu Jinghong,” An Jiu corrected sternly. “Gu Jinghong?!” the team leader exclaimed in shock. Gu Jinghong had always held a prominent position on the Konghe List, a name that resonated far and wide. No one had expected that such an invincible assassin was actually someone else’s medicine person! “Whoever it is, hand over the medicine!” The team leader drew his longsword, his entire body radiating murderous intent. This was like a signal; everyone assumed a stance ready to attack! An Jiu stood in the center, a Tang sword in one hand and an umbrella handle in the other. Her vision was blurred by a bloody haze, making it impossible to discern anything. She closed her eyes, and the umbrella slammed open, scattering water droplets and fine silver needles in all directions. “Take it!” With a low roar from the team leader, more than ten men pounced.

chapters.title: He
chapters.content: An Jiu’s mental power, seemingly accumulated over a long period, suddenly exploded, causing the three people closest to her to freeze abruptly. The twin swords swept past like the wind, splattering blood that landed on An Jiu’s head and mask, warm and sticky. The rich, sweet-smelling stench and the vivid crimson blood stimulated the fury deep within An Jiu’s soul. Her already powerful mental power instantly erupted like a snow-capped mountain collapsing; her chilling killing intent poured into the swords. A burst of white light flashed, like a giant wave churning up thousands of piles of snow, leaving only the sound of blades tearing through clothing and flesh. Under the crushing force of An Jiu’s ferocious mental power, even a ninth-level expert found it extremely difficult. A fourth-level martial artist turned deathly pale, watching helplessly as the blades approached, unable to move a muscle! An Jiu’s vision was blurred by blood; the world she saw shrouded in crimson. At close range, she could clearly see the pairs of eyes, filled with fear and ruthlessness, within the blood-soaked scene—the same eyes her father had when he died. Under normal circumstances, with wolves still present, her sword would have hesitated. But now, soaked in blood and severed limbs, only one word occupied her mind—kill! Destroying those eyes filled her with boiling blood, an overwhelming sense of exhilaration. In this moment, she felt as if she had returned to the days and nights in the training camp, hacking and slashing, endless hacking and slashing, using this method to vent the pent-up frustration and strange excitement within her. All the assassins of the Konghe Army had experienced life-or-death battles, but looking at this woman with bloodshot eyes and overwhelming killing intent, they felt for the first time that they were so close to death! The Konghe Army clearly had not expected to encounter such a formidable enemy. They rarely fought in groups like this, and their initial coordination was somewhat clumsy. After several exchanges, at great cost, they finally found their rhythm. “Do not panic! Concentrate your mental energy!” the team leader of Class A shouted. Mental strength was not invincible. Like physical combat, if one person could not defeat another, they could use sheer numbers. The team leader refused to believe that the killing intent emanating from dozens or even hundreds of assassins would be defeated by a woman! Even if she was a Transcendent Realm cultivator! Confirming that the heart’s blood was on this woman, the team leader immediately issued a yellow signal. Shortly afterward, rustling footsteps echoed through the forest, dense and numerous, like countless insects. The Konghe Army from all sides converged on this location. The Capital’s Dark Guard arrived first, glancing at the battle situation with a hint of surprise. “Transcendent Realm!” The team leader approached him. “My Lord, the medicine we need is on this woman. However, she is a Transcendent Realm cultivator.” The Capital’s Dark Guard stared intently for a long time, then relaxed slightly. “She is injured. Order everyone to attack with mental strength!” During An Jiu’s second assassination attempt, she inadvertently discovered that she could weave a net with mental strength. While experimenting, a large group of assassins broke into her territory, destroying the mental strength net and causing her to suffer a backlash from the mental strength. Normally, in such a situation, her mental strength would quickly deplete. After receiving the order, the assassins did not rush forward. Instead, they surrounded her, using their mental strength to pressure An Jiu! At this moment, An Jiu no longer felt fatigued. However, with the pressure of numerous powerful mental attacks, she gradually felt like a trapped beast caught in a net. If she did not find a way to break free, she was destined to die here. Meanwhile, more than ten crossbowmen aimed at An Jiu. External cultivation differed from internal cultivation. Internal cultivators with profound internal strength could form a protective aura around their bodies, protecting their relatively fragile bodies. External cultivators, however, had undergone repeated and brutal tempering, making their bodies inherently resistant to attack. An Jiu clearly had not reached this level; otherwise, her meridians would not have been unable to withstand the onslaught of her own mental strength. Fortunately, the Konghe Army surrounding her dared not be distracted for even a moment and were unaware of the crossbowmen ready to fire. Their encirclement of An Jiu actually protected her. As the Konghe Army employed its delaying tactics, An Jiu’s mental strength noticeably weakened, and the assassins launching mental attacks around her gradually found it less strenuous than before. An Jiu mechanically wielded her Tang sword, without any superfluous movements; every strike was designed to injure. Her wounds multiplied, the blood seeping from them soaking her black, tight-fitting clothes, obscuring the extent of her bleeding. By now, An Jiu had long forgotten why she fought. In her memory, surrender meant death or lifelong imprisonment, so she had never had the habit of surrendering. The Capital’s Dark Guard, seeing the tide of battle turn, slightly relaxed his tightly furrowed brows. Everyone thought that surrounding and killing An Jiu was only a matter of time, but at that moment, another powerful mental force suddenly pierced through the battle. An Jiu seemed encouraged; her gradually waning killing intent suddenly surged again, and her swordplay became fierce. A sudden gust of night wind swept through the forest, and a figure in a black robe appeared on the wind, landing beside An Jiu in the blink of an eye. An Jiu’s consciousness had long been consumed by excited killing intent, but at the moment Chu Dingjiang arrived, she surprisingly regained some clarity. “Chu Dingjiang!” Others might not recognize the figure, but the Capital’s Dark Guard recognized him immediately. “It is indeed I,” Chu Dingjiang’s deep voice came from beneath his hood. The Capital’s Dark Guard’s expression changed drastically upon seeing his movements. “You are going to protect this woman?” Apart from the Dark Commander, no one in the entire Konghe Army could surpass Chu Dingjiang in skill, not even him. Chu Dingjiang had reached the Transcendent Realm several years ago. Before that, he had remained unknown, and even after being promoted to Divine Martial Commander, he had not achieved much, instead being constantly pressured. The only time he truly demonstrated the terrifying strength of a Transcendent Realm expert was when he, with only a few men, wiped out the entire Piaomiao Mountain mansion. After this incident, the Emperor gradually began to rely on him. How much of a role could those rookies from the Konghe Academy play? No one doubted that even without them, Chu Dingjiang could still complete the mission. The presence of two experts at the Transcendent Realm caused everyone present to back down, resulting in a stalemate. “As you can see,” Chu Dingjiang said slowly, drawing his ancient-looking sword from his waist. The Capital’s Dark Guard was extremely wary of him, unsure whether he was there to protect the woman or to seize the rare elixir. He probed, “If you’ve come for her, hand over the medicinal blood, and we will immediately withdraw from the island. If you’ve come for the elixir…” “What?” Chu Dingjiang’s tone rose slightly, his palpable killing intent radiating outwards as the most direct threat. The Capital’s Dark Guard was a master with one foot in the Transcendent Realm. If the two were to truly fight, their strength would be evenly matched. He simply did not know that Chu Dingjiang’s power had declined considerably; otherwise, he would not have allowed himself to be threatened by his subordinate! “Then you are a traitor, deserving of death by everyone!” The Capital’s Dark Guard’s leg and waist muscles tensed, ready to fight at any moment. “You will obtain neither the woman nor the medicine, for His Majesty passed away half an hour ago.” Chu Dingjiang casually dropped this bombshell, speaking calmly and deliberately. “Indeed, martial artists crave rare medicines, but I hope you will weigh the advantages and disadvantages carefully.” “Really?!” The Capital’s Dark Guard sensed something was wrong. Chu Dingjiang chuckled lightly, “Otherwise, would you think I’ve lost all my courage to oppose my superior?”

chapters.title: Love
chapters.content: If it were not for the Emperor’s passing, the Capital’s Dark Guard would not have imagined such a possibility. When Chu Dingjiang spoke, he already believed it to a great extent. Upon hearing the news, the crowd felt both joy and worry. They were joyful because they were no longer in the palace and had a chance to escape if they received the news early. They were worried because their blood carried a special scent that made them easy to track. If the new Emperor ascended the throne and pursued the rebels, how confident were they in withstanding the pursuit? Chu Dingjiang was prepared. He untied a fist-sized cloth bag from his waist. “There’s a medicine here that can mask the scent of poison. This will save you all from the court’s pursuit. We are all in the same boat; why make things difficult for each other?” “Is it useful?” The Capital’s Dark Guard was somewhat tempted. “To be honest, I brought a group of people from the Konghe Army. If this problem is not solved, why would they be willing to betray us?” Chu Dingjiang waved the bag in his hand and tossed it to the Capital’s Dark Guard. “Please distribute it to everyone, My Lord.” The Capital’s Dark Guard handed the bag to a black-clad man beside him.
