The man opened his cloth bag, took out a pill, sniffed it lightly, and nodded to the Capital’s Dark Guard after a moment. The Capital’s Dark Guard was the third-in-command of the Konghe Army, but his position was vastly different from that of the Dark Commander and Deputy Dark Commander. His work was extremely demanding, and some important missions even required his personal involvement, like now… Despite possessing vast wealth, he had no time to spend it. Approaching forty, he remained alone. He had been intimate with several women in the Konghe Army, but female assassins forbade pregnancy; he had been forced to abort once. Without an heir, his best fate was to turn to ashes, his soul hanging on the eaves of the Konghe Army, or face endless slaughter in this eternal night. With this pill, whether the Emperor had died or not was no longer so important. The Capital’s Dark Guard weighed the situation briefly and quickly made up his mind, “Let’s go!” Some hesitated, but even the Capital’s Dark Guard retreated. The disparity in strength between the two sides made it impossible to obtain the miraculous medicine; it was better to take what they were confident of obtaining! A wise person knew when to yield; after a brief struggle, those people quickly followed suit and retreated. While Chu Dingjiang was negotiating, An Jiu remained vigilant, expending considerable effort to calm herself. Seeing the crisis averted, An Jiu relaxed slightly, bracing herself with her twin swords on the ground and exhaling. She asked, “Is the Emperor really dead?” “No,” Chu Dingjiang reached out to support her. An Jiu smiled. “I guessed so.” The Dark Capital’s commander would believe it firstly because Chu Dingjiang had betrayed them, secondly because they had the medicine to conceal the scent, and thirdly because even if the Emperor was not dead, his days were numbered. Taking advantage of the chaos to escape was the best strategy! Not taking the readily available path would surely bring divine retribution. Subduing the enemy without fighting. Chu Dingjiang conserved his energy; unlike An Jiu, he did not enjoy killing. The two sat down on a protruding tree root to rest. An Jiu closed her eyes and leaned against his arm. “Chu Dingjiang, the Emperor is dying; the Song Dynasty must be in chaos, right? Is the Second Prince not busy?” Chu Dingjiang paused slightly. “Not busy.” It was not that he was not busy, but rather that the situation was extremely critical! Since ancient times, the victor was the king, and the loser was the villain. For the Second Prince, one step forward was the pinnacle; one step back was an abyss. Chu Dingjiang had struggled internally for several hours but ultimately chose to consider both sides. Whether the Second Prince could successfully take over the empire was up to fate. As for An Jiu, he had come personally, determined to ensure her safety. “I am still too late.” Chu Dingjiang’s warm hand covered her eyes, roughly guessing that her mental energy had just been severely damaged. “Not too early, not too late.” An Jiu snuggled closer to him, a smile playing on her lips. “You always seem to appear out of nowhere when I am feeling overwhelmed. At this rate, my adaptability will only get worse.” “Then let me handle it.” Chu Dingjiang lowered his head and kissed her forehead. “I rarely make promises, but since I said I’d protect you, I will do everything in my power. Even if one day I cannot keep up, at least we can fight side by side.” “Go back.” An Jiu opened her eyes and tilted her head back to kiss his lips. Neither of them wanted to go any deeper, yet they felt their souls intertwined, drawing warmth from each other amidst the blood and corpses. Ending the long, shallow kiss, Chu Dingjiang scooped her up in his arms. “Wait a minute; the Konghe Army just retreated. I am worried.” An Jiu did not answer, her eyes closed as if she were asleep. Chu Dingjiang used his mental power to locate the others on the island and then took An Jiu there. Ling Ziyue had finished his meditation and was watching over the others who were still meditating when he suddenly noticed a black-robed man in the room. He tensed up, almost striking with his sword, but relaxed when he saw An Jiu. “Is she alright?” he asked. Chu Dingjiang placed An Jiu on the couch, found the medicine bottle on her person, poured out a pill, and fed it to her. “She’s fine; she will be fine after some rest.” Ling Ziyue felt ashamed looking at An Jiu, who was covered in blood. They were all men here, and a woman had taken the lead. “General Ling, do not overthink it,” Chu Dingjiang said, turning around and seeing Ling Ziyue’s expression. He roughly guessed what he was thinking. “Ah Jiu deliberately provoked the hundred-odd Konghe Army soldiers; otherwise, she would not be injured like this…” “It was an accident,” An Jiu suddenly interrupted him. Chu Dingjiang frowned, his anger rising. “If I had not come, a serious accident would have indeed occurred.” An Jiu subtly pursed her lips. “Based on general circumstances, I would have single-handedly wiped out over a hundred people. Your appearance disrupted everything.” “Whose plan?” Chu Dingjiang wanted nothing more than to drag her out of bed and beat her. “Did this plan even consider the consequences?” “It did!” An Jiu defiantly opened one eye, looking at him. “Even if we all perished, it would be a guaranteed win.” Dying while taking over a hundred people down with her—that was certainly worthwhile, An Jiu genuinely thought. “You just die so cleanly, and then I cannot even find anyone to avenge you! Have you considered my feelings?” Chu Dingjiang was truly enraged this time. He had even put his ideals below hers, rushing over to put out the fire at a crucial moment—was this how she treated him? An Jiu thought seriously for a moment, and seeing his burning anger, she carefully said, “It’s not certain we can kill them all; there will definitely be remnants…” So do not worry about not finding anyone to avenge me! Chu Dingjiang immediately deflated, knowing that if she did not want to understand, all his arguing would be useless. “You’ve thought it through. Go and rest!” An Jiu closed her eyes contentedly. Although she said those words this time, she understood Chu Dingjiang’s feelings deeply and cherished them in her heart. She gradually understood her mother’s state of mind back then. Her father used her as an experiment, and she endured it time and time again without resistance, not because of cowardice, but because she was somewhat willing. Love made people blind.

chapters.title: Candy
chapters.content: Sometimes, even knowing the unpredictable dangers of love, one still could not help but sink deeper, experiencing both anxiety and enjoyment. This was probably a common mentality among women, especially those who had had painful pasts. An Jiu had heard her mother say that they had also had a passionate love affair, but in the end, her father poured all his passion into his career, while her mother remained deeply in love. The cruelest love was not about mutual destruction, separation by death, or gradual fading into indifference and going their separate ways; it was about one person pulling away while the other continued to sink deeper. An Jiu had not experienced it firsthand, but as an observer, she saw it more clearly, which was why she feared repeating her mother’s mistakes. But… It seemed the harder she struggled, the faster she sank! Chu Dingjiang sat by the bed, staring at her slightly trembling eyelashes, unable to guess what she was thinking and unable to offer any comfort. After sitting for over an hour, and with everyone else in the room having finished their breathing exercises, Chu Dingjiang checked An Jiu’s pulse, confirming that her injuries were slowly healing, and then prepared to leave. In that hour, everything in Bianjing might have already been decided, but he still wanted to go and see, after all, it was the result of his hard work. Before arriving at Mei Mansion, Chu Dingjiang had been struggling internally. This was the only time in both his lives that he had agonized over making a decision. In his previous life, he had many successes, but also many failures and regrets. He was about to make up for those regrets, yet he was being forced to give them up! Sitting on the roof of the Second Prince’s residence, Chu Dingjiang thought a lot. If he truly abandoned his feelings for his ideals or family responsibilities, how would he be any different from his previous life? Having spent half his life wandering, he had tasted the bitterness of loneliness. Now that a relationship was before him, he should cherish it while he could! “Ah Jiu,” Chu Dingjiang gently stroked her hand, whispering, “Look at this peaceful moment; I wish time could stand still. I do not yearn for eternity, but I do yearn for the next life. Do not think too much or too far ahead; at least in this moment, everything is real.” The others, standing outside, heard this murmur, and their expressions varied. Sui Yuntong, Li Qingzhi, Lou Xiaowu, and the others did not seem particularly moved, but Ling Ziyue was suddenly filled with bitterness. If he had to name the person he had wronged most in his life, it would undoubtedly be his wife! She married him, bore him children, managed the household, and died for him, yet he could not even see her one last time before she died. Whenever he thought of this, Ling Ziyue was filled with immense pain. Chu Dingjiang’s casual remark not only touched Ling Ziyue but also echoed An Jiu’s earlier worries. “Alright.” An Jiu opened her eyes and saw his face buried in his beard. “You still look better this way.” “You mean I have to cover my face like this?” Chu Dingjiang feigned anger. An Jiu said lazily, “It’s rare to meet someone as self-aware as you.” Chu Dingjiang reached out and ruffled her hair, then pulled his hood up, instantly covering most of his face, leaving only his bearded chin visible. “I am leaving.” “Take some chestnuts with you when you come back.” An Jiu did not want to say things like “Be careful” or “Return safely.” She preferred this nonchalant attitude, as if whatever earth-shattering things he did were as simple as drinking a cup of tea. “Alright.” Chu Dingjiang smiled and turned to leave. The parting seemed swift and decisive, but as Chu Dingjiang reached the doorway of the outer room, he sensed the emanating mental energy. He raised his voice and shouted, “Behave yourself!” His voice was infused with a bit of internal energy, causing everyone to tremble. An Jiu wiggled her toes and turned her head towards the wall. She said disdainfully, “What’s so great about that?” Lou Xiaowu huddled in the corner, clutching her blanket. “It was so scary! It scared us to death!” “Please do not defend others. I was not scared at all,” the medicine boy retorted. Lou Xiaowu blinked, her eyes watery one moment, and then she made a face at him and roared like a tiger, “Roar!” The medicine boy instinctively shrank back. Lou Xiaowu snorted triumphantly, then glanced at Ling Ziyue’s gloomy face. She instantly felt the oppressive atmosphere and quietly moved towards the inner room, clutching her blanket. She stopped just before entering, lowered her head, and pretended to be invisible, crouching down beside Ling Ziyue, wrapping herself tightly in the blanket, only her face showing. She sat quietly for a long time, until everyone else had left. Finally, after a long pause, Lou Xiaowu managed to squeeze out a question: “Do you want some candy?” Ling Ziyue did not look at her, only shook his head. Lou Xiaowu rummaged around in her pocket for a while, finally pulling out a piece of candy and handing it to him. “My sister says eating candy makes you feel better.” “Lou Mingyue?” Having spent some time with Lou Xiaowu, Ling Ziyue had heard the name “Lou Mingyue” most often from her. “No, my older sister. She fell off a cliff during the trials at the Konghe Academy.” Lou Xiaowu’s expression darkened. “We really are sisters; our martial arts talent is both terrible!” Ling Ziyue did not know what to say, so he simply took the candy from her hand and put it in his mouth. The dried fruit was coated in maltose, and the sweetness was tinged with a tartness that stimulated every cell in his body, seemingly driving away much of his pain. “It worked, did it not?” Lou Xiaowu, sensitive to his change in mood, instantly smiled brightly. “Hmm, no wonder you like candy.” Ling Ziyue patted her head. “You’ve got cavities, have you not?” Lou Xiaowu quickly covered her mouth, her eyes filled with surprise, as if to say, “How did you know?” Then Ling Ziyue told her something that shocked her even more: “I have keen hearing, and I live not far from you. Every night around midnight, I hear a crunching sound. At first, I thought it was a mouse, but one time I followed the sound and saw you squatting in the corner, stuffing candy into your mouth.” Ling Ziyue’s story was not entirely true. He was not attracted by the crunching sound, but rather by Lou Xiaowu’s crying. Lou Xiaowu had a nightmare; she had gotten up with tears in her eyes, sobbing and munching on candy. Through a hole in the window paper, Ling Ziyue saw this usually innocent and carefree girl in the corner, like a mouse stealing food or like an abandoned child. From then on, Ling Ziyue, wanting to take better care of her, became closer to her. Lou Xiaowu leaned closer to him nervously, lowering her voice, “You have not told anyone, have you?” Ling Ziyue, chewing on a candy, raised an eyebrow and asked, “Why not tell others?” “You know, I am the head of the Lou family now, and I have to act like one.” Lou Xiaowu looked at him seriously and nervously. “You will not tell anyone, will you?” Ling Ziyue was silent for a moment, then asked instead, “Do you resent the Second Young Lady Lou?” Lou Mingyue had gone off to settle scores, leaving the heavy burden on the childlike shoulders of Lou Xiaowu. Lou Xiaowu took out a piece of candy and popped it into her mouth. “Auntie manages the family affairs; I only hold the title, and my martial arts are poor. I cannot avenge the family, so what’s there to resent?”

chapters.title: I am a Mushroom
chapters.content: Seeing Lou Xiaowu’s earnestness, Ling Ziyue could not bear to remind her that there was another person in the room. An Jiu lay on the bed, pretending not to exist. “As the head of the family, you’ve done very well,” Ling Ziyue encouraged her. Lou Xiaowu pulled the blanket down further, resting her chin on her hand, and said, “Do not comfort me. I know I have not done well. If it were not for Aunt, Second Sister would not have entrusted the family to me. But I am trying.” Lou Xiaowu leaned closer to him and whispered, “I’ve made many kinds of weapons. As long as the imperial army uses these weapons, it will definitely help in crushing the Liao Kingdom!” There was an old saying: those with nothing to lose were fearless. If the imperial court could not stand tall and lacked ruthlessness on the battlefield, the country could only be manipulated by others. With the people’s hearts weakened, even the most powerful weapons were like a child wielding a sturdy bow—ultimately just decorations. Having guarded the border for so many years, Ling Ziyue understood this deeply. But looking at Lou Xiaowu’s warm, sunny smile, he swallowed the words he was about to say, instead saying, “Well, then you must do your best!” An Jiu sensed the encouragement and helplessness in Ling Ziyue’s tone. Considering the state of the entire Song Dynasty, a small flame quietly ignited in her heart—was it anger, or perhaps—hope? She could accurately kill her targets, yet she was also wanted worldwide, living a life of constant hiding. She was the most formidable sniper and also a vulnerable person living in the shadows. Therefore, she understood better than anyone the thrill of being an arbiter and the stifling struggle of living in the dirtiest corners. Perhaps, from this moment on, she had finally found the meaning of life! An Jiu’s mental strength was injured, much weaker than usual, but her eyes shone with an unprecedented brightness. It turned out that life was more exciting only through constant pursuit. What she had always wanted deep down was not simply to retire and herd sheep! She wanted to change, to change her current situation. To live a more carefree and unrestrained life. In the past, whenever An Jiu hovered on the brink of life and death, she always longed for a peaceful life. But now, with a tranquil life laid out before her, she did not feel the ecstatic joy she had imagined, nor did she feel any satisfaction. She even doubted her own greed, wondering if she could never erase the ingrained dependence on killing deep within her blood and soul. Therefore, she felt conflicted and lost. However, only today did An Jiu finally understand—without breaking the shackles of her heart, even if she obtained the shepherding life she desired, it would only be shepherding sheep in chains. Like a prisoner laboring, there would be no enjoyment, so where would joy come from? “I do not want to be a rat, and my country cannot be a rat either…” An Jiu’s murmur grew louder and louder, finally bursting into unrestrained laughter. “I am not a rat! Hahaha! I am not a rat!” One must all live under the bright sunlight, towards hope, towards the future. Marching forward with triumphant songs! So this was the life she had always longed for. An Jiu’s laughter echoed through the plum blossoms. Lou Xiaowu and Ling Ziyue exchanged bewildered glances. Sui Yuntong rushed in carrying a freshly prepared meal, his face pale. “Fourteenth has had another attack?” Just then, An Jiu appeared in the doorway. Leaning against the doorframe, she looked at him with a broad smile. “I’ve decided! I do not want to be a rat, nor will I be a shepherd rat!” “Oh no!” Lou Xiaowu nervously grabbed Ling Ziyue’s sleeve, whispering, “Fourteenth’s condition seems worse. Before, her attacks were just minor tantrums, but this time she actually thinks she’s a rat! A shepherd rat at that!” The three of them stared intently at An Jiu. An eerie silence fell over the room. “Not from the same world, they really do not understand me,” An Jiu thought. If Chu Dingjiang were here, he would understand what she was saying. He would also understand how happy and excited she was at this moment. An Jiu did not explain, waved her hand, and hummed a little tune as she went out. “Fourteenth, where are you going?” Sui Yuntong asked hurriedly. “I am going out to get some sun.” Such a beautiful and memorable day deserved to be bathed in the bright sunlight. Sui Yuntong did not dare stop her, watching her go out, then turned to the other two and said, “She knows it is raining outside, right?” “Perhaps she forgot?” Ling Ziyue noticed a difference in her demeanor compared to her usual madness. “It’s over.” Lou Xiaowu was on the verge of tears, worriedly saying, “Fourteenth thinks she’s a shepherd’s rat, from a different world than us. She wants to go out in the sun on a rainy day, and to make matters worse, she sang!” “What should we do?” Sui Yuntong was completely convinced that An Jiu had gone mad again. Ling Ziyue remained cautious, offering a reliable suggestion, “We cannot forcefully subdue her, so let’s focus on gentle methods. Xiaowu seems the most harmless; try approaching and comforting her. If things get bad, prioritize your own safety.” Sui Yuntong thought about it carefully. An Jiu had not hurt anyone since her madness and sometimes even recognized them, so he agreed with this approach. Lou Xiaowu gritted her teeth, got up without hesitation, wrapped herself in the blanket, and moved outside. After An Jiu went outside, she saw misty rain and realized it had been raining during the battle. She had been so excited that she had forgotten. Regretful, but not in a bad mood, she simply squatted in the thatched hut in front of the house to watch the rain. From there, she could overlook most of the island; all the scenery was half-hidden behind the mist, appearing and disappearing like a traditional Chinese ink painting. Lou Xiaowu heard An Jiu humming something she could not understand and was worried that she would not be able to communicate since she did not understand rat language. With a nervous heart, she squatted down beside An Jiu, nervously preparing her words. An Jiu knew Lou Xiaowu had arrived. After waiting for a while without hearing her speak, she turned around and looked at her suspiciously. Lou Xiaowu quickly introduced herself. “I…I am a mushroom.” An Jiu was taken aback. Seeing her adorable appearance, she felt both curious and wanted to tease her. “Why can mushrooms talk?” Lou Xiaowu was secretly pleased; it seemed there was no language barrier. At the same time, she racked her brains to come up with a lie. As a researcher, she always pursued the truth and was a good, honest girl; she was completely clueless about making up stories. “This…this…I am actually a mushroom spirit. I absorb the mental energy of heaven and earth, the essence of the sun and moon here…so…and then…and then…and then…and then…and then…” Lou Xiaowu’s little face turned bright red. The thatched hut was not far from the pharmacy. The two people inside, hearing her words, could not help but facepalm. “Anyway, do not be afraid; I am a good person!” Lou Xiaowu solemnly assured her, her expression serious, as if she were about to swear an oath to the heavens if An Jiu said she did not believe her. “Are you a mushroom or a person?” An Jiu suppressed a laugh and continued to tease her. Lou Xiaowu immediately deflated, her head drooping. “You figured it out. I am actually human, but I am a good person.” An Jiu nodded. “What is it? Tell me.” “Do you not want to be a rat? Do you want to be human?” Lou Xiaowu’s face was full of worry, but she still seemed innocent when she asked this question. An Jiu raised an eyebrow, her expression neither confirming nor denying. Lou Xiaowu did not think twice, taking it as a yes. “Then do you want to be friends with someone?” Seeing An Jiu’s lack of answer, she tempted her. “I have candy!” After fumbling around for a while, she pulled out a piece of candy and handed it to An Jiu. Inside the house, Sui Yuntong muttered with a wry smile, “This child is quite strategic.” Ling Ziyue stood by the window, watching the two girls in the thatched hut with a smile. Putting everything else aside, this scene was so pure that it could not be more innocent. Having seen so much killing and treachery, Ling Ziyue found what he was seeing at this moment exceptionally precious. An Jiu picked up a candy, remembering Lou Xiaowu saying that eating candy would improve her mood. She did not mind making herself happier, so she smiled and popped it into her mouth. Lou Xiaowu was now convinced An Jiu was having an episode. An Jiu would never smile so much when she was normal. She seemed very easygoing and friendly now, but something felt off. She could not help but miss the cold-faced, barbed person she knew. Perhaps because her conversation with Ling Ziyue had touched a raw nerve, Lou Xiaowu was now particularly sensitive and vulnerable. Overcome by grief, she suddenly could not keep up the act anymore. She hugged An Jiu tightly and burst into tears. “Fourteenth, please do not give up on treatment! Xiaowu does not have many relatives or friends left in this world. Second Sister risked her life for revenge; Auntie will spend the rest of her life bearing the burden of the family’s survival. Xiaowu has no one to talk to! You have to take your medicine and get better soon, waaaaah…”

chapters.title: So Close
chapters.content: Even if An Jiu had always been a normal person, she and Lou Xiaowu would never have become close friends; they were two different kinds of people. Some people may not always understand what you were thinking, but they would always be there for you through life’s joys and sorrows—that was what true family and friends are. “I am not sick, and maybe I will not be sick anymore.” An Jiu stroked Lou Xiaowu’s head, her voice drowned out by her sobs. Like last night’s close-quarters battle, in the past, her consciousness might have been consumed by murderous intent, but last night, although she could feel the excitement in her soul and blood, she remained conscious from beginning to end—something that had never happened before. Sui Yuntong, seeing An Jiu’s demeanor, gradually relaxed, sat down, and poured a glass of water. “I wonder what the situation is outside.” “What do you mean?” Ling Ziyue turned to look at him. Sui Yuntong took a sip of water and smiled, “General Ling, do not play dumb. If His Majesty were still well, the Konghe Army would not be in such chaos. Since they dare to spread rumors that His Majesty’s time is near, it is highly likely that he really is going to die. Do you think the Crown Prince and the Second Prince can sit idly by?” “Last night in Bianjing…sigh!” Ling Ziyue could imagine what Bianjing had gone through in such a short time, feeling both worried and excited. “Change is always a good thing.” A sudden change on the path to decline and death—a change of good or bad—could accelerate demise, or it could be a rebirth. At this moment, the tightness in Ling Ziyue’s chest suddenly dissipated considerably. Hearing Lou Xiaowu’s clear sobs outside, Sui Yuntong lowered his eyes to stare at his reflection in the cup and, unusually gossipy, remarked, “Xiaowu is very dependent on the General. If the General could be with her…” “There is no General anymore,” Ling Ziyue said calmly. “I am a few years older than you. If you do not mind, call me Big Brother.” “Big Brother Ling,” Sui Yuntong readily agreed. Ling Ziyue hummed in agreement, then remained silent for a moment. “Xiaowu… deserves someone better. I am old enough to be her father. Let’s not talk about this again.” Ling Ziyue had already betrayed his wife. Even if he felt unworthy of Lou Xiaowu, and even if a woman of equal standing appeared before him, he would not entertain any thoughts. “I, Ling, will only ever have one wife in this life.” Sui Yuntong looked up at him with a smile, his long, narrow eyes clear and bright, as if he could see right into his heart. Ling Ziyue turned his head away, avoiding his gaze. Sui Yuntong understood. Ling Ziyue was an upright man. If his thoughts were as he spoke, he would not have such a calm tone. He would certainly have been furious. His reaction was probably due to guilt. He might even have felt that having those feelings for Lou Xiaowu was utterly despicable. Sui Yuntong looked at the tall figure before him. When he first met Ling Ziyue, he stood at the border in armor, like a towering mountain, unshakeable by anyone. Now, he was much thinner. His brows were furrowed with weariness and melancholy, a completely different person from before. Sometimes, Sui Yuntong felt they should not have saved Ling Ziyue. For him, perhaps dying under the corruption of the court was better than living a life of ignominy. Given Ling Ziyue’s situation, living required more courage than dying, and he was undoubtedly a very strong man. Even trapped in the abyss of regret and hatred, he had never considered suicide. His only purpose in living was to wait for the day he could return to the front lines and lead his troops into the capital! “The food’s here!” Li Qingzhi roared, pulling everyone out of their reverie. Li Qingzhi and the medicine boy, dressed in straw raincoats, entered the house, a thin layer of condensation clinging to the food box. An Jiu and Lou Xiaowu also returned. Li Qingzhi, oblivious to their unease, pulled off his raincoat, rubbed his hands together, and opened the food box. “Today, I, Old Li, have personally cooked! Come and try it. While on the island, my martial arts have not improved, but my cooking skills have certainly taken off!” An Jiu picked up a strip of meat and popped it into her mouth, smacking her lips. “Congratulations.” Li Qingzhi grinned honestly. “With two more years of hard work, you will be able to make something edible,” An Jiu encouraged, patting his shoulder. Seeing her pick up a bowl, Li Qingzhi snatched it away. “Hey! With your temper, how dare you complain about my cooking? If you cannot eat it, do not eat it!” “Your temper has definitely grown,” An Jiu said, picking up another bowl. “Who said I wanted vegetables? Did you steam that rice?” The rice was steamed by Sui Yuntong. Li Qingzhi did not say anything, but he pinched a few shredded pieces of meat and tasted them, saying with a displeased expression, “It tastes very good!” “Fourteenth’s appetite has been spoiled by Lord Chu. Brother Li, do not take it to heart,” Lou Xiaowu said fairly, but then she innocently raised a finger. “Fourteenth is exaggerating. You do not need two years. I think Brother Li can make something edible in just one year!” “Pfft!” Sui Yuntong sprayed rice all over the table. Noticing Li Qingzhi’s murderous glare, he silently turned away, bowl in hand. “Truth is like a knife, innocence kills without a trace,” Ling Ziyue remarked slightly, picking up his bowl and eating heartily. Li Qingzhi felt aggrieved, but looking at Lou Xiaowu’s still swollen eyes and her sincere “I have high hopes for you” expression, he wondered if getting angry would be too much. Apart from the medicine boy and Li Qingzhi, everyone else was just eating plain rice. Li Qingzhi rarely encountered someone who would support him, so he immediately found the medicine boy particularly pleasing and kept piling food onto his plate, saying, “Little Yao, you are growing, eat more!” The medicine boy mumbled a reply and stuffed mouthfuls of rice into his mouth, making Li Qingzhi’s heart swell with joy and a great sense of accomplishment. Sui Yuntong, seeing this, was slightly worried. Li Qingzhi was a genius in the world of dark cuisine; his dishes were comparable to poison. The first few times Li Qingzhi cooked, they did not take it seriously, thinking it was just a little unpalatable. As a qualified assassin, what had he not endured? But after eating, they either vomited and had diarrhea or felt weak all over; in short, everything felt wrong. “Little Yao, is it all right to eat so much?” Sui Yuntong asked. Li Qingzhi glared, “What do you mean?!” “Worrying about nothing. Even when Mo Sigui feeds him poison, he eats with the same death-defying attitude.” An Jiu lowered her eyes, picking at the rice grains. “Fourteenth Young Lady!” Li Qingzhi was furious, ready to explode at any moment. “Little Yao, tell me! Is it good or not?” The boy finished eating, put the bowl on the table, wiped his mouth, and said, “It’s great! Before Master left, he specifically told me to seize every opportunity to learn while he’s away. Do not worry, I will definitely concoct the antidote for Brother Li’s dish in three days!” The boy vowed confidently. Li Qingzhi abruptly stood up and strode out. At the door, he turned back, his face dark, and took his unfinished bowl with him. “Hmm,” An Jiu said slowly, “It seems something’s missing…” “Changying and Da Jiu!” Sui Yuntong exclaimed in surprise, “Go find them quickly!” The group went out to search for the man and tiger, who had been forgotten for a day and a night. In a small border town between the Liao and Song dynasties, thick, dark clouds seemed almost within reach. A bolt of lightning, like a winding dragon, flashed through the clouds, paused for a moment, and then a deafening clap of thunder roared. A few pedestrians on the street began to run. The raindrops pattered on the stone slabs, blooming like tiny flowers. “Quickly, put away the lanterns!” the innkeeper shouted at the attendant. A window in a second-floor room was pushed open a crack. Rain pattered against the windowpane, making a jumbled sound, yet strangely, it brought a sense of peace. Inside, wisps of smoke drifted from an ornate incense burner, the orange glow flickering in the wind. The bed curtains hung low, revealing a woman lying inside. Outside, a huge tiger lay prone. A thin man leaned against the window, a pipe glowing faintly. He exhaled rings of smoke, obscuring his captivating, almond-shaped eyes. Half a month ago, he arrived at the border and found Lou Mingyue, barely clinging to life, in a secluded cave. At that moment, only one thought occupied his mind—even if Lou Mingyue’s name was already written in the Book of Life and Death, he would strike it down stroke by stroke! Mo Sigui had never doubted his abilities, but he was still afraid, and even now, he still felt lingering fear. He turned back and, through the thin veil, through the thin gauze curtain, clearly felt Lou Mingyue’s even breathing, and only then did he feel a little relieved.

chapters.title: Waist!!!
chapters.content: He extinguished his pipe, gently placing it on the table. His figure moved like the wind, silently reaching the window in the blink of an eye. His long, slender, well-defined hands lifted the sheer curtain, and he stood by the window, quietly gazing at her face. After a long while, he slowly sat down, his fingers gently tracing the contours of Lou Mingyue’s face. A myriad of emotions welled up within him, but not a trace of desire. “Mo Sigui,” Lou Mingyue suddenly whispered. His fingers stiffened for a moment, then slowly withdrew, his voice hoarse, “Yes, you are awake.” As expected, he could not help but feel joy. “I am cold,” Lou Mingyue opened her eyes and looked at him. Their eyes met, and Lou Mingyue quickly closed them again. Mo Sigui had once been so dashing and handsome, but now he was so haggard. Even if she tried to escape, she had to face reality. Mo Sigui’s current state was probably all her fault! The room was quiet. Lou Mingyue felt a sudden tightness in her body as a warm embrace encircled her. In an instant, tears streamed uncontrollably down her face, as if releasing all her pent-up pain. Mo Sigui felt the hot tears sliding down his neck, remaining silent. However, the hatred was too deep; a few tears could not dispel it. When the tears were gone, only a dry, stinging pain remained. “Ah Ran,” Lou Mingyue thought, wanting to call him as she used to, but even in her current vulnerability, she could still control herself. If she could only cause Mo Sigui pain, she wanted to minimize it. “Say what you want to say,” Mo Sigui noticed her sudden breathlessness, as if a sentence was stuck in her throat. “No matter what you say or do, things cannot get any worse than they are now. I cannot see through the bonds of love. If you are willing, perhaps we could leave some tenderness between us, so that our meeting in this life would not have been in vain.” His words revealed her innermost thoughts. Lou Mingyue paused for a moment, her stiff body slowly relaxing as she sighed and murmured, “Ah Ran.” Mo Sigui closed her eyes, forcing back tears, and after a moment, said, “Ningyu.” “Qiu Ningyu…” Lou Mingyue felt that her past self was like a beautiful dream, as if from another world, now beyond her grasp, even in its fragments. The two embraced for a long time. After they separated, the atmosphere was slightly awkward; after all, it had been a long time since they had been so close. Mo Sigui helped her sit up, poured the medicine he had prepared earlier into a bowl, and brought it to her. “If you want revenge, I will go with you.” Lou Mingyue’s fingertips had barely touched the bowl when she abruptly withdrew them, saying resolutely, “No!” “Your temperament is not as cheerful as before. Yet you are still so unreasonable.” Mo Sigui sat down on the edge of the bed, scooped a spoonful of medicine, and brought it to her lips, urging, “This is the first time I’ve served someone like this. Open your mouth quickly.” “Mo Sigui!” Lou Mingyue felt a surge of panic. “You do not want your medical skills anymore? Heaven bestowed talent upon you; how can you bear to waste it! If you do this, I will go to the eighteenth level of hell after I die!” If one truly cared about someone and did not selfishly try to possess them, one certainly would not want to see them painfully sever what almost entirely occupied their life, just to accompany one’s path to hell. “Who said I am giving up?” Mo Sigui coaxed her softly. “Taking revenge while studying medicine is a good thing. Even scholars sometimes enjoy the company of beautiful women. Why can I not?” “That’s different!” Lou Mingyue retorted sharply. “Do you think revenge is child’s play?” Back then, Yelu Huangwu guarded the tomb alone, and many top assassins could not take her life. Now, she was back at the heart of Liao’s power! Killing Yelu Huangwu was not just fighting one person; it was facing thousands upon thousands of experts. Even if the two of them spent five or ten years plotting, they might not succeed. How many decades did one have in a lifetime? How could she bear to ruin Mo Sigui’s best years? “I appreciate your kindness, but any more pressure might break me. Mo Sigui, focus on studying medicine and saving lives.” For the first time, Lou Mingyue showed weakness and pleaded before him. “I am just one of the masses. You said you could save me anytime. Why did you suddenly change your mind?” Because every time he saw her covered in wounds, he could not remain calm. “Promise me,” Lou Mingyue stared intently at him. “Promise me.” Lou Mingyue understood Mo Sigui better than anyone. For him, life was for the sake of medicine. She was already content that he could say he would give up the Great Dao to accompany her in revenge. Mo Sigui remained silent. “Either I die, or you go back,” Lou Mingyue said. On this path of no return, she alone was enough. If the price of revenge was Mo Sigui, then she would rather die with regrets. Their gazes locked for a long time before Mo Sigui finally yielded. Hearing Lou Mingyue say this, he was filled with extreme inner conflict. Perhaps only Lou Mingyue’s death could bring him relief; only then could he gain freedom. But could he kill her with his own hands? No! Not only could he not, but he had always devoted all his efforts to saving her. Lou Mingyue breathed a sigh of relief and drank the bowl of medicine. “If it is convenient for you to take care of Xiaowu for me, I can never repay the debt I owe her.” “You do not owe anyone anything.” Mo Sigui was quite repulsed by her inexplicable sense of responsibility. “There’s no one in this world who needs your responsibility right now. Everyone has to survive on their own. Revenge is inherently painful; can you not think of something happy?” “Happy things… are all in the past.” Lou Mingyue frowned. “The happier I was then, the more painful it is to recall now.” “Then let me add something new for you.” Mo Sigui was worried she would refuse again. “Ah Jiu said that since you and I are walking on two completely uninterrupted paths, why torture each other? But I cannot see through it all. Since that’s the case, even if there’s a bottomless abyss between us, at least I can tell you a joke from this side of the cliff.” It would be good if it could alleviate the other person’s pain a little. “Zhu Pianxian said that everyone is inherently base; they always crave what they cannot have, but fail to appreciate what they have easily.” Mo Sigui did not care whether the speaker was reliable or not; he just pulled her over and tried to persuade her, “Maybe if we get to know each other, we will not feel this bad.” Mo Sigui looked at her expectantly. Outside, thunder rumbled, and the rain poured down harder. Bianjing remained peaceful and drizzly. Inside the artificial cave, Da Jiu, ears twitching, curled up in a ball like a frightened cat. “Idiot!” Da Jiu twitched its nose and quickly scrambled out, tumbling and crawling towards the person standing in the rain and mist. An Jiu frowned at its behavior, “You are the king of beasts, a fierce tiger! You are so scared, your legs are weak; even rabbits will laugh at you!” Da Jiu ignored her scolding, rubbing against her leg like a cat, the drizzle forming tiny droplets on its fur. An Jiu moved the umbrella in her hand closer to it. The man and the tiger returned to the hut. Sheng Changying had been dug out of the ground. When the Konghe Army fired arrows from the air, he was grazed on the waist by a falling arrow. Although he bled quite a bit, fortunately, it was only a superficial wound and did not affect any vital organs. “Someone’s coming,” An Jiu said. Everyone tensed up. Sui Yuntong peeked through the crack in the door and saw a figure in plain clothes rushing towards them with lightning speed. Only when she was within ten feet did Sui Yuntong recognize the person. “It’s Madam Zhu.” Before she finished speaking, Zhu Pianxian had already kicked the door open and rushed in. Sui Yuntong could not dodge in time, and his head slammed against the door with a thud. Li Qingzhi felt a chill run down his spine at the sound and could not help but rub his temple. Zhu Pianxian looked around. “Where’s Changying?” “He suffered a minor injury and is resting,” Ling Ziyue said. Zhu Pianxian’s eyebrows furrowed, and she strode inside. “Pianxian.” Sheng Changying had bled all night; even a small wound would be painful, and his complexion was naturally not good. “What happened? Let me see how serious your injury is! Those bunch of good-for-nothings outside, all of them so energetic, and you are the only one injured! You could not even protect one person! What kind of Konghe Army, what kind of general are you? Blind!” Zhu Pianxian roared. Everyone outside, except An Jiu, looked astonished. Zhu Pianxian was usually very good at disguising herself, always appearing delicate and weak, constantly calling herself “this humble servant,” her slightly plump figure giving the illusion of a frail willow. Who would have thought that when she got angry, her words were like a brick, striking people so hard they could not easily catch their breath. Sheng Changying was somewhat familiar with this side of her and remained relatively calm. “It’s nothing serious, just a minor waist injury.” “Waist!!!” Zhu Pianxian covered her mouth, her eyes wide. Sui Yuntong, Li Qingzhi, An Jiu, and Ling Ziyue outside instantly understood what she meant.

chapters.title: A Crisis of Survival
chapters.content: Before even getting married, he injured his waist. Judging from his complexion, the injury seemed quite serious. This…this future… Zhu Pianxian thought bitterly, she must have had the worst luck in eight lifetimes. First, she married a man who was half-dead, and now, after all these years of marriage, she was still a virgin. Damn it, was she destined to be a virgin forever?! She was shrewd yet selfish, thinking first about her future happiness, but also incredibly foolish, never considering that changing men would solve the problem. “Let me see,” Zhu Pianxian said, resigned to her fate after her internal groan. “Ahem.” Li Qingzhi cleared his throat awkwardly, glancing left and right. He found everyone else expressionless, as if they had not understood at all, and secretly thought his skin was still a bit too thin. Whether others understood or not was secondary; the key was that the innocent party involved had not considered that possibility at all. Seeing Zhu Pianxian’s face turn green, he felt a warm glow inside, thinking how good Pianxian was, caring so much about him! So, even though he was usually a bit shy, he blushed and lifted his clothes to let her see, reassuringly saying, “It’s nothing, just a superficial injury.” An Jiu peeked inside. Zhu Pianxian quickly covered Sheng Changying’s clothes, “Could you not have at least said anything before coming in?” An Jiu turned and went out, knocking on the doorframe, “You were not doing anything shady, were you? If not, I am coming in.” Zhu Pianxian had initially intended to keep her out, but hearing this, she was momentarily speechless with anger. “What are you doing in here!” Zhu Pianxian said irritably. “Our Changying is injured like this, and you still have the nerve to wander around here? Did you not see everyone else is cowering?” An Jiu went to the corner, grabbed the Dragon-Subduing Bow, turned back, and held out her hand. “Safeguarding fee!” Zhu Pianxian was confused. “What safeguarding fee?” “You did not give me any protection money. Why should I be your man’s bodyguard?” An Jiu scoffed. Sheng Changying did not care what An Jiu said. In that emergency, her first thought was to protect him. “You!” Zhu Pianxian’s annual salary as Chu Dingjiang’s head manager was considerable. She really had nothing to say, so she could only angrily say, “You are inhuman!” “If you are so capable, find someone who does not know martial arts. Why can you not keep him by your side?” An Jiu slowly added insult to injury, making Zhu Pianxian so angry she almost fainted. Just before leaving, she finally remembered to offer a word of comfort, “Regarding the waist injury, it is best if Headmaster Sheng is alright. If, however, it leaves a lasting condition that prevents you from working, you are so capable that you can take over. Things will work themselves out; do not worry too much.” Zhu Pianxian’s face flushed crimson. “Fourteenth Young Lady!” “Hey, I was giving you some serious advice. Why are you blushing?” An Jiu glanced at her, puzzled, and stepped out the door. Zhu Pianxian rushed forward and closed the door. Sheng Changying, on the bed, seemed completely oblivious to An Jiu’s words, his gaze full of tenderness. Seeing this, Zhu Pianxian relaxed and sat back down on the bedside. She instructed Sheng Changying, “Do not pay any attention to her anymore!” “Fourteenth, does Sister Zhu’s family own a lot of land?” Lou Xiaowu asked. An Jiu shook her head. Lou Xiaowu asked doubtfully, “Then what’s this talk of labor? At the very least, Master Sheng can sell his calligraphy to make money! Master Sheng’s calligraphy is so beautiful!” “Where’s Da Jiu?” An Jiu needed to give it a good scolding, while also feeling a bit resentful towards Mo Sigui. Look what he’d done to the tiger! Like father, like son. “Huh, it was just here.” Lou Xiaowu looked around. She could not find Da Jiu anywhere. Roar— A deafening tiger’s roar tore through the mist; even the ground seemed to shake, and a mountain wind suddenly rose. The rain fell even more heavily. “What’s going on!” Sui Yuntong’s expression changed slightly. Everyone knew Da Jiu’s temperament; describing it as gentle was an exaggeration. It was more like a little white rabbit than a tiger, and had never roared like that before. An Jiu was also somewhat startled. Was it an enemy or an evolution? The group quickly descended the mountain, rushing towards the direction of the sound. The leaves in the forest seemed to sense Da Jiu’s emotions, rustling and disturbing everyone’s peace of mind. The group quickened their pace. In a few breaths, they found Da Jiu lying motionless on the ground, like a corpse. Everyone was on high alert. An Jiu released her mental power to scan the surroundings. “No one’s here.” The group breathed a slight sigh of relief. An Jiu walked around to Da Jiu’s front. Da Jiu heard the footsteps and listlessly raised its eyes. Its fat tiger face was filled with a word—despair. “Da Jiu, what’s wrong?” An Jiu crouched down. Da Jiu’s ears drooped, and it glanced at the cluster of tender seedlings in front of it with utter despair. The Medicine Boy, whose lightness skill was the weakest, arrived last. “Little Yao, come and see if it is sick?” An Jiu said. The Medicine Boy walked in panting, saw the cluster of seedlings, and smiled, “I know.” “This looks like Dream Flower?” Sui Yuntong asked. “Yes,” the young apprentice said, “Da Jiu only eats poisonous things and has been coveting the Dream Flower for a long time. Master gave it a small packet before leaving this time. It likes to bury things, so maybe the Dream Flower has sprouted… Once it sprouts, its poison is almost completely gone.” “Ha!” An Jiu laughed out loud, “You truly live up to your reputation as a fool!” Da Jiu already felt that life as a tiger was meaningless, and had no interest in arguing with these unscrupulous humans. “Da Jiu, actually, Master hid all your food under the bed in the pharmacy.” The young apprentice squatted in front of Da Jiu, gesturing as he spoke. Da Jiu roughly understood that the good food was in the pharmacy, and immediately perked up, turning and rushing back like the wind. The atmosphere in the room was wonderful, and even the air was sweet. Sheng Changying held Zhu Pianxian by the back of her neck with one hand, kissing and gently biting her pink lips. The two were lost in their passionate kiss when the door was suddenly flung open. A huge shadow leaped into the room, darting around as if no one else was there, sniffing the floor. Zhu Pianxian shuddered and screamed in fright. The people in the woods, knowing the young lovers were enjoying their honeymoon, wisely slowed their pace, giving them some time to be affectionate. But they had only walked a short distance when they saw Zhu Pianxian standing halfway up the hill, hands on her hips, roaring, “Like father, like son! Fourteenth Young Lady, keep your tiger under control!” An Jiu clicked her tongue. “Da Jiu’s ‘upper beam’ is Mo Sigui, is it not?” “I did not expect Madam Zhu to be so fierce. Changying is doomed now,” Li Qingzhi sighed. An Jiu said, “That’s because you do not understand Headmaster Sheng.” Who was Sheng Changying? However, An Jiu, who compiled all sorts of gossip from across the land, had read the news from the Konghe Academy. It was written in great detail, almost like a storybook. As the saying goes, “Even if you have not eaten pork, you’ve always seen pigs run.” An Jiu did not believe he was unaware of any scandalous gossip. Even though he was indeed a bit thin-skinned and slow to react to matters of men and women, he was actually a shrewd person. “Who will be king is still uncertain,” An Jiu said. “Then we will have to wait and see,” Sui Yuntong said with a smile. Back at the pharmacy, Da Jiu was already lying on the floor, his belly round and full, paws in the air, burping contentedly. “Madam Zhu, how is the situation in the city?” Sui Yuntong could not help but ask. “How would I, a mere commoner, know?” Zhu Pianxian, still holding her breath, spoke with a harsh tone. “However, I saw Aunt Mei before leaving the city. She said the Emperor’s passing is only a matter of days, and many court officials have been forced to choose sides. The Hua family is siding with the Second Prince, so his chances of winning are slim. I really do not know what the Hua family is thinking!” “Why would the Hua family suddenly support the Second Prince?” Ling Ziyue asked, puzzled. He had spent most of his time at the border and was not well-informed about court affairs, but he knew that although the Hua family had not explicitly stated their stance, they had always leaned towards supporting the eldest son’s succession. Sheng Changying said, “Hua Rongtian has already secretly supported the Second Prince. The Second Prince is not the legitimate heir, and his strength is no match for the Crown Prince. To succeed him, he will have to make many sacrifices. The Hua family is paving the way for their own future.” Sui Yuntong sighed, “There are many cases of ‘the bird is shot down after the bow is used up.’ The Hua family does not think that by fully supporting the Second Prince’s ascension, they can protect their entire family in the future!” “What if the Hua family cuts its own feathers?” Sheng Changying countered. The Emperor feared the Hua family because their influence in the Song Dynasty was too deep and vast, posing a growing threat to imperial power. If the Hua family were to sacrifice 70% of their strength to help the Second Prince ascend the throne, even if the prince worried that their power would overshadow his own, he would not be quick to discard them due to public opinion. “Powerful families are truly terrifying!” Li Qingzhi could not help but sigh. For most people, there was no gain without pain. If one wanted to rise above others, one must consider the price one was willing to pay. The glory and survival of a family like the Hua family were inevitably built upon the countless bones of its members.

chapters.title: Entering the City
chapters.content: An Jiu packed her equipment, finally slung the Dragon-Subduing Bow over her shoulder, bent down to pat Da Jiu’s head, and said to the medicine boy, “Take care of it for a few days.” “Fourteenth, where are you going?” Li Qingzhi asked. “Fourteenth, you cannot go.” Sui Yuntong blocked her way. “The master said you are injured and ordered me to stop you. I cannot beat you, but if you insist on going out, you will have to step over my dead body!” At this moment, she could not reconcile gratitude and duty. Sui Yuntong still felt he owed An Jiu a life, and now he was threatening her with his own, which made her feel very insecure. An Jiu frowned, her killing intent seemingly bursting from her eyes. She concentrated her mental power and released it like an arrow. Sui Yuntong’s face turned pale, his mind went blank, and almost without resistance, he only felt a sharp pain in the back of his neck before his vision went black. Everyone gasped. They had always known that An Jiu lacked internal energy, but her strength was not to be underestimated. However, no one had expected that she would possess such terrifying power. Just now, they had only sensed a trace of killing intent emanating from An Jiu, barely perceiving her mental power. Seeing Sui Yuntong’s reaction, it was clear he had been subjected to a mental attack. Therefore, there was only one explanation: she could control her mental power at will! “Who wants to stop me?” An Jiu looked at Li Qingzhi, who had always been on Sui Yuntong’s side. Li Qingzhi was about to step forward when Ling Ziyue blocked him. “The chaos in Bianjing is difficult for one person to stop, but she can easily protect herself in the chaos. Do not stop her; you will not even have a chance to become a corpse.” If the two sides were evenly matched, An Jiu might use a deadly move to avoid entanglement, but against Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi, there was no need for that. Li Qingzhi paused. “No, a gentleman keeps his word. Since I was ordered to stop Fourteenth Young Lady, how can I go back on my word? Whether I can stop her or not is another matter, but I must stop her!” “Ahem!” Sheng Changying, supported by Zhu Pianxian, came out. Having overheard their conversation inside, she roughly guessed what had happened. “Are you going to stop me, too?” An Jiu raised an eyebrow at him. “Are you deliberately making fun of me?” Zhu Pianxian glared at An Jiu. She knew perfectly well that Sheng Changying did not know martial arts, yet she still said such things! “Those who are all looks and no brains should not talk nonsense,” An Jiu said calmly. Zhu Pianxian was about to roll up her sleeves and fight her when she suddenly felt a tightness around her waist. It was Sheng Changying blocking her way and holding her waist! Zhu Pianxian was stunned, her face suddenly turning crimson. Sheng Changying’s pale face also showed an unnatural flush, but he remained very calm. “I came out to remind you of something. Everyone’s mental power is different. Take Chu Dingjiang, for example. His mental power is thick and solid, extremely suitable for setting traps. Anyone who enters his mental power range will struggle and cause him almost no harm. Your mental power advantage lies in its explosiveness and sharpness. Do not try to use your mental power to set traps anymore; it is not worth it.” An Jiu was somewhat surprised. Sheng Changying seemed to have witnessed her being injured firsthand! “How did you know?” An Jiu could not help but ask. “A guess,” Sheng Changying smiled slightly. “With your level, unless you use the wrong method, you are unlikely to get hurt.” “Do not smile at her!” Zhu Pianxian covered his face. Sheng Changying was not the kind of man who was exceptionally handsome. Even his slightly upturned fox-like eyes looked a little strange at first glance, but after looking at them for a while, one could see a certain charm—not in his charisma, but in his earnestness. Even when he was lazy and drowsy, he never seemed absent-minded. Sheng Changying always appeared focused and serious in everything he did. As the saying goes, a serious man is the most charming. “Thank you,” An Jiu said sincerely. Sheng Changying continued, “You must have witnessed Wei Yuzhi manipulating external objects with his mental power, right? You can do it too. Try it when the time is right.” An Jiu’s heart stirred. “Is my mental power the same type as his?” “Yes. When it reaches a certain level, you can kill with just your mental power. But you are also easily injured. Once you cannot concentrate and control your mental power, you might end up hurting yourself instead of others. Wei Yuzhi’s poor health is probably related to this.” Sheng Changying raised his hand and grasped Zhu Pianxian’s hand that was covering his face, gently pulling it down, but not letting go. “I did not tell you at the Konghe Academy because I was afraid you’d hurt yourself like Wei Yuzhi did during practice.” The wounds left by mental power were terrible, especially difficult to heal. Even a medical prodigy like Mo Sigui would have to go to great lengths and require a long period of recuperation. Since it was the same mental power, that meant that when she kidnapped Wei Yuzhi multiple times, he had many opportunities to resist! But why did he not act? An Jiu could not understand. “Does not Wei Yuzhi know about this?” “So what if he knows? He’s in charge of Piaomiao Mountain mansion, so he’s bound to be out and about. How can he protect himself and command respect if he does not hone his martial arts?” Zhu Pianxian said irritably. “A cunning person like him will not completely entrust his life to someone else. Hurry up and leave, Changying needs to rest!” Knowing that they already knew pretty much everything, An Jiu did not intend to waste time. She glanced at Zhu Pianxian, turned around, and left, tossing out a comment: “All the good cabbages have been eaten by pigs.” “Who’s the pig! Explain yourself!” Zhu Pianxian was practically bursting with anger. She really should not talk to that venomous guy! “She’s obviously calling me a pig,” Sheng Changying said softly, squeezing her hand. “I have nothing; being with me is beneath you.” If anyone else had said this, Zhu Pianxian would have clearly understood that it was just flattery, but Sheng Changying’s expression showed no hint of a joke. He seemed to genuinely believe An Jiu’s words were directed at him and truly felt unworthy of her. Sheng Changying had this power; he made people feel that everything he said came from the heart. Zhu Pianxian’s eyes welled up with tears, all her anger vanished, and she lightly spat, “Do not say that.” These words made Zhu Pianxian feel incredibly proud, while simultaneously making her heart flutter with joy. Seeing this scene, Li Qingzhi roughly understood what An Jiu had meant. Sheng Changying’s popularity in the Konghe Academy was so high that he had no enemies, but it was not entirely due to his hard work. Thinking this, he suddenly came to his senses—what about his promise to block Fourteenth Young Lady?! The night in Bianjing was solemn and filled with murderous intent. A light rain fell as An Jiu wandered through the dark streets and alleys. Even the usually bustling night market was now shrouded in darkness, not a soul in sight. The entire capital, Bianjing, seemed to be trapped in a deep nightmare. Even the Second Prince’s residence was completely dark. Has he failed? Or succeeded? An Jiu circled the Second Prince’s residence, the air thick with the stench of blood. Corpses littered the ground, but not a single living soul was to be seen. She used her mental power to search the residence. Finding even one living person to question would save her a lot of trouble, but alas, they were all dead. Just as she was about to leave, she sensed a group of people rapidly approaching. Unsure whether they were friend or foe, she paused, then spun around and climbed up the corridor to hide.

chapters.title: Change
chapters.content: As the distance closed, An Jiu clearly discerned that there were twelve people on the other side. After entering, they split into four groups, searching various areas, seemingly looking for something. They were grouped in threes: one martial artist of level six or higher, and two below level six. An Jiu felt this grouping method was somewhat familiar, like… the Konghe Army? An Jiu peeked through a gap and indeed saw silver cranes embroidered on the hem of their clothing. Now that the Konghe Army was fragmented, it was impossible to determine whether these were Chu Dingjiang’s people based solely on their insignia. An Jiu considered capturing one to question them, but then changed her mind. A secret organization like the Konghe Army would definitely be tight-lipped. Rather than risk exposure and wasting time and energy forcing confessions, it was better to follow them. Having made up her mind, An Jiu chose a group with relatively higher martial arts skills to follow. Generally speaking, the higher the martial arts skill, the higher the rank and the more information they knew. She was not worried about being discovered; after all, no matter how high their mental strength was, it could not compare to hers. These men silently conducted a thorough search of the study, turning it upside down in about the time it takes to drink two cups of tea. Especially the bright yellow imperial edicts, which were laid out one by one on the table. After reading all the edicts, one of them said, “What do we do if we cannot find them?” The other two were silent for a few moments, then the tall, thin man said, “Keep looking.” “Boss, it is just an edict; he just took it so easily. We’ve probably wasted our time,” the man complained. “I do not know what His Highness is thinking. With the situation so dire, he’s still worried about an edict. Ascending the throne is the most important thing!” An Jiu’s heart sank. Could it be that Chu Dingjiang’s plan had failed? “As long as the Second Prince is not dead, and the edict is not found, that edict will always be a thorn in our side. The Second Prince…” Before he could finish speaking, a long, deep bell tolled in the silent night, each toll awakening the entire capital of Bianjing. “His Majesty has passed away!” The speaker’s voice clearly carried joy. An Jiu sensed something was amiss. They seemed to be working for the Crown Prince; their joy at the Emperor’s death meant the palace was now under his control. “No!” The tall, thin man was not so optimistic. “His Highness has not fully grasped the Second Prince’s strength. Even if the Emperor has truly passed away, he certainly will not announce it so quickly. That’s why the Second Prince’s men would not dare act rashly.” “Should we still look for the edict?” another asked. The tall, thin man pondered for a long time. “Since the death knell was not rung by His Highness, then it must be the Second Prince… Could it be that the Emperor has truly appointed the Second Prince? Whatever it is, since we’ve been ordered, we must continue searching.” They were only ordered to find the secret edict the Emperor had bestowed upon the Second Prince over the past six months; they did not know what it said. If it truly was an edict appointing the Crown Prince, the palace would immediately descend into chaos. The men searched every book in the study, leaving no page unchecked. An Jiu quietly slipped out and headed to the Hua residence. The Hua residence supported the Second Prince; Mei Jiu and Mei Yanran should be there too. Finding the person would reveal more information. Only now did An Jiu understand why Chu Dingjiang had been so slow to tell her how to contact him anytime, anywhere. She muttered to herself, “What a load of rubbish about fighting side-by-side.” The Hua mansion gates were tightly shut. Security was tight, but this was not enough to stop An Jiu. She sneaked into the mansion and headed straight for Mei Jiu’s residence. Passing a small garden, she saw two familiar figures. Hua Rongjian sat by a small pond, casually tossing food into it. Mei Ruyan sat on a stone stool not far behind him, with two burly black-clad men standing behind him. At first glance, an uninformed person would assume the two men were Mei Ruyan’s subordinates. But An Jiu noticed that the two men’s muscles were taut, their hands gripping the hilts of their swords, their eyes frequently glancing at Mei Ruyan—clearly, they were watching her. “Mei Ruyan.” Hua Rongjian did not turn around, his tone slow and casual, as if chatting. “Where do you want to go?” “What, can I not go out?” Mei Ruyan said coldly. “That depends on my mood.” Hua Rongjian placed the fish food on the low table beside him, stood up, walked to Mei Ruyan, bent down, and pinched her chin, forcing her to look up. “Did you hand the memorial to your master?” Mei Ruyan pursed her lips, her phoenix eyes meeting his gaze fearlessly. From An Jiu’s angle, she could not see Mei Ruyan’s expression, but she could clearly see the faint smile on Hua Rongjian’s face. His smile was lazy yet tinged with ruthlessness. The dim light of the lantern flickered in the wind, casting swaying shadows that made his face appear sinister. An Jiu was stunned. She remembered the first time she met Hua Rongjian; he was a playful young man whose smile was as warm as the morning sun. It had not been long since she last saw him, yet he seemed like a completely different person. “Was it worth it?” Hua Rongjian released her, his expression returning to normal. “That memorial was written by my father to protect General Ling. It was not presented to the Emperor. A mere scrap of paper can bring down the Hua family? Your master is far too naive.” Mei Ruyan’s chin flushed slightly, her smile exceptionally alluring. “So, that scrap of a memorial—do you know why I specifically chose that one?” Hua Rongjian looked down at her. “I am all ears.” “Because only that memorial contained the most information about Ling Ziyue. Someone could use that to forge Prime Minister Hua’s handwriting, creating a fake correspondence between Prime Minister Hua and General Ling, in which they incited and deceived General Ling into attacking the Liao Kingdom’s Xijin Prefecture,” Mei Ruyan said gleefully. “Similarly, they could also imitate Prime Minister Hua’s words about plotting to overthrow the dynasty. Think about it, if Prime Minister Hua plotted to eliminate loyal ministers and seize the throne, what would happen if this evidence fell into the hands of the Song Emperor?” No matter which Emperor it was, the Hua family would face annihilation. If the Crown Prince ascends the throne, then this evidence was unnecessary. The Hua family, supporting the Second Prince, was considered treasonous, and the Crown Prince could rightfully deal with them. However, if the Second Prince ultimately succeeds in ascending the throne, what would he do with this evidence? For a family whose achievements threaten the Emperor, holding this leverage allows him to have a legitimate excuse to destroy the Hua family at any time. Whether the evidence itself was flawed was no longer important. This was an unsolvable dilemma, and even knowing it now, there’s no better way to prevent it. “The Hua family was already on the verge of collapse. Just a slight push,” Mei Ruyan lightly poked Hua Rongjian’s waist with her slender index finger, her smile radiant, “and they will crumble. Instead of worrying about me, you should be thinking about your own future.” “No need for your concern,” Hua Rongjian smirked, ordering the two burly men, “Kill her.” An Jiu was surprised by Hua Rongjian’s drastic change and hesitated, wondering whether to save Mei Ruyan. Although An Jiu disliked Mei Ruyan, upon closer examination, Mei Ruyan had not truly harmed her. However, Hua Rongjian was her friend, and Mei Ruyan’s actions had greatly harmed the Hua family. Moreover, Uncle Chu seemed quite concerned about the Hua family… After some consideration, An Jiu decided to disregard their personal grudges. Hua Rongjian sat down again where he had been feeding the fish, staring blankly at the water. An Jiu watched for a while; he remained motionless in the same position. Could it be that learning of his birth mother’s murder and his father’s involvement had such a profound impact on him? Just a few days ago, he seemed to have come to terms with it. Men’s minds were hard to fathom. An Jiu avoided him and went to Mei Jiu’s residence. The light was on inside. Mei Jiu sat reading under the lamp, while Mei Yanran sewed opposite her; the mother and daughter seemed very harmonious. An Jiu stood outside for a while, then quietly slipped inside. Mei Yanran glanced warily out the window but saw no one. She inwardly cursed herself for being overly suspicious. An Jiu sat down like a ghost, pondering her opening line. “Hi, I am here.” Or perhaps, “Long time no see!” Neither seemed quite right. After much thought, she simply coughed softly. Mei Yanran turned around, her sword almost drawn, only relaxing when she saw it was An Jiu. Mei Jiu was delighted to see her. “Ah Jiu, you’ve left the island? So you are out of trouble in Mei Mansion?” “Yes.” An Jiu looked her over. “Were you not poisoned? Why are you getting fatter?” Mei Jiu blushed, stammering for a moment. Mei Yanran spoke for her: “Jiu’er is pregnant.” An Jiu opened her mouth, her gaze falling on Mei Jiu’s abdomen. She was wearing loose clothing, so it was not clear if her belly was protruding. “How many months along?” “Almost four months,” Mei Jiu said weakly. Just a few months ago, Hua Rongtian was sleeping in the study, and now the baby was four months old. An Jiu could not help but wonder if it was Hua Rongtian’s child, but then she remembered Mei Jiu’s chastity and virtue; if something had happened, she probably would have already drowned herself. For this reason, An Jiu refrained from asking such an infuriating question in front of the mother. However, she said something even more infuriating: “If you break up with Hua Rongtian in the future, you have to take the child with you. A child can live without a father, but not without a mother.” Mei Jiu’s expression darkened. Her relationship with Hua Rongtian was actually just an accident after drinking, not something born of love. Mei Jiu had no confidence for the future. Mei Yanran did not react much, casually changing the subject, “You came out because of something?” “Yes, what’s the situation in Bianjing now?” An Jiu asked. Mei Yanran said, “The Crown Prince seems to have the upper hand in the palace, but that’s not actually the case. The area outside the palace is almost entirely controlled by the Second Prince’s army. The Crown Prince, trapped inside, is out of touch. If it were not for that Grand Eunuch, he would not have lasted this long.” “Grand Eunuch?” An Jiu vaguely recognized such a person. “A Transcendent Realm expert serving the Emperor?” Mei Yanran nodded. “If the Crown Prince ascends the throne this time, this eunuch will have served three generations of Emperors. Because he’s in the palace and does not often fight, no one knows his true strength. They only know that he reached the Transcendent Realm fifteen years ago.” Transcendent Realm experts were extremely rare. Besides Chu Dingjiang, the Second Prince probably did not have anyone else. In other words, if the Second Prince wants to ascend the throne, he must first deal with this Grand Eunuch. Who could deal with him? Only Chu Dingjiang! An Jiu could not sit still any longer. “Where is the Second Prince now?” “I do not know, but listen.” Mei Yanran paused, the sound of the funeral bell outside ringing clearly in her ears. “Once the bell tolls, the Crown Prince and the Second Prince will clash within the next day or two. Because the Second Prince must attend the funeral, the Crown Prince will definitely take the opportunity to make his move. We will see how he manages to enter the palace.”

chapters.title: Hypocrisy
chapters.content: “How many Transcendent Realm experts are around the Crown Prince?” An Jiu wondered if there were any more hidden Transcendent Realm experts in the world. For example, even though she herself had only reached the Transcendent Realm in mental power, she still possessed extraordinary destructive power. “Also, how many people in the Konghe Army actually support the Crown Prince?” Mei Yanran said, “As far as I know, all four major families of the Konghe Army support the Crown Prince, including the Mei family. I do not know if there are any other hidden Transcendent Realm experts around the Crown Prince, but I know of two—the eunuch Feng Shi and Elder Zhi of the Mei family.” “Elder Zhi.” An Jiu had almost forgotten about him. Ever since he was suspected of being the mysterious person who attacked the Konghe Army and was detained in the palace, he had disappeared without a trace. Mei Yanran had mentioned that Elder Zhi taught at the Zishan Hall, where the princes studied. “The Emperor has more than one son. Could Elder Zhi possibly be supporting someone else?” An Jiu always thought the Crown Prince was a scoundrel; if he became Emperor, he would certainly live up to the description of “debauchery and tyranny.” Elder Zhi, who claimed to be wise, had been in close contact with the princes at Zishan Hall; surely he could see this? Mei Yanran shook her head. “I cannot guess that. You once protected the Crown Prince closely; I know what you saw, but what you saw was only the surface.” While the Crown Prince was indeed extremely lustful, he was even more obsessed with power. Over the years, he had never forgotten to seize any power he could exploit. After all, once he reached the highest position, what kind of woman could he not have? And the benefits that power brought him went far beyond that. An Jiu suddenly remembered something: Chu Dingjiang also had Gu Jinghong’s blood on him! At the border, to prevent the medicine from being stolen, it was divided into three parts. Mo Sigui kept one part, An Jiu took some, and Chu Dingjiang had some as well. He had once said that the Second Prince still needed more experience. It was not the right time for him to ascend the throne. If that were the case, why did he not use those medicines to prolong the Emperor’s life? If the Emperor were still alive, he would not be in this predicament. “I am leaving.” An Jiu suddenly stood up and strode out the door. Mei Jiu opened her mouth, but Mei Yanran stopped her. An Jiu searched the city thoroughly. Noticing that the armor of the guards at the North Gate differed from the others, she crouched down nearby to observe. Apart from their clothing, the North Gate seemed no different from the others, filled with a tense atmosphere. The defenses were heavier than usual. An Jiu used her mental power to probe the area bit by bit, discovering that many martial artists gathered near the city walls. She recognized the aura of one of them, a master at the Transcendent Realm. Confirming Chu Dingjiang was there, she quickly climbed the city wall, hung upside down from a pillar, and knocked on a window. The window was pushed open, and Chu Dingjiang, dressed in a black robe, stood before it, looking up at her, his face mostly hidden by his hood. “Why are you here?” he asked. An Jiu did not speak, glancing around the room. Besides seven or eight ninth-level martial artists, a richly dressed young man sat at the head of the table. She thought to herself, “This must be the Second Prince. He’s so young!” The Second Prince was not startled by the uninvited guest, calmly observing her for a few moments. Suddenly, he spoke, “Since you are a friend of the master, please come in.” It was unclear whether he was speaking to An Jiu or Chu Dingjiang. An Jiu, without hesitation, entered the room. Only after recognizing her did the Second Prince show a hint of surprise. The newcomer had been so close, yet the martial artists in the building had not noticed. He knew this was another master of the Transcendent Realm. Judging from Chu Dingjiang’s tone, the Second Prince had deduced he was a friend, not an enemy, and had taken the initiative to be friendly, only to find that this person appeared to be a young woman. “This is His Highness the Second Prince,” Chu Dingjiang introduced her. An Jiu, unsure of the proper etiquette, casually clasped her hands in greeting, said, “Greetings, Your Highness.” When in need of manpower, the Second Prince treated experts with great courtesy, smiling and nodding, “No need for formalities.” “This is My Young Lady,” Chu Dingjiang introduced, then requested permission. “Your Highness, may I speak with my wife privately for a few moments?” An Jiu hesitated for a moment, then did not deny it. “Please, My Lord,” the Second Prince said. Chu Dingjiang took her hand and pulled her out, walking a hundred paces along the city wall. “The Second Prince still seems like a little boy on the surface,” An Jiu commented. She said so on the surface, but in reality, when they met eyes just now, his gaze was steady, revealing no trace of youthful naiveté. Chu Dingjiang tapped her head. “Why are you not staying in the plum blossom grove? What are you doing here, causing trouble?” “Did you not say we’d fight side by side?” An Jiu brushed his hand away, disdainfully. “Your so-called ‘fighting side by side’ only means when I am in danger?” “I said ‘fight side by side,’ not ‘share the joys and sorrows,'” Chu Dingjiang said matter-of-factly. “My woman only needs to share the joys, not the sorrows.” “Are you keeping a pet?!” An Jiu stared at him, her tone turning serious. “If you need a pet, sorry, I am not one.” If she truly loved someone, she wanted to cherish every important experience they had. An Jiu had figured it out. She did not want to be timid and hesitant. To change, to live with dignity, she’d start by loving someone freely. “I am glad you have this intention. I… just do not want you to take risks!” Chu Dingjiang sighed. An Jiu protested. “I have plenty of risks to take in the future. One more will not make a difference.” “You are planning to become an assassin?” Chu Dingjiang was a little surprised. He had always thought she wanted to escape that kind of life. An Jiu was displeased with his tone. “There are good assassins and bad assassins. Since all I know is killing, can I not use this skill to do something good? Give me back that bounty post job. I will complete it myself after things in Bianjing are over.” How a person lived was not just related to their experiences but more often to their mindset. If there were shackles in one’s heart, even facing a vast ocean would not feel the immensity of the world. “You are quite optimistic,” Chu Dingjiang said with a helpless smile. An Jiu immediately became happy. “From birth until now, no one has ever commented on me like that. Since you have some insight, I’ve decided to help you without holding a grudge.” Chu Dingjiang suppressed his secret joy and said calmly, “Whatever makes you happy.” As a man, protecting his woman was a matter of course. However, they were not ordinary people. Chu Dingjiang could not help but think about sharing life and death, but An Jiu’s willingness to share hardship with him was one thing; dragging An Jiu into hardship was another. If this was her own wish, how could he not be happy? “Stop pretending.” An Jiu rolled her eyes, mercilessly exposing his lie. “If you really did not want me to come, you would not have just sent Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi to stop me.
