Besides, you always seize every opportunity to hint at things to me.” If Chu Dingjiang wanted to do something, even if it ultimately failed, he would have carefully planned it. How could he just casually give instructions? “Ha, our Ah Jiu is so smart.” Chu Dingjiang was not embarrassed at all, smiling as he ruffled her hair. “As for the hints you mentioned, I am innocent.” “Tch.” An Jiu scoffed, looking at him with a “I saw right through you” gaze. “You always tell me you will be with me through thick and thin, that you will fight side by side, never missing an opportunity to brainwash me. Do not think I do not know. What kind of brainwashing training have I not seen? Playing hard to get, humph.”

chapters.title: Near Death
chapters.content: This matter truly wronged Chu Dingjiang. He had not intentionally brainwashed An Jiu; it was entirely a subconscious act. Now that it was pointed out, he did not deny it. “How’s your physical recovery?” Chu Dingjiang asked. Mental injuries to the body were difficult to heal, but An Jiu did not feel any discomfort. “I am fine. It should not affect normal combat. I heard Elder Zhi has sided with the Crown Prince?” Chu Dingjiang said, “It seems so at the moment.” An Jiu paused, raising an eyebrow at him. “Does the Second Prince have other Transcendent Realm experts by his side?” Chu Dingjiang shook his head. “So you plan to deal with two Transcendent Realm experts by yourself?” An Jiu felt that Chu Dingjiang was a completely different man from her father, which was why she had gradually accepted him. However, now she felt that it was not good for him to silently bear everything alone. “Are you in such a hurry to die?” “Nonsense. Since I cannot fight them head-on, I will outsmart them. Strong martial arts do not mean being without weaknesses.” Chu Dingjiang was in a good mood at seeing her angry expression. “Chu Dingjiang, I have a question for you,” An Jiu said. Seeing her serious expression, Chu Dingjiang also asked earnestly, “What is it?” “You said the Second Prince is not suitable to be Emperor yet. Since that’s the case, and you have medicine, why not use it to prolong the Emperor’s life?” An Jiu tilted her head back, as if trying to see his expression through his hood. Chu Dingjiang had not expected her to ask about this. He remained silent for a moment before saying, “If it were before, I would not have even considered it. I would have directly used the medicine to prolong the Emperor’s life. Before I met you, I thought Heaven had given me a second chance so I could continue to contribute to unifying the land. I thought only a desperate battle would make my life worthwhile. But now my thoughts have changed.” An Jiu did not speak, waiting for him to continue. “Even if you have to fight for this your whole life, you have to leave yourself a bottom line.” Chu Dingjiang reached out and pulled her into his arms, his deep voice close to her ear. “If a person has no feelings, then they’ve lived in vain.” There was a greedy element in human nature; constantly gaining yet never satisfied, even those at the pinnacle of power still felt they lacked many things. From the moment we were born, we were all given gifts by heaven and earth. Some greedily seized power, money, and beauty, enjoying a lifetime of wealth and luxury, yet ultimately felt they had gained nothing, dying with endless regret and loneliness. In truth, what people needed most was companionship. Having someone to grow old with did not guarantee contentment. But without that person, the end would surely be filled with regret. This was the truth Chu Dingjiang had come to understand. No matter how earth-shattering his achievements, he hoped An Jiu would always be within his sight. “I do not understand.” Although An Jiu had also experienced life and death, her experiences were different, making it difficult for her to have any profound insights into life. Besides, she was too lazy to think about it so much. If she were as thoughtful about life as Chu Dingjiang, she would not be so lost until now, only now realizing what she wanted. However, simple thinking had its advantages. Once she set her goal, she ignored all obstacles and headed straight towards it. “Little girl, you do not need to understand these things,” Chu Dingjiang said, releasing her. An Jiu frowned, then steered the conversation back to the previous topic. “Then how do you suggest we outsmart him? That Elder Zhi is cunning and shrewd, just as cunning as you.” Chu Dingjiang leaned slightly forward. He whispered, “The Mei family might not be willing to support the Crown Prince; that’s the key.” Why would the Mei family not support the Crown Prince? An Jiu knew nothing about court politics and was unaware of many things. She could not understand the reason, so she simply stopped thinking about it and patted Chu Dingjiang’s shoulder. “Then it is up to you.” “Let’s go.” Chu Dingjiang took her hand. The two returned side by side. The Second Prince was carefully studying a map of the capital city at his desk, holding a steaming cup of tea. This map was already imprinted in his mind; with his eyes closed, every detail was crystal clear. “Your Highness,” Chu Dingjiang bowed respectfully. An Jiu followed suit. “No need for formalities.” The Second Prince put down his teacup and looked up at the two of them. Chu Dingjiang raised his head. “My Young Lady is worried about me and insists on coming along. I hope Your Highness will grant her permission.” He said this because he did not want the Second Prince to directly bring An Jiu under his command. After all, there was a difference in status between a subordinate and his wife. “You two are such a loving couple; it is truly enviable!” The Second Prince had not thought much of it at the moment, but he welcomed An Jiu’s arrival warmly. “Whatever the reason for Madam Chu’s willingness to help, Zhao Huo will remember this kindness.” “Your Highness is too kind,” Chu Dingjiang said. An Jiu carefully observed the Second Prince for a few moments. After all, if successful, he would be the future Emperor. The Second Prince had not expected this woman to be so bold, staring directly at him without any hesitation. He was not annoyed but rather met her gaze openly. In the dim candlelight, a pair of emotionless, dark eyes was devoid of emotion or murderous intent, yet their gaze felt tangible. The Second Prince felt as if he had one foot in the gates of hell! He needed to muster considerable composure to remain seated. An Jiu, completely unaware of her own strength, looked away after she had seen enough. The Second Prince secretly breathed a sigh of relief, his expression remaining unchanged. Chu Dingjiang, with his keen observation, could not help but probe An Jiu with his mental power. An Jiu glanced at him out of the corner of her eye. Chu Dingjiang quickly withdrew his mental power. Just as he had expected, An Jiu’s mental power had improved again. After the two took their leave and came out of the house, An Jiu asked him, “Why were you probing me just now?” “Your mental power has suddenly advanced again,” Chu Dingjiang was puzzled. “Why?” “Is it strange that this happens to a genius?” An Jiu asked seriously. Chu Dingjiang laughed twice. An Jiu was displeased. “You do not believe me? Countless facts prove that the vast majority of mentally ill patients possess extraordinary talent in a certain field.” “In what area does your talent manifest?” Chu Dingjiang asked with a smile. An Jiu told him firmly and earnestly, “In every aspect.” Chu Dingjiang could not help but want to laugh at her serious expression, but fearing he would annoy her, he suppressed his laughter. “Thank you for your guidance, genius.” An Jiu turned her face away in displeasure. “Do not think I do not know what you are thinking.” The night was hazy. Amidst the tolling of funeral bells, the entire city of Bianjing felt uneasy. A carriage stopped in a ruin in the west of the city. Two burly men dragged a bound woman out of the carriage and threw her into the grass. The woman groaned and struggled violently. Such an ordeal might have caused terror and despair in others, but in her phoenix eyes, all those emotions transformed into anger and sorrow.

chapters.title: Instinct
chapters.content: Anger stemmed from her own powerlessness, and sorrow from the regrets of her life. However, after these emotions subsided, Mei Ruyan’s heart gradually calmed. Perhaps dying like this was for the best, to avoid constantly worrying about those she could never reach. Thinking this, she simply stopped struggling, closed her eyes, and awaited death. For a long time, there was no pain as she had imagined. She slightly opened her eyes and looked up to see two burly men, their bodies stiff, their faces deathly pale, and the light in their eyes quickly fading. Only a few breaths later, the two men collapsed to the ground with a thud. Mei Ruyan rolled over and looked around. A figure carrying a lantern stood not far away in the misty grass. The wind blew, rustling the grass, and the dampness on his blue robe made him appear somewhat heavy. “My Lord,” Mei Ruyan stood up happily. Wei Yuzhi coughed for a while, then came over and untied her. “Why did you not resist? I always thought you had a strong will to live.” “I…” Mei Ruyan did not know how to explain. “Is it because of him?” Wei Yuzhi walked slowly through the grass, his tone flat. “It’s not worth it. He’s never stopped for anyone.” “At least he was sincere to me once!” Mei Ruyan retorted. “Otherwise, he would not have asked me to avenge him.” Mei Ruyan felt that Master Mo said this because he acknowledged their feelings for each other. “Ahem. I have no experience in this area, but logically speaking, if he truly liked and cared for you, should he not prioritize your safety?” Wei Yuzhi turned his head slightly to look at her. “Why would he ask you to avenge him?” Mei Ruyan pursed her lips. “Perhaps he has no experience either.” Wei Yuzhi pondered for a moment, then smiled slightly. “You are right. Before you, he had never liked anyone.” But Wei Yuzhi always felt that liking someone did not require experience; it was an instinct. Just like before, he anticipated his own feelings. He often put An Jiu in a difficult position, but subconsciously, he never wanted to hurt her. Wei Yuzhi withdrew his gaze, thinking, “A woman in love, no matter how clever, worldly, or cunning she was before, is still a moth drawn to a flame! Is Fourteenth Young Lady the same kind of person?” Perhaps even if he got the answer, he would only be an observer. People with high mental strength had a certain precognitive ability regarding certain things. For example, he knew from the first moment he saw An Jiu that this woman would ultimately not belong to him, yet he still uncontrollably sank deeper and deeper into this swamp. In this respect, the only difference between him and Mei Ruyan was that he was very clear-headed. Mei Ruyan broke the silence. “My Lord, will the Crown Prince succeed?” “Are you worried about Hua Rongjian?” Wei Yuzhi asked. “Speaking with you, My Lord, it seems there are never any secrets,” Mei Ruyan smiled. “He’s actually a good person. Knowing I harbored ill intentions, he still tolerated me and treated me well, but… later he seemed to change completely.” “Oh?” Wei Yuzhi’s impression of Hua Rongjian was so-so. If it were not for the fact that he was the second young master of the Hua family, he would not have even noticed this person. Compared to Hua Rongtian’s dazzling brilliance, Hua Rongjian was utterly ordinary. Mei Ruyan sighed and shook her head. “I do not understand either.” When she first met Hua Rongjian, although he acted rudely, he was actually a kind and refined man. Later, something happened to him, and his personality changed drastically, becoming increasingly cruel and sinister. Even though Mei Ruyan had no feelings for him, seeing someone as bright as the sun fall into darkness was unbearable. “Whether the Crown Prince ascends the throne or not is unimportant to the Liao Kingdom.” Wei Yuzhi was only ordered to create chaos in the Song Dynasty; his main task was to find the medicine. “Go to the Liao Kingdom; take this token with you.” Wei Yuzhi paused, taking the jade pendant from his waist and handing it to her. “Thank you, My Lord!” Mei Ruyan was overjoyed, carefully placing the token in her bosom. “Five li north, there’s a mansion. You can use your token to retrieve your horse and leave. The north is in chaos; be careful.” Wei Yuzhi’s face grew increasingly pale, beads of cold sweat appearing on his skin. Mei Ruyan asked worriedly, “Are you alright, My Lord? Should I stay and take care of you for a while?” “No need,” Wei Yuzhi said calmly. “It’s just an old ailment; I will not die. Go.” Mei Ruyan hesitated for a moment, then bowed deeply to Wei Yuzhi and turned to leave. Wei Yuzhi watched her retreating figure, murmuring, “Of all the sufferings in the world, the greatest is the suffering of not getting what you want.” He did not know if he was referring to himself or Mei Ruyan. The funeral bells tolled until dawn. A messenger was sent from the palace to the Second Prince’s residence, and soon the steward delivered it to the city gate. The Second Prince asked Chu Dingjiang, “My Lord, shall we go or not?” Currently, neither the Crown Prince nor the Second Prince dared to make any major moves, both vying for legitimacy. Neither wanted to be seen as a usurper, bearing eternal infamy. “Your Highness must go,” Chu Dingjiang affirmed. Chu Dingjiang’s release of the news of the Emperor’s death was not primarily to force the still-observant court officials to take sides, but rather to make the military generals supporting the Second Prince understand that the tide had turned, that they had begun their actions, and that success would make them meritorious ministers; failure would label them usurpers and traitors. One step forward, heaven; one step back, hell. The Second Prince hesitated. “The court officials…” “His Majesty not once bestowed upon Your Highness a secret imperial edict, did he not?” Chu Dingjiang smiled slightly. “My father knows the Crown Prince’s character well. That edict was merely a life-saving measure, given in case the Crown Prince could not tolerate me.” Now, this edict was something the Second Prince could not afford to lose, yet also felt like a hot potato. He desired the throne above all others, and this imperial edict was proof of his illegitimacy. The late Emperor had not intended for him to be the one to ascend the throne. But if he destroyed it now and his efforts failed, would he have no last straw to cling to? Chu Dingjiang asked, “How many people know the contents of this imperial edict?” The Second Prince’s eyes lit up. “What do you mean, My Lord?” Chu Dingjiang took a bright yellow silk scroll from his robes and spread it out on the table. The Second Prince, upon reading it, was utterly shocked. His hands trembled as he held up the imperial edict. “This…this is…!” The edict read clearly: “The late Emperor has suddenly passed away, returning to the Five Elements. I, by the grace of Heaven and the blessings of past sages, and in accordance with the late Emperor’s will… Deeply considering the weight of this entrustment, and with a heart full of diligence, I deem the Second Prince, Zhao Huo, benevolent, wise, filial, and fraternal, and beloved by the people. He is fit to ascend the throne. All civil and military officials, both inside and outside the court, shall work together to assist in governing and to bring peace to our people. Therefore, I respectfully inform Heaven and Earth today that I have ascended the throne to ensure a prosperous and harmonious reign… Next year shall be designated as the first year of Yuan Ning. A general amnesty is hereby granted to allow the people a fresh start…” This edict was written by a Hanlin Academy Attendant. The Second Prince had seen the seal on the back countless times and could not find any flaws. If he were told now that the edict was genuine, he would not doubt it. “This Hanlin Academy Attendant is willing to submit to Your Highness,” Chu Dingjiang said. Upon hearing this, the Second Prince immediately sobered up and calmed his agitated emotions. Since Chu Dingjiang said this person had surrendered, it meant the edict was not the Emperor’s will. “This edict is fake?” Chu Dingjiang replied, “It can be said to be true, or it can be said to be false.” The Second Prince asked in confusion, “What do you mean?”

chapters.title: Husband and Wife
chapters.content: “The imperial seal is genuine. His Majesty did indeed summon the Hanlin Academy Attendant a few days ago, and the handwriting on this edict is indeed that of the Hanlin Academy Attendant,” Chu Dingjiang said. The Second Prince understood. “Only the content is not Father’s original edict.” He did not know how Chu Dingjiang and the others had managed this, but his father still showed no intention of making him Emperor, which left the Second Prince feeling quite disappointed. However, this disappointment did not last long. “A will must be written with at least two high-ranking officials present. If not, the credibility of the will is greatly reduced.” Chu Dingjiang said, “Your Highness need not worry. With two pillars of the state, Prime Minister Hua and Grand Marshal, as witnesses, this imperial edict is an undeniable fact. Your Highness leading troops to the palace is perfectly justified.” “How did you manage this, My Lord?” The Second Prince was extremely surprised, as if Chu Dingjiang had paved a smooth road ahead, and those obstacles he once thought were insurmountable had vanished without a trace! This pleased the Second Prince, but also filled him with apprehension. After all, a subject whose talent far surpassed his own was difficult to control; he might easily become a mere puppet in name only! “There is something I must ask Your Highness to forgive.” Chu Dingjiang suddenly knelt on one knee. An Jiu was slightly surprised, hesitated for a moment, and then knelt after him. This was the first time she had shown submission to someone since arriving in this world, but it was not of her own volition. The Second Prince slowly sat down, looking at him and asking in a deep voice, “What is it?” “The Grand Marshal has a daughter who is of marriageable age,” Chu Dingjiang said tactfully. The Second Prince’s expression darkened slightly; young couples were usually very close. The Second Prince’s wife came from a declining noble family and was two years older than the Second Prince. Aside from her family background, which offered no advantage to the prince, she was exceptionally talented. She was kind, well-educated, and worldly-wise and had already gained fame for her talent in her youth, excelling in music, Weiqi, calligraphy, and painting, especially poetry. While not a stunning beauty, she was certainly elegant and graceful. It was difficult to dislike such a sensible and understanding woman. The Second Prince had been married to her for less than two years, and their love was still strong. Asking him to depose his first wife for the throne was absolutely out of the question! If he had to sacrifice his wife to obtain the throne, what would be the point of his pathetic fight for it? The Second Prince remained silent for a moment before speaking, “What does the Grand Marshal mean…? What rank would be appropriate?” Chu Dingjiang, sensing the Second Prince’s misunderstanding from his tone, explained, “Even with the greatest audacity, how could the Grand Marshal dare to use his merits to coerce the Emperor? He’s seeking a position second only to the Empress for his daughter.” The Imperial Noble Consort. The Second Prince remained somewhat displeased. The Imperial Noble Consort was essentially a secondary wife. In ordinary noble families, a secondary wife posed a significant threat to the primary wife’s status. However, in the royal family, family matters were matters of the realm, with strict rules and clear hierarchical boundaries. The Empress was the Empress, and even though the Imperial Noble Consort was equivalent to a secondary wife, she was still inferior to the Empress in every aspect. “Your Highness,” Chu Dingjiang advised, “those who achieve great things do not concern themselves with trifles. A mere rank can bring considerable benefits. The situation is urgent; Your Highness should reconsider.” The Second Prince did not hesitate for long. Having another Imperial Concubine might displease his wife, but considering her understanding and sensible nature, it was simply another woman by his side. “I will immediately send someone to inform the Grand Marshal that the betrothal will be presented tomorrow.” The Second Prince had never met the Grand Marshal’s daughter, but he had heard of her; she was a free-spirited and efficient woman. Such a background and character would be suitable to assist his wife. Besides, the Grand Marshal was taking a great risk, practically entrusting his entire family’s lives to him; making this request was not unreasonable. “Your Highness is wise.” Chu Dingjiang breathed a sigh of relief. He had truly feared that the Second Prince might act rashly in the heat of the moment, preferring death to submission. To appease the Second Prince, he quickly added, “The Grand Marshal is a pragmatic man. He says he is too old and fears he will be unable to continue serving the country after Your Highness ascends the throne. His sons are mostly unworthy, and he fears the family’s decline. Therefore, he devised this plan. The Grand Marshal’s concerns are not without merit; please forgive him, Your Highness.” The power to mobilize troops in the Song Dynasty rested with the Privy Council, but the Grand Marshal truly commanded the army. In these chaotic times, the Grand Marshal could mobilize troops even without bypassing the Privy Council. Moreover, those supporting the Second Prince include not only military generals but also Prime Minister Hua and his eldest son, who hold important positions in the Privy Council. The Grand Marshal understood the principle of “a new Emperor, a new court” and planned to relinquish military power immediately after the change of dynasty to avoid becoming too conspicuous and facing repercussions from the new Emperor. This was clearly an attitude of humbly seeking favor from the Emperor, which made the Second Prince feel slightly better, and his expression relaxed slightly. “Please rise, My Lord.” “Thank you, Your Highness.” Chu Dingjiang stood up. An Jiu also consciously followed suit. The Second Prince could not help but glance at her again, slightly surprised. This woman clearly had a tangible gaze and a very strong presence, yet when she was silent and did not meet his gaze, she was like air!

chapters.title: Brainwashing
chapters.content: The Second Prince tapped his fingers lightly on the table. “My biggest worry right now is that the Konghe Token will fall into the Crown Prince’s hands.” “Your Highness need not worry about this,” Chu Dingjiang said. The Second Prince raised an eyebrow, thinking, “Could it be that you’ve even dealt with the Konghe Army?” Chu Dingjiang did not bother to guess the Second Prince’s thoughts and said directly, “The Konghe Army is no longer as powerful as it once was. Over a hundred defected the moment they learned of His Majesty’s passing. Some followed me and surrendered to Your Highness, while the rest split into several factions. Not all of them may be willing to follow the Crown Prince. Therefore, even if he obtains the Konghe Token, the forces he can mobilize are entirely within Your Highness’s capabilities.” The Second Prince paused, his face filled with surprise. He had considered many possibilities, but he had never expected things to turn out this way! For the Song Dynasty, the Konghe Army was undoubtedly a powerful force protecting the nation. The Song Dynasty’s rise and fall since its founding could be described as “success and failure both stemming from the Konghe Army.” After the Second Prince harbored ambitions to usurp the throne, his greatest fear was the Konghe Army. He had invested considerable effort in trying to obtain the Konghe Token, but to this day, he had not even seen what it looked like. This was good news, but he could not immediately accept reality. When the Second Prince was seven or eight years old, he always thought the Song Dynasty was very wealthy, but as he grew up, he learned that the national treasury was often empty. It was like thinking he was a rich second-generation heir, only to find out when he was about to inherit the family business that his family had been borrowing money from others. And the matter that Chu Dingjiang spoke of so casually shocked the Second Prince even more than when he learned of the empty treasury! “Why?” the Second Prince murmured. Chu Dingjiang remained silent for a moment, then said, “The reason the Konghe Army has fallen into disarray is because it has long lost its sense of honor.” During the Chenqiao Mutiny, the Konghe Army seemed to be loyal only to Emperor Taizu, but in reality, they fought for the establishment of a nation. While Taizu was alive, the Konghe Army was a divine weapon, invincible and unstoppable. Every assassin within the organization, though living in darkness and leaving only a soul bell after death, experienced immense glory and exhilaration in life. Later, the Konghe Army internally betrayed its members, supporting Emperor Taizong and secretly plotting to assassinate Taizu, successfully seizing the throne. One’s character determined how one saw the world. Taizu became Emperor because of the Konghe Army’s betrayal. After ascending the throne, he constantly worried about becoming the next Taizu, so he began to control and suppress the Konghe Army. He feared that being too hasty would provoke a rebellion by the Konghe Army, so all his actions were cautious, gradually nurturing and controlling this iron-blooded fighting force. After his death, his will was left to the next Emperor. From that moment on, the fate of the Konghe Army was sealed. These were secrets the royal family kept hidden from outsiders. The Second Prince could roughly guess the reason, knowing now was not the time for sentimentality, and could only sigh. The proverb “the bow is put away when the birds are gone, the dog is cooked when the rabbit is dead” played out endlessly. The Second Prince composed himself and summoned all his advisors to discuss the details of their journey to the palace for the funeral before dawn. After the discussion, Chu Dingjiang led An Jiu to make the arrangements. There was one thing about the Second Prince that Chu Dingjiang greatly admired: although he had only served the Second Prince for a short time, at this crucial moment, the Second Prince dared to entrust him with many vital matters. Chu Dingjiang and An Jiu sped through the night, the two remaining silent. They stopped outside the imperial city for a temporary rest and preparation. “The Second Prince is indeed different,” An Jiu said, checking her equipment. Chu Dingjiang casually replied, “Just for that kind of boldness, I am sure I was not wrong about him.” “Are all people who do great things this unconcerned with trivialities?” An Jiu found it hard to understand. A man so readily accepting a woman he’d never even met—there was no attraction involved; it was merely a transaction. Chu Dingjiang paused for a moment, then chuckled. “I do have some principles. Ah Jiu, that’s the highest position in the world. To sit on it, one must endure what ordinary people cannot. Compared to other things, accepting a woman is the simplest. I do not need power or status, so I can be more particular about feelings.” An Jiu nodded in satisfaction. “Do you know the difference between prostitution and a one-night stand?” Chu Dingjiang replied helplessly, “No.” “Most prostitution is simply to satisfy desire, while most one-night stands are because of desire for a particular person. Both are animal instincts, but the difference is that the former is lower animal behavior, while the latter is closer to higher animal behavior,” An Jiu summarized. “What do you mean by that?” Chu Dingjiang brushed off his hood, looking at her with interest. “The higher the IQ, the more selective one is when choosing a partner, and the higher the loyalty to one’s partner. This is behavior possessed by higher animals.” An Jiu gave him a meaningful look. Chu Dingjiang chuckled softly, reached out and embraced her, then leaped onto the palace wall. An Jiu looked up at his stubble-covered chin, frowning as she wondered if the brainwashing had actually worked. His words were too roundabout and uninteresting; hints and such were definitely not her style.

chapters.title: Palace Coup
chapters.content: A sliver of dawn appeared on the horizon. A large-scale change of guard took place at the palace gates. The changing guards presented their tokens and began the handover. A moment after the change of guard, the Second Prince led two thousand men from the north city. The iron cavalry galloped along the stone-paved road, their thunderous roar echoing like war drums, and soon appeared before the Vermilion Bird Gate. The city guards, seeing the Second Prince’s banner, immediately opened the city gates. The two thousand men entered the first palace gate without hindrance. The guards at the second palace gate, seeing the large force approaching, were greatly alarmed and immediately went into battle alert. “Halt!” a guard at the palace gate shouted. However, the newcomers showed no sign of stopping. “His Majesty has passed away. We request that the Second Prince disarm and enter the palace!” The guards coldly blocked their path. The situation was clear: the Second Prince was plotting a rebellion. These guards, temporarily replaced by the Crown Prince’s men, naturally had no friendly attitude towards the Second Prince. Tensions were high between the two sides. Some ministers who had just arrived at the palace gates, fearing they would be caught in the crossfire, stopped their carriages at a distance to observe. The Second Prince, Zhao Huo, sat upright on his horse, his eyes downcast over the people blocking his path. A rider stepped forward from behind him, the officer on horseback producing a token. “Change of shifts.” The token presented was indeed a standard one, but they were the Second Prince’s men. Once the shift changed, the palace gates would fall under his control. In this critical situation, how could the guards willingly relinquish control? Zhao Huo, however, was merely making a gesture; he had no intention of easily controlling the gates. “Blocking my way, refusing to change shifts, what are your intentions?!” He roared, “I have my father’s edict! Who dares to stop me?!” As soon as he finished speaking, his long sword was drawn, and the guard, before he could react, was already bleeding profusely. This action served as a signal; the two sides clashed, weapons drawn, and a fierce battle ensued. One man rushed back to report the news. Inside the Dragon Palace, mourning clothes hung low. The Crown Prince, dressed in mourning attire, stood in the hall, his eyes red. Many civil and military officials, after paying their respects, offered words of comfort and condolences. “Report—” A guard rushed to the outside of the hall, bowing respectfully. “Your Highness, the Second Prince has led his men in and has reached the Baohua Gate.” The hall fell silent. “Hmph, he dares!” The Crown Prince sneered, then raised his voice, “Commander, summon the Tianwu Army to meet them in battle!” The Tianwu Army was the Imperial Guard’s designation, divided into the Southern and Northern Camps. The Northern Camp, led by the Second Prince, belonged to the Tianwu Army. “Yes!” The Commander accepted the order and went out to give the command. The old eunuch, who had been kneeling before the coffin, slowly stood up, his hair and eyebrows snow-white. “Your Highness.” The Crown Prince turned around, his expression softening. “This is the Konghe Decree. His Majesty is gone; it should be kept by the new Emperor.” The old eunuch took a brocade pouch from his sleeve and handed it to the Crown Prince. Prime Minister Hua glanced at the Grand Marshal out of the corner of his eye. The two exchanged a quick look, understanding each other implicitly, and neither made a move. “Did His Majesty leave a will?” someone asked. The Crown Prince gave the man a cold look. The old eunuch said, “His Majesty has passed away; naturally, the Crown Prince will ascend the throne. Does anyone have any objections?” Everyone knew the old eunuch’s identity. He was Feng Shi, who had served the previous Emperor since childhood and then the current Emperor, holding a very important position in the palace. The man who had asked the question broke out in a cold sweat. “Your subject has no objections. Please, Your Highness, understand.” “I know you have no objections.” The Crown Prince’s gaze slowly swept over the ministers in the hall. “Those who truly have objections would not be busy courting death like you.” White mourning clothes fluttered, and the hall fell silent. Feng Shi broke the silence, “Your Highness holds the Konghe Token. With just a command, the Konghe Army will obey.” The Crown Prince, having frequent access to court secrets, knew far more about the Konghe Army than the Second Prince. He knew their strength was greatly diminished, so he did not place much hope in this unstable force. However, it was a symbol of status. Since the founding of the Song Dynasty, only the Emperor could hold the Konghe Token. Therefore, holding this small token, the Crown Prince could not suppress his excitement, a slight smile appearing on his face. An Jiu and Chu Dingjiang concealed their presence, hiding in a side hall. An Jiu peeked through the crack in the door at the Crown Prince standing in the center of the crowd. His noble and dignified bearing betrayed no hint of his dissolute lifestyle; in fact, his composed demeanor inspired a strange sense of trust. An Jiu thought to herself, “Talent aside, these people certainly have the air of emperors!” However, her attention did not linger on the Crown Prince for long; it was quickly drawn to the snow-white-haired old eunuch beside him. The old eunuch had deep, unfathomable eyes and a restrained glint in his eyes. He appeared to be in his seventies, yet his movements showed no signs of age. An Jiu knew that this was a master of the Transcendent Realm hidden deep within the inner palace… To avoid alerting him, An Jiu could not use her mental power to investigate. She could only observe so much from the surface, so she quickly looked away. After scanning the hall, she finally spotted a familiar figure in a corner. Elder Zhi was at least ten years younger than Feng Shi, but his thin, withered frame made him appear older than Feng Shi.

chapters.title: A Great Battle Imminent
chapters.content: With the arrival of the Tianwu Army’s southern camp, shouts of battle filled the air, bringing a clandestine struggle into the open. The Crown Prince and the Second Prince had finally reached a point of no return. The Crown Prince gazed at the dim light outside, his eyes cold and calculating. As the Crown Prince, he possessed far more advantages than the Second Prince. He commanded hundreds of officials throughout the Eastern Palace, along with nearly a thousand guards. He had also cultivated relationships with many civil and military officials. However, the Second Prince, with the blood of a military family flowing through his veins, possessed a more warrior-like demeanor that appealed to the generals—something the Crown Prince greatly feared. However, what concerned him even more was a secret edict his father had given the Second Prince. What exactly was the content of that edict? Was it truly about deposing the eldest son and establishing the younger one in favor? Otherwise, how could the Second Prince have dared to so boldly lead troops to force the palace? But according to several ministers, this was not the case! The Emperor’s death was sudden. Only the eunuch from the Gushe Palace attended to him; even the Crown Prince did not have time to see him one last time. According to the eunuch’s message, the Emperor only mentioned leaving a will a few days prior, but the Crown Prince searched the entire palace and could not find it. Even the attendant who wrote the will had disappeared! The ministers who heard the will before the Emperor’s bedchamber said that the Emperor said: “The Crown Prince has ascended the throne; all ministers should do their utmost to assist him.” The Crown Prince’s lips tightened, his gaze deepened, and he suddenly said, “Bring me my armor!” The echo repeated itself throughout the hall. The eunuch beside the Crown Prince bowed and withdrew. An official in the hall advised, “Your Highness, you mustn’t!” The Crown Prince did not answer. He was never one to make decisions, but once he made up his mind, no one could sway him! Knowing he could not stop him, Feng Shi said, “Your Highness, order the Konghe Army to the battlefield as well.” “Just what I wanted!” As soon as the Crown Prince finished speaking, dozens of dark figures landed in the hall one after another. With a crane’s cry, the figures, like ghosts in the night, gathered in the Dragon Palace. In just a few breaths, there were already fifty or sixty people. The officials stared in disbelief at this scene. This was the first time they had witnessed the legendary Konghe Army, actually existing and always by their side. An Jiu noticed the figures closest to the Crown Prince and suddenly realized they were all Chu Dingjiang’s men! Previously, she and Sui Yuntong were responsible for protecting the Crown Prince, but Chu Dingjiang had someone take their place, allowing them to escape. So, Chu Dingjiang had planned this all along? An Jiu could not help but glance at him. Chu Dingjiang seemed to know what she was thinking and gently patted the back of her head. After the armor was retrieved, the Crown Prince moved to a side hall to change. Chu Dingjiang, carrying An Jiu, climbed onto the roof beam. Looking down, An Jiu saw that Feng Shi was following the Crown Prince closely. Besides him, there were several Eastern Palace guards. These guards were the Crown Prince’s private force; even if Chu Dingjiang had men in the Dragon Martial Guards, they could not possibly kill the Crown Prince in one fell swoop. By the time the Crown Prince was dressed, nearly two hundred members of the Konghe Army had gathered in the hall, all wearing ghost-face masks. The Mei family members among them saw Elder Zhi as soon as they entered and naturally chose the closest spot to him when choosing their positions. Feng Shi, with his snow-white hair and eyebrows, looked no different from an ordinary eunuch. Chu Dingjiang and An Jiu could not sense any mental power or internal strength from him, which only made him seem unfathomable. Chu Dingjiang had fought Feng Shi before and was injured in his attack, and was still not fully healed. Facing him again, he had no confidence in defeating him. The Crown Prince, having changed into his armor, led a large entourage towards Baohua Gate, leaving behind a room full of anxious ministers. Prime Minister Hua and the Grand Marshal breathed a sigh of relief. An Jiu pointed to the main hall. Chu Dingjiang understood and led her back to their original spot to continue spying. “Elder Zhi went along too,” An Jiu said in a low voice. At this time, there were no experts in the main hall or side halls, only some guards of first or second rank strength outside. Chu Dingjiang grasped her hand and said, “Let’s go. I will distract Feng Shi, and you deal with Elder Zhi, creating an opportunity for them.” An Jiu naturally knew who he meant by “them,” but she had some doubts. “Elder Zhi is practically my teacher. Are you really that confident I can defeat him?” Chu Dingjiang thought she misunderstood and explained, “Elder Zhi is selfish, but he’s obsessed with archery. He did not hesitate to cripple your meridians to reach the pinnacle of archery because he felt the peak was within reach. In the past two years, his mental state has deteriorated significantly. Since you surpass him in archery, he definitely will not kill you.” “I will distract Feng Shi,” An Jiu said. Chu Dingjiang paused for a moment. Seeing that he did not answer, An Jiu repeated herself confidently, “I will distract Feng Shi. I know your internal strength and mental power have declined significantly; you are no match for Feng Shi.” Chu Dingjiang was moved and wanted to embrace her, but in the end, he flicked her forehead with his finger. “You are still so unpleasant to talk to! Just you wait and see. I fought Feng Shi before; he’s still recovering from his injuries. Even if my skills are not what they used to be, he’s still no match for me.”

chapters.title: Subduing the Dragon (1)
chapters.content: An Jiu looked up at his confident expression, seemingly without a trace of suspicion, and did not insist too much. She was still shocked that she had said such a thing. Even Chu Dingjiang could not handle this person; if she rushed in, she would probably have a hard time surviving. But why would she want to go and die? “You and Elder Zhi will face off with bows. If there’s an opportunity, shoot the Crown Prince,” Chu Dingjiang said. “Alright,” An Jiu said. Chu Dingjiang picked her up and leaped out of the side hall. The Second Prince had already led his cavalry into Baohua Gate, fighting a large number of guards. Just as the guards were losing ground, the Crown Prince arrived with reinforcements. Amidst the chaos, the Crown Prince spotted the Second Prince locked in fierce combat and roared, “Father’s body is barely cold, and you dare to force the abdication!” The Second Prince, his face stained with blood, laughed and replied, “I led my troops into the palace with Father’s will. What do you intend to do by stopping me, Crown Prince?” “What do you intend to do? Since you’ve plotted rebellion, do not blame your elder brother for being ruthless.” The Crown Prince’s expression suddenly changed. He brandished his sword at the Second Prince and coldly commanded, “Konghe Army, heed my order! Slay this traitor!” No one answered. Yet, at his command, more than ten dark figures leaped towards the Second Prince. The Crown Prince watched the lightning-fast attack, a cruel smile playing on his lips. However, more than ten soldiers beside the Second Prince suddenly sprang into action, forcefully blocking the Konghe Army assassins. Then the Konghe Army dispatched more than ten assassins, but the Second Prince’s forces met them with an equal number of men. Then came the third batch, the fourth batch… The Crown Prince’s expression darkened slightly. “What’s going on?” He had been closely monitoring the Second Prince for years; he should not have had the opportunity to cultivate and recruit such a large number of assassins by his side. “Someone in the Konghe Army has betrayed us,” Feng Shi stated calmly. “Your Highness has another trump card.” The Crown Prince glanced at him. Feng Shi turned to Elder Zhi. The Crown Prince’s eyes showed doubt. Elder Zhi had been quite talented in his younger days and was now a master at Zishan Hall. He vaguely remembered him and wondered what a scholar with no physical strength could do. But the next moment, he knew he was wrong. Elder Zhi slowly straightened his hunched back. It was an extremely ordinary movement, yet it felt as if a giant mountain had stood before him. “Greetings, Your Highness.” Elder Zhi bowed respectfully. The Crown Prince steadied himself and reached out to help him up. “There’s no need for formalities on the battlefield. Use whatever skills you have, as long as you can kill that traitor!” Just as Chu Dingjiang had expected, Elder Zhi still harbored a sliver of hesitation. He had observed the character of both the Crown Prince and the Second Prince; neither was a good person, and the chances of the Mei family rising again after falling into either of their hands were slim. Now, he had to make a decision. Many thoughts flashed through Elder Zhi’s mind before he finally replied, “Yes.” He took a bow and arrow from a member of the Konghe Army and, through the fighting crowd, drew the bowstring. A faint blue light flowed from his fingertips, swirling around the arrow and finally converging into a small ball of light at the arrowhead. That fierce aura was awe-inspiring. The Crown Prince’s eyes lit up; he guessed this was most likely the legendary “Startling the String”! With one arrow, he refused to believe the Second Prince would survive! The arrow was on the bowstring. Chu Dingjiang arrived with An Jiu just in time to witness this critical moment. “Intercept his arrow!” Chu Dingjiang never doubted An Jiu’s strength. In an instant, he chose a relatively good shooting position and placed his hand on her shoulder. An Jiu felt her inner energy flowing into her body continuously. Without thinking, she reached back and untied the Dragon-Subduing Bow.

chapters.title: Subduing the Dragon (2)
chapters.content: A faint aura swirled around the Dragon-Subduing Bow, resembling a burning flame from afar. Chu Dingjiang’s face paled instantly, feeling as if his inner energy was being rapidly drained. The power contained in this arrow was astonishing; even those engaged in battle clearly felt a threat, as if they would be burned to ashes if they did not escape! This domineering aura swept across most of the palace, and Elder Zhi and Feng Shi, both experts at the Transcendent Realm, naturally noticed it as well. Feng Shi’s gaze shifted slightly, looking at the two people in the distance. Seeing that their arrows were not aimed at the Crown Prince, he calmly withdrew his gaze. His responsibility was to protect the monarch, including the future monarch, so as long as the Crown Prince’s life was not threatened, he only needed to stay by his side; everything else was irrelevant to him. Elder Zhi’s mind only wandered for a moment before quickly focusing again on the bow in his hand, the slightly scattered blue light recondensing. The stalemate did not last long, but it felt incredibly long for both sides. A crane’s cry pierced the sky. A brilliant blue light burst forth, shattering the pre-dawn haze and casting a ghastly blue hue upon everyone’s faces. Immediately afterward, a clear phoenix cry rang out. An Jiu released her grip, and a fiery phoenix, glowing red, shot from her fingertip, swooping down with lightning speed towards the blue light. Two powerful internal energies pressed down, slowing the movements of everyone fighting. The Crown Prince squinted, watching the arrow hidden beneath the blue light rapidly approach the Second Prince. Three hundred paces, two hundred paces, one hundred paces, ninety paces…As the distance closed, his heart leaped. So close, so very close to success! “Your Highness!” cried a guard beside the Second Prince, leaping into the air. In a flash, everyone held their breath; everything seemed frozen, then erupted in an instant. The arrow, imbued with Chu Dingjiang’s full cultivation, collided precisely in mid-air with the arrowhead beneath the blue light, instantly unleashing a raging inferno capable of swallowing a vast lake, like a colossal beast with its gaping maw, swallowing the icy water in an instant. It felt like ten years, yet also like a blink of an eye. The thunderous force seemed to shake the entire imperial city. The entire Bianjing, the entire land of the Song Dynasty, trembled. Hundreds upon hundreds of screams were drowned out by the immense sound; even the Crown Prince, standing hundreds of paces away, felt his internal organs nearly shattered by a tremendous force. The Dragon Palace was instantly illuminated as bright as midday, with white banners fluttering, all the ministers staring in shock at the crimson sky outside. The battlefield was ravaged by two forces, flesh and blood flying everywhere, falling like rain as the light gradually faded. The Crown Prince, pale-faced, stared intently at the center of the battlefield. “Did it succeed?” Feng Shi slowly shook his head. He had seen it clearly. Elder Zhi’s arrow was intercepted thirty paces away. Simultaneously, a ninth-level expert tackled the Second Prince to the ground, unleashing his entire cultivation level to form an invisible shield protecting him. Perhaps the Second Prince’s current condition was even better than the Crown Prince’s. Feng Shi was surprised and curious. Dispersing the cultivation level was self-destructive; at best, it would reduce one to an ordinary person. Yet, the Second Prince had managed to persuade a ninth-level expert, on the verge of reaching the Transcendent Realm, to sacrifice himself! However, he was even more curious about who had fired this astonishing arrow. The aura emanating from the arrow was familiar. It belonged to the Transcendent Realm expert he had fought during his nighttime infiltration of the palace, but the archer was a petite woman. Everyone seemed stunned by this turn of events, staring blankly at the carnage amidst the rain of blood. The ninth-level martial artist, having exhausted his life’s cultivation, slowly rose from the Second Prince’s body. Blood soaked his face covering, and his voice was hoarse. “Your Highness, are you alright?” The Second Prince was covered in blood but unharmed. A sixth-level martial artist, he naturally understood what had just happened. “Go back and rest. If today’s great undertaking succeeds, I will never forget this kindness!” Great kindness needed no words of thanks; the Second Prince’s promise was undoubtedly very sincere. The man did not waste any more words, cupped his hands, and staggered away. “Kill!” The Second Prince’s words shattered the calm. The Crown Prince stared at the blood-stained face, his face ashen, wishing he could personally step forward and fight him. The events that had just occurred left Elder Zhi unable to recover for a long time. Back in Mei Mansion, he knew that forcibly injecting internal energy into that child’s body would destroy her meridians, yet he still did it. Since Mei Yanran wanted her daughter to live like an ordinary person, he could grant that wish. However, only he knew that this was just an excuse. He was willing to ruin a promising martial arts talent from the Mei family, merely to witness Startling the String’s power! In the two years that followed, he comprehended the power of “Starting the String,” but his mental state steadily declined, yet he felt it was all worthwhile. But today, he finally understood how ridiculous he had been. “This is the true ‘Startling the String’…” Elder Zhi murmured, his weathered eyes growing brighter. How could one bring a weapon to its peak power? The wielder’s strength was certainly a crucial factor, but how could one surpass their opponent when their strength was equal? —It was fighting spirit! The pinnacle of all weapons lay in fighting spirit! From that “Startling the String” arrow just now, Elder Zhi did not pay much attention to the powerful internal energy wrapped around the arrow, but he sensed an extremely strong killing intent! As if being stared at by the Grim Reaper, the killing intent swept over him like Death slowly reaching out his hand, making even someone nearing the pinnacle of martial arts feel a chill run down his spine. Chu Dingjiang caught his breath for a moment, feeling his internal energy rapidly recovering. At this moment, he was no match for Feng Shi, but Elder Zhi was in a rare state of enlightenment, and this was an opportunity not to be missed. “I will distract Feng Shi. If Elder Zhi draws his bow again, just dodge.” “Alright,” An Jiu replied. Chu Dingjiang’s figure swept across the battlefield like lightning, his three-chi longsword aimed directly at the Crown Prince’s vitals without any fancy moves. Feng Shi raised an eyebrow, stepped forward, and shielded the Crown Prince behind him. Enlightenment sometimes happened in a flash of inspiration. Elder Zhi, disregarding everything else, immediately seized this fleeting insight, drew his bow, and aimed at the Second Prince again. He did not want to fight to the death for the time being, but rather wanted to gain more insight through the contest. An Jiu’s attention was mostly focused on Chu Dingjiang. He had just had much of his internal energy drained, and this battle would likely be extremely difficult. She felt a growing sense of worry. The Second Prince and his guards also saw the flash of blue light, but as the leader of the attacking force, he could not retreat now. A single burst of energy could quickly wane. Once they retreated, the hope of victory was slim. “Your Highness, we will fight our way through!” shouted a guard beside the Second Prince. If they could not avoid it, their only hope was for a ninth-level martial artist to sacrifice all their cultivation to save their life. An Jiu saw the Second Prince’s predicament, but she knew that Elder Zhi’s inner strength could not possibly recover to its previous fullness in such a short time, and the arrow’s power was unlikely to surpass the previous one. With so many experts fiercely protecting the Second Prince, moving left and right would not be difficult; he would most likely be alright. It was Chu Dingjiang’s situation that was more worrying. An Jiu paused, then drew the Dragon-Subduing Bow again. This time, she was not aiming to fight Elder Zhi, but rather directly at the Crown Prince. Feng Shi was following the Crown Prince closely, undoubtedly to protect him. If she wanted to distract him, the simplest and most direct way was to attack the Crown Prince. The Dragon-Subduing Bow was fitted with a specially made feathered arrow. When fired, the hexagonal arrowhead would spin at high speed, capable of piercing through a human body, leaving a bloody hole. This arrow, inspired by the Liao Kingdom’s blue-fire crossbow, was created by Lou Xiaowu. While not as powerful, it was highly practical. An Jiu concentrated all her mental energy into the arrow. This way, as long as the arrow approached within ten zhang of the target, her mental energy could subdue the target, turning them into a stationary target and preventing anyone nearby from rushing to their aid, thus increasing her accuracy. An Jiu believed that, apart from the three Transcendent Realm experts whose attention was completely elsewhere, no one here could withstand her mental energy. “Archers! Protect His Highness!” a guard shouted. Numerous archers lay prone on the rooftops and walls, all with only one target—the girl with the bow opposite them. Chu Dingjiang successfully distracted Feng Shi, and the assassins lurking on the Crown Prince’s side tensed, preparing to strike. They were the Dragon Martial Guards, and the closest to the Crown Prince were the Eastern Palace’s Dark Guards. They had to find a way to hit him with a single blow! They knew that Chu Dingjiang’s previous attack had exhausted much of his inner strength, and the time they were buying for him was running out. They exchanged glances, deciding on a strategy. In the chaos, no one noticed the subtle movements of these people. Being targeted by hundreds of crossbows forced An Jiu to confront the last task of her previous life: continue shooting her target or temporarily retreat? Life and death hung in the balance. In her previous life, she had not needed to choose, but now she hesitated. Once a person had hope in life, they were reluctant to die. An Jiu had just found meaning in life and was naturally unwilling to die immediately. After a brief struggle, An Jiu decided to retreat. She had just stopped when she caught sight of Feng Shi’s and Chu Dingjiang’s battle reaching a critical point. The two were locked in a fierce fight, their figures obscured. Shooting Feng Shi was clearly not going to be easy. She still needed to target the Crown Prince. An Jiu frowned and scanned the area. If so many archers attacked simultaneously, a hail of arrows would be unavoidable unless she had protective qi. Many thoughts raced through her mind, but her body acted before her consciousness. Drawing the Dragon-Subduing Bow again, An Jiu’s mind was clear, yet her senses were clearer than ever before. She could clearly sense every aura targeting her and seemed to hear the taut bowstrings. The figures of her targets were exceptionally vivid, as if they were right before her eyes. Feng Shi had maintained the upper hand since the start of his fight with Chu Dingjiang. However, being confined to the palace, most assassins were dealt with by other guards. He had not personally taken action in a long time, so his killing intent was far less than Chu Dingjiang’s. Although he had maintained firm control of the battle, he could not kill Chu Dingjiang immediately. Now, noticing An Jiu aiming at the Crown Prince, he lost all will to fight and became even more ruthless. An Jiu knew that if she continued the stalemate, it would be more disadvantageous for Chu Dingjiang. Her goal was to distract Feng Shi, not to ensure the death of the Crown Prince, so after roughly aiming, she immediately released the arrow. However, before she could release it, hundreds of archers had already fired their arrows. Arrows rained down like wasps.

chapters.title: You Can Only Die by My Hand
chapters.content: Although An Jiu’s arrow did not contain internal force, the powerful fluctuations of her mental energy made Feng Shi uneasy. The Crown Prince’s level was only second-tier; even with the Konghe Army surrounding him, they might not be able to avoid the arrow! Chu Dingjiang also noticed the changes around him. He had his back to the battlefield and had not witnessed the events firsthand, but when the arrow, imbued with An Jiu’s mental energy, struck the Crown Prince, and a rain of arrows filled the sky, he understood what had happened without much thought. Too far from An Jiu, Chu Dingjiang could not reach her unless he could teleport. Chu Dingjiang knew An Jiu’s abilities well; this rain of arrows would most likely not harm her, but his breath still inexplicably caught in his throat. For the first time, he felt so timid, afraid to turn around and see the outcome. In the brief moment Feng Shi was distracted, Chu Dingjiang’s sword blazed brightly, unleashing a deadly attack, carrying an unyielding will to fight to the death! Over there, An Jiu was in grave danger. Faced with hundreds of arrows raining down from different directions, she had no way to escape, but being unable to escape did not mean she could not dodge. An Jiu’s mental energy manifested in wisps, her clear senses able to pinpoint the location of most of the arrows. As long as she was not hit in a vital spot, there was still hope for survival. An Jiu stared motionlessly as the arrows approached bit by bit. In the world of mental energy, everything before her seemed incredibly slow; she could even judge a safe position based on the air currents created by the arrows. Just as she dodged an arrow, the barrage of arrows suddenly stopped! An Jiu was slightly startled, instantly enveloped by a familiar aura. The arrows, frozen in mid-air, seemed to be propelled by a tremendous force, rebounding with terrifying power. She turned to look, and in the hazy morning light, a greyish-blue robe fluttered in the wind, his fair face undisguised—it was Wei Yuzhi, the second master of Piaomiao Mountain Mansion. His face was pale, as if he might be swept away by the wind at any moment. “How did you get here?” An Jiu’s mind raced with thoughts. It was clearly Wei Yuzhi who had saved her. She was not ungrateful, but the sudden appearance of a Liao strategist disrupting the Bianjing palace coup was a cause for serious concern. Wei Yuzhi’s lips parted slightly, a trickle of blood flowing from the corner of his mouth. An Jiu frowned, speechless, somewhat confused. “We are enemies; why did you save me? Although with my strength, I do not need your help at all.” Wei Yuzhi smiled suddenly, said nothing, and turned to leave. “Stop!” An Jiu stepped forward, blocking his path. Wei Yuzhi looked at her. He took out a handkerchief and calmly wiped the blood from his mouth. “Unless you tell me why you came here, I cannot let you go!” An Jiu said. The sounds of battle roared behind them, yet Wei Yuzhi remained eternally serene. He paused before replying, “It seems I’ve saved a poisonous snake.” An Jiu remained silent, but her footsteps, blocking his path, did not budge. After a moment of stalemate, Wei Yuzhi smiled faintly. “If you die, it can only be by my hand.” An Jiu stared into his eyes for a long time, then nodded. “I accept this explanation.” The explanation was absurd but honest. If Wei Yuzhi intended to fabricate a lie, an ordinary person would find no flaws. “Master Chu seems to be in a bad situation right now,” Wei Yuzhi reminded her. Wei Yuzhi seemed to be powerless to fight now; this was the perfect opportunity to kill him! She had no concept of morality; she simply did not want to owe him anything. Besides, killing him would take time, and An Jiu did not have that time right now. An Jiu paused, then took a small bottle from her bosom and handed it to him. “There are only three pills inside, a medicine concocted by Mo Sigui. It can heal your injuries, and we will be even.” Ordinary medicines had a negligible effect on damage to mental strength. Wei Yuzhi knew this contained a medicine made with heart’s blood, so he did not pretend and took it. An Jiu leaped away. Wei Yuzhi froze, his face growing paler and paler. After a few breaths, he suddenly vomited a mouthful of dark red blood. He opened the bottle, hesitated slightly, and then put one pill in his mouth. A faint metallic taste of blood lingered between his lips and teeth, a nauseating sensation, but he did not swallow it hastily, letting the medicine linger in his mouth. Thinking that it contained the blood of the Yelu royal family, he felt a surge of pleasure. Wei Yuzhi was a Song person and did not have a strong sense of belonging to the Liao Kingdom. Perhaps this was why Yelu Quancang valued Yelu Huangwu more than him. Sending him to find the medicine was practically entrusting his life to him. Yelu Quancang was indeed decisive and trusted him implicitly, but that was not what he wanted. Wei Yuzhi, confident in his strategic acumen, hoped that one day Yelu Quancang would ascend the throne so he could realize his ambitions. That was why he spared no effort to secure the throne for him. However, reality was never as perfect as imagined. Even with his exceptional talent and strategy, he could not have foreseen that even if he gained Yelu Quancang’s trust, it would not be enough to secure his position in the Liao Kingdom. If he succeeded in seizing the medicine this time, could he enter the Liao court? Even if not, would Yelu Quancang allow him to participate in politics? Wei Yuzhi was not sure. He walked slowly, leisurely strolling amidst the fighting and flames of war. Xiao Shi stood at the entrance of Baohua Palace. On the other side. Although Chu Dingjiang knew that An Jiu’s mental strength was more than enough to handle this scale of arrow rain, she had never experienced it before. Who knew if something unexpected might happen? Thinking of this, Chu Dingjiang’s killing intent grew even more unstoppable. Feng Shi, distracted by blocking An Jiu’s arrow, was now being relentlessly pursued by Chu Dingjiang and was temporarily at a disadvantage. When An Jiu’s arrow came, the guards surrounding the Crown Prince moved, and the assassins hidden among them took the opportunity to approach the Crown Prince, feigning a rescue. He Cai looked at a female archer, signaling her to prepare to act. The female archer was closest to the Crown Prince, but was only at the fourth level. Surrounded by numerous seventh- and eighth-level martial artists, she could not inflict any effective damage on the Crown Prince. However, He Cai needed to disrupt the Crown Prince’s defenses to seize the opportunity to act. The female archer’s eyes flashed with determination as she drew her bow and aimed at the Second Prince amidst the chaos. Those around her were not too surprised. Circumstances created heroes; now, anyone with the ability wanted to show themselves before the Crown Prince. The Crown Prince turned his head to look at the female archer. The Crown Prince was fond of women, but he knew when to stop. He had not paid much attention to the female archer’s curvaceous figure, only noticing an extremely alluring aura about her. However, in an instant, he knew what that aura was! The female archer slightly deflected her arrow, released her grip with two fingers, and her left hand suddenly pointed at the Crown Prince. The Crown Prince met her gaze, clearly seeing the ruthless determination in her eyes. Three short crossbow bolts, illuminated by the morning light, shot towards the Crown Prince’s brow, throat, and chest, respectively. Because of the close proximity, before the Crown Prince could react, the arrows were already a chi away. To ensure his safety, one of the Crown Prince’s bodyguards rushed forward, using his body to block the arrows. There was a traitor among his close guards! The Eastern Palace’s secret guards’ killing intent surged, and two of them drew their swords to kill the female archer. At that moment, two more people suddenly attacked the Crown Prince from the crowd. If an attack had occurred from the outside, the guards would have remained completely calm. However, the sudden rebellion from within disrupted the defenses around the Crown Prince. All opportunities were fleeting! The other hidden assassins immediately rushed forward, but He Cai remained still. She stood on the other side of the Crown Prince, the only one there who followed Chu Dingjiang. Any movement from her would immediately expose her; she needed to wait for her chance. Sure enough, the number of traitors was too large, forcing the Eastern Palace guards to join the fray, protecting the Crown Prince behind them. He Cai, following the shift in formation, successfully approached the Crown Prince. She remained calm, not immediately launching an assassination attempt. On the surface, she appeared no different from the other guards, all on high alert, protecting the Crown Prince. Meanwhile, seven zhang away, Elder Zhi noticed that An Jiu showed no intention of engaging, and his arrow remained unreleased. Seeing An Jiu approaching, Elder Zhi instantly realized that Chu Dingjiang was far more important to An Jiu than the Second Prince. He then changed his aim, pointing the arrow at Chu Dingjiang. Chu Dingjiang and Feng Shi were locked in a fierce and unpredictable battle, their movements swift and elusive, making them incredibly difficult to aim at! An Jiu hesitated, realizing that going over there would only endanger Chu Dingjiang. If she joined the fight with Feng Shi, Elder Zhi, that old fox, might kill them at any moment. Thinking of this, An Jiu immediately found a good position to shoot. “Take out your bow and arrows.” Elder Zhi had now recognized that the one who had just fired the powerful arrow was none other than the Fourteenth Young Lady. The scene of Fourteenth Young Lady shooting an arrow in Mei Mansion flashed through Elder Zhi’s mind. Her aura could completely blend into the darkness, without the slightest ripple, yet it made him feel a tremendous threat. Therefore, even though he knew that An Jiu would no longer be able to fire such a powerful arrow after Chu Dingjiang left, he still chose to confront her. He wanted to know the power of An Jiu’s unarmed arrow. Elder Zhi was practically An Jiu’s master; she had learned archery from him in this world, and even her mental power attack, the “Startling the String,” was taught to her by him. Faced with such a formidable opponent, An Jiu lacked confidence in her ability to win. However, confidence was one thing; fighting with all her might was another. Staring at the eerie blue light, she showed no fear or hesitation. The Dragon-Subduing Bow was in An Jiu’s hands; she seemed to feel its subtle tremor, the bowstring connected to the wielder. She knew it was not fear, but excitement, just like An Jiu’s current state. “You are using internal force; that’s not fair,” An Jiu shouted. Although discussing fairness on the battlefield seemed foolish, An Jiu remembered Chu Dingjiang’s words: Elder Zhi did not really care about this battle, so crucial to the Song Dynasty. He was exceptionally intelligent, but in archery, he was extremely selfish. “Once the inner force has been released, how can it be withdrawn? If you can withstand this arrow from me, I will retire from the world and never concern myself with worldly affairs again.” Elder Zhi’s voice, full of vicissitudes, seemed to echo in her ears.

chapters.title: The Arrow of the Hidden Dragon (1)
chapters.content: Although An Jiu felt that Elder Zhi’s retirement was none of her business, she still had no choice but to draw the Dragon-Subduing Bow. Faced with the powerful, internally charged bowstring, even those with profound internal strength like Chu Dingjiang and Feng Shi might not be able to withstand it. An Jiu certainly did not have that kind of confidence, but she had one strength—she could always keep a clear head no matter what kind of danger she faced. In a short time, countless thoughts flashed through her mind, such as Wei Yuzhi’s powerful and strange mental strength and Sheng Changying’s statement that her mental strength was characterized by concentrated attacks. Therefore, her mental strength’s destructive power should not be weaker than Wei Yuzhi’s. If so, it might not be a dead end. An Jiu pursed her lips slightly, her gaze as dark as the night before dawn. The Dragon-Subduing Bow, shaped like a full moon, surged with murderous intent, as if trying to obscure the rising sun on the horizon. If An Jiu noticed the current state of the Dragon-Subduing Bow, she would be astonished. Originally jet-black and only able to draw one-third of its length, it could now be nearly fully drawn, its surface shimmering with a faint golden-red hue! A tearing pain spread throughout An Jiu’s arm. A murderous aura formed a faint arrow shape between the bowstrings, the small arrowhead seemingly imprisoning countless roaring dragons. However, from the outside, this arrow appeared completely different; to onlookers, An Jiu had merely drawn an empty bow. Elder Zhi knew An Jiu lacked internal energy, so he quietly dissipated two-thirds of his inner force from the arrow. However, his attitude towards this arrow was extremely serious and focused. He knew this was both a beginning and an end. At this crucial moment, he had grasped the essence of the Startling the String, but his mental state had already been breached, and would continue to decline in the future. His pursuit of the way of the bow would be merely form without substance, making it difficult to reach the peak again. A clear and resonant phoenix cry, as if from beyond the heavens, cleaved through all darkness and obstruction. At the same time, An Jiu suddenly released her grip, and countless roars and howls intertwined, like several giant dragons writhing and breaking free from the Dragon-Subduing Bow. They seemed to have been trapped for millennia, carrying boundless rage, slaughter, and exhilaration as they rushed towards their target. Everyone on the other side felt this terrifying, direct force. Elder Zhi froze. He was not suppressed by this power but rather realized that this was actually the mental energy-based “Startling the String” he had concocted! This purely mental energy-based technique had always been useless to him; he had never imagined that he would one day witness such a magnificent arrow! The two arrows collided in mid-air. The dragon roared, cleaving the Phoenix Cry in two, still possessing an unstoppable speed and momentum. In that instant of stunned silence, the Dragon-Subduing Arrow was already upon him. He saw the greatest fear of his life. Several giant dragons opened their jaws, roaring ferociously, ready to devour him in the next moment. He felt his mind go blank, with only the dragon’s tail churning wildly in his consciousness with terrifying power, seemingly determined to shred his awareness. The Crown Prince, not far away, was initially stunned by this scene, then immediately felt the same immense terror that Elder Zhi had witnessed. The mental energy that the arrow had gathered after passing through Elder Zhi had dissipated, and the entangled dragons were finally freed, scattering in all directions. Although this dissipated mental energy lacked a powerful, destructive force, it was enough to strike the consciousness of any martial artist below the seventh rank as if struck by lightning. The Crown Prince swayed precariously. Seeing this, He Cai rushed forward to support him, and then, in a flash of cold light, her sword sliced ​​across his neck.

chapters.title: The Arrow of the Hidden Dragon (2)
chapters.content: The shock of An Jiu’s arrow was far less than the spurt of blood from the Crown Prince’s neck. As soon as He Cai succeeded, the Crown Prince’s guards went berserk, wielding their longswords in a frenzy. Surrounded by dozens of men, He Cai had almost no chance to resist. Her body was instantly pierced by more than ten longswords, blood spurting out, her chest and abdomen riddled with holes like sieves. Feng Shi, seeing the Crown Prince assassinated right before his eyes, was enraged. He let out a shrill cry, his sword flashing even faster. Feng Shi knew that with the Crown Prince dead, he would surely die here if he did not fight his way out. Every Emperor wanted a legitimate claim to the throne and would certainly try to whitewash himself after ascending. As the most credible insider, the Second Prince would absolutely not tolerate Feng Shi. Seeing the Crown Prince dead, the Second Prince suppressed his inner elation and ordered the surrounding Konghe Army to help Chu Dingjiang deal with Feng Shi. However, how could ordinary martial artists interfere in a battle between masters of the Transcendent Realm? The Konghe Army could only clear out the Crown Prince’s remaining followers on the outskirts; they offered no help to Chu Dingjiang. An Jiu paid a heavy price for firing her final Dragon-Subduing Arrow. She stood motionless for a long time, her right arm trembling uncontrollably. Blood oozed from her ears and eyes; the amount was not large, but it looked gruesome against her deathly pale face. Mental energy was not inexhaustible. Like internal energy, excessive depletion caused immense damage to the body. An Jiu’s vision was bloodshot. Looking at the chaotic battlefield in the distance, her mind was in turmoil. When the unease subsided, only one clear thought remained—sleep. I want to sleep… Elder Zhi’s condition seemed slightly better than An Jiu’s; only his eyes were gradually losing their luster, as if wisdom was leaving his body. In the chaotic battlefield, few noticed the change in Elder Zhi and An Jiu. Both were Transcendent Realm experts, so others instinctively avoided them during the fighting. Chu Dingjiang was gradually finding himself outmatched against Feng Shi. If it were not for the initial arrow that drained his inner strength, he might still have a fighting chance. But if things continued, he risked death at any moment. “Where there’s life, there’s hope,” Chu Dingjiang thought, always extremely calm. Taking advantage of a brief opening, he quickly retreated ten chi. Feng Shi, also trying to escape, naturally would not pursue relentlessly and also took the opportunity to retreat. No one present could stop him. He stood on the rooftop, staring down at Chu Dingjiang for a few moments before swiftly leaving. The sun rose. The area in front of Baohua Gate gradually returned to calm. Rivers of blood flowed, the stench filled the air, and the sky above the palace was bathed in a crimson glow. Chu Dingjiang turned around and saw An Jiu standing in a pool of blood, leaning on the Dragon-Subduing Bow, like a stone monument. His heart sank slightly. Using his remaining inner strength, he stood before An Jiu in the blink of an eye, calling out in a hoarse voice, “Ah Jiu.” An Jiu slightly raised her head. The morning breeze was cool, carrying a strong stench of blood. Chu Dingjiang’s robe was already torn to shreds, his strong body clad in a tight-fitting outfit. There were over a dozen wounds of varying depths on his chest and arms, some still bleeding, but An Jiu knew these were superficial wounds; his condition was not too bad. “Hi.” She grinned, her hair fluttering in the morning breeze, reflecting on her pale face, creating a breathtaking beauty. However, the smile froze on her face the next moment, and her entire body fell backward. “Ah Jiu!” Chu Dingjiang grabbed her, the small wound on his arm that had already congealed reopening, blood gushing out again, soaking both of their black robes.

chapters.title: Wounds
chapters.content: The chaotic battlefield behind him could no longer shake Chu Dingjiang; his eyes, ears, and heart were filled with An Jiu. He barely regained his senses from the shock and heartache, found three pills for her to take, and then quickly led her away from the palace, rushing back to Shayun Residence in Mei Mansion. The lake in Mei Mansion was shrouded in mist as usual, the bloody stench of the recent battle still lingering in the air. The two boarded a boat and landed on the island. The small boat darted swiftly across the water, Chu Dingjiang frequently glancing down at An Jiu’s condition. The damage to one’s mental energy was no small matter; at best, it would take months to heal; at worst, it could lead to mental breakdown or death. Chu Dingjiang was certain that An Jiu had fainted due to a sudden depletion of her mental energy. If there were no serious consequences, An Jiu would wake up naturally; however, if she had been severely injured, the only physician he could think of in the world capable of treating her injuries was Mo Sigui. Regardless, he needed to find a quiet place nearby, and Mei Mansion was the best choice. “My Lord!” Sui Yuntong greeted him as soon as the boat docked. Chu Dingjiang did not speak, casually tossing the oars on the shore and carrying An Jiu back to her room. Before Sui Yuntong could ask what had happened, only a blur remained before his eyes. Seeing the injuries on the two, he guessed that the war in Bianjing was nearing its end; otherwise, he could not imagine who could have injured two Transcendent Realm cultivators like this. Sunlight broke through the clouds, casting a golden glow. Light streamed in through the latticed window, scattering wisps of dust in the beams. Chu Dingjiang had already placed An Jiu on the bed and bent down to check her pulse. He was skilled at treating external injuries but helpless against internal ones, let alone such mysterious mental power! He frowned and checked for a long time, only feeling half relieved after confirming her pulse was normal. “My Lord, please have your wound bandaged first,” Sui Yuntong said, carrying a medicine box. Chu Dingjiang remained silent for a long time before turning around and saying, “Watch over her for a while.” “Yes,” Sui Yuntong replied. Chu Dingjiang strode away with the medicine box. Sui Yuntong was filled with doubt. An Jiu, lying on the bed, had no external injuries whatsoever and even a slight smile on her face.
