If it were not for Chu Dingjiang’s extremely low-key demeanor, he would not have doubted that An Jiu was simply asleep. Chu Dingjiang did not stay away for long. After only a short while, he tidied himself up, wearing a wide-sleeved robe, his black hair flowing freely, and walked in. Chu Dingjiang’s attire was always mysterious and restrained, mostly consisting of a conservative, close-fitting outfit, with a cloak covering his entire body. This was the first time Sui Yuntong had seen him dressed so casually, and he felt that the person before him exuded an ancient aura, as if he had stepped out of the distant past. Chu Dingjiang sat motionless on the embroidered stool before the bed, his robes draped to the floor, his posture upright and powerful, a perfect blend of refinement and ruggedness. Sui Yuntong looked at this still scene, feeling the unconscious pressure emanating from Chu Dingjiang. He struggled for a moment, finally mustering the courage to ask, “My Lord, what happened to Fourteenth?” Chu Dingjiang moved slightly, and after a long pause, replied, “Her mental energy is depleted. Go and fetch Mo Xiaoyao.” Mo Xiaoyao was Mo Sigui’s apprentice. Sui Yuntong thought to himself that Mo Xiaoyao was not even half-baked; how could he possibly cure An Jiu? Despite his doubts, Chu Dingjiang’s words were always unquestionable, so he did not ask any more questions and immediately went to find Mo Xiaoyao. A short while later. Sui Yuntong entered with a human and a tiger. Da Jiu, smelling An Jiu’s scent, happily rushed to the bedside, patting her arm with its chubby paws. After receiving no response for a while, it tilted its head, struggling to think with its not-so-bright brain. “Do you know how to find Mo Sigui?” Chu Dingjiang turned and asked Mo Xiaoyao.

chapters.title: Unbreakable (1)
chapters.content: Mo Xiaoyao said, “The master did not say how to contact him, but Da Jiu is a tracking tiger, so he should be able to find him.” Chu Dingjiang looked at the tiger with a silly expression and hesitated. He knew that Da Jiu and Xiao Yue were tracking tigers raised by Mo Sigui, but Da Jiu was specifically used to track An Jiu’s whereabouts. Whether it could find Mo Sigui was still unknown. Perhaps it had some connection with Xiao Yue, but no one knew how strong that connection was. “Go on with your work,” Chu Dingjiang said. Mo Xiaoyao glanced at Da Jiu and, seeing that it did not intend to leave, went out alone. Sui Yuntong guessed Chu Dingjiang’s worries: “My Lord, you stay and guard the Fourteenth. I will take Da Jiu to find the Divine Physician.” Chu Dingjiang nodded, “Alright, can you control this tiger?” “As long as there is food, it is easy to control.” Sui Yuntong smiled and stepped forward to rub Da Jiu’s head, then took out a poison pill and waved it near its nose. Lost in thought, Da Jiu followed him out, a look of pure bliss on its face. Chu Dingjiang rubbed his temples, his expression complex. He wondered if this tiger’s gluttony had also come from An Jiu. The sun set in the west; the moon rose in the east. Chu Dingjiang remained motionless, staring at An Jiu, like an unyielding mountain. When Zhu Pianxian and Sheng Changying entered, they saw this frozen scene. “Dingjiang,” Sheng Changying said. Chu Dingjiang’s clothes fluttered slightly, and he turned his head, revealing a profile. “You’ve come.” The two walked to the bedside and looked at An Jiu lying on it. Sheng Changying said, “She looks quite well; it seems she’s alright.” Chu Dingjiang smiled at this. “No need for words of comfort. I can handle whatever comes my way. If she really does not wake up, I need to be even better. Only when I am better can I take good care of her.” He was a man of calm to the point of being cold-blooded, but as he spoke these words, his whole body trembled slightly. No one noticed; only he knew that these were the words that truly comforted him. Sheng Changying, who knew Chu Dingjiang somewhat, gave him a deep look and said, “It’s best if you think this way.” Zhu Pianxian suddenly asked, “Was it Elder Zhi’s doing?” Chu Dingjiang hummed in agreement. Although Elder Zhi valued talent, he was extremely selfish in archery. He believed that it was better to reach the pinnacle himself than to let others do so. The places many could reach through hard work were not the true peak; the true peak was a tiny space, only large enough for one person. Therefore, those who were only one step away from that point were lonely. While striving to reach the top, they also wanted to eliminate other threatening masters of equal skill, especially strong individuals like Elder Zhi, who seemed forever stuck just one step below the peak. When An Jiu first displayed her archery talent, Elder Zhi decided to nurture her carefully. At that time, the difference in strength between her and Elder Zhi was like heaven and earth. Yet, this seemingly insignificant individual had fired the first shot! Elder Zhi’s usually calm heart shattered instantly. Now, facing each other again, he realized that the ant he once looked down upon had climbed to his head in such a short time. At this moment, his emotions were complex; he could not even discern whether it was jealousy, joy, astonishment, or resentment. In truth, if An Jiu had not been there, Elder Zhi might have considered his own position and would not have acted so recklessly. The Crown Prince was too ruthless, resorting to any means to achieve his goals. If the Crown Prince truly ascended the throne, the Mei family’s situation would only worsen. Although the Second Prince, who had been scheming to usurp the throne, was not exactly honorable either, he was still far better in comparison. With Elder Zhi’s wisdom, he should have known which choice to make. But if that arrow had not been so dangerous, there would have been no need to expose An Jiu, and she would not have been targeted by Elder Zhi. “An enemy arranged by fate,” Zhu Pianxian sighed. “This calamity was destined; there was no escaping it.” She wanted to say that evil lasted a thousand years and Fourteenth Young Lady would not be finished so soon, but looking at Chu Dingjiang’s expression, she pursed her lips, mustered her courage, and did not dare to say it aloud. “Having seen so much of the martial world, are there any precedents of someone collapsing from exhaustion of mental energy?” Chu Dingjiang asked Sheng Changying. Sheng Changying hesitated. “You know, people who can completely drain their mental energy are incredibly powerful in both spirit and willpower, so it is rare. I’ve only heard of one case, and that was fifty years ago.” “What happened to that person?” Chu Dingjiang knew he had laid out so much to ease the tension of that tragic ending, and he was somewhat prepared, but he still had to listen; even a little more experience was beneficial. Sheng Changying said, “He was a powerful cultivator at the internal cultivation realm. He was in a coma for a year…and then he passed away.” To live in this world, besides the vitality of the physical body, one also needed mental support. Ordinary people also had mental energy, but it was too weak, barely enough to sustain life. If mental energy collapsed, even the strongest physical vitality was nothing more than that of a living dead person. The silence made the atmosphere very oppressive. Chu Dingjiang seemed too strong, as if he did not need any comfort; even his company seemed superfluous. The two sat for a while before leaving. “Sigh!” Chu Dingjiang sighed deeply as the person had already gone far away. His rough fingers gently stroked An Jiu’s face, tracing her beautiful facial features.

chapters.title: Unbreakable (2)
chapters.content: Everyone on the island believed that Chu Dingjiang was not a man of sentimentality, but it was not until three days later that they began to worry. During those three days, he neither ate nor drank, sitting constantly by An Jiu’s bedside. “My Lord, please eat a few bites,” Li Qingzhi urged. No one answered. Undeterred, Li Qingzhi brought a cup of water to him. “My Lord, have some water.” Still no response. Li Qingzhi persisted for a while, but seeing that Chu Dingjiang remained unmoved, he had no choice but to leave. The others stood in the courtyard. Zhu Pianxian asked, “Still not eating?” “Yes,” Li Qingzhi said with a bitter face, “I am not good with words. How can I say anything touching? The master is sitting motionless by the bed, determined to stay there forever. He will not move until Fourteenth wakes up!” “He’s as cunning as a devil; what sweet talk can fool him?” Zhu Pianxian glanced at the tightly closed door. “You are the most honest; maybe he will listen to what you say.” Li Qingzhi had been bringing food for three days, saying almost the same things, and Chu Dingjiang’s reaction was always the same. “We underestimated Dingjiang’s feelings for Fourteenth,” Sheng Changying sighed. A silence fell over the courtyard, then soft footsteps echoed along the path. Li Qingzhi glanced warily, and Zhu Pianxian said, “It’s Aunt Mei.” As soon as she finished speaking, Mei Yanran appeared in everyone’s sight. “Why are you all sitting here?” Mei Yanran found it odd. The people on the island did not particularly enjoy crowds, and they generally would not gather in one place during the day unless it was something important. Li Qingzhi, as if grasping at a straw, hurriedly said, “Fourteenth is unconscious, and the master has been watching over her without eating or drinking.” In the eyes of others, An Jiu was Mei Yanran’s daughter; having someone share the pain might make Chu Dingjiang less insistent. Zhu Pianxian rolled her eyes at Li Qingzhi. She thought to herself, “Could you not have been more tactful? Although the mother and daughter’s relationship was not good, they were still mother and daughter.” “Unconscious?” Mei Yanran asked in surprise. “Inside the house,” Li Qingzhi said. Mei Yanran paused for a few moments, then went inside. The room was bathed in sunlight, yet the scene remained frozen. Mei Yanran walked to the bedside, looking at the familiar face that seemed to be sleeping peacefully, and her heart slowly clenched. She knew her daughter was in the Hua mansion, yet she felt as if the one lying here was also her daughter. “Rest for a while,” Mei Yanran said softly to Chu Dingjiang after taking a deep breath. “There’s a group of Konghe Army soldiers loitering in the plum grove by the lake. They are your men, are they not? They want to see you.” Chu Dingjiang stirred, his voice hoarse, “The Second Prince won.” It was a statement, not a question. The Crown Prince was already dead, and although there were many remnants, it was nothing more than a bloody battle. “Yes, the Second Prince has donned the yellow robe and chosen ten days later for his enthronement ceremony,” Mei Yanran elaborated. “Meritorious officials are all promoted and ennobled. I do not know what role you played in this incident, but you poured your heart and soul into it. Was it not all for today’s reward?” No, he was not doing it for fame or fortune, but simply to prove his existence. Realizing his ambitions, fame and fortune were merely byproducts. At this point, accepting credit would only be a burden. Chu Dingjiang chuckled softly, offering no explanation. “No matter what, you have to give your subordinates an explanation. She…she is, after all, my daughter.” Mei Yanran’s voice choked as she said this. “Let me take care of her. What else are you worried about?” Yes, this was her daughter. Even if another soul inhabited her body, she was still a piece of her own flesh and blood. Mei Yanran finally understood why she was so distressed. She could not bear to see the loneliness and indifference in those familiar eyes. Initially, when she learned the truth, her emotions were complicated. She hated this wandering ghost who had taken over her daughter’s body. However, as time went on, she found herself increasingly unable to clearly distinguish between soul and body. Now, seeing An Jiu lying in bed, Mei Yanran felt not only heartache but also deep sorrow. This child had always approached her cautiously, and she had not missed the filial piety hidden behind the indifference. “I will be right back.” After three days, Chu Dingjiang stood up for the first time. Mei Yanran nodded and sat down by the bedside to watch over her. Those outside were overjoyed to see Chu Dingjiang emerge, but before they could even exchange a glance, only a blur remained. Mei forest. Chu Dingjiang appeared silently among the group of black-clad individuals. “My Lord.” The group appeared and knelt before him on one knee. Chu Dingjiang’s gaze swept over each person, finally settling on a man holding a knife. The man felt an immense pressure, his bones feeling as if they were about to shatter. He knew why, but gritted his teeth, refusing to beg for forgiveness. “Su, I arranged for you to lead men to obstruct Elder Zhi. Why did you not act?” Chu Dingjiang’s tone was calm, but the pressure was like a mountain crashing down from the sky, seemingly causing the earth to tremble uncontrollably. Su’s back was instantly soaked with sweat. Feeling Chu Dingjiang’s pressure ease slightly, he could finally speak, “At the time, another archery expert was confronting Elder Zhi, and I thought the plan had changed.” “That’s not an excuse. Tell the truth,” Chu Dingjiang said coldly. They were all trained members of the Konghe Army, and without orders to change the battle plan, they were absolutely forbidden from acting arbitrarily—a rule etched into their very bones. Under his oppressive aura, Su struggled and roared, “Because of He Cai!” Just as he was about to lead his men to surround Elder Zhi, he saw He Cai sneak up alone to the Crown Prince’s side. He knew that if she made a move, regardless of success or failure, she would surely die. Therefore, he secretly changed the battle plan, attempting to protect He Cai. Su gave up struggling, collapsing to the ground, looking utterly disheveled. “You know she likes you.” Chu Dingjiang raised an eyebrow. He truly did not know He Cai had feelings for him. When he said he needed to leave a few men to protect An Jiu, He Cai volunteered for the task. Apart from that, he had very little interaction with her; he had not even revealed his face to these people. “Because she likes you, she risked everything to help you accomplish your great cause.” Su felt the oppressive aura loosen slightly, forcing himself to sit up, tilting his head back to carefully examine the man who led them. Judging by appearances, Chu Dingjiang was indeed superior to him in every way. “After meeting that woman, she agreed to return to my hometown with me.” Su’s resolute and cold gaze softened. “I followed you so that one day I could retire with He Cai and lay down my arms. If she dies, what’s the point of everything I’ve done?” Chu Dingjiang was silent for a moment. “You may leave.” Su seemed surprised that Chu Dingjiang let him go so easily and was stunned. Chu Dingjiang said, “Those who wish to retire may leave now. Those who wish to claim a reward may stay.”

chapters.title: Unbreakable (3)
chapters.content: Dozens of people present gradually got up and left; only Su remained. “He Cai is gone, and I want to find a reason to live,” Su said. Su was an orphan, taken into the Konghe Academy at the age of twelve. After countless life-and-death trials, he finally joined the Konghe Army. He came into contact with assassins relatively late, and in the monotonous battles of his later days and nights, everything before the age of twelve became increasingly vivid and clear. Even the times he was nearly beaten to death while fighting for food with beggars became precious memories. He could never truly achieve a heart as cold as ice. In the dead of night, his mind was filled with the people he had killed. He began to look for playmates in the Konghe Army, using desire and the warmth of their bodies to drive away the cold night. He was attracted to He Cai, initially because of her stunning physique. His initial intention was simply to spend a night with her, like any other day. In the Konghe Army, life was a matter of survival, and female assassins did not place much importance on chastity. However, He Cai, like a virtuous woman, not only refused but also fought with him. From that moment on, his desire to conquer her was ignited. He did not know when he fell in love, only that he was overjoyed when He Cai agreed to retire with him, and felt utterly devastated when she died. Su murmured, “I thought that after so many years as an assassin, I had become indifferent to life and death, but only after He Cai died before my eyes did I realize that I had never truly understood.” What he could not understand was not life and death, but love. Chu Dingjiang looked at him, feeling as if he were looking at himself. Up to this moment in this life, he thought he had achieved enlightenment, but who would have thought that by letting go of his ambitions, he would fall into another trap? “Life needs a touch of madness to be truly fulfilling,” Chu Dingjiang thought. “I’ve lost,” Chu Dingjiang sighed. Su Wei was surprised. He’d so easily annihilated the Crown Prince’s forces with such a meticulously laid trap, and this was not considered a failure? What then constituted victory? He suddenly became angry. “We risked our lives for this result. You call it a defeat?” Compared to most power struggles in history, this battle was indeed relatively easy, largely due to Chu Dingjiang’s influence. “You won; I lost,” Chu Dingjiang said calmly. “Even though I overthrew the empire, I could not protect one person, so I lost.” Chu Dingjiang felt he had lived two lives, having an advantage from the start, yet in the end, having seized the empire, he could not protect his woman. This was fate’s naked mockery of him. Amidst the raging flames of the Warring States period, Chu Dingjiang had once thought that, given the chance, he might not be inferior to Zhang Yi, Song Chuyi, or Xi Shou. Now, he felt he was far inferior. “No wonder He Cai liked you.” Su felt somewhat relieved. Although he was still saddened by He Cai’s death, he also felt that He Cai’s death for the person she loved was a fulfillment of her wish, a kind of perfection in itself. Some people rarely had romantic feelings, yet they always attracted many who did. Chu Dingjiang took off a jade pendant from his person and tossed it to Su. “This is a token given to me by the Second Prince. Taking it to the Second Prince might bring you great rewards and important positions, but great gains are often accompanied by great dangers. You should weigh the advantages and disadvantages yourself.” Su held the jade pendant as if it were a burning power. Chu Dingjiang watched as Su slowly tightened his grip on the pendant. He said slowly, “It might fill the emptiness in your heart, or perhaps you will feel increasingly empty.” Without waiting for Su to say anything, Chu Dingjiang vanished. He did not know He Cai’s feelings, nor did he feel obligated to repay anyone for He Cai’s death. He simply felt a sudden weariness. He was exhausted. Perhaps he was just too old mentally; he could never recapture the stubbornness he had in his early twenties, the kind of relentless determination that would not give up even after hitting a wall. He thought, even if An Jiu never woke up again, he would still sit by her bedside until the end of time. In Bianjing. The palace still reeked of blood after the recent massacre, and was stained with the stench of blood. The area around Baohua Gate was soaked in blood, the blood seeping into the bluestone bricks, leaving traces no matter how much they were washed away. Finally, they had to be pried off one by one and replaced with new bricks. In ten days, Zhao Huo’s coronation ceremony would be held. Such a massive undertaking kept the entire palace in a frenzy. Zhao Huo was currently busy with three main things: dealing with the remnants of the Crown Prince’s faction; declaring to the world that he was the rightful heir; and honoring meritorious officials, as well as posthumously honoring those loyal ministers who sacrificed themselves for his cause during the Baohua Gate Incident. Zhao Huo kept his ministers busy in the Zichen Palace until late at night. During brief breaks, he would stand outside the palace and gaze into the distance. The Baohua Gate was brightly lit, illuminating the inky sky. A cacophony of voices filled the air, and perhaps due to his state of mind, he even sensed a subtle liveliness and joy. Taking over the mess left by his own father, Zhao Huo truly felt the heavy pressure on his shoulders. The Song Dynasty was internally corrupt, surrounded by powerful enemies on the outside; a single misstep could lead to its downfall. Excessive officials and soldiers, an overemphasis on civil affairs, and a neglect of military matters—from the court to the common people, there were factors permeating the Song Dynasty’s current development. Where should he begin? In the past, Zhao Huo would have been eager to tackle everything from all angles. However, this battle, coupled with the heavy workload of the past few days, had quickly made him more mature and composed. Thinking of the mysterious Master Chu’s evaluation of him, Zhao Huo felt a growing sense of caution. Chu Dingjiang had once bluntly told Zhao Huo that while he was doing well in every aspect and his passion was a good thing, as an Emperor, passion alone was not enough; what he lacked most was composure and calmness. At the time, Zhao Huo did not fully understand. He felt that he had spent so much effort and risked so much to seize the throne, all for the immense power that came with the position above all others—the power to change this crumbling country according to his own will. But now, actually sitting on that throne, he realized that even with the entire country at his disposal, not everything could be done as he pleased. To achieve his goals, he had to suppress his temper and passion. “Your Majesty,” Prime Minister Hua bowed respectfully. Zhao Huo pulled himself out of his thoughts and sighed, “Prime Minister, why is everything so different from what I initially imagined?” Prime Minister Hua paused, quickly considering the meaning behind his words. He had a fairly accurate grasp of Zhao Huo’s thoughts, but aloud he said, “This old minister is foolish; please enlighten me, Your Majesty.” In this atmosphere, clearly one of intimate conversation between ruler and subject, a competent minister must not guess the Emperor’s inner thoughts. In this matter, only feigning ignorance would ensure safety. “I once thought that, sitting in this position above all others, I could decisively eliminate the deep-seated problems of the Song Dynasty. I was certain I could do better than anyone else, but…” Zhao Huo turned to look at Prime Minister Hua, “I now feel constrained. Prime Minister, you are my father’s right-hand man; please advise me.” Prime Minister Hua bowed again. “Your Majesty is too kind to this old minister.” Zhao Huo helped him up. “No need for such modesty. I have always trusted your loyalty to the country and the Emperor.” His words were tactful, but the gist was: “My father may not trust you, but I do, so you can rest assured!” “I would gladly die for Your Majesty’s word,” Prime Minister Hua said politely, then dropped the subject. He had known the Second Prince’s character before supporting him; he was a straightforward man who disliked evasive words and actions. Therefore, abandoning his previous diplomatic approach, he said directly, “Your Majesty’s thinking is a blessing for the Great Song Dynasty. This old minister shares Your Majesty’s desire for reform, but unfortunately, the foundations of the Great Song are already showing signs of wavering. We should not act too hastily. If we wish to rebuild it, we must be patient and proceed gradually.” “Where do you think we should begin?” Zhao Huo, suddenly burdened with such a large task, was already bewildered and urgently needed to hear the opinions of these veteran ministers. Prime Minister Hua paused, then said succinctly, “In my opinion, the most urgent task is military action.” Prime Minister Hua was also an ambitious man. He was not saying this to flatter Zhao Huo, but because he truly could not wait any longer. The Liao Kingdom was eyeing the city covetously, and it was highly likely that they would launch a large-scale invasion while the Song Dynasty was still in turmoil. If the Liao army were to successfully capture Bianjing, what use would any other measures be? Zhao Huo’s eyes lit up, and he clapped his hands, saying, “Prime Minister’s words are exactly what I was thinking.” Prime Minister Hua glanced at the dark circles under the young man’s eyes, then quickly looked away, feeling that he had made the right choice. Regardless of how Zhao Huo would treat these veteran officials in the future, at least he had focused his efforts on saving the country from crisis. “Does the Prime Minister know of Chu Dingjiang?” Zhao Huo suddenly asked. Prime Minister Hua’s heart skipped a beat. Had the fact that Chu Dingjiang was his son been exposed? Thinking of this, Prime Minister Hua felt not only astonished but also filled with resentment and injustice.  This bastard had been different from ordinary people since childhood, which was truly frightening. Whether it was taking his concubine’s child as a substitute or joining the Konghe Army, it was all his own decision and had nothing to do with him, his father. He had long since stopped considering that person his son, but if this scoundrel’s background were to be exposed, the Hua family would still be the first to suffer.

chapters.title: Unbreakable (4)
chapters.content: If it were truly exposed, the relationship between Chu Dingjiang and the Hua family would not be so easily cleared up. Even the seasoned and experienced Prime Minister Hua could not help but break out in a cold sweat. Given the current unclear situation, he could only grit his teeth and say, “Your Majesty, I do not know.” “This person inexplicably appeared by my side, clearing obstacles for me, but now he has inexplicably disappeared,” Zhao Huo murmured to himself at the end. “Could it truly be Heaven’s help?” Prime Minister Hua breathed a barely perceptible sigh of relief. Chu Dingjiang had performed such a great service, yet Prime Minister Hua had not been foolish enough to reveal the truth to the young Emperor. The Hua family had barely managed to pull themselves out of the mire; he could not let the Emperor think, “Success and failure both stem from the Hua family.” Since the Emperor believed it was a gift from Heaven, then so be it. “Heaven should protect the true dragon.” Even Zhao Huo, who disliked flattery, found these words quite pleasing. He was currently extremely busy and had no time to dwell on this, but he kept the matter to himself. The new Emperor’s ascension to the throne brought bustling activity throughout the land, but Mei Mansion remained eerily silent. On the fourth day after An Jiu’s fainting spell, Chu Dingjiang revealed his true, sorrowful face—An Jiu had lost control of her bladder. The reason adults did not lose control of their bladders in their sleep was due to their mental strength. An Jiu had been unconscious before, yet had not lost control, which gave Chu Dingjiang a glimmer of hope. For someone with strong mental strength and unwavering will, even a trace of remaining mental strength could lead to awakening. But now…it seemed there was practically no mental strength left. Mei Yanran silently wiped An Jiu’s body, then cleaned the bed. After finishing, she stood blankly by the bed, just like Chu Dingjiang. She pondered, remembering how An Jiu had inexplicably appeared inside Mei Jiu’s body—perhaps it was some kind of predestined encounter? There were no other options at the moment, so she decided to try anything, even if it was a desperate measure. It would not hurt. Mei Yanran went off the island to fetch Mei Jiu, hoping she could awaken An Jiu. With the late Emperor’s passing and the disintegration of the Konghe Army, the relationship between Hua Rongtian and Mei Jiu had improved considerably. Leaving the mansion was no longer a difficult task, although her pregnancy made it somewhat troublesome. Hua Rongtian sent many servants to accompany her, and it took a whole day of preparation before they could finally set off smoothly. Mei Jiu had died amidst the plum blossoms, and she had an inexplicable feeling about this place—a mixture of fear and a strange sense of exhilaration. Perhaps it was because she had been too incompetent in the past, clinging to everything like a dodder vine. Now, although she still relied on her husband, she had clearly found her place. Previously, when her relationship with Hua Rongtian was strained, it was inconvenient for her to interfere in household affairs, but now, she was quick to take charge, much like a wife who had been in power for many years. Most of the servants under her command were completely obedient. Having died once, Mei Jiu’s mindset had undergone a significant change. Upon reaching the lakeshore, most of Hua Rongtian’s servants who had come with her were left behind. Mei Jiu only took two trusted confidantes with her to the island with Mei Yanran. Mei Jiu saw An Jiu again. This was an unexpected scene. Looking at An Jiu’s tightly closed eyes, Mei Jiu’s tears welled up uncontrollably. She had not cried like this in a long time since her rebirth. “Mother, An Jiu is a woman of misfortune.” Mei Jiu recalled the hellish scenes she had witnessed when she and An Jiu were one. Her heart ached even more. She had originally intended to never tell anyone about An Jiu, but now she could not help herself and told Mei Yanran everything about her past. Chu Dingjiang listened from the side. His throat felt like it was blocked, with a painful lump in his throat. Mei Jiu sat down on the edge of the bed and took An Jiu’s hand. “The good days have just begun; you cannot fall asleep. I know you’ve found someone you love, and I am so happy for you. I bought you a large horse farm where you can raise many sheep and a beautiful house in Jiangnan as a wedding gift. If you keep sleeping, who will I give it to?” Mei Yanran glanced at Mei Jiu, knowing that things had not been very good at the beginning at the Hua’s mansion. Even if she had saved some money on the side, it would have been difficult to secretly arrange this. Since she could do it, she was clearly no longer the naive girl she once was. Mei Yanran felt both melancholy and gratified. “You said you wanted to herd sheep?” Mei Jiu held An Jiu’s slightly cool hand, feeling as if her left hand was holding her right, as if she had instantly returned to the days when their souls were one. Foolish humans, my ambitions had long since changed! Mei Jiu was delighted. “An Jiu, can you hear me?” Seeing the change in Mei Jiu’s expression, Chu Dingjiang tensed up, his whole body stiffening. His gaze was fixed on An Jiu’s face, which had not changed at all, as if trying to find some change he might have overlooked. Mei Jiu waited a long time, but An Jiu did not react again, as if she had just imagined what she had heard. Mei Jiu smiled bitterly. “If you could still speak, you could mock me every day.” “What happened just now?” Chu Dingjiang asked in a hoarse voice. “I heard her say, ‘Foolish humans, my ambition has long since changed!'” Mei Jiu thought about it again and suddenly felt something was strange. “She originally said she wanted to herd sheep, but then changed her mind?” Mei Jiu suddenly realized that Chu Dingjiang and Mei Yanran were not there that day, so they naturally did not know about her conversation with Lou Xiaowu, and Mei Jiu could not possibly know either. “I know, I know!” Lou Xiaowu rushed in, howling, “Fourteenth said that even if she were a rat, she would be a free rat under the sun.” “What does that mean?” Mei Yanran asked. Lou Xiaowu shook her head but then recounted the events of that day in detail to the three of them. Everyone else was still confused, but Chu Dingjiang understood. An Jiu had once told him about “rats,” comparing herself to a filthy rat in the dark. She said she wanted to herd sheep, but without breaking free from the shackles of her mind, she was nothing more than a rat herding sheep in the night. Chu Dingjiang looked at her pale face, his eyes stinging with pain. She had lived such a painful life, and finally, she had come to terms with it. What did this ordeal mean? Was the purpose of being reborn by heaven just to help her understand this? Then what was the purpose of his own rebirth? “Ah Jiu,” Chu Dingjiang said, “are you really conscious?” Mei Jiu felt she was not hallucinating, so she decided to stay on the island longer until she could communicate with An Jiu again. However… Day after day, she never heard a single word again, as if Mei Jiu had truly hallucinated that day. Mei Jiu was also stubborn; once she set her mind on something, she threw herself into it. Every day, except for mealtimes and sleep, she stayed by An Jiu’s bedside, pushing Chu Dingjiang aside. However, she had too many worries these days; besides the baby in her belly, there was another person at home who was pacing anxiously. Although Mei Jiu sent a message back, Hua Rongtian, who was always a very composed person, finally could not resist riding his horse to Meihua Mansion half a month later.

chapters.title: Bringing Her in
chapters.content: Now that the late Emperor had passed away, the Konghe Army was fragmented, and the new Emperor had usurped the throne; it was unlikely he would fulfill the late Emperor’s wish to destroy the Hua clan. Mei Jiu was the legitimate eldest daughter-in-law of the Hua clan, and she was carrying the future eldest grandson of the Hua clan. How could she be allowed to remain outside for so long? Mei Jiu had always been a model wife, but this time she was unusually willful. She felt that only she and An Jiu had had that peculiar relationship, and she seemed to have heard An Jiu say something just half a month ago—how could she give up so easily? A light rain was falling in the mountains, and everything was shrouded in mist. Hua Rongtian and Mei Jiu sat in the pavilion for a long time before he spoke, “Why not bring Young Lady Mei to the Hua residence?” Mei Jiu’s eyes lit up, but then she asked worriedly, “Will Master Chu agree?” “Is that her husband?” Hua Rongtian asked. Mei Jiu shook her head. Although they had no formal title, Mei Jiu knew very well that An Jiu’s closest person in this world was Chu Dingjiang. “Since she’s not her husband, we can consult her mother. Besides, bringing her to the Hua family is for recuperation, not a bad thing. Since she’s your sister, I will do everything I can to help.” Seeing the lingering sorrow on her brow, Hua Rongtian took her hand, his tone softening considerably. “The Hua family is a powerful clan, and you are the matriarch. Even if I wanted to stay here with you, it would not be appropriate.” Mei Jiu knew Hua Rongtian was thinking of her best interests. “I will go ask them.” Hua Rongtian nodded and helped her back into the house. Mei Jiu told Mei Yanran and Chu Dingjiang about their discussion. Mei Yanran looked at Chu Dingjiang. “You make the decision.” Chu Dingjiang paused, then turned and bowed to Hua Rongtian. “Then I will trouble you.” Going to the Hua family was not to rely on the Hua family’s power, but rather to cling to a sliver of hope regarding the connection between Mei Jiu and An Jiu. With her mental energy dissipating, the longer it dragged on, the worse the situation would become. Chu Dingjiang did not want to sit idly by until Mo Sigui returned. The Hua family’s carriages were already waiting outside the plum grove; it was only for moving a few people, which would have been enough even without prior preparation. There was only one carriage, quite spacious. An Jiu and Mei Jiu lay inside without feeling cramped at all; there was even room for one or two maids to serve them. The two lay side by side, their hands clasped tightly, just like their souls had nestled together years ago. Mei Jiu heard clear breathing beside her, yet she could not feel her presence. Memories flooded back. Mei Jiu suddenly remembered that many years ago, An Jiu had also been silent for a long time due to trauma. She could not help but sit up, looking at An Jiu’s face and sighing, “I hope it is the same as last time.” This was a scenario Mei Jiu never imagined. She had always thought that the weak, like herself, would die young…Of course, she had indeed died once, but should the strong, like An Jiu, not live longer? Instead, she became a living dead at a young age. The carriage traveled slowly, finally entering the city at dusk. Hua Rongtian secretly arranged for An Jiu to stay in a courtyard closer to Mei Jiu, instructing the servants not to disturb her, with only Chu Dingjiang and Mei Yanran staying to watch over her and bring her meals daily. Chu Dingjiang was very satisfied with this arrangement. As dusk settled, Pan Tower Street began to bustle. Chu Dingjiang remained seated by the bed, taking out a roll of silk and placing it beside An Jiu’s pillow. “I’ve retrieved the task you accepted. It is due in less than half a month. You promised to do it yourself, so do not break your promise.” This was a task An Jiu had accepted from the bounty list. Chu Dingjiang had previously delegated it to his subordinates, but before it could be completed, the Emperor passed away, and the matter was temporarily shelved. Even in his busy schedule, Chu Dingjiang remembered An Jiu’s promise to retrieve it and complete it herself. Knock, knock, knock! Someone knocked on the door. Chu Dingjiang immediately recognized it was not Mei Jiu or Mei Yanran, but it was a familiar face—Hua Rongjian.

chapters.title: Threat
chapters.content: “Come in,” Chu Dingjiang said. Hua Rongjian pushed open the door and entered. Seeing that Chu Dingjiang did not intend to get up, he walked to the bedside and stood there for a while before uttering a provocative remark, “Since you cannot protect Ah Jiu, then let me do it.” Chu Dingjiang glanced at Hua Rongjian indifferently. He could despise himself for being useless, but that did not mean anyone could boss him around, let alone try to take away his beloved. Hua Rongjian looked at this somewhat familiar man with a complicated expression. “I only regret that I did not pay attention; that is why Fourteenth is like this today.” Hua Rongjian was not being arrogant. If An Jiu were with him, at least her safety would be guaranteed. Leaving aside the Hua family’s immense power, he would not let his woman risk her life. Chu Dingjiang understood his meaning. However, even without the Hua family, with An Jiu’s abilities, she would definitely not die unless she deliberately sought her own death. Now, Chu Dingjiang was too lazy to argue with him, only telling him a simple fact: “This is the path she chose herself. I can indulge her, but you cannot.” How could the Hua family tolerate their daughter-in-law committing assassination? After all, this was still a world where most people were normal. Hua Rongjian looked at An Jiu’s pale, thin face and sighed. He liked her very much, but this liking was complicated by other emotions. He had many fair-weather friends, but only two truly close ones. Being with An Jiu felt different from being with others. To put it nicely, she was a very pure person; to put it another way, she was single-minded. He could be childish and shameless to his heart’s content, and she would still be that trustworthy friend. Unfortunately, Chu Dingjiang took all of that away! Chu Dingjiang killed Hua Rongjian’s birth mother, and An Jiu, as someone who knew the truth, chose Chu Dingjiang over him and lied to him. Hua Rongjian could not accept this fact. Objectively speaking, having a son born to a concubine raised as a legitimate son was a good thing for Hua Rongjian. Even if his birth mother had not died, she would only have been a concubine. He only had one real mother. However, there’s always something inexplicable about a man’s dignity, and Hua Rongjian could not bring himself to treat him like a wolf. Seeing Chu Dingjiang’s current state, his early schemes seemed like a joke. He suddenly wondered if Chu Dingjiang had ever regretted it. “Do you regret it?” Chu Dingjiang remained silent. He was out of place in this world. His pursuits and ideals seemed too naive to people today, incomprehensible to them. If he said he did not regret it, others would probably just think he was being stubborn, so it was better to remain silent. Seeing his silence, Hua Rongjian did not jump to conclusions. “Abandoning your family background and status to become someone who cannot see the light of day, unable to even protect the woman you love—was it worth it?” Chu Dingjiang truly felt a destiny-bound connection between himself and Hua Rongjian; every word pierced his heart. However, Hua Rongjian underestimated Chu Dingjiang’s resilience. To him, even if the sky were to fall, he would simply laugh it off. “Whether it is worth it or not is my life.” Chu Dingjiang’s calm and understated words made Hua Rongjian grit his teeth in frustration. What he hated most was having his life arranged by others, without even a choice. He had once asked An Jiu if thinking like this seemed pretentious. He was living a wonderful life; few in the entire country could be richer or more carefree than he was. Yet, upon learning of past grievances, he began to despise his life! If he could make an exchange, countless people in the world would be willing to trade places with him. But Hua Rongjian was a man of deep feelings. Some were willing to sacrifice a concubine for a prestigious position, but he wasn’t. Some would rather forgo a close friend for a lifetime of carefree living, but he wasn’t. “You are not as good as a woman.” Chu Dingjiang easily understood his current dilemma. Hua Rongjian frowned, not immediately becoming angry. “I’d like to hear the details.” “Do you know the Lou family?” Chu Dingjiang asked. Hua Rongjian paused. “Yes.” “The Lou family was almost completely wiped out because of the Liao people. Second Young Lady Lou vowed revenge.” Chu Dingjiang held An Jiu’s hand and succinctly explained Lou Mingyue’s situation. “She and Physician Mo were childhood sweethearts; their feelings were extraordinary. Since there’s no way to have both, she was able to ruthlessly sever ties with Mo Sigui. Regardless of whether her choice was right or wrong, at least she acted decisively. You, on the other hand, struggle even to make a choice. Are you not far inferior to her? If you came to me seeking revenge, perhaps I would respect you more.” There were always people in this world who did not want to offend anyone, only wanting to make everything perfect. If an ordinary person had this kind of personality and some social skills, they could only earn a good reputation for harmony through hard work and could not achieve anything more. When Chu Dingjiang was Hua Rongjian’s age, he already held the fate of his entire clan in his hands, decisive and ruthless. “With your personality, it is not surprising you missed out on An Jiu.” Chu Dingjiang knew that Hua Rongjian and An Jiu were already acquainted long before he met An Jiu, and he knew that Hua Rongjian had boasted about wanting to marry An Jiu. However, given his personality, Chu Dingjiang never considered him a competitor. In Chu Dingjiang’s view, Hua Rongjian’s competitiveness was even less than Gu Jinghong’s and Wei Yuzhi’s. It must be said that men understood men best. Chu Dingjiang did not sense any ambition in Hua Rongjian for An Jiu. Leaving aside Gu Jinghong, who was already dead, Wei Yuzhi, on the surface, appeared gentle and unassuming, but deep down, he possessed a strong sense of determination. Chu Dingjiang had not missed any of Wei Yuzhi’s interactions with An Jiu, so he knew that this man truly cared for An Jiu. Hua Rongjian initially showed interest in An Jiu, but his efforts were somewhat slow. Firstly, their relationship was more of a friendship than romantic love; secondly, his upbringing was quite normal, and subconsciously, he harbored various concerns about the female assassin’s identity. Hua Rongjian, seemingly carefree and unrestrained, actually had many inner constraints. “Yes,” Hua Rongjian chuckled. Chu Dingjiang looked at him seriously upon hearing this, noticing a significant change in his demeanor; the sunny young man was long gone. “It seems you’ve been thinking about a lot lately.” Has he figured things out? Or had he gotten stuck in a rut? Chu Dingjiang, born in a chaotic era, could not understand the word “mediocrity.” He believed that people needed passion and the drive to pursue their dreams, so no matter how Hua Rongjian changed, he thought it was a good thing. A man should always have some spirit. Thinking of this, Chu Dingjiang paused slightly. After all, what did it matter to him what Hua Rongjian became? “Ah Jiu, let’s fight again when you wake up.” Hua Rongjian reached out to touch An Jiu’s face. However, before he could reach her, Chu Dingjiang grabbed his wrist. The atmosphere instantly became tense. In the past, Chu Dingjiang had never felt that Hua Rongjian posed a threat, but this time was different.

chapters.title: Yearning and Ruthlessness
chapters.content: Chu Dingjiang’s skill far surpassed Hua Rongjian’s, but he was unwilling to take advantage of the situation. Hua Rongjian, knowing he was no match, simply did not use his internal energy either; the two were locked in a stalemate purely by brute force. The intense pain in his wrist caused a fine layer of sweat to instantly bead on Hua Rongjian’s forehead. Chu Dingjiang remained calm and collected. “I once wanted to have my cake and eat it too, but now I’ve given up the fish. Anyone who dares to touch my bear’s paw will have to kill me first.” “Is that so?” Veins bulged on Hua Rongjian’s forehead, his tone as flippant as ever. “You want me to give it up? Why not kill me first?” “I will not kill you.” Chu Dingjiang flicked his arm, using his inner force to send Hua Rongjian flying half a zhang away. “If I unfortunately die young in this life, it certainly will not be at your hands. You are too weak.” Hua Rongjian, in terms of both cunning and martial prowess, was on a completely different level from Chu Dingjiang. Even though he was rapidly growing stronger, he could not match Chu Dingjiang, who had lived two lives. “Feelings are unpredictable,” Hua Rongjian smiled. He had spent most of his time contemplating life lately and was no longer as easily provoked as before. Chu Dingjiang was not as dismissive as he seemed. Perhaps Hua Rongjian was inferior to him in many ways, but there were two things he could never regain. —Young and passionate. Because of his youth, he had not experienced much hardship, so he possessed abundant emotions, his love and hate vivid and intense. That kind of emotion was truly captivating. In comparison, the emotions he could offer were bland and weathered; his love would never be impulsive or lead to heartbreak, lacking any real excitement. “Ah Jiu, would you like this kind of love?” Chu Dingjiang asked her. An Jiu could not answer. So Uncle Chu sat alone by the window, lost in thought. When he came to his senses, Chu Dingjiang could not help but smile. It seemed everyone in love became a bit eccentric. Thinking about such things was pointless; he should spend his time thinking about what he could do for An Jiu. Now, all his subordinates had been dismissed, leaving only a few loyal followers. Chu Dingjiang did not want to sit idly by, so when Mei Yanran came to see An Jiu, he went out and sent people to find things that could boost her mental energy. For example, the fragments of the Heavenly Book and those jade boxes. At Chu Dingjiang’s behest, Zhu Pianxian began purchasing such items. However, good things were hard to come by, and those acquired at great expense were not very effective. Fortunately, Lou Xiaowu contributed an Ice Soul Pillow. This item could concentrate mental energy. The Lou family had these items in the mountains where they had lived for generations, which was why the women of the Lou family were all exceptionally intelligent and resolute—a great benefit for nourishing mental energy. An Jiu used the Ice Soul Pillow, and Mei Jiu came to talk to her every day, yet her body continued to grow thinner, her once plump cheeks becoming sunken. Chu Dingjiang watched with a calm expression. His temples were now streaked with white frost. Mei Jiu felt that he was sometimes like a stone monument standing in the wilderness, weathered by the years, appearing exceptionally desolate and lonely, yet so distant and resolute, offering no comfort, only the helpless, watchful gaze of those who grew old and weary. Chu Dingjiang disregarded everyone’s opinions, focusing solely on doing what he could. He originally wanted nothing more to do with the Hua family. But now, the things provided by the Hua family and those secretly sent by Hua Rongjian were all placed around An Jiu. As long as they served their purpose, he could not refuse, no matter how much he resented the Hua family. This deep attachment struck him as he reflected. He could not pinpoint the source of his feelings. Lost in thought, Chu Dingjiang heard Mei Yanran’s footsteps approaching. “The Mei family is here. Do you want to see them?” Mei Yanran asked. “The Mei family.” Chu Dingjiang remembered that the Mei family had not been wiped out; Mei Zhengjing and a few younger members remained, holed up in the capital. They had been silent for a long time, as if they had disappeared. “The new Emperor has ascended the throne. They’ve become active again.” “The new Emperor needs power,” Mei Yanran said. With domestic affairs riddled with problems and surrounded by powerful enemies, Zhao Huo desperately needed to cultivate his own power base to handle such a mess. The withered but experienced Mei and Lou families were undoubtedly good choices, at least for the short term, and their power would not slip out of his control. “Are the Mei family coming to see An Jiu or me?” Chu Dingjiang asked. Mei Yanran stared at the white hair at his temples and said, “You.” Chu Dingjiang was silent for a moment. “Tell them that taking anything from me will come at a huge price, and they must have a reason to convince me; otherwise, do not waste your time.” This tone did not displease Mei Yanran at all. Sometimes she was curious why Chu Dingjiang, who was much younger than her, could speak with the air of an elder without feeling out of place. When talking to Chu Dingjiang, she would even forget his age. Mei Yanran quickly regained her composure. “I think Sixth Master Mei understands very well.” She had left home early and did not know Mei Zhengjing very well, but she knew that her cousin was intelligent and pragmatic. “Then bring them in,” Chu Dingjiang said. Mei Yanran responded and went out to bring the people in. This courtyard was within the Hua family compound, but a side gate led directly outside. The Hua family was large and powerful, with strict rules, and Mei Yanran did not want to enter or exit directly through the main gate, so she used this side gate as her own. Shortly afterward, rustling footsteps sounded in the courtyard. Afraid of disturbing An Jiu, Mei Yanran led the people from the Mei family to a side room. Only after Mei Yanran came to look after An Jiu did he get up and go over. Mei Zhengjing sat in the side hall, lost in thought. He noticed the light in the room suddenly dim, and when he looked up, he saw a tall man with a full beard walk in. His footsteps were so light they did not stir up a speck of dust, yet he appeared incredibly composed. His eyes held a sharp, restrained light, and although he deliberately concealed his aura, he still exuded a powerful sense of pressure. “Junior Mei Zhengjing greets Senior.” Mei Zhengjing rose and bowed. Mei Tingzhu and Mei Tingyuan followed suit. Mei Yanran had not told them Chu Dingjiang’s age. “Sit.” Chu Dingjiang took the main seat, cutting to the chase without any pleasantries. “What brings you here?” “Junior knows Senior holds great prestige within the Konghe Army. Senior’s contributions were indispensable to His Majesty’s ascension to the throne. The Mei family is now determined to rise again but is no longer willing to engage in assassinations.” Seeing his directness, Mei Zhengjing did not beat around the bush. “I wish to ask Senior if you know the whereabouts of the Secret Manual of Konghe.” The Secret Manual of Konghe contained information about the secret guards and methods for controlling them. The new Emperor ascended the throne through a coup; without the previous Emperor’s legacy, he certainly would not know the whereabouts of the Secret Manual of Konghe. They must destroy it before the Emperor could find it, so that the Mei family would not be put in a passive position and repeat the mistakes of the past. This was their only chance. The Secret Manual was of paramount importance. It was certainly hidden carefully, but no matter how well concealed, it would eventually be found, remaining a constant threat to the Mei family. Chu Dingjiang had anticipated the Mei family’s request. However, Mei Zhengjing’s constant use of “senior” reminded him of what An Jiu had said: that although he and Hua Rongjian were roughly the same age, he looked like Hua Rongjian’s uncle. Mei Zhengjing sensed that this serious and aloof man seemed to be in a good mood, so he said, “If senior has any requests, as long as the Mei family can fulfill them, I will certainly not refuse.” “Do you know that the Mei family and I have a grudge?” Chu Dingjiang asked quietly. Mei Zhengjing’s heart skipped a beat. He had not witnessed the Baohua Gate incident, but Elder Zhi was very likely on the Crown Prince’s side. Besides him, he could not think of anyone else who could have the power to offend the person before him. “Senior, are you perhaps referring to Elder Zhi? He is now mentally impaired; living is more unbearable than dying.” The once wise man. Suffering immense mental trauma, his intelligence was less than that of a three-year-old child; living was worse than death. “Does he still enjoy archery?” Chu Dingjiang asked casually. Some people were indeed exceptionally intelligent and brilliant. With a little cunning, they could easily manipulate others. But in Chu Dingjiang’s view, Elder Zhi was not a strategist because he was too obsessed with archery; that fanaticism could make him disregard everything. A qualified strategist should not be too fixated or fanatical. For Elder Zhi, the hardest thing to let go of was not his intelligence but archery. As long as he could still touch a bow and arrow, he was not useless. Mei Zhengjing understood Chu Dingjiang’s meaning but hesitated to answer. He wanted to keep Elder Zhi alive. Aside from familial ties, although Elder Zhi’s mental strength was destroyed, his pure internal energy remained, which would still be of great use to the Mei family. “I cannot quell my hatred without destroying this man,” Chu Dingjiang said, rising to his feet. “If you have not made up your mind, do not waste your breath.” Mei Zhengjing hardened his heart. “This junior will hand him over to you, senior.” If Elder Zhi could exchange for the freedom of the entire Mei clan, it would be worth it. Schemers were almost ruthless. Elder Zhi had rendered meritorious service to the Mei clan, but he was not close to any of them. Although Mei Zhengjing was reluctant, as the head of the clan, he had to weigh the advantages and disadvantages and made this ruthless choice. In the backlight, Chu Dingjiang’s face appeared blurred and mysterious, his slightly upturned lips revealing a cold cruelty. “Even if your Mei clan does not agree, killing him is just a piece of cake for me. Do I need your consent?” The three members of the Mei clan’s expressions changed slightly. Mei Tingzhu said, “You mean you want us to kill him ourselves?” Elder Zhi, besides being devoted to archery, had dedicated almost his entire life to the Mei clan, only to be dealt with by the Mei clan themselves in the end…All three felt that Chu Dingjiang was extremely cruel. However, Chu Dingjiang was far more ruthless and cruel than they had imagined. “Kill him?” Chu Dingjiang shook his head, pulling out a small bottle and tossing it to Mei Zhengjing. “Not only do I not intend to kill him, but I also plan to help him regain his memories, on the condition that his hands are returned to him.” The medicine in the bottle was acquired at great expense, specifically for treating the aftereffects of mental trauma. However, An Jiu had lost even her mental strength, let alone any aftereffects, so the medicine was naturally ineffective. Chu Dingjiang was unwilling to haphazardly feed An Jiu medicine and used various items beneficial to mental strength recovery to care for her instead. He had received a message from Sui Yuntong that Mo Sigui was already on his way back, and only after a proper diagnosis could he prescribe the right treatment. “I’ve taken some time these past few days to retrieve the Secret Manual of Konghe. You will exchange it for Elder Zhi’s hands within a month,” Chu Dingjiang said. Mei Zhengjing pursed his lips, remaining silent, almost crushing the porcelain bottle in his hand. Mei Tingzhu asked, “If we do not exchange it, what do you plan to do with the Secret Manual?” “I do not want to be too blatant in my threats, but since you asked, I will tell you: good things never lack buyers.” Chu Dingjiang’s words were barely out of his mouth before he vanished. The few people left in the room felt as if they had fallen into an ice cave.

chapters.title: I Want to See Him
chapters.content: The Mei family’s enduring glory stemmed from its unity. The family could not tolerate traitors, nor would it turn siblings against each other for personal gain. “We must not be lenient with traitors!” Mei Tingzhu said coldly. Mei Yanran, who fled Mei Mansion with her daughter, was a traitor to the family. The elders initially planned to eliminate the mother and daughter, but the Fourteenth Young Lady’s displayed archery talent during a crisis changed the plan. At the time, the family was short of talent and intended to cultivate the Fourteenth Young Lady. The family’s stance had always been to spare the daughter and eliminate the mother. Mei Yanran, being wary, made a deal with Elder Zhi, voluntarily joining the Konghe Army to save her life. If Fourteenth Young Lady were already dead, why would they need to personally sever Elder Zhi’s hands for her sake? “What should we do?” Mei Tingyuan, having experienced several setbacks, had become much more mature and composed, yet faced with such a difficult choice, she still had no idea. To all the younger generations of the Mei family, Elder Zhi was a mountain-like figure, someone to worship and rely on. Even now, though he was mentally impaired, his very existence was a source of mental support! They had never even entertained the thought of surpassing the mountain, let alone destroying it. This was less a revenge against Elder Zhi and more a revenge against the entire Mei family. “Let’s go.” Mei Zhengjing strode away. “Sixth Uncle,” Mei Tingyuan hurried after him, “you are not really going to attack the Elder, are you?” No one answered her question. Only after leaving the Hua Mansion and boarding the carriage did Mei Tingzhu whisper, “Who knew this man would seek revenge for Fourteenth Young Lady? Now that he knows what we want, he will probably seize the Secret Manual to blackmail us.” Initially, Mei Zhengjing thought Chu Dingjiang, a high-ranking member of the Konghe Army, would be extremely ruthless. Although he knew An Jiu had fallen into a coma during the coup due to Elder Zhi, he had not taken it seriously, assuming Chu Dingjiang merely valued An Jiu; the entire Mei family could offer Chu Dingjiang far more than just An Jiu. “I misjudged their relationship.” Mei Zhengjing closed his eyes and slowly exhaled. Previously, Mei Zhengjing had always criticized his elder brother for being too cautious and conservative. Only now did he understand the weight of the burden on his brother’s shoulders—not that he was unwilling to move, but that a single misstep could lead to an even more difficult and passive situation. He approached Chu Dingjiang with a gamble in mind. He had anticipated Chu Dingjiang’s various demands and was prepared to be turned away, but he never expected Chu Dingjiang to harbor hatred for the Mei family because of someone else. The Mei family was a Konghe Army family, and Mei Zhengjing understood that assassins who killed many people became emotionally numb, and life and death became trivial matters. Love and hate were even less important. Mei Tingzhu heard the self-reproach in his voice and advised, “We cannot predict the future; unexpected things are perfectly normal.” Mei Tingyuan said, “Since he values ​​Fourteenth Young Lady so much, he should be busy saving her rather than seeking revenge, right?” These words were like a wake-up call. Mei Zhengjing opened his eyes and exchanged a glance with Mei Tingzhu. Both of them sensed a sense of relief in each other’s eyes. Indeed, if they had not come to him…Chu Dingjiang had no intention of seeking revenge. Since that was the case, they had some time to search for the Secret Manual. If they could not find it, they would have to sacrifice Elder Zhi’s hands. “If only the Grand Madam were still alive,” Mei Tingyuan sighed to herself. Mei learned about the Secret Manual of Konghe from the Grand Madam. The Grand Madam had mentioned the location of the Secret Manual, but during the Baohua Gate Incident, they had secretly sent people to search for it. The secret chamber where the book was hidden was there, but the legendary Secret Manual was not. After all, the Grand Madam had been gone from the Konghe Army for some years; perhaps the Secret Manual had already been moved. The Baohua Gate Incident was merely a bloodbath in the Forbidden City. However, the world above had changed; the entire Song Dynasty was in a state of disarray, awaiting reconstruction. The clouds in the sky grew thicker, and rain began to fall at dusk. As night fell, the rain carried many icy pellets. Winter had arrived in the Song Dynasty, and countless people longed for a different atmosphere after spring. In the Liao capital, Shangjing. The palace had been under a state of high tension for over ten days, only slightly easing last night when a rider rushed into the city. In a side hall, Yelu Huangwu sat on a couch, staring at the kneeling girl in red, and coldly sneered, “That good-for-nothing Wei Yuzhi.” Mei Ruyan felt indignant for Wei Yuzhi, and words of rebuttal almost escaped her lips, but she swallowed them back, ultimately only lowering her body even further. “Mei Ruyan.” Yelu Huangwu frowned upon seeing her movement. “A lowly ant, daring to covet the heavens—how laughable.” Mei Ruyan slowly raised her head, looking directly at the woman in brocade purple robes seated on the throne. “Your Highness, with your busy schedule, still finds time to care for a commoner like me. I am deeply honored.” Yelu Huangwu rested her chin on her hand, smiling contemptuously. “You have the right to speak to me today because of Wei Yuzhi. I spare your life also because of Wei Yuzhi. It has nothing to do with whether you try to be clever or not. Therefore, clinging to his coattails is the most urgent matter.” Mei Ruyan felt a surge of anxiety as she watched her rise. Seeing the purple figure descend the steps, pass through the beaded curtain, and about to enter the inner hall, Mei Ruyan bit her lip. “I want to see him.” Yelu Huangwu paused, turning to look at her, a slight smirk playing on his lips. It was a subtle expression, but brimming with mockery. As Yelu Huangwu departed, the maids and eunuchs followed, leaving only a few guards standing like pillars on either side, as if Mei Ruyan were the only one left in the hall. “Lady Mei.” A eunuch entered the hall. Mei Ruyan rose. The eunuch glanced at her almost imperceptibly, then quickly lowered his eyes. “His Majesty summons you.” Mei Ruyan’s eyes immediately lit up, as if a vibrant life had sprung from ashes. Following the eunuch to the Liao Emperor’s bedchamber, Mei Ruyan’s tightly clenched hands were already covered in sweat. The eunuch stopped at the door. “Lady, please go in.” Mei Ruyan raised her hand, a feeling of trepidation rising within her. After a moment’s hesitation, she mustered her courage and pushed open the door. A fragrant medicinal aroma wafted towards her. Smoke curled from the bronze incense burner, emitting a pleasant fragrance. Mei Ruyan walked past the draped curtains, and upon seeing the bed, tears streamed down her face without her realizing it. Yelu Quancang, dressed in a long, wide-sleeved black robe, stood not far behind her, holding a cup of tea, quietly watching the girl he had not seen in so long. Mei Ruyan began to sob slightly, taking a while to gradually calm herself before softly calling out, “Sir.” Yelu Quancang gently placed the lid of the cup on the saucer, making a crisp, subtle sound. Mei Ruyan turned around abruptly, and that dignified and handsome face unexpectedly came into view.

chapters.title: The Word “Love” (1)
chapters.content: Mei Ruyan wanted to speak, but after a long while, she was speechless and choked with emotion. She had followed Wei Yuzhi in committing treason, and her constant longing was simply to see him again. Master Mo, known in the martial arts world as “Sound Killer,” also had a well-known name: Wei Chuzhi. Apart from that, only a very few people knew that he was a direct descendant of the Liao Dynasty’s Yelu royal family, and his real name was Yelu Quancang. The world knew that Piaomiao Mountain Mansion had a First Master, Wei Chuzhi, and a Second Master, Wei Yuzhi, but only Wei Yuzhi was seen in charge; no one had ever seen what Wei Chuzhi looked like. At this moment, he was not the leader of that mysterious assassin organization, not the feared Sound Killer, nor the ethereal and eccentric Master Mo that Mei Ruyan remembered, but an Emperor who ruled the country. Mei Ruyan was momentarily at a loss. That year, the valley entrance to Mei Mansion was charred. She identified Master Mo’s body from his clothing and weapons. At that moment, she felt an overwhelming grief, a profound despair. She had never imagined that someone like herself, struggling to survive, would one day suffer such a fate, utterly disillusioned by something as extravagant as love. Mei Ruyan buried “Master Mo’s” body in the bamboo grove of Mei Mansion, his favorite spot for quiet contemplation and playing the zither…After sitting for days before his grave, she encountered Wei Yuzhi, who had come to find an old friend. Wei Yuzhi’s appearance was no coincidence; he had come specifically to meet Yelu Quancang. “You’ve lost weight,” Mei Ruyan said, looking at his thin yet increasingly dignified face, her heart filled with mixed emotions. “Sit down,” Yelu Quancang said, sitting down near the window. Mei Ruyan hesitated for a moment, then found a seat not too close to him. Even after so long apart, she still clearly remembered that he did not like people getting too close. “You said you’d ask me to avenge you if you died; does that mean you accept my heart?” If it were the Mei Ruyan of the past, she might have deliberately flattered him to obtain the Liao Empress’s position that was so close at hand, but at this moment, nothing was more important to her than this. Even if he remained Master Mo, still forced to live a life of hiding and wandering the world, she was willing to follow him without hesitation, without regret. Yelu Quancang looked intently at the girl, his face devoid of any superfluous expression. The hall was eerily silent; Mei Ruyan felt her heart pounding like a deafening drum. “I bestow upon you ten thousand taels of gold.” Yelu Quancang’s words immediately caused Mei Ruyan’s face to change, but he seemed oblivious. “Return to the Song Kingdom and live a good life.” Mei Ruyan’s face was pale, but her gaze grew even more stubborn. “Regardless of the outcome, I want to know the answer!” As the Emperor of a nation, Yelu Quancang was not angered by Mei Ruyan’s pressing tone. He answered her calmly but earnestly, “I have never been moved by you.” “Then why did you want to see me today? Why did you bestow ten thousand taels of gold upon me?” Mei Ruyan asked persistently. Yelu Quancang said, “You married Hua Rongjian and stole many secrets for the Liao Kingdom, making great contributions. You deserve a reward, but I no longer wish to see you.” “If what you say is true, then why did you say those things in the first place?” Mei Ruyan had already vaguely guessed the answer in her heart. She was afraid to hear Yelu Quancang say it himself, but if she had not heard it with her own ears, she probably would never have given up hope. Yelu Quancang lowered his eyes and slowly said, “If I had not said that, would you have willingly risked your life for the Liao Kingdom?” “You…” Mei Ruyan’s phoenix eyes welled with tears. “You are not that kind of person.” Mei Ruyan thought she would give up after hearing the answer, but even after hearing it, she still refused to accept the appointment. Master Mo was so proud; he would never do such a vulgar thing for the sake of a woman’s service! Yelu Quancang raised his eyes, his majestic gaze mixed with surprise and helplessness. Mei Ruyan was far more intelligent and stubborn than he had imagined. After a moment of heart-wrenching pain, Mei Ruyan’s mind gradually cleared, and memories flooded back, vivid and clear. She became increasingly certain that Yelu Quancang had not been entirely without affection for her. “I heard you were plagued by illness, and you sent me away. Is that the reason?” Yelu Quancang did not answer. Mei Ruyan continued, “I just do not understand. If you are the Emperor of Liao, why did you grow up in the Song Dynasty? Why was it a sound attack? And why did you hide among the Mei family?” Yelu Quancang leaned back, one hand supporting his chin, looking somewhat languid. “The struggle for imperial power is too fierce; I had no choice but to avoid the limelight.” The previous Emperor of Liao was actually from a branch of the Yelu royal family. When Emperor Taizu of Liao was thirty-five years old, he had no sons. Therefore, he had to select outstanding boys from collateral branches to raise. Unexpectedly, three years later, Empress Xiao gave birth to a legitimate son! Having a son in old age should have been a great joy, but what should be done with those collateral branch children who were being groomed as heirs? If Emperor Taizu of Liao had lived a long life, Yelu Quancang might have smoothly inherited the throne. However, time was not on his side. Yelu Quancang was made Crown Prince at the age of eight. The following year, Emperor Taizu was injured while hunting. His injury was chronic, and he passed away a year later.

chapters.title: The Word “Love” (2)
chapters.content: One of the collateral disciples chosen by the founding Emperor launched a coup and ascended the throne. Empress Xiao sensed the impending coup and, knowing the situation was irreversible, ordered Ghost Shadow to secretly send Yelu Quancang to the Song Dynasty, where he would hide his identity and await his opportunity. Afterwards, Empress Xiao was honored as Empress Dowager, rivaling the new Emperor and wielding power for over a decade. She also raised a daughter with excellent abilities in all aspects, Yelu Huangwu. “As for hiding in Mei Mansion, it is because my identity in the Song Dynasty has been exposed, and the Liao Dynasty’s pursuit is even more intense. Therefore, I needed an opportunity,” Yelu Quancang said, “to make the Liao Dynasty believe I pose no threat.” Thus, “Master Mo” “died” in the battle within Mei Mansion. “I have no choice in this matter; you should leave.” Yelu Quancang rarely spoke so many heartfelt words in his life; this was the most care he could give Mei Ruyan. “I offended the Hua family, and only escaped death thanks to Master Wei’s help. Do you really want me to go back to the Song Dynasty to die?” Mei Ruyan said angrily. “You, as the Emperor of a nation, cannot even protect a woman?” Yelu Quancang suddenly smiled, like the first melting of snow. He stood up, walked to Mei Ruyan, and gently stroked her cheek, his expression showing an unprecedented gentleness. Mei Ruyan was stunned. “I still have some old subordinates in the Song Dynasty; that is enough to protect you. You do not understand; there’s truly no place for you in the Liao Dynasty,” Yelu Quancang said directly. “I was able to ascend to the throne entirely thanks to the Xiao family’s strong support. I will soon marry a woman from the Xiao family as my Empress.” “As long as I can stay by your side, even as a slave or maid, I will be willing.” Mei Ruyan knew her words were shameless, but she was never a noble person to begin with. “Listen to me; go.” Yelu Quancang’s tone left no room for argument. Placing Mei Ruyan in the palace meant he could protect her while he lived, but he did not know how many days he had left. Yelu Quancang was born with the weight of the empire on his shoulders. Countless people and families placed their bets on him, leaving him no choice. Illness, scheming, and power struggles destined him for a life filled with darkness. The days hidden among the plum blossoms were like a dream, and Mei Ruyan was a vibrant color within that dream. He preferred this dream to remain forever in his memory rather than have it destroyed before his eyes. Mei Ruyan was stunned for a long time, then stammered, “Can you not be Emperor…?” After saying this, she suddenly came to her senses, her face flushing red. This was probably the most foolish and presumptuous thing she had ever said in her life. Even if Yelu Quancang truly had some feelings for her, he would not give up the empire for it. But for some reason, even knowing that being by his side was fraught with danger, just seeing him made Mei Ruyan feel safe, as if there was no safer place in the world than being with him. “It was not my will, but fate.” Yelu Quancang unfastened a token from his waist and handed it to Mei Ruyan. “This token can mobilize the remaining forces of the Piaomiao Mountain Mansion.” Mei Ruyan hesitated for a moment, then took the token. “Can I use this however I want?” Yelu Quancang nodded. “Good!” Mei Ruyan put the token away and reached out to ask him, “Where’s the promised ten thousand gold pieces?” Yelu Quancang guessed what she was thinking, but let her be and had someone bring her the currency of the Song Dynasty. Mei Ruyan had followed Wei Yuzhi for a long time and knew that he had been searching for a certain medicine, and that medicine was with the Fourteenth Young Lady. This time, when Yelu Quancang was critically ill, Wei Yuzhi gave her the few pills he had obtained and sent them to the Liao Dynasty by fast horse, fulfilling her wish to see him one last time. At this point, what else could Mei Ruyan not understand? The medicine in Fourteenth Young Lady’s possession was Yelu Quancang’s life-saving medicine! Mei Ruyan resolved to return to the Song Dynasty and help Wei Yuzhi obtain the medicine!

chapters.title: A Lifetime of Protection
chapters.content: The first snow covered Bianjing. The sky was hazy, and as soon as the city gates opened, two riders and two tigers entered the city, galloping all the way to the Hua residence. Mei Yanran was already waiting at the gate with an umbrella. Seeing the newcomers, she hurried forward a few steps. “Finally back.” The rider on the back was almost completely obscured by a large camel-colored robe. He dismounted, pulled back his hood, revealing a thin face, “Aunt…” “Come with me quickly.” Before he could finish speaking, Mei Yanran pulled him inside, saying as they walked, “Fourteenth has been unconscious for many days. Without you, we can only use items beneficial to her mental strength to keep her alive, but her body is growing thinner day by day.” “Let me catch my breath, let me catch my breath.” Mo Sigui was practically dragged into the room while running. Da Jiu happily darted in, snuggled up to An Jiu’s bedside, and nudged her with his big head. Seeing that she did not react at all, he looked at Mo Sigui in confusion. “You must be tired from your journey.” Chu Dingjiang rose to offer him a seat. Under normal circumstances, Mo Sigui would have certainly teased him, but seeing An Jiu lying on the bed, barely recognizable, he said nothing more. After calming his breathing, he began to take her pulse. The room was quiet; even the sound of Da Jiu’s tail lightly swishing across the floor was crystal clear. After what seemed like an eternity, Mo Sigui slowly exhaled. Chu Dingjiang hoped every day that Mo Sigui would return with an answer, but now that it was finally here, he was somewhat reluctant to know. “How is she?” Mei Yanran asked. Mo Sigui said, “On the way here, I tried every method imaginable. Mental energy is ethereal and cannot be replenished by ordinary medicine. However, the heart is connected to all the orifices, which is the best way to nourish mental energy.” “I’ve been feeding her that pill every day, but it has not worked,” Chu Dingjiang said. Mo Sigui knew what medicine he was referring to. “It has some effect, but it is negligible! Gu Jinghong’s blood is full of medicine. It was not originally intended for long-term healing, so how can it be effective?” Sui Yuntong exclaimed in surprise, “Does this mean we need to find someone with high mental strength to raise a ‘medicine person’?” “Medicine people are best raised from the womb. We do not have that time. The best method is to use blood as a medicinal guide.” Mo Sigui had been thinking about how to treat mental trauma all the way, considering many solutions, waiting to personally examine the patient before deciding on a method. “But this blood…” “Use mine,” Chu Dingjiang said without hesitation. Mo Sigui shook his head. “Your mental power is at its peak, and your physique is exceptionally strong. You certainly seem like the perfect candidate, but your mental power differs from Ah Jiu’s, so the effect might not be very noticeable.” “Where can we find someone like that in such a short time? We cannot just sit here and wait for her to die.” Mei Yanran watched An Jiu’s aura weaken day by day, her heart filled with anxiety. “My mental power is not high, but I do not know if it is similar to hers.” Mo Sigui looked at Chu Dingjiang and said, “There’s one right here.” A name suddenly popped into Chu Dingjiang’s mind: “Wei Yuzhi.” “Yes!” Mo Sigui said. “His mental power is not only similar to Ah Jiu’s, but it is also more concentrated and solid. If we can receive nourishment from his heart’s blood, Ah Jiu’s condition may recover.” “We have to capture Wei Yuzhi alive?” Mei Yanran frowned. Wei Yuzhi was elusive. How could he be so easy to capture? Chu Dingjiang pondered, “What are the chances of success if we exchange Gu Jinghong’s heart’s blood?” Mo Sigui replied without hesitation, “Less than ten percent. Ah Jiu’s and Wei Yuzhi’s kind of mental power is a double-edged sword. It hurts others and themselves. I’ve heard Wei Yuzhi has always been in poor health, often vomiting blood. Although I have not personally examined him, I can roughly guess that his lifespan is not long.
