If we take a few more drops of his heart’s blood, he probably will not live for many more years.” Wei Yuzhi still had ambitions; he was not the kind of blindly loyal person willing to sacrifice his life for his master. Chu Dingjiang was silent for a moment, then said, “I will go find him.” Wei Yuzhi would not leave any contact information. The only way was to have Zhu Pianxian use the merchant guild to spread the news and lure him out. The winter night in Bianjing was exceptionally cold. Chu Dingjiang sat on the rooftop carrying a jar of wine, the fierce wind unable to dispel the gloom in his heart. Mo Sigui, having washed up, was about to rest for a while when the light inside flickered, and a strong smell of wine filled the air. Without turning around, Mo Sigui knew Chu Dingjiang was right behind him. “It’s rare that Lord Chu wants to chat with me,” Mo Sigui said, sitting down and pouring two cups of tea. “However, I’ve given up drinking.” “I have some worries,” Chu Dingjiang said, sitting down opposite him. Mo Sigui raised an eyebrow, watching him with interest. In Mo Sigui’s memory, Chu Dingjiang was an extremely reserved person, someone who would never want to confide in anyone. Chu Dingjiang was puzzled. “Ah Jiu has been taking pills made from Gu Jinghong’s heart’s blood without any concern, but the thought of using Wei Yuzhi’s blood makes me uneasy. Are there any hidden dangers in using Wei Yuzhi’s blood?” Mo Sigui was somewhat surprised by Chu Dingjiang’s keen perception; even without a full understanding of the interaction of mental forces, he could sense something amiss. “This kind of mental force is too aggressive; it is always a double-edged sword. I can use medicine to restrain it somewhat, but ultimately it depends on whether Ah Jiu can bring it under her control.” Chu Dingjiang had never fought Wei Yuzhi. “How strong is he?” “He can kill without lifting a finger, simply through imagination,” Mo Sigui thought for a moment. “That might not be entirely accurate, but it is roughly like…” “This.” Chu Dingjiang slowly frowned. “Ah Jiu’s current condition, with almost all her mental power gone, how can she suppress Wei Yuzhi’s power?” “Wei Yuzhi’s heart’s blood contains his will, so it is best to make him willing.” Mo Sigui lit a cigarette, squinting as he exhaled smoke. “If that is not possible, we will have to use drugs to forcibly guide him, which will inevitably be dangerous, but there’s no better way right now.” Chu Dingjiang asked, “How confident are you that you can suppress him?” Mo Sigui replied, “Mental power outside the body weakens, so I am about 80-90% confident.” The smoke was like gauze, and Chu Dingjiang saw the undisguised melancholy between Mo Sigui’s brows. Looking closer, he realized that Mo Sigui had changed drastically compared to before. He still had those captivating peach blossom eyes, but his appearance had diminished considerably. He was no longer the dashing young man he once was. His carefree demeanor was no longer languid but rather carried a deep weariness. Judging from her appearance alone, Mo Sigui was not as handsome as before, but he was even more attractive. Mo Sigui noticed Chu Dingjiang’s gaze and glared at him, saying, “What kind of look is that? Do not fall in love with me.” “Finally, you are showing some maturity.” His tone held a hint of pride, like a father watching his son grow up. Mo Sigui took a drag of his cigarette, the smoke billowing from his mouth and nose as he spoke. “Ah Jiu said you are her uncle, but I think that assessment is too biased. Tell me honestly, which grave did you crawl out of?” Chu Dingjiang remained silent. Mo Sigui continued, “Before, Ah Jiu risked having her meridians crippled by Elder Zhi so that I could leave Mei Mansion. Back then, I thought that girl was really stupid! Now I know she’s not stupid at all; she’s used her meridians to protect me for life!”

chapters.title: To Save or Not to Save
chapters.content: Mo Sigui initially began treating An Jiu partly out of interest in her condition, and partly because he felt that if it were not for him, Elder Zhi would not have destroyed her meridians. “Her meridians alone can sustain you for life? How many people would you be supported by?” Chu Dingjiang retorted, displeased with his choice of words, his reply laced with sarcasm. Mo Sigui, however, remained oblivious. After carefully considering Chu Dingjiang’s words, he found them quite reasonable. “That is right; ultimately, it is her personality that suits my taste.” Chu Dingjiang did not bother arguing with him. “Do you not need my help with anything?” Mo Sigui seemed quite vengeful, but upon closer examination, his temperament rarely exhibited the intense love and hate of Lou Mingyue. He simply enjoyed finding amusement in trivial matters. His decision not to take advantage of the situation this time was not out of consideration for An Jiu. Chu Dingjiang suspected that, besides being somewhat tired, he probably needed his help with something. Mo Sigui tapped his pipe on the table. “I have not decided yet.” “You want me to help Lou Mingyue kill Yelu Huangwu?” Chu Dingjiang had once again hit the nail on the head. Mo Sigui glared at him. “You can guess everything. Are you not tired of living?” “Revenge is only meaningful when you do it yourself.” Although Chu Dingjiang thought Lou Mingyue’s actions were not very clever, he still admired her. As the saying goes, you envy what you lack, and Chu Dingjiang lacked this drive. “Meaningful?” Mo Sigui raised his voice. “Why do I never think avenging that old man is important? Whether he’s alive or dead, I know he most wanted me to achieve something in medicine. Is that not more important and meaningful than revenge?” The “old man” he referred to was naturally Elder Qi, the Divine Physician of Mei Clan. Chu Dingjiang looked at him with a half-smile, offering no comment. A person with a detached and open mind could never understand narrow-mindedness and extremism. The phrase “empathy” was merely an empty word; no one could truly understand another person’s feelings. Hatred never reached a certain level, so naturally, one could not comprehend Lou Mingyue’s emotions. Chu Dingjiang did not say it aloud; these things, if they could be understood, would eventually be. If they could not, even the most straightforward explanations from others would only allow them to grasp the principle. However, emotions were never governed by logic. “There’s at least a 30% chance that Wei Yuzhi will offer his heart’s blood, and will not accept Gu Jinghong’s blood,” Chu Dingjiang suddenly changed the subject. Mo Sigui was taken aback. “Impossible, right? Has he gone mad lately?” “Precisely because he’s not mad,” Chu Dingjiang said. “Intelligent people have their pride. Why would he exchange his own blood? If he were to sacrifice his heart’s blood, it would be because he loves Ah Jiu.” Exchanging his own blood for Gu Jinghong’s blood would be a win-win situation, but since it was a transaction, there was no affection between him and An Jiu. And with his pride, he would never believe that achieving his goals required sacrificing himself. Mo Sigui opened his mouth but remained silent for a long while. Chu Dingjiang said, “There’s nothing surprising. The smartest people often have the most foolish side.” “No,” Mo Sigui recovered. “What surprises me is, when did that girl Ah Jiu become so popular?” Chu Dingjiang was slightly displeased. “A woman as outstanding as her naturally attracts attention.” Alright, Mo Sigui reluctantly admitted that An Jiu was outstanding. After all, she was indeed admirable in some aspects, but describing her as an “outstanding woman” was going too far! Were all the women in the world dead? Looking at An Jiu as a woman, she did not even have a passing grade in any aspect, let alone being outstanding. She really had not expected Chu Dingjiang to be so humorous! Mo Sigui felt quite indignant for all women. “She’s just good-looking.” “She’s a rough diamond.” Chu Dingjiang smiled gently, not annoyed by Mo Sigui’s assessment. Mo Sigui felt a chill run down his spine at this sudden softening aura, thinking silently to himself, “Calling her a gilded iron block would be more accurate.” Looking at An Jiu’s gleaming exterior, what else did she have besides her looks? She was nothing like his Mingyue, who was both beautiful and intelligent. Chu Dingjiang, unaware of Mo Sigui’s thoughts and not being particularly close friends, took his leave after speaking. Mo Sigui thought of Lou Mingyue, his thoughts becoming chaotic again. The drowsiness he had painstakingly cultivated with those sleeping pills had almost completely dissipated. He opened the window, watching the snowflakes fall softly outside, and lit another pipe. During his time with Lou Mingyue at the border, Mo Sigui glimpsed the vulnerability hidden beneath her toughness and stubbornness. Her efforts to armor herself only made Mo Sigui’s heart ache more. Deep or shallow feelings, Mo Sigui did not know, but he could no longer allow himself to remain a bystander. After finishing his pipe, Mo Sigui picked up a brush and wrote on a piece of paper: “If you live, return to me; if you die, I will long for you forever.” Then he crossed it out again and wrote the character for hatred next to it. He felt he still could not generate a deep-seated love or hate in his heart, but he finally accepted Lou Mingyue’s hatred as his own. As for medicine, he could just work harder. Drowsiness gradually crept in, and Mo Sigui felt the mountain weighing on his heart lighten slightly. He picked up the paper, brought it close to the brazier, squinted as he watched it burn to ashes, then got up and swayed off to sleep. In a courtyard buried deep in snow in Bianjing. A man in a blue robe sat beside the brazier, intently staring at a letter, as if trying to see through the thin paper. A sickly pallor appeared on his gentle face. The guard outside glanced at the light inside several times, finally unable to resist knocking on the door. “My Lord, it is past midnight; you should rest early.” Wei Yuzhi looked up, coughed a few times, but did not answer. The guard knew he could not control him, so he kept quiet, reminding him every so often. Fourteenth Young Lady. Wei Yuzhi’s lips moved slightly, but no sound came out. His mind was a complex mix of emotions. Even if he liked a woman, she was merely a small part of his life, a diversion outside of his schemes. To maintain a connection with her and to satisfy his own selfish desires, he could even allow himself to make things difficult for her, to hurt her. This current situation was completely unexpected; he had never considered facing the question of whether or not to save her. That girl was dying, needing his heart’s blood to save her life. “I already hate that my life is too short,” Wei Yuzhi murmured. If this meant shortening his remaining time, he could not afford to be careless. Thinking of this, Wei Yuzhi was startled. Had he subconsciously considered saving her? He raised his hand and touched the wound on his chest through his thick clothing. It was left by An Jiu. Although he had captured her first, this sword wound had indeed worsened his condition. In a sense, they were enemies. Wei Yuzhi gave a self-deprecating laugh, thinking he must have been crazy to even consider saving her. “My Lord,” the person outside knocked on the door again, reminding him, “it’s getting late.” “Alright,” Wei Yuzhi replied helplessly, turning off the light and going to sleep.

chapters.title: A Long Future Awaits
chapters.content: Wei Yuzhi usually slept very little, but his sleep quality was excellent, and he rarely dreamed. Tonight, however, he unexpectedly fell into a beautiful dream. After a light rain, the thick layer of fallen leaves in the woods reflected a beautiful face. Wei Yuzhi had never seen a woman like this before, a woman embodying both innocence and aloofness. Before that moment, he had always believed himself to be almost heartless, never capable of falling for any woman. Life was unpredictable; his suddenly flustered heart caught him off guard. Wei Yuzhi was always adept at seizing opportunities. At that time, he had not even figured out why he liked An Jiu, yet he immediately proposed. He had never been engaged, nor had he ever had a romantic relationship with a woman. He did not know how to pursue someone, so he simply expressed his feelings immediately. However, what happened afterward was also beyond Wei Yuzhi’s expectations. They were on opposing sides, and although they had many opportunities to spend time together, none of them were pleasant memories. During An Jiu’s imprisonment, Wei Yuzhi said he “once liked her,” and he truly felt that way. He thought of her less and less each day, so why did he later sacrifice his mental power to save her during the Baohua Gate incident? On the bed, Wei Yuzhi opened his eyes. Darkness still surrounded him, yet he stared intently. The most complex people yearned for simplicity. Wei Yuzhi liked living in spotless places, wearing clean and simple clothes, and needing no unnecessary accessories. He thought that the woman he could not forget, besides her beauty, was also because of her unchanging simplicity. The human heart was so complex; it was truly rare for An Jiu to maintain such purity, even if that simplicity was not exactly beautiful. Wei Yuzhi got up, put on his cloak, and went out through the back window. His solitary figure crossed the open fields, entering the heavily guarded city of Bianjing as if it were empty. Upon arriving at the Hua Mansion, Wei Yuzhi was covered in a thick layer of snow. The icy air made him cough twice. “Master Wei,” a deep, resonant voice seemed to whisper in his ear. Wei Yuzhi looked up and saw a man standing against the wall, untouched by the snow, like a tombstone. “Master Chu,” Wei Yuzhi recognized the man. Chu Dingjiang approached. “Master Wei, you’ve arrived earlier than I expected.” Wei Yuzhi did not reply. “Please,” Chu Dingjiang gestured. The two entered the courtyard one after the other. It was pitch black inside, but after passing the second gate, it suddenly lit up. Wei Yuzhi saw several rooms brightly lit. To his left, wisps of smoke were seeping from the window cracks of a building, suggesting a fire. Chu Dingjiang led him to that room and knocked on the door. A lazy voice came from inside, “The door’s unlocked.” Chu Dingjiang pushed the door open and went in. A face with an ethereal air peeked out from the thick smoke, a lazy gaze passing over Chu Dingjiang and landing directly on Wei Yuzhi. The light in his peach blossom eyes suddenly sharpened. “Ah, this must be Master Wei.” Mo Sigui, pipe in hand, strode forward, his excitement barely concealed. Wei Yuzhi remained calm, cupping his hands in greeting. “Greetings, Divine Physician Mo.” “Oh dear, no need for such formalities.” Mo Sigui picked up his pipe, grabbed Wei Yuzhi’s wrist, and forcefully dragged him into the inner room. Wherever Mo Sigui was, he always had piles of medicinal herbs. He lived in the Hua residence, and since An Jiu was ill, Hua Rongjian and Chu Dingjiang would gather a large quantity of rare herbs and send them over every two days. Hua Rongtian had also sent many herbs on behalf of the Hua family. Therefore, although he had only been there a short time, his room was already overflowing with medicine, leaving only a small space for sleeping; the room was now filled with bottles and jars. “Please, sit wherever you like,” Mo Sigui said warmly. Wei Yuzhi did not sit down. “I received news that Fourteenth Young Lady is critically ill.” Mo Sigui smiled and said, “Yes, but if you are willing to give a few drops of blood, she will not be critically ill anymore.” Even though Wei Yuzhi had taken many lives, seeing Mo Sigui’s excited smile still made him feel a little uneasy. “I want to see her.” “That is no problem,” Mo Sigui agreed without consulting him. Chu Dingjiang did not refuse either. “Master Wei, please come with me.” Wei Yuzhi nodded. For the first time, Wei Yuzhi saw An Jiu so quiet and peaceful, like an infant untouched by the world. Da Jiu, lying by the bedside, saw a strange man enter and immediately bared its teeth in a threatening manner. Wei Yuzhi acted as if he had not seen him, but his mental power swept over him like a tidal wave. Da Jiu’s eyes widened, and it stood frozen for a long time. When Wei Yuzhi approached, it came over like a cat and nudged his sleeve in a gesture of friendliness. Mo Sigui leaned over and tapped its head with her pipe. “You are such a wimp! Ah Jiu’s only redeeming quality is its fierceness, and you have not even learned that, yet you’ve got all those flaws. I despise you!” Da Jiu twitched its ears, its face blank, indicating it had not understood a word. “Fourteenth Young Lady.” Wei Yuzhi bent down, took her hand, and closed his eyes. Chu Dingjiang frowned, about to step forward, but Mo Sigui stopped him, saying softly, “Bear with it, bear with it. Touching a little hand is nothing. I’m…um, I mean, it would not hurt to let him use his mental power to probe.” Chu Dingjiang narrowed his eyes, making a mental note. Mo Sigui had only said half of what he meant, but he could guess three or five parts of it. Now was not the right time to settle scores; there would be plenty of time later.

chapters.title: Unexpected Incident
chapters.content: Physical contact between physicians and patients was unavoidable. Chu Dingjiang naturally disliked it, but it was not intolerable. He had not even minded witnessing An Jiu’s intimacy with Hua Rongjian last time. However, just seeing Wei Yuzhi holding her hand now filled him with uncontrollable unease, as if someone were tearing a piece of his heart out, causing him to doubt his decision. Perhaps he should not have let Wei Yuzhi get close to An Jiu. He thought this to himself, but his body remained completely still, even expressionless. Love was selfish, but love was also selfless. From a personal emotional perspective, Chu Dingjiang would rather An Jiu lie there forever than have her worry about another man in her life. Yet, he was willing to pay any price to save her, even if it meant losing her. Mo Sigui knew Chu Dingjiang’s love for An Jiu and understood his contradictions and struggles. Seeing that he did not step in to stop him, he sighed, thinking him a true man. Wei Yuzhi meticulously probed An Jiu’s pulse with his mental power for a long time, and when he withdrew his hand, fine beads of sweat appeared on his temples. Seeing this, Mo Sigui frowned and stepped forward to grasp his pulse, several streams of mental power and true qi instantly permeating his meridians. After a long while, Mo Sigui sighed, his expression grave, and after a moment of silence, he said, “Master Wei, let’s talk.” “No need.” Wei Yuzhi stared at An Jiu’s thin, pale face. “My body cannot withstand another stab to the heart, but since I am here, I will not back down.” Wei Yuzhi had thoroughly investigated Mo Sigui and knew him all too well! As a physician, he was always very ethical and would inform patients of serious conditions, but he was even more passionate about medicine. Faced with this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to explore, he would inform him, and regardless of Wei Yuzhi’s final decision, he would not let it slip away. “Talking to a wise man is so convenient and effortless. It is wonderful!” Mo Sigui said cheerfully. “Then I will go prepare! Do not worry, YOU will not die!” Mo Sigui rushed out like he’d been injected with adrenaline. The room fell silent. “Master Wei is willing to sacrifice his life to save Ah Jiu; I thank you on her behalf,” Chu Dingjiang said. Wei Yuzhi turned his head, his face handsome and gentle, his eyes calm and undisturbed. “No need. I also have a request.” Chu Dingjiang raised an eyebrow slightly. “Exchange it for Gu Jinghong’s blood,” Wei Yuzhi said. Chu Dingjiang was slightly surprised; this was unexpected. He thought Wei Yuzhi was a proud strategist and would not agree to exchange his own blood for the Liao Emperor’s life-saving medicine. He had not expected Wei Yuzhi to make this request himself. “That is exactly what I was thinking,” Chu Dingjiang paused, then asked, “Even without this method, is it possible that Master Wei could not obtain the medicine?” Wei Yuzhi shook his head. “Even if the medicine were in your hands, I am confident I could retrieve it, though it would take a considerable amount of time. My Lord cannot wait, and neither can I. As for Fourteenth Young Lady…” He sighed softly, “If I had lived longer, I would certainly have fought you for it. But what use would it be now? I do not have time to grow old with her. Besides, a few drops of blood cannot win someone’s heart.” Since he had already dedicated the first half of his life to scheming, then he would use this short life to accomplish one thing, which would be enough to leave no regrets. As for matters of the heart… “I will forgo leaving a mark in her heart. That will be all my love for her.” Wei Yuzhi, supporting himself on the edge of the bed, rose, glanced deeply at An Jiu, and turned to leave. “I wish Master Wei great success.” Chu Dingjiang’s words came from the bottom of his heart. He held strategists like Wei Yuzhi in the highest esteem. Only now did Chu Dingjiang realize that his defeat to Zhang Yi, Xi Shou, and others was not due to intelligence. In terms of strategy, Xi Shou might not even be as capable as him. The problem was that he always had something more important than dreams in his heart. Shang Yang lived and died for his dreams—something Chu Dingjiang could never do. In his past life, it was for his family; in this life, it was for a woman. What a person valued ​​most determined their breadth of vision and ambition. Chu Dingjiang shed his last shred of pride and resentment, admitting that he could only ever be a free spirit, wandering the world with his wife. Outside, snowflakes fell sparsely. Wei Yuzhi stood on the veranda, sensing Chu Dingjiang emerge. Without turning back, he said, “Master Chu, you’ve wasted your talent.” Chu Dingjiang replied calmly, “What life does not have its regrets? It is better to have wasted one’s talent than one’s wife; at least one’s talent will not be wounded, and I need not be.” Wei Yuzhi turned around, scrutinizing Chu Dingjiang. Seeing his upright and unrestrained demeanor, he could not help but ask, “Not a trace of resentment?” Chu Dingjiang smiled but did not answer. He had felt more than just resentment before. He even felt that fate was unfair, that his lack of achievement was due to a lack of opportunity. Thinking back to his naive and arrogant thoughts, Chu Dingjiang’s smile deepened. It was not that people were not afraid of being foolish in the past, but that they remained foolish without realizing it. “Master Wei, let’s begin!” Mo Sigui poked his head out of the window. Since Chu Dingjiang announced Wei Yuzhi’s arrival, Mo Sigui had prepared all the medicinal herbs and utensils. Now, they only needed to be laid out and used immediately, requiring little time. Wei Yuzhi glanced past Chu Dingjiang’s shoulder at the room behind him, then walked towards Mo Sigui’s room. Mo Sigui’s room was still filled with smoke and the strong smell of medicine. The area in the center of the room, which had previously been piled with medicinal herbs, had been cleared out, replaced by a low couch. Beside it, a small table was covered with various knives, silver needles, and small bottles. Seeing Wei Yuzhi sit down on the edge of the couch, Mo Sigui, while tossing a knife into the medicinal solution to disinfect it, said, “Although Master Wei generally knows the situation, I still need to explain some details.” “Please speak, Divine Physician,” Wei Yuzhi said. Mo Sigui glanced at him sideways. “You look so refined, like a bookworm. You show no signs of cunning. No wonder you’ve been wandering the martial world for so long without being recognized.” Wei Yuzhi raised the corners of his mouth. “Divine Physician, you flatter me.” Even this meaningless smile of his was full of scholarly air, making him appear gentle and approachable. He did not seem like a ruthless and cunning fellow at all! Mo Sigui pursed his lips, continuing the previous topic. “My Lord, you should know what heart’s blood is, so a cut to the heart is unavoidable, but I will try my best to minimize the wound.” Wei Yuzhi listened and simply said, “I have a request.” “Speak, I will try my best to fulfill it.” Mo Sigui wiped the silver needles one by one. “I want to be awake,” Wei Yuzhi said. Mo Sigui’s hands paused. “I believe that with your mental strength, you will not hinder me from drawing blood, but I must remind you, even if you are unconscious, you may not be completely unaware of the pain. If we only use local anesthesia, I am afraid…as a physician, I must advise you to abandon this idea.” The wound for drawing blood from the heart was too deep; even Mo Sigui could not guarantee the effectiveness of local anesthesia. However, pain was one thing; personally experiencing being dissected was truly terrifying. Seeing his determined gaze, Mo Sigui immediately said, quite shamelessly. “Alright, since you insist, I will go along with it. I’ve already tried to dissuade you.” “Hmm,” Mo Sigui continued, “Drawing blood is risky; what if…” Wei Yuzhi interrupted him, “I trust Physician Mo.” Mo Sigui gathered his sleeves, placed his hands in the medicine basin to wash them, and heard this. Suddenly, he laughed. “Oh dear, you are really putting pressure on me like this, but I like it. Take off your clothes!” Wei Yuzhi silently loosened his belt, revealing his upper body. Mo Sigui glanced at him; he was not as shabby as he had imagined. Wei Yuzhi’s frame was naturally broad and large; even a skinny camel was bigger than a horse. Although long-term illness had left him with very little flesh, he did not look particularly frail. However, his body was covered in wounds, making him look quite gruesome. This contrasted sharply with his gentle and refined face. “What happened to these wounds?” Mo Sigui frowned, staring at the numerous scars on his chest. He had no time to pity a man; normal skin was elastic, making wounds easy to stitch, but scarred skin lost this advantage, becoming difficult to treat. The facts were clear, and Mo Sigui felt it necessary to know which bastard had ruined his “experiment.” “Most of them are from childhood,” Wei Yuzhi said, raising his hand to cover a fresh wound. “This is from Fourteenth Young Lady.” Speaking of which, he also had something from her…this scar. Mo Sigui nodded with an expression that said, “She really is a bastard. Lie down.” Although a brazier was lit in the room, Wei Yuzhi was weak and more susceptible to cold than most. His bare upper body made him even more alert, as the cold seeped into his body. “Logically speaking, if you had forced yourself to exercise, you should not be in this state today. I am rather curious; how did you get yourself into this state?” Mo Sigui asked. Wei Yuzhi lay on the couch, not answering but staring blankly at the roof beams. His father, a military general of the Song Dynasty, was unjustly convicted and sentenced to beheading, while the entire family was exiled. For women and children, the remote and desolate place of exile was a near-certain death sentence. But as members of a military family, both the women and children were physically stronger than ordinary people. If that incident had not happened, his mother and sister might not have died. On the road to exile, a group of soldiers, lusting after his mother’s and sister’s beauty, raped them. Unable to bear the humiliation, the two women committed suicide from the rafters of the post station’s stable. He would never forget the rat-infested cell, the lewd looks those men gave his mother and sister, or waking up one morning beside a haystack to find their two disheveled corpses. At that moment, his spirit was greatly stimulated, his mental power suddenly erupted, and he killed everyone in the post station. For Wei Yuzhi, the corrupt Song Dynasty should not linger on! His hatred could not be quelled simply by killing his enemies! He was originally only unsuitable for martial arts due to his meridians; his body was perfectly healthy. It was only during his years of exile that he suffered greatly, and the sudden surge of his own mental power severely damaged his body, preventing him from ever fully recovering. Wei Yuzhi pursed his lips slightly, waiting until he felt Mo Sigui apply a cool liquid to his chest before asking, “Physician Mo, how much longer do I have to live?” “This blood draw will shorten your life by two years. And you originally only had four or five years left to live anyway.” Mo Sigui spoke bluntly, unafraid to discourage his patient, because his next words offered Wei Yuzhi some comfort: “That was before you met me. If you can afford the consultation fee, I can extend your life by a few years.”

chapters.title: Vinegar
chapters.content: “If the consultation fee you speak of is money, then I have plenty,” Wei Yuzhi said. For him, money was one of the tools to achieve his ambitions; he had amassed a considerable amount over the years while managing the Piaomiao Mountain Mansion within the Song Dynasty. Mo Sigui said, “If you could offer something that interests me, that would be even better.” “Does the Divine Physician mean he will take me as his patient?” Wei Yuzhi found it unbelievable. Would Mo Sigui treat a strategist from an enemy state? Mo Sigui lowered his eyes and wiped his knife. “You do not need to look at me like that. What happens to the Song Dynasty or the Liao Dynasty is none of my concern.” “I believe that even if the Divine Physician does not have a heart for protecting his country, he must at least have the compassion of a physician.” Wei Yuzhi did not spell it out; everyone knew that the Liao Dynasty, having invaded the rich lands of the Song Dynasty, would inevitably plunder. “In times of prosperity, the people suffer; in times of ruin, the people suffer.” Mo Sigui covered his face with a handkerchief and lit a censer of medicinal incense. As wisps of smoke filled the room, a faint, sweet fragrance permeated the air. Wei Yuzhi felt his limbs growing increasingly numb, initially like the sensation of suddenly standing up after squatting for a long time. After about a quarter of an hour, this feeling gradually disappeared. Mo Sigui gently made a cut in his chest with a thin knife, and a bead of blood instantly welled up. Wei Yuzhi’s blood was different from ordinary people’s; it was not only thin but also very pale, appearing beautiful against his fair skin. Mo Sigui frowned. At this rate of blood loss, he could easily bleed to death… He paused, then turned and added another medicine to the incense burner, making the fragrance suddenly even stronger. Wei Yuzhi felt his eyelids growing heavier and heavier. He knew Mo Sigui had broken his promise, but he did not struggle, letting himself drift into unconsciousness. Perhaps this was the most indulgent Wei Yuzhi had ever been, completely entrusting his life to someone else—and that person might be an enemy. Outside, the snow continued to fall, piling up thicker and thicker on the ground. Chu Dingjiang stood on the veranda for a while, watching until Mei Yanran had cleaned An Jiu, then turned and went inside. During An Jiu’s coma, he had done his utmost to maintain her current state. But just now, merely receiving nourishment from Wei Yuzhi’s mental energy had caused her complexion to change, leaving him both happy and conflicted. It might seem like a typical man’s mentality, but it wasn’t. Having been reborn from the Warring States period to the Song Dynasty, Chu Dingjiang believed in destiny and the cycle of fate; one person would not have an unwarranted connection with another. He worried that this was yet another cruel joke fate had played on him. In his previous life, he had given everything for his family, only to be abandoned and betrayed in return. In this life, he had fallen deeply in love with a woman, and he worried that one day the ending would be the same as before. Holding An Jiu’s hand, Chu Dingjiang could not help but chuckle self-deprecatingly. The once spirited and shrewd man had actually begun to fret over something intangible. “I’ve never done anything against the heavens. Surely I should not be so fooled,” Chu Dingjiang thought back. In the past, although everything he did was for the family, he had never truly cared about human nature. He had even harmed many family members for his schemes, and even when he was punished, it was out of emotion. He would not treat An Jiu like this; surely he would not be betrayed by her… As dawn approached, Chu Dingjiang heard the sound of Mo Sigui’s door opening. Before he could get up, Mo Sigui rushed in like a whirlwind, carrying his medicine box. He yanked off the blankets covering An Jiu and began undressing her to administer acupuncture, oblivious to everyone else. The sight made Chu Dingjiang’s veins throb. If he were not a calm person, he would have already rushed over and beaten that guy to death! Seeing An Jiu’s naked body, Chu Dingjiang felt a surge of anger. He turned and left to avoid disturbing her treatment, but he was determined to backstab him afterward and wait until An Jiu recovered… Mei Yanran stopped a short distance away. “The Mei family is here.” “Tell them it is too late,” Chu Dingjiang said indifferently. When the Mei family came to him for the Secret Manual of Konghe, he demanded they personally punish Elder Zhi with a one-month deadline. There were still a few days left until the deadline, but his mood was extremely bad. Even if the Mei family tore Elder Zhi to pieces, it would not make him happy in the slightest, so he had no desire to see them. Mei Yanran did not try to persuade him further, instead asking, “Is Sigui inside?” It would have been better if she had not mentioned it! The mere mention of it made Chu Dingjiang’s heart churn with jealousy, the sourness practically oozing from his mouth and nostrils! He took a deep breath, calmed himself slightly, and gave a deep, resonant “Mmm.” Mei Yanran, unaware of the details, assumed he was overly worried and reassured him, “Everything will be alright.” She genuinely believed everything would be alright. Mei Jiu had thrived since her rebirth, enjoying a harmonious relationship with Hua Rongtian and demonstrating remarkable skill in managing her subordinates. She now possessed the demeanor of a matriarch of a prominent family, a true Madam Hua. An Jiu, also reborn, should not have died so young. The sky gradually brightened. Mo Sigui finally emerged from the house. Chu Dingjiang turned to look at him. His eyes were bloodshot, but his gaze was filled with excitement. Chu Dingjiang knew it was due to his immersion in medical practice, but he still could not help feeling hostility towards him. Mo Sigui exclaimed happily, “Alright, alright! I cannot sense Ah Jiu’s mental power, but she has a faint reaction, which means she’s regained consciousness.” Having received no response, he slightly suppressed his excitement and carefully examined Chu Dingjiang in the dim morning light. The man’s face was stiff, his thin lips pressed into a line, his gaze fixed on him with a piercing intensity, as if he wanted to poke two holes in him. He could not help but say, “What’s with that expression? Should you not be happy?” After a moment’s thought, Mo Sigui happily exclaimed, “Oh dear, you are just too happy! Invite me to dinner another day!” Today, he had made progress in his medical skills, equivalent to turning a new page in the history of medicine, truly something to be happy about! It could be said that this was the happiest thing in the past two years. So, humming a little tune, he headed to his room, intending to take a bath and then get a good night’s sleep before observing An Jiu and Wei Yuzhi’s condition, completely unaware that the air behind him was practically frozen. Mei Yanran noticed Chu Dingjiang’s unusual aura and was a little puzzled, but as soon as she entered the room, she understood everything! An Jiu was disheveled on the bed, her clothes scattered on the floor. Mo Sigui, of course, had not bothered to dress her properly when he left, only hastily covering her with the blanket. The scene looked rather jarring. She understood that Chu Dingjiang was angry because he needed to remove her clothes for acupuncture, and if he saw this scene again… Mei Yanran quickly lowered the curtain, hastily tidied up the mess, and helped An Jiu dress. Only after everything was in order did she realize that Chu Dingjiang had entered the room sometime earlier. Meanwhile, in a mansion on the outskirts of Bianjing, the usual tranquility had vanished due to Wei Yuzhi’s disappearance. Although his subordinates had seen the letter, he left without saying goodbye, and this was not the first time he’d done something like this; they could not help but worry because his health was so poor. Just as they were fretting, a rider arrived at the mansion. A woman draped in a dark cloak, travel-worn, was recognized by a guard who stepped forward to help her horse. “Lady Ruyan,” the guard said. Mei Ruyan nodded and went inside to find Songxi. Songxi was Wei Yuzhi’s most capable subordinate, skilled in both literature and martial arts. Wei Yuzhi often entrusted him with many affairs of the Piaomiao Mountain Mansion. Although Yelu Quancang had given her the Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, she did not even know where it was located and needed help. “Where is Master?” Mei Ruyan asked. Songxi was anxious. Seeing Mei Ruyan’s sudden arrival, he was slightly startled and hesitated before saying, “Master left a letter and went out.” His momentary hesitation made Mei Ruyan sense something was amiss. A thought flashed through her mind, and she knew that something must be wrong with Wei Yuzhi’s health, but she pretended not to know and took out the token given to her by Yelu Quancang. Songxi saw the familiar token and immediately knelt. Before he could speak, Mei Ruyan said, “Rise.” She was speaking for the Emperor. Mei Ruyan’s martial arts skills were not high, but she played the zither exceptionally well, killing with her music. It seemed she had received some of the Master’s true teachings. Songxi had always been humble towards her but never truly respected her. Now, he had to reassess Mei Ruyan’s position. “The Master has entrusted Piaomiao Mountain Mansion to me,” Mei Ruyan said. Songxi was stunned. After a moment, he felt indignant. His master had devoted so much effort to Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, and in the end, it had been taken away by a woman! Mei Ruyan knew that Songxi was only loyal to Wei Yuzhi and probably only felt awe towards Yelu Quancang. Therefore, she wanted him to help her and prevent him from opposing Wei Yuzhi. “The Lord ordered me to take over Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, but in reality, it is just to shut the princess up,” Mei Ruyan said, feigning reluctance to seize power, “explaining” Yelu Quancang’s good intentions to Songxi. “The princess does not want you to return to court and will surely try every means to destroy all your power. The Lord does not want the princess to become too powerful, and considering your years of dedication, he naturally cannot allow Piaomiao Mountain Mansion to fall. Therefore, he sent me to take over. Actually, it is just a formality; my main purpose is to help you find the medicine.” Mei Ruyan was the Master’s person, and Piaomiao Mountain Mansion was under the Master’s direct jurisdiction. Even if Yelu Huangwu was incredibly audacious, he would still have reservations. After hearing this, Songxi believed her somewhat, and his hostility towards her lessened. “I often need to report some information to the Lord. If there’s anything I do not understand in the future, please do not hesitate to enlighten me, Master Song,” Mei Ruyan said, rising and bowing. Songxi quickly avoided her. “I would not dare; it is my duty.” Mei Ruyan smiled and said nothing more. Songxi arranged accommodations for her to rest. A day passed. Mo Sigui carefully checked on An Jiu and Wei Yuzhi, finding them both unharmed. Since An Jiu was out of danger, Mo Sigui focused most of his attention on Wei Yuzhi.

chapters.title: Awakening
chapters.content: “How is he?” Chu Dingjiang asked. Mo Sigui immediately became wary. “Let me tell you, you are not allowed to touch him. Killing someone in my room is not the act of a hero. If you are so capable, go outside and fight him when he’s better.” Chu Dingjiang, his expression unchanged, found a stool and sat down. “When have I ever killed someone and then talked nonsense?” Mo Sigui thought about it and realized it was true, so he relaxed. “Anyway, I will not let him die in this room. As for the rest…” “Shortened lifespan?” Chu Dingjiang glanced at the person on the bed, whose breathing was weak. “Logically speaking, that is how it would be, but since he saved Ah Jiu, I will give him a few years of lifespan.” Mo Sigui sat on the ground, his body almost submerged in the pile of medicine, his posture casual, but once he said this, no one could question it. After he finished speaking, he asked suspiciously, “Are you not always concerned about the country and its people? Why did you not kill him?” Chu Dingjiang was a man who would stop at nothing to achieve his goals. If he wanted to kill someone, there would be no reason to stop him. “I have withdrawn from the Konghe Army and am no longer a subject of the Great Song.” This was only one reason; Chu Dingjiang’s thoughts ran far deeper. He had not acted when he had the chance to kill Wei Yuzhi, and he would not now either. Without Wei Yuzhi, the Liao Kingdom would quickly unify, and that would truly be a nightmare for the Great Song. Mo Sigui neither confirmed nor denied his explanation, nor did he press further, as it was not important to him. “Wei Yuzhi will wake up tomorrow, but Ah Jiu… Sigh! I cannot say for sure.” She might wake up quickly; she might lie there for ten days, half a month, or even years; or she might never wake up again. This was Mo Sigui’s first attempt to nourish someone with a damaged mental force using blood. According to medical books, it was theoretically effective, but reality was not always so. Mo Sigui was not one to blindly believe in medical texts; he had been repeatedly verifying and refuting the information left by his predecessors. He was also beginning to accumulate his own experience. “It will be useful.” Chu Dingjiang did not know if he was comforting himself or speaking to Mo Sigui; his tone resolute, as if he had personally confirmed it. He paused for a moment, then reminded him, “Just because I will not harm Wei Yuzhi does not mean everyone else will not. Do not forget, this is the Hua Mansion.” It’s the residence of the Prime Minister of the Song Dynasty! Hua Rongjian and Mei Jiu often came to visit An Jiu. “I know.” Mo Sigui lit a cigarette, the aroma of medicine spreading with the smoke. He leaned against the edge of the bed, squinting at Chu Dingjiang. “I never thought we could live under the same roof peacefully. It is only because I am a good person; otherwise, I would have poisoned you a thousand times over.” Chu Dingjiang said calmly, “Thank you for your mercy, Divine Physician.” “Tch!” With a sneer, wisps of smoke escaped Mo Sigui’s mouth. “What do you know?” “I know you are enduring this to gain a favor so that one day you can save Lou Mingyue from danger,” Chu Dingjiang said. Lou Mingyue had ventured alone into the Liao Kingdom; sooner or later, she would be discovered. Once that happens, there would be no escape. Only a master of the Transcendent Realm had the ability to bring someone out amidst such danger. Mo Sigui raised a pair of peach blossom eyes. “I really do not understand how you and Ah Jiu, both such boring people, could become a couple.” Chu Dingjiang remained silent. Their humor was something others could not understand. Mo Sigui finished a cigarette, a hazy sleepiness clouding his eyes. Chu Dingjiang quietly went out and returned to the room, lying down beside An Jiu. He quickly fell into a deep sleep as well. In the six months since An Jiu had been in a coma, Chu Dingjiang had never slept so well and even had a dream. In his dream, he was in the State of Zhao. The countryside was a sea of ​​pink and white peach and apricot blossoms, the sun shining brightly. He was napping on a woolen blanket, the falling petals almost burying him. He opened his eyes, the light blinding. He vaguely saw someone standing beside him with arms crossed, watching him. His vision cleared for a long time, but the person’s features remained blurry. “Are you awake?” a slightly hoarse voice asked. Chu Dingjiang abruptly opened his eyes. Bright sunlight streamed in through the window, and An Jiu stood by the bed, arms crossed, her back to the light, looking down intently at him. Perhaps the sunlight was too dazzling, but tears suddenly slid down Chu Dingjiang’s cheeks. An Jiu leaned down and hugged him. Chu Dingjiang was filled with emotion, thinking that An Jiu had been bedridden for so long, and finally understood the coldness of human relationships. This time, she actually took the initiative to hug and comfort him; it was truly precious. As he was thinking this, An Jiu sighed, “You’ve suffered so much these past years.” “These past years?” Chu Dingjiang asked, puzzled. An Jiu released him, touching his face and the white hair at his temples. “I’ve been bedridden for at least ten years, and you’ve aged so much.” An Jiu was indeed deeply moved, thinking that Chu Dingjiang’s ability to care for a living dead person for so many years was truly love. Chu Dingjiang sat up, rubbing his temples and chuckling wryly, “You are infuriating the moment you open your eyes.” After calming himself for a moment, Chu Dingjiang turned to An Jiu. “You’ve only been in a coma for about half a year.” An Jiu slightly opened her eyes. “In just over half a year, you’ve gone from being an uncle to a grandfather! Why the rush?” “…” Chu Dingjiang stared at her speechlessly for a long time, then reached out and pulled her into his arms. She was so thin; even with one arm around her, it felt empty. “Master Chu, Madam Hua has come to see Ah Jiu.” Mei Yanran knocked on the door from outside. “Come in!” Chu Dingjiang was in a great mood. Mei Jiu was nine months pregnant, nearing her due date, but she still insisted on coming to see An Jiu every day. She entered, supporting her belly, and paused, stunned, when she saw An Jiu standing by the bed. Mei Yanran was also taken aback. “How did you get so fat!” An Jiu thought Mei Jiu, this aristocratic lady, had become too carefree and plump! But then she remembered that Mei Jiu had been pregnant before she fainted. Mei Jiu burst into tears of joy and was about to rush over to hug An Jiu when she suddenly froze. “Mother, my water broke!” Mei Yanran immediately called out, “Someone, come here!” A group of servants rushed in. The woman at the head, upon hearing that Mei Jiu’s water had broken, quickly ordered her to be carried into the delivery room. Mei Jiu was about to give birth and had been running around all day. Hua Rongtian was worried about unexpected situations, so he had prepared three delivery rooms in the mansion, one of which was next to this small courtyard. “Lie down and rest for a while. I will go prepare some food for you,” Chu Dingjiang said. Upon hearing the word “food,” An Jiu’s stomach rumbled. Having been standing since waking up, she was now sweating slightly and had no choice but to lie down obediently. Chu Dingjiang went to Mo Sigui’s room first, finding him lying among piles of medicine, reading medical books. He said in as calm a tone as possible, “She’s awake!” Mo Sigui jumped up, and before Chu Dingjiang could ask An Jiu what she could eat, he rushed out like the wind, leaving a shoe on the threshold without even returning to pick it up. The woman was lying in bed anxiously waiting for food when a madman kicked the door open. Seeing she was indeed awake, he grabbed her and howled. “Mo Sigui.” An Jiu recognized him only by the scent of medicine on him. Luckily, she had been lying in bed for so long that her body’s reactions had become sluggish; otherwise, she would have already struck him down! Chu Dingjiang sighed, went to the kitchen, and found that Mei Yanran had already cooked white porridge, so he took the pot and bowl away. Inside the room, Mo Sigui was already sitting on a stool, taking An Jiu’s pulse. “Her qi and blood are insufficient; she should not talk much for the next two weeks,” Mo Sigui told Chu Dingjiang with a dark face. Chu Dingjiang knew perfectly well that this had nothing to do with blood and qi; An Jiu had probably offended him again with her words. So he did not reply, simply saying, “The kitchen has cooked porridge; have some first.” Mo Sigui touched his stomach and went over to get a bowl. “I will have some too.” The three of them ate a pot of porridge around the bed while Mei Jiu next door screamed her lungs out. At first, the news came in so many waves that Mei Yanran was a little confused. Then, seeing that An Jiu was alright, she went to Mei Jiu’s side. “She’s screaming so terribly; is she alright?” An Jiu asked. “She’s screaming with such vigor; what could be wrong?” Mo Sigui smacked his lips twice. “If only there were some pickled vegetables.” Mo Sigui had checked Mei Jiu’s body; her baby was in the correct position, and she was taking good care of herself, so there should not be any problems. After dinner, An Jiu went to the bathing room to wash up, then felt a little dizzy. She quickly fell asleep after returning to her room. Mei Jiu, on the other hand, would rest for a while and then scream again, her voice becoming hoarse. Mo Sigui calculated the time; Wei Yuzhi should be waking up soon. He picked up the things he had scattered on the floor as he rushed over and returned to the house. “Physician Mo,” Wei Yuzhi said. “Huh, you woke up earlier than I expected.” Mo Sigui tossed the things in his basket and put on his shoes. “I just woke up.” Wei Yuzhi’s voice was slightly weak. “Who is shouting?” “The First Madam of the Hua family is giving birth. You just woke up, so do not talk too much. The pervert next door woke up, ate, and even took a bath. I’ve never seen anyone more energetic than her!” Mo Sigui sat back on the couch, picked up the book, poured a bowl of medicine from the stove, and held it to Wei Yuzhi’s lips, sticking a straw in the bowl. “It will be easier to drink with this.” Wei Yuzhi smiled faintly, did not ask anything, and drank the bowl of medicine with the straw. The medicine was brewed by Mo Sigui beforehand and kept warm on the stove; it was just the right consistency for drinking. After taking his medicine, Wei Yuzhi felt a bit better. “I slept very well last night.” It was the best sleep he’d ever had in his life. Previously, his sleep quality was very high, so even if he slept little, he could still get the necessary rest. But this time was different. He knew he had slept for a long time, and when he woke up, his body and mind felt more relaxed than ever before, as if all burdens had been lifted. “Of course,” Mo Sigui said without surprise. The medicinal smoke he had smoked last night was from a newly changed prescription. Even someone like him, with severe insomnia and strong drug resistance, could sleep well, let alone an ordinary person. “I can prolong your life by a few years, but you know that heart’s blood is the essence of the body’s vital energy. Your appearance is much older than before,” Mo Sigui said. Wei Yuzhi had a gentle demeanor and fair skin and did not look much different from before, except that his once black hair was now completely white, even his eyebrows.

chapters.title: Meeting
chapters.content: His white hair, like frost, contrasted with his pale face. He did not actually look old, but rather like the morning mist, about to dissipate with the rising sun. Even Mo Sigui could not help but sigh at how fragile life was. “Speak less, rest more,” Mo Sigui said, lowering his eyes to read his medical book. The jubilation in the courtyard caused by An Jiu’s awakening quickly subsided. Mei Jiu’s shouts were hoarse, and about three hours later, the baby’s loud cry was heard. Hua Rongtian stood outside the delivery room, his face as serious as ever. “Congratulations, My Lord! Mother and child are safe. It is a little gentleman!” The midwife ran out beaming. Hua Rongtian relaxed slightly, gave a reward, and went inside to see his wife and child. The delivery room was a place stained with blood, and the midwife should have stopped Hua Rongtian from entering. However, seeing his imposing presence and having received a considerable reward herself, she only gave a soft reminder, considering it fulfilling her duty. The room reeked of blood. Mei Jiu was drenched in sweat, and maids were carefully cleaning her away the blood and sweat from her. Another midwife was wrapping up the tiny infant. Everyone was startled when they saw Hua Rongtian, then stopped what they were doing and bowed. “Continue,” Hua Rongtian said. The others responded and resumed their work. Mei Jiu heard Hua Rongtian’s voice, opened her mouth, but had no strength to speak. “Rest well; the baby is fine,” Hua Rongtian said softly, holding her hand. “Thank you for your hard work, Madam.” A smile appeared in Mei Jiu’s eyes. She thought to herself that her child and An Jiu were destined to be together, having come out so eagerly as soon as she woke up. Seeing Mei Jiu had fallen asleep, Hua Rongtian touched her cheek before turning to look at the infant. He had an eldest daughter from his previous marriage, and he believed that as a father, he had given her plenty of care and education, but he was always very busy. He rarely saw his daughter, but now, holding his tiny, soft son, he suddenly realized how little attention he had given her. Fortunately, he had married Mei Jiu. Seeing that his daughter treated her like her own mother, Hua Rongtian knew Mei Jiu truly cared for his daughter. Therefore, he not only loved Mei Jiu deeply but also felt gratitude towards her. Hua Rongtian found it hard to imagine how the Mei family, a clandestine line of assassins, could have raised such a refined and cultured woman as Mei Jiu. Mei Jiu’s skills in poetry, calligraphy, weiqi, and painting were no less than any man’s. Together, they could play music in harmony, engage in fierce weiqi battles, and discuss classical texts and poetry. She understood everything he said, requiring no further explanation; most of the time, she simply listened quietly, comforting him after a long day. In daily life, Mei Jiu managed the household impeccably, requiring no effort from him, and often prepared meals with her own hands, taking meticulous care of his needs. Hua Rongtian’s love for his ex-wife was passionate and pure, a love that caused him both deep love and profound pain. The deep, enduring love between him and Mei Jiu filled him with immense satisfaction. He felt incredibly fortunate to have married such a woman. The entire Hua household was filled with joy because Mei Jiu had given birth to their eldest son. Mei Jiu, however, felt a pang of regret, as she could not properly talk to An Jiu due to her postpartum confinement. But this regret did not last long. An Jiu and Mo Sigui came to offer their congratulations. Mo Sigui, being a physician, was able to enter the inner chambers openly under the pretext of taking her pulse. As soon as the two sat down, Mei Jiu looked at An Jiu with teary eyes. A maidservant quickly reminded her, “Madam, you must not cry. Crying during your confinement will damage your eyes.” “You may leave now,” Mei Jiu said. The head maidservant led the others out. An Jiu got up and went to the bedside to look at her. “Where’s the child?” “With the wet nurse.” Mei Jiu pulled her hand, making her sit on the edge of the bed. “You’ve suffered so much.” An Jiu had been bedridden for half a year, her body reduced to skin and bones. Mo Sigui had carefully nursed her back for several days, and her complexion had only slightly improved. “I always feel that the suffering you are experiencing now should have been my fate,” Mei Jiu sighed. “Every time I think about this, I cannot eat or sleep.” She was enjoying herself here, while others suffered for her. “You are overthinking it,” An Jiu comforted her. “If you were in this situation, you would have died long ago. What fate would you have? This is my own fate; do not be sentimental.” “Cough cough.” Mo Sigui felt a pain in his liver, yet also wanted to laugh. Mei Jiu was already used to her sharp words. “I know what you are saying, but sometimes I cannot help feeling uneasy.” An Jiu was too lazy to comment on Mei Jiu’s deeply ingrained saintly nature. Seeing that although she still appeared weak and vulnerable on the outside, her heart had become strong, she felt a little gratified. Mei Jiu then became enthusiastic, saying, “My husband and I have discussed it, and we will have you become the child’s godmother after the baby’s 100-day celebration. What do you think?” An Jiu looked at her expressionlessly. “If you do not agree, then do not disagree. Why put on that face?” Mei Jiu muttered softly, like a wronged little girl. “I’ve thought about it, and I’ve decided to agree.” An Jiu’s face immediately lit up with joy, and she explained casually, “I already felt unfortunate enough to have anything to do with someone as troublesome as you, and I did not want to add to my troubles. But considering that Hua Rongtian is quite outstanding, this child might not be bad in the future.” Mei Jiu was not angry at all; instead, she was even happier, feeling honored. “I did not expect you to be able to praise someone. It shows how outstanding my husband really is.” Mo Sigui, who had been silent for a while, chuckled and interjected, “As the saying goes, daughters resemble their fathers, and sons resemble their mothers.” An Jiu’s face immediately darkened. Mei Jiu hurriedly said, “You’ve already agreed; you cannot go back on your word. My son rushed out as soon as he saw you; it shows our deep connection.” “Or maybe he’s here to collect a debt,” Mo Sigui said. Mei Jiu became anxious and scolded, “Cousin!” Mo Sigui clicked his tongue and stepped forward to take her pulse. “Women in postpartum confinement really cannot take a joke.” An Jiu ultimately did not change her mind and decided to adopt a godson, but she truly felt a heavy pressure in her heart. For an assassin, having too many attachments was a fatal thing; even though she might not necessarily be an assassin now, her mindset of many years was difficult to change overnight. After sitting for a while, An Jiu and Mei Jiu both felt a little tired, so Mo Sigui went back with An Jiu. Chu Dingjiang was already waiting at the door. Chu Dingjiang’s spirits had improved a lot in the past few days; he had shaved and looked much younger. However, his temples were still gray, and he still looked like he had experienced many hardships. An Jiu took his hand, saying, “Before, after shaving, you could be considered the same age as Hua Rongtian. Now, no matter what, you are an uncle.” Chu Dingjiang remained calm: “I will be an uncle sooner or later. What difference does it make if it is sooner or later?” Mo Sigui returned to the house and saw Wei Yuzhi leaning against a pile of medicine, reading. The room was softly lit, and he appeared as serene as a still pool. “Physician Mo is back,” Wei Yuzhi said, looking up with a faint smile. “Seeing how well they get along, do you not think it is not worth it?” Mo Sigui asked. Wei Yuzhi could not see, but with his exceptional mental abilities and keen senses, he had overheard every word of Chu Dingjiang and An Jiu’s conversation. “I feel sad, but not that it is not worth it,” Wei Yuzhi replied. Mo Sigui raised an eyebrow, feeling his words were insincere, because Wei Yuzhi was not someone who selflessly loved. Wei Yuzhi saw through his thoughts but simply smiled without speaking. A drop of his heart’s blood had earned him two years of life from the Divine Physician. He had once again obtained Gu Jinghong’s heart’s blood, and the reward he received was substantial; it was not a waste. However, the sadness was genuine. He realized that An Jiu and he ultimately had no connection, except for that drop of blood that nourished her. He no longer even had an excuse to seek her out and retrieve the medicine. Wei Yuzhi was conflicted. Sometimes he wanted her to be well, and sometimes he was willing to hurt her just to have some connection with her, to leave a mark on her heart. … After a long sleep, An Jiu felt much better and had a good appetite. However, she could still only eat liquids recently. Chu Dingjiang promised to cook many delicious things for her in the future. “Ah Jiu, someone saved you. Go thank him.” Chu Dingjiang decided to tell An Jiu the truth. He did not think he would lose An Jiu because of this, and he did not want to hide it. An Jiu, touching her half-full stomach, paused upon hearing this. “Wei Yuzhi?” “You know?” Chu Dingjiang asked in surprise. “He’s in Mo Sigui’s room. I’ve always known.” For some reason, An Jiu had a special connection to Wei Yuzhi ever since she woke up. She did not need to consciously use her mental power to find him; she knew where he was. At the time, An Jiu did not think much of it, assuming Wei Yuzhi had come seeking medical help and that being able to sense him at such close range was normal. But now that Chu Dingjiang brought it up, she immediately guessed. An Jiu was silent for a moment, then stood up and said, “I will go see him.” “Alright.” Chu Dingjiang tied her cloak around her neck and watched her leave. The wind was strong outside, so An Jiu pulled her cloak tighter and quickened her pace. Before she reached the door, Mo Sigui’s door opened. An Jiu went straight in, and a warm, comforting scent mixed with the aroma of medicine wafted towards her. “Why are you running around in this cold weather?” Mo Sigui glared at her. An Jiu ignored him, untied her cloak, and looked towards the bed. Wei Yuzhi was indeed there, his hair as white as frost, his face almost translucent with paleness; even his lips were nearly the same color as his skin. He looked like a blank sheet of paper, almost transparent. Their eyes met, but neither spoke, as if they already knew what they wanted to ask and there was no need to say it aloud. The only sound in the room was the sound of Mo Sigui pounding medicine. After a while, Wei Yuzhi smiled and said, “Sit down.” An Jiu sat down not far from him. “Are you alright?” “I am fine.” Wei Yuzhi’s gaze fell on her face. Due to her long illness, her face was no longer the stunning beauty that had once made his heart flutter, but their eyes meeting again still stirred his heart. Wei Yuzhi frowned slightly, feeling a sharp pain in his wound. “Calm down,” Mo Sigui advised. Wei Yuzhi felt his secret exposed, and a few drops of color suddenly returned to his pale cheeks. “You saved me twice,” An Jiu said. “You mean at Baohua Gate?” Wei Yuzhi quickly calmed down. “Even if I had not intervened that time, you would have escaped unscathed.” An Jiu nodded, but even so, Wei Yuzhi had risked his own life to save her, and she would not be ungrateful for that favor.

chapters.title: Little Darling
chapters.content: “Great kindness needs no thanks,” An Jiu said. Wei Yuzhi said calmly, “I saved you this time with conditions; there’s no debt of gratitude to speak of.” Silence fell in the room again. Mo Sigui could not help but say, “Since you have nothing to say, go back and rest quickly.” An Jiu wanted to say that she would do her best to help him if he needed her in the future, but after a long pause, she ultimately did not make a promise. Wei Yuzhi watched her leave, seeing her slender figure disappear into the blinding snow light, before finally looking away. All communication between them became silent and slow, carrying an indescribable affection and a subtle, unspoken pain. Before the Baohua Gate incident, there was no doubt that Wei Yuzhi was An Jiu’s enemy; however, since then, An Jiu did not know how to face him. An Jiu saw Chu Dingjiang standing under the eaves and quickly walked over. “Chu Dingjiang…” Chu Dingjiang grasped her cold hand, a smile spreading across his face. “You cannot always call me by my full name like that; it sounds like you are swearing.” Whether in the Song Dynasty or even earlier, it was generally considered formal to address someone by their full name as a sign of respect. “Then what should I call you?” An Jiu thought for a moment. In her memory, husbands and wives always addressed each other by their first names, or “darling,” but she always felt that saying “darling” in Chinese felt a little awkward, and calling him “Dingjiang” felt even more awkward! “How did others address you before?” An Jiu wanted to learn from him. Chu Dingjiang leaned close to her ear and said, “Hua Rongjian, Gongsun29 Rongjian, Jizi.” An Jiu paused slightly, then remembered that he had been called Hua Rongjian in his previous life. “What does Jizi mean?” Chu Dingjiang coughed lightly. “It means ‘youngest son.'” An Jiu stared at his face, thinking carefully for a moment. “With your weathered face, I cannot bring myself to call you ‘little darling.'” Was that not exactly what the youngest son was? A little darling? “Never mind, there’s no rush. After we are married, you can call me ‘husband.'” Chu Dingjiang had intended to find a more private way to address her, but it seemed he’d only gotten himself into trouble. He should not have had any hope in that regard. “Married?” An Jiu’s voice rose slightly. Chu Dingjiang thought to himself, “Oh no.” This girl had quite a few quirks, especially regarding marriage. She was very averse to the idea. “You can call me that even if we are not married.” “Hmm.” An Jiu gave a vague reply. Actually, after everything they’d been through, she understood Chu Dingjiang quite well. She was not as resistant to the idea of ​​marriage as before. She knew Chu Dingjiang was not the same kind of person as her father; he was responsible and dependable, which made her feel at ease. Seeing her lack of reaction, Chu Dingjiang felt a little relieved. Heaven truly rewards those who persevere! An Jiu was lost in thought when she suddenly felt someone watching her from behind. She turned around to find the source of the gaze. There was only Mo Sigui’s room, with shadowy figures behind the latticed window. Inside, wisps of smoke drifted from the incense burner. A figure in blue robes with white hair stood by the window, his gaze seemingly peering through the paper window at the two conversing outside. Noticing An Jiu looking over, Wei Yuzhi lowered his eyes. Mo Sigui was still diligently grinding medicine, huffing and puffing. After a while, he looked up and said, “Everyone’s gone back inside! I do not understand you people who are always so lovey-dovey. An Jiu obviously has an eye on you, too. If you like her, just say so openly. Why bother spying?” “I proposed to her the moment I saw her.” Although Wei Yuzhi’s heart fluttered at first sight, it was not to the point of instant infatuation. Perhaps it was related to his usual way of doing things—he did not want to waste too much time and energy on such matters—or perhaps his strong willpower gave him keen intuition; he knew that even if he was not deeply in love yet, he would definitely grow to like her more and more in the future. “Oh, is that so!” Mo Sigui could not help but feel sorry for him. “She must have really made fun of you back then!” Mo Sigui thought to himself, An Jiu’s mouth was always so sharp; she must have been even more ruthless in this situation. Unexpectedly, Wei Yuzhi shook his head. “No, I’ve rarely had a verbal exchange with her since we met.” They were always on the brink of life and death; either she was on the run, or he was in trouble, either he captured her or she captured him—someone always had to suffer. Mo Sigui was a little surprised. Wei Yuzhi did not allow him to continue questioning, changing the subject to one he absolutely would not avoid: “The Divine Physician went through fire and water for Young Lady Lou; I admire that.” “What’s the use of going through fire and water? She’s just a stubborn mule; she will not stop until she knocks down the wall.” Mentioning this made Mo Sigui worried; he had no mood to gossip about others. Wei Yuzhi slowly walked back and lay down on the bed. “Extremes meet, and deep affection is short-lived. Perhaps this world cannot tolerate extremes, which is why there is such great suffering. Divine Physician, you must try to relax.” Deep affection was short-lived; whatever kind of affection it was—love or hate—falling too deeply would never last; otherwise, it would ultimately lead to destruction. Wei Yuzhi closed his eyes. He was not actually advising Mo Sigui, but rather himself. Mo Sigui seemed to understand his meaning. To alleviate his depression, he pulled out some medicinal smoke from the pile of medicine. “This is my latest formula, ‘Divine Bliss.’ Would you like to try it?”

chapters.title: Divine Bliss
chapters.content: Wei Yuzhi lay on the couch, looking at him. “Thank you for your kindness, Divine Physician, but I do not need it.” Mo Sigui lit a medicinal incense stick and lay among the pile of herbs, puffing out clouds of smoke. The smoke became transparent after it dissipated, but Wei Yuzhi still smelled a sweet aroma, feeling an indescribable relaxation. He could imagine how comfortable it would be to inhale this medicinal power. “Every medicine has its side effects. Divine Physician, you surely know this better than I do. Why…” In Wei Yuzhi’s eyes, he was humiliating himself. “Medication is not something you can stop whenever you want,” Mo Sigui said slowly, squinting. “I’ve had severe insomnia for several years now, and I’ve always relied on medicated cigarettes to fall asleep. I used to test the drugs on myself a lot, so I’ve developed a tolerance. If someone else uses 10% of the dosage, I need 50%. Over time, a lot of toxicity has accumulated in my body. This ‘Divine Bliss’ is not purely for comfort; it is an antidote.” He flicked the dregs from his pipe and chuckled, “Perhaps after using ‘Divine Bliss’ for a while, I will need another antidote. Eventually, my body will not be able to handle the potency, but it is not a big deal. That day is far off. While I cannot escape death, living to seventy or eighty should not be a problem.” Wei Yuzhi remained silent. For him, even living to forty was a luxury. “But what’s the point of living this long? Enough is enough,” Mo Sigui sighed, continuing, “There’s one thing I am destined to never have in this life.” From the day he began to suffer from insomnia, he had been sinking into an endless cycle of medication. For some, love was a driving force; for Mo Sigui, it was a tremendous obstacle. “You are born with a talent for medicine that surpasses others, and you have a long lifespan, which means you are destined to lose something else,” Wei Yuzhi said. Mo Sigui did not answer, and Wei Yuzhi did not say anything more. The two fell into a deep sleep amidst the fragrant aroma of the room. The next morning. Except for Mei Yanran, who got up early to cook, everyone else was still snuggled in their warm beds when Hua Rongjian arrived with a servant. When Chu Dingjiang and An Jiu got up, he had already been waiting in the hall for half an hour, having changed the tea several times. Hua Rongjian was leaning back in his round chair, skimming off tea leaves. He looked up and saw An Jiu enter and could not help but scoff. “I’ve been here for half an hour! Even if you got up from outside the city, you should have arrived long ago! If it were not for the fact that you are sick, I would have lost my temper.” “Who told you to come?” An Jiu, her face swollen, sat down opposite him. “I knew you could not expect anything nice from a dog’s mouth.” Hua Rongjian pointed to a pile of things on the table. “These are tonics for you. Have Aunt Mei make you more often.” An Jiu did not resist the food at all, accepting whatever was given. “What are all these?” “Ginseng, bird’s nest, and other common things,” Hua Rongjian said. “They do not taste good.” An Jiu did not like ginseng, especially since she had been kept alive by ginseng soup while unconscious for a while; she felt she smelled strongly of ginseng. Looking at her pale, lifeless face, Hua Rongjian suddenly said, “You should stay here. At least I can guarantee your safety, and you will not have to suffer like this again.” There were two people here whose mental power had reached a transcendent level. Everything in the courtyard was no secret to them. As soon as Hua Rongjian spoke, both of them listened intently. “If I do not court death, I will not die. If I choose to die, no one can protect me.” Similarly, An Jiu wanted a peaceful life, and she did not need anyone to provide it for her. Now she had a choice.

chapters.title: Mystery
chapters.content: Seeing the seriousness in her voice, Hua Rongjian stopped trying to persuade her. “You’ve changed,” An Jiu frowned. In just half a year, Hua Rongjian had matured rapidly, both in appearance and temperament. An Jiu disliked this change. The carefree young man who used to watch the stars hang low over the river, drink and chat with her, was gone. His depth was too similar to Chu Dingjiang, Mo Sigui, and Wei Yuzhi. An Jiu did not dislike this depth; she simply admired the warm-hearted young man even though he was considered quite absurd by others. “No one stays the same,” Hua Rongjian said, smiling at her. “You have not changed.” An Jiu was constantly searching for spiritual liberation, and her mindset was naturally changing, yet her purity had never disappeared. “Being able to protect one’s true self is a skill,” Hua Rongjian, dressed in a blue brocade robe with a black cloak over it, a black fox fur collar around his neck, highlighting his radiant face, spoke with a smile that tinged with melancholy. An Jiu suddenly stepped forward and took his hand. Hua Rongjian looked up, his face full of surprise. Feeling the warmth from her palm, An Jiu smiled slightly. “Some things about you have not changed.” Hua Rongjian slowly closed his fingers, returning her grip on her cold, slender hand. His eyes suddenly welled with tears. Just when even he himself was lost in thought, she said that some things about him had not changed. “Thank you.” After a moment, An Jiu withdrew her hand. Hua Rongjian felt an emptiness in his heart. He sighed, took a pendant from his waist, and handed it to her. “If you ever have trouble, take this to the Hua residence and find me. I will do everything in my power.” The pendant was different from ordinary accessories. It was a human face carved from black jade. Only the features were vaguely discernible; the exact features were indistinct. Upon closer inspection, the jade shimmered with tiny points of light, like the night sky. An Jiu did not stand on ceremony and took it, putting it in her sleeve pocket. Hua Rongjian smiled involuntarily at this. She had always been this kind of person. Only those who consider each other friends would give or receive without hesitation. “I am leaving.” Hua Rongjian looked at the motionless An Jiu, abandoning the idea of ​​waiting for her to get up and saw him off. “Take good care of yourself; there’s no need to see me off.” Seeing her about to explain, Hua Rongjian quickly interrupted, “I know you did not intend to see me off.” An Jiu nodded. Hua Rongjian was speechless. He walked to the door, then suddenly stopped and turned back. “If you change your mind, you can come back and marry me anytime. Although I married Mei Ruyan that year, she was not my legal wife until she was listed in the family register.” Perhaps afraid of hearing an answer he did not want to hear, he hurriedly left without waiting for An Jiu’s reply. Reality was so beautiful, yet so hurtful. An Jiu sat for a while, then got up and went out for breakfast. Chu Dingjiang was still standing under the eaves, waiting for her. The patients in the courtyard could now move freely, so Mei Yanran no longer brought meals to each person’s room; everyone had to go to the dining hall. When An Jiu and Chu Dingjiang arrived, Wei Yuzhi and Mo Sigui were almost finished eating. “Sigui said you can eat today, so I made some light snacks,” Mei Yanran said, placing a bowl of porridge in front of her. An Jiu’s attention was completely drawn to the various breakfast items on the table. She quickly thanked them and began to eat. Wei Yuzhi held half a steamed bun in his hand. Looking at the wolf-like figure, he was momentarily stunned. After eating her tenth bun, An Jiu grabbed an eleventh, but Chu Dingjiang stopped her, saying, “You cannot eat anymore.” An Jiu silently let go. She picked up her porridge and took a sip. Mo Sigui picked up the bun and sighed softly. “I am full, but Auntie’s cooking is just too good. I cannot resist having another one.” He took a big bite, making loud smacking noises. Wei Yuzhi glanced at An Jiu, noticing her thin and frail appearance. Holding a bowl of plain porridge, she instantly resembled a little girl being abused by her stepfather and stepsiblings. So, with a slight release of his mental energy, he pushed half a salted duck egg in front of her. Chu Dingjiang noticed but did not stop him. Instead, he proactively scooped half an egg into her dish. After the meal, Mei Yanran cleared the table, and the group sat down to talk. “Physician Mo, is Ah Jiu’s condition alright?” Chu Dingjiang asked. Mo Sigui replied, “She’s just a little weak. She will recover slowly. There’s nothing seriously wrong.” Chu Dingjiang smiled. Mo Sigui, seeing his forced smile, felt a chill run down her spine. “You…” Mo Sigui looked around, then grabbed Wei Yuzhi. “You are not the only one at the Transcendent Realm. You cannot act recklessly.” “How can it be reckless? Physician Mo has done his utmost for Ah Jiu’s condition. Today, I just want to settle accounts,” Chu Dingjiang squeezed out the last few words through gritted teeth, remembering how Mo Sigui always examined An Jiu naked during treatments, and he could not hold back his anger. “Divine physician.” Wei Yuzhi did not know what it was about, but it concerned An Jiu, and Chu Dingjiang’s anger meant it would not be good for An Jiu. So he silently withdrew his arm. “I am the patient.” “Aow!” Mo Sigui howled and leaped away. “Chu Dingjiang, if you dare touch me, do not even think about ever needing my help again!” Chu Dingjiang checked Mo Sigui’s pulse, making sure he would not abandon An Jiu! The sounds of fighting and Mo Sigui’s screams filled the air. An Jiu casually grabbed a steamed bun and stuffed it into her mouth, only to be glared at by Wei Yuzhi after he noticed. Wei Yuzhi smiled shyly and lowered his head. Mei Yanran quickly cleared everything away to prevent An Jiu from sneaking another bite. After breakfast, the two patients moved around in the courtyard. Both had just suffered serious injuries and were not suited for strenuous exercise. Wei Yuzhi, wrapped in a blanket, sat on the veranda basking in the sun, a weiqi board beside him, working on a game. The white plum blossoms beside him, covered in snow, shimmered in the sunlight, their fragrance subtle and delicate.
