Wei Yuzhi was not particularly handsome, certainly not as striking as Chu Dingjiang or Mo Sigui, but he possessed a unique charm when deep in thought, as if drawing people in. An Jiu stood in the courtyard watching him play weiqi, slightly drawn in, but mostly puzzled. He would place the pieces on the board and then pick them up again, seemingly finding nothing of interest, yet he appeared completely absorbed and enjoying it. The courtyard was small, and Wei Yuzhi had already noticed An Jiu, picking up a white piece, seemingly about to place it. He hesitated, as if pondering, before finally turning to her and asking, “Want to play?” An Jiu leaned closer to look at the board. “Is it interesting?” Wei Yuzhi smiled and nodded. Seeing An Jiu sit down opposite him, he reached out and gathered the entire astonishingly complex weiqi board. “Black or white?” An Jiu preferred light, so she chose white. “The board has nineteen lines horizontally and vertically, with three hundred and sixty-one intersections; these are points. The small dots on the board are called ‘star points’; there are nine in total, the central star point being the tengen…” Wei Yuzhi slowly explained the rules and methods of weiqi to her. An Jiu did not like long-winded explanations, but Wei Yuzhi’s words were concise and to the point, each sentence meaningful and intriguing, making her want to explore further. She unusually listened patiently. “When a piece is on the board, the empty points directly adjacent to it in a straight line are its ‘liberties.’ If there are pieces of the same color directly adjacent to a piece in a straight line, they are connected and form a unit. Their liberties should also be calculated. If there is a piece of a different color directly adjacent to a piece in a straight line, that liberty is lost…” An Jiu frowned. “It’s just a game; why make it so complicated?” Wei Yuzhi said. “Why are humans superior to wild beasts, able to hunt and kill them?” “Intelligence?” An Jiu asked. Wei Yuzhi nodded, pointing to the weiqi board. “So only humans could conceive this game, and only humans can play it.” “Alright, continue,” An Jiu said. Wei Yuzhi continued explaining. After explaining the basics, Wei Yuzhi led her to slowly set up the weiqi board, practicing each basic form several times before starting a game. In the first round, Wei Yuzhi gave her an eighteen-piece handicap, occasionally pointing out her mistakes, but An Jiu was still completely crushed. The second round, again with an eighteen-piece handicap, and she was still completely crushed. The third, fourth, fifth rounds…although she was utterly defeated each time, An Jiu’s basic mistakes decreased. Chu Dingjiang, after beating Mo Sigui, watched several rounds, and seeing An Jiu’s increasing confidence despite setbacks, he remained an observer. After seven rounds, An Jiu finally could not resist and grabbed a volunteer. “You play against him!” It was not because she was anxious about losing, but because she realized this game truly required wisdom and skill; brute force would never beat Wei Yuzhi. She thought Chu Dingjiang was quite clever, so she brought him over to play against him, learning from observing the game. The two sat cross-legged facing each other. Wei Yuzhi shifted slightly, his posture no longer as casual as before. The atmosphere shifted abruptly, as if swords could be drawn at any moment. The blanket slipped from Wei Yuzhi’s shoulders, and he gathered his wide sleeves. “Please.” Chu Dingjiang reached out and took the bowl of white weiqi pieces. Black moved first. Wei Yuzhi took the bowl of black pieces and seemingly casually placed one on the board. The two exchanged moves, initially placing pieces rapidly. However, as more pieces accumulated on the board, the saying “one wrong move and the whole game is lost” became true, and both took more time to think before placing their pieces. An Jiu squatted to the side, watching with great interest. She would ask questions when she did not understand, but the answers were always vague and incomprehensible to her. After watching for half an hour, An Jiu realized she did not understand what they were doing at all. She yawned and went to play with Mo Sigui. The room was still piled with medicine, looking exactly the same as before. An Jiu did not see anyone and followed the sound of the medicine being pounded. Mo Sigui, crouching amidst a pile of medicinal herbs, suddenly looked up and glared fiercely at her, but it lacked the menacing aura he had imagined. “Ha!” An Jiu laughed unkindly, noticing his purplish-black eyes. “Chu Dingjiang seems to be quite considerate of your eyes.” Mo Sigui did not actually have many injuries; his panda eyes were the most striking. His once bright and beautiful eyes were swollen, like slits in the middle of walnuts, and it was unclear whether he could even see clearly. Mo Sigui pouted. He knew perfectly well that Chu Dingjiang’s actions were not because of the steamed bun from that morning but because he had seen An Jiu’s body during the treatment. “Luckily, I was smart enough not to say I touched you; otherwise, both of my arms would be ruined!” Mo Sigui said resentfully. An Jiu squatted down, resting her chin on her hand, and said, “He probably knows by now.” “I…” Mo Sigui wanted to explode, but his eyes stung like needles, so he covered them. “Ouch! What happened? I have amnesia!” An Jiu patted his shoulder. “It was not anything serious. He hit you over this? I will get revenge for you later.” Mo Sigui paused. “Are you serious?” “Have I ever favored you?” An Jiu asked. “He has to be beaten like this!” Mo Sigui pointed to his face. “I told you I still need my looks to make a living! My Mingyue does not even care about me. If my face is ruined, I will have no hope left.” “Lou Mingyue is not the kind of person who cares about looks,” An Jiu comforted him. “No matter how good-looking you are, she will not give you a second glance.” Mo Sigui roared, “Go away! Go away! Do not let me see you again! Take that heartless Chu Dingjiang and go as far away as you can!” “I am not feeling well right now; I cannot go very far,” An Jiu said seriously. Mo Sigui lay down on the pile of medicine, looking utterly resigned, and asked irritably while applying medicine to his eyes, “Have you seen Wei Yuzhi?” “He’s playing weiqi outside with Chu Dingjiang,” An Jiu replied. Mo Sigui threw the cotton ball into the medicine jar and, as if finding an outlet for his anger, rushed out. He saw the two still playing weiqi and roared, “Are you tired of living?! You just got stabbed, and instead of lying in bed, you are playing weiqi here! That Chu guy, you are despicable! This is not how you kill your rival! Let me tell you, a person will not die in my hands. Forget about it!” His words were noble and righteous. The two were locked in a fierce battle on the weiqi board, feeling they had met their match, oblivious to everything else. Mo Sigui was quite pleased with himself after his outburst. But after waiting for a while and seeing no one paying him any attention and seeing Wei Yuzhi’s pale face with a bluish tinge, he was truly enraged and strode forward. He slammed his palm on the weiqi board, shattering it into dust that was scattered by the wind onto the snow, leaving a messy stain. Only then did the two come to their senses. Mo Sigui grasped Wei Yuzhi’s pulse, channeling his inner energy into his body to examine him thoroughly. His face turned ashen. “Come back with me!” Wei Yuzhi felt a dull ache in his chest, nodded to Chu Dingjiang, and got up to follow Mo Sigui back to the house. “You do not even cherish your own life. Even if I were a god, granting you fifty years would not be enough!” Mo Sigui took out silver needles, made Wei Yuzhi lie down, stripped him of his clothes, and swiftly inserted the needles. After finishing in one go, he poured out a pill and stuffed it into Wei Yuzhi’s mouth. “Is he alright?” An Jiu asked. “You should go back and rest, too!” Mo Sigui said unhappily. “Do you think you are a perfectly healthy person? You still have the nerve to worry about others?” Seeing Wei Yuzhi fall asleep after taking the medicine, An Jiu said nothing more, her gaze sweeping over his wounded body before turning and leaving. Chu Dingjiang went back to the house with her. “You’ve been playing all day. Rest for a while before having lunch,” Chu Dingjiang said. An Jiu said, “I do not feel tired.” “Following the physician’s orders is correct.” Chu Dingjiang could naturally see that An Jiu did not look tired; otherwise, he would not have allowed her to play for so long. But Mo Sigui was right; after all, An Jiu had only been awake for a few days. An Jiu took off her cloak and went to lie down on the bed fully clothed. “I will go help Aunt Mei; you get some sleep,” Chu Dingjiang said. An Jiu quickly said, “Do not beat Mo Sigui anymore! I promised to avenge him!” Chu Dingjiang raised an eyebrow. “I will let you avenge him when I get back, but you are a patient now, you do not have much strength, and you cannot do strenuous activity. Mo Sigui knows that.” An Jiu nodded in agreement. Chu Dingjiang left, leaving An Jiu alone in the room. Braziers were burning in the corners, but she still felt cold. Her chest felt like it was being squeezed, a dull ache, and she could not breathe. This feeling grew stronger and stronger until she finally fell into a deep, exhausted sleep. Mo Sigui, carrying his medicine box, sat on the edge of the bed and took An Jiu’s pulse. After a long while, he sighed softly, “Heart’s blood is truly wondrous.” Mo Sigui had pondered for a long time, roughly grasping the wonders of heart’s blood. It nourished one person with their mental power and life force; naturally, the fresher the blood, the better. If he had given An Jiu all the blood he had taken from Gu Jinghong immediately, she would have undoubtedly benefited greatly, perhaps even inheriting Gu Jinghong’s ability to perceive the seven orifices. Unfortunately, he did not understand then, missing the optimal opportunity. However, this was for the best. Gu Jinghong had been dead for several years, and the blood had been re-refined with medicine, so its remaining efficacy was no longer what it once was. Therefore, even if the Liao Emperor’s condition was alleviated after receiving it, he probably would not be cured. This was for the best. Wei Yuzhi differed from Gu Jinghong in that he excelled in powerful mental energy. This powerful mental energy nourished An Jiu’s injuries, but it also merged into her body. If An Jiu had not fully assimilated it by the time Wei Yuzhi died, she was highly likely to suffer another severe injury. Such strong and solid mental energy could not be subdued in a short time. Without Wei Yuzhi, mental energy was a powerless and unconscious force; whether it yielded to An Jiu’s mental energy was no longer related to Wei Yuzhi’s will. Fortunately, Wei Yuzhi had willingly given his blood, so this power currently seemed quite gentle, and there was no need to worry too much. What worried Mo Sigui more was that An Jiu now had some kind of connection with Wei Yuzhi; it seemed that An Jiu also had to bear some of Wei Yuzhi’s pain. Would death spread to An Jiu because of this connection? Mo Sigui did not know; this was beyond his understanding of the medical arts. As his thoughts gradually cleared, Mo Sigui became excited. This discovery undoubtedly opened a new door for him. He had a premonition that if he could figure out the relationship between them, his medical skills would rise to another level! He had to carefully observe these two people! Mo Sigui shouldered his medicine box and happily went back. At lunchtime, two people were missing. The two patients who had been lively in the morning were now back in bed, recuperating. Chu Dingjiang asked Mo Sigui, “Ah Jiu seemed fine before; why did she suddenly fall ill? Is it related to Wei Yuzhi’s illness?” Mo Sigui had not intended to speak to him, but hearing Chu Dingjiang’s insightful question, his hostility towards him immediately lessened. His emotions were so strange and unpredictable. “Yes, this matter is very mysterious.”

chapters.title: National Hatred and Family Feud
chapters.content: Having more people involved in the discussion would provide a more comprehensive picture, so Mo Sigui shared everything he had thought of that day with Chu Dingjiang. If he could gain some insight from him, Mo Sigui might consider letting go of his grudge. After listening, Chu Dingjiang picked out a question: “Since you believe the mental power carried in that blood is no longer under Wei Yuzhi’s control, why is there a connection between them?” “This…” Mo Sigui fell into thought and, after a moment, replied, “My conclusion was indeed a bit hasty, but I cannot rule out other possibilities. I believe that people do not just have memories in their brains; various parts of the body should also have memories, and the blood in one’s heart should also have them.” These things sounded very mystical, and Mo Sigui thought they would not be accepted by most people, but to his surprise, Chu Dingjiang said, “Perhaps.” Having had his own experience, he was even more convinced of these things than Mo Sigui. “Ah Jiu has gotten involved with someone else, and you are upset about it?” Mo Sigui intended to gloat, but the words inevitably carried a sense of shared misery. Chu Dingjiang, hands clasped, gazed at the birds in the snow outside. After a long pause, he replied, “Human hearts are the most unpredictable.” Mo Sigui clicked his tongue. “You do not trust Ah Jiu’s character?” “I trust her,” Chu Dingjiang said. He believed in An Jiu’s character, but human hearts were fickle, and who one liked or disliked was not something one could control. He had come to terms with it. He could not let a minor setback ruin everything. If he wanted to spend his life with someone, he had to give it his all; there were no shortcuts. “Sorrowful,” Mo Sigui said. If he set aside his feelings, he felt life was full of hope, but every time he thought about this matter, he felt like he was falling into an abyss. He could not let go, yet he could not hold on. It was truly agonizing! Mo Sigui took out some medicinal tobacco from the pouch at his waist and stuffed it into his pipe. A moment later, the room was filled with smoke again. After finishing the tobacco, Mo Sigui felt a little more relaxed and went back inside to sleep. After waking up, he devoted himself to studying the medicinal formula. Living in the Hua family mansion had one advantage: Hua Rongtian could usually find whatever he wanted. Mo Sigui was very satisfied with Hua Rongtian’s efficiency, so when Chu Dingjiang suggested leaving, he was the first to object. An Jiu spent her days eating and sleeping, and within a little over a month, she had recovered to her former self, though her mental strength still needed time to recover. An Jiu’s originally planned body reconstruction would be postponed for the next six months due to her coma, so Mo Sigui focused all his attention on researching the connection between her and Wei Yuzhi. “What did you feel when Little Wei was unconscious last time?” An Jiu frowned. Mo Sigui had been asking the same question for over a month, and his address for Wei Yuzhi had changed from “Master Wei” to “Wei Yuzhi,” then to “Little Wei,” and now, just a few days later, to “Little Wei Wei.” This indicated that Mo Sigui considered Wei Yuzhi very important. Aside from Lou Mingyue, this was the first time An Jiu had heard him address someone else like that. “Does your chest hurt?” Mo Sigui reached out to point to the location, but he sensed a sinister glint in Chu Dingjiang’s eyes. He had no choice but to hold back and continue, “Where does it hurt? How does it hurt?” “You’ve asked at least forty times. I refuse to answer,” An Jiu said. Mo Sigui held the parchment scroll he used for notes, his thoughts drifting elsewhere. These past few days, he had searched for many Taoist books, hoping they might be helpful. Fortunately, Chu Dingjiang was extremely knowledgeable about Taoism, knowing everything about its origins, doctrines, and scriptures. It was as if he had witnessed the rise and fall of Taoism firsthand; every conversation Mo Sigui had with him gave new insights. Even before the bruises around his eyes had faded, he had already forgotten his grudge. Mo Sigui snapped back to reality and turned to ask Wei Yuzhi. Wei Yuzhi’s patience was unparalleled; despite his short life, he was willing to waste time answering such trivial questions. Today, he answered patiently as usual, but seemed somewhat distracted. “What’s wrong?” An Jiu seemed to see through the heavy mood beneath his calm expression. Wei Yuzhi smiled slightly. “Nothing.” He was never one to confide in others. Wei Yuzhi was walking a rugged and treacherous path. One wrong step and neither the Song nor the Liao would tolerate him. No one could tell him how to walk this path, and no one could understand the feelings of standing on this perilous road. Twenty days ago, after receiving the medicine, he contacted his subordinates and learned that Yelu Quancang had handed over Piaomiao Mountain Mansion to Mei Ruyan. Even Yelu Quancang did not know that Wei Yuzhi held many other private forces besides Piaomiao Mountain Mansion. From the beginning, he knew that Piaomiao Mountain Mansion would ultimately be a discarded pawn, and he might be abandoned along with it. The Liao people were not lacking in talent; how could they tolerate a Song person occupying a high position? Yelu Quancang, as a ruler, made a correct decision, but he was not ruthless enough. He was not a heartless scoundrel, but he still could not bring himself to kill Wei Yuzhi after he had served his purpose. When Yelu Quancang was afflicted with a serious illness and was almost unable to manage affairs, Wei Yuzhi single-handedly supported him, even trying to prolong his life. That year, when Yelu Quancang was on the verge of death, and it seemed he would not live to see the medicine made from the heart’s blood, it was Wei Yuzhi who imprisoned Wei Yunshan and used Wei Yunshan’s profound inner strength and his own mental power to revive Yelu Quancang. It could be said that without Wei Yuzhi, there would be no Yelu Quancang. Besides, in their early years, before they knew each other’s identities, they had shared a period of brotherhood. Although Yelu Quancang was older than Wei Yuzhi, due to his poor health, Wei Yuzhi usually took care of him. The reason Yelu Quancang did not kill Wei Yuzhi to silence him was more because he remembered that pure brotherly affection they had once shared, rather than the later mutual exploitation. “Since Yelu Quancang has treated you this way, why cling to the Liao Kingdom?” A deep voice interrupted his thoughts. Wei Yuzhi snapped out of his reverie, only to realize that Mo Sigui and An Jiu were nowhere to be found. “You know?” Wei Yuzhi was somewhat surprised; after all, this matter was highly confidential, but he quickly understood. Chu Dingjiang could guess what he was thinking, but he could not guess what had happened. Chu Dingjiang shook his head. “I no longer pay attention to these matters. I just want to say one thing.” “Please enlighten me,” Wei Yuzhi said. “Do you not feel you’ve wasted your talent?” Chu Dingjiang returned the question Wei Yuzhi had asked that day, verbatim. “What do you mean?” Wei Yuzhi asked. “If it were not for certain concerns, your talent would not have led you to this state. There’s more to this world than just Liao. With the new Emperor of the Song Dynasty on the throne, there’s so much to be done. You must know that.” Chu Dingjiang put down the book in his hand and looked at him. “But you’d rather fawn over someone cold to you than pledge allegiance to the Song Dynasty. Can I interpret that as hatred?”

chapters.title: New Year
chapters.content: Having his deepest secret guessed, Wei Yuzhi showed no surprise, only a calm smile. “Yes.” He understood the meaning of Chu Dingjiang’s words: family or country, which was more important? Anyone with a modicum of insight knew that “without the skin, where will the hair attach?” Only with a country could there be a family. But Wei Yuzhi had long since lost his family, and his closest relatives were unjustly imprisoned because of this corrupt court. He possessed immense talent, yet he could not use it for the sake of the nation. Chu Dingjiang gazed at Wei Yuzhi’s full head of silver hair. “What you ultimately want is nothing more than revenge. It has nothing to do with the country or the people. And your enemy, is it the Emperor of the Song Dynasty, or the entire Song Dynasty? Or is it merely the corruption of the Song Dynasty?” Chu Dingjiang’s words were like a thunderbolt. Wei Yuzhi was blinded by hatred, but deep down, he had always known the truth. Now that the truth had been so blatantly revealed, he could no longer pretend not to understand. However, despite understanding, he smiled bitterly. “I am the descendant of a disgraced official here. Even if I could conceal my identity and enter the court, the truth will eventually come out.” There were too many reasons not to choose this path. What he said was only a tiny fraction. Even if he could hide his identity for his entire life, rising to a position of immense power in the officialdom would require not only enormous effort but also a very long time. Wei Yuzhi had no good starting point, no connections, and no assistance. To reach the pinnacle of power, even with everything going smoothly, would take at least ten or twenty years. Unfortunately, he did not have that long of a life. Wei Yuzhi said, “How many more years do I have left? When I can gamble, I have no choice but to go all in.” Chu Dingjiang was also thoroughly fed up with the Song Dynasty. He had never seen such a weak court. Outwardly prosperous, it was actually crumbling. What was even more infuriating was that those living inside, instead of reinforcing it, continued to decorate it. Although it looked more prosperous, the heavy burden only accelerated its collapse. “I no longer concern myself with court affairs, but if I see hope and have the ability to lend a hand, I am still willing to lend a hand.” Every citizen had a responsibility to the nation. Chu Dingjiang had seen himself clearly; he would no longer strive for fame, fortune, or ambition, but he would not become an idle man. “There are thousands like me in the Song Dynasty. The Liao Kingdom will not succeed with or without you.” The Song court was corrupt. Many truly talented people would rather remain inactive than serve. And when the dynasty was in danger of collapse, who could stand by and watch the country perish? “If I were you, I would rather pursue a career in government. Perhaps I will not live to see the world at peace, but at least I will have done something.” Chu Dingjiang’s tone was calm, but his words were like sharp knives, each word piercing Wei Yuzhi’s heart. Wei Yuzhi felt his healed wounds begin to ache again. A sweet taste rose in his throat, and a surge of heat threatened to burst forth. But he swallowed it back. Seeing Wei Yuzhi’s expression instantly crumble, Chu Dingjiang did not continue. Wei Yuzhi’s powerful and solid mental strength indicated that he was undoubtedly a person of extremely strong will, not easily defeated. It was just that this matter was too important, and he was momentarily unable to calm his emotions. Bang! Mo Sigui rushed in like a gust of wind, carrying An Jiu on his back. “Little Wei, what’s wrong?” Just now, he and An Jiu had smelled the aroma wafting from the Hua family’s kitchen and were both restless. So they decided to go and borrow some, but An Jiu had just reached the outside of the kitchen when she suffered a sudden sharp pain in her heart and almost fainted. Mo Sigui knew that something must have happened to Wei Yuzhi. He quickly carried An Jiu back. “It’s nothing.” Wei Yuzhi’s face was pale, but his expression was extremely calm. He looked at Chu Dingjiang. “Thank you for your guidance, Master Chu.” Mo Sigui put An Jiu down and took the pulses of both of them simultaneously. Feeling the pulse of both in his fingertips, it was as if he were taking the pulse of a single person! Mo Sigui was surprised. He first released Wei Yuzhi’s hand, carefully checked An Jiu’s pulse, and then focused on taking Wei Yuzhi’s pulse. The result was the same. “I knew…something felt off these past few days,” Mo Sigui muttered to himself, pressing several acupoints on Wei Yuzhi. After a conversation, Wei Yuzhi’s condition worsened, and he subsequently fell into a coma. Mo Sigui was initially worried he would not make it, but seeing An Jiu return to her energetic self after a day’s rest, and his pulse gradually stabilizing, he gradually felt relieved. Because of boredom, this winter seemed exceptionally long. Suddenly, the Hua mansion became bustling, and everyone was hurrying along with cheerful expressions. An Jiu, who had been watching from the wall for several days, could not help but ask Chu Dingjiang, “What are they busy with?” The well-informed Chu Dingjiang said he did not know. After observing for another half month, Chu Dingjiang finally remembered, “They are preparing for the New Year!” “The New Year?” An Jiu frowned. The Mei family did not value festivals as much as the Hua family. When An Jiu lived in Mei Mansion, she focused most of her energy on the clan school and archery, so naturally, she did not pay much attention to these things. Her impression of the New Year was that the entire Mei Mansion would gather for a meal, a meal that resulted in rivers of blood and mountains of corpses. Chu Dingjiang was even less concerned about such things. A few days later, Mei Jiu arrived with a large group of maids and servants, personally overseeing the New Year preparations in the courtyard. Except for Mei Yanran, everyone in the courtyard was unaware of the large-scale preparations and remained awkwardly squatting in Mo Sigui’s room. Mei Jiu took a sip of tea and said with a smile, “The New Year is almost here, so I brought people over to clean up and also to offer everyone some things.” The four people and the two tigers remained silent. Mei Jiu, slightly embarrassed, put down her teacup and took An Jiu’s hand, saying, “I’ve had many clothes and jewelry prepared for you. A woman should dress up nicely. Come with me.” An Jiu, her face expressionless, was pulled into the newly prepared bedroom. Upon entering, An Jiu froze, feeling as if she had entered the wrong room. Everything before her was indescribably luxurious; everything had been replaced, from the large tables and chairs to the smallest teacup. “You did not come here to steal anything, did you?” An Jiu asked. Mei Jiu was enthusiastically taking newly made women’s dresses out of the trunk when she heard this. “What do you mean?” she asked, puzzled. An Jiu plopped down on the newly replaced chair, which had a soft, plush cushion underneath. “You seem to want to tear the whole house down and rebuild it from scratch,” she said. Mei Jiu laughed, “I’ve been wanting to tidy it up for a while now. No one lives here, and the things inside are all old and worn. It is just a makeshift place with some everyday items—it’s too shabby. But since you are still sick, I did not want to bother you. Now, with the New Year approaching, I can finally get some new clothes. Come and see, which one do you like?” Mei Jiu laid out the items one by one on the bed and table, but the trunk still seemed to be full.

chapters.title: Dirty
chapters.content: An Jiu, who mostly wore dark-colored close-fitting clothes, was also curious about these garments. She casually pointed to a dark blue dress with silver trim and an embroidered magnolia bud at the hem. “This one’s a bit old-fashioned,” Mei Jiu said, knowing An Jiu would not change her mind, before handing her the dress. An Jiu took the dress behind the screen and struggled for a long time, sweating profusely, before finally managing to put it on. After coming out, Mei Jiu’s eyes lit up. She came over and, while straightening An Jiu’s clothes, praised her, “You look good in anything.” An Jiu glanced down at her. Mei Jiu had recovered very well after giving birth, much fuller than before, her skin flawless. “So all your weight gain was in your face.” Mei Jiu remembered that this was her own body; praising her was tantamount to praising herself. She blushed. “I really cannot get along with you. Have you ever said a single nice word in your life?” “I am just telling the truth. If you do not want to accept the facts, do not blame me,” An Jiu said sharply. “…” Mei Jiu did not reply. After straightening her clothes, she stepped back a few paces to examine her carefully, then nodded. “Very good, you just need to comb your hair. Come sit over there.” Mei Jiu had seen a lot in life, and with years of pampered living, she was no longer the timid person she once was. Even facing An Jiu, she was not as fearful as before. An Jiu sat down at the dressing table as instructed, watching in the mirror as the elegantly dressed Mei Jiu personally combed her hair. Outside the window, the plum blossoms were vibrant, evoking memories of those days spent amidst them, when the two were one, so intimate yet so distant, a feeling that remained unchanged. Mei Jiu had returned to a normal life, while An Jiu was still struggling in the swamp. Actually, it was not about her circumstances. Mei Jiu, as a spy for the Konghe Army, married into the Hua family—a near-death experience. Yet, she survived under such circumstances and became a true Madam Hua. While luck certainly played a part, Mei Jiu’s wisdom and hard work were indispensable. In contrast, An Jiu’s situation was one of flexibility, but what was tightly bound was her heart. A person who understands what they want and strives for it would not have a bad life. But if one were lost and directionless, one could only pray for divine favor. It was a matter of character and luck! “You are stronger than me,” An Jiu suddenly said. Mei Jiu paused slightly, then continued combing her hair, her face still bearing a serene smile. “It’s rare to hear you praise me in my lifetime.” “Sigh!” An Jiu tapped her fingers on the dressing table, a hint of melancholy in her voice. “Even someone like you can do it. I need to work harder.” “What kind of talk is that? What do you mean, ‘even someone like me can do it’?” Mei Jiu feigned annoyance. “Was I inappropriate?” An Jiu thought for a moment. She raised an eyebrow, looking at her in the mirror. “The early bird catches the worm?” “I really cannot argue with you!” Mei Jiu carefully braided her hair. “You are such a strange person—arrogant, sharp-tongued, and ruthless. Yet you always seem like a decent person.” An Jiu raised an eyebrow, tapping a hairpin against her jewelry box. “Who has ever seemed bad to an innocent rabbit like you?” “An Jiu, I’ve changed.” Mei Jiu took a comb, dipped it in osmanthus oil, and gently smoothed her hair. Leaning over to check her hair in the mirror, Mei Jiu said, “I am no longer that fool who thought everyone in the world was good. I…I can kill now.” “Oh,” An Jiu replied expressionlessly. “Tell me about it, let me see how a rabbit bites.” “Although I have not killed anyone with my own hands, I’ve taken more than one or two lives. In the dead of night, I always feel my hands are incredibly dirty.” Mei Jiu’s hands, gripping the comb, trembled slightly. “They wanted to harm me; it was either you or me. I did not want to die, so I had to kill them, but I still feel my hands are dirty.” Whenever she felt this way, Mei Jiu would imagine she was still living in the same body as An Jiu, as if that would bring her some peace of mind. An Jiu suddenly grabbed her trembling hand. “Killing will never stop in this world; it is a natural thing. People kill animals to eat meat because they need to survive. If you will die if you do not eliminate your enemies, why feel guilty?” In the mirror, An Jiu’s dark eyes were cold and composed. “You do not need to kill anymore. Forget about it. Just pretend I killed those people.” Mei Jiu smiled, her eyes glistening with tears. “Actually, you really are a good person.” It was just that An Jiu’s goodness was reserved for a very small number of people. Mei Jiu quickly composed herself and advised, “An Jiu, do not do those things anymore. Live a good life. You said you wanted to herd sheep, did you not?” An Jiu lowered her head and remained silent for a moment. When she looked up again, her eyes were resolute. “I can realize my dream now, but I cannot live like this right now. If I cannot find liberation one day, even herding all the sheep in the world will not bring me joy.” She held out her fair hands to her eyes. “I feel dirty too. Whenever the uncontrollable urge to kill surges in my blood, I feel even dirtier.” An Jiu also understood why she used to dislike Mei Jiu so much. Besides being disgusted by her cowardice, she also resented her purity. An Jiu was not someone who wanted the whole world to fall into depravity just because she herself had fallen. Now that Mei Jiu said she had killed someone, she felt no joy, but rather an indescribable heartache. “Alright, let’s not talk about these upsetting things. Now that you are awake and I’ve given birth to your godson, there’s still a long life ahead of us,” Mei Jiu said, quickly tying her hair up and then starting to choose suitable jewelry. Mei Jiu liked the hanging style very much. She thought that with such accessories on her head, she would look charming when walking. But it was obvious that she had miscalculated. An Jiu only took a few steps before he became annoyed and reached out to pull out the hairpins all over his head. “Wearing a skirt is already very inconvenient, and you are doing these things just to make trouble for yourself!” “What does it matter for a woman to be patient for the sake of her beauty?” Mei Jiu wanted to fuck her. “I could not do anything to you before.” An Jiu turned to stare at her. “Now I can beat you.” Mei Jiu’s hand shook, and she quickly put away her walking stick. Based on her understanding of An Jiu, she would not think it was a joke. An Jiu had always said that she would definitely be beaten, no matter if she were the Empress Dowager or the Emperor! “That is all; if you do not want to wear it, do not wear it.” Mei Jiu was discouraged. But thinking of Chu Dingjiang’s expression when he saw An Jiu, Mei Jiu immediately became excited again. He put a fox fur on her and said, “Let’s go to my cousin.” An Jiu did not object and followed her to the house. Inside, the herbs were piled up in a mess, resembling a haystack. In the hazy smoke, three men lay sprawled out. An Jiu pushed open the door and entered. Chu Dingjiang was the first to see them and was momentarily stunned.

chapters.title: The Fallen Face
chapters.content: Amidst the swirling smoke, An Jiu’s slender figure was illuminated by the dazzling snowlight behind her, creating a dreamlike effect. Her flowing sleeves resembled a resting butterfly or a folded eagle, an appearance that was difficult to define as either delicate or strong. Chu Dingjiang’s gaze fixed on her face. A dark blue dress accentuated her fair, jade-like complexion. Her black hair was styled in a simple updo, devoid of any unnecessary jewelry, giving her an exceptionally serene appearance. For some reason, Chu Dingjiang suddenly recalled the night he first saw her body. His face flushed, and the book in his hand fell with a thud into the pile of herbs. The sudden sound startled Wei Yuzhi, who was also stunned. An Jiu now appeared somewhat different from the one who had captivated him at first sight. It was not just her appearance; even her demeanor possessed a gentler, calmer quality. Before, when An Jiu was not killing, she seemed quite quiet, but that quiet was like the calm before a storm, as if it could erupt at any moment. “You look quite like a woman dressed like this!” Mo Sigui clicked his tongue. An Jiu sat down next to Chu Dingjiang, followed by Mei Jiu, who nodded slightly to the three of them as a greeting. “Beautiful,” Chu Dingjiang praised softly. An Jiu nodded. “I know.” “Can you not be a little more modest?” Mo Sigui said disdainfully. An Jiu turned to look at him. “You have a problem with that?” “I do have a problem!” Mo Sigui blurted out, immediately sensing the awkward atmosphere. He suddenly remembered that the other two men in the room were interested in her, but words spoken were like water spilled—it was too late to take them back. The atmosphere was tense. Everyone thought An Jiu was about to impulsively punch someone, but she calmly glanced away. “I am wearing this for Chu Dingjiang. I do not care about your opinion. You probably will not have a chance to complain later anyway. Lou Mingyue will not wear it for you.” Mo Sigui instantly felt a pang of sadness, turning his face away with an “I will never speak to this woman again” expression. Wei Yuzhi lowered his eyes, concealing the sadness within. The entire room was divided by Mei Jiu. One side was bathed in bright sunshine, while the other was shrouded in gloom. “Cousin, shall I have someone tidy up this room as well?” Mei Jiu said. “No!” Mo Sigui quickly replied. “My room is perfectly tidy; it does not need tidying.” There was not even room to step inside; calling it tidy would be an understatement. But Mei Jiu understood Mo Sigui to some extent; she was just trying to ease the tension, not genuinely wanting to tidy the room. “Then forget it.” She then looked at Wei Yuzhi. “Would you like a room prepared for this gentleman?” “No need,” Mo Sigui refused again. “You should go and hold your son; do not come here and cause trouble.” Mei Jiu was not angry. With a forgiving smile, she said, “I know you are heartbroken and in a bad mood; I do not blame you. It’s almost the New Year; I want everyone to have a better time.” Mo Sigui felt even more heartbroken. If it were not for Chu Dingjiang, that living devil, he would have thrown these two out immediately! The group sat awkwardly for a while, then Mei Jiu asked Mo Sigui to check her son’s pulse. Chu Dingjiang and An Jiu then returned to their room. Only after An Jiu’s figure disappeared from view did Wei Yuzhi turn away. An Jiu stood in the corridor. She glanced back, her mood inexplicably low. She could feel Wei Yuzhi’s gaze, and she could sense his inner emotions. If there were someone in this world with whom you could clearly see and constantly feel their sincerity, could you still remain a stranger? An Jiu could not. Having witnessed her father’s cruelty, she knew how rare true feelings were. How could she remain unmoved by genuine affection? Her mother’s loyalty had a profound influence on An Jiu. Back then, she despised such foolish behavior, but when it happened to her, she was surprised that she was willing to dedicate her entire life to one person. “It’s you.” An Jiu grasped Chu Dingjiang’s hand. “Hmm?” Chu Dingjiang looked at her in confusion. An Jiu stamped her foot. “I’ve started to care about other men, but I still believe you are the one who will never change my heart.” Chu Dingjiang was silent for a moment, then smiled slightly and patted her head. “Good girl,” Chu Dingjiang was a very perceptive person; nothing escaped his notice. However, it was different for him to see it himself and for An Jiu to admit it herself. He was glad An Jiu was so honest. “It’s alright to daydream sometimes. I believe you,” Chu Dingjiang said in a deep voice, pulling her into his arms. Inside the room, Wei Yuzhi lay on the bed, staring at the ceiling beams. His white hair fell from the bedside to the floor, like snow and frost. He rarely had moments like this, letting himself think of nothing, his mind a complete blank. … Bianjing had been sunny for many days. Because the snow had been melting, it was even colder than when it snowed. Most people chose to stay indoors. Two days before the New Year, it suddenly started snowing again, like goose feathers, with the force of burying the city and its tall buildings, falling thickly and densely. An Jiu loved sitting by the fire pit in this kind of weather, wrapped in a blanket and wearing only a comfortable shirt, nestled beside Chu Dingjiang. “Let’s go after the New Year,” An Jiu said, frowning, her eyes reflecting the firelight. “I just remembered I accepted a bounty and have not completed it yet! What about that post?” Chu Dingjiang poked the embers with a fire poker. “Too late. You probably already accepted the bounty.” He noticed An Jiu’s puzzled expression. “Those who accept a post but do not carry it out will be hunted down by the bounty board.” Being hunted by the bounty board was equivalent to being hunted by assassins from all over the world—no good news. “Ugh.” An Jiu was unhappy. She’d come to this again! In her past life, she was also wanted by the entire world… Chu Dingjiang did not take it to heart. “It’s nothing serious. If there’s no better way, just kill the bounty board manager, and all posts will be replaced.” That was the rule of the bounty board: one manager, one post; no post would be delayed until the next manager. “Who’s behind the Bounty List?” An Jiu asked. Chu Dingjiang’s gaze fell on the pendant at her waist. It was a black jade human face pendant, which had only arrived in her possession a few days ago. “Hua Rongjian!” An Jiu sat up straight. Chu Dingjiang hummed in agreement. “Are you sure?” An Jiu was a little skeptical. Hua Rongjian used to be quite notorious, practically living under the public eye in Bianjing every day. If he could still secretly manage the Bounty List under such circumstances, how deep must his cunning be! “He’s been in charge of the Bounty List for less than two years,” Chu Dingjiang explained, anticipating her doubts. “This information is accurate. It was the Yu Clan who, along with him, wiped out the original forces of the Bounty List. Then, Second Master Hua exchanged the land and water passage permit for the Yu Clan to relinquish control of the Bounty List. The Yu Clan never intended to be involved in this, so naturally they agreed.” The current head of the Yu Clan was Yu Pianfei, Zhu Pianxian’s younger brother. Chu Dingjiang said, “The jade pendant he gave you is one of the tokens of the bounty list. If you do not want to kill him, you can use this to remove your name from the list.” “Since he has the right to remove names, why not just withdraw them directly? Why give me this instead?” An Jiu asked. Chu Dingjiang said, “The bounty list has a long history, and many people have been in charge, but the rules have never changed. For the sake of fairness, the bounty list has never been a one-man show; there are many rules that govern it. This jade pendant has existed since the bounty list came into being, given to those who have rendered meritorious service in the bounty process. The holder can use it to make the bounty list do one thing.”

chapters.title: Ten Li of Lanterns Amidst the Snow
chapters.content: “Then would I not owe him another favor?” An Jiu’s face scrunched up; she disliked being in debt. “You owe him many favors?” Chu Dingjiang asked. An Jiu nodded. “He helped me a lot when I first left the Mei family.” “You’ve known him longer, have you not? Why are you so fixated on me?” Chu Dingjiang asked with a smile. “His kindness to me is mostly icing on the cake, while your kindness to me is a lifeline in the snow.” An Jiu had always understood this clearly. She was grateful for Hua Rongjian’s help and would repay it later, but Chu Dingjiang had shared life and death with her and repeatedly saved her from danger; this kind of relationship was different from ordinary ones. Chu Dingjiang raised an eyebrow. “That is all?” An Jiu crossed her arms and thought carefully. “I do not feel that kind of urge when I see him, but I do when I see you. Does that count?” “Of course.” This was far more important to Chu Dingjiang than the first reason. He leaned closer to her and whispered, “We have not felt that urge in a long time.” An Jiu had been in a coma for half a year. After she woke up, Chu Dingjiang, concerned about her weak health, had always tried his best to restrain himself. “You know, I’ve been abstaining for so many years.” Chu Dingjiang pulled her hand to touch his bulge. “Wow!” An Jiu exclaimed in surprise. “You really have been holding back a lot!” Even a mention of it made him instantly erect! An Jiu did not rush to comfort him but instead said with admiration, “It’s really not easy for you to have abstained for over twenty years.” Chu Dingjiang was speechless. The whole story was not like this! He was not a beast in heat; how could he have become so sensitive if it were not for long-term abstinence? He did not argue, but instead said melancholically, “Yes, it is very hard.” His breathing was heavy, and his voice was already slightly hoarse. “Ah Jiu.” He leaned in, slowly approaching her lips. Chu Dingjiang’s face was shrouded in the firelight, seemingly blurred by the warmth, appearing hazy even at such close range. There was a unique gentleness about him, but the gray at his temples and the fine lines under his eyes were clearly etched into An Jiu’s heart. A faint warmth mixed with a bittersweet feeling spread from her heart to the tip of her tongue. As their breaths drew closer, An Jiu felt her heart almost leap into her throat, and it took a great deal of effort to suppress it. Looking at Chu Dingjiang’s lips so close to hers, she swallowed hard, reached out, wrapped her arms around his neck, and kissed him fiercely. Outside, the sky was overcast, and snow was falling heavily. It was already like evening, though it was just past noon. The plum blossoms in the courtyard were covered in snow, exuding a faint, cool fragrance, while inside the house, it was warm and cozy. Two days passed. Hua Rongjian, dressed in simple, plain clothes, came to find An Jiu. “It’s New Year’s Eve today; shall we go for a stroll in the streets?” Hua Rongjian’s smile was as radiant as ever, showing no trace of someone who worked as an assassin. An Jiu glanced at the still-falling snow outside. “Anyone going out in this weather?” Hua Rongjian exclaimed excitedly, “Strolling through a market in the snow is quite interesting! A few years ago, I encountered a heavy snowfall. The snow fell heavily, and lanterns stretched for many li—that scene is still unforgettable! It is rare to have such perfect weather this year; it is sure to be even more lively!” “I am going too!” Mo Sigui shouted, poking his head out of the house. Hua Rongjian opened the window. “Go yourself!” Mo Sigui gripped his pipe. He sighed wistfully, “Back then, you were so reluctant to part with me on Zhuque Street, but now you’ve forgotten how you used to cuddle in my arms.” Hua Rongjian angrily retorted, “Tch! With your little frame, you dare call that an embrace? Get lost!” As the two were arguing heatedly, Chu Dingjiang draped a fox fur coat over An Jiu’s shoulders. He then took her hand and led her outside. “Hey! Where are you going?” Hua Rongjian hurriedly followed. Mo Sigui also quickly put on a cloak, turning back to look at Wei Yuzhi. “Let’s go together.” Wei Yuzhi hesitated for a moment. “Alright.” Anyway, he would be leaving after the New Year. The market was so vast, and Wei Yuzhi’s mental power was extremely high; he could simply avoid Hua Rongjian. He had not enjoyed the life of an ordinary person in a long time; life was short, so he should cherish every moment. Because of the snow, it got dark early. The streetlights, just coming on, illuminated the snow-covered landscape with a warm glow. Some people on the street carried umbrellas, and some didn’t; everyone was dressed in new clothes, their faces beaming with joy. Standing on Pan Tower Street, one could see two long, illuminated streets stretching to the horizon, the surrounding shops and stalls gleaming like stars surrounding a long dragon. Chu Dingjiang did not take An Jiu for a leisurely stroll; instead, they went straight to a restaurant. “My Lord, we are full. Have you made a reservation?” the attendant asked with a beaming smile. Chu Dingjiang hummed in agreement. “Chu.” “Oh, it is Master Chu. Please follow me.” The attendant’s tone was familiar, and he bowed slightly, inviting the two upstairs. It turned out Chu Dingjiang had made preparations all along. An Jiu glanced at him, her profile cold and aloof, giving off an unapproachable air. The luxury of the private room was self-evident. A brazier had been placed inside, and elegant incense was burning. The scent was not as strong as elsewhere; it carried a subtle herbal fragrance. “What’s that smell?” An Jiu asked. “Do you not like it?” Chu Dingjiang asked before the attendant could answer. “I like it, it smells wonderful.” Even the lightest fragrance could become cloying, affecting one’s appetite if overused, but this one was not cloying at all. The attendant, who had not intended to interrupt, saw the beauty’s enjoyment and quickly glanced at Chu Dingjiang, exclaiming, “This is a fragrance blended by Master Chu! Our manager offered a hefty sum, but he refused. So this fragrance was blended just for you, My Young Lady!” Such a small matter would not make An Jiu feel any desire to marry him, but she was very happy that Chu Dingjiang had blended the fragrance for her. The attendant, being tactful, poured the water and left, saying, “I will stay outside so you can summon me at any time, My Lord.” “Hmm.” Chu Dingjiang was as taciturn as ever in front of outsiders. “You can blend fragrances?” An Jiu discovered a side of Chu Dingjiang she did not know and was intrigued. Seeing her interest, Chu Dingjiang smiled and said, “Noble families used to love collecting these little things. I also pondered them for a while, but then I gave up.” “Was it not quite good? Why did you give it up?” An Jiu approached the incense burner, a refreshing scent wafting towards her, instantly clearing her mind. “Playing with trinkets leads to the loss of ambition,” Chu Dingjiang said, bringing over a cup of water, handing it to her, then leaning against the window, watching her, his stern expression melting away, replaced by a faint smile. “Back then, there were many incense masters who specialized in the art of incense. I had no interest in it; a little knowledge was enough. This is Qingling Incense; its fragrance can clear the mind, a favorite of strategists. I slightly modified the scent.” Originally, this incense was very strong, giving a refreshing sensation that rushed to the brain when lit. Chu Dingjiang softened it. An Jiu was about to speak when she suddenly sensed several familiar auras approaching her. Soon, Sheng Changying’s voice was heard: “Slow down, slow down.” “Master Chu. The people you invited have arrived,” the attendant said from outside. “Let them in.” Chu Dingjiang put down his water glass. An Jiu’s eyes brightened slightly. The door opened, and Sheng Changying helped Zhu Pianxian in, followed by Sui Yuntong, Li Qingzhi, and the young medicine boy. An Jiu had seen Mei Jiu pregnant before, so she naturally would not assume Zhu Pianxian had simply gained weight. “You are pregnant?” Zhu Pianxian was in a good mood, happy to play the lady, and answered shyly, “Yes. I am over six months along.” An Jiu paused, then asked, “Whose?” A vein throbbed on Zhu Pianxian’s forehead, and she gritted her teeth, saying, “Can you not see my husband is supporting me!” An Jiu nodded, lost in thought. “Madam, have some water.” Sheng Changying poured water and handed it to Zhu Pianxian before greeting Chu Dingjiang. “Please sit down. It is New Year’s; time for a family reunion dinner,” Chu Dingjiang said. The group took their seats one by one. A commotion erupted outside the door, and Mo Sigui roared, “Who dares to stop me!” Hua Rongjian arrogantly threatened, “Get out of my way!” Chu Dingjiang gave Sui Yuntong a look, and Sui Yuntong stood up and went to the door. “Let them in.” Two arrogant men strode in. As soon as Mo Sigui saw everyone had gathered, he immediately said, “Chu Dingjiang, you did not even invite me! You narrow-minded, despicable scoundrel!” Mo Sigui was a physician, and treating patients inevitably involved close contact, which Chu Dingjiang understood and accepted. However, this did not stop him from finding Mo Sigui an eyesore, so his attitude was naturally not pleasant. “Sit or get out?” Hua Rongjian glared at Chu Dingjiang. “Look at his attitude! Sigui, let’s go!” After he finished speaking, he noticed that Mo Sigui had already sat down next to Sheng Changying. Everyone at the table stared at Hua Rongjian standing there. He coughed and yelled at the attendant, “What are you standing there for? Can you not see I do not have a seat?!” The attendant glanced cautiously at Chu Dingjiang. Seeing that he did not object, he quickly said, “Yes, yes, I will get you a seat right away.” The seat was added next to Mo Sigui. Hua Rongjian was quite satisfied with this and was about to instruct the attendant to move the chair next to An Jiu when Chu Dingjiang gave him a cold look. “If you are not going to sit, get out.” Mo Sigui laughed gleefully. “The pot calling the kettle black!” Hua Rongjian reluctantly sat down, but he quickly cheered up because An Jiu was right across from him. Well, it was not a bad spot. Mei Yanran had just arrived when the dishes were served. “Something came up, so I am late,” she explained. Mo Sigui understood. She must have really wanted to have a family reunion dinner with her daughter at this special time. Chu Dingjiang stood up and invited Mei Yanran to the seat of honor. “Oh, you are pregnant!” Mo Sigui stared at Zhu Pianxian’s face for a while, then looked at Sheng Changying teasingly. “Pretty good, congratulations!” Zhu Pianxian’s belly was hidden by the table, so it was not visible from the opposite side. However, no one was surprised; Mo Sigui could tell if someone was ill just by looking at their face. Sheng Changying blushed slightly and cupped her hands in thanks. Mo Sigui clicked his tongue twice, noticing An Jiu’s thoughtful expression, and could not help but say, “Hey, does Ah Jiu also want to have one?” Everyone’s eyes turned to An Jiu. She pursed her lips, thinking for a long time. She had seen Mei Jiu’s chubby son before, so heavy and fragile in her arms. Normally, she could kill a strong, powerful man without breaking a sweat, but holding a baby felt like it would break at the slightest pressure, making her heart soften.

chapters.title: A Young Man’s Journey
chapters.content: “Let’s have one,” An Jiu said. Chu Dingjiang was a little surprised, and Mo Sigui also looked at her strangely. An Jiu paused, then continued, “But not yet. I need to think about this carefully.” Mo Sigui rolled his eyes. “Tch, can you stop pausing for breath?” An Jiu said, “I am very careful with my words, unlike you.” “Hey, what do you mean by that?” Mo Sigui rolled up his sleeves aggressively. Feeling Chu Dingjiang’s gaze on him, he immediately picked up his chopsticks, grabbed a piece of green vegetable, and put it in his mouth. Green vegetables were very common, but they were quite rare in winter. Mo Sigui, tired of eating meat all day, found the green vegetables particularly refreshing. In an instant, he forgot his earlier unpleasantness and focused on eating. Mo Sigui did not speak, making the room much quieter, but everyone was used to it. Chu Dingjiang asked, “Why have Young Lady Lou and Master Ling not arrived?” Sui Yuntong replied, “Master Ling accompanied Young Lady Lou back to the Lou mansion to pay respects to their ancestors; they will be a little late.” “Hmm,” Chu Dingjiang said, “Tell the attendant to add more seats.” Chu Dingjiang had not told the innkeeper how many people were in the private room when he booked it, so only eight seats were prepared beforehand; the rest were placed against the walls for easy access. The drinks and snacks were served first, and everyone drank while waiting for the others to arrive. The room was silent. Hua Rongjian could not stand it anymore. “The wine is good, but is this kind of drinking really fun?” The others stopped eating and drinking, all looking at Hua Rongjian; the scene was momentarily still. “Drinking is only fun when it is lively,” Hua Rongjian said enthusiastically. “How about we play a drinking game?” “A drinking game?” An Jiu turned to look at Sheng Changying, the most knowledgeable among them. Sheng Changying said, “The book says that drinking games are games played while drinking, and the rules vary, but I’ve never actually seen one played.” “None of you know how?” Hua Rongjian was astonished that there were people in the world who did not know how to play drinking games! “Since no one knows how, let’s play a simple one.” Hua Rongjian took a spoon and placed it on a porcelain plate. “Spin the spoon; whoever the handle points to drinks. If you do not want to drink, you can compose a poem or have someone drink for you.” Everyone had no objections, and Hua Rongjian began to spin the spoon. He did not use much force; the spoon spun a few times and then slowly stopped, the handle pointing directly at An Jiu. An Jiu raised her cup and drank it all. Hua Rongjian was embarrassed and decided to try again, so he used some skill to turn the handle back to An Jiu. The others sat silently, and An Jiu drank another cup. Hua Rongjian could not believe it. He spun it again, and it still pointed to An Jiu. The reaction from everyone was still the same! “What’s wrong with all of you? Do you know what ‘cheering’ means?” Hua Rongjian roared. Normally, people would cheer and encourage others when they saw someone being forced to drink, naturally livening up the atmosphere of the banquet. Who knew these people would behave like this? This drinking game was inherently very simple; without proper cooperation from the participants, the game would become utterly boring. Just then, the door was pushed open. A tall, burly man led in a young girl. Hua Rongjian’s gaze was fixed on the man’s face, unable to look away for a long time. The man had already concealed the sharp edge he once possessed when leading troops against the enemy. He had become more profound, but Hua Rongjian would not forget this face. “General Ling!” Previously, Ling Ziyue was stationed at the border for most of the year, only occasionally returning home. He was either busy going to the palace to report to the Emperor or spending time with his family, so he naturally did not have a deep impression of Hua Rongjian, a young master without official rank. Ling Ziyue, as a famous general of the Song Dynasty, was the focus of everyone’s attention, and many people recognized him. He did not recognize Hua Rongjian, but seeing him present, he seemed like a trustworthy person. He did not deny it. “This young master is…” “His surname is Hua, and his given name is Rongjian.” Hua Rongjian quickly stood up. At that time, Prime Minister Hua had already written a petition for leniency, but ultimately did not submit it. This showed that Prime Minister Hua knew Ling Ziyue was wronged and genuinely did not want him to be harmed. If he had known the man was alive, he would not have been so ruthless; he might even have helped to clear his name. Chu Dingjiang knew this, which was why he did not hide it from Hua Rongjian. Hua Rongjian stood up. “General, please sit here.” The two additional seats were only considered the last seats; his seat was not the most prestigious, but it was still much better than the last. “Do not be so formal, Brother Hua; please sit,” Ling Ziyue said. Hua Rongjian quickly said he did not dare. Ling Ziyue was practically of the same generation as Prime Minister Hua; how could Hua Rongjian dare call him “brother”? After sitting for a while, Lou Xiaowu recovered from her sadness and raised her cup to An Jiu. “Fourteenth, it is so good that you’ve woken up!” “Thank you.” An Jiu raised her cup and drank it all. Seeing so many familiar faces filled An Jiu with joy, but this joy was tinged with an undeniable sense of desolation. The arrival of Lou Xiaowu enlivened the banquet atmosphere, and An Jiu unknowingly drank quite a bit of wine. Chu Dingjiang watched her silently the whole time. Outside, the snow fell heavier and heavier, yet there was almost no wind. Fine snowflakes swirled gently down from the sky, forming a thick layer on the lamps. Wei Yuzhi walked alone in the snow, a thick black cloak covering his head, the hood completely concealing his white hair. Two rows of lampposts lined the road. Wei Yuzhi walked slowly, examining each one carefully, as if it were his last. He stopped in front of a teahouse. A burly man strode out from a nearby alley, bowed beside him, and said, “Sir.” Wei Yuzhi opened his mouth, a rush of cold air filling his throat, and he could not help but cough. The burly man noticed a stray strand of white hair on Wei Yuzhi’s shoulder and exclaimed in surprise, “My Lord, has your condition worsened? Let’s go to Liao to find Physician Ning!” “Do you not know who Physician Ning works for?” Wei Yuzhi asked indifferently. “But…” Wei Yuzhi interrupted him, “It’s Physician Mo treating me now.” “Really!” the burly man exclaimed happily. “Do not spread this around for now,” Wei Yuzhi said, catching his breath, “including Mei Ruyan.” “Yes,” the burly man replied, his expression composed. Wei Yuzhi said, “Wait for me to return safely at the mansion.” The burly man hesitated for a moment. “Or perhaps I should protect you personally, My Lord?” Wei Yuzhi slightly turned his head, his gaze light and indifferent. The burly man quickly lowered his head. “Your subordinate obeys.” With that, he disappeared into the crowd. In the bustling crowd, their conversation was brief, and they quickly passed each other without attracting any attention. Wei Yuzhi heard the sound of gongs and drums ahead and continued walking forward. He stood in the middle of the road and glanced over. A sea of ​​people was gathered, and a puppet show was being performed on stage. One of the puppets, dressed in magnificent robes, paced back and forth while someone sang, “Morning clouds scatter like black silk, pavilions pale in spring’s beauty. Willows weep, flowers cry. Heavy mud covers the nine streets, swallows fly late outside the gate. Now the sun brightly shines on the golden house, spring’s color resides in the peach branches…” Wei Yuzhi sensed a familiar person approaching. Turning around, his gaze passed through the crowd and met someone’s eyes. Then the song continued, “Not like before. Rain pours down on the small building; only two know the hidden sorrow.” An Jiu saw Wei Yuzhi standing in the crowd from afar, and her heart skipped a beat. The lyrics, which had been just background noise, suddenly became crystal clear in her ears. She knew this was Wei Yuzhi’s feeling. “What does the song on stage mean?” An Jiu murmured. Sheng Changying, standing beside her, said, “The poem tells a story of Emperor Wu of Han keeping a mistress in a golden house. It roughly says that the woman he loved in his youth is now someone else’s mistress.” Chu Dingjiang accurately located An Jiu’s gaze among the crowd, and his grip on her hand tightened. An Jiu snapped out of her reverie and pointed to the fried dough sticks beside her. “I want some. Buy some.” Chu Dingjiang immediately took out his money. Before the vendor could even wrap the dough sticks, her gaze was drawn to the dragon’s beard candy next to them. She tugged at Chu Dingjiang’s sleeve. “Buy some.” Chu Dingjiang continued to take out his money. Without even asking the price, he tossed out silver ingots one by one. After getting the fried dough sticks and the dragon’s beard candy, An Jiu first pinched one and popped it into her mouth. The sweetness made her eyes squint, and she then picked up another one and fed it to Chu Dingjiang. Eating as they walked, An Jiu had not gone ten steps when she saw the sugar figurines ahead and tugged at Chu Dingjiang’s sleeve again. “Buy some.” Zhu Pianxian clutched her heart. “My hard-earned money…I cannot bear to watch anymore, husband; please help me back.” Sheng Changying told Sui Yuntong to tell Chu Dingjiang, then helped Zhu Pianxian while shielding her from any bumps. “They only spend this much money all year; it is not much. Why not buy some to try, Madam?” “Oh!” Zhu Pianxian said with heartache. “How come I did not realize you were such a spendthrift before I married you!” Sheng Changying quickly comforted her, “I grew up in a place where I did not need to spend money; I do not know much about these things. From now on, Madam will manage all the money; I will listen to you.” Hearing him say this, Zhu Pianxian looked up and saw his eyes…With heavy dark circles under her eyes, she tenderly hugged his arm, her tone softening instantly. “Husband, do not work so hard in the future. Spending money is a small matter; we cannot let you suffer because of it.” Sheng Changying blushed slightly and whispered, “I used to think I suffered too much, but now it seems I must have suffered even more in my past lives to have such good fortune to marry you in this one.” Mo Sigui listened to the voice fading into the distance and could not help but click his tongue. “I thought Changying was a simpleton, but I did not expect him to be such a clever fox.” Sui Yuntong laughed. “In a place like the Konghe Academy, you cannot win everyone’s favor just by being a nice person.” “Huh, where did he go?” Mo Sigui craned his neck to look around, only to find that he had lost track of the foodie who could not resist the sight of snacks. Sui Yuntong said, “It’s alright; the adults are with us.” “Tch, I am not worried about her at all.” Mo Sigui clicked his tongue. “She just drank so much; I just want to come and see the show.” An Jiu’s drinking manners were not very good; when drunk, she was a complete madwoman, a truly shocking sight. However, Mo Sigui was not really that bored. He was just curious that An Jiu was clearly drunk this time, yet showed no signs of going crazy. He wanted to investigate whether it was related to Wei Yuzhi’s hard work. Chu Dingjiang and An Jiu had reached the noodle stall and were about to sit down when a black-clad man approached. “Sir.” Chu Dingjiang did not turn around, coldly saying, “Leave.” The black-clad man was Su, who had once followed Chu Dingjiang but had turned against him for a woman. Su said, “I have urgent business; otherwise, I would not wish to see you again.” The noodles were not ready yet, and An Jiu stood up, saying, “I will go across the street to buy chestnut cakes to take back.” Chu Dingjiang looked up and saw a chestnut cake stall a hundred paces ahead, so he nodded, “Go ahead.” An Jiu carried a bag of silver over. Su glanced at An Jiu, sat down opposite Chu Dingjiang, took a letter from his robes, placed it on the table, and said softly, “This is a letter from His Majesty to you, My Lord.” Chu Dingjiang raised an eyebrow but did not reach out to take it. Now, the only person Su could refer to as “His Majesty” was the current Emperor. “I do not know what the letter says, but I think His Majesty intends to invite you back, My Lord.” Su’s feelings were complicated. Since returning to the palace with the token given to him by Chu Dingjiang, the Emperor had directly put him in charge of the new Konghe Army, and he now held a high position. However, the higher his rank, the clearer the woman’s figure became. Chu Dingjiang did not look at him; his gaze followed a figure in the crowd. Clutching her silver pouch, An Jiu walked briskly towards the chestnut cake stall, her mood brightening as she smelled the faint, sweet aroma. She rushed to the stall, bent down, and pulled out a piece of silver. “Boss, chestnut cake.” “Boss, chestnut cake.” Another gentle male voice rang out simultaneously. An Jiu turned her head in surprise, seeing the man also turn around. Their eyes met, and Wei Yuzhi nodded slightly. An Jiu nodded hastily, shoving the silver into the stall owner’s hand. “I want a lot.” “Five taels of silver can buy ten jin. Do you want that much, miss?” the stall owner asked. An Jiu nodded, pointing to Wei Yuzhi. “Give him half.” “Alright.” The stall owner quickly wrapped up the chestnut cakes and placed them in a basket. “Since you bought so many, this basket is for you.” Wei Yuzhi had only come to buy a few pieces, remembering the chestnut cakes he ate as a child, but unexpectedly, his arms were now overflowing. The chestnut cake was still warm, its warmth seeping through his thick clothes and touching his heart. An Jiu craned her neck, waiting for the stall owner to put the wrapped chestnut cake into the basket. She was not using an umbrella; large snowflakes fell on her dark hair, quickly forming a thin layer. The orange-red light from the surrounding lanterns illuminated her face, making her radiate warmth. In the distance. Chu Dingjiang put away the letter and said, “Go back. I’ve decided to live in seclusion, detached from worldly affairs.” Su said, “He Cai died for you. I think I will never be able to let go of that for the rest of my life, and I never want to see you again in my lifetime. But I still want to say that the current ruler is wise.” Before he could say anything more, the person before him was gone. A gentle breeze stirred on the street, slightly disturbing the snow, but no one noticed anything amiss. An Jiu noticed Wei Yuzhi’s gaze and turned to look at him. “Why are you staring at me?” Wei Yuzhi tried to brush the snow off her hair with his mental power, but sensed a powerful force rapidly approaching. In the blink of an eye, a tall figure appeared behind her, opening an umbrella over her head. An Jiu did not need to turn around to know it was Chu Dingjiang. Wei Yuzhi nodded slightly to Chu Dingjiang and said, “Thank you for the chestnut cake, Fourteenth.” An Jiu waved her hand somewhat guiltily. Chu Dingjiang reached out and brushed the snow off her hair, then took the basket from the stall owner. He had not said a word the entire time, but his imposing aura said it all. As they walked back, An Jiu confessed, “I shared half of the chestnut cake with him.” “I see,” Chu Dingjiang said. “Are you angry?” An Jiu asked.

chapters.title: The Secret Realm
chapters.content: Chu Dingjiang looked down at her. “Why did you think I was angry?” “Intuition,” An Jiu said. Just now, Chu Dingjiang had indeed been angry for a moment when facing Wei Yuzhi, but it was only for a fleeting instant. He was extremely good at controlling his emotions. Chu Dingjiang smiled slightly. “Even if I was angry, it was not at you.” “At Wei Yuzhi? Why?” An Jiu was confused. After thinking it over, she realized Wei Yuzhi had not done anything. “Those chestnut cakes were given by me willingly…” Chu Dingjiang knew An Jiu was possessive of her food. For her, sharing her favorite foods with others was very important. But he said, “Just because you gave them to him does not mean he has to keep them. Does he not know you have a fiancé? It is obvious he has ulterior motives.” His serious face clearly said, “It’s always someone else’s fault; My Young Lady is innocent.” The two had already consummated their marriage. Since An Jiu did not want to get married, Chu Dingjiang positioned himself as her “fiancé.” An Jiu thought about it carefully and muttered, “That seems to make sense.” “I’ve crossed more bridges than you’ve walked roads. It is fine if you do not understand these principles yet; I will teach you slowly.” Chu Dingjiang patted her head and continued, “Before, you did not want to share food with others because of circumstances. Now we do not lack these things, so learning to share is not wrong. When we get back, give some of these chestnut cakes to Aunt Mei and Mo Sigui as well. I will buy you chestnut cakes every day from now on.” An Jiu tightened her grip on the chestnut cakes, and her brows furrowed. After thinking for a while, she said, “They are also very important to me. Why do I feel a little heartache when I share the chestnut cakes with them? But I did not feel heartache just now?” Chu Dingjiang did not need to think about the reason. “That is because the chestnut cakes had not reached you yet!” “That makes sense…I guess.” She had only instructed the shopkeeper to pack the chestnut cakes for Wei Yuzhi, and now she had to personally deliver them… Just thinking about it made her heart ache! Chu Dingjiang said earnestly, “An Xiaojiu, you cannot eat this much today. We can buy new ones tomorrow.” “Alright.” An Jiu imagined giving the food to her mother and felt no remorse. She even felt it was not nearly enough. The two returned to the noodle stall and ate a large bowl of noodles, both slightly sweaty. An Jiu held her stomach, while Chu Dingjiang held an umbrella in one hand and carried chestnut cakes and various snacks in the other. Seeing her satisfied expression, a smile appeared in Chu Dingjiang’s eyes. However, after the smile came helplessness. An Jiu’s fear of marriage was already a big problem, but then Wei Yuzhi appeared out of nowhere! If it were just an ordinary man, he would not have cared, but they had a blood connection, a kind of unspoken understanding. This made him go from being an “insider” to an “outsider.” An Jiu and Wei Yuzhi understood each other’s feelings naturally, while he could only guess based on familiarity and wisdom. A beautiful woman’s heart was hard to uncover. “Uncle Chu.” An Jiu stopped and looked up at him. Chu Dingjiang snapped out of his daze. “Hmm?” Snowflakes fell heavily outside, people came and went, but under the umbrella, a small world seemed to exist, warm and safe because the person holding the umbrella was Chu Dingjiang. “Let’s get married,” An Jiu said. When she said those words, the blizzard seemed to freeze for a moment, then resumed its heavy descent, as if someone’s heart had collapsed. An Jiu’s face paled slightly, and she tasted a metallic sweetness in her mouth. She swallowed it. Chu Dingjiang keenly sensed something was wrong and immediately pulled her close, their figures blurring through the crowd. Behind the wall of lights, Wei Yuzhi steadied himself against a pillar. He had just been facing those two. Thinking he should avoid them, he walked behind the wall of lights, and just as they passed each other, he heard An Jiu say those words. He knew he should control his emotions. But the news came too suddenly, catching him completely off guard. The extreme emotional fluctuations triggered a relapse of his heartbreak. Wei Yuzhi sensed something was wrong, and his powerful mental energy suddenly surged forth, pinpointing Mo Sigui’s location amidst the bustling crowd. He rushed over. Everyone on the street felt a chill flash by, their minds momentarily blank. Some with weaker self-control even stumbled and fell in the snow. Mo Sigui, who was admiring a pretty young woman, suddenly shivered. “Something’s strange.” Sui Yuntong also felt it; the chill penetrated his brain directly, and resisting it would cause a splitting headache. Mo Sigui looked around when his arm was suddenly grabbed. “Divine Physician!” Wei Yuzhi’s deathly pale face came into Mo Sigui’s view. He immediately thought of An Jiu. “What happened! Where’s Ah Jiu?” “Master Chu must have taken her back.” Wei Yuzhi swayed slightly. Seeing An Jiu’s reaction, Chu Dingjiang knew what had happened. Since she had such injuries, Wei Yuzhi must be even more seriously injured. His mental power could not distinguish between different people, but Wei Yuzhi could quickly find Mo Sigui in a crowd. Therefore, he decided to take An Jiu back to wait rather than search aimlessly like headless flies. Mo Sigui grabbed Wei Yuzhi’s pulse and checked it briefly. “Carry him, let’s go!” Li Qingzhi immediately carried Wei Yuzhi on his back, and the group, ignoring the stares of those around them, lightly leaped onto the roof and quickly returned to their lodgings. Chu Dingjiang was already waiting in Mo Sigui’s room with An Jiu. Two beds were placed side by side, with Mo Sigui sitting in the middle, checking pulses as well. The onlookers held their breath, afraid to disturb him. “Ah Jiu is fine. Get some medicine from the pharmacy and prepare it. Rest well,” Mo Sigui said. Chu Dingjiang was relieved and took An Jiu back to her room to recuperate. Mei Yanran came out of the kitchen and ran into the two of them. Seeing An Jiu’s pale face, she quickly followed her into the house. After An Jiu lay down, she asked, “What happened?” Chu Dingjiang briefly explained the situation. Mei Yanran seemed thoughtful. “I will go brew the medicine first.” She left the house, grabbed the medicine, and went to the kitchen. The medicine was simmering on the stove. Mei Yanran held a palm-leaf fan in her hand, lost in thought. She had been guiding An Jiu in practicing Plum Blossom Fist and roughly guessed why An Jiu was practicing it, but the results had not been great after so long. Plum Blossom Fist was an external martial art. Everyone thought that the most important thing about external martial arts was tempering the body, but Mei Yanran vaguely felt that was not the case. Take herself, for example. While her body was strong, when she fought against masters, she mainly used her mental strength, not brute force. As a direct descendant of the Mei family, Mei Yanran had thoroughly mastered the Plum Blossom Fist style, but she had not achieved the terrifying destructive power rumored to be hers. She had always thought it was due to insufficient mental strength, but after teaching An Jiu, she discovered that although An Jiu possessed strong mental strength, her application of the technique was actually inferior to hers. Mei Yanran also knew the secret Plum Blossom Fist manual that the Mei family had confiscated, so this was not the reason for An Jiu’s stagnant progress. “The Plum Blossom Fist Heart Sutra,” Mei Yanran murmured. She recalled a story she had heard many years ago when she still held some power within the Mei family. Legend had it that the Mei family’s ancestor originally practiced internal martial arts, and even Plum Blossom Fist was originally an internal cultivation style. Later, just as the ancestor was about to break through to a higher realm, he was ambushed and lost all his internal energy. One step to heaven, one step to hell. Filled with hatred, the ancestor endured ten years of hardship and created Plum Blossom Fist. He avenged his great grudge but also suffered a backlash from his powerful mental strength. On his deathbed, a flash of inspiration struck him, and he wrote a hundred-character Heart Sutra to leave to his descendants. Later, someone in the Mei family’s history mastered the technique, and it was from then on that the Mei family rose to fame. However, for some reason, the Heart Sutra disappeared without a trace. Mei Yanran knew that Elder Zhi had only broken through to the Transcendent Realm in recent years, and the reason he was unharmed was because his body had been tempered to the point where it could withstand powerful mental energy, not because he had practiced the Heart Sutra. After the medicine was brewed, Mei Yanran took it to Chu Dingjiang and then went to Mo Sigui’s room. The treatment there had already been completed. Mo Sigui asked Sui Yuntong to brew the medicine while he rested against the pile of herbs. He was about to get up when Mei Yanran stopped him. “Sit down. I came to ask you something.” “Aunt, please speak,” Mo Sigui said.
