Mei Yanran sat down. “If there were a mental cultivation manual that harmonizes mental and physical strength, would it benefit Ah Jiu?” Mo Sigui straightened up abruptly. “Of course! It is not just her problem anymore. If she could practice with Wei Yuzhi, their connection might weaken or even disappear.” “Plum Blossom Fist actually has another mental cultivation manual, but I’ve never seen it. No one in the Mei family has practiced it in the past hundred years.” Mei Yanran had been trying to figure out where to find it. “I suspect it is in a secret realm.” “A secret realm?” Although Mo Sigui had lived in the Mei Mansion for many years, he was not surnamed Mei and naturally did not know the Mei family possessed any mental cultivation manuals or secret realms. Mei Yanran nodded. “Yes, I know the entrance to the secret realm, but the paths are intricate and complex. If I rashly enter, I could easily get lost forever. Besides, the key to open the secret realm has been kept by successive family heads, and I’ve never seen it.” Mo Sigui asked, “Aunt, do you mean Sixth Uncle knows?” “Zhengjing was groomed to be the next family head from a young age. He entered the secret realm when he was young and was counting on you to come out. He’s the current family head…” Mei Yanran sighed. “However, the Mei family suffered a sudden misfortune at the time, and it is unknown whether the key was lost. But asking cannot hurt.” “If it is really as Aunt says, the Plum Blossom Fist Heart Sutra can bring mental power and physical body into harmony; that would be wonderful!” Mo Sigui pondered for a moment. “Tell Chu Dingjiang about this and let him bother him.” After all, something even Mei Yanran did not know must have a reason it could not be revealed. Even if he asked for it, Mei Zhengjing would never give it to him. Mei Yanran said, “I am just a little worried. If the Heart Sutra is truly a valuable treasure, why would the Mei family choose to hide it, and why would even the Mei family members not practice it?” “We will only know once we obtain the Heart Sutra. Aunt, do not worry. If I see the Heart Sutra, I think I can judge the advantages and disadvantages,” Mo Sigui said. Mei Yanran nodded. “It just so happens that the Mei family recently sought help from Master Chu. If I mediate, I should be able to obtain the Heart Sutra.” If Chu Dingjiang were to ask for it, Mei Zhengjing might not be willing to give it to him, but Mei Yanran was, after all, a direct descendant of the Mei family, so it would not be considered outside the family.

chapters.title: Letting Go
chapters.content: Wei Yuzhi remained unconscious for three days before waking up. These three days had exhausted Mo Sigui, and, for the first time, he fell into a deep sleep without the aid of medicinal smoke. Upon waking, he felt refreshed, even more so than before. Sunlight shone on the snow, dazzlingly white. Mo Sigui stretched, turning his head to see Wei Yuzhi, dressed in a blue robe, leaning against the couch, reading a letter. His khaki fur coat almost slipped off his body, and his snow-white hair was tinged with a faint gray from the roots, like ink wash. “Oh my, the Divine Physician is truly amazing!” Mo Sigui exclaimed excitedly upon seeing the gray streak, shoving a mirror into Wei Yuzhi’s hand. “Take a look! In a year or two, your hair will be back to normal, and your face will be as handsome as before.” Wei Yuzhi put down the mirror, his slender fingers holding the letter, and presented it to Mo Sigui. “My letter?” Mo Sigui asked, puzzled. Wei Yuzhi said, “No. But I think the Divine Physician would like to know about Young Lady Lou.” Mo Sigui paused for a moment, then quickly took the letter and read it carefully. After reading it, his expression softened slightly, and he handed the letter back to Wei Yuzhi, saying, “Thank you.” “It’s my pleasure,” Wei Yuzhi replied. It turned out that a month ago, Lou Mingyue had again attempted to assassinate Yelu Huangwu, severely injuring her. However, she herself was in dire straits, and it was only through Wei Yuzhi’s covert influence in the Liao Kingdom that she was able to escape danger. This was Lou Mingyue’s second action after lying low for half a year, clearly a step further than before. “If given another chance, Young Lady Lou will surely be able to avenge her great grudge.” Wei Yuzhi and Yelu Huangwu were both allies and mortal enemies. If Lou Mingyue truly succeeded, he would benefit immensely, so of course, he was willing to lend a helping hand. Besides, this would also repay Mo Sigui’s favor, so why not? What Chu Dingjiang said last time was not without merit. National hatred and personal vendettas were not necessarily mutually exclusive. With the Liao Kingdom ostracizing him, even if he exerted all his efforts, he could not destroy the Song Dynasty. Some people who went astray could turn back before it was too late, but for Wei Yuzhi, there was no second chance. Now that he had realized this path was blocked, should he bang his head against the wall or turn back from his misguided ways? Wei Yuzhi looked at the blinding sunlight outside and slowly said, “To be able to accomplish one thing in a lifetime is something to celebrate.” Mo Sigui sighed deeply. “You cannot have your cake and eat it too. Some people think they are all in control and want to have it all, but in the end, they lose everything. Alas! Chu Dingjiang was a wise man.” He could not help but pick up his pipe and light another puff of medicinal smoke. “It seems I am very likely to be the one who loses everything.” “Young Lady Lou is also a wise woman,” Wei Yuzhi paused for a moment, then added, “If Physician Mo could communicate with her… I suggest you try to persuade her. Young Lady Lou’s assassination attempt this time was driven by a desire for mutual destruction. Perhaps she wants to be free sooner…and free you as well.” “I know. She’s never liked causing trouble for others. I am the one who insisted on getting involved.” Mo Sigui exhaled a puff of smoke, a bitter taste spreading across his tongue. “I am the one who pushed her to this point.” Otherwise, Lou Mingyue would not be in such a hurry. As the saying goes, “A gentleman’s revenge is never too late.” She could have had more time to observe the enemy to plan the assassination, striving for a swift and decisive strike, or perhaps she could have found another way to retaliate against Yelu Huangwu. She chose to take risks time and again, even if it meant mutual destruction, because she feared the painful entanglement with Mo Sigui. No one was wrong; fate was. “It’s time to let go.” Mo Sigui walked to his desk, picked up a pen, wrote a letter, then took Xiao Yue and tied the bamboo tube to it. Wei Yuzhi had not expected him to make such a decisive decision. “A clean break, truly admirable.” “She and I are childhood sweethearts. Since this bond is a burden for both of us, why hesitate?” Mo Sigui patted Xiaoyue’s head and fed it a bag of herbs. “Go!” Seeing Mo Sigui’s decisiveness, Wei Yuzhi felt he should also make a decision sooner. … Bianjing, Mei Mansion. Two people sat in the main hall, yet the room was silent. Mei Zhengjing, dressed in a plain robe, sat in the head seat, looking at the woman in a light blue dress. After a long pause, he said, “Cousin, I am afraid I cannot make the exchange. I’ve known since childhood that the lives of Mei family members can be given away casually, but there are two things they cannot give away: the Heart Sutra and the Cold Plum.” The Cold Plum was actually a plum tree carved from a rare type of jadeite. It could help external cultivators temper their bodies and spirits, and legend had it that if used properly, it could even bring the dead back to life. Both should be effective for An Jiu. The Cold Plum was a treasure of the Mei family, and they would never part with it. However, the Plum Blossom Fist Heart Sutra was useless. Mei Yanran could only choose one she was confident she could use to negotiate. “You cannot even exchange the Konghe Secret Manual? Jiu’er and I are not outsiders. Exchanging just for a glimpse of the manual is a deal you would not lose by any measure.” “Cousin,” Mei Zhengjing said lazily, resting his chin on his hand, “If you truly consider yourself a member of the Mei family, you should not be doing this deal with me.” “Do you think I wanted to?” Mei Yanran’s eyes reddened slightly, her anger barely contained. “The Konghe Secret Manual is not even in my possession. It is only because Master Chu treated Jiu’er differently and was willing to exchange it that I do not even have the right to negotiate with you! Let me ask you, in the six months since Jiu’er fell into a coma, has the Mei family offered any help? I consider myself a member of the Mei family, but if the family abandons my daughter to her death, do not blame me for looking out for myself!”

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.content: “Cousin, you can blame me for being ruthless,” Mei Zhengjing said seriously. “Back then, when you were away on the run for over a decade, the Mei family spared your lives, not only because Fourteenth Young Lady was indeed talented in archery, but also because the clan valued blood ties and was unwilling to be ruthless unless absolutely necessary. If I did not care about blood relations, I should have killed Fourteenth Young Lady today! We crippled Elder Zhi in exchange for the secret manual, but Chu Dingjiang did not keep his promise! The Mei family also has dignity! Besides kicking someone when they are down, what has Fourteenth Young Lady done for the family?” Mei Zhengjing, abandoning his usual nonchalance, said coldly, “Fourteenth Young Lady grew up away from home; she has no sense of belonging to the Mei family, and I do not blame her. You fled to escape the abyss, and I will not hold that against you either. Cousin, what right do you have to question me, to question the Mei family!” Mei Yanran’s lips tightened; she truly had no right to question. At that time, she had not originally intended to escape the Mei family. But when her husband died a violent death, and she learned she was pregnant, her first thought was that she could not let her child be trapped in this quagmire! Later, Elder Qi examined her pulse and said that this child’s talent would definitely rival Mei Zhengjing’s. It was this statement that solidified Mei Yanran’s plan to escape. Mei Zhengjing was exceptionally talented, but he was a male heir and the next head of the family. He would not have to fake his death at a young age and live in darkness forever, making a living by killing. But Mei Jiu was different; she might not only be trained as an assassin but also become the Emperor’s concubine! Originally, this was the path she should have taken, but she used cunning to have her stepsister take her place. For this, her stepmother hated her intensely, not even sparing her husband, let alone her daughter. Thinking of all this, Mei Yanran felt unbearable heartache. So, after understanding the situation, she resolutely left. “The debts I owe must be repaid sooner or later,” Mei Yanran said, her eyes red and her voice slightly choked. “Why? I just did not want to succumb to fate. I struggled a little, and now I have to bear the consequences alone? Why does the retribution have to fall on my daughter? If my sister had not deliberately harmed me, I would not have even thought of dragging her down with me.” Others could harm her, but she did not even have the right to resist? Mei Zhengjing’s anger gradually subsided. “We, the young and strong of the Mei family, are forced to feign death, forever living in darkness to serve the royal family, all because of this inescapable place. Before I succeeded as family head, I thought my elder brother was cowardly, but now I know it was not so. The Mei family has now withered to this state. I am not afraid to reveal this secret. There’s a poison in the blood of the four great families. With a special medicine, we will all lose consciousness and become walking corpses, only capable of killing.” Mei Yanran’s heart skipped a beat. “Is there no antidote, Sigui…” “No. Every generation of Divine Physicians in our Mei family has dedicated their lives to researching how to cure this poison, but they’ve found it impossible. This poison has become part of our blood. It is inherited from generation to generation; it is impossible to completely eradicate it.” Mei Zhengjing recalled his conversation with his brother that night at the “Loyalty and Righteousness” building. He was so shocked by this news that he could not speak. After a long while, Mei Yanran finally recovered. “Is the Konghe Manual related to this?” Mei Zhengjing replied, “Yes, the Konghe Manual contains methods to activate the poison within our bodies, as well as the genealogies of the four great families and their martial arts specialties.” In other words, obtaining the Konghe Manual would force the four great families to serve, and if they refused, they could be forced into submission! If this were in the hands of the current Emperor, the fate of the four great families might not change much. At worst, they would continue to serve the royal family as before, seeking an opportunity to steal the manual. The problem was that the current Emperor had usurped the throne and was unlikely to be familiar with the Konghe Manual. The eunuch who knew many secrets escaped during the palace’s fall, and someone discovered that Liao people were present in the palace that day, seemingly searching for the manual. If the Liao people were to obtain it, their fate would be unimaginable. Thud! A book fell from the rafters, landing directly on the table beside Mei Zhengjing. Immediately afterward, a figure in black leaped down and sat down next to Mei Yanran. Mei Zhengjing was first startled, then his heart leaped with joy as he looked at the book. “It’s the Secret Manual!” he exclaimed. The cover bore the four characters “Secret Manual of Konghe” in neat seal script. “Do not be too happy yet,” Chu Dingjiang said in a deep voice. “There are three copies of the manual, each kept in a different place. I took this one first, and when I went to look for the others, I found they had all been taken.” Mei Zhengjing, caught off guard by this sudden outburst of joy, was momentarily stunned. “Fortunately, there’s only one secret manual, divided into three parts. The one I obtained contains most of the names of the Mei and Lou families,” Chu Dingjiang said, but his tone remained firm. “From now on, you either live in anonymity or continue searching for other secret manuals.” Mei Zhengjing glanced through it. The method for activating the poison was not in this manual. If it fell into the wrong hands, those of the Mei family who had been hiding in the shadows would be relatively safer, but those like Mei Zhengjing, who were in the open, would be in much greater danger. Chu Dingjiang saw through his thoughts immediately. “The Konghe Army has already been infiltrated by the Liao people. It is hard to say how much intelligence they possess. If Gu Jinghong passed everything he knew to the Liao, destroying this manual would be pointless.” Mei Zhengjing knew the renowned chief assassin on the Konghe List. He was surprised. “Even he’s a Liao spy!” Chu Dingjiang did not speak, but his tone was firm. After Mei Yanran arrived, he followed. The Mei family and An Jiu were already enemies. When Mei Zhengjing lowered his dignity to beg him, this outcome was inevitable. Mei Yanran was unaware of the details, always believing that Chu Dingjiang was the one interfering, determined to settle scores with the Mei family. An Jiu was the victim; even if the Mei family wanted to hate her, they should not hate her. Although she had not contributed anything to the family, she had not done anything to harm their interests. Who would have thought it would escalate to this point? Mei Zhengjing could guess some of Chu Dingjiang’s intentions. Fourteenth Young Lady, whom he protected, also had Mei family blood. If the secret genealogy was not retrieved, An Jiu would also be in danger. This secret genealogy did not contain specific details, only the genealogies of the Mei and Lou families. Even if Chu Dingjiang was clever, he could not have guessed that. Mei Zhengjing unleashed a burst of internal force, shattering the secret genealogy into dust. “I destroyed Elder Zhi. Master Chu, give me the secret genealogy, and we are even.” “I have no objections.” Chu Dingjiang stood up. Mei Yanran’s gaze paused slightly. Mei Zhengjing also had a bad feeling; Chu Dingjiang was definitely such a gentleman!

chapters.title: Blood Poison
chapters.content: “Hide the things well, and whatever you do, do not let me find them,” Chu Dingjiang said calmly, his eyes lowered. Today, Chu Dingjiang had been hiding in the house for who knew how long, and Mei Zhengjing and Mei Yanran had not noticed a thing. Who in this world could stop him? However, after confronting Chu Dingjiang once, Mei Zhengjing knew that his despicable nature was far more than this. “Stealing? I will not do something as despicable as that,” Chu Dingjiang smirked. “If you refuse to hand over the Heart Sutra, I will kill everyone in the Mei clan, take the key, and search slowly. There are not many Mei clan members left; even if I kill one a day, it will not take long.” Mei Zhengjing said, “Do you think coercion will work? My Mei clan is only trying to survive; we are not that afraid of death.” “Your backbone is admirable. But what’s the use of reckless courage? You know the person I am protecting is on the same cliff as you. If you cooperate, you will not only avoid another enemy, but you will also gain an advantage,” Chu Dingjiang said. “A temporary ally is still an ally. You are a pragmatic person; I do not think I need to waste any more words. I will give you two days to think it over. If I do not hear a definite answer after two days, I will start killing.” “No need for two days. I agree,” Mei Zhengjing said. Chu Dingjiang’s solemn face revealed no emotion. “When will you fulfill your promise?” Mei Zhengjing thought for a moment. “The secret realm’s paths are complex, and they become even more dangerous in the summer. If you want to find the Heart Sutra, the sooner the better, but a round trip would take at least three months.” Chu Dingjiang asked, “I heard you’ve been to the secret realm before, but you cannot even remember a hundred characters?” “I went in for training. I touched the gate to the secret realm, but I never actually entered.” “Then you do not know why the Mei family has kept the Heart Sutra hidden?” “I do not know.” This had always been a question for Mei Zhengjing. Unfortunately, he had resisted becoming the head of the Mei family back then, so there were many things he did not know. Now, even if he wanted to know, no one could tell him. Only the successive heads of the family were qualified to know these things. Perhaps this trip to the secret realm would provide the answer! Chu Dingjiang continued to ask, “Since you hold this secret, why did you not tell me directly instead of letting me threaten you?” If Mei Zhengjing had revealed this secret back then, Chu Dingjiang would have been immediately at a disadvantage. “This matter concerns the life of the Mei family. How could I reveal your secrets without knowing your background!” Mei Zhengjing knew this explanation was not convincing enough, so he said, “After returning to the mansion, I ordered everyone to search for the secret manual with all their might. With the agreed-upon one-month deadline fast approaching, I did indeed have the thought of destroying Elder Zhi’s hands…” Such things were common in large families, especially assassin families like the Mei family, where individuals were often sacrificed to protect the greater good. Although Mei Zhengjing felt reluctant and guilty, he did not think there was anything wrong with what he was doing. Chu Dingjiang had given Mei Zhengjing medicine to treat his mental injuries, which Mei Zhengjing immediately gave him upon his return, but the medicine had no effect. Until Mei Zhengjing hesitated outside Elder Zhi’s door, Elder Zhi regained consciousness for a moment. Mei Zhengjing was overjoyed, feeling as if he had found a pillar of support. He told Elder Zhi everything, hoping he could find a solution that would benefit both sides. However, Elder Zhi remained silent for a long time before suddenly destroying his own tendons and then begged Mei Zhengjing to give him a quick death after obtaining the secret manual. “Sixth Brother. Everyone says I sacrificed a great deal for the family. Indeed, I lived my entire life for the family. But in my old age, during the family’s most difficult time, I chose the wrong path out of selfishness. As a result, all my sacrifices over the years were reduced to ashes. I spent the first half of my life risking my life for the family, but in the second half, I abandoned it all, pouring all my energy into archery. In the end, I achieved neither success nor fame. This fate is the consequence of my own actions.” “Elder Zhi said, ‘In life, once the arrow is released, there’s no turning back.’ Once you’ve given everything for something, there’s no going back until death. Although you may not achieve perfection, giving up halfway guarantees a mediocre life.” Mei Zhengjing sighed. “He’s awakened, and he’s made me believe in you.” From Elder Zhi’s words, it was easy to hear regret. Intelligent people were quick to realize their mistakes, but unfortunately, he realized them too late. Now, all he felt was endless pain. This pain had nothing to do with anyone else; it was because he knew he had not done his best to protect the Mei family, and his mind had been distracted by archery. Chu Dingjiang nodded, indicating his belief in the explanation. Mei Yanran felt a pang of sorrow. Compared to the greater good of her clan, she was merely a selfish mother, a failed mother. “I will go with you,” she said. Mei Zhengjing nodded in agreement, then looked at Chu Dingjiang. “While I am gone, I will trouble you to look after the Mei family, My Lord.” “Twice.” Chu Dingjiang could not forever be a slave to protecting the Mei family. His power had declined significantly; if twenty ninth-rank cultivators attacked him simultaneously, they would surely kill him. Although there were not many ninth-rank cultivators left in the world, did the Liao Kingdom not still have those pseudo-ninth-rank cultivators whose power had surged due to elixirs? If they could only hold out for half a day, Chu Dingjiang would still be defeated. Mei Zhengjing understood. Chu Dingjiang was only willing to save the Mei family from danger twice. He calculated his departure time and figured the promise could be postponed. “Deal!” he said. This deal was still a win for Mei Zhengjing. The Mei family was in grave danger, and gaining a Transcendent Realm expert to protect them was like a windfall. Mei Zhengjing was decisive. Having agreed, he immediately entrusted all Mei family affairs to Mei Tingzhu and packed his bags to go to Mei Mansion with Mei Yanran. Chu Dingjiang was burdened with responsibilities and felt somewhat annoyed, but mostly relieved. If he had not overheard this huge secret today, allowing this hidden danger to lurk within An Jiu would have been far more terrifying; his wife might have become a heartless killing machine one day. At least now that he knew, there was still room for redemption. Back at the Hua Mansion, Chu Dingjiang decided to take Mei Jiu back to the Mei Mansion to wait. “Are you coming or not?” Chu Dingjiang told Mo Sigui his thoughts. Mo Sigui looked at the room full of medicine and decisively shook his head. “I am not leaving.” Chu Dingjiang nodded, not insisting. He had wanted to ask Mo Sigui if he knew about the poison in Mei’s blood, but with Wei Yuzhi present, he did not speak. He was always a decisive person; once he said he would leave, he would. He only left a letter on the table and left lightly with An Jiu in a carriage, so no one paid any attention, assuming it was just an ordinary outing. Everything in Mei Mansion remained the same. Lou Xiaowu saw An Jiu return and happily pulled her around. “Rat, you are back!” An Jiu pouted, “Yeah, Mushroom.” Their originally very affectionate “heart-to-heart talk” left behind a lingering effect—two nicknames. “Mushroom is much better than Rat!” Lou Xiaowu said smugly, secretly glad she had not called herself a weasel. Chu Dingjiang saw An Jiu and Lou Xiaowu looking quite innocent together and liked it very much. “You two go play.” Lou Xiaowu glanced at Ling Ziyue. “Go on!” Ling Ziyue said. Lou Xiaowu happily pulled An Jiu along and skipped out. The two uncles inside watched them leave, looking like doting fathers who had just seen their daughters grow up.

chapters.title: Sweet Words
chapters.content: As dusk settled, the islanders, having finished their dinner, were busy in their courtyards when two dashingly handsome men in flowing robes and a small hill emerged from the mist. One was dressed in blue with white hair, the other in brown robes with phoenix eyes—undoubtedly Wei Yuzhi and Mo Sigui. Mo Sigui, always impulsive, had initially declared resolutely that he would not come, but then turned around and started packing his things, ultimately coming after them. Wei Yuzhi knew no one would welcome him here, but to get treatment for his illness, he had no choice but to shamelessly follow. Mo Sigui, fanning himself with a folding fan, said, “Ah Jiu, I abandoned all wealth and status to come find you for your treatment. Are you not moved?” Mo Sigui was only joking, but he had not expected An Jiu to suddenly rush over. He panicked slightly, not for any other reason than fear that Chu Dingjiang would find a secluded place to beat him up. But An Jiu’s enthusiasm was truly touching… He hesitated, his hands half-raised, half-closed. Unexpectedly, An Jiu pushed him aside, walked to the small mountain of medicine, and began tearing open the large and small bags. Everyone looked closely and saw that the small mountain contained Da Jiu. “Do not throw it away! Do not throw it away! That medicine is expensive! That medicine is extremely rare!” Mo Sigui, disregarding his image, tucked his fan behind his back and hurriedly began picking up the medicine. Da Jiu’s eyes welled with tears, filled with deep regret for not having come with An Jiu first. He should not have been tempted by Mo Sigui’s newly concocted poison. “Mo Sigui, you are utterly heartless! I think all you can do now is bully this idiot!” An Jiu said coldly after rescuing Da Jiu. Everyone was speechless, wondering if this was supposed to be protection. Luckily, Da Jiu could not understand human speech. Mo Sigui, clutching the medicine bag, argued, “Wei Yuzhi is seriously ill; I cannot let him carry me!” An Jiu scoffed, “How delicate are your hands? Your wife’s? You cannot bear to use them for anything other than masturbation!” “Who said I did not bring anything?” Mo Sigui threw the medicine bag on the ground and loosened his belt. Ling Ziyue silently covered Lou Xiaowu’s eyes. Lou Xiaowu was incredibly curious and kept pulling at his hand. “Look!” Mo Sigui pulled open his outer robe, revealing many pockets sewn inside, filled with various kinds of medicine. Zhu Pianxian, spitting out sunflower seed shells, said, “Divine Physician, we all know you always carry so much medicine with you.” Mo Sigui, exposed, turned to glare at her. Bang! Before he could turn his head, he was attacked by a palm-sized medicine packet. “You are childish!” Mo Sigui said indignantly. An Jiu, leading the swaggering Da Jiu with his backer, walked past him, casually tossing out, “Hurry up and put it on; do not ruin the island’s scenery. We are still pretending you are a man.” “Hey, explain yourself!” Mo Sigui said. Zhu Pianxian leaned against Sheng Changying’s chest, continuing her sarcastic remark, “Husband, you look refined and frail, but once you take your clothes off, you are worth two divine physicians!” Sheng Changying blushed slightly, turning his face away uncomfortably. “Do not talk nonsense.” Zhu Pianxian clung to his arm, saying sweetly, “Husband, do not be angry. I am not talking nonsense anymore; you are worth three!” Chu Dingjiang had never understood why An Jiu liked the pretentious Zhu Pianxian, but now he finally understood. One stabbed; the other finished him off, leaving no room for maneuver. “Arrange accommodations for Master Wei.” Although Chu Dingjiang was bothered by Wei Yuzhi’s arrival, he was not so petty as to be unable to tolerate the other person for even a moment because he had unwavering confidence in this relationship. Sui Yuntong stepped forward to accept the order. “Master Wei, please follow me.” Ling Ziyue lowered his hand, and as they brushed past each other, Lou Xiaowu finally saw Wei Yuzhi clearly and could not help but sigh. “So beautiful.” Wei Yuzhi paused slightly, turning his head slightly to nod at Ling Ziyue and Lou Xiaowu, revealing no other emotion, as if he had not recognized Ling Ziyue at all. In reality, no one here harbored deep hatred for Wei Yuzhi; it was merely a matter of differing stances leading to some mutual repulsion. Li Qingzhi was the most resistant, turning to Chu Dingjiang before Wei Yuzhi had gone far, saying, “My Lord! Why would the Divine Physician save a traitor and bring him to the island?” It was not a question, but rather dissatisfaction. Chu Dingjiang said, “This man serves the Liao Kingdom for a reason. If he can see things clearly, he would be a rare talent for the Song Dynasty. But…” Chu Dingjiang did not allow him to speak. “It depends on whether the new Emperor has the courage.” After all, he had once been a key minister under the Liao Emperor. In the Warring States period, this would not have been a problem. Which strategist did not move from one faction to another, choosing their path carefully before making a decision? It was normal. Now, things were much more rigid! Chu Dingjiang thought to himself. He would not attribute all the blame to Confucianism. Any single school of thought from the Warring States period, if taken as a model for the entire world, would have numerous problems. In times of peace, Confucianism, aligned with the Great Way, had flourished to this day; it was the choice made by the tide of history. “Dingjiang, His Majesty requests your return. What are your plans?” Sheng Changying asked. This letter could not be taken lightly. Chu Dingjiang faced only two paths: one, obediently return to accept orders; two, prepare to flee for his life. Chu Dingjiang thought that the reason he stepped down, besides seeing things more clearly, was probably because he could not accept this era of absolute monarchy. “I am used to freedom, and I do not like to grovel before people. Who knows, one day I might lose my temper and start cursing the Emperor. The Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods were much better in that respect.” Zhu Pianxian groaned, clutching her stomach. “Absolutely! With more businesses, everyone naturally puts in their best effort. Treating your employees well makes them more enthusiastic about serving customers and less likely to go elsewhere. If only one business remains, who cares about the rest!” “The words are common, but the meaning is profound,” Chu Dingjiang said. Seeing Sheng Changying nod, Zhu Pianxian could not help but pinch him. “Who’s common?” “I am common, I am common. The most remarkable thing I’ve ever done in my life is marrying My Lady.” Sheng Changying used to be a little embarrassed to say flirtatious things, but after discovering that Zhu Pianxian was particularly susceptible to them, he now spoke fluently, each sentence unique. Chu Dingjiang was amazed and began to ponder. He returned to the house, lost in thought. An Jiu was feeding Da Jiu the medicine Mo Sigui had prepared. She squatted on a chair, holding the pill in her hand, while Da Jiu lay on the ground like a dog, head tilted back, mouth agape, waiting to be fed. An Jiu glanced at it, then tossed it. The pill fell accurately down Da Jiu’s throat. “Awooo!” Da Jiu jumped up. Awooo! What had it missed? What had it missed? A faint taste of medicine lingered in its mouth, but it had not enjoyed it at all! After a moment of frustration, remembering that An Jiu still had some, it quickly lay down obediently, tilting its head back and opening its mouth. For the first time, a bright, shrewd light flashed in its tiger eyes. It was determined that this time, it would catch it. It! Must! Catch! It! An Jiu noticed Chu Dingjiang enter and initially did not pay much attention. But seeing him hesitate, as if he had something important to say, she dumped a handful of pills into Da Jiu’s mouth. Happiness came too suddenly. Driven by his foodie instincts, Da Jiu began chewing without even having a chance to savor it. Only after the pills had warmed his throat and entered his stomach did the tiger have time to think of reserving a little for later.

chapters.title: Retirement
chapters.content: The series of blows left Da Jiu motionless, staring blankly at the floor in front of its paws. Chu Dingjiang took out a handkerchief and handed it to An Jiu. She took it and wiped her hands. “What do you want to say?” Chu Dingjiang’s style of sweet talk differed from Sheng Changying’s. After thinking for a while, he decided to go for the “bitter memories” approach. So he took An Jiu’s hand and sincerely said an opening line, “Ah Jiu, it is so good to have met you in this life.” Perhaps because the atmosphere had not been properly built up, An Jiu paused, unsure how to react. Chu Dingjiang had initially wanted to say something like “I wish we could be together for life,” but upon reflection, he realized that saying that now would be too abrupt and seemed too sentimental. So he went straight to the point, “Do you remember the first time we met?” At that time, Chu Dingjiang had not intended to capture her alive and had no intention of harming An Jiu, while she had been ruthless in every move. An Jiu nodded. “Yeah, you came to arrest me, and I stabbed you.” “That is not the point.” Chu Dingjiang ignored the jarring remark. “I was astonished when I first met you. Despite having no internal energy, you were able to hold your own against a Transcendent Realm expert. Such peculiarity and excellence compel one to investigate.” “I know,” An Jiu replied, completely unaware of the concept of humility. Chu Dingjiang sighed, feeling the conversation was going nowhere, and continued, “Later, when the incident at Mei Mansion happened, I brought you out. You heard about the Mei Clan’s annihilation, but you remained calm and composed…” “I remember,” An Jiu nodded. “Later, I mustered all my strength and fought you, and it felt much better.” “That is not the point,” Chu Dingjiang said, patting her back and continuing, “The important thing is that at that moment, I suddenly discovered another side of you hidden behind your cold, bloodthirsty nature.” An Jiu stiffened for a moment, then relaxed, reaching out to wrap her arms around his waist. Chu Dingjiang felt a warmth in his heart, holding her close, and asked with a smile, “Do you remember when we fought our way out of the siege of Piaomiao Mountain Mansion together?” An Jiu remained silent. Chu Dingjiang knew she was lost in memories, so he did not rush to disturb her. After a moment, An Jiu said, “I killed eighty-nine experts.” So she’d been counting people all this time! “That is not the point,” Chu Dingjiang said, used to her being a professional “game-changer,” and continued, “What I want to say is, when we fought side by side, I knew you were the partner I was looking for.” An Jiu paused, frowning. “Because I can kill?” “No. Because seeing you fight like a madman, my heart ached, and I developed the desire to protect you for life.” It took Chu Dingjiang a while to understand that this was not pity, but love. The two had always been on different wavelengths, but on this issue, An Jiu strangely resonated with him. Because neither of them was particularly compassionate, it was only because they loved this person and cared about this person that they felt heartache. “I used to think a true man should aspire to rule the world. Even a beautiful woman by his side was merely an embellishment. But I do not know when it started; I changed,” Chu Dingjiang sighed. “I willingly put aside important matters just because I am afraid you will be in danger.” Later, he would even abandon things he once valued, just to see her once more, to spend a little more time with her. At first, he struggled. He felt himself becoming increasingly decadent; it was ridiculous that his lofty ambitions could not overcome the allure of a beautiful woman. However, it did not take long. He became content with his decadence. Giving up his ideals for a woman seemed cowardly, but Chu Dingjiang no longer cared. “With one woman by my side, what need is there for the world?” Chu Dingjiang said half-jokingly. “Chu Dingjiang, let’s go back,” An Jiu said. Chu Dingjiang paused slightly. “Is this alright?” An Jiu liked the sense of security Chu Dingjiang gave her, yet she could not bear to see him suppress his brilliance and become a free spirit. “I feel like you were born for intrigue.” “Ah Jiu, I am old,” Chu Dingjiang said softly. “My heart is old.” This was the generation gap between them. An Jiu was just beginning to search for the meaning of life, while Chu Dingjiang had already experienced the vicissitudes of life. From the very beginning of his rebirth, Chu Dingjiang felt no joy in being reborn. Wealth, status, family—he discarded them all so easily. He deceived himself into believing he could let go of everything and start anew, but in reality, his heart was still full of resentment, feeling that his sacrifices in his previous life were not worthwhile. Everything he did was purely instinctive, driven by an unwillingness to accept defeat; the youthful passion had long since subsided. If he had been born in the Warring States period, Chu Dingjiang would surely have sought to turn the tide for himself. However, time had passed, and the past was irreversible. Looking back at the history from the Warring States period to the Liao and Song dynasties, he seemed to see through the unseen laws governing the rise and fall of dynasties. Even the most brilliant strategies could only become fleeting ripples in the long river of history, leaving him feeling utterly disillusioned. Until he met An Jiu, he gradually felt a renewed vitality. Rebirth, truly beginning from this moment, perhaps many years later, would reignite his fighting spirit? But now, he genuinely wanted to let go of everything, take his beloved woman, invite a few close friends, and immerse himself in nature to truly experience the world with a carefree and relaxed mindset—only then would he have lived a worthwhile life. He did not voice these thoughts because even if he described them clearly, those who had not experienced them would not truly understand. “But I…” An Jiu did not know how to express her inner thoughts. Chu Dingjiang gently stroked her hair, his gaze tender. “Let me guess…you must not have lived long in your past life.” An Jiu nodded. “Your killing skills are not something you acquired in three or five years. You must have spent your past life either undergoing brutal training or killing.” Chu Dingjiang’s tone softened further as he spoke. It could be said that, besides honing her skills, An Jiu’s past life was essentially wasted. She was merely a killing machine, devoid of her own identity. Those memories steeped in blood made her heart different from that of ordinary people. If she wanted to live a normal life, she first needed to find herself, to become a normal person, and to experience what normal people should experience. They, one in the twilight of their lives and the other at the dawn of a new day, were both at the juncture of night and day, were they not? Chu Dingjiang remained optimistic. “Do what you want to do. I will always be by your side. I also have things I want to do; they do not conflict.” “Since you like it, that is good.” An Jiu’s eyes shone brightly as she thought about what she wanted to do in the future. “I want to rebuild the Dragon Martial Guards.” The worry on Chu Dingjiang’s face vanished instantly, and he calmly asked, “Why?” “After hearing about the Dragon Martial Guards, I found it very interesting, and it is the only thing I can do well.” An Jiu thought it over; organizing a force and stopping it with force were different. “I want to be a good person, the officially recognized kind.” Hearing that she was not influenced by the lingering thoughts in Gu Jinghong’s blood, Chu Dingjiang breathed a slight sigh of relief. “Alright, do your best, but before that, quickly settle the bounty list matter.” “Alright,” An Jiu said. “Do you want me to come with you?” Chu Dingjiang asked. An Jiu shook her head. Chu Dingjiang was a little dissatisfied. “We should have found someone to do the job right away.” Chu Dingjiang was very busy at the time, which delayed things for a while. Later, An Jiu suddenly wanted to do it herself. He looked at it and saw it was not a big task, so he readily left it to her to handle. Now, thinking about it, he felt a little regretful. Thinking about it, Chu Dingjiang suddenly felt embarrassed. Was he not just saying sweet nothings? “Oh, right, I promised Sui Yuntong I’d help him find a wife. He likes someone a bit feisty. Anyway, you’ve had some free time lately; why not help with that?” An Jiu had a new plan, but she was still thinking about the “task” she had not been able to complete.

chapters.title: Drunkenness
chapters.content: Chu Dingjiang never expected that after retiring from the political stage, he would have to work part-time as a matchmaker! However, since it was An Jiu’s request, he did not refuse. The sweet talk ended there, but Chu Dingjiang was not too bothered; there would be plenty of opportunities later. He wanted to ask a question right now: “Can you explain ‘masturbation’?” “It’s just…” Chu Dingjiang quickly covered her mouth. “Never mind, I knew you’d be so blunt.” Even the fun of teasing was gone; how sad. An Jiu had finally learned to read his expressions. Seeing that his mood was a little off, she tentatively asked, “Are you unhappy?” For someone as carefree as her to care about his feelings, what more could he ask for? Chu Dingjiang reached out and touched her face. “No, Ah Jiu, no matter what happens, remember I will always be by your side.” “Mm.” A gentle smile appeared on An Jiu’s face. Knock knock knock! “Ah Jiu!” Mo Sigui shouted from outside the door. “Come in,” Chu Dingjiang said. The door was not bolted. Mo Sigui pushed open the door, carrying a large jar of wine. “Today’s a good day; let’s have some to celebrate!” He winked at Chu Dingjiang, smiled, and left, not forgetting to close the door behind him. “Did you have him prepare this?” An Jiu had naturally noticed Mo Sigui’s little gesture. “No.” Chu Dingjiang watched An Jiu unseal the jar. “Unsolicited kindness is always suspicious.” The aroma of the wine wafted through the air, carrying a faint floral scent, like plum blossoms and orchids, with a hint of milkiness. The smell did not quite resemble wine; it was more like a dessert infused with alcohol, incredibly tempting. “Then you do not drink it, I will drink it! If anything happens to me, you will avenge me!” An Jiu said righteously, picking up the jar and taking a large gulp. The intoxicating aroma lingered on her lips and teeth. First, she tasted the rich milkiness; then, the aroma of wine; and finally, a delicate plum and orchid fragrance remained in her mouth. An Jiu squinted, like a fox stealing a bite. Chu Dingjiang could not help but chuckle. “Try a sip,” An Jiu said, handing him the jar. Chu Dingjiang could roughly guess what Mo Sigui wanted to do, so he only took a sip. “Not bad; drink more.” Mo Sigui seemed unreliable, but in the medical field, he was absolutely measured. He would not harm An Jiu; he just wanted to get her drunk. An Jiu almost always caused a ruckus when she was drunk, but last time she was surprisingly quiet. Mo Sigui had always wanted to understand if her mental illness had stabilized because of his efforts. Chu Dingjiang also wanted to know. The delicious taste tempted her to drink one sip after another, and soon the jar was empty, her cheeks flushed. Frowning, she complained to Chu Dingjiang, “This jar is too small; let’s go ask him for another one.” “Ah Jiu,” Chu Dingjiang knew she was drunk, so he pulled her into his arms. An Jiu found a comfortable position and lay still. After a long silence, Chu Dingjiang heard a soft snoring sound beside him. Mo Sigui peeked out furtively and whispered, “Is she drunk?” Chu Dingjiang nodded. “She’s asleep.” Drunk and yet sleeping peacefully? “Then I will go back first.” Mo Sigui could not wait to get Wei Yuzhi drunk. The wine was personally mixed by Mo Sigui, and it had a therapeutic effect on the spirit. However, Wei Yuzhi was too weak to drink too much. Fortunately, Mo Sigui had gotten reliable information from Sheng Changying that Wei Yuzhi was a “two-cup wonder,” so getting him drunk would not take much effort. Mo Sigui, carrying the wine jar and humming a little tune, went to the library. The island’s library had once been the second matriarch’s private study. The second matriarch did not like reading, but she enjoyed indulging in refined pursuits, and the library contained quite a few books. The most remarkable thing about this small building was not its book collection, but its structure. From the outside, it appeared to be two stories high. However, upon entering, one would find it was only one story. A terrace surrounded the building, offering panoramic views of the vast, misty lake. Crystal windows connected the interior to the exterior, allowing light to filter through and often creating rainbows. Sometimes, sitting here felt like being in a fairyland. When Mo Sigui entered, he saw Wei Yuzhi standing in the center of the room, gazing up at the crystal windows. Moonlight bathed him in a hazy glow, his flowing blue robe and snow-white hair shimmering with iridescent light, giving him an ethereal, otherworldly appearance, yet also an undeniable air of loneliness. Mo Sigui hesitated, unable to bear breaking the silence. Wei Yuzhi turned and saw him, nodding slightly. “Divine Physician.” Mo Sigui then walked in, waving the wine bowl in his hand. “Want a cup?” “Can I drink?” Wei Yuzhi asked. Mo Sigui sat down on the floor, setting out the wine bowl. “Yes, this is a specially prepared wine, with many benefits.” Wei Yuzhi also sat down, his white hair cascading down his back to the dark blue-green floor. “A rough earthenware bowl, please make do,” Mo Sigui said. The milky white liquid poured into the yellowish-brown bowl, easily arousing the desire to drink. Mo Sigui watched Wei Yuzhi’s slender, pale fingers pick up the wine bowl, simple yet elegant. “Please,” Mo Sigui said. “Please.” Wei Yuzhi lowered his head and took a sip. It did not have the pungent, harsh taste he remembered; instead, it was incredibly smooth and fragrant, not at all like alcohol. “I never expected the Divine Physician’s bartending skills to be so superb.” Mo Sigui smacked his lips. “Of course, you do not drink often, do you?” “I’ve only drunk alcohol twice in my life,” Wei Yuzhi replied. Mo Sigui was a little puzzled. Wei Yuzhi, with such a low alcohol tolerance, had drunk without hesitation. Curious, he asked, “Never been drunk?” “Yes, I have.” But being drunk or not made little difference to him. “The point of drinking is to reach a state of slight intoxication. What’s the point if you are not drunk? Come on, bottoms up!” Mo Sigui raised his bowl. Wei Yuzhi smiled, tilted his head back, and drank it all. This drink tasted like sweet soup, but it was actually more intoxicating than strong liquor because it contained drugs to accelerate the effects. These drugs had little effect on Mo Sigui, who drank the bowl without hesitation. A faint blush crept onto Wei Yuzhi’s pale cheeks, making him seem even more approachable. Seeing that his eyes remained clear, Mo Sigui offered him another bowl of wine. After two bowls, Wei Yuzhi’s face turned even redder, with fine beads of sweat appearing on his nose and temples. Mo Sigui thought to himself, “Was he not supposed to have a low alcohol tolerance? Why is he not showing any signs of drunkenness? Could Sheng Changying’s information be wrong?” “I am drunk,” Wei Yuzhi said, smiling slightly. “Do you believe me?” Before Mo Sigui could answer, he collapsed to the floor with a thud. The wine bowl slid down his sleeve, making a dull thud against the thick fabric, but it did not shatter. “Huh?” Mo Sigui was speechless. He’s already unconscious?! He was perfectly fine just a moment ago! “Wei Yuzhi?” Mo Sigui poked him, not noticing Chu Dingjiang standing behind him. He looked just like An Jiu—so quiet, so sudden. Chu Dingjiang frowned deeply. He had not realized that his hard work had affected An Jiu to this extent…

chapters.title: A Man Is In His Prime At Forty
chapters.content: Love and romance were only a small part of An Jiu’s life. Although she and Chu Dingjiang had consummated their marriage, she was still quite naive about matters of the heart. Chu Dingjiang understood her and knew he had plenty of time to penetrate her life, so he was not in a hurry. Since the day he had those heart-to-heart talks with An Jiu, Chu Dingjiang had truly devoted himself to being a retired old cadre, spending his days watching the snow and flowers, playing the zither and weiqi, and keeping hawks and tigers company. Under his care, An Jiu was getting fatter and fatter, her figure rapidly heading towards that of a pig. That day, after finishing her breakfast, An Jiu sat by the stove, playing with a human-faced pendant while thinking about the reorganization of the Dragon Martial Guards. Her gaze fell on Chu Dingjiang by the window. He was feeding a hungry eaglet with a handful of bait, his head bowed. He wore a wide-sleeved, azure robe, the white collar of which accentuated his long neck. His profile was as handsome as mountains and rivers, and his wet hair was half-draped over his back, leaving a water stain. They had known each other for so long, yet she had only seen Chu Dingjiang this clean and tidy twice. Chu Dingjiang’s temperament was quite different from that of people of his time. He possessed a more untamed spirit than Wei Yuzhi’s refined manners and a more meticulous attention to detail than Ling Ziyue’s ruggedness. Even when he was quietly reading, exuding a scholarly air, his overall presence commanded respect. “Handsome?” Chu Dingjiang could feel An Jiu’s intense gaze even without looking up. An Jiu nodded honestly. “It’s beautiful.” Honesty could hurt, but it also had its advantages. After feeding the eaglets, Chu Dingjiang took out a handkerchief and wiped his hands clean. “What are you thinking about?” His movements were natural and elegant, but An Jiu was not quite used to it. In her memory, Chu Dingjiang was a man like a monument, casual in life, calm, and sharp-witted, yet gentle only towards her. However, upon closer reflection, she could see from some details that Chu Dingjiang was not a carefree person. An Jiu brushed aside her sudden thoughts and answered, “I am thinking about how to reorganize the Dragon Martial Guards.” “That is not difficult.” Chu Dingjiang sat down and poured himself a cup of tea. An Jiu stared at his long, strong hands, the flowing sleeves revealing a gentle strength within his rigidity. Why could even pouring water look so beautiful? Chu Dingjiang put down the kettle, raised the cup, and took a sip. An Jiu’s gaze followed his movements to his slightly moving Adam’s apple. When he put down his teacup, his lips glistened faintly; An Jiu felt inexplicably thirsty. Seeing her swallow, Chu Dingjiang poured her a cup as well. She did not drink but instead leaned in and licked his lips. “Ah Jiu…” Chu Dingjiang was somewhat surprised, reaching out to embrace her waist and returning the kiss deeply. Their lips and tongues intertwined, but after the kiss ended, they did not go any deeper, only lingering close for a while. An Jiu was not the shy type; if she needed something, she would be very proactive, regardless of whether it was daytime! And now, she clearly only wanted a simple kiss, so even though Chu Dingjiang was already aroused, he did not force it. For him, this small intimacy was even more precious. Their eyes met, and Chu Dingjiang silently questioned. An Jiu understood and said, “You look so beautiful like this. Why did I not notice it last time?” She was confused, but Chu Dingjiang understood perfectly. An Jiu was not the type to be smitten by looks. When her feelings were not deep, he might look no different from Hua Rongjian or Mo Sigui. But as her feelings deepened, she noticed more and more about him. This was a good sign; Chu Dingjiang smiled broadly. “I suddenly remembered a proverb I heard in my past life,” this was one of the few proverbs An Jiu knew. “Hmm?” Chu Dingjiang could not hide his smile. An Jiu said, “A man is in his prime at forty.” Chu Dingjiang was speechless, completely unprepared for her conclusion! He was too lazy to emphasize that he was only in his twenties. Seeing that the topic had reached this point, Chu Dingjiang wisely chose to return to the starting point to avoid being stabbed in the back again: “Tell me about your plan to rebuild the Dragon Martial Guards.” An Jiu suddenly remembered this important matter! “It sounds simple, but I do not want to be controlled by the court, and I want to become an officially recognized organization.” An Jiu did not want to act entirely on orders without any room for objection; she wanted to have her own stance. When An Jiu first used this term, Chu Dingjiang thought she wanted to return to serve the court. Although he did not quite understand, he unconditionally supported her. Only now did he realize that “official certification” did not mean that. “You mean you want to create an organization that does not need to hide and is recognized by the court?” In other words, the Dragon Martial Guards she wanted to organize was not a hidden assassin organization but an organization that could be recognized by the court as righteous. “That is indeed difficult,” Chu Dingjiang said, tapping his finger lightly on the table. “The court will not tolerate private forces among the common people. However, I have a method you can consider.” An Jiu’s eyes lit up. “I knew you had a way! How do you suggest I go about it?” Chu Dingjiang said, “Find a reliable person to be sent to a post outside the capital, and you will send him to train local soldiers for the government.”

chapters.title: The Tanhua
chapters.content: “I trust you the most,” An Jiu said. Although Chu Dingjiang was pleased to hear this, it was clearly impossible. “My appearance is too similar to Hua Rongtian’s. If I show my face in Bianjing, it will inevitably cause unnecessary trouble. Disguise and a beard will not solve the problem; the truth will eventually come out.” The Emperor had many capable people around him; it was absolutely impossible to deceive him with clumsy methods. “I not only know a lot about the palace coup, but I also orchestrated part of it. The Emperor will not let me off the hook.” “He needs you now; why would he be in such a hurry to kill you?” An Jiu knew that the Song Dynasty was currently in dire need of talent; why would the Emperor be wary of abandoning such a talented person? Chu Dingjiang said, “The current situation seems promising, but the Emperor has only just weakened the Hua family’s power; how could he allow another force to rise?” The Song Dynasty had many prestigious families, but none possessed the overwhelming power of the Hua family, which supported a large part of the country. The new Emperor paid a heavy price for weakening the Hua clan. Imagine the consequences of suddenly removing a few load-bearing pillars from a building! He needed his trusted confidants to take the lead, and these confidants had to be independent, without powerful families behind them. Chu Dingjiang met this condition, but he controlled a portion of the Konghe Army. Even if he disbanded them, the Emperor would believe he had the ability to recall them. Based on this alone, the Emperor was unlikely to trust him with full authority. “I do have a suitable candidate,” Chu Dingjiang said. An Jiu did not know many court officials, and after much thought, she could not think of anyone suitable. “Who?” “Wu Lingyuan.” “Him?” An Jiu had a strong impression of this man: a blind, impoverished scholar who eked out a living with a run-down, rarely visited wonton stall yet was remarkably calm and collected. Chu Dingjiang said, “Hua Rongjian had his blindness cured and used his connections to get him into the imperial examinations, where he became a Tanhua30.” If it were not for someone’s recommendation, Wu Lingyuan would have had to pass the prefectural examination first. Hua Rongjian originally intended for him to test the waters first and then retake the exam after passing the prefectural one. Unexpectedly, Wu Lingyuan proved himself capable; after recovering his eyesight, he only studied intermittently for a few months and actually passed! He then performed exceptionally well in the palace examination and was personally selected by the Emperor as the Tanhua. Wu Lingyuan wanted to test his abilities, so he did his best in the exams. After all, he had been blind for many years and had no opportunity to continue his studies; even he himself had not expected to pass with such high honors. However, this was not entirely a happy event for him. Not participating in the prefectural examination could not be hidden from others. Everyone knew he had powerful backers, and they could not help but suspect that his third-ranked scholar title was fabricated. This would make him a target of public criticism and an indelible stain on his official career. He would have opportunities to prove his abilities in the future, but the key was whether he would even have those opportunities! After explaining the situation to An Jiu in detail, Chu Dingjiang added, “This matter has already reached the Emperor’s ears. If we investigate further, it will inevitably expose Hua Rongjian behind it all, which would be even more fatal for Wu Lingyuan.” Hua Rongjian held no official position; how could he have gotten this special treatment? Was he connected to the Hua family? Did the Hua family form cliques with other officials? These questions were unavoidable. Chu Dingjiang said, “The best way is to overshadow this with a bigger incident. If he requests to be transferred to a county magistrate position under the jurisdiction of Hejian Prefecture, the Emperor should agree.” Hejian Prefecture was located on the border between the Liao and Song, and was constantly embroiled in war. In the past ten years alone, not only county magistrates, but even prefects had been killed by the Liao. Everyone avoided it like the plague. An Jiu thought about it; that place was indeed very suitable for development! Because of the need to deal with Liao attacks, the number of soldiers in the Hebei Circuit was greater than in other places. “It’s good, but is Wu Lingyuan willing to go and die?” An Jiu asked. “He will be willing to go; fortune favors the bold. If he can defend a county now, he will be a hero. He will definitely have many concerns, like what are his chances of winning? Is it worth the risk?” Chu Dingjiang took out a jade token and gave it to her. “I can recall the disbanded Konghe Army. You take these men and lend him a hand, and he will naturally go!” An Jiu did not accept it. She knew very well that those people only trusted and respected Chu Dingjiang; no one else could control them. “I do not want this. I want you with me.” If she were to take over, she would have to conquer them, not rely on Chu Dingjiang’s token to intimidate them. “Alright,” Chu Dingjiang replied. “These people all come from the Konghe Academy; none of them are from the four great families. They grew up in bloodshed and should share your ideals.” No wonder Chu Dingjiang was so familiar with the Konghe Academy! An Jiu asked suspiciously, “Sheng Changying is in cahoots with you, is he not?” Chu Dingjiang flicked her head with his finger. “He’s helped me a lot. Sometimes I’d meet people with good potential, and he would pass me their information. I then secretly trained them so I could recruit them for my own use.” An Jiu nodded, thinking of Wu Lingyuan and worrying, “What exactly is Hua Rongjian’s motive for going to such lengths to train Wu Lingyuan?” Since learning that Hua Rongjian secretly controlled the bounty list, An Jiu understood that he was no longer the wayward young master he used to be. She did not believe that Hua Rongjian’s painstaking efforts to help Wu Lingyuan were purely out of loyalty.

chapters.title: Playing with Birds
chapters.content: Even Hua Rongjian himself probably could not say whether he had any ulterior motives. If it was to gain strength to kill Chu Dingjiang and avenge himself, what about everything he had enjoyed in the Hua family over the years? His father treated him absolutely as a legitimate son. Regardless of whether his stepmother knew the truth or was kept in the dark, recalling their time together, Hua Rongjian could not deny that her love for him was genuine. To change everything he had now for a concubine would be an unwise choice. However, she was, after all, his birth mother. If he simply pretended it never happened, he could not get over it. Chu Dingjiang understood Hua Rongjian’s feelings, which was why he could not answer An Jiu’s question accurately. He only said, “As long as there are common interests, even enemies can become allies.” An Jiu asked, “What if he wants revenge on you?” So that was what she was worried about! Chu Dingjiang asked with a smile, “If he retaliates against me, how do you plan to deal with it?” An Jiu’s expressionless face slowly crumpled. “I will not let you face that day.” Chu Dingjiang patted her head. “Go find Wu Lingyuan.” He knew An Jiu did not have many friends. She usually liked to be sarcastic and seemed arrogant, looking down on everyone, but in reality, she valued and cherished people deeply. If Hua Rongjian really wanted revenge on Chu Dingjiang, although she was certain she would side with him, she could not bring herself to harm Hua Rongjian. “What do you mean?” An Jiu asked worriedly. “Whether he seeks revenge or not is not something you can control.” “Do I look like the kind of person who’s easily killed?” Chu Dingjiang fiddled with the daffodils he’d recently grown. “Go quickly and come back quickly.” “Alright, I will be back later.” An Jiu waved the human-faced pendant in her hand, telling him she had to deal with the bounty list that night. “Alright.” Chu Dingjiang seemed reassured, put a fur coat on her, and then stood with his hands behind his back on the porch, watching her leave. Only after she was out of sight did Chu Dingjiang return to the house and sit cross-legged on the low couch to stroke Da Jiu’s fur. Da Jiu fawned over Chu Dingjiang, gently resting its large head on his lap. It squinted its eyes, feigning ecstasy. In its heart, this man was its biggest meal ticket, and it had to cling to him! “Hmm…” Chu Dingjiang hesitated for a moment, then suddenly got up and went to the screen to retrieve his black cloak. Because he got up too quickly, his knee bumped into Da Jiu’s chin, startling the tiger. “Let’s go.” Chu Dingjiang, now completely cloaked, bent down and patted Da Jiu’s head. An Jiu had already gone far away, and Chu Dingjiang could not track her, but no matter where she was, Da Jiu could always pinpoint her location. Uncle Chu was conflicted. He felt he was becoming a lazy, unambitious man. He could not just become a leech, sticking to An Jiu every second. However, after much deliberation, he still did not feel comfortable letting An Jiu go out alone. Secretly following her would not be a problem, right? He grabbed the dazed Da Jiu, and the two of them followed her off the island. An Jiu did not know Wu Lingyuan’s whereabouts, so she went to the Hua residence to find Hua Rongjian first. Their parting with a letter had left Hua Rongjian feeling disappointed for quite some time. Seeing her return, he suppressed his excitement. Sipping wine in the warm pavilion, he said coolly, “At least you still have some conscience.” An Jiu ignored this meaningless remark, sat down casually, and said, “I mainly came to ask you where Wu Lingyuan lives.” “Wu Lingyuan?” Hua Rongjian scoffed. “What do you want with him?” An Jiu thought for a moment and decided to tell him her plan, since Hua Rongjian was behind Wu Lingyuan. He would find out sooner or later. “I heard he’s been in trouble lately. I have a mutually beneficial plan I’d like to discuss with him.” Hua Rongjian raised an eyebrow with interest. An Jiu was not a cunning person; the so-called mutually beneficial scheme was mostly the idea of ​​the shrewd old fox Chu Dingjiang by her side, and she had to be wary. “Tell me about it,” she said. An Jiu nodded. “You and Wu Lingyuan are birds of a feather; I can tell you.” Hua Rongjian’s face darkened. “You cannot use that word! He and I are friends!” “Something like that. As a man, you should not be so fussy about small details; it is not good,” An Jiu sincerely advised, then, without giving him a chance to object, continued, “Have him request a posting to Hejian Prefecture. I will take men to protect him, on the condition that they will be given some positions as city guards after he becomes an official.” Hua Rongjian’s expression turned serious. “You want to create an army? Is this your own idea or Chu Dingjiang’s?” “He’s already planning to retire at home; of course, it is my idea,” An Jiu said. “Retirement?” Hua Rongjian scoffed. “What kind of retirement is he talking about? He’s only in his twenties! He’s just trying to fool you!” As he said this, he completely ignored the fact that he had just mentally labeled Chu Dingjiang as “cunning and treacherous.” An Jiu frowned. “Can you not be a little more honest? He’s at home playing with birds and walking his tiger; he would not have time for this!” “Pfft!” Hua Rongjian could not help but burst out laughing. “Playing with birds?” “Let’s get down to business,” An Jiu said sternly. “Alright! Let’s get down to business!” Hearing that Chu Dingjiang was at home playing with birds, Hua Rongjian’s mood inexplicably improved. “I’ve thought about this, and it is indeed a good idea. Come on, I will take you to find him!” Joking aside, Hua Rongjian was quite efficient when it came to business. He immediately ordered a carriage to be prepared. The carriage stopped directly at the second gate. Hua Rongjian got in first, then turned back to offer An Jiu a hand. An Jiu looked up at his handsome profile, his smile as dazzling as the sun yet as chilling as early spring. She no longer longed for this version of Hua Rongjian. “I can get in.” “Fine.” He withdrew his hand and got into the carriage first, showing no embarrassment. They had shared a carriage several times. “I always feel a little uneasy riding with you.” An Jiu looked at him, her eyes questioning. “Do you not remember how horribly we fought?” Hua Rongjian reminisced fondly, recalling his feelings at the time. “Hmph.” An Jiu sighed, giving him a proper lesson in the world. “You, a fourth-level martial artist, fighting a woman with no internal energy—what’s there to be uneasy about? You’ve been a bit twisted lately. Do not disbelieve me; I am very experienced in this area.” Hua Rongjian was speechless for a long time. “Also, actually, Chu Dingjiang is not as bad as you think. How much do you know about what happened back then?” An Jiu asked. Hua Rongjian’s expression turned indifferent. “He killed someone; what else is there to know?” “As far as I know, he only went to talk to your birth mother about your future, and she chose to pave a bright future for you,” An Jiu said. After all, it happened more than a decade ago, and the clues left behind were extremely scarce. Hua Rongjian had spent a lot of effort to find out even a tiny bit of information, so this was naturally the first time he had heard of this. “Then…did she choose to commit suicide?”

chapters.title: You Are a Real Man
chapters.content: “I do not know the specifics; I only know that your birth mother expressed this wish.” Even if An Jiu was intentionally trying to gain favor with Chu Dingjiang, she could not bring herself to lie. Hua Rongjian understood her, but still sneered, “Whatever he says goes?” “To be honest, he has no reason to lie to gain your favor. Even if it is a blood feud, he can bear it,” An Jiu said. She always focused on objectivity, never on phrasing. Hua Rongjian, already extremely depressed, suddenly flared up upon hearing this. “When have you ever stopped telling the truth? Yes, I am an insignificant ant; he does not need to care about me, but can you guarantee that he did not say these things to preserve his image as a good person in your eyes?” “You think he’s a good person?” An Jiu asked, quite surprised. “What’s so good about him?” Hua Rongjian said angrily. “Even you can tell he’s not a good person; I am not blind.” An Jiu thought he was really going crazy; his logic was starting to crumble. “Then why do you think he’s wasting his energy maintaining this image?” Hua Rongjian said, “I think he’s not a good person because I have a grudge against him, but he might not be bad in your eyes. If he were bad, why are you with him?” “He’s very good to me; does that prove he’s a good person?” An Jiu retorted. Hua Rongjian was speechless and could only roll his eyes, ignoring her. An Jiu asked curiously, “How can someone like that manage the bounty board?” “What kind of person am I?” Hua Rongjian said irritably. “Naive.” The carriage stopped, and a servant’s respectful voice came from outside, “My Lord, we’ve arrived.” An Jiu immediately glared at him. Such a short distance, and they still took a carriage? They would have arrived long ago if they had time to get on and off! Seeing her displeasure, Hua Rongjian grinned. Wu Lingyuan had recently passed the imperial examination and was not yet officially appointed, so he was temporarily residing in a small courtyard next to the Hua residence. An Jiu noticed that the entire street was lined with wealthy families. The sudden appearance of a small courtyard here piqued her curiosity. Hua Rongjian, observing her expression, explained, “Our mansion has a traditional Jiangnan-style courtyard layout, with no formal walls separating the courtyards. This small courtyard used to belong to our family, but it was specially separated to prevent the tutor from accidentally offending the women.” However, Hua Rongtian’s generation suddenly became small, with only their eldest daughter. They usually hired a female tutor, and Prime Minister Hua and Hua Rongtian would occasionally teach her themselves when they had free time, so there was no need for a private tutor. Therefore, the courtyard became vacant and was given to Wu Lingyuan. An Jiu said, “Rumors are circulating that Wu Lingyuan’s Tanhua title was manipulated by the Hua family. Why are you letting him stay here so openly?” “If someone wants to investigate, even if I hide it well, the truth will be revealed. It is better to admit it openly,” Hua Rongjian said, laughing. “I asked my elder brother to take Lingyuan as his disciple.” Hua Rongtian, at a young age, had already risen to a third-rank official, a unique talent in the dynasty. As his disciple, it was not surprising that he had achieved such remarkable success. While the two were talking, a servant knocked on the door. Hua Rongjian, without waiting for an announcement, went straight in with An Jiu. Just as they crossed the threshold, Wu Lingyuan strode over. Upon seeing Hua Rongjian, he stopped and bowed respectfully from a distance. “Lingyuan, what are you doing?” Hua Rongjian strode forward and helped him up. Everything Hua Rongjian had given Wu Lingyuan was worthy of gratitude, even kneeling in thanks. Even though he had become indifferent to many things, he was still grateful for this opportunity to display his talents and ambitions. He cherished and was grateful to the person who gave him this opportunity. Hua Rongjian said, “This is the female benefactor you’ve been talking about all day. How come you cannot recognize her even when she’s right in front of you?” “Ah!” Only then did Wu Lingyuan dare to look at An Jiu. Just now, he saw Hua Rongjian bring in a beautiful woman, and thinking she was his confidante, he felt it would not be appropriate to stare at her face, so he only glanced at her from afar. At such close range, he immediately saw a pair of bright, jade-like eyes, but upon closer inspection, he could only see dark pupils like black lacquer, filled with a cold, murderous aura, and no longer could he find that fleeting beauty. “Benefactor!” Wu Lingyuan came to his senses and bowed deeply again. An Jiu glanced down at him. “You do not need to do this. Today, I will get my money back with interest.” These words left Wu Lingyuan no room for refusal. Hua Rongjian felt a bitter taste on his tongue and could not help but feel even more jealous of Chu Dingjiang. He knew An Jiu fairly well. Although her words were sometimes harsh, she was not the type to speak without thinking. She considered Wu Lingyuan’s wonton stall one of her few quiet places, occasionally going there to eat wontons and find a moment of relaxation. She rarely said anything sharp. The reason she spoke so bluntly today was simply that Wu Lingyuan had chosen his side, siding with him, while he and Chu Dingjiang were enemies. Wu Lingyuan wore a gentle smile, as warm as a spring breeze. His once empty, blind eyes now held a sparkle, adding to his charm. “If there’s anything I can do to help, Lingyuan will certainly do my utmost.” An Jiu glanced at his still nonchalant smile and could not help but ask, “Are you telling me to die?” “My benefactor will not,” Wu Lingyuan said firmly, as if stating a fact he had already confirmed. An Jiu did not know where his confidence came from, nor did she want to waste any more time trying to find out. If they had the opportunity to go to Hejian together in the future, there would be plenty of time to understand him. Though small, the courtyard was fully equipped with a study, guest rooms, and a kitchen. The three went directly into the study to discuss matters. Knowing An Jiu was not much of a talker, Hua Rongjian first gave a general overview of the situation, then tilted his head and asked, “Is there anything I’ve omitted?” “That is exactly it,” An Jiu nodded. “I agree,” Wu Lingyuan answered almost without hesitation. Hua Rongjian reminded him, “Lingyuan is not just doing this to repay a debt of gratitude, is he?” “No,” Wu Lingyuan seemed to breathe a sigh of relief. “Given the current situation, if I stay in Bianjing, I will at most achieve a lowly official position for life. I’d like to be transferred to the vicinity of Hejian, but I worry that I am too weak to even kill a chicken; I might not return. Luckily, my benefactor has arrived! She’s my lucky star.” “Then it is settled. The rest is up to you,” An Jiu glanced at Hua Rongjian. If Wu Lingyuan had not been there, he would have yelled, “Why do you act so entitled?!” But then he thought, Wu Lingyuan was the first person he’d tried to win over, so he should indeed cover for her; after all, he was not losing out. “Let’s go have a meal together now that we’ve settled things.” Hua Rongjian secretly winked at Wu Lingyuan, signaling him not to come along. Wu Lingyuan then said, “I should treat my benefactor to a meal, but I have urgent business to attend to today…” “How busy can a disgraced scholar like you be?” An Jiu said coldly, then glanced at Hua Rongjian, “So much trouble for a meal! So effeminate.” With that, she turned and left. The first part of her words was directed at Wu Lingyuan, the second part clearly stemming from noticing Hua Rongjian’s subtle actions. Two gleaming throwing knives were firmly embedded in their hearts. For a moment, both were speechless. “You are the only real man here!” Hua Rongjian angrily chased after her. Wu Lingyuan hesitated for a moment, then had no choice but to follow.

chapters.title: An Jiu’s Gift
chapters.content: The three traveled by carriage to the most famous restaurant in Bianjing, a place known for its fine wines, delicious food, and beautiful women. However, this was a place for the refined and wealthy to indulge in. While there were beautiful women, they were not there to sell their smiles; they merely served drinks. These women were specially trained experts, skilled in brewing, boiling, and warming wine, and knowledgeable in the best and most elegant way to drink each type. Hua Rongjian was a regular customer. As soon as he entered, an attendant greeted him with a smile, “Second Master Hua, would you like Xin-niang to serve you drinks?” Hearing this, Hua Rongjian glanced at An Jiu’s face. Seeing no reaction from her, he felt relieved but also disappointed. For a fleeting moment, he recalled the times he and his cronies had drunk with women in brothels. His friend’s wife had ordered an attendant to tell him directly in front of a group of patrons: “Go home immediately, or you will be kneeling in the ancestral hall and repenting to your ancestors.” He had led a group of people to mock that man mercilessly, but now he wanted An Jiu to do the same to him. Snapping out of his daze, Hua Rongjian thought to himself that he must be crazy—how could he have such an absurd thought! An Jiu stood on the stairs, turning to look at him. “Are you coming or not?!” “What’s the rush?” Hua Rongjian strode after her. Whispers began to circulate in the lobby. “Judging by Second Master Hua’s erratic behavior, could this be the woman who abandoned him?” “She’s truly beautiful. No wonder Second Master Hua is so infatuated and does not like men anymore…” Since the “carriage sex” incident and the “Hua Rongjian’s declaration of marriage” incident, nothing had happened. Those who had been eagerly awaiting the outcome were still clueless. Someone had seen Hua Rongjian drinking alone, looking dejected, and many rumors began to circulate. Some said Hua Rongjian had been abandoned by a woman, while others said there was no such woman at all, and it was merely an excuse for Hua Rongjian to openly engage in homosexual relationships…There were all sorts of rumors, but the explanations were all far-fetched. As Hua Rongjian gradually faded from public view, these unfounded speculations gradually disappeared from conversation. Gossipmongers were the most “forgetful,” easily distracted by many things. In the past year or two, they had almost forgotten about Hua Rongjian. “I only recently found this quiet place,” Hua Rongjian explained after sitting down. An Jiu nodded, quickly drawn to the dishes on the table. Ignoring them, she picked up her chopsticks, sniffed them, and popped them into her mouth. Just as her mouth was full of food, someone gently knocked on the door of the private room. When Hua Rongjian responded, a woman in a light blue silk dress entered, her head bowed.
