She was slender and graceful, her black hair half-tied up with a sandalwood hairpin. An Jiu’s first impression of her was that she was very fair-skinned and had beautiful hair. Her jet-black hair cascaded over her shoulders without a single frizz, shimmering softly like silk. It was so alluring; one wanted to reach out and touch it. The woman did not look up, but simply bowed respectfully to the patron, then silently walked behind the long table to stand and prepare wine. The light shone on her face, revealing fine downy hairs from the side—flawless. Her hands were slender and delicate, with short, clean nails, unlike many noblewomen who would deliberately grow them long and meticulously trim them. As she prepared the wine, her hands danced like white butterflies, so beautiful that one could not look away. An Jiu chewed her food while staring at those hands, the thought unconsciously crossing her mind that she could shoot down a white butterfly with an arrow. Seeing her mesmerized, Hua Rongjian chuckled and said, “You see the difference between you and a woman now, do you not?” Upon hearing his words, An Jiu quickly used a method taught by her former psychologist to banish the thought from her mind—”Do not be too violent, do not be too violent…” She thought she could not hold back, but to her surprise, her emotions miraculously calmed down! This feeling suddenly reminded her of a pair of eyes. Deep gray eyes, forever gentle and serene, yet their hands never ceased scheming and killing. That was Wei Yuzhi. Thinking of him from time to time, An Jiu felt somewhat troubled. Hua Rongjian noticed the slight change in her expression and immediately abandoned his playful mood, carefully asking, “Are you angry?” “No.” An Jiu buried her head and continued eating. Wu Lingyuan, sensing this strange atmosphere, kept his eyes down, elegantly picking up a piece of green vegetable and slowly biting into it. After the meal, the three returned to the Hua residence together. Seeing that it was still early, An Jiu went to see Mei Jiu. When she was invited into the inner room, she saw Mei Jiu coming out to greet her, while a young girl was lying by the bed, teasing her godson with a cloth tiger, making his eyes dart around. “You are here,” Mei Jiu looked at her reproachfully. “You left without even saying goodbye, just a note, making me worry all the time.” An Jiu did not answer, but after looking her over, she commented honestly, “You’ve really gained weight this time.” Mei Jiu glared at her, then turned to the girl over there. “Yu’er has come to greet her aunt.” The girl handed the cloth tiger to the maid beside her, gathered her skirts, and walked over, bowing gracefully to An Jiu, “Aunt.” The girl’s features resembled Hua Rongtian by three or four points. An Jiu knew this was the daughter left behind by his ex-wife, and said, “No need for formalities.” Mei Jiu nudged her, feigning displeasure. “This is my daughter. As her aunt, should you not give her a gift?” “Oh.” An Jiu thought for a moment, then pulled a dagger from her outer thigh pocket. “This is for you.” Before the dagger could be handed to Hua Yu, Mei Jiu stopped her. “My daughter does not like fighting. Quickly find a decent gift.” The dagger was somewhat inappropriate as a gift for a girl, but its exquisite craftsmanship clearly indicated its high value, making it a reasonable gesture. Mei Jiu stopped her because she knew the dagger’s special properties; it could penetrate internal protective qi, which was crucial for An Jiu. An Jiu rummaged around and finally pulled out a small crystal tiger. Crystal was almost nonexistent in the Song Dynasty market; even if it was available, it often had many flaws or impurities. Crystal as clear and transparent as this was extremely rare, and the carving of an adorable tiger made Hua Yu fall in love with it. After sending Hua Yu and the maids away, An Jiu finally breathed a sigh of relief. “Where did you get this strange little thing?” Mei Jiu knew she liked collecting toys that looked childish, but she never expected her to carry it with her. An Jiu replied, “I dug one out last night in the study in Mei Mansion and whittled it into a large shape with a dagger.” Mei Jiu had also been to Mei Mansion, but she did not know many places there, and naturally had never seen the peculiar study of Shayun Residence. An Jiu moved closer to the bed, glanced at the little thing lying on it, met his grape-like eyes, and grinned. The little thing dared to be disrespectful, pouting as if about to cry. Mei Jiu reached out and picked him up, not caring whether the little child could understand her, and said softly, “This is your godmother. Quickly greet your godmother; she has a gift for you!” An Jiu readily drew a long sword from behind her back and held it in front of the mother and son. “Here,” She thought to herself that giving a weapon to a boy was never a problem!

chapters.title: The Steward
chapters.content: The little one in the swaddling clothes had only recently opened his eyes; whether he could see clearly was still unknown. But the little guy seemed very curious about An Jiu, his bright black eyes fixed on An Jiu’s hand. “He likes it.” An Jiu grinned. Mei Jiu had not had high hopes for her in this regard, but seeing her happy, she happily accepted the gift on behalf of her son. It was past noon, not yet dinnertime, so the two sat down for tea and a chat. Mei Jiu gently patted the child as she asked, “An Jiu, what do you think of my second brother?” An Jiu stared at the little one and casually replied, “He’s alright.” “He used to be a bit of a troublemaker, but I think he’s not a bad person at heart. He does not go to those shady places anymore. He married Mei Ruyan out of necessity; the Hua family would not allow Mei Ruyan to be listed in the family register.” Mei Jiu, as if afraid she would not believe her, leaned closer and whispered, “On the surface, we are all girls without family backing. Even if the Hua family would not let us be listed in the family register, they did not stand up for us. I only had the chance to have a child and be listed after the change of dynasty…” An Jiu felt something was off. “What do you mean?” Mei Jiu coughed lightly, embarrassed. “If you think Second Master is good, how about we become sisters-in-law?” “Is this your idea or Hua Rongjian’s?” An Jiu asked. “It was my own decision, but I asked Second Master, and he likes you very much.” Mei Jiu knew her too well. Seeing her slight displeasure, she quickly explained, “I was just asking. If you do not want to, that is fine. I…I just feel that Master Chu is not a good man. You want to live a normal life, but you probably cannot with him unless he’s willing to serve in the government.” Mei Jiu knew that Chu Dingjiang was a meritorious official who helped the current Emperor usurp the throne. At a time when the country desperately needed talent, if he willingly served and was controlled by the Emperor, everything would be fine. If he refused, he would only face death! However, even if he could maintain temporary stability, once the country was stable and the Emperor had the time to deal with him, he would definitely not be lenient. “Can you imagine me at home putting on makeup, doing housework, having children, and raising them?” An Jiu had not expected Mei Jiu to think so deeply about her situation, and she was slightly moved. So she said more, “I cannot. If I am with Hua Rongjian, that is all he can give me. The freedom I want is the freedom here.” She pointed to Mei Jiu’s heart. “Freedom lies in inner peace, and it has nothing to do with the kind of life one leads. I am slowly finding myself again. You do not need to worry about me,” An Jiu said, a slight smile playing on her lips. Mei Jiu had never seen An Jiu like this before. Her smile held a calm quality, no longer as volatile as before. She thought about it carefully and could not believe that someone like An Jiu could stay home and raise children. The Hua family was, after all, a powerful clan. Even if circumstances forced them to forgo a marriage alliance with a prominent family, they would still have to arrange for Hua Rongjian to marry a virtuous woman from a scholarly family, not someone like An Jiu. Mei Jiu would never mention this again. After dinner, An Jiu left the Hua residence. She strolled around Zhu Pianxian’s shop, changed into a black robe, and headed to the bounty board near midnight. It was the same wall again. A black list was prominently displayed, without a name, but clearly describing An Jiu. The targets on the black list were all extremely dangerous individuals; those without ninth-level strength should not even consider taking the challenge. So, despite her notice being posted for over half a year, no one dared to take it down. As soon as the night watchman passed, the black-clad men, hidden in the shadows, swarmed to snatch the notice. An Jiu remained atop the wall, watching. Only after the notices were claimed and the person in charge of the bounty list came to confirm did she leap down. Seeing her arrive so leisurely, the man said, “The rest of the notices have been confirmed; there’s one more on the list.” He was very curious; could this petite and frail person actually be here to take down the black notice?! The assassins who were about to leave also stopped. An Jiu took a human-face pendant from her waist and tossed it to him. Upon seeing the pendant, the man’s attitude immediately became respectful. “What would you like the bounty list to do?” Human-face pendants were rare to begin with; after changing hands several times over the past century, many had disappeared without a trace. Only the steward still possessed one. An Jiu did not speak, tore the black notice apart, stuffed it into her bosom, and turned to leave. Exchanging a human-faced pendant for a blacklist item was a huge loss. In the history of the bounty list, some had used these pendants to manipulate its members into usurping power. Many families within the current Konghe Army were originally bounty hunters. The moment the bounty list pendant appeared, many began to stir. If they could seize the pendant, they would enjoy endless wealth and glory, making the continued pursuit of the list pointless! The man sensed the change in the surrounding atmosphere and gripped the pendant tightly. The atmosphere was like a sword hanging overhead, about to strike. At that moment, the rustling sound of clothing could be heard, especially clear in the darkness. Judging from the sound, there were at least a hundred people. Dozens of masked black-robed men arrived first, landing in front of the bounty list and spreading out in a semi-circle to protect the person holding the human-faced pendant. Soon, a large number of masked men arrived. Seeing this, the surrounding assassins knew they had no chance of obtaining the Human-Faced Pendant that day and hurriedly left, lest they overhear too many secrets and be silenced by the bounty board. The person holding the Human-Faced Pendant saw a man wearing a bamboo hat and a black robe emerge from the shadows of the side wall and immediately knelt on one knee, presenting the pendant with both hands. “Master.” Many of those who had come with him were puzzled. The new master of the bounty board was only at the fifth level of martial arts and only relied on the Human-Faced Pendant and a huge fortune to command the entire bounty board. He rarely showed himself; why had he received news of the Human-Faced Pendant’s appearance so early and rushed over so hastily? Hua Rongjian reached out and took the pendant, placing it in his robes. “Master, why have you made such a fuss?” an aged voice asked from not far away. Hua Rongjian’s gaze, hidden in the shadow of his bamboo hat, darkened slightly. His shrill, altered voice sounded particularly sinister. “Of course, it is to take back what rightfully belongs to me.” Many elders resented his taking over the bounty list. If it were not for the restraint of the Human-Faced Pendant, they would have rebelled long ago. They would not tolerate a fifth-tier martial artist in charge; it was an unprecedented humiliation for a bounty list based on killing by force. “You are playing such childish games right under our noses, huh?” the old man sneered. “Do you really think the Bounty List has fallen on hard times and can become a toy for a little kid like you?” Hua Rongjian coldly replied, “I can step down at any time. However, without my wealth and connections, the Bounty List is nothing but a rat’s den. So, Elder, you’d better think carefully before you speak.” He knew that these old fogies could easily oust him. The reason they had not acted, besides being constrained by the Human-Faced Pendant, was that everything he had brought to the Bounty List could restore it to its former glory. They would not kick him out until they had squeezed out all his usefulness.

chapters.title: You Are Like Corn
chapters.content: Of course, he would not give them the chance to betray him after he’d served their purpose. The old man remained silent for a long time, and Hua Rongjian, impatient, ordered, “Withdraw!” The group of black-clad men vanished into the streets in the blink of an eye. A ragged old man emerged from a nearby dead-end alley, staring intently in the direction An Jiu had just left, his face thoughtful. Initially, they agreed to let Hua Rongjian take over the entire Bounty List because of his wealth, connections, and the fact that his martial arts skills were low; he seemed like a fat pig, and they could decide to remove him at any time. But now, everything seemed to be slipping out of control. This young, weak-skilled leader was not as easy to deal with as they had imagined. “The Hua family,” the aged voice softly murmured. He had spent some time investigating the new leader’s identity, and his apprehension only deepened. Was Hua Rongjian taking over the Bounty List out of personal interest or at the behest of his family? The Bounty List absolutely could not be subservient to any family! This was one of the conditions under which the imperial court retained the Bounty List after establishing the Konghe Army, but now the court was preoccupied with its own problems and could not concern itself with this matter for the time being. The night was deep. When An Jiu returned to the island, Da Jiu was lying on the ferry landing, dozing in a cat-like sitting position, its large head nodding and purring softly. “Da Jiu, Da Jiu!” An Jiu called several times but could not wake it, so she kicked it lightly. “How can you, a tiger, be so unwary!” Da Jiu shook its head and followed her back in a daze. An Jiu reached the door and realized Da Jiu had not followed. Turning her head, she saw the tiger sprawled on the stone path, fast asleep! Although Da Jiu was usually lazy and gluttonous, it would never act this way. An Jiu dragged the tiger by its leg all the way to Mo Sigui’s door and knocked. No one answered. She knocked again. Still no response. An Jiu’s heart sank, and she raised her leg to kick the door. Just then, the door creaked open, and Wei Yuzhi, dressed in a loose blue robe, entered. His white hair was disheveled, and his deep gray eyes seemed veiled by a thin mist, giving him a captivating, dreamlike appearance. An Jiu was startled when she met his eyes. She roughly guessed what had happened! Even someone with Wei Yuzhi’s formidable mental strength could not escape it; the entire island must have fallen into a deep sleep. The lingering smell of medicine in the room was already making her dizzy. “Go back to sleep,” she said. “Fourteenth…” Wei Yuzhi steadied himself against the doorframe, and seeing her dragging the tiger along, he said, “Physician Mo had insomnia tonight. The usual medicinal smoke did not work, so he prepared a new one, and…” He stopped mid-sentence, swaying precariously. An Jiu grabbed him. The force was too great, and Wei Yuzhi stumbled and bumped into her. An Jiu could clearly feel his body temperature, his breath brushing against her neck. Her heart skipped a beat, and her whole body stiffened. She was no longer an inexperienced virgin. Even the first time she was with Chu Dingjiang, she had not reacted so strongly to such a small closeness. After standing there for a while, An Jiu helped him into the house. When they came out, she saw Chu Dingjiang standing in the courtyard and suddenly felt a little guilty. “It’s getting late; let’s rest,” Chu Dingjiang said, turning and going back inside. His tone was calm, but An Jiu sensed his anger. He dragged An Jiu back into the dark room and groped his way onto the bed. After groping around for a while, she could not touch Chu Dingjiang’s body. Normally, An Jiu could sense his presence unless he deliberately concealed it. Helplessly, An Jiu turned on the bedside lamp. The orange light slowly illuminated the entire room, and Chu Dingjiang, dressed in a black robe, sat at the table drinking tea. “Are you angry?” An Jiu explained, “It was just an accident…” Chu Dingjiang put down his cup. His dark eyes stared fixedly at An Jiu, a feeling of helplessness and sorrow welling up inside him, much like the feeling he had when betrayed by his family in his past life. Whether someone had fallen in love or not, an observer could discern it from subtle clues, let alone someone as knowledgeable as he was of An Jiu. At this moment, Chu Dingjiang did not know how to react. Feelings came unexpectedly and went without a trace. When someone did not like you, no matter what you do, no matter how much you beg, it would not stay. An Jiu only had a vague feeling for that person now, but what about later? Chu Dingjiang drank a glass of cold water, calming himself down. “Ah Jiu, today I only have one sentence to say to you.” “What?” An Jiu asked quickly. He noticed her nervousness, walked over, and gently pressed her head against his chest. “No matter where you go in the future, no matter who you stand beside, I will always wait for you.” It was not that Chu Dingjiang lacked confidence, but rather that he saw things too clearly. An Jiu was about to relive her missing piece of life. Judging from her choices, beneath her cold exterior lay a passionate heart. Their seemingly bland relationship was unlikely to last, or there would inevitably be unexpected twists and turns. He was bothered by An Jiu’s feelings for someone else, but forcing her to suppress them would backfire. He had enough patience and tolerance to prove that all passionate encounters were not fleeting. Commandeering might win over other women’s hearts, but it was definitely not suitable for An Jiu. He needed to use a gentle, persuasive approach. “Chu Dingjiang, let’s get married,” An Jiu said, her voice muffled. “Alright,” Chu Dingjiang agreed. “Chu Dingjiang, I know what you are worried about.” An Jiu looked up at him. “I do have different feelings for Wei Yuzhi, but I will not try. You should trust me.” “I believe you,” Chu Dingjiang believed she was telling the truth, but even someone with Wei Yuzhi’s exceptional self-control could not resist. “You are just giving me the runaround.” An Jiu pushed him away, sat cross-legged on the edge of the bed, and glared at him with dissatisfaction. “When I was little, I heard a story about a big, hungry bear that sneaked into a cornfield and picked a lot of corn. On its way back, it saw a watermelon patch, so it dropped the corn and picked two watermelons. Then it saw a sesame field, so it dropped the watermelons and started picking sesame seeds. Later, an old man tending the sesame field chased after it, and it ran away. When it got home, it found it had only brought back a few sesame seeds.” “When I was little, I wondered why the old man dared to chase the bear and why the bear was afraid of an old man. Later, I realized the story was telling us that people should learn to be content and cherish what they already have; otherwise, they will suffer losses.” Chu Dingjiang had always felt that she did a lot but thought very little, and hearing these words refreshed his perception of her. “When did you start thinking about these things?” “A long time ago. I figured it out, so when carrying out missions with multiple targets, I only focus on one target, and I never pursue my accomplices until I’ve killed that target.” Chu Dingjiang smiled. “You really put your learning to practical use.” “I only focus on the first target. Even if there are people in the world better than you who move me more, I will not shift my gaze to try them,” An Jiu said earnestly. “You are like corn.”

chapters.title: A Difficult Problem
chapters.content: An Jiu’s words were sincere, but as an “old man,” Chu Dingjiang subconsciously still trusted his own experience. Extremes met; if one invested too much emotion and attention in something, the happiness gained would be far less than expected. Therefore, one should maintain a calm and balanced perspective. Knowing he was taking it too seriously, Chu Dingjiang tried to fill his time as much as possible, raising various small animals and planting a large vineyard on the island. Leisurely time on the island passed by, but outside, the winds of change were still blowing. In just one month, Chu Dingjiang received three imperial edicts. The consequences of continuing to disobey were predictable. Meanwhile, Wu Lingyuan’s matter had been settled. Initially, Hua Rongtian recommended Wu Lingyuan to be a county magistrate in the Jiangzhe region, but Wu Lingyuan, with great integrity, requested to be transferred to Hejian, making a great impression on the Emperor. The Emperor even took time out of his busy schedule to write a calligraphy piece for Wu Lingyuan. —Strong winds reveal the strength of the grass. With such praise, Wu Lingyuan would undoubtedly be highly valued if he returned alive. Everyone resented his cunning but dared not voice it. After all, going there meant facing the Liao cavalry head-on; a gamble with one’s life! Anyone with the guts could volunteer for a transfer there! The position of magistrate of Hexi County in Hejian had been vacant for over three months. If Wu Lingyuan’s request was approved, he would take office within a month. An Jiu would have to accompany him. Chu Dingjiang, bound by the imperial decree and burdened with responsibilities for the Mei family, could not leave immediately and had to remain in Bianjing. An Jiu, feeling utterly bored, felt a deep reluctance at the sudden separation. Before leaving, she repeatedly instructed him to meet her in Hejian after he had finished his business here. Mo Sigui packed his bags as quickly as possible, taking Wei Yuzhi and two tigers with him to travel north with An Jiu. Chu Dingjiang supported Mo Sigui going with her, but he was very dissatisfied with Mo Sigui’s decision to have Wei Yuzhi accompany him, and he held Mo Sigui responsible for this. However, he was not worried that Wei Yuzhi would cling to An Jiu; Wei Yuzhi was not one to be sentimental. Once he recovered, he would definitely leave. The one who suffered the most was Wu Lingyuan. On the day of his departure, he discovered that there was no “large entourage” protecting him as rumored. There was only An Jiu, Sui Yuntong, Li Qingzhi, Mo Sigui, and a seemingly weak scholar. In an assassination mission, fewer but more skilled assassins were always better. The problem was that they were a visible banner; with this kind of setup, could they really survive the Liao army’s iron cavalry without fleeing? He strongly doubted it. Doubts aside, An Jiu had done him a favor. As the saying goes, “A drop of kindness should be repaid with a spring of gratitude.” What harm was there in risking his life to gamble with her? Besides, if he won this high-stakes gamble, he would also reap significant benefits. Hexi County was not located at the northernmost tip of the Song Dynasty, but unlike Pingbei County, it lacked the natural barrier of the Yellow River. Bordering the Liao Dynasty, it was surrounded by vast plains, making it a prime target for Liao cavalry raids. The group traveled day and night, discreetly arriving at Hexi County. The journey was filled with nothing but bad news. Wu Lingyuan could not help but sigh deeply. Upon entering the county yamen, his unease only intensified! The office was utterly desolate. Most of the officials were over forty-five years old, and there was no county magistrate, not even a county lieutenant or assistant magistrate. Only a registrar was in charge. The county warehouse had been looted by Liao cavalry a year prior, leaving not a single copper coin. Wu Lingyuan could hardly believe it. This was supposed to be a prestigious county of the Song Dynasty, reduced to such a state! Mo Sigui was even more dissatisfied, throwing a tantrum. Only when Wei Yuzhi promised to send a batch of medicinal herbs in a couple of days did he finally smile. The next day, before Wei Yuzhi’s medicinal herbs even arrived, more than ten men escorted several cartloads of herbs and daily necessities. Upon inquiry, they learned it was an order from Chu Dingjiang. Mo Sigui felt quite clever; following two wealthy patients had really saved them trouble. After breakfast, the group sat in the main hall until the sun was high in the sky before the county clerk arrived. The clerk of Hexi County shared the same surname as Wei Yuzhi. Looking at his thin, slightly hunched figure and wrinkled face, it was hard to believe he was only thirty-eight years old. Wu Lingyuan only mentioned it briefly before Clerk Wei, with a melancholy tone, continued, “Back in my day, I was a handsome and spirited young man, but being tormented in a place like this has turned me into this…” Seeing that he was about to launch into a tirade, Wu Lingyuan quickly interrupted, “Tell me about the county’s affairs first.” Clerk Wei placed a nearly torn county gazetteer on the table. “Your Honor,” he said, “the room in the county office where official documents and files were kept was burned down by the Liao bandits. The county magistrate died a violent death last year; it was a truly gruesome death… I was hiding under the desk at the time, and I witnessed his intestines spill out…” As he spoke, he raised his sleeve to dab at the corner of his eye. Seeing that he had veered off-topic again, Wu Lingyuan could only say, “Clerk Wei, please accept my condolences. Tell me about the official affairs of the past year…” “Oh,” Clerk Wei said, “The people in the city were all captured by the Liao bandits. Fortunately, General Ling once again led a decisive attack on Liao that year, rescuing many people. This past year, I’ve been busy resettling and providing relief to the people.” He slightly raised his eyes and cautiously said, “The county granary is also…completely empty.” “Heavens! What kind of hellish place is this?” Mo Sigui finally could not take it anymore. “Does this mean I will have to eat herbs to avoid starvation in the future?” Wu Lingyuan remained silent for a long time. “I will take a walk around first. Clerk Wei, please organize the affairs of the past year and report for duty tomorrow.” Wu Lingyuan also realized that Clerk Wei did not want him to take over Hexi County smoothly. Without a magistrate, county magistrate, and county commandant, this small area would still be his domain. Clerk Wei readily agreed. However, Wu Lingyuan held no hope for his promise. Since this was a place where even the established systems had been destroyed, he only needed to rebuild a system; he did not need to know in detail how things had worked before. But to gain a foothold, he could not underestimate the local power brokers. In the afternoon, Wu Lingyuan, accompanied by Sui Yuntong, Li Qingzhi, and An Jiu, went for a walk. “Devastation” was the perfect word to describe Hexi County. Few pedestrians were on the streets; only a few shops were open for business, their doors and walls bearing many traces of fire. From the wide stone-paved streets and the houses on either side, one could glimpse that this place had once been prosperous. Sui Yuntong sighed, “Even the city is like this; the surrounding villages are probably in even worse shape.” An Jiu was somewhat worried. Reorganizing the Dragon Martial Guards required manpower first; without even a regular population, how could they train elites?

chapters.title: The Qian Volume
chapters.content: The soldiers of Hexi County were even worse off; many were either crippled in the war or too old. After looking around, the men were all frowning. If the Liao army broke through the Hebei army’s defenses, this place would have no chance of self-defense. Sui Yuntong saw Wu Lingyuan staring blankly at the setting sun and asked, “What are you thinking about, My Lord?” Wu Lingyuan snapped out of his reverie and joked, “I am thinking about how to write the surrender document to achieve the best effect.” Li Qingzhi did not understand the joke and raised an eyebrow. “We have not even fought yet; how can you be thinking about surrendering to the Liao dogs?” Wu Lingyuan smiled but did not argue. A scholar’s blindness meant his future was ruined. Wu Lingyuan had experienced the most desperate and darkest times of his life, and even then, he could remain calm. Now, he would not immediately have the thought of retreating because of a little difficulty. He already had many plans for this place in his mind, but the most important thing first was to solve the problems of defending the city and the population. An Jiu also considered this. “Defending a city does not necessarily require strong and robust men. Lou Xiaowu designed many weapons that even the old and weak could use.” Throwing bombs was something anyone with hands could do! Wu Lingyuan immediately thought of Hua Rongjian’s mention of a skilled mechanic among the Lou family, his eyes brightening. “That is perfect! We cannot let ourselves become pigs waiting to be slaughtered by the Liao bandits!” The other three nodded in agreement. Actually, Hexi County’s location and climate were quite advantageous. If it had a stable environment to recuperate, it could quickly recover its vitality. However, the Liao cavalry raids every year, and they could not rely entirely on the Hebei army’s resistance. If the garrison were effective, Hexi County would not be in this state! The Liao cavalry was elusive, and the Hexi garrison lacked a capable mobile force to counter them. By the time the main army reacted, the cavalry had already finished their looting and plundering. Even when Ling Ziyue led the army, this was not entirely avoidable. Let alone now? Wu Lingyuan said, “Let’s check the household registration tomorrow about the population issue.” Sui Yuntong suggested, “After the natural disaster, many people were displaced. We can take them in.” Li Qingzhi scoffed, “Come on, I reckon they’d rather starve than come to this place to feed the wolves.” “How will we know if we do not try?” Sui Yuntong felt that increasing the population through childbirth was a dead end. “I will go,” An Jiu said. “You cannot go!” “You cannot go!” Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi said in unison. “The master ordered us to protect you. If you leave, we will have to go with you. Only the defenseless Lord Wu is left in Hexi County…” Li Qingzhi hurriedly explained, “The Divine Physician Mo is highly skilled in martial arts, but he also has a powerful Liao lackey by his side.” Before he finished speaking, he felt a blur before his eyes, and An Jiu’s dagger was already against his neck, and he did not even have time to react! “You say you will protect me?” An Jiu sneered. Li Qingzhi’s face instantly turned red. An Jiu was slapping him in the face with her actions—with this kind of strength, he dared to claim he could protect her? Sui Yuntong pushed away her dagger. “Fourteenth, you misunderstand. The master meant that more people make things easier.” “I did not misunderstand him; it was Li Qingzhi who misunderstood.” An Jiu sheathed her dagger, making a decision that brooked no argument. “You’d only be a burden if you came along. I will go myself.” Things were settled amicably! However, only An Jiu was happy. Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi were both furious. If Chu Dingjiang knew, they’d have had to pay with their lives! Seeing this, Wu Lingyuan advised, “Let Master Sui accompany you. I do not doubt Fourteenth Miss’s abilities, but getting someone to willingly come along will require a lot of persuasion.” Fortunately, An Jiu recognized her weakness; language was an art. She was always good at putting others down, but she did not know how to manipulate people’s emotions with words… After thinking for a while, An Jiu finally nodded in agreement. Sui Yuntong breathed a sigh of relief. Even if his martial arts skills were indeed inferior to An Jiu’s, at least he could be of some use in times of danger. At the very least, he could promptly notify Chu Dingjiang for a rescue, which was far more reassuring than letting her disappear right under his nose. Wu Lingyuan watched the birds foraging in the courtyard, his gaze calm and distant, but a thought involuntarily surfaced in his mind: These liars. What happened to the promised expert guards?! What could he do after being tricked by his benefactor? He would just have to accept it! … All things revived; spring was in full bloom. In a spacious courtyard in Xijin Prefecture of the Liao Kingdom, an ancient tree was just beginning to sprout tender green buds. This ancient tree, with its intertwined roots and countless branches layered upon each other, reached towards the sky. Even though it had not yet grown lush leaves, most of the courtyard was already covered in shadow. A man in a wide robe reclined on a chaise longue, a snow-white wolf pelt beneath him, a thick wool blanket covering his legs. His long, dark hair flowed freely, winding across the white fur with a soft, silky sheen. A book covered his face, revealing only his refined, angular chin. Sunlight filtered through the dense, bare branches, casting dappled patterns on the bark. “My Lord,” a man dressed in foreign attire entered, bowing respectfully. “Hmm,” the man responded. The man in foreign attire had studied the Song script and recognized the four characters on the book’s cover: “The Secret Manual of Konghe.” A small character, “乾” (Qian), was marked at the bottom of the page. This was the “乾” volume of the Secret Manual of Konghe, the first volume, containing secrets about the Song Kingdom’s Konghe Army. “I’ve received word that a new magistrate has arrived in Hexi County.” Such a trivial matter would not warrant a special report; there must be something else going on. The man removed his book, revealing his face, his narrow phoenix eyes filled with authority. However, even though the man in the foreign attire had seen this face countless times, he still felt a sense of dazzle. He paused for a moment, then quickly continued, “The scouts report that Wei Yuzhi is traveling with the new magistrate and that Divine Physician Mo Sigui is also here.” “Oh.” He smiled slightly, sitting up. “I am here to enjoy my retirement; I will not concern myself with such matters.” As he spoke, he beckoned a maid standing on the veranda to come and comb his hair. The man in the foreign attire said, “If Your Majesty does not intervene, the Liao Kingdom will be doomed.” His phoenix eyes narrowed lazily, his slender fingers lightly strumming the Secret Manual of Konghe, making his emotions impossible to discern. This man was none other than Yelu Jinglie, the Northern King of Liao, who had announced his abdication a month ago to “enjoy his retirement” in Xijin Prefecture. For the Yelu clan, living to their thirties was considered an advanced age. “My Lord, shall we secretly assassinate Wei Yuzhi?” the man dressed in barbarian clothes asked. The maid behind him trembled slightly, lightly tugging at Yelu Jinglie’s hair. His expression remained unchanged; still squinting at the tree branches, he said calmly, “Drag her out and deal with her.” The maid did not even have time to utter a word of “Spare me” before she was covered in the mouth and nose and dragged away. “Two short-lived devils, I will see what trouble they can cause.” Yelu Jinglie unleashed a storm of energy in his palm, like thousands of sharp blades, shredding the book into dust. Watching the dust drift away in the wind, a faint smile appeared on Yelu Jinglie’s face. “Interesting things should always be tried. Send someone to deliver a message to Ah Ning, tell her to come over.”

chapters.title: A Wrongful Conviction Resolved
chapters.content: As spring warmed, everything began to revive. Even the ills accumulated in the Song Dynasty due to the dynastic change seemed to grow wildly in the gentle spring rain. Yet, even in this desolate place, a vibrant life force could be seen. In the Forbidden City’s inner palace, after a long silence, bursts of hearty laughter suddenly erupted. The laughter of the newly appointed Emperor, who had quickly shed his youthful naiveté, seemed to pierce through the oppressive dark clouds, instantly dispelling the clouds and revealing the sun. The cabinet ministers had different thoughts, but ultimately, they were happy. “General Ling is truly still alive! Heaven blesses the Song Dynasty!” the Emperor exclaimed. Prime Minister Hua, who had hesitated over whether to reveal that Chu Dingjiang had saved Ling Ziyue, fell silent upon hearing the Emperor’s exclamation. The Song Dynasty had only one heaven: His Majesty. Prime Minister Hua harbored complex feelings towards his rebellious son, even a hidden fear. However, he could not deny the son’s unwavering dedication to protecting the Hua family, nor could he deny the crucial role his son’s decision to infiltrate the Imperial Guard played in the family’s survival. After all, he was still his blood relative, and Prime Minister Hua wanted to help him escape his current predicament. Those who entered the cabinet were no pushovers. Having served the Emperor for so long, they understood his temperament. At this moment, they were all weighing whether they should volunteer to help clear Ling Ziyue’s name. Prime Minister Hua, however, asked softly without much thought, “Your Majesty, helping General Ling overturn his case will inevitably involve the late Emperor…” No matter the method, the late Emperor’s personal judgment on Ling Ziyue was an unavoidable fact, and it would more or less affect the late Emperor’s reputation. The Emperor was unconcerned, thinking that the late Emperor’s reputation was not affected by this matter! Although such thoughts might seem disrespectful, he had always been respectful to the late Emperor, but never truly revered him. This was largely due to his mother’s instilling in him from a young age the idea that he should grow up to be a true man and never follow in his father’s footsteps! After a moment, the Emperor said wistfully, “My father dedicated his life to the country and its people. The Song Dynasty now needs General Ling. His spirit in heaven will not blame us. Entrust this matter to Prime Minister Hua. Go ahead and do it.” “This old minister obeys!” Prime Minister Hua hurriedly rose to accept the order. The Emperor spoke frankly, but in reality, he could not truly abandon his duties. Even if not for the late Emperor, he had to consider the dignity of the imperial family. Early in the fifth month, Ling Ziyue appeared in Bianjing to seek an audience with the Emperor to plead his case. His appearance caused a huge uproar. Many people had witnessed General Ling being shot dead by a hail of arrows before being led to the execution ground. However, upon careful recollection, no one had seen the true face of the so-called “General Ling.” The court acted with unprecedented speed, overturning the case in just half a month. It was said that a villain fabricated “evidence” that General Ling was a traitor, and because the evidence was so convincing, the late Emperor was initially deceived. He issued an edict to punish Ling, but the late Emperor, being wise, discovered the truth before Ling Ziyue’s execution and secretly saved him to capture the traitor. How the traitor was captured and who he was were not clearly stated, only that it was a secret. In short, the late Emperor was wise and decisive, and General Ling endured humiliation and hardship. Everything was forced by circumstances. The current Emperor also bestowed upon the unjustly killed Madam Ling the title of First-Rank Lady and personally inscribed a poem for the Ling family, praising their loyalty and bravery. Ling Ziyue moved into the brand-new General’s Mansion, standing alone in the empty and silent courtyard. He was filled with loneliness. No matter how much he told himself that he had returned to protect the country, he still felt injustice, feeling unworthy as a husband and father. His entire family had died unjustly at the hands of the late Emperor, and now he was still forced to serve the Zhao family’s empire. One general’s success was built on the bones of ten thousand. Whether in pain or not, he could only step over this pile of bones to become a war god revered by thousands. He would build an impregnable Great Wall for the Song Dynasty, and only then would he not have failed the many sacrifices. Ling Ziyue closed his eyes. No matter how dazzling the “Loyal and Valiant” inscription on the door plaque was, he would always feel indebted, forever unable to erase the sense of baseness hidden deep within his heart. “Brother Ling, are you not happy?” Lou Xiaowu had been there for a while, standing under the porch watching him. She did not understand. It was supposed to be the day his injustice was redressed, so why did he look so sorrowful? Ling Ziyue composed himself and turned to look at her. “Why are you here?” Lou Xiaowu pouted, her large tears silently accusing him. Before, Ling Ziyue was silent and stern, and they were not particularly close, but since they were both free on the island, they had more contact. He had never deliberately ignored her like he had these past two days. Seeing that he remained silent, Lou Xiaowu could not help but say, “I want to live with you.” A statement that sparked much speculation, but Ling Ziyue did not misunderstand. Lou Xiaowu was still quite naive about romantic relationships; her idea of “go back and take good care of your things. If the Liao and Song dynasties ever go to war, they will be very useful.” “We used to be so close. Why have you suddenly become like this?” Lou Xiaowu finished speaking, pursing her lips tightly, looking at him stubbornly. Lou Xiaowu was simple-minded, and there were too many things she could not understand. In her eyes, Ling Ziyue’s state of mind was a mystery. Ling Ziyue’s dark eyes were calm, revealing no emotion. “Xiaowu, go live with Sheng Changying and his wife. I will be heading to the border in a few days, and this place will be empty.” “I want to go with you.” “No.” Ling Ziyue refused outright. Lou Xiaowu was stunned for a moment, then suddenly burst into tears like a child abandoned by their parents. Those who knew Lou Xiaowu knew that although she was naive, she was resilient and not a fragile person. Even when the Lou clan was wiped out, she had not cried as loudly as she did now. A person could grit their teeth and persevere in adversity, bleeding but not shedding tears, but once their loved ones appeared before them, they suddenly felt they’d suffered an immense injustice. Lou Xiaowu was probably feeling that way right now! Ling Ziyue hardened his heart, no longer looking at her, and turned to leave. Behind him, Lou Xiaowu’s crying stopped abruptly, only the sound of her sobs escaping. Ling Ziyue’s heart ached: “Xiaowu, because you are the person I want to protect, I am so afraid that you would become the next sacrifice while you are by my side.” Being a general was such a strange profession; you could protect millions of people, but the price was sacrificing those closest to you. Lou Xiaowu watched his figure disappear among the flowers and trees, her eyes brimming with tears, her mind a blur, a complete mess. She could not understand or accept this reality. Everyone seemed preoccupied with their own affairs, leaving her aside—her mother, her sister, her friends, even Ling Ziyue. “Fine, ignore me then, hmph.” Lou Xiaowu wiped away her tears, leaving angrily, muttering, “It’s like I have nowhere else to go, though so many people like me!”

chapters.title: A Quarrel Upon Meeting
chapters.content: Back on the island, Lou Xiaowu packed her luggage. The petite girl, carrying luggage larger than herself, headed towards Hejian Prefecture. The farther she got from Bianjing, the less angry she felt. An unknown emotion spread through her, like the high, distant, and desolate gray sky above. Looking back, Lou Xiaowu could no longer see the city walls. “Hmph, going to find Ah Jiu to play.” Lou Xiaowu pouted, trying to forget her troubles, and prepared to buy a carriage in the nearest county. “It’s all the General’s fault! He made me so angry I forgot to take a carriage!” …It was the perfect season for nomadic life, and a brief period of peace had emerged between Liao and Song. The new magistrate of Hexi County was making his mark; his three major reforms were in full swing. An Jiu and Sui Yuntong were tasked with recruiting talent from the south, while Wu Lingyuan encouraged agriculture and sent all the soldiers guarding the city back to work in the fields. After all, even if a battle broke out immediately, these men would not last a single round; why waste labor? An Jiu, dressed in men’s clothing with a bamboo hat covering most of her face, arrived at Xingzhou, which was relatively close to Hejian Prefecture. Xingzhou was located behind the Hebei garrison, rarely disturbed by Liao cavalry, and its people lived in peace and prosperity. Sui Yuntong suggested that An Jiu go to Xingzhou first because a locust plague had struck the area a couple of years prior, causing chaos and a large influx of refugees into Xingzhou. Settling down in the city was no easy task; many would inevitably be homeless. The two arrived at the city gates to find a bustling crowd, a stark contrast to Hexi County’s quietness. Because this was behind the Hebei army’s lines, entry checks were extremely strict. Everyone entering the city had to queue and register, and those from out of town had to undergo body searches. An Jiu frowned at the long queue ahead. “It will be almost afternoon by then!” It was such a waste of time! Sui Yuntong guessed she wanted to wander around the area first, then sneak into the city under the cover of night. “We are on official business. We have to follow the rules.” “Mm,” An Jiu nodded in agreement. She’d promised to be a good person! Thinking about how ordinary people queued to enter the city, she suddenly became interested. An hour later, they finally reached the city gate. A soldier approached, preparing to search them. Sui Yuntong pulled out a token. “Hejian Prefecture Garrison.” An Jiu quickly pulled out her token as well. The soldier examined it carefully, then bowed and said, “After you register, you may enter the city.” Sui Yuntong went to a long table nearby, wrote down their identities, and the guard let them through. An Jiu stroked the token hidden in her sleeve, her heart leaping with joy. In her previous life, she had also disguised herself as a government official, using a pass to sneak into special institutions, but the feeling of impersonation was completely different from the feeling of being genuine. “Do you know how I feel right now?” An Jiu asked. Sui Yuntong paused, unsure what she meant. An Jiu’s eyes gleamed. “I feel like someone who’s been a liar has finally told the truth. I feel so at ease, so proud.” Sui Yuntong did not know her past and naturally did not understand the meaning behind her words; she was just stating the facts. “If you are a liar, then no one in this world tells the truth.” One of An Jiu’s special talents was—revealing ugly truths. It was still early, so the two strolled around the streets, looking for a suitable inn. Sui Yuntong’s eyes lit up when he saw strong, ragged men. An Jiu, on the other hand, used her mental power to sense if there were any martial artists around. “Huh?” An Jiu suddenly detected a familiar aura in the crowd and immediately looked around. Seeing her intently searching, Sui Yuntong did not interrupt. The crowd was noisy, but a sharp voice abruptly “stood out” from the noise. The person said, “Are you blind?!” An Jiu strode over. A handsome scholar in plain clothes, with a pale face, glared at a veiled woman. “Get lost!” Those around, seeing his distinguished attire, dared not offend him and quickly gave him a wide berth. Sui Yuntong smiled. “Lord Gao.” The pale-faced scholar glanced at him sideways. “Oh, who is it? It is just Little Sui and the little dwarf!” “Gao Dazhuang,” An Jiu said. Upon hearing this name, those around covered their mouths and snickered. He was clearly an effeminate man; where was the ‘great man’? The woman who had been yelled at by Gao Dazhuang hurriedly left with her maid while no one was looking. She had seen Gao Dazhuang from afar and assumed he was a young master from some noble family, so she planned a chance encounter. Who knew he would speak with such an effeminate voice and such a violent temper? What a waste of such a handsome face! The woman thought bitterly. Gao Dazhuang’s face darkened, and he coldly surveyed his surroundings. The onlookers felt a chill run down their spines and quickly dispersed. The street was not a place to talk, so Sui Yuntong said, “Has Your Excellency had dinner yet? Shall we join you?” “No, I am too angry to eat. Let’s find somewhere to have tea.” Gao Dazhuang vigorously patted the spot where the woman had bumped into him, still feeling uneasy. The three of them entered a nearby teahouse. After they sat down, Sui Yuntong asked, “Why has Your Excellency come here?” Gao Dazhuang outwardly appeared loyal only to the late Emperor, but his true master was the Second Prince, the current Emperor. Someone as loyal as he should be highly valued; his presence here must indicate something important. “I’ve volunteered to be stationed here as a garrison commander,” Gao Dazhuang said, sipping his tea and raising an eyebrow smugly. “I told you all to follow me, but you insisted on running away. Tsk tsk, are you doing better than me?” If they had not left, they might have gotten some official positions by now, but who could predict the future? Besides, it was one thing for men, but even if the Second Prince ascended the throne, An Jiu, a woman, still would not be able to become an official, nor would she be released. An Jiu, holding her teacup, said honestly, “You are barely half a man, but I am a woman. Even if I followed you, I would not be any better off than I am now.” Gao Dazhuang slammed the cup on the table and reached for his sword. Sui Yuntong quickly stopped him. “My Lord, please calm down. You know how outspoken the Fourteenth Prince is! Do not take it to heart.” Gao Dazhuang stopped, huffing. “My Lord, you’ve taken command of the military in Xingzhou?” Sui Yuntong poured him another cup of tea and eagerly offered it to him. “Hmph.” Gao Dazhuang took the tea with satisfaction but did not drink it. “What are you doing here?” Sui Yuntong glanced at An Jiu, subtly flattering him, “We are currently under the command of the Hejian garrison, responsible for Hexi County, but you know the situation in Hexi better than anyone…” “You’ve come to Xingzhou to recruit people?” Gao Dazhuang asked. “There are many people in Xingzhou, are there not?” An Jiu was most concerned about this. “Shut up, I do not care about you!” Gao Dazhuang rolled his eyes and continued speaking to Sui Yuntong. “I originally requested to go to Hejian Prefecture, but the Emperor disagreed and assigned me here instead. Wow, it is so peaceful here; everyone’s bored out of their minds! Xingzhou does have some people with unclear household registrations, but I can help you with that.” “Thank you so much, My Lord!” Sui Yuntong had worked under Gao Dazhuang for a while and knew his temperament well, so he said, “Hexi County is now mostly populated by elderly soldiers, numbering only a little over a hundred, practically nonexistent. Our lord has already informed the Emperor to rebuild the garrison. If all goes well, the Fourteenth and I will be responsible for rebuilding the army. Thinking back to the glory days of the Dragon Martial Guards, I yearn for it.” Gao Dazhuang was slightly taken aback, then scoffed, “Just the two of you?” An Jiu said, “It’s all about human effort.” Gao Dazhuang got angry when he heard her speak. “You are not allowed to speak; otherwise, forget about recruiting soldiers in Xingzhou. I will have you dragged out of the city!” “Try it?” An Jiu said. Seeing the tense atmosphere, Sui Yuntong quickly tried to smooth things over. “My Lord, please calm down. It was Fourteenth who discovered you just now. She may not say it, but she really misses you; otherwise, she would not have come forward to greet you. You know she’s never been one for small talk.” After saying this, seeing An Jiu about to speak again, he immediately stepped on her foot. “Disgusting,” Gao Dazhuang said, though his anger had subsided somewhat. “I will have the government check the household registers in the next few days and expel the unregistered. You can take this opportunity to recruit people.” “Great! Thank you, My Lord!” Sui Yuntong secretly stepped on An Jiu’s foot again. “Hmph.” An Jiu turned her head, refusing to flatter. “I am leaving,” Gao Dazhuang said and stood up. “My Lord, why not have dinner together before you go?” Sui Yuntong stood up to persuade him to stay. Gao Dazhuang sneered, “This is my territory! But I will not be inviting you to dinner, especially this little dwarf! Get out of here after you’ve recruited enough people!”

chapters.title: Where is the Martial World?
chapters.content: Sui Yuntong watched Gao Dazhuang sway as he left and could not help but sigh, “Lord Gao is a good man, but he’s only responsive to gentleness. Next time you see him, be more accommodating; after all, he’s nominally half a master!” “Where are the good people in the Konghe Army? I only acknowledge that he has a heart full of passion.” An Jiu paused. “A heart full of passion fueled a fiery, womanly heart.” “Cough!” Sui Yuntong almost spat out his tea. An Jiu frowned. “What’s wrong?” Seeing her serious face, clearly not joking, Sui Yuntong quickly waved his hand. “Nothing, nothing.” Since her old friend was not going to oblige, the two casually ordered some snacks at the teahouse and then found an inn to stay in. An Jiu lay on the bed fully clothed, pondering. She knew she could not quickly organize a powerful army by training new recruits from scratch. So where should she recruit martial arts masters? Martial arts master…Martial arts master…Konghe Army…Konghe Army…Assassin… An Jiu sat up abruptly and went next door to find Sui Yuntong. She silently slipped into the next room, crouched on the roof beam, and saw Sui Yuntong undressing to take a bath. She pondered for a moment, then suddenly said, “I’ve thought of a plan. Can you help me see if it is feasible?” Sui Yuntong was startled, nearly dropping the hidden weapon between his fingers. “Phew!” Sui Yuntong put on his outer robe and exhaled. “Our rooms are only a few steps apart. Why did you not knock?” Even a clay Buddha would be startled. An Jiu could not help but reflect on herself. “That makes sense. I am serving the court now!” “We’ve always served the court,” Sui Yuntong said. An Jiu lightly jumped down, her expression noncommittal. Sui Yuntong asked, “What plan did you say you had?” “I want to recruit assassins on the bounty list! The bounty list is just an organization; there are not many assassins under its command. Those who accept bounties are mostly ‘freelancers,’ with a few martial arts masters occasionally coming out to earn a little money.” Sui Yuntong pondered. “That is one way.” An Jiu was secretly pleased. “I want to know how to subdue them.” “Force, benefits, or perhaps appealing to their emotions and reasoning!” Sui Yuntong answered without much thought. “The simplest way is to defeat them, forcibly establish a subordinate relationship, and then entice them with benefits. This is a common method in the martial arts world. But there’s another shortcut: compete for the title of Martial Arts Alliance Leader.” “Martial Arts Alliance Leader?” An Jiu had never heard this term before, but she roughly understood its meaning from the literal meaning. Sui Yuntong was slightly surprised to see her seemingly confused. He explained, “It’s the person who commands the martial arts world.” “That is good,” An Jiu asked enthusiastically. “Where is the martial arts world?” “Huh?” “Sui Yuntong was stumped by the question, “The martial world…is everywhere…” What kind of answer was that?! Since he did not know either, An Jiu had to change the question to, “How do you compete to become the leader of the martial arts alliance?” “The martial arts world holds a martial arts tournament every three years. At that time, a fighting arena will be set up. Whoever defeats everyone can challenge the leader. If you lose, the leader can take your place.” Sui Yuntong thought for a moment. “This leader only took office last year, and the martial arts tournament is still two years away.” An Jiu scoffed, “By the time I become the leader of the martial arts alliance, Wu Lingyuan’s grave will probably be overgrown with weeds!” Sui Yuntong thought of the fates of the previous two magistrates of Hexi County and felt that this statement was not a joke or an exaggeration at all. If Hexi County could not protect itself, the magistrate would definitely not have a good end. “It’s more reliable to subdue them one by one. We will split up these two days. You are responsible for recruiting ordinary strong men, and I will challenge martial arts masters.” An Jiu was not overconfident in her martial arts skills; she was overly insecure in her eloquence. Although Sui Yuntong did not doubt her martial arts abilities, he was still worried about her handling the matter alone. ‘We are in a hurry for a day or two. Once things are settled, I will go with you. After all, I understand the rules of the martial world better.'” An Jiu thought for a moment and reluctantly nodded in agreement. After agreeing, the two went to rest. Sui Yuntong, still shaken, checked all the doors and windows to avoid being startled again. The next day, news of the government starting to register households spread quickly, causing widespread anxiety. The entire city of Xingzhou became lively thanks to Gao Dazhuang’s swift and decisive actions. Sui Yuntong simply contacted the Xingzhou yamen and erected a sign in the teahouse next to the office, stating that Hejian Prefecture could accommodate the homeless with generous conditions: First, each adult would be allocated four mu of land; second, for ten years, they would not only be exempt from rent and taxes, but the imperial court would also provide a subsidy of five taels of silver; third, regardless of social status, once registered in Hejian Prefecture, they would be registered as free citizens. These three conditions were unbelievably generous, especially the last one, which was like heavenly music to those who had been of lowly birth for generations. Becoming a free citizen meant no longer being driven like cattle, being able to marry a respectable woman, and having children eligible to take the imperial examinations! Sui Yuntong hired a clever attendant from the teahouse to explain the notice’s contents to the onlookers at the entrance. However, a morning passed, and while the number of onlookers had not decreased, no one had come to register. After all, no matter how generous the conditions, one first needed to be alive to enjoy them! An Jiu, dressed in men’s clothing and wearing a bamboo hat, sat behind a screen drinking tea. She sat there listlessly all morning, somewhat puzzled. “Is what you are doing not blatantly telling them that Xingzhou and Hejian Prefecture colluded to initiate this household registration cleanup? Do you think they will willingly follow along? Besides, what kind of place is Hejian Prefecture? It would not be an exaggeration to call it a hunting ground of the Liao Kingdom.” Sui Yuntong lowered his eyes, glancing at the tea in his cup, and said slowly, “Our situation there is already bad. If we trick and forcibly recruit a bunch of rabble, they will only hold us back if something goes wrong. What we need are people who understand. Only when they understand what they want will they dedicate themselves to protecting these hard-won things. If they want to protect hope, then Hexi County has hope.” The last sentence was a bit convoluted, but after careful consideration, An Jiu found it quite reasonable. She thought to herself that Wu Lingyuan’s decision to send Sui Yuntong along was indeed prescient. “Hope…?” A faint smile appeared in An Jiu’s eyes. Sui Yuntong’s notice sparked a heated discussion in Xingzhou, but two days passed, and no one had volunteered. Sitting idly like this was not An Jiu’s style; she was always a woman of action. On the third day, she continued to sit in the teahouse. After finishing her breakfast, An Jiu sat at the table, legs crossed, watching the sparse crowd of onlookers outside. Her gaze fell on one who looked short and thin…The middle-aged man’s eyebrows were slightly raised. Sui Yuntong followed her gaze and saw that the man was ragged, his hair was like dry straw, and his face was covered in dirt. He looked like a beggar from the city, but he quickly noticed that his gaze was deep and focused. A person with such a gaze was no ordinary person. Just as Sui Yuntong was about to ask An Jiu what level of martial arts this man possessed, he turned his head and found that the seat was already empty! Looking back, An Jiu had already approached the man. A fourth-level martial artist was not particularly high, but An Jiu’s mental power far surpassed that of his. When they were only half a zhang apart, the man glanced at her but did not notice anything amiss. “Hey,” An Jiu stopped and called out to him. The man looked around. “You called me?” An Jiu slightly raised her chin, gesturing for him to look at the notice. “Interested?” The man became wary. He could not sense any mental power from An Jiu, nor could he discern any internal strength in her. Yet, this mysterious woman had chosen him directly from among the onlookers. He instinctively felt this was not a coincidence. He thought carefully for a moment, then nodded. “Then come with me,” An Jiu said. Her tone was calm, even cold, but the way she spoke so matter-of-factly gave her an air of authority, creating an undeniable sense of pressure. The man’s heart skipped a beat. “Who exactly are you?” An Jiu curled her lip. Her bamboo hat covered half her face, and this curled lip appeared to him as a profound, enigmatic smile. Just as he was feeling uneasy, he heard that clear, cold voice say, “What’s the point of hiding? Do you dare to come with me to snatch food from the tiger’s mouth?” A petite woman speaking so arrogantly in such a calm tone startled everyone around. No one dared to question her, because they would not even dare to utter such a question. “Haha! Good!” A tall, burly man beside him said, “The young lady is right! I am off to snatch food from the tiger’s mouth!” He then strode into the teahouse. The man was robust but not a martial arts master; An Jiu continued to stare intently at the beggar.

chapters.title: Xue Sha
chapters.content: In the teahouse, Sui Yuntong noted down the man’s basic information while keeping an eye on the situation outside. The man, who looked like a beggar, had originally intended to go to Hejian but was startled by An Jiu’s sudden appearance and began to hesitate. These days, women making a living outside were either widows or had special identities; he dared not agree, yet dared not refuse either. “I am truly sorry, brother. You are free to leave. My younger sister is young and playful; please forgive her,” Sui Yuntong broke the stalemate. An Jiu peeked at Sui Yuntong through the gap in her straw hat, clearly not understanding why he had suddenly lied. Upon hearing this, the man turned and quickly left. An Jiu’s mental power relentlessly followed him. “Why?” she asked Sui Yuntong. Sui Yuntong said, “Forced love is never sweet.” “Forced is forced; what’s the point of force?” An Jiu said, following the aura. Sui Yuntong sighed, letting her be. But he absolutely had to write to Lord Chu to complain about this matter; who else but he could handle such a tyrannical woman? Sui Yuntong truly felt powerless to do anything about it. An Jiu walked around two streets and arrived at a dilapidated courtyard, then climbed over the wall and went inside. The man was sitting by the well. Seeing the ghostly black-clad woman, he widened his eyes in surprise, staring blankly for a long time before finally standing up. “Who are you, young lady?” An Jiu was silent for a moment before speaking, “I am An Jiu, a soldier in the garrison of Hejian Prefecture. Would you like to join the army?” How could there be a woman in a regular army? It was obvious what she meant. The man smiled bitterly. “What, even Hejian Prefecture has secret guards now?” “Are you from the Konghe Army?” An Jiu asked in surprise, always spotting him right away. The man nodded honestly. “Code name: Xue Sha.” He was an assassin from the Konghe Army. He had been pardoned for his service in helping the current Emperor ascend the throne, following Chu Dingjiang. He knew this was not an imperial decree, but merely Chu Dingjiang giving them a chance to start a new life. Furthermore, lacking a registered residence, he had kept a low profile since arriving in Xingzhou. His money was almost gone, and if he did not find a way to survive soon, he feared starvation. Just then, a notice was posted in Hejian Prefecture recruiting people, and he was very tempted. Having a registered residence would allow him to go out and find normal work—that would be the real beginning! Moreover, even if the Liao and Song dynasties went to war, with his skills, he could protect himself in Hejian Prefecture, and when he returned, he would finally have a proper status! An Jiu looked at his ragged clothes and thought it was a real disgrace to his cool and arrogant code name. “Then you should not be so destitute. Were the assassins of the Konghe Army supposedly not poor, with only money left?” “Who carries silver around when they kill someone?” Xue Sha plopped down on the stone steps, his face utterly dejected. “I did not expect to have a chance to get out so soon. It was exciting for a few days at first, but then I realized that whether I got out or not made no difference, and I even felt emptier.” “Of course, you will feel empty if you have nothing to hold you back.” No one understood this feeling better than An Jiu. She tried to persuade Xue Sha, “We are a normal army, unlike the Konghe Army. Besides, what else can you do besides kill?” Everything assassins learned was for killing. For example, An Jiu, besides that, all she knew was herding sheep. But Xue Sha clearly disagreed. “I know a lot more. As long as I have a household registration, I can live openly and honestly.” An Jiu did not speak, staring at him without moving. After a while, Xue Sha said, “You do not believe me? I can concoct poisons, make silk flowers, and even write calligraphy!” “You are quite skillful. It is a pity you are not a girl; otherwise, you might be doing very well in the backyard.” An Jiu could not connect a scruffy old man with activities like “making silk flowers.” After a moment’s thought, she said, “I do not discriminate against you. Come with me.” Xue Sha was speechless. He tossed the water ladle back into the bucket and leaned against a pillar, sunbathing and dozing. An Jiu simply squatted down in front of him, staring at him more closely. As a seasoned assassin, Xue Sha was always the one staring at others; he had never been stared at like this before! Moreover, An Jiu’s mental energy was almost solidified; her gaze was almost tangible. He felt as if a knife was scraping across his body, and a slight tremor could end his life. After enduring this for a while, Xue Sha finally opened his eyes. “You are also from the Konghe Army?” An Jiu nodded. “Why should a fellow assassin make things difficult for another?” Xue Sha said, but inwardly, he was calculating whether he could win in a fight. The girl before him had no internal energy whatsoever, so how could she have found him so easily? And why did she show no fear upon hearing his name? Unable to ascertain her background, he hesitated to attack, only continuing to talk, hoping to find a way to escape her. Knowing your enemy was half the battle, so he decided to probe her identity. “Code name?” “An Jiu,” An Jiu blurted out, then remembered her code name in the Konghe Army was Xuan Ren. “What does this code name mean?” Xue Sha frowned, thinking carefully. In the Konghe Army, apart from ranked officers, most assassins used the Heavenly and Earthly Branches to identify themselves. Only assassins on the Konghe List were given special code names, and only the top ten had the right to choose their own names. Furthermore, only after an assassin’s death would a soul bell be engraved with their original name and hung on the building. An Jiu’s codename originally meant “Angel,” but that was not the case here. She thought for a moment, “Little Baby? Hmm, something like that.” Xue Sha looked at her with a conflicted expression, wondering if the Konghe Army really had such bizarre codenames. An Jiu was also full of curiosity about Xue Sha; it was the first time she’d seen an assassin with such a rich range of expressions. “You really do not recognize me?” Xue Sha asked. An Jiu looked at his seemingly warm but actually cold gaze and suddenly realized why he was so insistent on this answer. “You are on the Konghe List? Sorry, I only know three people on that list.” Xue Sha smiled. “I bet Gu Jinghong is one of them.” An Jiu remained silent. Xue Sha continued, “I heard he died while assassinating Yelu Huangwu. I’ve never understood why they would send him alone. Ah! What a pity he died!” Assassinating Yelu Huangwu was incredibly dangerous. Even if Gu Jinghong was at the top of the rankings, how could the Konghe Army send only him on a mission? Was that not practically sending him to his death? An Jiu scrutinized the seemingly melancholic middle-aged man and said calmly, “You do not need to go to such lengths to escape; you will not have that chance.” Xue Sha’s heart trembled. From the moment he saw An Jiu at the teahouse entrance until now, he felt trapped in an impenetrable net, unable to find a weakness. Now that he’d been exposed, he was too lazy to waste any more words. “I cannot go back to that kind of life! Do not force me to fight to the death!” He looked determined to die rather than submit. An Jiu wondered why there were so many effeminate men in the Konghe Army. Although Xue Sha looked like a normal man, not as flamboyant as Gao Dazhuang, he was clearly a somewhat feminine woman at heart. An Jiu did not know how to approach such a person, so she remained silent, simply watching him—watching him drink water, watching him eat, watching him go to the outhouse… “Are you not hungry?” Xue Sha could not hold back any longer and spoke first, handing her a piece of flatbread.

chapters.title: What Kind of Seed Is This?
chapters.content: An Jiu twitched her lips, reached out and took the pill, and then ate it directly, leaving Xue Sha stunned. What assassin could be so careless! An Jiu smacked her lips, savoring the sweet taste, then took a pill of Hundred Poisons Antidote and popped it into her mouth. “Do you know Mo Sigui?” “Divine Physician Mo?” Xue Sha straightened up. “He’s in Xingzhou too?” An Jiu had only wanted to show off her immunity to poison, but she had not expected Xue Sha to be so interested in Mo Sigui. “He’s in Hejian Prefecture.” “Really?” Xue Sha’s eyes lit up. Being in a profession that involved living on the edge, even if one did not die in the end, they would inevitably suffer from many ailments. An Jiu, realizing this, immediately used it. “Mo Sigui is our military physician. There are not many of us, and he personally takes care of everyone.” Currently, Mo Sigui was indeed responsible for everyone’s health, but that might change in the future. He was very busy and would not waste time on trivial matters. Xue Sha pondered for a long time. “You are all too naive. The Liao Kingdom’s overall military strength is superior to that of the Song Dynasty. Even if you rebuild a Konghe Army in Hejian Prefecture, it will not save the entire Song Dynasty.” “If everyone thought like you, the Song Dynasty would truly be doomed!” An Jiu, considering her own perspective, said, “Do not try to fill the void with other things. I am telling you from experience, it is impossible. Even if you spend your days visiting prostitutes, gambling, marrying, and making silk flowers, your heart will still be empty because even life is fragile and vulnerable. How utterly tasteless these trivial things are!” Xue Sha was momentarily lost in thought. He had done what An Jiu had described these past few days. Initially, he felt excited by the freedom and novelty, but as the days passed, he felt a longing growing within him, a strange longing that made him feel increasingly lonely. At the time, he did not know what he longed for, but now, hearing An Jiu’s words, he suddenly understood. It was blood; what he craved was the thrill of reaping lives with a blade. He had always thought he was weary of killing, but it turned out that beyond that weariness, he was also addicted. This was not contradictory; addicts loathed drugs, yet that did not stop them from continuing their descent. Seeing his expression soften, An Jiu said, “Do you not want to try? It is very interesting, much more interesting than your empty, wasted life. Protecting your country and satisfying yourself at the same time—why not?” In the past, the people in the organization had tempted her to kill in the same way, saying, “Kill him, kill him, and your soul will find peace.” An Jiu now knew that was wrong, but given the current situation, protecting the country inevitably meant killing people. She figured it was acceptable to say that… “I only made it onto the Konghe List three years ago,” Xue Sha said, gazing at the azure sky, his eyes softening. “It was because I killed ten assassins from Piaomiao Mountain Mansion in a clandestine battle. I originally intended to annihilate them all, but in the end, one named Xue Sha escaped. From the moment I was qualified to have my own special codename, I took the name Xue Sha. There is only one Xue Sha in this world, and he must die. However, before I could even make my move, Lord Chu led his men to raid Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, and Xue Sha died in that attack.” His expression was pained. His eyes were bloodshot. It was as if Xue Sha was his own flesh and blood, but An Jiu knew that he had an unresolved knot in his heart because he had not personally killed that person. An Jiu suddenly remembered something her former psychologist had said: “As a top assassin, you were either numb and indifferent, always wearing an eternally cold, expressionless face, or you were a psychopath with uncontrollable emotions.” Now it seemed Xue Sha was a psychopath too. “I will go with you,” Xue Sha said. Seeing that he did not go berserk, An Jiu thought to herself, “His condition is not that serious after all!” “Alright!” An Jiu said. Since that day, she had entered a completely new field in her life, deciding that she could now act as a psychological counselor for the assassins around her. An Jiu found a martial arts master and was quite satisfied with the trip, but recruiting in Xingzhou was not progressing particularly smoothly. In seven whole days, she had only managed to gather a total of about sixty people, including men, women, and children. After all, some people would rather be slaves than go to their deaths. Thanks to Gao Dazhuang’s help, Sui Yuntong decided to go and thank him in person before leaving and also ask him for another favor. At the Xingzhou military camp. Gao Dazhuang, with his delicate fingers raised, sipped his tea, his narrow eyes slightly narrowed. While his manner was somewhat effeminate, it was undeniable that he was handsome, not in a seductive way. If he removed that hint of femininity, he would likely be a dashing young man. “My Lord, I must thank you for this matter,” Sui Yuntong said. “This is a tonic prescribed by Physician Mo, which can aid in cultivating mental power. Please accept it.” Gao Dazhuang remained expressionless but did not refuse. An Jiu, looking at his lowered eyes, suspected he was secretly overjoyed. Back in the Konghe Academy, he had desperately tried to curry favor with Mo Sigui but failed! “If you are so tough, just say what you are thinking!” Gao Dazhuang could not stand her gaze any longer. An Jiu paused, then asked, “What kind of seed is ‘so tough’?” Gao Dazhuang scoffed, his face a mask of utter sarcasm, as if to say, “You illiterate fool.” Sui Yuntong thought to himself, An Jiu was truly a naive woman. “I understand,” An Jiu admired her own comprehension. “My Chu Dingjiang has it, I don’t.” Sui Yuntong wiped his sweat, secretly retracting his earlier assessment. An Jiu looked at Gao Dazhuang and added, “You do not either.” Clang! Gao Dazhuang instantly went berserk, smashing his teacup and drawing his sword! An Jiu reflexively drew the sword hidden behind her back. “My Lord!” In the blink of an eye, Sui Yuntong, caught off guard by this turn of events, rushed between the two without a second thought. A murderous aura surged. The tip of the blade was about to pierce Sui Yuntong when Gao Dazhuang and An Jiu simultaneously deflected their attacks, clashing five chi in front of him! Sparks flew as the blades rubbed together, neither giving in. They were both assassins; their moves meant death. Sui Yuntong was frantic. “Fourteenth, stop! We have more important matters to attend to.” An Jiu, hearing this, indeed stopped. Gao Dazhuang’s blade continued its momentum, slashing straight at An Jiu’s face. Sui Yuntong tried to block it, but he was no match for the blade. An Jiu, seeing the cold, sharp edge, did not flinch; instead, her back straightened even more. The blade deflected again, a powerful surge of energy grazing past her, shattering the doors and windows behind her. An Jiu’s clothes and hair flew wildly, but her expression remained unchanged. “You’d better take this little dwarf and get out of here!” Gao Dazhuang pointed at Sui Yuntong with his blade. “Get as far away as you can!” “We are fighting the Liao people. Are you interested?” An Jiu suddenly asked. A bead of sweat trickled down Sui Yuntong’s temple. He thought, “How can you be so clueless! Is this the time to be saying such things?” He quickly tugged at An Jiu’s sleeve. “Let’s go.” Since persuading Xue Sha, An Jiu’s confidence had soared. She felt that recruiting Gao Dazhuang would definitely make things much easier.

chapters.title: Shattered Worldview
chapters.content: “I really underestimated you!” Gao Dazhuang sneered. “Did you also lose face at Chu Dingjiang’s place today?” “Yes,” An Jiu nodded. “Luckily, I have Chu Dingjiang.
