Who did you leave yours with?” “You!” Gao Dazhuang’s chest heaved with anger, his expression suggesting he wanted to tear her to pieces. Sui Yuntong grabbed An Jiu’s sleeve and dragged her out. Once they were out of the military camp, he whispered, “I was hoping Lord Gao could help keep the proclamation posted in Xingzhou! You’ve angered him so much; I cannot ask anymore.” What use were the people recruited in such a short time? If the proclamation was kept up, there would always be people who might want to go to Hexi County. “He’s not a short-tempered or easily angered person.” An Jiu could not see through people’s hearts, but she was very sensitive to killing intent. Gao Dazhuang’s killing intent was stable; his emotions clearly were not fluctuating much. “But just now…” “I do not know. I only know he did not intend to kill me.” In An Jiu’s eyes, Gao Dazhuang was an anomaly; he seemed to have a rich array of emotions yet also possessed strong self-control. “You said…” An Jiu pondered. “Could Mo Sigui reattach Gao Dazhuang’s penis?” Sui Yuntong coughed awkwardly twice, not wanting to discuss this issue with a young girl. “I do not know. Let’s stay for two more days, and I will go see him after Gao Dazhuang’s anger subsides.” An Jiu nodded haphazardly, lost in her own world. “I wonder, if he can recover, will he come with us?” “Fourteenth, Gao Dazhuang is now an official of the court. Without the Emperor’s permission, he cannot go anywhere.” Sui Yuntong decisively cut off her unrealistic thoughts. “Gao Dazhuang also said that he initially applied for a posting to a distant post at Hejian Prefecture, but His Majesty rejected it. I think His Majesty has a deeper meaning in arranging him here.” “What deeper meaning could there be? Is it not because he feels the Hebei army is not strong enough, and he wants him here as a second line of defense? General Ling is returning to court. Sooner or later, he will have to take over the Hebei army. Gao Dazhuang can be the first line of defense, and General Ling the second. Is that not good?” An Jiu looked at him earnestly. “I only started thinking of winning him over because I heard he was interested in going to Hejian. It is possible, is it not?” Sui Yuntong said, “You are right, but you forgot to consider Gao Dazhuang’s importance in His Majesty’s heart.” An Jiu paused slightly, then nodded in agreement. The current Emperor had only recently ascended the throne. He had a mess to deal with, and there were not many capable people to begin with. A loyal follower like Gao Dazhuang was even more precious. His Majesty would never let Gao Dazhuang be the vanguard until his position was completely secure. Sui Yuntong smiled. “But your words have reminded me. Lord Gao is interested in Hejian Prefecture and will most likely help us.” An Jiu realized that recruiting Gao Dazhuang was impossible, so she lazily grunted and offered no opinion. The two stayed in Xingzhou for another two days. Afterwards, Sui Yuntong went alone to see Gao Dazhuang, asking him to help recruit people in Xingzhou who wanted to go to Hexi County. Gao Dazhuang agreed without hesitation. The two returned to Hexi County with the sixty-odd people they had recruited. During their absence, Wu Lingyuan had reorganized Hexi County, and the belated spring planting was underway. The sixty-odd people were immediately struck by the vibrant scene upon arriving in Hexi County. They immediately felt they had made the right choice. Hexi County had been looted for so many years; while it could not be said that nine out of ten houses were empty, more than half were already abandoned. The houses, having been looted and empty for so long, were more or less dilapidated. But these people were either homeless or living under the roof of others; now, suddenly having their own homes and land, they were overjoyed. No one complained. Besides houses and land, Wu Lingyuan also had enough five days’ worth of rice and grain delivered to each family on the first day. The yamen was short-staffed, and when Wu Lingyuan saw that An Jiu had brought back a martial arts instructor, he insisted on making him the head constable. This greatly troubled Xue Sha. He grabbed An Jiu and lamented, “Were we not supposed to fight the Liao people? What am I supposed to do if all I know is killing?” Unfortunately, Wu Lingyuan overheard him and confiscated his swords and hidden weapons, handing him a wooden stick about the thickness of a finger. “If anyone commits a crime, use this to whip them. Do not use your internal energy.” Wu Lingyuan patted his shoulder. “I heard from Ah Jiu that you used to be very skilled. I believe you can do it. The yamen has confirmed it. You will have to bear with it for a few days.” Under Wu Lingyuan’s expectant gaze, Xue Sha gritted his teeth and accepted the stick. “Does the constable have uniforms?” “Oh, I suddenly remembered I have some things to take care of. You two chat first; we can talk about it tomorrow.” Wu Lingyuan slapped his forehead and hurried away. An Jiu said, “Hexi County is poor and cannot afford to issue clothes right now. I have a few new ones; I will get them for you later.” Xue Sha nodded, brandishing the wooden stick in his hand. “Does he not know you can kill with a stick…?” “He does not know martial arts,” An Jiu said. “Just whip them around. If you really encounter a murderer or arsonist, you can still count it as a martial arts achievement.” “That is good,” Xue Sha tucked the stick into his belt. An Jiu reminded him, “Hexi County has a small population; it is best to leave some alive.” Xue Sha asked, puzzled, “What’s the point of keeping criminals alive?” Yes, what was the point? They were just wasting food! The magistrate of Hexi County was struggling to make ends meet, and there was no prison food available. An Jiu thought carefully and finally came up with a reasonable explanation: “More people will reproduce.” Xue Sha exclaimed in admiration, “I did not expect you to have such foresight at such a young age.” An Jiu smiled subtly yet proudly. “My family has a good upbringing; I’ve been influenced by what I’ve seen and heard. I will introduce you to my Master Chu sometime.” Wu Lingyuan had not gone far, and overhearing their conversation, he nearly burst out laughing. What was all this about? There were strange people everywhere, especially in the Konghe Army. Wu Lingyuan was relieved that Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi were relatively normal! However, he soon witnessed Sui Yuntong’s “abnormality.” A month later, Chu Dingjiang sent another batch of valuables. The escort was a burly woman named Xu Huniu, in her early twenties. Because of her fierce reputation and unattractive appearance, she had remained unmarried. Chu Dingjiang always took An Jiu’s words to heart. An Jiu had instructed him to find a fierce woman for Sui Yuntong as a wife, and he promptly arranged for someone to come for a blind date. After reading Chu Dingjiang’s letter, An Jiu enthusiastically dragged Sui Yuntong to the meeting. Xu Huniu was also aware of the blind date. When she saw such a handsome man as Sui Yuntong, her eyes widened, and her face radiated delight. Wu Lingyuan was inwardly lamenting that the supposedly reliable Chu Dingjiang was a bit unreliable this time when he saw Sui Yuntong’s handsome face slightly flushed as he said, “Miss Xu is very nice.” That very day, the two held hands and watched the sunset. Wu Lingyuan’s worldview was shattered; he needed some time to recover. Seeing his dejected appearance, An Jiu comforted him, “Do not be envious. I will write a letter to Chu Dingjiang and ask him to find you one, too.”

chapters.title: Silk Flowers
chapters.content: Wu Lingyuan was so frightened that his heart was pounding wildly. He hurriedly said, “No, no, I’ve been betrothed since childhood; once I’ve made a name for myself, I will go and marry her.” An Jiu patted him on the shoulder, said nothing, and walked out, leaving him feeling utterly unsettled. As a renowned assassin on the Konghe List, Xue Sha handled his role as a head constable with ease. Since the government currently lacked the funds to issue uniforms, he spent his days dressed in ordinary clothes, sitting on street corners, making and selling silk flowers. Whenever he spotted someone up to no good, he’d step in and knock them out with a single blow. Having been an assassin for so long, he had a habit of concealing his movements; none of the people he struck ever saw his face. Word spread like wildfire, and people began to believe that Hexi County was protected by ghosts and gods. For a time, no one dared to commit any misdeeds, and in just a short while, Hexi County became a place where people did not pick up what others dropped on the street and left their doors unlocked at night. With no criminals left to deal with, Xue Sha grew bored and began beating even those who failed to care for children. There were not many children in Hexi County to begin with, and each parent doted on them, leaving Xue Sha no opportunity to shine. When An Jiu arrived on the street, she saw Xue Sha dressed in an ancient blue outfit, sitting cross-legged under a willow tree. His hair was casually tied up with a withered willow branch, and his excessively pale face made him look like a frail scholar, incapable of even killing a chicken. He was quite ordinary-looking; he would have gone unnoticed in a crowd, but his appearance stood out in the Konghe Army. An Jiu watched as his slender fingers moved swiftly, and a beautiful flower bloomed from his pale fingertips. Beside him was a blue cloth covered with many neatly arranged flowers. “Uncle, the silk flowers you made are so beautiful!” A girl of about ten years old stopped in front of him. Xue Sha paused slightly and looked up at her. The girl was startled by his cold gaze but quickly regained her composure. Xue Sha smiled and offered her a pink peach blossom. The girl breathed a slight sigh of relief, smiling and shaking her head. “I do not have the money to buy it.” Her clothes were clean and tidy but faded from washing and patched in places. Xue Sha did not speak, but stood up and pinned a peach blossom in her hair, whispering, “It’s free.” The girl was somewhat surprised but quickly frowned, reaching out to take the silk flower back and return it to Xue Sha. “My mother said I should not take other people’s things, or I will be punished by ghosts and gods.” The girl reluctantly put the flower down, turned, and ran away quickly. Xue Sha picked up the peach blossom, examined it, and flicked it lightly, the flower landing precisely on the girl’s head. “Looks like you are adapting quite well,” An Jiu said. Xue Sha then noticed An Jiu. “I’ve never been able to see through your cultivation level. How can you so easily deceive me when you clearly have no internal energy? Could you be a Transcendent External Cultivator?” He had never heard of any powerful external cultivators in the Konghe Army. “Guess,” An Jiu squatted down in front of the blue cloth, examining the silk flowers on the ground closely. They were even more vibrant and dazzling than real flowers. “Your craftsmanship is indeed excellent! Where did you get the fabric?” “I bought it back in Bianjing,” Xue Sha replied. An Jiu was speechless. He did not think to bring money when he was killing people, yet he thought to buy fabric. What was she to say? “Looking at your age, why not find a wife?” She had been holding a grudge ever since Wu Lingyuan rejected her offer. “Find one for Li Qingzhi. I am not interested in that,” Xue Sha said. An Jiu thought to herself, “Will it not be another tall, strong woman?” Xue Sha seemed to read her mind. “I had a few lovers in the Konghe Army. For me, matters of the heart are just a way to relieve stress. I am fine now; I am not interested in that kind of thing.” Those living in darkness may have hearts as hard as ice, but in certain aspects, they could be unrestrained and wild, such as in sex. An Jiu had heard about the practice of finding companions within the Konghe Army, and seeing that he truly had no interest in that, she did not press the matter. Instead, she asked, “Do you know of any other members of the Konghe Army?” Xue Sha thought for a moment. “There might be some in Zhending Prefecture.” “Great! Come with me tomorrow!” An Jiu exclaimed happily. Zhending Prefecture was not far, only about thirty li away. An Jiu said, “I just discussed it with Mo Sigui; we will examine you today.” “Alright,” Xue Sha smiled. The two returned to the yamen and went straight to Mo Sigui’s room. His quarters were, as usual, shrouded in mist, making one drowsy upon entering. In the hazy mist, a gray-haired man in blue robes sat cross-legged on a futon, his handsome face possessing a touch of otherworldly beauty. Xue Sha assumed this was the Divine Physician Mo and was about to greet him when a lazy voice came from deeper within the mist: “Come here; let me see.” An Jiu nodded to Xue Sha. He glanced at the gray-haired man and walked inside. In the dim light, Xue Sha saw a man in a wide, gray-blue robe leaning against a low couch, a long pipe in his left hand and a thin letter in his right. His brows were furrowed, and his peach-blossom eyes held a mixture of contemplation and languor—truly the dashing and unrestrained figure of legend. Mo Sigui tapped his extinguished pipe, looked up, his gaze sweeping across Xue Sha’s face, and reached out to feel his pulse.

chapters.title: You Are A Puppet
chapters.content: A gust of wind blew the letter Mo Sigui had placed on the couch to the ground. An Jiu picked it up, glancing at it as she went. It was a secret letter from Wei Yuzhi’s subordinate, detailing the Liao Kingdom’s secret medicine for cultivating experts and also containing information about Lou Mingyue. “There’s residual poison in your body. I’ll prescribe some medicine first.” Mo Sigui swiftly wrote a prescription. “The internal organ injuries are quite interesting; we will treat them after clearing the poison.” Xue Sha, seeing that he had accurately described all his problems, was even more convinced. “Thank you, Divine Physician.” Mo Sigui glanced at An Jiu. “Thank her.” “Did you not say you’d severed all ties with Lou Mingyue?” An Jiu handed over the letter. Mo Sigui did not take it. He stuffed another wad of medicine into his pipe, lit it, took two puffs, and then asked, “Who is Lou Mingyue?” An Jiu shook the letter in her hand. “I glanced at the message Yuzhi sent out of boredom. Ning Yanli’s internal energy-boosting drug has improved again. Looks like I need to get the antidote!” Mo Sigui smiled, his peach blossom eyes curving slightly, like a faint peach hue spreading through swirling clouds. An Jiu was not one to meddle, but she felt that his entangled relationship with Lou Mingyue would not end well. Seeing that he did not seem to care, she did not ask further. “Can you not also concoct a drug to boost internal energy?” She thought that would be more useful. Mo Sigui laughed, “Ha! How can doing what others have done demonstrate my skill?” An Jiu said, “So you can concoct it?” “Do not even think about it.” Mo Sigui slowly exhaled a puff of smoke, which coalesced in the air into a shape resembling a lingzhi mushroom. “That kind of potent drug that boosts potential will inevitably have a fatal backlash. After the effects dissipate, it is either death or permanent damage. Who do you plan to give it to?” “When will the antidote be available? We might have to fight the Liao army after autumn,” An Jiu asked. Seeing her serious expression, Mo Sigui chuckled, “Seriousness ages you prematurely. Just look at Chu Dingjiang! Haha!” “You know Lord Chu?” Xue Sha could not help but interject. “You do not recognize a great man, do you?” Mo Sigui glanced at An Jiu. “This lady! She’s Lord Chu’s lover.” “Lover…” Xue Sha could not help but look at An Jiu. To be fair, she was an absolute beauty. “Lover.” An Jiu silently prayed for “world peace,” suppressing her rage, and slowly said, “There’s nothing wrong with that. Some people are practically begging to be someone’s lover, but others avoid them like the plague.” “Someone as dashing and handsome as me, anyone who does not want me is blind!” Mo Sigui scoffed. There was a knock on the door. Then Sui Yuntong said, “Lord Wu said he’s been busy with official duties since arriving in Hexi County, and today he’d like to take some time to treat everyone to a meal.” Mo Sigui, always picky about food, had been eating simple meals for almost half a month since arriving and was feeling quite frustrated. Hearing this, he quickly got out of bed and put on his shoes. “When do we eat?” “The food is ready; we are just waiting for you all,” Sui Yuntong said. An Jiu, not bothering to argue with him, went out first. Sui Yuntong peeked out and saw Wei Yuzhi sitting cross-legged, seemingly resting. “Master Wei, Lord Wu said he would also like you to join us if you have the time.” Wei Yuzhi did not move, only giving a faint “hmm.” The banquet was set up in the flower hall, with Wu Lingyuan, dressed in a dark brown casual robe, sitting at the head of the table. He rose to greet everyone as they entered, but no one paid him any attention; everyone was focused on the dishes on the table. Mo Sigui, pipe in hand, looked around and commented. “Not bad.” Hexi County did not have much to offer, but fortunately, it was the transition from spring to summer, and the mountains and fields were full of good things. Wu Lingyuan had Li Qingzhi hunt some game, and they managed to prepare a decent meal. “Little Sui, quickly go to my room and get some good wine!” Mo Sigui said, “It’s next to the bookshelf on the south wall.” Sui Yuntong was willing to go without complaint, but An Jiu was unhappy. “Do not go; let him go by himself!” “An Da Jiu, I’ve been your slave, and this is how you treat me?” Mo Sigui sighed softly. “People’s hearts are no longer what they used to be.” Just then, Wei Yuzhi entered, carrying a wine jar in each hand. “Oh dear! Yuzhi, how can you be so considerate!” Mo Sigui hurriedly took the wine jars. Wei Yuzhi’s sudden appearance made Xue Sha suddenly feel that this place was full of hidden talents. When had he approached without him noticing at all? “I knew you forgot to bring them, so I just grabbed them,” Wei Yuzhi said. Mo Sigui had recently been trying to quit smoking and drinking drugs, so he had personally mixed some alcohol to help him sleep when he could not sleep at night. It worked for the first two days, but now he was addicted to both. Wei Yuzhi had tried to persuade him, but he replied, “If I am going to fall into depravity, I should fall into it completely. Otherwise, it is not in line with my usual pursuit of perfection.” After everyone was seated, Wu Lingyuan raised his wine cup and said, “Great kindness needs no thanks. I will drink this first as a sign of respect.” Everyone raised their cups and drank. Mo Sigui tasted each dish, then ate only what he liked, refusing to touch anything else. After devouring the meal, Wu Lingyuan put down his bowl, rinsed his mouth, and sat up straight. “I am sure everyone knows the situation in Hexi County. Everything is in ruins, and there’s much to be done, but we are currently too poor. If we rely solely on agriculture, we cannot even defend the city. So I’ve come up with a plan, but I still need your help.” With that, he rose and bowed deeply to everyone. Sui Yuntong quickly offered a gesture of support: “We came here precisely for this purpose. We will do our utmost to fulfill any orders, My Lord.” Wu Lingyuan smiled gratefully, looked around, and said, “Compared to the surrounding counties, Hexi does not really have any advantages. It only has more rivers and lakes than other places. Summer is approaching, and I’ve had people catch fish and shrimp to make some side dishes to sell, but there’s no way to do so. The court does not allow officials to engage in commerce themselves, so I will have to trouble you all to spread the word in the surrounding counties.” “Go to the streets and shout?” Li Qingzhi asked nervously. They were all used to hiding their tracks and acting alone; asking them to stand on the streets and shout was really asking too much. “No,” Wu Lingyuan smiled slightly. “You all should first go to each county and find a shop, hire a few honest managers and employees, and run your own businesses. If they sell well, then you can start mass production, since these are perishable goods.” “I knew it was a trap.” Mo Sigui leaned back in his chair, casually lighting a cigarette. “I am not going.” “The Divine Physician does not need to go,” Wu Lingyuan paused, then said with difficulty. “But the government is currently facing serious difficulties. If the Divine Physician has time, could you perhaps make a couple of house calls…?” Mo Sigui was silent for a few moments, then finally nodded. “I will not treat patients with fees below five thousand taels, and I will not treat patients within a radius of twenty li.” Wu Lingyuan’s clear eyes smiled slightly. He took out a piece of paper from his sleeve and handed it to Mo Sigui. “Divine Physician, take a look. Are these a good option?” Mo Sigui opened his mouth, staring at the strict, disciplined handwriting on the paper. The paper listed far more than just a few! It clearly listed more than a dozen! He lived right here in this courtyard, and he had not even known when Wu Lingyuan had contacted these people! “The renowned physician is too good to be true; they would not dare let him travel back and forth so much. I am planning to prepare some courtyards for them to stay in.” Wu Lingyuan said, then asked respectfully. “What does the physician think?” “Damn it!” Mo Sigui could not help but slam his fist on the table. “These are all emergencies! You want to work me to death!” “The capable should give more; the capable should do more! Haha.” Wu Lingyuan laughed weakly. Seeing Mo Sigui staring at the paper without speaking, Wu Lingyuan then looked at Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi. “A security escort agency in Hejian Prefecture recently received a large order to transport goods to Xijin Prefecture, but they lack good escorts, so they are hiring two at a high price…” Sui Yuntong’s heart skipped a beat. “You’ve already agreed, My Lord?” If it were an assassination mission to Liao, Sui Yuntong would be more accepting. Escorts—if nothing went wrong, they were fine; but if something did, they were sitting ducks! “Haha. I think you two are both capable people from the Konghe Army; this is just a small matter…” Li Qingzhi could not sit still any longer. “You’ve really agreed!” Wu Lingyuan pursed his lips, remaining silent, his calm gaze carrying a hint of apology. “Never mind. It is not far anyway; I was just thinking of going to the Liao Kingdom!” Li Qingzhi said. Sui Yuntong had no choice but to nod. Wu Lingyuan breathed a sigh of relief. “Then I will immediately tell them you’ve agreed.” “…” “Xue Sha…” Wu Lingyuan looked over. Xue Sha immediately said. “I will follow Miss An, even if it means death.” Everyone looked at An Jiu. An Jiu glanced at Xue Sha, then got up and ran! Xue Sha’s figure blurred as he followed. “Ah, there’s even such a rogue method!” Mo Sigui blew on his cigarette. “What kind of mess is this!” The reason they followed them to Hexi was mostly because of An Jiu, so while everyone obediently let Wu Lingyuan exploit them, she ran away! Wu Lingyuan had not expected his seemingly stern benefactor to have this side to her. Helpless, he turned his gaze to Wei Yuzhi, who had been sitting quietly. Wei Yuzhi, sleeves tucked in, slightly raised his eyes, meeting Wu Lingyuan’s gaze with a half-smile. He appeared incredibly gentle, his light gray-brown eyes possessing an inexplicable depth. Under his indifferent gaze, Wu Lingyuan felt as if a mountain were pressing down on him. But Wu Lingyuan, always composed, withstood the pressure and said seriously, “My Lord, Hexi County is short of a county lieutenant. Would you be willing to accept the position?” Even Mo Sigui, who was nearly asleep, was startled by these words. Wei Yuzhi smiled, surprisingly shy. “I am afraid I will never have the chance to serve as an official in the Song Dynasty.” Wu Lingyuan was astute; he knew this seemingly harmless man was actually the most capable. Asking him to be his deputy was already audacious; if the man refused, he would not dare to coerce him as he had with Mo Sigui and the others. Just as Wu Lingyuan was about to give up trying to persuade him, Wei Yuzhi unexpectedly threw him a choice: “I am willing to be your advisor, helping you gain absolute power. Are you willing to be a puppet for five years?” Anyone in Wu Lingyuan’s position would not be happy to hear this, yet the temptation of absolute power was too great, almost on par with usurping the throne. Everyone expected Wu Lingyuan to say he would consider it, but to everyone’s surprise, he smiled openly and calmly, “If you truly have the ability, My Lord, why not accept?” The conversation seemed playful, yet both were incredibly serious. “Tsk tsk, you two, find a quiet place to play your game. I am leaving,” Mo Sigui said, standing up and leisurely walking out. Sui Yuntong and Li Qingzhi also left. Only the two of them remained sitting facing each other in the room. Wu Lingyuan said, “I still do not know your esteemed name, My Lord.” “Wei Yuzhi?” Wu Lingyuan was slightly surprised. “The Second Master of Piaomiao Mountain Mansion!” He did not know the inner workings of Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, but Wei Yuzhi was known as a wise man. Living in the chaotic Jiangkou area, he had heard of him, but he did not know what Wei Yuzhi had done to achieve his reputation. Wu Lingyuan’s years of blindness had cultivated a magnanimous nature, allowing him to think things through. If someone more capable than he existed, being a leisurely county magistrate would not be so bad. However, he was somewhat puzzled. “With your abilities, obtaining an official position through the imperial examinations would not be difficult, My Lord. Why do you insist on condescending to be my advisor?” “Because of my status as a monk. Besides, my lifespan is limited. If I wait until I pass through layers of selection, perhaps I will not have time to do anything before I am gone.” During this time, Wei Yuzhi had thought a lot. When he saw Wu Lingyuan, he felt this was an opportunity presented to him by heaven, perhaps a guiding hand in the dark. Wu Lingyuan sighed inwardly, “I do not seek absolute power; I only wish to do something for the Song Dynasty.” “No. These are my conditions for becoming your advisor,” Wei Yuzhi said calmly but firmly. “I can help you do anything you cannot or dare not do, but you must stand at the pinnacle of power to eradicate the Song Dynasty’s century-old woes, fearless even against imperial authority.” Looking at Wu Lingyuan’s shocked expression, he continued, “The so-called ‘puppet’ is merely a test. I am willing to serve you, as long as you swear before me to fulfill the conditions I have stated above.” “Power?!” Wu Lingyuan’s throat went dry. He had never considered such a crazy thing; he only wanted to do something for his country and its people. Wei Yuzhi slightly curled his lips. “If the Emperor is weak, he will be fooled, wielding absolute power. If the Emperor is strong, he will be obeyed, disregarding personal reputation.” If the Emperor were as unreliable as before, he would be fooled, wielding immense power and controlling everything. If the Emperor were capable, he would serve him, doing anything to rectify the court and eliminate corruption, regardless of the infamy. But Wu Lingyuan had always wanted to be a loyal minister… Wei Yuzhi had already seen through his thoughts. “This world is not someone’s plaything. The Emperor, by the mandate of heaven, bears the heavy responsibility of governing the world. If he cannot bring prosperity to the world, why should we, with our aspirations, serve him like dogs and horses?” “You are right, My Lord.” Wu Lingyuan did not intend to be a slave to the Emperor; it was only under the influence of the “loyalty to the Emperor” ideology that he did not harbor such a bold idea as Wei Yuzhi. Wei Yuzhi’s expression remained unchanged. “Since we’ve come this far, I am not afraid to be frank with you; I previously worked for the Liao Kingdom.” “Why?” Wei Yuzhi sensed he had a reason. Wei Yuzhi remained silent for a moment, then briefly recounted his background. “My family has been loyal and virtuous for generations, yet were unjustly killed. I wanted to personally destroy this decay, but recently I’ve come to realize that there are other ways to achieve my desires. It is just that destruction is more painful than change, so I subconsciously chose that path first.” Most people facing the injustice of their family’s extermination would think of seeking justice and revenge. Wei Yuzhi, however, had long seen through the corruption beneath the prosperous facade of the Song Dynasty. His path to justice was hopeless; his family was not wiped out by any one person, but by the environment itself. Now he had killed the mastermind behind the case and had understood many things. “You want me to overturn your case?” Wu Lingyuan asked.

chapters.title: Betrayal
chapters.content: Wei Yuzhi lowered his eyes. “If there’s a chance, it would be good to seek justice.” “My Lord, you do not seem to care much about the family’s reputation?” Wu Lingyuan asked, puzzled. “You’ve read many history books, have you not?” Wei Yuzhi raised his eyes, his eyes slightly red. “My father’s affair, if it leaves any trace in the history books in the future, will only be a few words, not worth anything that scoundrel Emperor did. It is not worth spending a lifetime scheming for a few words. Besides, right and wrong, people do things, and Heaven is watching.” He sat with his back to the door. The sunlight outside was too bright for Wu Lingyuan to clearly discern his expression, but he had a feeling that he was not exaggerating. “When I met Yelu Quancang, the Liao Kingdom had no place to tolerate a monk. Over the years, I’ve used every trick in the book to help him ascend the throne. Now, his reign is still unstable, and he already has no place for me.” Wei Yuzhi lightly tapped the armrest, a smile playing on his lips. “If I were to help you gain absolute power in the Song Dynasty, then my life…would not have been in vain.” Even after his eye ailment healed, Wu Lingyuan’s eyesight was still not as good as normal, so he did not see Wei Yuzhi’s reddened eyes, nor the rare look of pain on his face. His entire life had been a stepping stone for others. Wei Yuzhi pursed his lips and rose to leave. An old pear tree in the courtyard was in full bloom with white blossoms. Wei Yuzhi walked beneath it, petals falling but none touching him. He reached the courtyard, then suddenly stopped and turned back, looking up at An Jiu sitting on the roof. The surrounding petals seemed to pause for a moment. An Jiu had excellent eyesight; even from this distance, she could clearly see his reddened eyes. Even without seeing him, she could not suppress the dull ache in her heart. Never before had An Jiu so desperately wanted to sever this tie with him. “You want to kill me?” Wei Yuzhi asked with a smile. An Jiu was slightly taken aback. She admitted to herself that for a moment, the thought had crossed her mind, but the thought of Wei Yuzhi as her savior quickly suppressed it, so fast that she did not even realize it. He looked at An Jiu’s face, his smile deepening. But it also appeared resolute and cold, his powerful mental strength instantly tearing the surrounding pear blossoms to shreds. A chill ran through An Jiu’s heart. After a long while, she sensed a trace of desolation within it. Although Wei Yuzhi had spent his entire life giving to others, he was not the kind of person who gave without expecting anything in return. He had sacrificed himself twice to save An Jiu because of an inexplicable feeling, yet he had received no response. He was angry because he clearly saw everything and clearly did not want to continue giving like this, but could not stop. An Jiu jumped off the roof and followed the path he had taken to the pavilion. “Let me be alone,” Wei Yuzhi said calmly. “Since you have Chu Dingjiang, you should avoid me; otherwise, I cannot guarantee what I might do.” “I chose Wu Lingyuan, and you chose Wu Lingyuan too. We cannot be two parallel lines,” An Jiu frowned. “Do you mean you want me to give up? You saved my life. If you demand repayment in this way, I will leave.” Wei Yuzhi’s face darkened. Fate was too cruel. It did not give him even the slightest chance to escape. “Have Lord Wu request permission for you to take command of the troops stationed outside the city,” Wei Yuzhi said. This was exactly the result An Jiu hoped for. She nodded, hesitated for a moment, and asked, “How about I introduce you to a girl?” Even the composed Wei Yuzhi could not help but laugh in exasperation. “Like Xu Huniu?” “What kind of girl do you like?” An Jiu asked seriously. She did not like owing favors and was eager to repay them. She had finally found something she could do for him, so naturally, she was even more attentive. Wei Yuzhi remained silent for a moment before speaking, “She cannot be less attractive than you. She must be intelligent but pure of heart, never deceive me, have only me in her heart, be caring and attentive, skilled in music, weiqi, calligraphy, and painting, gentle and charming, and resilient.” Finding a woman who met these requirements was difficult, but it would at least repay his kindness, so An Jiu readily agreed, “Alright.” Wei Yuzhi watched her figure disappear among the lush flowers and trees before withdrawing his gaze. When one had not met that person, one had a bunch of requirements in one’s mind; once one fell in love, all those requirements ceased to be requirements. Wei Yuzhi had never mentally visualized what a partner would look like; all his requirements today were just casual remarks. Even if such a woman were before him, he might not be moved. An Jiu went back and found paper and pen, preparing to write a letter to Chu Dingjiang. Sitting at her desk, biting the brush holder, An Jiu suddenly felt a tightness in her chest; she longed to see him. After thinking for a long time, An Jiu sighed, picked up her brush, and wrote, “I miss you.” And then, “Please find Wei Yuzhi a wife! Requirements are as follows…” … Night fell. In a courtyard in Xijin Prefecture, lush ancient trees completely shaded the entire courtyard. A lantern hung from each branch, illuminating the courtyard as if it were daytime, yet only faint lights could be seen from the outside. A small table sat in the middle of a low couch on the veranda. On one side sat Yelu Jinglie, dressed in plain robes, and on the other sat a woman in blue wearing a half-mask. Yelu Jinglie slowly took a sip of tea and smiled, “Ah Ning is becoming more and more capable.” “You flatter me,” Ning Yanli said, bowing her head. “I told you, you do not need to be so respectful in front of me. I am not Huangwu,” Yelu Jinglie said, laughing. His handsome appearance was unparalleled. Although Ning Yanli knew this man was a ruthless character, she still could not resist the allure of his smile. “What obstacles do you think lie ahead for this plan, Ah Ning?” Yelu Jinglie asked. Ning Yanli snapped out of her reverie. “Mo Sigui. Every poison has an antidote. Whether it is a medicine to boost internal energy or one to neutralize the poison within the Konghe family, Mo Sigui could potentially sabotage it.” “I’ve already sent men to kill him. Ah Ning, you cannot afford to hesitate this time.” Yelu Jinglie’s style was to completely eliminate all potential threats. “Actually…I know one of his weaknesses, perhaps more beneficial than killing him.” Ning Yanli could not quite explain whether she felt a pang of reluctance, but she truly did not want Mo Sigui to die like this. “Lou Mingyue.” “Second Young Lady Lou?” Yelu Jinglie leaned back on the cushion, the soft touch making him comfortably squint his phoenix eyes. “A woman of unyielding spirit.” Ning Yanli said, “She has been trying to assassinate the princess. If you were to exchange the princess for Mo Sigui, I wonder if she would comply?” Yelu Jinglie looked at her half-unadorned face. “Eh, you are actually willing to part with your princess?” “From the moment the madman died, I’ve harbored thoughts of leaving.” Ning Yanli’s fingers gently caressed the warm teacup. “I can see that the princess also loves the madman, but she’s willing to sacrifice anyone for the sake of the Liao Kingdom. However, that is not reason enough for me to betray her.” Yelu Jinglie raised an eyebrow, waiting for her to continue.

chapters.title: Secrets
chapters.content: “What grand cause of the Liao Kingdom?” Ning Yanli said calmly. “It’s just an excuse for personal desires.” “Oh? Is that what you think?” Yelu Jinglie asked with a smile. Ning Yanli did not answer but asked in return, “Is that not how it is?” “Who knows?” Yelu Jinglie sighed, seemingly genuinely. “The struggle for power is the most boring thing.” Ning Yanli sneered inwardly: “If it was so boring, why did you even bother to fight for it?” “Go back. I will seriously consider what you said. In short, go ahead and do it. I will clean up the mess for you.” Yelu Jinglie could see through her thoughts, but he let her guess without offering any explanation. What he sought was far more than just power. After Ning Yanli left, Yelu Jinglie sat for a while, then got up and carried a lantern into the study. The study was unlit, but as he entered, the warm light of the lantern slowly illuminated the surroundings. The room contained few books; portraits hung on three walls, each with distinct features, yet all sharing the same phoenix eyes and extraordinary bearing. “Yelu Jinghong,” Yelu Jinglie murmured, gently stroking one of the portraits. “He truly is my nephew. For a moment, I thought my elder brother had come back to life.” Although Yelu Jinglie and his brother were only a few years apart, they looked like twins, their bond incredibly strong. His secret plot had failed, and establishing a foothold in the Liao Kingdom had consumed all his energy. The various factions were locked in a power struggle, preventing him from freely searching for Gu Jinghong, yet he had never given up. He never imagined that after so many years, he would find only a mangled corpse. It was said that he was a child with seven orifices of spiritual insight… The room was quiet, save for Yelu Jinglie’s increasingly heavy breathing. Seeing the furrowed brow in Gu Jinghong’s portrait, he seemed to see himself ten years ago again. Back then, he was fed various poisons daily by special servants, and even now, in the dead of night, the excruciating pain still terrified him, leaving him drenched in cold sweat! Moreover, he lived in constant fear, feeling like a lamb waiting to be skinned and devoured. His cousin, the Emperor, treated him extremely well, yet looking at his cousin’s pale face filled him with utter terror! Yelu Jinglie withdrew his hand, pressing it to his heart, a smirk playing on his lips. “Yelu Jinghong, you probably do not know that I was once their puppet, but so what? My cousin, waiting to drink my blood, died at the hands of this puppet! Many secrets were sealed with the death of the previous generation, known only to me…” “Rest assured, this Emperor will meet the same end.” “Your hatred. I will end it.” Yelu Jinglie’s eyes were filled with coldness. He removed the lampshade and burned all the paintings one by one. After leaving the study, he still maintained his air of a refined young master, with his personal guards waiting outside, closely following. “Master, has Ning Yanli truly betrayed Princess Huangwu?” the guard could not help but ask. This man was named Bai Wu, who had followed Yelu Jinglie since childhood, as half playmate and half bodyguard. “Would you betray me?” Yelu Jinglie asked, turning his head. Bai Wu immediately bowed, his voice soft but firm. “This subordinate swears to follow you to the death!” “Over the years, I’ve done many ruthless things, yet you still follow me. Has Ning Yanli become disloyal after being ruthless a few times because of that girl?” Though he said this, Yelu Jinglie knew that people were different. “It cannot be generalized,” Yelu Jinglie said. “I just need to know she will complete what I assigned her. As for the rest…” He glanced back at the study. “As long as she does not try anything against me, keeping her is fine.” He’d heard that Wei Yuzhi had recently retrieved Gu Jinghong’s heart’s blood, but unfortunately, it had already been refined by Mo Sigui. Ning Yanli had to exert all her strength to barely extract it. However, the remaining amount was too small. Furthermore, Gu Jinghong was still dead, and the blood’s potency had been almost completely destroyed. He suspected that Yelu Huangwu had guessed something, so she sent Ning Yanli to approach him to investigate whether he was a medicine person! The Yelu direct descendants all suffered from the same illness, and his heart’s blood was essentially identical in potency to Gu Jinghong’s. Thinking of this, Yelu Jinglie felt a strong sense of nausea. “Those whom Heaven has ordained to die do not die peacefully. Hmph, let them fight! Let’s see who can defy fate!” Bai Wu lowered his head and remained silent. Yelu Jinglie fell into deep thought. A century ago, the Yelu royal family was embroiled in internal strife. Two brothers from the direct line vied for the throne, with the elder brother emerging victorious but suffering a devastating poison planted by his younger brother. This poison would remain forever in their blood, passed down through generations. The Emperor searched far and wide for a renowned physician, who eventually offered an antidote—the blood of a medicine person’s heart. The physician also claimed that the medicine person’s heart’s blood would be doubly potent if nurtured with blood from close relatives. Thus, the Emperor secretly ordered the capture of his younger brother’s illegitimate son to nurture the medicine. That attempt failed, but he left a secret decree that these sons be used to nurture the medicine person generation after generation until the poison was cured—this was a debt they owed! The struggle for the throne was always fraught with deceit and treachery. Their ancestors had already paid the ultimate price; what debt could there be? It was simply a matter of the victor taking all! Emperor Taizong still retained a sliver of affection for his sworn brother, only ordering the capture of his younger brother’s illegitimate son to be used as a breeding subject. However, breeding a person for the medicine was an extremely difficult task; a single misstep could result in the poisoning of the subject, or the recipient might succumb to the unbearable pain and commit suicide. Thus, by the next generation, the number of potential breeding subjects dwindled sharply. By the time of Yelu Jinglie, only two legitimate sons and two illegitimate sons remained. Both illegitimate sons were used for breeding; one died at six, and the other at nine. Only then did the Emperor consider using Yelu Jinglie. However, Emperor Taizong had decreed that only illegitimate sons could be used. The previous Emperor, cowardly and afraid of death, desperately sent beauties to seduce Yelu Jinglie and his elder brother, Yelu Jingcai, but to no avail. Later, Yelu Jingcai fell in love with one of the beauties, resulting in her pregnancy. However, the breeding process would take at least fifteen years, which he could not wait for, yet he could not openly defy ancestral rules. The use of Yelu Jinglie for breeding was conducted in secret, and thus, few knew of it. Yelu Jinglie was already six years old at the time, and the process of receiving the drug was a thousand times more painful than for children who had been drugged in the womb. The phrase “dying and coming back to life” was no exaggeration. Yelu Jinglie was cruel and ruthless, with a particularly cruel fetish in matters of the bedroom. He generally would not refuse a woman who willingly entered his bed, but after sleeping with her, he would kill her without exception. Only those who knew the inside story understood that such a proud man would never allow his own flesh and blood to be used like animals! “Only I am left,” Yelu Jinglie said softly. If he still could not succeed this time, he would die, leaving them no hope. Whether it was ascending the throne or mutual destruction, the thought of either was incredibly exciting! A faint smile appeared on Yelu Jinglie’s handsome, almost otherworldly face, quiet yet arrogantly unrestrained.

chapters.title: The Realm of Cunning
chapters.content: In Bianjing. The weather grew increasingly hot, and even rumors seemed to spread more rapidly. Just as people were still immersed in the joy of General Ling’s resurrection, a horrifying incident occurred in Bianjing—the Li and Feng families, two prominent clans, vanished overnight, and over six hundred servants from both families were brutally murdered. Among the dead were children from both clans. Unlike the servants who were hacked to pieces, they all died of poisoning, yet more than ten imperial physicians, after examining the poison, could not obtain a definitive result. The case was earth-shattering; for a time, the court and the public were speechless, and it took several days for people to recover. Upon hearing this news, Mei Tingzhu rushed to Mei Mansion that very night to see Chu Dingjiang. “Master Chu, the Konghe Secret Manual has been deciphered!” Her voice trembled as she spoke; even someone as composed as she felt a chilling fear at this moment. Chu Dingjiang clearly already knew the news. “Take everyone from the Mei family to Hexi County to find Mo Sigui immediately.” Mei Tingzhu gripped the armrest of her chair tightly, her face pale. “What if…” What if the poison within her was activated halfway there? Mei Tingzhu’s mind was a mess; she could not think of any solutions. Only two clear words remained—”it’s over!” Like a prisoner already on the execution platform, a beheading was only a matter of time. Hoping someone would break them out of the execution ground was too naive; the chances were extremely slim, and they would not encounter that. “If they could control all the Konghe families in one fell swoop, they definitely would not do it in two stages,” Chu Dingjiang calmly analyzed for her. “First, we do not know how to activate the poison, but judging from the current situation, the poison in the blood of the four families is very likely not the same. There are probably three reasons why they have not attacked the Mei and Lou families: First, activating the poison might require some price, and the Mei and Lou families have too few people left to pay that price; second, activating the poison requires a specific list of each person, and they have not obtained the Mei family genealogy; third, the Mei and Lou families still have people or things they want to use.” Mei Tingzhu listened to his words. As she gradually calmed down and her thoughts cleared, although her face was still deathly pale, her eyes no longer betrayed panic. She pondered for a moment. “You are right. I think all of these possibilities exist. The remaining fighting strength of the Mei and Lou families is indeed not worth their effort in activating the poison. But that is not entirely true. The Lou family has Lou Xiaowu, and the Mei family has Mo Sigui and Fourteenth Young Lady.” The abilities and lethality of these three were definitely several times stronger than the remaining assassins of the Mei and Lou families combined. After activating the poison, they would lose their original minds. Then, these three top talents would become mindless killing puppets, especially Lou Xiaowu, whose fighting strength was even inferior to that of a third-rate assassin. “The current strength of the Mei and Lou families should be like a chicken bone to the mastermind, but these three are different.” Mei Tingzhu’s thoughts gradually became clearer. If Mo Sigui did not understand medicine, his strength was not top-tier either. Lou Xiaowu was even less so. And more unfortunately, if Fourteenth Young Lady lost her mental power, she would be just a fragile external cultivator. She could not possibly fire the Startling the String! The reason the mastermind was not in such a hurry to act was probably that they wanted to control these three people through other means. Chu Dingjiang said, “Now that you’ve calmed down, think carefully about the key to controlling these three people.” Mei Tingzhu frowned, a name flashing through her mind. “Lou Mingyue!” Chu Dingjiang nodded slightly. “But I still have some doubts. Lou Mingyue has no connection with Fourteenth, right?” Mei Tingzhu asked. “Controlling Lou Mingyue is equivalent to controlling Lou Xiaowu and Mo Sigui, and controlling Mo Sigui means controlling Ah Jiu. No one understands Ah Jiu better than him.” Chu Dingjiang had to admit that Mo Sigui understood An Jiu better than he did. From physical to psychological, Mo Sigui was the physician who understood her best. Mei Tingzhu only knew that Mo Sigui and An Jiu were close, but did not know the deeper connections. Although she did not quite understand, she did not press further. She knew that what Chu Dingjiang said was credible enough. “So what we need to do now is find Lou Mingyue.” Mei Tingzhu clasped her hands together, looking expectantly at Chu Dingjiang. “Will you be traveling with us, My Lord?” Chu Dingjiang ignored her. “You go first. I need to prepare some things and will catch up later.” Mei Tingzhu stood up and bowed. “Farewell.” “Take care.” Chu Dingjiang had a fairly good impression of this young girl; she was clear-headed and efficient, quite like his An Jiu. A gentle smile appeared on Mei Tingzhu’s pale face. Chu Dingjiang stood up, hands clasped, by the window, admiring the vibrant apricot blossoms in the courtyard. After a long while, he lowered his head, took out two books from his sleeve, and began to read. Suddenly, he smiled and said softly, “Ah Jiu, I’ve delivered the people to you. Do a good job.” His inner energy shattered the two books into dust, which danced in the east wind, mingling with the apricot blossoms shaken down by the residual force of the energy, creating a flurry of snowflakes. The four volumes of “The Secret Manual of Konghe” seemed to still be in his hands. Only he knew the truth: the mastermind’s failure to target the Mei family was not due to his analysis but rather because after he recreated the Secret Manual of Konghe, erasing the poison-inducing methods of the Mei and Lou families, it “coincidentally” fell into the hands of Yelu Jinglie’s forces… The Secret Manual of Konghe was an extremely important document. How could Chu Dingjiang not examine it carefully after finding it, and how could he allow others to obtain its more crucial contents? Of course, he did not deliberately leave it behind for a specific purpose; it was purely based on a strategist’s intuition, believing it would be useful later. When An Jiu expressed her desire to rebuild the Dragon Martial Guards, he devised a plan to tightly bind the Mei and Lou families to An Jiu. Even if he could not completely control them, he could play a crucial role in her early stages. His initial reluctance to acknowledge Mei’s request for help was partly due to Chu Dingjiang’s lack of interest in scheming but also a strategic move to lay the groundwork for future plans. The less he cared about the matter, the more Mei would believe he was uninvolved. How could Chu Dingjiang possibly miscalculate and be forced into a position where Mei would negotiate with him? When Chu Dingjiang laid the groundwork, he had not really planned what he would do with the Mei family. It was just his nature; more foreshadowing never hurts, even if it was just a wasted effort. The highest level of cunning was digging pits even when there was nothing to scheme for, seeing who you could trap. Uncle Chu was truly a paragon of cunning. Having concealed himself so deeply, orchestrating a massive crime with a single, effortless move without leaving a trace, Chu now gazed at the falling blossoms outside the window, filled with melancholy and a deep sense of inferiority—truly only capable of petty schemes. How he envied the peerless strategist! It was unknown how the Konghe family would react when they learned of the true mastermind’s intentions, but Chu certainly was deeply mired in feelings of inferiority. If asked if he felt any regret for causing such a bloody tragedy and the deaths of so many people, the answer was absolutely, “No!” His actions were not purely to satisfy An Jiu’s personal needs; he believed her work was meaningful. The Song Dynasty needed a truly cohesive and highly effective army. The process of weeding out the weak and retaining the strong would inevitably involve sacrifices—history had witnessed countless such instances, and he had long anticipated them. An Jiu had always aspired to stand on the side of justice, so Chu Dingjiang did not mind doing these dark things for her, bearing the burden of those who died in the process. His feelings for her were never expressed verbally, nor were they confined to what she could see. Chu Dingjiang took out the letter he had received yesterday from his pocket. Looking at its highly personal style, all his feelings of inferiority and resentment vanished. He was exceptionally intelligent, far surpassing ordinary people. From childhood, his ambition had been to become an unparalleled statesman, like Shang Yang, who could save a collapsing empire and turn the tide. For such a man of high aspirations to suddenly realize that while he possessed intelligence, he lacked the necessary breadth of vision was a devastating blow. Seeing reality clearly was easy; accepting it was an unimaginably painful process. It took him two lifetimes, and even now, thinking about it still made his heart ache. As wise as he was, it would not take decades for him to see the truth. Looking back, he actually knew what kind of person he was long ago, but he stubbornly deceived himself. Now, he acknowledged and gradually accepted it because of one person. This person showed him another kind of life. “Ah Jiu, thank you for appearing in my life,” Chu Dingjiang murmured.

chapters.title: Unexpected Change
chapters.content: An Jiu, who was preparing to set off for Zhending Prefecture to reform an assassin, had not even left yet. She realized everything was developing in a favorable direction. First, Lou Xiaowu arrived with a mountain of bundles; then Zhu Pianxian, on Chu Dingjiang’s orders, sent her most profitable manager. Just as everything was arranged, the entire Mei family arrived with their bags packed. On the surface, only a few members of the Mei family remained, but the number who escaped the Konghe Army was quite considerable—twenty-six people. Among them was Elder Qi’s eldest son, Mei Yongting, who was skilled in medicine. The morning mist swirled, mingling with the light smoke exhaled by Mo Sigui, like an ink painting. He squatted by the newly cultivated herb garden, watching Mei Yongting busy himself. “It’s a good thing the old man did not take me as his apprentice; otherwise, the generations would be messed up.” According to blood relations, Mo Sigui should call him his cousin; if Elder Qi had taken Mo Sigui as his apprentice, he would have to call Mei Yongting his senior brother. “The Mei family has always been chaotic.” Mei Yongting’s voice was pleasant but deep and cold, seemingly devoid of any emotion. Mo Sigui said, “The old man left behind all his life’s knowledge, which I burned, but it is all in my mind. I will write it down for you.” “No need; it is what he left you.” “His greatest regret was being too obsessed with medicine. His dying wish was that I not repeat his mistakes.” Mo Sigui looked at Mei Yongting’s tall figure through the thin mist. Mei Yongting stared blankly at the fresh, dew-kissed herbs at his feet, then turned to look at him after a long while. “He…he never said anything to me…” Mo Sigui, holding his pipe, paused for a moment, then said, “You know he does not like to say those sentimental things.” “I did not know,” Mei Yongting said, straightening up, looking at the yellowing sky in the east, and sighing. “I rarely even saw him when I was at home. I hated him when I first joined the Konghe Army. If he had put even a little thought into me, I would not have been forever deprived of the light of day. Now that he’s dead, I do not resent him anymore, and I will never know about his guilt.” “You know,” Mo Sigui said calmly, “you saw him at the ancestral hall.” “So what? It was just a glance.” This father and son clearly both cared for each other, but refused to express it. If Mei Yongting only felt hatred or indifference towards Elder Qi, he would not have gone to such lengths to return to the Mei family to see him again. Mo Sigui did not expose him, continuing their previous conversation. “If he knew you had left the Konghe Army, he could rest in peace. Those medical books are the culmination of his life’s work; I hope you will not refuse them.” Mei Yongting nodded. Seeing him silently continuing to tend the herb garden, Mo Sigui did not disturb him further and went back to copying the medical books. He stroked the only handwritten medical record left by Elder Qi. Someone called from outside, “Cousin!” Mo Sigui put away the medical record. “Come in.” An Jiu, Mei Tingzhu, Mei Tingyuan, and seven or eight others entered. “Please find a comfortable place to sit. Make yourselves at home.” Mo Sigui already knew about the Mei family’s blood poison and was not surprised that they had come together. Everyone found a place to sit. Mei Tingzhu asked, “Cousin, did you detect any toxicity?” Mo Sigui shook his head. “Leaving aside others, I’ve been treating Ah Jiu for so long and have not noticed anything unusual, so it is clearly not an ordinary poison.” “Could it be a Gu poison?” Mei Tingzhu asked. “Even less likely,” Mo Sigui said. “I’ve used my true qi to check Ah Jiu’s pulse several times. If there were any Gu poison, I would have detected it long ago.” “I have an idea,” An Jiu said. Everyone looked at her. An Jiu said, “Is it possible that our ancestors were initially poisoned? But after several generations, the poison disappeared, yet it mutated our blood? Even after the mutation, it can still be activated by some kind of drug.” “Mutation!” Mo Sigui was stunned for a moment, then suddenly laughed. “Ah Jiu, you are a genius!” Mei Tingzhu understood An Jiu’s meaning, her expression changing slightly. “If that is true, there would not be an antidote, would there?” They were not poisoned, but rather inherently different from ordinary people in certain aspects. “There’s more.” Mo Sigui showed no worry, his eyes shining with excitement. “Do you not think the Liao Emperor’s illness is strikingly similar to ours? I wonder which predecessor created such a potent poison.” Thinking about it carefully, the Liao Emperor’s hidden ailment also seemed to be a hereditary poison; the difference being that the poison they were afflicted with shortened their lifespan, while the Konghe family’s did not. An Jiu felt this was somewhat like genetic manipulation; even the blue-fire crossbows of the Liao Kingdom were similar in principle to guns and cannons… The more she thought about it, the more chilled she became, sensing that someone was controlling everything from an unseen place. Sui Yuntong said, “I did not expect the Feng family to be a family of the Konghe Army.” Li Qingzhi asked curiously, “Could it be the Feng family that used to monopolize the Song Dynasty’s river transport?” “Yes, I’ve never heard of anyone from the Feng family in the Konghe Army,” Mei Tingyuan said. On the surface, the Feng family, like the Mei family, was a merchant family. They monopolized the Song Dynasty’s river transport for many years and were skilled in shipbuilding. Mei Tingzhu, however, felt it was expected. “If it were not for the court’s tacit approval, a single family could not possibly control so many docks.” Both waterways and land routes were strategically crucial. How could the court allow these to be controlled by a private family? If this family were to rebel, the entire Song Dynasty could be destroyed in an instant. An Jiu said, “Then the Yu family…” The Feng family was a thing of the past; now the Yu family held a significant position in water transport. Mei Tingzhu thought for a moment. “The Yu family is most likely not. The current head of the Yu family seems to be very shrewd. After swallowing the Feng family’s river transport business, they only controlled the Jiangnan area, at most acting as local bullies. They sold off everything else to others.” “Let’s not talk about others yet,” Mo Sigui said with a smile. “Let me tell you some terrible news.” The room fell silent. He coughed. “If what Ah Jiu says is true, we have no cure.” “We can only wait to die!?” Mei Tingzhu found it hard to accept this fact. She was a resilient woman; she could fight back no matter what happened. But to become meat on a chopping block, at the mercy of others—what would she do? She had not even considered it. An Jiu was calm. She had experienced the days of being a killing machine and did not find it terrifying, but she did not want to go back to the past. Therefore, no matter the situation, she had to fight to the death. Mei Tingzhu suppressed her unease and asked, “Cousin, do you know the whereabouts of Second Young Lady Lou?” Mo Sigui seemed surprised by her sudden mention of this topic and paused slightly. “No, why ask about her?” Mei Tingzhu said, “I think the Secret Manual of Konghe has probably fallen into the hands of the Liao people. They might use Second Young Lady Lou to coerce you and Lou Xiaowu into doing things for them.” “Heh,” Mo Sigui scoffed. “Coerce me with Second Young Lady Lou? They might as well use Ah Jiu.” He was completely unconcerned! Mei Tingzhu looked at him scrutinizingly, sensing that he was not pretending. “That is good. But we still need to find Miss Second Young Lady Lou as soon as possible. Lou Xiaowu is a rare military genius; she cannot be controlled by the Liao people.” An Jiu kept staring at Mo Sigui, intuitively feeling that his words were not feigned. She just could not understand why someone who had been so persistent had suddenly become so indifferent. “I will try my best to find a way to make amends. You can leave now; I have things to do,” Mo Sigui said. Everyone knew he was referring to resolving the anomaly, so they all left as instructed. An Jiu did not move, waiting until everyone had left before saying, “I only want to ask one question before I leave.” “Speak,” Mo Sigui said. “Why did you change so quickly?” An Jiu paused, then added, “Your feelings for Lou Mingyue.” “You really have the leisure to think about such things when your life is hanging by a thread,” Mo Sigui smiled, spreading out papers on the table and beginning to write a medical case. After writing a few lines, he looked up and saw An Jiu still sitting there, sighing, “Sometimes you cannot understand these things your whole life, and sometimes you understand them in an instant. Continuing to dwell on this will only add to our troubles. Why harm ourselves and others?” An Jiu thought about his words, finding them quite reasonable, yet still feeling there was something she did not quite understand. “Go away and ponder it, do not get in my way,” Mo Sigui said dismissively. An Jiu, lost in her own thoughts, got up and strolled out. Lou Xiaowu had just finished breakfast and could not find anyone. She ran to Mo Sigui’s courtyard and bumped into An Jiu, rushing up to grab her. “Rat, rat, I am Mushroom!” An Jiu snapped out of her daze and, incredibly, understood Lou Xiaowu’s meaning perfectly: she wanted a heart-to-heart talk. “Speak quickly; I am busy,” An Jiu said.

chapters.title: A Kind Heart for An Jiu
chapters.content: Lou Xiaowu hung her head. “The General used to be very good to me, but lately he does not seem to want to talk to me much. I am so depressed.” An Jiu looked at her with satisfaction. “You made the right decision.” “What?” Lou Xiaowu looked at her blankly. “I mean, no one is better at comforting people than me,” An Jiu said confidently. “Clearly, your choice was wise.” Lou Xiaowu exclaimed happily, “Right? Right?” The two found a sunny spot to sit down, and Lou Xiaowu began to ramble on and on about General Ling’s recent changes. “He does not seem happy at all after he was exonerated,” Lou Xiaowu had been thinking about this all the way here, but still could not figure it out. After listening, An Jiu said, “It’s simple. Although he’s been exonerated, his family was all unjustly killed. The mastermind behind their deaths is the current Emperor’s father. Now he has to serve the Emperor. No one would be happy in that situation.” “Family feud.” Lou Xiaowu understood immediately, nodding, and felt even more convinced of An Jiu’s abilities. “I understand now, but why was he nice to me before and not now? It has nothing to do with a family feud, right?” “Well…” An Jiu thought carefully. “Because he was bored before, but he’s not bored now.” Lou Xiaowu stared with her almond-shaped eyes. “He actually thinks like that!” An Jiu glanced at her. “Why are you angry? He was kind to you after all; you should be grateful. No one had to be nice to you. “ “What you said… makes sense, but why am I still angry?” Lou Xiaowu tilted her head and asked, “What if Uncle Chu treats you badly in the future? Will you be angry?” An Jiu was silent and asked, “Why would he treat me badly?” “Oh, you mean I deserve to be disliked?” Lou Xiaowu said angrily. “I am obviously still so smart!” “If he treats me badly,” An Jiu felt a dull pain in her heart when she thought of this possibility. “I will die with him or stop treating him well. Since he treats me well, I cannot just say I dislike him.” “You are right; I will find him and die together!” Lou Xiaowu got up and rushed out. An Jiu raised her hand and looked up at the old pear tree in the courtyard, thinking, “Would Chu Dingjiang really dislike me one day? Apart from taking advantage of Mei Jiu and being good-looking, I do not have any other good qualities…” Hmm, it seemed that this was really possible! Someone suddenly fell into an unprecedented sense of crisis, and it was urgent to improve her personal charm. Xue Sha walked over and saw An Jiu staring blankly, standing there for a moment before asking, “An Jiu, are you still going to Zhending Prefecture?” “Yes,” An Jiu snapped out of her reverie. In Bianjing, the Imperial Palace. The Grand Secretariat was in a frenzy. Prime Minister Hua finished reviewing a memorial and placed it on a stack on the corner of the table, then picked up another. He quickly glanced at the contents, his pen hovering over the paper for a long time, but ultimately did not write a reply, setting it aside. Memorials submitted from the provinces all first passed through the Grand Secretariat, where Grand Secretaries would review them. The Grand Secretaries would write their proposed solutions on the memorials and then present them to the Emperor. If there were no objections, the Emperor would consider it the final decision. However, some memorials could not be directly reviewed by the Grand Secretaries and would be presented directly to the Emperor. The memorial that Prime Minister Hua had not reviewed was the one submitted by Wu Lingyuan, tucked among a stack of memorials from Hejian Prefecture and inconspicuous. The request from Hexi County for a self-defense force of two thousand men was not excessive; the Song Dynasty was notorious for its overstaffed military. Tens of thousands were commonplace, so two thousand was a trivial matter. However, Wu Lingyuan was a protégé of Hua Rongtian. He did not handle the matter directly to avoid suspicion, lest the Emperor think his family was planning something shady on the border. Fortunately, the memorial fell into his hands. If it had fallen into the hands of someone with differing political views, it would likely have been immediately rejected or led to another lawsuit. After all the ministers had finished their business for the day, the eunuchs exchanged the processed memorials, ensuring each Grand Secretary reviewed them. If there were no objections, they would sign their approval; if there were objections, they would be kept for discussion until a consensus was reached before being reprocessed. If no decision was reached, the Emperor would have to make the final decision. After noontime, the Grand Secretaries gathered for a meeting. Half an hour before the meeting, Prime Minister Hua secretly slipped the Hexi County memorial into the meeting. Because of the heavy workload, everyone who saw the memorial assumed they had missed it or that it was just their turn. One of the Grand Secretaries flipped to the memorial and asked suspiciously, “Hexi County is going to build a private army?” Prime Minister Hua seemed completely oblivious, frowning as he asked, “How many men?” “Two thousand,” the Grand Secretary replied. Everyone present knew that the newly appointed magistrate of Hexi County had some connection with the Hua family, but they could not suspect the Hua family of any ulterior motives based on a mere two thousand men. The room fell silent. After everyone had read the memorial, “Let the memorial be submitted to His Majesty for a decision,” Prime Minister Hua said. The others had no objections. If Wu Lingyuan did not have such an unusual relationship with the Hua family, the Grand Secretariat could have handled this minor matter. However, it was not advisable to interfere now; doing so could offend Prime Minister Hua and incur His Majesty’s wrath, especially since border defense was of paramount importance. Another reason the Grand Secretaries were reluctant to speak out was the shocking content of Wu Lingyuan’s memorial. The entire Hexi County had a mere four hundred households, with a total population of less than three thousand men, women, and children—not even counting the lower-level counties. As for the self-defense force, even if they recruited women, they probably could not muster two thousand men. In contrast, a prominent county in the south typically had around six thousand households, and even a lower-level county had nearly a thousand. After the meeting, subordinate officials compiled and presented all the memorials, allowing the Grand Secretariat a brief respite. Prime Minister Hua personally brewed a pot of tea, opened the window, and sat in a round-backed chair, admiring the lush green banana trees outside. It was just past noon, and the sky was overcast. Soon, raindrops fell on the banana leaves, making soft, rhythmic sounds, and the muggy air seemed to gain a touch of coolness. After finishing his tea, Prime Minister Hua returned to his desk to continue his work. As dusk settled, he looked outside, rose, and went out. The eunuch, noticing his surprise, quickly opened an umbrella. “Prime Minister, are you going home so early today?” Prime Minister Hua smiled. “Going home to see my grandson.” He took the umbrella and left. He walked slowly, passing through a palace gate. He happened to meet Hua Rongtian, who was coming out of the Privy Council. “Father,” Hua Rongtian said quickly. Prime Minister Hua nodded. The father and son waited in silence for the carriage to arrive, as if only the sound of rain filled the air. “Rongtian, I am getting old,” Prime Minister Hua suddenly said. Hua Rongtian turned to look at his father. Prime Minister Hua was nearly fifty. He had previously taken good care of himself and looked like a man in his prime, but in recent years, he had become increasingly aged. “You must work harder,” Prime Minister Hua said to him. “The Hua family is now in your hands.” Hua Rongtian understood that the Emperor would not allow the father and son to control the cabinet. Hua Rongtian had secretly supported His Majesty since he was a prince, and now, deeply favored by the Emperor, his official position had not changed much, but he was always responsible for important matters. If the cabinet were reorganized, Hua Rongtian would undoubtedly be a strong contender for the next Grand Secretary; however, he had not yet even entered the cabinet because Prime Minister Hua was still in power. Hua Rongtian suspected he was considering retiring, “His Majesty relies heavily on Father now, why…” “The court is short-handed, and if I, Father, am useful, His Majesty will certainly not abandon me.” But ultimately, he was not a trusted confidant, and a deep distance remained. Prime Minister Hua did not say the second half of his sentence aloud. He only leaned forward and whispered, “You are different from your father.” No matter how capable the old ministers of the previous dynasty were, they were never as good as the old acquaintances he had relied on since he was a prince, especially since the Emperor did not think Hua Rongtian’s abilities were inferior to Prime Minister Hua’s. At most, he just lacked a little experience. When the late Emperor was still the Crown Prince, Prime Minister Hua had already been assisting him, so he had always been deeply trusted by the late Emperor, but the late Emperor was very suspicious. Furthermore, the Hua family’s power was truly worrisome, which led to his gradual loss of trust. Even so, until the late Emperor’s death, he remained firmly in his position as Grand Secretary. Prime Minister Hua had realized that he only had one chance in his life to reach that level of power, but the Hua family was different; they still had Hua Rongtian. Now was a time of national crisis. If Hua Rongtian could seize this opportunity and firmly secure a place in the Emperor’s heart, even if he was currently inexperienced and barely managed to squeeze into the cabinet, he would not have to worry about not eventually reaching that position second only to the Emperor. Conversely, if Prime Minister Hua continued to block the cabinet and refused to make room while everyone else rushed forward, Hua Rongtian would be limited by his position, and the things he could do for the Emperor would be limited, and the advantage of being an “old hand” would diminish. This opportunity only came once. The carriage arrived, and Hua Rongtian helped Prime Minister Hua into it. The rain poured down in the twilight, mirroring Prime Minister Hua’s current mood. Sometimes, seeing things too clearly was painful. For example, if he could not see his own predicament, he could stubbornly remain in court for another twenty years. Unfortunately, he had not even made a move before he saw the end. Even more tragically, his body was already in this state, but his spirit remained unbroken. Prime Minister Hua was filled with resentment. The late Emperor was incompetent, and he had devoted a large part of his energy to maneuvering against him. His true ambitions had not been realized, yet his stage had already ended. For his family, for his son, retirement was the best way out. He could not help but wonder, what if he had chosen to support the Second Prince? The answer was impossible. Even with ten chances to start over, he would still choose neutrality. Because if he chose a side, it meant his entire family had chosen a side. Trying to protect the family through such means would ultimately lead to ruin. How could the new Emperor tolerate the vast power that the late Emperor wanted to eradicate? He could only use the late Emperor to put the Hua family to death, and then rely on Hua Rongtian’s support for the Second Prince to allow the Hua family to be reborn. This was not a matter of whether he had foresight or not; it was that he never had a choice. Family, sometimes, was a lifeline to success; sometimes, it was a mountain of burdens. So be it! Rather than a resentful, death-defying struggle, he’d rather go home and raise his grandson, leaving his unfulfilled ambitions to him. Perhaps one day, he would succeed. In the rain, the sound of wheels rumbling over the stone slabs was mixed with the indistinct voice of Prime Minister Hua, “Have more children.” “Your son will try his best,” Hua Rongtian said in a deep voice.

chapters.title: Yuji
chapters.content: An Jiu and Xue Sha traveled together to Zhending Prefecture. On the way, Xue Sha introduced her to the assassins hiding there. Ranked ninth on the Konghe List, codenamed Yuji, a woman, an eighth-level martial artist. “Actually, she and I were together for a while.” At the gates of Zhending Prefecture, Xue Sha said with a hint of pride. An Jiu looked at the long queue ahead, then turned to him, puzzled. “Why would she ruin herself?” “Because…uh,” Xue Sha realized, his face darkening. “Am I that bad? It is clearly me ruining myself!” “Oh, so you knew that yourself?” An Jiu thought for a moment. “Perhaps people in this line of work have some issues.” Xue Sha did not refute, but his expression became conflicted, a mixture of anticipation and resistance, excitement and fear. An Jiu often monitored her targets for months at a time, and many had strange fetishes. She whispered, “Yuji…likes sadomasochism?” Xue Sha looked at her in shock. An Jiu knew she’d guessed right. “Looks like you enjoy it.” “Ahem.” Xue Sha suddenly became shy. “It’s usually pretty boring, just looking for something interesting to do.” An Jiu understood. “No wonder you kept urging me.” “Actually, I am not sure if she’s here either,” Xue Sha said wistfully. “Little one, take a look.” The woman behind her took a lotus leaf from a bamboo basket and handed it to An Jiu. “You do not look well; do not get sunburned.” An Jiu was dressed in men’s clothing, her hair tied in a bun, and wearing a human-skin mask. Everyone else’s faces were reddened by the sun, but she remained pale, looking particularly sickly in this environment. An Jiu quietly put away the hidden weapon between her fingers, took the lotus leaf, and stammered, “Th…thank you.” She subtly twirled the lotus leaf in her hand. Finding nothing amiss, she slowly placed it over her head. Xue Sha sighed; good looks were always an advantage. Ahead, for some unknown reason, the snail-paced procession suddenly came to a halt. Xue Sha peered out, and An Jiu simply squatted down, a lotus leaf obscuring half her face, letting her gaze wander. These past few days, certain things had been swirling in her mind, refusing to leave. Blue-fire crossbows, power-enhancing drugs, blood mutations… each one felt strangely familiar. Given the current state of affairs, these things seemed to be beyond the norm. But if they should not exist, then what about Mo Sigui and Lou Xiaowu? Everything they did was outside the realm of the ordinary. Alright, even if these things were plausible, what about all the coincidences? “What’s going on…?” An Jiu murmured. The procession began to move again, and An Jiu stood up and walked forward, still lost in thought. Showing her token at the city gate was An Jiu’s favorite thing to do, and she immediately cast aside all her worries. With a righteous air, she pulled out her token. As expected, the two entered the city smoothly. “Hehehe.” An Jiu could not suppress her laughter.
