Xue Sha paced back and forth. “Why am I so excited?” “Is it not exhilarating?” An Jiu had finally found someone who understood her feelings. “It’s like when I was little and stole my older sister’s hair ornament to give to the girl in the next village,” Xue Sha said excitedly. An Jiu’s smile vanished instantly, her eyes narrowing. “You are obviously a masochist, a perpetual masochist.” Life was as lonely as snow, sigh! With a sigh, An Jiu began to wander around the city. Xue Sha followed behind her. “Yuji is good at hiding. I left a mark on the street; let her find us when she sees it.” “What if she does not come?” An Jiu grumbled. “You expect me to rely on your charm, which is completely below average?” Xue Sha said sullenly, “Why make things difficult for fellow travelers? Everyone has their struggles.” An Jiu swiftly traversed the city, her mental energy filtering through the surrounding crowd like a vast net. Xue Sha, realizing that An Jiu could silently monitor him and might find Yuji in the vast crowd, silently followed behind. In less than two hours, the entire city had been searched, and An Jiu finally stood outside the yamen. There were only three martial artists in the whole city, two at the fifth level and one at the seventh, all of whom were inside the yamen. An Jiu was a little puzzled. Yuji was supposed to be an eighth-level martial artist, was she not? Why was she not there? “Let’s eat first and go in tonight to take a look,” she said. Xue Sha followed her into a restaurant and found a private room with a view of the yamen’s front gate. “You mean, Yuji is inside the yamen?” “If she’s in Zhengding, then she’s most likely in the yamen,” An Jiu said. “What could a woman like her do in the yamen…” Before the food even arrived, An Jiu tapped the kettle with her chopsticks. “She’s probably become the prefect’s concubine.” “You are talking nonsense!” Xue Sha snapped, like a cat whose tail had been stepped on. An Jiu knew exactly how to tease this kind of person. Xue Sha enjoyed being tormented by Yuji, so he probably saw Yuji as an empress in his heart. How could an empress be a concubine? With satisfaction, An Jiu watched him bristle, feeling exceptionally pleased. After the food was served, he ate five bowls with a great appetite. Night fell. The two quietly sneaked into the mansion. An Jiu first went to find the location of the seventh-level martial artist. “Prefect,” Xue Sha whispered, “I did not expect the Prefect to be such a master.” An Jiu did not speak, but scaled the wall and climbed onto the roof. Lifting a tile, warm yellow light shone from inside. “Master, you’ve had a hard day,” a woman said. Upon hearing this voice, Xue Sha froze, looking into the room in disbelief. A woman in fine clothes smiled and took a handkerchief from a maid to wipe the face of a middle-aged man who looked like a scholar. The man grasped her hand in return. “Madam is pregnant; these matters should be handled by the servants.” “It’s nothing,” the woman said softly. An Jiu estimated the woman to be around twenty-five or twenty-six years old. She had fair skin and was quite beautiful, but her smile was so gentle it seemed almost ethereal. Her gaze toward the prefect was full of tenderness, clearly a different person from Xue Sha’s description. Moreover, the prefect did not seem to have any peculiar tastes. Xue Sha’s face was cold and stern. He flicked his finger, as if a wisp of smoke had drifted into the room. The scent of jasmine filled the air. The prefect’s wife’s expression changed slightly. She pulled out a handkerchief and gently pressed it to her nose. All the maids in the room collapsed. The prefect’s wife reached out to support the reclining prefect. Seeing her help the prefect to the soft couch, Xue Sha turned back, opened the window, and jumped down. The two were about two zhang apart when Xue Sha felt the murderous aura emanating from her. “Yuji,” Xue Sha said. “What are you doing here?” Yuji asked coldly. Her expression was utterly devoid of gentleness, as cold as an ancient, unyielding iceberg, and even more chillingly murderous than before. This was the Yuji that Xue Sha was used to. He was slightly pleased. “I knew you were faking it. I have something to discuss with you.” “Whatever it is, do not come looking for me. I am the Prefect’s wife; my name is Zheng Yuhua. There is no Yuji.” Yuji’s lips curled into a smile. “Everything I did for him was not an act. He gave me a peaceful life. Anyone who tries to destroy that is my mortal enemy.” So, that murderous aura was not so sharp because she was protecting someone. “Let’s go,” An Jiu suddenly said. Yuji was shocked. She had not even noticed someone else hiding here. Seeing Xue Sha’s hesitation, An Jiu added, “Since she’s already an ordinary person, we no longer need her.” Xue Sha grunted, stood for a long time, and finally spoke, “I wish you…a lifetime of peace and a house full of children and grandchildren.” Yuji’s expression softened slightly. She could not discern Xue Sha’s expression in the shadows, nor did she want to say anything more, so she simply said, “Thank you.” Xue Sha dashed away. An Jiu leaped off the roof, glanced back at Yuji, and then left the prefectural yamen. An Jiu found Xue Sha in a dead-end alley. “Are you alright?” Xue Sha did not answer. An Jiu rubbed the loose stones on the wall with her toes, waiting for him to calm down. “Take the lotus leaf down! What are you doing wearing a lotus leaf in the middle of the night?” Xue Sha complained. “Alright, I understand you are annoyed by everything right now.” An Jiu took the lotus leaf and put it in her pocket. Xue Sha grabbed his hair. “She was not like this before!” “I know,” An Jiu shrugged. “I was not like this before either.” Xue Sha paused. “How?” An Jiu said, “Not this normal! Until I met Chu Dingjiang. Your Yuji probably had a similar experience to mine. But let me clarify, I do not have a sadomasochistic fetish.”

chapters.title: The Hunter (1)
chapters.content: Xue Sha thought to himself, “I do not think you are that normal!” “Did you not say she was an eighth-level martial artist? How come she’s only seventh now?” An Jiu asked. Xue Sha exclaimed in surprise, “You even know what level someone else is?” At first, when An Jiu went to the prefect’s bedroom, Xue Sha thought the prefect was a master, but later, seeing Yuji with him, he realized that the master was Yuji. Seeing An Jiu’s tacit agreement, he said. “She’s pregnant. Perhaps it is because she damaged her body back then, making it difficult to keep the pregnancy, so she’s using only a fraction of her power to protect it.” Xue Sha felt a vague jealousy, unsure whether it was jealousy that the prefect had Yuji, or jealousy that Yuji had found the ordinary life they both longed for. In his heart, his relationship with Yuji was limited to drawing warmth from each other’s bodies in the darkness; as for feelings, he had never thought about them. “Let’s go back,” An Jiu said. “Women are truly powerful,” Xue Sha sighed. Emotions permeated every nerve in a woman’s body. The killings within the Konghe Army might temporarily numb them, but they could never be extinguished; once exposed to the light of day, they quickly reawakened. But for men, once their blood cooled, it could never boil again. Rich emotions made women vulnerable, yet they could also make them invincible. Xue Sha possessed a gentle smile, but his heart remained cold. He needed to ignite himself, and what would ignite him was not love. The two hurried back to Hexi that very night. The night was deep, the dew heavy, and the moonlight obscured by thick clouds, making visibility extremely poor. However, An Jiu clearly remembered the route they had taken, managing to avoid obstacles in the darkness. After traveling for about an hour, An Jiu suddenly sensed people ahead! And they were all martial artists! “Xue Sha, slow down,” An Jiu whispered. The two slowly stopped, the martial artists still rapidly closing in. An Jiu knew the sound of hooves had attracted them. Unsure whether they were friend or foe, she had no choice but to retreat. “Dismount and hide!” They were too far from the group. Xue Sha had not noticed, but hearing An Jiu’s cautious voice, he knew they were formidable. The two dismounted, led their horses into the nearby woods, and hid nearby. An Jiu had not tied the reins, so the horses could escape in case there was an emergency. An Jiu crouched on a branch of a thick poplar tree, peering through the dense foliage, and could vaguely see the horses’ silhouettes. Xue Sha hid in a tree about ten chi away on the opposite side. The group approached with astonishing speed; even Xue Sha sensed the chilling killing intent emanating from them. In the shadows, a horse neighed and suddenly bolted into a gallop. Xue Sha’s eyes widened. He saw about twenty men chasing the horse, swift and ruthless like a pack of wolves hunting their prey! In the blink of an eye, the two horses were killed, and more than twenty men pounced on them, tearing them apart. A thick stench of blood quickly spread through the woods. After their feast, they suddenly awoke and gathered in this direction. Xue Sha had been discovered! An Jiu gripped her longbow tightly. The group, reeking of blood, approached. The slightly overweight man at the front raised his hand. Three men leaped into the trees, and in an instant, the group moved like lightning towards the tree where Xue Sha was hiding. Xue Sha knew he had been exposed. He quickly tossed down a vial of poison and gripped his sword. The poison’s smoke dissipated rapidly, but it did not slow the group’s advance. Xue Sha’s pupils contracted, and he swung his sword, attacking the three men approaching from the tree! Two against more than twenty. Xue Sha thought he was going to die here today, but having witnessed the horses being torn apart, he was determined not to suffer the same fate and attacked with all his might, seeking a way to break through the encirclement. An Jiu drew her bow. Whoosh! Her mental energy blasted from the bowstring and the arrow simultaneously, the arrow piercing a man’s chest accurately, but the man thrashed about for a long time before collapsing. An Jiu’s heart skipped a beat. Her mental energy could conceal her, but against these people, it had lost its offensive power! In this way, her greatest advantage was halved. While the others were unaware, An Jiu changed positions, continuously firing arrows. Each arrow seemed precisely measured, hitting its target accurately. Because both sides were moving, the accuracy decreased somewhat, but even so, it opened an escape route for Xue Sha. Xue Sha possessed rich combat experience. Seeing a path, he risked taking two arrows to break through the encirclement and immediately ran towards the main road. An Jiu, having achieved her goal, rushed to meet him. An Jiu had originally planned to use her advantages to ambush them, but her mental energy was ineffective against these people. Now that her position had been discovered, her situation was not much better than that of Xue Sha’s. After a moment’s assessment, An Jiu decisively abandoned the fight and chose to flee. Although these people were swift, they clearly had not been their primary target at the beginning. The two ran frantically, but the group behind them relentlessly pursued them. Xue Sha could not help but ask, “Who are these people? Why are they staring at us like that?” “You are asking me? Who should I ask!” An Jiu retorted irritably. It was truly a bolt from the blue. They had not offended anyone, and even just walking at night resulted in being chased! “This is fucking unlucky!” Xue Sha spat, gritting his teeth and quickening his pace. They walked for over ten li, but the tail was still firmly stuck behind. “Let’s kill them!” An Jiu said as she ran. “What did you say? They outnumber us!” Xue Sha said incredulously. An Jiu said, “We will not reach Hexi anytime soon. This cannot go on. Those people seem tireless; we will be caught soon! Rather than waiting to be exhausted and overtaken, we should fight now!” Xue Sha agreed. “Alright!” “Head back!” An Jiu and Xue Sha stopped simultaneously, drew their swords, and turned to attack again. The group clearly had not expected their sudden return, and several were already cut down before they could react. The fat leader let out a long roar, and the group’s attack and defense gradually became more organized. An Jiu and Xue Sha were surrounded. Both sides faced off, neither showing any intention of attacking. An Jiu and Xue Sha stood back to back, taking the opportunity to catch their breath. “We have no past grudges or recent enmity; why are you pressing us so relentlessly?” Xue Sha asked coldly. No one answered. “Do not ask; look them in the eyes,” An Jiu said. Xue Sha examined them closely and noticed that the men’s eyelids were abnormally red, and their whites were filled with bloodshot veins, making them look terrifying and no longer normal. Recalling how they had torn apart the horses earlier, he knew these men had likely lost their humanity. “Kill that fat man,” Xue Sha ordered. The fat man seemed to be the leader of the group; his signals commanded them. “Cover me!” She swiftly drew her bow and arrow, aimed at the fat man, and fired two arrows in quick succession. The fat man had not expected An Jiu to move so quickly and could not dodge in time, being struck in the right chest by the arrow. This arrow enraged the fat man completely. With a roar, the others pounced on her like mad wolves.

chapters.title: The Hunter (2)
chapters.content: The shadows of blades enveloped An Jiu like a curtain. An Jiu drew her bow again and aimed at the fat man, silently estimating his explosive power, which would determine his evasive speed. This time, the opponent was prepared; aiming alone would not guarantee a hit. She had to predict his next move and shoot the arrow there beforehand, neither too fast nor too slow. Her highly concentrated mental energy made it easier for her to lock onto the target than before, and she could also sense the opponent’s internal energy flow. Through the flashing blades, An Jiu stared intently at her target. The fat man’s gaze was terrifying, seemingly possessing intelligence, yet completely unlike a human; he was like a blade in the hand of death. The target’s muscles suddenly tensed, and he leaned to the right—in an instant, by a mere millimeter! Now! An Jiu released her grip and shot an arrow half a foot to his right. As the arrow drew ever closer, the fat man’s eyes narrowed, and he abruptly stopped. Even so, he stumbled forward, and the arrow, whistling through the air, pierced his heart. “An Jiu!” Xue Sha was nearly overwhelmed. He was an excellent assassin, but even he could not withstand the frenzied attacks of over a dozen martial artists. Upon seeing her attack succeed, An Jiu immediately drew her soft sword from her waist and joined Xue Sha in the fight, urgently shouting, “Find a chance to escape!” Without their leader, the attacks and defenses of these men gradually fell into disarray. An Jiu and Xue Sha fought their way through, sprinting along the main road once more. An Jiu assumed these men, lacking human consciousness, would pursue them. However, to her surprise, they all stopped after discovering the fat man had been struck by the arrow. The two still dared not linger, running for over ten li before finally stopping to catch their breath. “I’ve never, ever run this far in one go!” Xue Sha gasped. “We can see the city gate. Let’s go inside first,” An Jiu said. Xue Sha took a deep breath and followed her, running to the city wall. The defenses of Hexi County were practically negligible. The two easily scaled the wall and entered the city, heading straight for the county yamen. The eve of dawn was the darkest hour. It was almost pitch black. To save fuel, only Mo Sigui’s courtyard had a lantern. Both were exhausted and had several external injuries, so they went to his courtyard without prior arrangement. The lantern swayed in the wind, and the flickering yellow light carried the wisps of medicinal smoke. Mo Sigui sat on the veranda, puffing on his pipe, when he suddenly heard a rustling sound from the flowers and trees by the wall. Turning around, he was startled to see two people covered in blood, like demons who had just crawled out of hell in the flickering lamplight. He was about to throw his folding fan. “It’s me!” An Jiu said. Mo Sigui paused, clicking his tongue. “What are you two up to in the middle of the night?” “We just got back from Zhending Prefecture,” An Jiu said, relieved. Mo Sigui raised an eyebrow. “Why are you all like this?” “We ran into a group of assassins,” An Jiu said, wiping her face and sitting down on a nearby stone stool. “They attacked us without warning.” Xue Sha continued, “Those people seemed unconscious, only knowing how to kill. But strangely, that one fat man was able to command them.” Xue Sha then recounted the entire ordeal, then asked, “Was it the Feng and Li families?” That major case from a while ago. Hundreds of people from both families died. Apart from the poisoned children and the elderly, all the servants were killed with a single sword stroke to the throat. And all the able-bodied men from both families disappeared. Those unaware of the details found it terrifying and bizarre, but those in the know could easily imagine what had happened—the poison within the two families had been activated, leading to a massacre in their own homes, with the elderly and weak unable to withstand the poison’s effects and dying. “It’s probably true. I heard that the head of the Feng family, Feng Fang, is a fat man. If that is true, we must capture a couple alive to see!” Mo Sigui’s eyes shone with excitement, his hard-won drowsiness vanishing instantly, but he did not care at all. Turning to the tightly closed doors and windows, he asked, “What do you think?” Inside the room was Wei Yuzhi. He was very alert. He had already noticed An Jiu and Xue Sha outside the county yamen, but he had not come out to avoid meeting An Jiu. Even when Mo Sigui asked, he pretended to be asleep and did not answer. Mo Sigui chuckled, “I also have Mei’s blood flowing through my veins. If I die, how long do you think you will live?” “I do not know what’s written in the Secret Manual of Konghe, but I can guess that either he does not have Mei’s method for inducing poison, or he’s keeping it for other purposes. Sooner or later, he will come looking for you.” Wei Yuzhi sat up, pulling the covers over his head, and looked at the closed door. “Since he has something to ask for, there’s no need to be too nervous.” Mo Sigui noticed that Wei Yuzhi used “he” and asked, “Do you know who got the manual?” “It’s just a guess,” Wei Yuzhi replied. “For an ordinary person to obtain this item, the best option would be to threaten two families into working for them. Even a family that has lost power would be more useful than obtaining a batch of inanimate objects. But the person behind it quickly activated the poison, and these inhuman assassins traveled to the border. Such a long journey could not have been accidental; they must have been summoned. A mere twenty-odd people could not possibly cause any damage to the border defenses. That means someone wanted to use assassins. I’ve thought of everyone in Hebei Road with the power to obtain the Konghe Manual and activate the poison; none of them had a motive to do this. I suspect they were passing through this area on their way to the Liao Kingdom.” Wei Yuzhi, slightly out of breath, continued, “There’s only one person in the Liao Kingdom who would act this way—Yelu Jinglie.” The three people in the courtyard were stunned. “Why must it be Yelu Jinglie?” Mo Sigui asked. Wei Yuzhi remained silent for a moment before replying, “I understand them. Yelu Huangwu has Ghost Shadow under her command; she does not lack manpower. It would be more useful for her to keep them in Song to work for her. The same applies to Yelu Quancang. The other forces in Liao are preoccupied with seizing power, but Yelu Jinglie acts recklessly and arrogantly, disregarding the consequences. I do not know what grudge he holds against Yelu Quancang and his sister, but I have a vague feeling that his actions are not purely for power grabs. His haste and recklessness suggest he’s eager to accomplish something significant. If…” Wei Yuzhi sighed. “Why would Yelu Quancang spare your life?” “My time is running out, and he’s doing me a favor,” Wei Yuzhi said calmly. His mental strength was so great that it harmed both himself and others. As long as he lived and could think, this damage would continue. Even with a Divine Physician like Mo Sigui by his side, it was just a matter of constant healing; he still would not live more than a few years. A few years? How could that be enough to conquer this vast land? Wei Yuzhi raised a hand to rub his temples and slowly lay down. For a moment, silence fell both inside and outside the room. After a long while, Wei Yuzhi slowly opened his eyes. As if talking to himself, or perhaps prophesying, “Yelu Jinglie will not succeed.” All these years, he had been the one running around. Yelu Quancang had never displayed any great abilities, but just the way he switched between various identities, all under the watchful eyes of everyone, without anyone noticing anything amiss, and how he had remained hidden for so many years in the assassin-filled Mei Clan without being exposed—that was enough to show he was no ordinary person. Moreover, when had he started working for him? Reflecting on the past in his idle moments, Wei Yuzhi finally understood Yelu Quancang’s methods. He was arrogant and clever. But Yelu Quancang saw him clearly, exploiting him to the fullest extent when he could be used and discarding him without hesitation when he couldn’t. Over the years, the only favor Yelu Quancang had shown him was that he had not killed him in the end. Yelu Quancang’s method of governing subservient subordinates subtly compelled them to act according to his will. Now, looking back, Wei Yuzhi understood that half of his choice of this path was due to Yelu Quancang’s influence. He had been orchestrating the game all along, completely unaware that he himself was a pawn in someone else’s game. For Wei Yuzhi, it was never too late to realize this; at least it was better than dying in a daze. The sky was just beginning to lighten. An Jiu returned to her room after taking a bath. Upon entering, she sensed something was amiss. There was no murderous intent, only a feeling that someone was behind her. She turned sharply. Through the blurry vision, a familiar, tall figure suddenly came into her view. A moment of silence. Then Chu Dingjiang’s deep voice rang out, “So happy you went crazy?” An Jiu snapped out of her daze and rushed over with a cry, “Chu Dingjiang! You are here!” Her voice was filled with undisguised joy. Hearing this, Chu Dingjiang could not help but smile and hug her tightly. The two embraced silently, needing no words; the sense of security they felt was enough. They separated after a while. An Jiu lit a lamp and began, “It’s faster than expected. I thought you’d be tied up with the Mei family and the Emperor for a year or two before you could escape.” “If I want to leave, nothing can hold me back,” Chu Dingjiang said, carefully surveying the room. “There’s a batch of things outside; I will have someone bring them in at dawn.” “Things for me?” An Jiu asked. Chu Dingjiang nodded. “Something you like to eat.” “That is great.” An Jiu sat down and began recounting their time in Hexi County. “There are so few people here. Forget the army, we cannot even muster enough constables. Luckily, the Mei family came; we can use them for now. By the way, I took on my first subordinate, Xue Sha. I think he used to be one of yours!” “I only have one person,” Chu Dingjiang said. An Jiu did not think much of it and casually asked, “Which one?” Chu Dingjiang looked at her and smiled, “Guess.” An Jiu instantly understood his meaning and retorted, “No, you are mine.” As expected, Chu Dingjiang’s eyes crinkled with pleasure at the reaction. “Mm.” An Jiu then realized he was teasing her in a roundabout way and pouted. “I will not argue with you. By the way, let me tell you about tonight.” Chu Dingjiang had smelled blood as soon as she entered the room. She brought it up herself to avoid his questions, so he adopted a listening posture. An Jiu then recounted the events of the evening from beginning to end. “Hmm.” Chu Dingjiang poured her a glass of water. “Go do your own thing; do not think too much. I am just retired, and I am bored anyway, so leave it to me.” “Alright.” An Jiu stared at his smiling face, leaned in, and kissed him. Chu Dingjiang did not move, so she simply dragged a stool over, sat down, and hugged his neck, kissing him again. “Ah Jiu,” Chu Dingjiang’s voice was slightly hoarse, “I missed you.” An Jiu’s heart felt as if something had gently squeezed the softest spot, a dull ache spreading through her. Her eyes welled up, and warm tears slid down her cheeks. This was the first time Chu Dingjiang had seen her with teary eyes. Unlike other women who were pitifully beautiful, her bewildered expression softened his heart. The tough, resilient woman, who never shed tears, was still wondering why she was crying over a single sentence when Chu Dingjiang suddenly swept her up and placed her on the bed. An Jiu reacted instantly, and their eyes met—it was as if something had exploded. … Liao Kingdom Palace. Yelu Quancang stood holding a lamp, surrounded by a dozen tall bookshelves filled with books. “You’ve come,” a voice said from the darkness ahead. “Grand Preceptor,” Yelu Quancang placed the lamp on the table and stepped into the darkness. “Has the blue-fire crossbow been successfully improved?” The man did not answer but asked, “Did you find the person I asked you to investigate?” “Fourteenth Young Lady, codename Xuan Ren, also known as An Jiu.” Yelu Quancang took a piece of paper from his sleeve and handed it to him. “This is her detailed information,” a hand wearing a white glove emerged from the darkness. After taking the letter, the man did not seem to be in a hurry to read it, only sighing, “Accurately hitting a moving target across a cliff with fierce winds, truly…intriguing.” Yelu Quancang sensed that the man’s final thought was not about that. If he were truly curious, he would have taken action long ago, but for the past two years, he had only been secretly observing her. “An Jiu,” he murmured.

chapters.title: The Hunter (3)
chapters.content: The person in the darkness seemed to fall into a brief moment of contemplation before speaking again, “The blue-fire crossbow has been modified; its power is somewhat reduced compared to before.” “So, it can be used in large quantities now?” Yelu Quancang asked. The biggest problem with the previous blue-fire crossbows was the scarcity of arrow materials and the dangerous manufacturing process; a single mistake could cause an explosion, resulting in countless losses over the years. The person responded softly, and a white-gloved hand emerged from the darkness, holding a token engraved with an eagle. “The Hunter is yours. Kill Chu Dingjiang and bring back An Jiu. I want her alive; this task cannot be done by the Hunter.” “Understood.” Yelu Quancang knew that the Hunters under his command only knew how to kill. These people, called “Hunters,” were strange. Their martial arts skills were not high, but they all possessed extremely high mental strength and unparalleled archery skills. It was unknown when they existed or what cruel methods they used to train such terrifying precision. The Grand Perceptor was named Xiao Che. He was already the Grand Perceptor of the Liao Dynasty before Yelu Quancang became Emperor. He was the youngest Grand Perceptor in Liao history, seemingly blessed by heaven with handsome looks, wisdom, and strength. However, he was not as mysterious then as he was now; a fire had disfigured his face, making him so aloof. Yelu Quancang had investigated and found that Xiao Che’s first twenty-odd years were incredibly smooth sailing. Shortly after he assumed the position, a fire broke out in the Grand Perceptor’s study one night. He had been reading memorials late into the night and had fallen asleep at his desk. The oil lamp had tilted over a pile of memorials and caught fire. The room was full of flammable materials, and the fire quickly spread uncontrollably. When he awoke, he found himself engulfed in flames. This whole affair seemed suspicious, but after investigation, it turned out to be entirely Xiao Che’s own doing. He had just become Grand Perceptor and was full of ambition. He read memorials until the wee hours every night and disliked being disturbed. His personal servant attending him was sent outside. At midnight, as he prepared to sleep, he asked the servant to bring him a bowl of calming soup. After drinking it, he still could not sleep and continued reading memorials. It was winter, and the servant went to a side room to escape the cold. While waiting, the servant urged him twice, but was scolded both times. The servant had no choice but to return to the side room to continue waiting. Inside, the brazier was warm and cozy, and he accidentally fell asleep, only to be startled awake by a scream from next door. Shortly after Yelu Quancang left the secret chamber, the Grand Preceptor sent someone with a blueprint and two craftsmen to oversee the construction of the blue-fire crossbow. To bring back An Jiu alive, the obstacle and potential threat that must be eliminated was Chu Dingjiang. That man was as shrewd as a fox and a master of the Transcendent Realm. Even with Hunters, killing him would not be easy. Yelu Quancang stared blankly at the Divine Eagle Token. After nightfall. At Physician Mo Sigui’s request, An Jiu led the Mei family assassins to capture the poisoned killers. Starting from the location of yesterday’s attack, they searched a ten-li radius. Traces were everywhere, but they could not find the person until just before dawn, when they discovered the fat man lying in the grass. The fat man’s body was still warm, suggesting he had only recently died. An Jiu then ordered the others to follow the traces. She first sent the body back to Hexi County. Late spring and early summer, with abundant water and grass, was the perfect time for livestock. The Liao people were increasingly busy. Meanwhile, the Song Dynasty had a slight respite after spring planting. Wu Lingyuan mobilized all the men in the county to repair the city walls, while the women stayed home to make drunken fish. Drunken fish was a family recipe passed down through generations in Wu Lingyuan’s family. Freshly caught fish were kept in clean water for several days, then washed and soaked in wine. Once the fish was drunk, it was killed and marinated with ginger, garlic, salt, and other seasonings. If it was not too hot, it could be kept for ten days to half a month without spoiling. After preparation, the fish was immediately transported by fast horses to Hejian and Zhengding for sale. With a shopkeeper personally trained by Zhu Pianxian overseeing the business, sales quickly took off. This product only lasted a few days, but Wu Lingyuan insisted on fast delivery, refusing to buy fish from elsewhere and producing only small quantities of exquisitely prepared fish to sell at high prices. Later, he opened a restaurant in Hexi County, where the signature dish was this drunken fish, made fresh daily for an even more delicious flavor. Everyone knew it was the season of truce, and travel was safe, so scholars and literati from the surrounding area came to try it. Anyone who composed a poem could sample it for free. Then everyone learned that a free primary school had been established in Hexi County. Not only was it free, but the government also ensured the children’s safety, providing transportation home every five days for a couple of days. If family members came to visit, accommodation was provided free of charge. The school was run by Wu Lingyuan himself, a top-ranking scholar in the imperial examinations, who was guaranteed to pass, though he could also secure a salary through a government position in the county government. The county already had few children needing early education, so even providing two meals a day would not cost much. However, the number of children sent from nearby areas gradually increased, putting mounting pressure on the county. Wu Lingyuan’s main daily task was writing memorials pleading poverty. Every few days, he would personally go to the prefect to lament, “Our county is poor, our county is short-staffed, our city walls have collapsed, our yamen cannot even afford uniforms for the constables…” In short, although they had not suffered natural disasters, they had been ravaged by war, and the court needed to provide some subsidies. Wu Lingyuan was just a minor county magistrate; his memorials could not reach the Emperor directly. However, his constant urging of the prefect to also plead poverty had a considerable effect. The court exempted the entire Hejian Prefecture from taxes for six years, allocated funds for city defense repairs, and provided some disaster relief grain. After learning about these resources and entering Hejian Prefecture, Wu Lingyuan was the first to rush to request money and grain. As the first county magistrate to plead poverty and offer the prefect many suggestions, he naturally received more than other counties. Receiving these gifts finally eased the financial straits of Hexi County. Before this, the expenses for the primary school and the restaurant had all been covered by Chu Dingjiang. Wu Lingyuan assigned tasks to everyone, but he exclusively treated Chu Dingjiang, this god of wealth, with deference and privately worked even harder to persuade the Privy Council to appoint An Jiu as the commander of the self-defense army. Hua Rongtian was appointed as the Vice Minister of the Privy Council. For appointing the commander of an army of two thousand men, he still had some say, and besides, the Song Dynasty had precedents of women leading troops, so it was quickly approved. However, the army was only allowed to have one thousand men. The Privy Council had always controlled military power in the Song Dynasty. After the deployment was confirmed, the commander would only know which army she would lead. However, no one wanted to go to a place like Hexi County, and the Song Dynasty was in dire need of manpower. It was not worthwhile to specifically appoint a commander for a one-thousand-man city defense army. Therefore, all appointments were left to the prefect, who would then report to the court. Wu Lingyuan obtained the authority to handle the matter independently from the prefect, thus giving An Jiu complete control over the self-defense force. On the day she received her appointment, An Jiu was overjoyed, exclaiming, “Chu Dingjiang, I’ve become an official appointed by the imperial court!”

chapters.title: An Elder at Home
chapters.content: Chu Dingjiang patted her head. “Do a good job.” “But why are there only a thousand men? Two thousand is not much!” An Jiu was happy but also a little dissatisfied. “You think they are only making exceptions for Hexi County? Hua Rongtian does not have that much power,” Chu Dingjiang smiled slightly. “The entire Hebei Circuit will probably need a self-defense army. A lower-level county will have a thousand, a higher-level county might have three thousand, and prefectures will have even more. It is not a small number. If there are more, it is hard to guarantee that someone will not use the self-defense army to rebel.” These were all war-torn areas. The court could not give special privileges to a particular county; otherwise, would other places not cause trouble? “Alright, even if it is a thousand for everyone, my army will definitely be the strongest thousand.” An Jiu began to think about where to recruit more people. “As long as we can afford to keep them, it does not matter if we secretly recruit a few more.” Chu Dingjiang walked to the window, picked up a blade of grass to tease his beloved hawk, and casually said, “I recruited a few on the way here. Go check if they are useful when you have time.” “Which ones?” An Jiu remembered that the convoy had at least eighty or ninety people escorting it. “All of them,” Chu Dingjiang said. An Jiu exclaimed happily, “Really! That old saying is so true!” Chu Dingjiang paused slightly, turning his head to prepare for her attack. “An elder in the family is a treasure!” Snap. The blade of grass was pecked off by the hawk. Chu Dingjiang smiled and shook his head, continuing to tease the hawk with the remaining half of the grass. “Ten sentences will be a hundred unpleasant to hear.” An Jiu asked, “Why a hundred?” “Your face. It is written all over your face, those unpleasant words.” Seriousness was often more lethal than sarcasm, and An Jiu was the kind of person who took everything very seriously. “Hehe.” An Jiu touched her nose, then suddenly remembered something else. “We are moving to a tent outside the city in a few days. I promised Wei Yuzhi I’d avoid him.” Chu Dingjiang stroked the hawk’s feathers. “It’s a good thing he’s come to his senses. Avoid him then; we owe him our lives anyway.” An Jiu looked up at his profile. “Chu Dingjiang, has your skill diminished again?” Ever since he appeared in Hexi County, she had been able to sense his presence. He seemed unable to hide his presence from her any longer… “Hmm,” Chu Dingjiang, used to her erratic topic-jumping, went along with her. “Losing a little is enough.” An Jiu hesitated, “That is true…but you will not keep falling, will you?” Chu Dingjiang sensed her worry, so he ignored the hawk, turned around, and hugged her, whispering comforting words, “I never imagined I’d end up like this when I chose to practice such a domineering technique. I will keep falling from the Transcendent Realm. Breaking through again, I am currently at a bottleneck.” He always planned ahead, but he never thought he would fall in love with a woman willing to give up the readily attainable pinnacle of martial arts for her. An Jiu exclaimed in surprise, “You’ve already fallen from the Transcendent Realm?!” As the saying goes, “Even a starved camel is bigger than a horse.” Even though they were both at the ninth level, Chu Dingjiang’s internal energy was far more profound and refined than that of the average ninth-level cultivator. The boundary between his mental power and the Transcendent Realm was very blurred, so An Jiu could not accurately judge his level. An Jiu pushed him away. “What are the chances of recovering?” she asked. “Staying here a little longer is beneficial, waiting for the right opportunity,” Chu Dingjiang said. “Nonsense.” An Jiu could not tell if he was telling the truth, but her intuition told her it would not be that easy. Since he did not want to tell the truth, she did not press further. “So what if you lose it? Even if you lose it all, it is fine. I will protect you.” “Alright,” Chu Dingjiang smiled. “Thank you, wife.” He addressed her as “wife” so naturally, as if he’d used that term for a long time. Yet, it made An Jiu’s heart skip a beat. It was not resistance or joy, but tension. That simple word made the once cold-blooded killer’s palms sweat. “Ha, ha,” An Jiu chuckled awkwardly, unsure how to respond. The bright sunlight outlined Chu Dingjiang’s sharply defined features. He gazed at her quietly, a gentle smile in his eyes, melting away her embarrassment. An Jiu seemed to see peace and tranquility in his eyes, a longing for time to stand still, and she smiled unconsciously. “Go ahead and get busy,” Chu Dingjiang said softly. “Alright,” An Jiu, as if receiving a command, darted out like a rabbit. Chu Dingjiang went to the desk to find the account book, intending to take stock of their belongings so they could move out of the city tomorrow. Just as he picked up the account book, An Jiu, her face flushed, rushed in like a bull, pounced on him, kissed his cheek, and cried out, “Husband!” Chu Dingjiang was slightly taken aback. She then dashed out again, as if someone was trying to catch her tail. Watching her hurried retreating figure, Chu Dingjiang could not help but smile. His bright eyes and brows were like springtime returning to the earth; his beard covered half his face, but could not conceal his captivating charm. Perhaps it was time to prepare something else, he thought. “Hey, what’s the good news? You are all smiles!” Mo Sigui stepped in and immediately saw Chu Dingjiang grinning broadly. Most of the time, Chu Dingjiang was like a deep, dark pool, cold and mysterious. Seeing him like this suddenly made Mo Sigui a little uneasy. Chu Dingjiang was in a great mood and did not argue. “Sit.” Although his smile had faded, his attitude towards Mo Sigui was a hundred times gentler than before. Mo Sigui sat down hesitantly. “Do not be like that; it is giving me the creeps. I feel like I am being tricked.” Chu Dingjiang’s face turned cold. “What is it?” This was more normal! Mo Sigui breathed a sigh of relief, took a puff of his pipe to calm his nerves, and got down to business. “I’ve examined the body Ah Jiu brought back. I am not sure if it is a mutation, because it seems to have been poisoned by some kind of Gu poison. But I searched the body thoroughly and could not find any Gu. Logically, when the host dies, the Gu poison should also die or go dormant. I came here to ask you if you can think of any Gu poison that can be passed down through bloodlines?” “Are you not a know-it-all?” Chu Dingjiang said. Mo Sigui said, “Even I do not know. More people thinking might help!” “I will think about it,” Chu Dingjiang said. Mo Sigui waved away the smoke and carefully examined him. “What…happened to you?” Previously, Chu Dingjiang’s aura surrounded him, making him impossible to look at directly. Now, that aura had clearly weakened. His aura suddenly burst forth, circling his body, and then dissipated in an instant. Chu Dingjiang said calmly, “As you can see, I intend to be more approachable.” “Hehehe,” Mo Sigui chuckled dryly. “Very good, very good.” “Anything else?” Mo Sigui saw his “get lost if you have nothing else” look and thought angrily, “What happened to being approachable?!” “Speak.” Mo Sigui cleared his throat. “If you have time, could you go and catch two more people for me? Just grab one Liao person whose cultivation has been boosted and another poison-afflicted assassin.” “Do you not already have one?” “Well…” Mo Sigui shifted his position. “I accidentally broke it.” “Insane.” Mo Sigui said discontentedly. “Hey! How dare you, a ruthless killer, say such a thing!” “I never chop up corpses,” Chu Dingjiang said. “Besides, why should I help you with this?” “Can you not just consider it a favor I owe you?” Mo Sigui said urgently. “Both types of people are hard to find.” “If they were easy to find, would I be asking you for help?” Mo Sigui thought for a moment, then held up three fingers. “I owe you three favors.” Chu Dingjiang was satisfied. “Deal.” Mo Sigui asked, “Can you catch them anytime soon?” “Both types of people can be found in Xijin Prefecture.” Chu Dingjiang leaned against the edge of the table, one hand propping up his cheek. “Ning Yanli is currently close to Yelu Jinglie, and he has many assassins under his command who can boost one’s cultivation level. The ‘Konghe Secret Manual’ is also in his possession. Those poisoned will be summoned to Xijin Prefecture. I have the address of his secret residence in Xijin Prefecture. If you change your mind and want to go and catch them yourself, I will consider it a favor you owe me.” “They are all as cunning as ghosts,” Mo Sigui said, already numb to it. “I do not like owing favors, but one is one favor, two is another, and a few more do not bother me. I am not worried about having too many debts, so it is better if you catch them for me directly.” “I will go in a few days.” “Why a few days?” Mo Sigui asked, intrigued and eager to find out. “It’s more important to settle my Ah Jiu down properly.” “Do not worry, I will take care of it!” Chu Dingjiang glanced at him. “I am not at ease.” Mo Sigui slammed his hand on the table. “What’s there to worry about? It is just moving house; what’s the big deal!” Chu Dingjiang flipped through a page of the account book, lowered his eyes, and said, “Our Ah Jiu cannot live your messy life.” “How am I living a messy life! I am living it up; I am living it like a man,” Mo Sigui retorted defiantly. Chu Dingjiang sat up straight, wrote a few words in the account book, and ignored him. Mo Sigui found it pointless and waved his hand dismissively. “Fine, go whenever you want; I will find something else interesting to do first.” “Take care,” Chu Dingjiang said without looking up. “Hmph!” Mo Sigui returned to his room, seething with anger. Meanwhile, several carriages stopped outside the county government gate. A servant alighted from the carriage and asked the old gatekeeper, “Old man, is Young Lady Mei here?” Seeing that the group was dressed in fine clothes, the old man politely inquired, “And your family is…?” “My mistress is Madam Mei,” the servant replied. Upon hearing that they were from the Mei family, the old man warmly said, “They are a large family, residing in the western residence. They are all out working during the day and not home. However, Fourteenth Young Lady is at the yamen.” The servant bowed and said, “Then please, old man, inform her.” “No trouble at all,” the old man said, “Please wait a moment.” He turned and went into the courtyard, approaching the old woman guarding the second gate and informing her. The old woman quickly found An Jiu. “Fourteenth Young Lady, your Madam Mei has arrived and is outside the main gate.” “Madam Mei?” An Jiu was currently gathering the people Chu Dingjiang had brought, and upon hearing this, she could not immediately recall who Madam Mei was! “Oh,” An Jiu realized. The Mei family had two matriarchs. On the day the Mei clan was wiped out, the second matriarch fell seriously ill and had been bedridden ever since. This time, they were rushing to Hexi County to find Mo Sigui to resolve the poisoning issue, so they could not take her along and only left a few loyal servants to care for her, waiting for things to improve before making further plans. The matriarch of the eldest branch had disappeared that day; her body had not been found, and she had not reappeared. How could she suddenly appear? An Jiu turned to the people who had just gathered and said, “I will go check on her. You all go about your business.”

chapters.title: Betrothal Gifts
chapters.content: An Jiu arrived at the entrance of the yamen and saw several carriages parked there. A middle-aged woman alighted from one of the carriages and walked towards her. “This servant, Ling-Xi, greets Fourteenth Young Lady,” the woman said, bowing slightly. Ling-Xi had always been the Old Madam’s right-hand woman. Seeing her now, An Jiu could not help but recall the disaster at Mei Mansion. Memories flooded back, and the faces of many members of the Mei family suddenly appeared, causing her to freeze for a moment. “Fourteenth Young Lady?” Ling-Xi called softly. “Our Old Madam of the Mei family is dead,” An Jiu said calmly. Ling-Xi’s face darkened slightly. “Fourteenth Young Lady is joking. The Old Madam was seriously injured. As soon as she recovered, she went to the capital to find the rest of the Mei family. I heard the whole family moved here, so I followed.” An Jiu sneered, “The Second Old Madam is still recuperating in the capital, is she not?” “The Second Old Madam has always disliked our Old Madam. How could she tolerate her?” Ling-Xi, cornered at the door and bombarded with questions, grew angry. “Fourteenth Young Lady, is this behavior because you do not want to acknowledge your grandmother?” “You will not even let us question you if you do not tell the truth? I remember it has been almost two years since the incident at Mei Mansion, has it not? What illness requires two years of hiding and recuperation?” An Jiu then looked at the carriage. “The carriage is clean and tidy; the wheels only have slight wear. Are you telling me you traveled all the way from Bianjing to find us? Go find whoever you want. Anyway, Sixth Uncle told me the Old Madam is dead.” “Ling-Xi, let’s go,” The Old Madam’s voice came from inside the carriage. Ling-Xi gritted her teeth, glared fiercely at An Jiu, turned around, and quickly walked to the carriage. The old gatekeeper watched the carriage drive away and whispered, “Why did you have to come out yourself if you do not acknowledge them, young lady?” “If I do not come out and see for myself, how will I know if it is true or false?” She would not acknowledge the falsehoods, and she certainly would not acknowledge the truth. An Jiu could not understand why this Old Madam had suddenly reappeared. If she could not figure it out, she’d ask Chu Dingjiang. An Jiu ran to the courtyard gate, then suddenly remembered calling him “husband” earlier and abruptly stopped. Her cheeks flushed slightly. After hesitating for a moment, she strode inside. “You are back?” Chu Dingjiang looked at her with a half-smile. An Jiu pouted. “Let’s get down to business.” Chu Dingjiang nodded. “That Old Madam from the Mei family, who disappeared, has suddenly reappeared. I have a feeling she’s up to no good. What do you think they are planning?” An Jiu asked. “The Old Madam was sent to the Mei family by the late Emperor, but she also served Yelu Quancang,” Chu Dingjiang thought for a moment. “The late Emperor is dead. If she has any plans, it is most likely Yelu Quancang’s.” “They’ve done a terrible job as spies. You know everything.” An Jiu smiled and sat down next to him. “What does Yelu Quancang want?” “Do you know who was in charge of her?” Chu Dingjiang smiled and changed the subject. An Jiu thought of everyone she knew. “Gu Jinghong.” “Yes.” “Could it be that Gu Jinghong persuaded them to serve the Liao Kingdom?” An Jiu moved closer to his legs. “How did you know?” Chu Dingjiang leaned down and placed a light kiss on her forehead. “I know many more things. I will tell you slowly later.” I will tell you slowly later… An Jiu’s heart burned. She stammered, unsure whether to respond. “Take a look at this first.” Chu Dingjiang handed her a notebook. An Jiu took the book suspiciously and glanced at it. Many items were circled in red ink. “Why am I looking at this?” she asked. “Betrothal gifts,” Chu Dingjiang replied. The book listed Chu Dingjiang’s various properties. An Jiu flipped through a few pages. Almost all of them were circled in red ink. “You have so much money!” she exclaimed. Chu Dingjiang said, “Half of it was earned by Zhu Pianxian. The rest, the uncirculated ones, are her earnings.” He looked at her face, his gaze softening. “I should have gone to the Mei family to propose marriage, but I thought you might not accept them, so I gave up. How about we wait for Aunt Mei to return and discuss the marriage with her? What do you think?” Although An Jiu had called him “husband,” it was just a title, and the sudden prospect of marriage still felt somewhat unacceptable to her. Chu Dingjiang’s suggestion to wait for Mei Yanran’s return suited her perfectly, so she quickly nodded. Chu Dingjiang had anticipated this outcome, so he was not disappointed. He had enough patience to wait. “If you give me all this, what will you do?” An Jiu flipped through the book to the end and found that Chu Dingjiang seemed to have left himself nothing. “Ah Jiu, I am entrusting the rest of my life to you.” Chu Dingjiang held her hand, half-jokingly. “What difference does it make whether I leave these or not?” Chu Dingjiang had never cared about money. He was very adaptable; he was frugal when he had the means and easygoing when he didn’t. He could manage either way. “I do not want it. I do not know anything about management,” An Jiu tossed the book aside. “It’s just a matter of whose name to put on it. I am not good at these things. If you want to rebuild a strong army, the rations from the court will not be enough. There will be many other expenses in the future.” Chu Dingjiang picked up the book, thought for a moment, and sighed. “Let’s discuss it again when Aunt Mei comes back,” An Jiu’s expression was strange. Chu Dingjiang frowned. “Just say what you have to say.” “I feel like you are acting a bit childish by calling her Aunt Mei,” An Jiu said. “Do I look that old?” Chu Dingjiang looked in the mirror. He was indeed a bit rough-looking, but even so, he was clearly no more than thirty. “I did not say you look old!” An Jiu roughly brushed aside his beard, confirming before saying, “It’s just that you actually look older.” “It’s fine, as long as you do not mind.” Chu Dingjiang simply gave up struggling. An Jiu shook her head, returning to the initial topic, “You still have not said what Yelu Quancang really wants to do.” “I do not know; too many possibilities,” Chu Dingjiang pondered. “It could be planning an attack on the Song Dynasty, or it could be that he learned of Wei Yuzhi’s betrayal and sent someone to silence him. He’s the Emperor of Liao; he has many things he wants to do…I will tell you after I see things more clearly.” It was midday outside, the sunlight dazzling. Chu Dingjiang squinted, concealing his deep, unfathomable eyes. At the western courtyard. The Old Madam and her entourage arrived at the Mei family’s temporary residence. Mei Tingzhu returned from the restaurant and, seeing the carriages and horses at the entrance and Ling-Xi standing beneath them, paused slightly. A moment later, she quickly stepped forward. “Aunt Ling-Xi?” Ling-Xi turned and saw Mei Tingzhu rushing to greet her. “Fourth Young Lady has grown into a beautiful young lady.” Mei Tingzhu smiled faintly, not responding, and glanced at the carriage. “Aunt Ling-Xi, who is this?” “It’s the Old Madam,” Ling-Xi sighed. “It’s a long story…” Mei Tingzhu straightened her clothes, not asking what had happened, and said solemnly, “Since it is the Old Madam, I should go and pay my respects.” “Fourth Young Lady is so polite,” Ling-Xi said with a smile, leading her over. Mei Tingzhu reached the carriage and slightly crouched down. “Old Madam.” The Old Madam lifted the curtain and glanced at Ling-Xi. “Hurry up and help Fourth Young Lady up!” Ling-Xi reached out to help, but Mei Tingzhu had already straightened up. “The doorway is not the place to talk. It is just that the door is too small for a carriage to pass through. I am sorry to trouble you to get out of the carriage, Old Madam.”

chapters.title: I’ve Come, Do You Know?
chapters.content: A fair hand reached out from inside the carriage, and Ling-Xi offered her forearm. The Old Madam, dressed in a dark green jacket, had skin that appeared radiantly white. Her beautiful face was adorned only with a few crow’s feet at the corners of her eyes, making her look no older than thirty. Standing next to Mei Tingzhu, it was impossible to tell that the two were grandmother and granddaughter. Upon entering the house, the Old Madam looked around, sighing with emotion, “The Mei family has fallen so low.” Mei Tingzhu poured her a glass of water, saying, “It was expected. We were all prepared for this day.” “Why have you come, Old Madam?” Mei Tingzhu interrupted Ling-Xi, seeing her about to object. “Let’s not beat around the bush. We all know your true identity, Old Madam. Now that the Mei family has fallen, you should return to your former position. Even in times of wealth and power, you could not be of one mind; how can you be now?” “Fourth Young Lady has always been intelligent,” the Old Madam said calmly, showing no embarrassment at having her secret exposed. “Marrying into the Mei family was the luckiest and most painful thing in my life.” Before marrying into the Mei family, she was a member of the Dragon Martial Guards. One by one, the female guards around her were placed on the Emperor’s bed to become his alchemy vessels for ascension. She thought she would be forever trapped in this dark abyss, never seeing the light of day again. However, fate showed her a glimmer of light—the Emperor bestowed her upon the Mei family as their second wife, the eldest son’s wife. Without hope, there was no greater despair. It was this glimmer of false light that granted her rebirth, yet simultaneously plunged her into another abyss, forcing her to endure a life of even greater pain and torment. Thinking of this, the Old Madam’s brow furrowed slightly, her tone as calm and slow as before. “Everyone has unspoken feelings. You do not need to ask my purpose. I swear on my deceased daughter’s oath, I will not do anything to harm the Mei family.” This Old Madam of the eldest branch was not always so aloof; she only changed suddenly after the death of her only biological daughter. If there was anything she cared about most, it was, undoubtedly, her daughter. Since she dared to say this, it could not be false. “Although the Mei family has declined, they can still support you, Old Madam. Hexi is poor; Old Madam should return to the capital to retire,” Mei Tingzhu said. The Old Madam smiled. “I’ve come to acknowledge my kinship today because I still hold onto this affection. I am the matriarch of the first branch, even though the first branch is extinct. My fate is not for the younger generation of the second branch to decide. Do you not agree?” “The Old Madam is right,” Mei Tingzhu replied with a smile. “If the Old Madam needs anything, she can come to me anytime. I will handle the affairs of the second branch for now.” The Old Madam straightened her cuffs. “Then please find me a place to stay in Hexi, Fourth Young Lady.” Mei Tingzhu nodded. “That is a small matter. Magistrate Wu has allocated nineteen houses nearby to the Mei family. There are two empty rooms. If the Old Madam does not mind, she can stay there.” “Alright,” the Old Madam readily agreed without even looking. After all, no hardship could compare to the days of sleeping in the open, and no wealth could compare to owning an entire island with the Mei family. Mei Tingzhu had originally led her clansmen to Hexi County to find Mo Sigui in order to cure her poison, but after arriving here, she had the idea of ​​staying. In Bianjing, they could only live with their tails between their legs. They constantly worried whether the Emperor was thinking of them again. Hexi County was vast and open, though not as grand as Bianjing, and life was much more comfortable. Now, An Jiu controlled the thousand-strong self-defense force of Hexi County. If the Mei family intervened now… In the Liao Kingdom, Shangjing. Inside the secret room, a beam of moonlight shone through the ceiling, landing at the feet of a black-clad man. He sat in a wheelchair. Well-fitting clothes outlined his slender figure. His long hair was loose, cascading over his broad shoulders. A half-silver mask was tightly fastened to his skin, reflecting a faint, cold light and outlining the sharp lines of his profile. He exuded a cold and austere air. “Grand Preceptor, His Majesty has sent someone into Hexi.” A shadowy figure emerged from the darkness, bowing as he reported Yelu Quancang’s actions. “That person is the matriarch of the Mei family’s eldest branch, the grandmother of Young Lady An Jiu.” The person never disobeyed Xiao Che’s orders, but could not understand why a genius like the Grand Preceptor, who was so fixated on important matters, would be so obsessed with obtaining a completely unknown stranger. Xiao Che had a book on his lap, his long, gloved hands turning the worn pages. “What does she look like?” he asked. Xiao Che had asked this question at least ten times. If he truly wanted to see An Jiu, he would have done so long ago, whether by capturing her or going to see her himself. The person in the darkness was wary, yet still described An Jiu’s appearance as before: Beautiful, cold. From others, he could only glean these two vague descriptions. “Go, continue keeping watch,” Xiao Che said. The person acknowledged and disappeared into the darkness. Xiao Che paused, gazing up at the beam of moonlight, motionless for a long time, like a handsome statue. “An Jiu…” Every time he uttered this name, a strange emotion welled up within him. The book on his lap was written by his own hand. At that time, he still retained some fragments of memory, hastily scribbling down many things. In the years that followed, he used these fragments of memory to commit many horrific acts, yet his heart grew increasingly empty. Confusion, like a shadow, followed him, deepening as his memories faded. Until he learned of An Jiu’s existence. His stubborn, almost obsessive pursuit of perfection led him to constantly ponder how to embed her into his life. When he formed the “Hunter,” An Jiu was the first person he thought of. From any perspective, An Jiu was the perfect weapon he sought. Yet, for some reason, he ultimately abandoned this idea. Just as he was still struggling to find the answer, someone unexpectedly approached An Jiu, protecting her completely. It turned out, to possess, one must first have interaction. “Are you my cure?” Xiao Che’s fingers traced the frantic handwriting on the paper, a long-lost heat igniting in his blood. It was the excitement of challenging his deepest fears. Whether he wanted to admit it or not, he could not erase the fear deep within him. If An Jiu could not help him regain his memories, if her appearance could not change the status quo in the slightest, what should he do next? What should he do? She was like hope, something that could sustain him as long as she was there. But he could not live in ignorance forever. One day, he had to touch it to see if it was the truth or just a bubble. Xiao Che closed the book, leaning forward to touch the beam of moonlight before him. His ten slender fingers intertwined, as if trying to catch it, but instead shattered the white frost on the ground. An Jiu, I’ve come. Do you know?

chapters.title: Sweet Words
chapters.content: An Jiu sat up abruptly, sweat beading on her forehead. “Dreaming?” Chu Dingjiang reached out and put his arm around her. An Jiu took a deep breath. “I have not dreamt about these things in a long time.” Chu Dingjiang did not ask, only gently patted her back. In her dream, she repeatedly killed her father by accident and repeatedly watched her mother die before her eyes, like an endless cycle, until finally, that person opened the car window, flicked away a cigarette butt, and smiled slightly at her. “I once thought that person’s waiting was my destiny, but I never imagined he would be my true nightmare,” An Jiu said, hugging Chu Dingjiang tightly. “You have to promise me…” “Hmm?” “Never leave me, always be good to me, just like now.” “Hmm.” “Maybe you think you are not successful enough, but in my heart, you are the strongest man in the world, so strong that as long as I see you, I feel that nothing can make me despair.” Chu Dingjiang raised his hand to stroke her hair, his voice slightly hoarse. “I always thought you could not say sweet words, but I never expected you could be so captivating.” An Jiu smiled. “I am telling the truth.” “I promise you,” Chu Dingjiang said softly. “Sleep.” The two lay back down, An Jiu clinging to him like a sloth. In her drowsy state, she murmured, “Husband.” This time, An Jiu was not embarrassed; it sounded perfectly natural. “Hmm.” Chu Dingjiang patted her gently, thinking to himself that it was time to prepare for the wedding. The next morning. Mei Tingzhu came looking for An Jiu. After taking their seats, she first spoke of the Old Madam’s affairs. Seeing An Jiu’s perfunctory attitude, she then turned to the issue of the Mei family’s resettlement. “Your army is still short-handed, is it not? The family cannot offer much help in this situation, but after all, generations have served in the Konghe Army. If needed, just let us know,” Mei Tingzhu said. Just a few days ago, Chu Dingjiang had analyzed the Mei family’s development with her. They were clearly asking for her help, yet they were acting as if they were doing her a favor. However, considering she did need manpower, she echoed Chu Dingjiang’s instructions, saying, “We do need people, but it is not good to trouble the clan too much…” “We are all family, so let’s not talk about that,” Mei Tingzhu said. “Until the poisoning issue is resolved, we can only stay here. Being able to help is better than being idle.” “Then I will not stand on ceremony.” An Jiu readily accepted her kindness. The Mei family only had a limited number of people. After receiving the list, An Jiu grouped them together, choosing a member of the Mei family as the leader. According to Chu Dingjiang’s plan, the thousand men would be divided into ten groups of one hundred each. The Mei family would not be in any of these ten groups; they would exist independently as a scout team. Of course, the Mei family was unaware of this for the time being. Mei Tingzhu originally thought that An Jiu would definitely train the new recruits, and the Mei family members, mostly seasoned assassins, would be perfect for training them. This would give the Mei family an opportunity to control the entire Self-Defense Force. However, Mei Tingzhu never expected that An Jiu would assign the powerful former members of the Konghe Army as scouts. An Jiu was busy recruiting in the morning and did not eat until after noon. “Is your division not too simplistic?” An Jiu’s mouth was full of food. She shifted it on her cheeks, frowning as she looked at Chu Dingjiang, who was engrossed in writing at his desk. Chu Dingjiang did not look up. “A thousand people is not much, so the internal hierarchy does not need to be too complicated. But simplicity has its drawbacks. The leaders of these ten groups should all be trusted confidants.” An Jiu, holding her bowl, leaned closer. Chu Dingjiang calmly put his things away. “What are you writing?” Chu Dingjiang pulled An Jiu towards the dining table. She turned her head sharply and saw a letter peeking out from a stack of books. “Writing a letter?” “Yes, I am writing to ask Sheng Changying if his child has been born yet and also to ask him to keep an eye out for good girls for Wei Yuzhi in the capital,” Chu Dingjiang pressed her down to sit at the table. An Jiu nodded hurriedly. “Yes, yes, we need to pay attention to that. He seems very anxious.” Chu Dingjiang raised an eyebrow. “Very anxious?” “Yes, the first time he saw me, he said he wanted to marry me. He seems very eager.” An Jiu stuffed another mouthful of food into her mouth and mumbled, “Oh, and most importantly, beautiful.” Although they were rivals, Chu Dingjiang could not help but shed a tear of sympathy for Wei Yuzhi. Thinking back, his relationship with An Jiu had been a bit difficult, but at least she had noticed him and was willing to put in the effort. Chu Dingjiang suddenly felt that he and Wei Yuzhi were both masochists—ignoring so many normal girls, they chose this heartless one! An Jiu, oblivious to his thoughts, was lost in her own reverie. “Do you think Wei Yuzhi can sense my emotions?” “He’s the one who bestowed blood; he should not be able to sense it,” Chu Dingjiang said. “Alright, having taken someone’s heart’s blood, this price is insignificant.” An Jiu finished her rice quickly, put down her chopsticks, and hastily wiped her mouth. “I’ve arranged to go to Bianjing with Xue Sha.” “To snatch someone from Hua Rongjian?” Chu Dingjiang silently cleared the table. They were not used to having outsiders wandering around their territory, so they never had servants. An Jiu was the type to eat dinner, wipe her mouth, and leave, leaving all the cooking and washing to Chu Dingjiang. “Where are we going to find people so quickly? Summer’s here, winter’s not far off,” An Jiu said defiantly. “Those people are attracted by the money; they are not on the bounty list.” Winter was the season for the Liao cavalry to “hunt” within Song territory. Chu Dingjiang said, “Although they are doing it for money, the truly capable ones are the bounty hunters who are already on the list. If you try to rob them, Hua Rongjian will not let you off easily.” An Jiu, having spent a lot of time with Mo Sigui, had picked up his bad habit and clicked her tongue vigorously. “Is that so? What should we do?” She did not have many friends, and even though there was a rift between her and Hua Rongjian now, she still cared about him a little. “If it were anyone else, I would have snatched it from them, but since I met Hua Rongjian, he’s always been the one helping me. In the end, I even lied to him for your sake,” An Jiu sighed. “I owe him more.” The death of Hua Rongjian’s mother was arguably entirely caused by Chu Dingjiang. As someone in the know, when Hua Rongjian came to her in despair, An Jiu pretended not to know anything about it and even developed a closer relationship with Chu Dingjiang. These were the root causes of her estrangement from Hua Rongjian, and she was powerless to change them because she could only choose one of the two. “If it were the old you, you would not have had so many concerns, would you?” Chu Dingjiang asked with a smile. An Jiu said, “My life was not that complicated!” Before, her entire life revolved around receiving orders, executing orders, and completing tasks. “I remember Piaomiao Mountain Mansion has quite a few assassins, right?” An Jiu’s eyes suddenly lit up. “I can go ask Wei Yuzhi if he still has any connection with Piaomiao Mountain Mansion. If not, I will go and kidnap them.” This was a shortcut. Whether it was Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, the Konghe Army, or the Bounty List, they were essentially the same—assassin organizations with the same habit: obedience. These assassins were used to obeying the strong. An Jiu’s suggestion of kidnapping was quite apt. “I have some concerns. Do not rush into action. Let me think about it.” Chu Dingjiang instinctively felt she could not kidnap someone from Piaomiao Mountain Mansion. It was not because he was afraid of offending anyone, but rather because of some inexplicable reservations. He needed to clearly consider all the advantages and disadvantages before he felt comfortable letting An Jiu do it. An Jiu considered the complex background of Piaomiao Mountain Mansion and did not know who the assassins were currently under. It was indeed not advisable to kidnap them rashly. Since Chu Dingjiang had reservations, she subconsciously trusted him and immediately decided to postpone action. “Alright, then you think about it. I will go wander around town and see if I can find anyone with decent aptitude.” An Jiu had thoroughly sifted through the town’s able-bodied men, and had indeed found a few with good potential. Even so, the army, with a thousand slots, had not even recruited a tenth of them yet. Chu Dingjiang watched her leave, picked up her bowl, and went to the well to scoop water to wash the dishes. As he washed, his mind began to wander, a complex web of thoughts connecting and knotting together. Many tangled issues became clearer after he carefully sorted them out. And what he was thinking about was not just Piaomiao Mountain Mansion. When they stormed the fake headquarters of Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, they found many blue-fire crossbows hidden inside. Ever since his first encounter with the blue-fire crossbow during the trials, he had been secretly investigating. However, due to the limited number of spies he had in the Liao Kingdom and the various upheavals in the Song Dynasty diverting most of his attention, he had yet to discover who had created these blue-fire crossbows. It was time for an open and honest conversation with Wei Yuzhi! Chu Dingjiang put down the clean bowls, wiped his hands, and turned to leave.

chapters.title: A Formidable Rival
chapters.content: Wei Yuzhi had always lived in Mo Sigui’s courtyard. He did not hold any official position in Hexi County, only serving as Wu Lingyuan’s advisor. Due to poor health, he could only spare a maximum of one hour each day to discuss matters with Wu Lingyuan. After lunch, he was strolling around the courtyard. He circled the peach tree in the northwest corner to the main gate, where he saw Chu Dingjiang standing under the eaves. Without any pleasantries, Wei Yuzhi’s first words were, “Lord Chu has truly sacrificed a great deal for Fourteenth Young Lady; I am no match for him.” His mental power was far superior to An Jiu’s, so Chu Dingjiang’s decline in skill naturally could not be hidden from him. “My Lord, you are staying with the Divine Physician, yet your complexion still does not seem to be improving?” Chu Dingjiang descended the steps. Wei Yuzhi indifferently looked away. How could he be improving? He listened every day to the woman he cared about in bed with another man, to their various risqué conversations, and yet he had not been driven to death by anger—it was only because he was so easygoing! He wondered if Chu Dingjiang was deliberately trying to provoke him, bringing up the very thing he did not want to hear! In an instant, Wei Yuzhi calmed down and sat down at the stone table. “Please sit, Master Chu.” “Master Wei is a sensible man, so I will not beat around the bush.” ​​Chu Dingjiang sat opposite him and stated his purpose directly. “The blue-fire crossbow is terrifyingly powerful, unlike anything found in this world. You were once an old friend of Yelu Quancang; do you know who made this weapon?” “You’ve been quite patient, only asking now,” Wei Yuzhi said. Chu Dingjiang smiled slightly. “If I had asked two months earlier, would you have told me?” Wei Yuzhi smiled and shook his head. “In the previous Liao dynasty, there was a prodigy, the young Grand Perceptor Xiao Che.” Chu Dingjiang considered all the people in Liao who might have been involved in this scheme, and this was the person he suspected most. Wei Yuzhi could not help but scrutinize Chu Dingjiang closely. At first glance, he appeared to be a martial artist, yet his every move, seemingly rough and unrestrained, exuded an air of nobility, his gaze deep and unfathomable. He radiated an aura of ageless strength, like a pine or bamboo that had withstood countless years. No wonder An Jiu often teased him about looking old; indeed, even though he was younger, Wei Yuzhi felt as if he were facing an elder, unconsciously inspiring respect. “Not bad,” Wei Yuzhi said, withdrawing his probing gaze. Chu Dingjiang remained outwardly calm, but inwardly, he was alarmed. Wei Yuzhi’s gaze was almost tangible, as if it could see through his skin to his bones, as if it could touch his soul through his body. Even with his mental power bordering on the ninth level and the Transcendent Realm, he felt somewhat outmatched. “Ever since Xiao Che’s face was disfigured in a fire, he’s become reclusive, imprisoning himself in a secluded room. In recent years, he’s become increasingly strange,” Wei Yuzhi said. “I’ve been to the Liao capital several times, but I’ve never entered the secret room. So I tried to probe him with my mental power, but… I could not sense him.” Wei Yuzhi slightly raised his eyes, looking at the drooping green peach. Recalling that feeling from that day, a chill still ran down his spine. “I wondered if there was anyone in the world with mental power surpassing mine. I kept searching, and when I finally encountered one, fear welled up from the bottom of my heart.” When Wei Yuzhi first met An Jiu, besides being amazed by her appearance, her almost equal mental power was also one of the reasons he was attracted to her. “That feeling was as if it touched the vastness of the heavens, the primordial universe. An ordinary person’s life is but a fleeting moment.” Wei Yuzhi’s gaze passed over the peach, looking up at the sky. “I know that the assassins of the Konghe Army hang a soul bell after death to leave a mark on this world. But in truth, none of us leaves anything behind. Even if we’ve done earth-shattering things, after the vicissitudes of life, perhaps not even a single word will remain. Thinking of this,” Wei Yuzhi withdrew his gaze, a faint smile appearing on his pale, handsome face, “I actually find it terrifying. I… I always thought I was not afraid of death.” “Perhaps the higher one’s mental power, the more afraid they are of annihilation.” Chu Dingjiang’s words struck at the heart of the matter. “I’ve heard that Taoist cultivation emphasizes consciousness and soul. For you, the death of the body is insignificant; only the dissipation of consciousness can evoke the same fear as ordinary people. I am curious: what kind of person could evoke such fear in you?” Wei Yuzhi was silent for a moment, then replied, “The vastness of time, the immensity of heaven and earth.” Yes, that person was like the endless night sky, without end, eternally existing. “Such a person actually exists in this world,” Chu Dingjiang said. Wei Yuzhi paused, then continued, “He was a high-ranking official of the previous dynasty, capable of influencing the political situation even in his youth. With his abilities, if he had started plotting back then, overthrowing the Yelu Dynasty would have been a piece of cake. Yet, all these years, he has never amassed troops or consolidated power, only sitting in his secluded room meditating. I wonder what he’s thinking.” He thought Xiao Che’s thoughts were beyond the reach of ordinary people. If he knew that this man spent his days immersed in questions like “Who am I? Where do I come from?”—questions only felines ponder—he wondered what Wei Yuzhi would think. What Wei Yuzhi could not believe was that someone with such powerful mental strength had spent years cautiously contemplating whether or not to reach out and touch the tiny dream within his grasp. “What exactly is going on with Piaomiao Mountain Mansion?” Chu Dingjiang asked. “The Piaomiao Mountain Mansion… It feels like a lifetime ago. Yelu Quancang and I co-founded it. Just as the rumors say, I was in charge of its operation, while he stayed to recuperate. Sometimes, when he felt better, he would act as an assassin, carrying out missions and earning the title of the mansion’s top assassin.” He lowered his eyes, concealing his emotions. “From the moment he proposed building the fake mansion, I knew he wanted to undermine my power. It was from then on that he started acquiring those blue-light crossbows. Their power was immense; just a hundred could destroy tens of thousands of men.” How could flesh and blood withstand such power? “Everything was personally overseen by Yelu Quancang. I am not entirely clear on the specifics, but I can guess that the battle at the ancient temple was merely a test of the bows, and the bows and arrows hidden in the fake mansion you massacred were leftovers from that test. Those were prototypes of the blue-fire crossbow; they might still be improving them.” Wei Yuzhi suddenly laughed, a hint of untamed spirit creeping into his usually gentle demeanor. “The path I’ve chosen is to fight against fate, against heaven, against an enemy so powerful it inspires trembling. Even if I die, I will have no regrets.” His life had been too stifled; to challenge such a terrifying opponent like this allowed him to release some of the pent-up frustration in his heart. Leaving Wei Yuzhi, Chu Dingjiang felt somewhat worried. The Liao Kingdom harbored such a powerful enemy. Could Lou Xiaowu’s abilities rival this man’s?
