Chu Dingjiang knew An Jiu was determined to clear her name and become an upright and conscientious person. That was why she wanted to do something for the Song Dynasty and its people. However, she could not suddenly become a savior of the people, wielding a powerful army. Right now, she could only care about her own immediate territory. But when the nest was overturned, no egg remained unbroken. If the two countries went to war and the Song Dynasty fell, her dreams would be shattered. He could not bear to see her heartbroken and disappointed. Chu Dingjiang sighed. He was destined to worry! At this moment, he felt he had been tricked. When he first met An Jiu, she was clueless and did not have the idea of “being a good person.” Just when he was about to retire gracefully, she found a way to go against the tide. What could he do? Having married such a woman, expecting to spend his days watching birds, walking the tigers, and indulging in nature was nothing but a pipe dream. So be it… Could it be that Heaven could not bear to let him be buried in obscurity? Chu Dingjiang could not help but smile self-deprecatingly.

chapters.title: Feeding
chapters.content: Late at night. Several groups of figures moved swiftly across the open fields, like ghosts, skimming over the tall grass. These people had blank stares, yet they moved with unwavering focus in one direction. The rustling sounds grew increasingly dense, and the number of people had swelled to seventy or eighty. Standing atop the city wall of the capital was a woman in a grey robe, her face completely covered, her gaze calmly fixed on the courtyard. Behind her, inside the city wall, sat another woman, her dark purple robes highlighting her fair complexion. Her phoenix eyes, unlike their usual sharp gaze, were now fixed on the grey-robed woman standing by the city wall. “Ning Yi,” a soldier on the watchtower ran over, “They are here, less than two li.” “Hmm,” the grey-robed woman nodded slightly. After a moment’s hesitation, she turned and walked outside the city gate, looking at the fleeting figures reflected in the window. “I am leaving. Does My Liege have anything else to say?” Yelu Huangwu opened her mouth, wanting to say something, but ultimately let out a soft sigh. Ning Yanli waited a moment, but hearing no words, she turned and left. “Ningzi,” Yelu Huangwu’s voice called out. Ning Yanli stopped and turned back, seeing the city gate open. Yelu Huangwu slowly walked out, the moonlight like a white veil draped over her, making her face appear pale and hazy. “You must hate me very much,” Yelu Huangwu said. Ning Yanli shook her head. “You saved my life, and now I am returning it to you. There’s no question of hatred.” “You’ve served me for so many years; you’ve repaid any debt of gratitude you could have for me.” Yelu Huangwu stood there, not taking a step closer. Ning Yanli closed her eyes, no longer looking at her. “You saved me, taught me so much, and your most successful lesson was ‘loyalty.’ Even though I’ve seen through many things, I am still willing to help you, even at the cost of my life. Compared to that, my pursuit of medicine and the life I envisioned are all just illusions. I have no complaints. Now that I’ve repaid your kindness, everything is over. I only hope… Never to meet you again in the next life.” Ning Yanli did not look at Yelu Huangwu’s expression, turning and walking away, saying, “But even though I was just a dog you raised in this life, I’ve developed a little bit of affection for you. I will use that last bit of affection, wishing you a beautiful dream.” Having said that, she quickened her pace and left. In her mind, if she had not died from testing the medicine, even dying at Mo Sigui’s hands would have been a decent end. Medicine-feeding. She used her own flesh and blood to feed those walking corpses, controlling them with her consciousness to achieve her goals. Only a physician like her could do this. The methods described in the Secret Manual of Konghe were incomprehensible to ordinary people. She herself had studied it for a long time before finally understanding it. The moment she grasped it, she knew Yelu Huangwu would sacrifice her. This was expected, so why did she still feel such pain, such resentment? Yelu Huangwu on the city wall had not uttered her last words before the woman was gone, leaving only a blurry image. “Do not go,” she murmured. She struggled internally but ultimately chose to sacrifice Ning Yanli. The death of the Madman could be excused as an accident, but Ning Yanli’s sacrifice was beyond dispute. If she truly could not bear it, there was still a chance to stop it. But she did not. Yelu Huangwu stood by the parapet, seeing Ning Yanli standing alone in the distance, slowly removing the coarse robe she wore, revealing only a snow-white undergarment. Her jet-black hair fell quietly down her back as she drew a dagger and slashed her hand. Blood flowed, the smell slowly spreading. The group of people, smelling the scent, suddenly went berserk. Like ravenous wolves, they pounced on Ning Yanli. She did not dodge, even extending her bloodied hand to the first assassin who lunged at her. Yelu Huangwu pressed her lips tightly together, her gaze fixed intently on the scene below. As more and more assassins pounced, patches of blood stained Ning Yanli’s snow-white undergarment. She did not resist, but she had to prevent these assassins from biting her vital points from the outset because she had to live until the last assassin drank the life-giving blood. Her flesh was torn off piece by piece, and she trembled with pain. “Ah—” “Hahaha!” Her screams turned into maniacal laughter; her already disfigured face was now even more horrifying. The assassins who ate the blood and flesh would momentarily lose consciousness; one wave fell, and another surged in. It was a nightmare! Blood tears streamed from Ning Yanli’s eyes as she glanced towards the city walls. Everything was a blur of blood; she could not see anything, but she knew Yelu Huangwu was watching her, and she was weeping. She ultimately became like a madwoman—pathetic, tragic, and laughable! “Ningzi, from now on, your name will be Ning Yanli.” “Do you not like Song Dynasty pastries? Ningzi, I will take you.” “Ningzi, why do you think I am persisting like this?” “Ningzi, I am not alone. I know that no matter who betrays me, you will always be by my side.” “Ningzi, whatever you like, I will find it for you.” …Ning Yanli could not deny that Yelu Huangwu’s importance in her heart was unparalleled. Back then, that person would risk her life to secretly take her deep into Song territory to eat a pastry she liked until they were sprawled on a chair, laughing together endlessly. Yelu Huangwu had always treated her specially, and it was precisely because of this that she had developed a sliver of hope. But in the end, she, Ning Yanli, was no different from any other pawn and even died a more tragic death. “Is this the price of having enjoyed happiness…? So many happy people in the world; do they all meet the same end…?” This fleeting thought crossed Ning Yanli’s mind, and she focused all her mental energy, channeling her will into all the assassins. “Kill Yelu Quancang!” With the powerful mental energy spreading, Ning Yanli’s body was instantly torn apart, leaving only a few drops of blood. The soldiers guarding the city witnessed this scene, their faces turning deathly pale. They were men who had faced death many times, and they considered themselves unafraid of death, yet not one of them dared to choose to die like Ning Yanli! When they came to their senses, they were filled with awe for Ning Yanli and utterly convinced of Yelu Huangwu’s power. The Liao Kingdom had a long tradition of women holding power, but Yelu Huangwu had not performed particularly well before, even being confined to the imperial mausoleum for many years as a loser. Her ambition and methods had been too restrained; now it was time to reveal her true colors! She raised a hand to wipe the tears from the corner of her eyes, her gaze as cold as ice. This scheme had no room for defeat! Otherwise, she would be betraying the countless bones beneath her feet! Yelu Quancang must die, for he blocked her path to the pinnacle of power. Yelu Jinglie must die, for only by using his heart’s blood in her medicine could she achieve longevity! “Uncle, you probably do not know, Ningzi never needed to check your pulse.” Yelu Huangwu raised the corners of her mouth and stepped down from the city wall. She had already taken control of the city’s defenses and the palace’s security. The assassins could not be Liao assassins, and Yelu Quancang could control most of the Ghost Shadows. Any unusual movement would surely be detected by him. Fortunately, Yelu Jinglie had obtained the Secret Manual of Konghe and intended to use Ning Yanli to mobilize the Konghe Army families within the Song Dynasty to assassinate Yelu Quancang. She decided to play along. If the plan failed or was exposed, she could extricate herself from the situation; at most, Yelu Quancang would only suspect her. The assassins below the city walls gradually awoke. Driven by the will left behind by Ning Yanli on her deathbed, they seemed to regain a degree of intelligence and managed to infiltrate the city during the changing of the guard. Only a few traces of blood and a faint smell of medicine remained before the city gates. A gentle breeze blew, and everything seemed to have returned to calm. As morning came. Chu Dingjiang dragged two men into Mo Sigui’s courtyard. Wei Yuzhi glanced at them. “The Divine Physician went to the herb garden.” “Please tell him these are the people he wants,” Chu Dingjiang said. Wei Yuzhi noticed his frosty aura, clearly indicating he had not rested all night. He approached and examined the two unconscious men closely. “This is…” “Ask Mo Sigui,” Chu Dingjiang said, turning to leave. “Master Chu’s plan was brilliant,” Wei Yuzhi said. Chu Dingjiang remained silent. Wei Yuzhi’s intelligence network far exceeded his expectations, but it did not matter. “Master Chu, are you truly content with a mediocre life?” Wei Yuzhi asked. Chu Dingjiang turned around. “You flatter me; I am just a rough man.” “Why belittle yourself?” Wei Yuzhi said. “I understand the Liao Kingdom best and am most likely to see through your scheme, yet you predicted I would work for Wu Lingyuan.” The Mei family, remaining in Hexi, ultimately benefited the Hexi magistrate; Wei Yuzhi, as an advisor, would not expose this. “I heard the Mei family obtained part of the Konghe Secret Manual from you. I wondered if the other manuals might have fallen into your hands until the poison within two members of the Konghe family was activated, which confirmed my suspicion.” Chu Dingjiang deliberately left the Konghe Secret Manual to Yelu Jinglie, not Yelu Quancang or Yelu Huangwu. Of these three, Yelu Jinglie had already lost power; his sudden acquisition of this power, coupled with his already precarious military control, would likely lead him to take risky actions. Both harbored ambitions to usurp power. If Yelu Jinglie made a move, Yelu Huangwu would most likely use it against them. And the reality unfolded exactly as Chu Dingjiang had predicted. He could not predict what would happen next, but who the ultimate winner would be was not his concern. “Ah Jiu wants to build an army; I just want to provide her with some men and, incidentally, give her some time to reorganize.” “To buy time for a mere county’s Self-Defense Force, you are letting Liao descend into chaos.” Wei Yuzhi, for one, did not believe he was truly doing all this for An Jiu’s sake. However, in reality, Chu Dingjiang’s main objective was not to destabilize Liao; he simply felt uneasy seeing things incomplete. “You knew all along I would work for Wu Lingyuan; why?” Wei Yuzhi asked. Chu Dingjiang smiled. “Master Wei is resourceful, but his true intentions are not so difficult to understand.” A complex yet simple person. He was a man of deep cunning; Chu Dingjiang might not be able to fathom all his schemes, but he could see that his choices in matters of the heart were simple. Which country he served and whom he served were, in reality, merely emotional decisions. “If there’s nothing else, I will take my leave,” Chu Dingjiang said. “One last question: What did you see last night when you captured those two men?”

chapters.title: Pain
chapters.content: Chu Dingjiang paused. “Ning Yanli fed those mindless assassins with her blood.” “Yelu Huangwu is so ruthless; perhaps she really can succeed.” Wei Yuzhi abandoned all his previous sacrifices more or less because he anticipated this situation. Internal strife within Liao continued, and even if he remained in Liao, he would only be a henchman for Yelu Quancang to consolidate his imperial power, never having the chance to exact revenge in his lifetime. The hatred was long gone; he had already killed his enemies many years ago. He hated the darkness and corruption of the Song Dynasty, but where there was light, there was shadow. He understood this, but he still could not swallow his anger. “Ning Yanli is dead!?” Mo Sigui stood at the door, carrying a medicine basket, his face filled with shock. Chu Dingjiang turned to look at him. “Dead without an intact corpse.” “How could she die?” Mo Sigui hated Ning Yanli intensely, but as a fellow physician, he could not help but feel a little sympathy. The life of a medical prodigy had come to such an abrupt end, suddenly leaving him with a heavy heart. “These are the two people you wanted.” Chu Dingjiang paused, then asked, “When can Ah Jiu be reforged for the second time?” Mo Sigui snapped out of his thoughts. “Based on the timeline, she can do it now. However, she was unconscious for a while, so it will be better if she rests for a few more days.” “What are the disadvantages of reforging now?” Chu Dingjiang asked. “Aside from the effect being slightly weaker, there are no disadvantages.” Mo Sigui asked curiously, “Why are you asking this?” “A storm is brewing; it is better to be prepared. I will discuss it with her, and if she agrees, I’d like her to be reforged in the next few days,” Chu Dingjiang said. Mo Sigui was a perfectionist, but he had already sensed the impending danger, so he made an exception and agreed. After Chu Dingjiang left, he dragged the two people back to the house. Remembering how he had asked Chu Dingjiang to capture someone just a few days ago, he had not expected Chu Dingjiang to capture them so quickly, and he had not expected that Ning Yanli, who made the potion to boost cultivation, was already gone without a trace; Mo Sigui could not help but sigh. “Truly, life is unpredictable!” “With many things about to happen, even a Divine Physician should prepare in advance,” Wei Yuzhi said. Mo Sigui waved his hand dismissively. “Whatever happens, I will just mind my own little herb garden.” Wei Yuzhi said, “Second Young Lady Lou is not in this little herb garden.” Mo Sigui paused, then laughed. “Oh, I did not even remember such a person!” His expression changed, and he said unhappily, “She walks her narrow path. I walk mine. From now on, we will have nothing to do with each other. Second Master Wei, if you mention this person again, do not blame me for turning on you!” Wei Yuzhi’s lips curled slightly. “Since she’s insignificant, why get angry?” He turned and left, giving Mo Sigui no chance to retort. Hatred was harmful in every way, but how easy was it for a truly compassionate person to let go of hatred? Wei Yuzhi could understand Lou Mingyue very well and admired her courage and perseverance. Only then did he, being nosy, speak up, reminding Mo Sigui that he hoped Lou Mingyue could have a good ending. Could Mo Sigui really go his own way, as he himself said? Wei Yuzhi did not believe it. “What do you mean? Hmph. I said I’d cut ties completely, and you do not understand me at all!” He paced angrily around the room for a few moments, then found his pipe and lit it again after only two days of abstinence. He puffed out smoke. His mood gradually calmed down. Mo Sigui stared at the slowly rising smoke from his pipe, his thoughts drifting away. Currently, the most ambitious person in Hexi County was undoubtedly An Jiu. She had been searching throughout Hebei Road for months and had actually recruited quite a few people. Although her strength was far from what she had imagined, she was still enjoying it immensely. Chu Dingjiang was wholeheartedly devoted to being her “wise wife,” building a camp in the city, and quickly moving there to set up camp. An Jiu was leading her men in drills on the training ground. Chu Dingjiang, still clad in a black robe, stood on a slope not far from the ground, a hawk perched on his shoulder. The sky was a clear, deep blue; time seemed to stand still. After a long while, a dark dot in the distance drew closer. Chu Dingjiang narrowed his eyes and patted the hawk on his shoulder. “Lei Che.” The hawk, receiving the command, spread its wings and soared into the sky, circling once before suddenly swooping down towards the approaching dark dot. The dot panicked, darting about haphazardly. Chu Dingjiang watched the two intertwined shadows approach in the sky and whistled. The hawk’s cry echoed through the sky, and the dark dot plummeted straight down. Halfway down, it stiffly flapped its wings a few times, managing not to fall to its death. Chu Dingjiang swooped over and saw a pigeon covered in blood lying on the ground, a thin bamboo tube still bound to one of its legs. Lei Che circled back onto his shoulder, its head bowed as it stared at the pigeon, seemingly curious. Chu Dingjiang picked up the letters from the bamboo tubes and read them. A smile played on his lips, a cold glint in his eyes. He had long noticed pigeons flying out of Hexi County every few days, but had not acted rashly. Today, he’d released his hawk to test its skills; the pigeon had not died, and with some care, it could still be used. Chu Dingjiang took the pigeon back to camp, carefully cleaning and bandaging it before placing it in a cage. Lei Che seemed quite pleased with its first interception, standing proudly atop the cage, its chest puffed out, guarding it closely. At noon, An Jiu returned for lunch and saw this strange scene as soon as she entered the room. “What’s wrong with this bird?” An Jiu asked. Lei Che turned its head alertly, staring intently at An Jiu. “Its name is Lei Che,” Chu Dingjiang said. Lei Che stood atop the cage, head held high, radiating discontent. Seeing its stubborn expression, An Jiu walked over and glared at it. “Small bird, big temper! You’d better be polite, or I will stew you tonight!” Lei Che took two steps back uneasily but still stared proudly at An Jiu, looking utterly defiant. “How old are you? Still arguing with it?” Chu Dingjiang chuckled. An Jiu pointed to the trembling pigeon in the cage. “Which one is this? Have you recently developed a liking for docile animals?” “This one is indeed docile, but it is not mine. I am just keeping it for a few days,” Chu Dingjiang said, setting out food. An Jiu examined it closely. “A carrier pigeon?” Chu Dingjiang nodded. “Recently, someone has been using carrier pigeons to transmit our whereabouts.” “Is this reconnaissance?” An Jiu asked suspiciously. “Someone wants to kill us? Have we offended anyone?” Chu Dingjiang felt that An Jiu’s mental illness had not fully healed. Ever since she openly served the court, she had revealed all her past dark secrets. It seemed she had always been such a positive and kind person. Seeing her frowning, Chu Dingjiang could not bear to expose her. When she was an assassin, she had not just offended people; she had made mortal enemies. He could only say something else. “The secret letter detailed our movements, and we have almost no common enemies.” The answer was both easy and difficult to guess. Chu Dingjiang knew the secret letter was sent by the Old Madam of the Mei family, who was both a spy for the late Emperor of the Song Dynasty and a Liao spy. The carrier pigeon was flying north. Clearly, it was a message delivered to the Liao Kingdom. But Yelu Quancang should be too preoccupied with his own troubles to bother with his and An Jiu’s whereabouts. They neither wielded significant power nor launched any attack on the Liao Kingdom; they were merely running a small self-defense force in Hexi County. Surely that would not arouse the Liao Emperor’s suspicion? “How much do you know about Old Madam Mei?” Chu Dingjiang wondered. If he were to capture the Old Madam and interrogate her, what were the chances of getting her to talk? “Probably not as much as you do.” Seeing the carrier pigeon, An Jiu immediately understood Chu Dingjiang’s meaning, recalling their first meeting. “Although she’s quite unscrupulous on both sides, you can tell from her eyes that she probably will not succumb to force.” “Bribery?” Chu Dingjiang said, then chuckled to himself. “No matter how great my offer, it cannot compare to the Emperor.” This Old Madam was quite capable. She’s served two Emperors. An Jiu, her mouth already full of food, mumbled a retort, “That is not necessarily true. It depends on what she wants.” Chu Dingjiang paused slightly. “That makes sense.” With the late Emperor of the Great Song Dynasty deceased, any promises of benefits were now null and void, and the relationship between the old woman and Yelu Quancang was difficult to fathom. Chu Dingjiang did not waste time on aimless speculation. Since he was not sure what Yelu Quancang was up to, and to avoid alerting him, he planned to carefully raise the pigeons, forge a secret letter in the original handwriting, and replace the note inside. Afterwards, he took Lei Che every day to intercept the carrier pigeons and replace the secret letters. With a few experiences, Lei Che learned to force the pigeons down without harming them, saving Chu Dingjiang a lot of trouble. Regarding the matter of rebuilding her body, Chu Dingjiang only mentioned it briefly. An Jiu agreed without asking why, and after arranging things for the next few days, she went to Mo Sigui’s courtyard alone. Mo Sigui, with a cigarette dangling from his lips, flipped through a medical book. “Does he know you are coming?” “He’s the one who sent me,” An Jiu said. Mo Sigui stopped what he was doing and looked up at her. “He did not come along?” Reconstructing the body required stripping naked and applying medicine, and Mo Sigui could not believe Chu Dingjiang would be so generous as to let him do it. “When did you say that?” “A couple of days ago.” An Jiu sat down opposite him, tapping the table and urging, “You do not seem busy; hurry up.” Mo Sigui secretly wiped a bead of sweat from his brow. “Luckily, I was smart.” He almost got tricked by An Jiu! If he had just started doing it, he’d probably have his eyes gouged out and his hands crippled! “The medicine was prepared six months ago; we can start anytime, but can you be a little more reserved?” Mo Sigui looked at her with disdain. “After all, you are taken. Can you just casually take your clothes off for another man to see? I feel so sorry for Chu Dingjiang!” “You are not another man,” An Jiu said. Mo Sigui leaned back, exhaling a string of smoke rings, lazily squinting his eyes. “I am a respectable, handsome man, unmarried. You cannot speak so vaguely.” “You misunderstand,” An Jiu explained earnestly. “What I mean is, in my eyes, you are not a man.” “Then I will continue to misunderstand,” Mo Sigui said. An Jiu actually meant, “In my eyes, you are not a man but a friend, a physician,” but she still had not made herself clear. The self-proclaimed highly cultured An Jiu naturally did not think it was her fault. “So stubborn, just like Zhu Pianxian.” “I am too lazy to get angry with you,” Mo Sigui said, fiddling with his pipe. “Let’s wait until Chu Dingjiang arrives before we start.” “He does not know I am coming.” “What in the entire Song Dynasty can be kept from him! You really do not understand your own man at all. I am really worried for him!” Mo Sigui said. An Jiu, hands tucked in, said coolly, “Judging by your eagerness to get involved, you are not interested in him, are you?” “Cough!” Mo Sigui choked on his cigarette. “Nonsense! Chu Dingjiang is a man!” “A man?” Chu Dingjiang had just entered when he heard Mo Sigui gritting his teeth and speaking ill of him. Mo Sigui rubbed his forehead. Meeting these two was the most frustrating thing in his life. Just looking at them made him feel suffocated! For example, he had just said so many good things about Chu Dingjiang, but the guy had not heard a word, deliberately choosing this moment to come! It was clear that even fate would not let them be friends. “I do not want to talk anymore! Let’s begin!” Mo Sigui said, stubbing out his cigarette and getting up to find medicine. Now, irritated, he carried over several bags of medicine and tossed them into Chu Dingjiang’s hands. “Crush these medicines first.” An Jiu, seeing him ordering Chu Dingjiang around, immediately protested, “He’s not a physician; why should he crush the medicine?” “Heh heh, this is the first time I’ve heard that only a physician can crush medicine,” Mo Sigui lay down on the low couch, smiling at An Jiu. “You underestimate your Chu Dingjiang. He can fly and dive; crushing medicine is nothing to him!” Then, he looked at Chu Dingjiang smugly. “Crushing medicine and applying it are the same job. If you say you cannot, Yuzhi does it very well.” The implication was that if he would not crush the medicine now, he’d leave the application to Wei Yuzhi later. Mo Sigui understood; he could only show off in front of Chu Dingjiang now, and this opportunity would not come again. Chu Dingjiang remained silent, pouring the medicine into the mortar and pestle and beginning to crush. When Mo Sigui and Chu Dingjiang met on a narrow path, Mo Sigui had never gained the upper hand! He really wanted to grab a handful of fruit and eat it while watching. But thinking about it, he decided against it, lest he suffer a terrible revenge later. Only the sound of pounding medicine remained in the room. An Jiu went over and said, “Let me pound it for a while.” “You rest. You will have a hard time later. Pounding a few pills is nothing to me.” Chu Dingjiang was not an external cultivator and had never used such a cruel method to temper his body, but he knew about the so-called reforging. In a sense, it was like crushing the body, filtering out impurities, and then forging a new body—a process that could be described as worse than death. Although his words were calm, An Jiu could hear his concern and worry, and she could not help but feel happy. Chu Dingjiang’s heart softened, and he reached out to ruffle her hair. Mo Sigui let out a soft snort, turning his head away from them. These two seemed to exist only to annoy him. From pounding the medicine to brewing it, it took nearly two hours. Normally, anyone who asked Chu Dingjiang to do a favor would have to pay double the price. He only worked tirelessly for An Jiu. Mo Sigui, with the mentality of “might as well use him,” did not even lift an eyelid as he directed Chu Dingjiang’s work. By the time everything was ready, the moon was high in the sky. Only An Jiu and Chu Dingjiang remained in the room. An Jiu hesitated for a long time before finally loosening her clothes. Logically, having been naked with Chu Dingjiang many times before, she should not be shy. But the opposite was true. At this moment, the simple loosening of her clothes seemed extremely awkward. Every movement added a thrilling, heart-stopping feeling to the surrounding air. It was far less satisfying than undressing in front of Mo Sigui. The ties of her undergarment were tied too tightly. An Jiu tugged hard twice, but the knot became indestructible. “I will help you,” Chu Dingjiang said, leaning closer. His deep, resonant voice was close to her ear, seemingly sinking into her heart. An Jiu felt all the blood and heat rush to her ears and then spread to her cheeks and neck as he undressed her. Each piece of clothing fell to the ground until she was completely naked. An Jiu felt a little awkward. Her eyes met Chu Dingjiang’s for a moment, then she quickly looked away, cleared her throat, and whispered, “I think I am becoming more and more timid.” “Not timid,” Chu Dingjiang said with a deep smile, embracing her. “You are very good like this.” The fabric of Chu Dingjiang’s clothes touched her skin, sending a strange tingling sensation through her body. An Jiu thought to herself that she must be having an attack; otherwise, how could she feel this way with similar fabric? Chu Dingjiang had not expected to see another side of An Jiu in this situation. He felt both happy for the moment and heartbroken for the pain she would endure in the next moment. His complex emotions overshadowed his passion. After a while, they separated, and An Jiu lay down on the table that had been prepared beforehand. Chu Dingjiang carefully applied the medicine with a bamboo skewer. The dark ointment gradually covered her fair, smooth skin, suppressing the various emotions within him and restoring his composure. The moonlight outside was bright. Mo Sigui smoked two pipes, reminiscing about the past three times, and lost in thought several times. Looking back, he saw the door was still tightly closed and paused, startled. “Just two things! Are you going to dawdle until dawn?!” He went to knock on the door. After waiting for a while, there was still no answer. “I said, are you planning to come out after the baby is born?!” About a quarter of an hour later, Chu Dingjiang finally opened the door and came out. Mo Sigui’s face darkened. “You are the ones who are in a rush to rebuild, but when it comes down to it, you are the ones who dawdle the most.” Chu Dingjiang was not angry, only giving him a faint glance. “People without wives would not understand.” “You, you, you, stay outside!” Mo Sigui slammed the door shut, huffing as he walked to An Jiu’s side. “I do not have a wife because I do not want one! Believe me, if I said I wanted to get married right now, all the young ladies in Bianjing would line up in Hexi County!” “But ultimately, none of them are the girls you want to marry.” An Jiu’s mouth was covered with a cloth, her voice muffled and contorted by the intense pain. Yet, even so, her words were sharp and cutting. Mo Sigui sighed helplessly. “Can you all not shut up? If I get really angry, I will just quit and see where you can cry then.” “We did not mean it.” Most of the time, she genuinely did not think there was anything wrong with her words. But, “This time it was intentional.” Mo Sigui remained silent, only glaring at her hatefully. To distract herself, An Jiu kept talking to him. “Although I should not meddle in other people’s business, I just cannot stand that you clearly have her in your heart, cannot forget her, yet you’d rather torture yourself to the point of being unrecognizable than go to her.” “I am still handsome and dashing; who said I am unrecognizable!” Mo Sigui tried to change the subject. However, An Jiu was completely absorbed in her own thoughts and did not listen to him at all. “You chose different paths, but she’s on a dead end. If you could rush up and pull her back, that would be so good. Even if you couldn’t, you could accompany her on her final journey so she would not be too lonely in hatred.” These words were not necessarily directed at Lou Mingyue or herself. At that moment, An Jiu longed for someone, something, or even just an object to possess, something that could bring her a sliver of warmth and comfort. “You think letting go is mutual liberation? You do not know, some bonds can never be severed, not even in life or death…” “If it were before, facing the same situation, I would have been completely lost, but now, if I were you, I would cling even tighter, even if it means getting myself trapped.” If, just if, she wanted to go back to her childhood, even if it was only to give her mother a kiss. “If you only stand by and watch, you will regret it, this life, the next life, and the life after that…” An Jiu promised Lou Mingyue she would not interfere in their affairs, and she would keep her promise. However, this did not stop her from using the matter to provoke Mo Sigui every time. “What I said does not mean I am breaking my promise to Lou Mingyue. I did not interfere; I just chimed in.” An Jiu wanted to laugh, but the tearing pain all over her body only allowed her to let out two strange “whooshes.” Still, she was quite pleased with herself. “Such a brilliant idea—how come…it only came to mind now…? Being with Uncle Chu for so long has really made me…cunning…” An Jiu was the kind of person who would not stutter even with a hole in her body. Chu Dingjiang, listening from outside, could not imagine the pain she was in. He felt his heart was a tangled mess. Extremes meeting; that was true. She was so strong, so strong yet so fragile and so heartbreaking. Chu Dingjiang had seen many beautiful, pitiful women. He was a man, too, and he liked those kinds of women, but this one was etched into his bones, ingrained in his blood. He could not help but push open the door and enter. “Ah Jiu.” An Jiu did not answer for a long time, only breathing heavily. After what seemed like an eternity, she finally caught her breath. “Why do I suddenly feel like I cannot hold on anymore?” Just now, she felt she could endure it, but hearing Chu Dingjiang’s voice suddenly made her feel an overwhelming pain. “Chu Dingjiang, it hurts,” she said. Chu Dingjiang did not dare touch her, afraid it would worsen the pain, only saying, “Do not be afraid; I am here with you.” “Alright.” Mo Sigui had been touched by An Jiu’s words, but the current situation shocked him. Chu Dingjiang said, “Do not be afraid; I am here with you.” But where was he when Lou Mingyue was suffering? Was it really just because she was strong and rejected him that he chose to give up? Mo Sigui sighed deeply, feeling somewhat lost. This time, during the reconstruction, Chu Dingjiang was mostly busy with everything, while Mo Sigui only gave verbal instructions, spending the rest of the time daydreaming, which was why time seemed to fly by. Only after he pulled An Jiu out of the medicine tub did he realize that he had not slept or rested for so long.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.content: An Jiu was limp and red all over, her skin wrinkled like a newborn mouse. Even a tiny baby would look ugly like this, so An Jiu, now a grown woman, was unbearably ugly. Yet, Chu Dingjiang carried her back to the house with the utmost care, as if holding his own child, cherishing her like a precious treasure. After all this fuss, Chu Dingjiang fell into a deep sleep, holding the unconscious An Jiu. Mo Sigui, who had also been exhausted for so long, had bloodshot eyes but still could not fall asleep. Pipe after pipe of tobacco filled the courtyard with smoke. There was not a single living creature awake for a one-li radius, yet even with his eyes closed, he felt no sleepiness. The smell of medicine was spreading throughout the city. The sky was beginning to lighten. In the Liao Kingdom’s capital palace, a fierce battle raged. Yelu Quancang’s face was as sickly pale as ever. He seemed oblivious to the sounds outside, calmly reviewing memorials. Dozens of black-clad men stood inside the hall, lifeless and silent. Outside, the sounds of battle were deafening, but inside, all was quiet. Half an hour later, a general rushed to the hall’s entrance. “Your Majesty!” “How is the battle?” came Yelu Quancang’s steady voice from within. The general replied, “The rebels have already crossed Chongxuan Palace and are approaching the study. If Her Highness the Princess’s reinforcements do not arrive soon, we cannot hold them off. Your Majesty should move elsewhere for safety.” Yelu Quancang put down his brush. “Surrender to the rebels.” The general was startled. “Your Majesty! I…” Yelu Quancang interrupted him. “This is an imperial edict.” “I would rather die than surrender!” the general shouted. “I will say it one last time: this is an imperial edict. However, to the outside world, you are only allowed to claim it is your own will.” Yelu Quancang’s tone was calm, without a trace of anger, yet it inexplicably sent chills down one’s spine. The general remained silent for a few moments, then, after calming down, he realized this was probably not a genuine surrender and thus prostrated himself to accept the order. Just after he rose to leave, a sudden change occurred within the hall. Assassins, seemingly appearing from nowhere, suddenly stormed into the hall, engaging the guards in black. Yelu Quancang, seated on his throne, lowered his eyes and toyed with a bamboo flute. As the guards in the hall fell one by one, he brought the flute to his lips to test its sound. The mournful music was plaintive and sorrowful. At Chongxuan Palace, with the surrender of the garrison, the fighting had ceased. Yelu Huangwu, dressed in a tight-fitting outfit, trudged through mountains of corpses and blood towards the imperial study. A group of ghostly figures arrived first, lining up outside the door. Yelu Huangwu stood at the foot of the steps. “Royal Brother, I am late in coming to your rescue!” No one answered from inside. “Go in,” Yelu Huangwu whispered. The ghostly figures burst through the door. The study was already a mess. The once spacious hall was now piled high with hundreds of corpses, leaving almost no room to step. Upon entering, the ghostly figures found their feet soaked with warm liquid. High on the throne, a handsome man in magnificent robes lay wounded by several swords, his body covered in blood, only his face pale and clean. His head hung low, a flute lay at his feet, and streams of blood flowed down the steps, trailing long like a phoenix’s tail. Yelu Huangwu looked up and immediately saw him. A strange expression appeared on her face, a mixture of crying and laughing. She stared at him for a long, long time. Yelu Huangwu slowly walked in. Reaching Yelu Quancang’s side seemed to take a long time, yet also an instant. “Brother,” Yelu Huangwu touched his nose with her fingertips and found he was still breathing. Her expression stiffened slightly, and she raised her voice, “Drag all the survivors out.” The ghostly figure searched among the corpses and found several people still breathing. “Your Highness. Five people are confirmed alive,” The ghostly figure bowed and reported. “Leave,” Yelu Huangwu bent down to pick up the flute that had fallen to the ground. “I want to say goodbye to my brother alone.” “Yes!” The ghostly figure led the five survivors out and closed the palace door. The large study was filled with corpses. Only Yelu Huangwu was alive, and Yelu Quancang was half-dead. “Brother,” Yelu Huangwu gently touched his slightly cool cheek, “I did not want to do this; you forced me. If you were a good brother, I would be a good sister, but you are truly heartless. Since you do not treat me like a sister, then for me, your life has no meaning.” As she spoke, her fingers paused, noticing a faint mark at Yelu Quancang’s temple! Her expression suddenly changed. “Is that so?” A deep, resonant voice suddenly rang out. Before Yelu Huangwu could react, the sound of wind cutting through the air reached her ears. Looking down, she saw a gaping hole in her chest. A spurt of blood shot out like an arrow, splattering onto the imperial desk like a cluster of vibrant red plum blossoms. Yelu Huangwu’s eyes widened in horror. It was a fake! This Yelu Quancang was indeed a fake! Too bad she discovered it too late… She clutched her chest and turned around. Three zhang away, Yelu Quancang, clad in white, vanished amidst the mountain of corpses and sea of ​​blood. “If you have not lost your memory, you should remember what I am best at,” he said. Yelu Quancang had many identities in the Song Dynasty, some real, some fake, some true, none discernible. “Heh, I was careless.” Yelu Huangwu tried to protect her heart with her inner strength, but found she could not muster even a trace of it! “Do you think I enjoy being Emperor? It’s my responsibility. If you told me you wanted this position and could uphold the Yelu family’s rule, I would not have returned. Retiring to the mountains with Mei Ruyan would have been better.” Yelu Quancang looked at her calmly. “You said that as long as I am a good older brother, you will not covet the throne. You’ve misjudged yourself.” Yelu Huangwu had painstakingly helped him return to Liao over the years, and he had not doubted her at first. He was not a sentimental person, usually quiet and reserved, and rarely expressed himself. Asking him to shower someone with tender care and affection was beyond his capabilities. But regardless, he would not mistreat her for the greater good. Yelu Huangwu laughed sarcastically. “Ha, you do not like it?” If he did not like it, would he kill her to protect the throne? If he had the ability to save his own life, should he not have let go? “This time, I gave you free rein to scheme. If you have the means to kill me, proving you are more capable than I am, then it is fine for you to sit on the throne.” Yelu Quancang said, “But you have disappointed me greatly.” Yelu Huangwu slowly stopped smiling, blood trickling from the corner of her lips. “I concede.” At this point, what else could she not understand? Yelu Quancang had long seen through her scheme. He had set this trap to lure her in, even calculating that once she discovered he was still alive, she would not kill him in front of everyone! She herself had sealed the trap. But if she could do it all over again, she still could not kill her brother without restraint, because those ghostly figures were there to rescue the Emperor, completely unaware that she was plotting a rebellion! She only regretted not seeing through the deception sooner. “I am not reconciled.” Yelu Huangwu collapsed to the ground, her vision blurring, yet her eyes remained wide open. Her every plan had been flawless; where had things gone wrong? The one who forced the abdication was Yelu Jinglie. It was also Yelu Jinglie who sent assassins. She was the one who reaped the benefits, the one who came to the rescue—how could she have exposed herself? “You should be resentful, because you’ve never understood yourself. You are clearly an ambitious person, yet you cling to a sliver of tenderness; you crave tenderness, yet you act with ruthlessness. If you had understood yourself from the beginning, if you had cut off those petty thoughts from the start, you would have already possessed the empire. Because I saw through you, I knew that when the Imperial Uncle forced the abdication, I already guessed you would not let this opportunity pass.” Seizing imperial power was inherently the most perilous path in the world. One must not be half-hearted. Know yourself and know your enemy, and you will never be defeated. The most terrifying thing was not knowing yourself, but not your enemy, nor knowing your enemy but not yourself, but that your enemy knows you better than you know yourself. Although she was unwilling, she was not someone who could not accept defeat. “You…helped…cleared my mind, and I will return the favor.” Yelu Huangwu’s voice was very weak, but she knew he could hear her. “Yelu Jinglie is also a medicine person.” This was something Yelu Quancang did not know, but he was not too surprised, nor did he ask further about it, only saying, “If Ning Yanli were still alive, you probably would not be dead either.” Although the hidden weapon injured her heart meridian, she would not have died if treated promptly, only suffering some lasting health problems. The key issue was the medicine applied to the weapon, which prevented her from using her internal energy to protect her heart meridian, thus depriving her of the chance to be saved. If Ning Yanli had remained by her side during crucial moments as before, she might not only have survived but might even have had a chance to escape. Yelu Huangwu’s pupils were unfocused; it was unclear whether she had heard these words. It was also unclear whether she felt regret. “I was only guessing at first, but it was Ning Yi’s death that confirmed my suspicions about your scheme,” Yelu Quancang murmured. Ning Yanli was utterly loyal to Yelu Huangwu. Without her authorization, even if Ning Yanli secretly worked for Yelu Jinglie, she would never sacrifice her life for it. Only Yelu Huangwu herself did not believe in this loyalty. Yelu Quancang went over and removed the mask from the double, taking off his outer garment to reveal a black outfit underneath, then mixed it with the other corpses. He put on his outer robe and, with a slight push of his feet, leaped out of the palace gate. The Ghost Shadow, seeing that he was still alive, immediately knelt. “Greetings, Your Majesty!” “The princess died saving me. After dealing with the traitor, she must be posthumously honored and given a grand funeral!” Just now, when they entered, Yelu Quancang was clearly dead, while Yelu Huangwu was perfectly fine. How come he was the one who came out alive? However, the Ghost Shadow knew that Ning Yanli’s medical skills were extraordinary; even if the person was dead, it would not be surprising if she left behind some method of exchanging life for life. “Her Highness is loyal and righteous!” the ghostly figures all cried out. Only those who followed Yelu Huangwu knew in their hearts that her death was suspicious, but now that she was dead, could they openly question the Emperor? Yelu Quancang’s phoenix eyes were majestic and cold as he surveyed the crowd. “Capture the traitor Yelu Jinglie alive!” “Yes!” With Yelu Huangwu dead, military power naturally returned to the Emperor’s hands. This war was not yet over, but everyone could already foresee its outcome. When news of the Liao internal strife reached the Song Dynasty, the atmosphere in the entire court relaxed, and some officials were eager to celebrate. The Emperor personally drafted an edict appointing Ling Ziyue as Grand General, commanding the three border defense armies. He felt this was a golden opportunity to reclaim the Sixteen Prefectures of Yan and Yun. The Emperor was not blinded by joy. He had been monitoring the Liao Dynasty for the past two years and knew that the Liao ruler, seemingly sickly and reclusive, appeared to have accomplished nothing significant but was actually a formidable figure. It was impossible to seize the opportunity to destroy the Liao Dynasty in one fell swoop. Moreover, given the current state of the Song Dynasty, even if the Liao Dynasty were destroyed, there would be no spare capacity to control it. The only one in the entire Song Dynasty who was unhappy about the Liao internal strife was Wu Lingyuan. Previously, the situation in the Liao Dynasty was tense, with three forces checking and balancing each other, and none daring to easily disperse most of their forces. This minimized the impact on Hexi County. If the internal strife was quelled and power was unified, coupled with the heavy financial drain after the war, the Liao Kingdom’s autumn hunts would undoubtedly be a hundred times more ferocious. “Fortunately, we have General Ling,” Wu Lingyuan consoled himself. Wei Yuzhi, guessing his thoughts, added, “General Ling might not be able to play a significant role.” Wu Lingyuan thought about it and could not help but sigh. Song generals did not lead a single army for long, so the strength of an army was not necessarily linked to the strength of its commander. Everyone needed time to meld, let alone lead troops in battle. Making so many people work like one’s own limbs was no easy feat. “Is Yelu Huangwu really dead?” Mo Sigui suddenly interjected. “Really dead,” Wei Yuzhi replied. Wu Lingyuan said, “You’ve asked me countless times these past two days. What happened?” The person Lou Mingyue risked her life to kill but could not was dead just like that. Mo Sigui truly found it hard to believe, but he felt mostly joy. With this woman dead, Lou Mingyue was finally free. “Life is full of unexpected turns,” he sighed, rising to his feet. “I will go pack!” He hummed a little tune, happily wandering around the room, quickly picking out a package, and even patting Xiao Yue’s head in his haste. Wu Lingyuan was unaware of what had happened between them. He was quite surprised to see this. In Wu Lingyuan’s memory, Mo Sigui was always unrestrained yet still had his manners, but now he seemed somewhat carried away. “Yuzhi, I’ve prepared over a dozen jars of medicine and put them on the shelf. You two chat. I am off.” Mo Sigui, along with Xiao Yue and Da Jiu, left like a gust of wind. “Over a dozen jars.” Wei Yuzhi’s lips curled slightly. It seemed he planned to travel around after finding Lou Mingyue. “She was defeated so easily by Yelu Quancang.” Wei Yuzhi felt a pang of regret thinking of Yelu Huangwu; she clearly seemed capable of fighting for ten or twenty years. He could not help but wonder what it would be like if he were to fight Yelu Quancang. What exactly happened? “Yelu Huangwu actually lost just like that.” An Jiu, in the city camp, could not believe the news. “Since ancient times, whenever there’s a power struggle or usurpation, someone has to die. What’s so strange about that?” Chu Dingjiang was not interested in that. He was more concerned about Yelu Quancang’s methods; he absolutely could not let his guard down. An Jiu was still recovering and had been ordered by Chu Dingjiang to stay in bed and not run around. Right now, she was sitting with her legs crossed, accepting his feeding. “But she seems very powerful.” “Those who show off their strength often do not last long.” “Hmm, that makes sense. There’s a saying that a barking dog does not bite.” An Jiu had heard this from someone in the camp a while ago and immediately put it to use. Usually, using it was not wrong, but she insisted on listing someone, “Like you and Wei Yuzhi.” Seeing his aura change, An Jiu quickly said, “Xue Sha is here.” Chu Dingjiang was considerate of her and never criticized her in front of her subordinates. After a while, Xue Sha indeed came from outside the door. “Master, I saw the Divine Physician leading two tigers out of the city.” An Jiu was not surprised at all. “I know.” “If Master has no other instructions, I will take my leave.” “Hmm.” “He’s getting quite the air of a superior,” Chu Dingjiang smiled. An Jiu could not help but purse her lips. “Ever since Xue Sha saw you again, he’s been obsessed with following you. I do not know how you managed to bewitch him so completely.” “Nonsense.” How could Chu Dingjiang, a grown man, bewitch another grown man so completely? How could she even say that? An Jiu’s thoughts drifted back, and she sighed, “Now Mo Sigui and Lou Mingyue can finally be together. I was not doing well before either, but somehow, seeing them still made me feel exhausted.” Chu Dingjiang peeled a large piece of apple and stuffed it into her mouth. “Look how worried you are. You should think about yourself.” “Myself? I think I am doing great now.” An Jiu took the apple, freeing her mouth to speak. “I can be a good person, and I’ve fulfilled my wish of herding a flock of sheep.” She was referring to the Self-Defense Forces. Chu Dingjiang laughed. “You cannot herd them like sheep; you have to hone them like sharp weapons. Otherwise, are you waiting for the Liao cavalry to come hunting?” “Hmph, my sheep! Who dares to catch them?” An Jiu retorted. Chu Dingjiang looked at her smug expression, amused, and reached out to shove the whole peeled apple into her mouth. An Jiu reached out to hit him. Her skin was as tender as a baby’s; a little pressure could leave a mark. Chu Dingjiang dared not lay a hand on her, letting her hit him, saying, “Do not hit too hard, do not hit too hard, what if you hurt your hand? How about I hit myself a few times?” An Jiu laughed heartily. After a while of playful banter, An Jiu grew tired and fell asleep. Chu Dingjiang looked at her increasingly delicate and beautiful face, still bearing the lingering smile, and his heart softened considerably. Darkness fell. Chu Dingjiang got up and went to the window, gazing intently at the stars. Nearly an hour later, he instructed a few trusted men to guard the courtyard before sneaking into the city alone. Within a short while, he returned with two unconscious people, dumping them in an empty house. He took a bath, changed his clothes, and then leisurely went to see the two people he had brought. Xue Sha held a lantern in front. Upon entering the house, he saw two middle-aged women, and upon closer inspection, one of them was none other than Old Madam Mei! Xue Sha put down the lantern. Unable to resist, he asked, “My Lord, did Master know you tied up Old Madam Mei?” He knew An Jiu and Old Madam Mei did not get along. But despite their strained relationship, An Jiu was quite peculiar; for example, she herself could be very critical of Mo Sigui, but she would never allow anyone else to say a bad word about him. “Which eye of yours saw me tie her up?” Chu Dingjiang asked slowly. The Old Madam was not actually tied up. But this kind of “tying up” was different! However, Chu Dingjiang’s tone reminded him that this man was no pushover. Xue Sha simply lowered his head, pretending he did not exist and had not seen anything. “Go brew a pot of tea.” Xue Sha obeyed and went out. A moment later, he brought back the tea, put it down, and was about to quietly leave when he heard Chu Dingjiang say, “Take her to the west room and keep her under guard. You stay while she’s here.” “Yes.” Xue Sha resignedly picked up Ling-Xi and went out. This cluster of houses was built by Chu Dingjiang within a few months. Due to the rush, only the main house was properly decorated; the side rooms, though empty, were neat and clean. This room was quite large but contained only a few round-backed chairs and two tall tables. Old Madam Mei let out a soft groan, regaining consciousness. A dull ache in the back of her neck reminded her of what had happened before she fainted, so she pretended to be asleep, using her mental power to sense if anyone was around. “Open your eyes if you are awake,” Chu Dingjiang exposed her. Old Madam Mei was surprised to find someone there and opened her eyes, looking towards the source of the voice. The room was unlit, but the bright moonlight outside allowed her to make out the interior. A tall man sat in one of the round-backed chairs opposite her, dressed in black wide-sleeved robes with a white undergarment collar peeking out. He had a neatly trimmed beard, and his hair was half down, seemingly freshly washed. He poured two cups of tea and personally placed one on the tall table beside her. Standing so close, Old Madam Mei realized he was taller than she had imagined. “Chu Dingjiang,” Old Madam Mei had been keeping a close eye on his movements and recognized him. “Why did you bring me here?” Chu Dingjiang picked up his tea and took a sip. “Old Madam, please do not be so harsh. I invited you here because I have a few questions to ask you.” Even though knocking her unconscious and bringing her here had already offended her, Chu Dingjiang still intended to be polite first. “If you want to ask questions, why resort to such petty tactics?” Old Madam Mei asked with a smile. Her face appeared gentle, but her gaze was unapproachable. “Considering what you’ve done, I think my actions have been more than polite,” Chu Dingjiang said. Old Madam Mei then realized that her mission to deliver the message had been exposed. “Your master is very busy right now and probably will not have time for you for the next few days. So, Old Madam, please think carefully about your situation before answering my question,” Chu Dingjiang said. “What is his purpose in ordering you to come and keep an eye on Ah Jiu and me?” “You actually know that I work for His Majesty; that is quite remarkable.” Old Madam Mei had to reassess Chu Dingjiang. “You flatter me,” Chu Dingjiang said, not in a hurry to urge her; he had plenty of patience. “I can tell you the truth; I do not know.” Young Lady Mei straightened her clothes, sitting upright as usual, without any unease. “I am just following orders; how could I have the opportunity to hear my master’s explanation?” Chu Dingjiang nodded, not doubting her explanation. “Then please tell me about Yelu Quancang and Xiao Che, Old Madam.” “Why should I tell you this?” Old Madam Mei asked with a half-smile. “I do not want to say anything too forceful right now, but if I had any reservations, you would not be sitting here.” Saying it was not forceful was, in reality, saying it was as forceful as it could possibly be. Old Madam Mei’s tongue tasted bitter; she picked up her tea and took a sip. She was not afraid of Chu Dingjiang’s threats; she just felt that her whole life had been filled with bitterness, and it just surfaced unintentionally.

chapters.title: Daily Life
chapters.content: Old Madam Mei’s code name in the Konghe Army was Hong You, and her original name was long forgotten. She was an assassin trained by the Konghe Academy, without a family backing her, like a drifting duckweed, going with the flow. Her martial arts skills were ordinary, but she survived among many assassins through cunning. The path of an assassin was cold and bloody; cunning alone was far from enough. She remembered that her last trial before leaving the Konghe Academy was not a mission but a one-on-one duel, like when she first entered. At that time, strength was everything; cunning was futile. She knew very well that if that day truly came, she would become an insignificant sacrifice in this trial. She was unwilling to accept this, so before going on stage, she used various ruthless schemes to kill the three experts in her group. Even being executed for violating the rules was better than having her throat easily slit on the field! Unexpectedly, after the incident, instead of being punished, she was praised in front of everyone. At that time, she understood a crucial truth: this path had no rules, only the survivors and the dead. It was precisely because of this incident that her superiors noticed her and decided to send her into the Konghe Army family as an inside agent. “I met Yelu Quancang in Mei Mansion. You might not believe it, but after serving him for so many years, I know absolutely nothing about him. As for that Grand Preceptor, I know even less,” said Old Madam Mei. Chu Dingjiang asked, “Why did you serve him?” “Why…” Old Madam Mei was momentarily lost in thought, her eyes lowered as she murmured, “If not for him, for whom?” She was like a parasitic vine, needing to cling to something to stand. There were many such people in the Konghe Army, including An Jiu, accustomed to receiving orders, accustomed to being commanded, and yearning for freedom. When they finally gained freedom, they felt lost. Old Madam Mei grew up in that environment; having left behind familiar rules, she could no longer live like an ordinary person. “I know the current ruler is wise, but there was no turning back. One step down, and we sink deeper and deeper.” Although she always spoke of melancholy, relying on others for survival, Chu Dingjiang did not mistake her for a weak woman; it was merely a habit. “You contacted him. Did you use any code?” Old Madam Mei remained silent. Chu Dingjiang knew that whether working for Yelu Quancang was submission or voluntary surrender, once she acknowledged a master, she would have a certain degree of loyalty. Therefore, she must be hiding something. Chu Dingjiang guessed that Old Madam Mei was a single agent in Yelu Quancang’s hands and would not know much. Tonight, he only wanted to confirm if she was hiding anything, not to pry into her openly. “Old Madam, take your time thinking. Until you’ve decided, please stay in this room.” Chu Dingjiang got up and left. Old Madam Mei’s smile slowly faded, and the cup in her hand shattered with a crash. Chu Dingjiang had not gone far. Hearing the sound of breaking porcelain, he smiled faintly and quickened his pace towards the place where Ling-Xi was imprisoned. Xue Sha went to greet him. “The person inside is awake.” Chu Dingjiang nodded. “Take a few men and watch over Old Madam Mei. No matter what excuse she gives, do not let her out, not even to the outhouse.” Xue Sha thought to himself, “Killing is just a matter of beheading; this is too despicable!” Despite his thoughts, he immediately did as he was told. The room was pitch black, and Chu Dingjiang could move freely in the darkness without even looking. He found a stool and sat down not far from Ling-Xi. “You should understand why I asked you to come here.” “Tying us up is just that; do not make it sound so nice.” “I just went to see the Old Madam.” “Ha, do not tell me she told me everything.” Ling-Xi knew very well that this man had separated them for this very purpose! However, Chu Dingjiang’s answer surprised her somewhat. “No, she would not say anything, only lamented her past, saying her life had been very bitter.” “Bitter?” Ling-Xi chuckled softly, offering no comment. “Actually, I do not intend to force her to tell the truth, because I believe you will.” Chu Dingjiang sensed her desire to deny it and continued, “You do not need to argue. She’s been the Old Madam of the Mei family for so many years, enjoying wealth and luxury. You are even more skilled in martial arts than she is, yet you are just a maid. Do you not feel resentful?” Ling-Xi was silent for a moment, then spoke again, noticeably less forcefully than before. “I am used to it… Habits are truly terrifying. Sometimes I really forget that I am actually the same person as her, not just a servant serving her.” Ling-Xi was assigned to Old Madam Mei’s side to assist her. If the Old Madam were not there, she would have no reason to exist. Whether it was the Konghe Army or Yelu Quancang, what mattered was only the position of Old Madam Mei, and she, Ling-Xi, had always been an appendage. “I am not like an Emperor, who can give you countless wealth and status; I can only give you the opportunity to choose your own life.” Chu Dingjiang remembered that when Mei Mansion was attacked, Old Madam Mei was seriously injured, and Ling-Xi risked everything to save her. He absolutely did not believe it was out of deep affection between master and servant; it was simply because Ling-Xi knew that once Old Madam Mei was gone, she would lose everything. If she did not care about money and status and only wanted freedom, she certainly would not have done this. “Ten thousand taels of gold, a mountain villa, and you will leave. There will be no more Ling-Xi in this world, only you.” Ling-Xi’s heart skipped a beat at Chu Dingjiang’s offer. After a moment, she asked, “How can I trust you?” “Tell me the truth, and I will kill Old Madam Mei, find someone to take your place, and give you the money, the land deed, and a household registration in Hexi County. With these things, you can go wherever you want. That is my plan. Whether you are willing to take the gamble is up to you. I do not have the time or energy to gain the trust of a suspicious person.” “And if I do not tell you?” “You die.” In the darkness, Chu Dingjiang sat motionless, his tall figure like a tombstone. Yelu Quancang promised much more than Chu Dingjiang, but this meant they would have to pay a much higher price. Ling-Xi knew without a doubt that even if things succeeded, what she gained would be less than what Old Madam Mei received, perhaps even less… “I need to think about it.” “I will wait for your good news.” Chu Dingjiang took out a stack of banknotes from his pocket and placed them on the high table beside him. “Here is fifty thousand taels of gold.” Chu Dingjiang walked to the door and stopped. “Do not even think about running away. There are two Transcendent Realm experts here.” Ling-Xi did not answer. She reached for the banknotes worth fifty thousand taels of gold. The Mei family was designated imperial merchants, possessing immense wealth. Old Madam Mei had accumulated a considerable amount of private savings over the years since marrying into the family. However, no matter how wealthy the Mei family was, Ling-Xi, as a servant, had no chance of touching it. The price Chu Dingjiang offered was very tempting to her, and he said he would kill Old Madam Mei, so what about those private savings…? Chu Dingjiang returned to his bedroom. An Jiu was already awake, sitting at the table, eating the leftovers from lunch. “Why can you not wait a moment longer to eat, instead of these leftovers?” Chu Dingjiang touched the plate. “It’s still cold!” “I will eat a few bites first, then wait for you to come back.” “What do you want to eat tonight?” “It’s late, so just make something simple.” Chu Dingjiang’s daily meals consisted of two cold dishes, three stir-fried dishes, one stew, and a soup, and he rarely repeated the same dishes, unless it was something An Jiu particularly liked. “I will make you a bowl of noodles with two poached eggs and some stir-fried beef.” “Mmm, alright, alright.” An Jiu nodded contentedly. Chu Dingjiang flicked her head with his finger. “To think that I, a dignified young master, have fallen so low, even though I’ve willingly degenerated, I never dreamed I’d stooped to this level,” Chu Dingjiang said, turning and heading towards the kitchen. An Jiu thought for a moment, put down her chopsticks, and followed him out. “Why did you follow me?” Chu Dingjiang turned to look at her. An Jiu grasped his hand. “I am just curious. What were you doing just now?” “Guess?” Chu Dingjiang said. An Jiu possessed powerful mental strength; she knew exactly how many people in Hexi County knew martial arts. How could she not know that two martial arts masters had suddenly appeared in this courtyard? “I do not know,” An Jiu honestly replied. Chu Dingjiang said helplessly, “You are smart; it would not be hard for you to guess. It is just that you do not usually like to use your brain.” Faced with this accusation, An Jiu retorted, “In your eyes, only someone like Wei Yuzhi is considered to use his brain.” “I captured Old Madam Mei.” Chu Dingjiang had not wanted her to worry about these things, but since she asked now, he would not deliberately hide it. An Jiu asked curiously, “Were you not afraid of alerting them?” “We should be able to keep it a secret for a while longer,” Chu Dingjiang told her. “This time, it was actually Yelu Jinglie and Yelu Huangwu who plotted a rebellion together. However, news of Yelu Huangwu’s death has already spread, but we have not been able to find out whether Yelu Jinglie is alive or dead. We only hear that he was executed, but someone clearly saw him captured alive. So I’ve been thinking about the reason these past few days.” An Jiu had seen Yelu Jinglie before; he looked a lot like Gu Jinghong, so she was particularly concerned. “You’ve figured it out?” “I suspect Yelu Jinglie is also a medicine person.” An Jiu suddenly stopped. “He is also one? Are you sure?” “I’m just guessing. First, Yelu Huangwu is also a direct descendant of the Yelu royal family. Judging from her age, she shouldn’t have many days left to live. She’s not someone who’s obsessed with power and doesn’t care about the big picture, yet she still rebelled. Why? Second, Yelu Huangwu has countless ways to scheme against Yelu Jinglie. She didn’t necessarily have to send Ning Yanli to help Yelu Jinglie. The fact that she sent a mysterious and unpredictable physician to get close to Yelu Jinglie suggests that she probably has other motives.” “The answer is simple: Yelu Huangwu found a way to prolong life, and this method is related to Yelu Jinglie.” An Jiu pursed her lips, recalling Jinghong’s various encounters, and then Yelu Jinglie’s strikingly similar face, even their shared past… “If I had known last time that Gu Jinghong was determined to die, I think I would have stopped him.” An Jiu gripped Chu Dingjiang’s hand tightly. “If I remember correctly, Yelu Jinglie is his uncle, right?” Chu Dingjiang nodded. “I wanted to save him.” An Jiu knew it would be difficult, but she simply said it aloud. “Ah Jiu, his decision to leave his heart’s blood for you might not be entirely benevolent.” Chu Dingjiang had to tell her the harsh truth. “He hates the direct line, but he only wanted to give them a sliver of hope, which they could not obtain.” Obtaining the heart’s blood did not necessarily require a Divine Physician. Gu Jinghong sought out Mo Sigui because of his exceptional medical skills, anticipating that Mo Sigui would not give the heart’s blood directly to An Jiu but would instead refine it into a pill suitable for her, thus destroying more than 60% of the heart’s blood’s effectiveness. “Obtaining his heart’s blood will expose you to the pursuit of the Yelu direct line. He did not consider your life at all.” “But I did benefit from it,” An Jiu said. Chu Dingjiang shook his head, saying nothing more, simply releasing her hand and walking forward alone. Whether it was because she had used Gu Jinghong’s heart’s blood or because of their past familiarity, An Jiu admitted that she felt he was more than just a benefactor. She herself did not know why her heart would tighten whenever she thought of him. Perhaps she considered him a friend? An Jiu was not in the mood to think about that right now because Uncle Chu seemed unhappy! She went to the kitchen, where Chu Dingjiang was cutting beef. Even oxen were scarce for plowing in Hexi County, so who would be slaughtering cattle to sell meat? An Jiu had no idea where he got the fresh meat from. He was tall, and the chopping board looked low in front of him, forcing him to bend over to cut the vegetables. In the flickering lamplight, he looked serious, his eyes downcast. An Jiu leaned closer. “Are you angry?” “Do you think I am that petty?” Chu Dingjiang asked, chopping vegetables rapidly. “Then why did you just leave without a word?” “You usually do not think about unrealistic things when you are full, so I thought to hurry up and cook!” Chu Dingjiang neatly arranged the chopped beef, scallions, and ginger on a clean plate, then poured flour into a bowl, washed his hands, and began kneading the dough. “I was worried you might send me to rescue someone when you are in the mood. You’d do anything for me, but to rescue the uncle of an old rival, I feel guilty.” “Am I that desperate? You are much more important than he is. How could I abandon you for him?” An Jiu finished speaking, then remembered a phrase he had just used and asked blankly, “Old rival?” “In my opinion,” Chu Dingjiang said. Actually, Chu Dingjiang really wanted to ask what she would do if it were him, not Gu Jinghong’s uncle, who was trapped, but considering that the man was already dead, asking such a question was pointless, so he gave up. “Gu Jinghong did me a favor by chance, so it is not unreasonable for us to repay it. However, we do not know what Yelu Quancang’s purpose is in investigating our whereabouts. The Liao capital is now a den of dragons and tigers for us. Rescuing someone would not be a simple matter; it is not worth risking our lives.” “Understood.” Chu Dingjiang acted quickly, having prepared everything in the time it took to speak. He lit the stove, had An Jiu tend the fire, and cooked the noodles first, and then, with a roaring fire, a plate of stir-fried beef was ready in no time. After bringing the food back to the house, An Jiu forgot about what had just happened and began to eat with gusto. Seeing her enjoying her meal, Chu Dingjiang also ate a bowl of noodles. Just as he put down his chopsticks, someone outside reported, “My Lord, Ling-Xi wants to see you.” “She’s certainly impatient,” Chu Dingjiang said to An Jiu. “You play for a while; I will come back after I’ve finished my business and then boil water for you to bathe.” “No washing.” Chu Dingjiang laughed, “Are you going to keep them covered up to grow fungi?” Chu Dingjiang called mushrooms fungi.

chapters.title: Eternal Night
chapters.content: Chu Dingjiang was far more particular than An Jiu. When he could afford it, he would bathe every day, which An Jiu found too much trouble. She aimlessly wandered around the room, bored, when suddenly a very important thought occurred to her—could any physician use their heart’s blood to cure illness? If only those with exceptional medical skills could do it, would Mo Sigui not be in grave danger? Thinking this, she put on her cloak and went to chase after Chu Dingjiang. Over there, Chu Dingjiang had already sat down. The room was lit, and Ling-Xi said, “I’ve thought it over. I will take a gamble.” She had spent half her life being cautious and prudent; what had she gained in the end? She might as well take a gamble. If she lost, she would simply die; if she won, she would be free and wealthy forever. “You can rest assured cooperating with me, Chu,” Chu Dingjiang said. Ling-Xi took a deep breath and looked at him, saying, “We know very little, but one thing I can tell you definitively is that the person looking for you is not Yelu Quancang, but Xiao Che.” “Xiao Che?” This was strange. Chu Dingjiang had never seen this person before. A thousand possibilities flashed through his mind. “Is he looking for me, or Ah Jiu?” Ling-Xi’s eyes flickered slightly, and she lowered her head, gently rubbing her fingers. Chu Dingjiang took out a stack of paper money and placed it on the table. Ling-Xi looked up, smiled, reached out and took the item, pointed at it, and tucked it into her sleeve. “Our task from above is simply to keep an eye on you and report your movements carefully. However, I suspect Xiao Che is mostly looking for Fourteenth Young Lady, because we once received information requiring us to focus on investigating her strength. I cannot give you a precise answer to this question, but since I’ve been paid, I cannot remain silent. Yelu Quancang is meticulous. Hong You and I first served the Song Dynasty, then joined him. He’s been neglecting us for a long time, practically discarding us, and then suddenly assigned us to this task. Is that not strange? He must have sent others to monitor us, but I do not know who.” “A clever feint.” An Jiu had been recruiting people recently, making it easy for someone to infiltrate. Yelu Quancang sent two blatantly obvious spies to distract them, making it easier for the real spies to transmit genuine information. “Do you know how they contact each other?” Chu Dingjiang placed the mansion deed in front of her. Ling-Xi looked at the land deed but did not take it. “I do not know.” “You can leave,” Chu Dingjiang said. Ling-Xi straightened her back warily, and only after realizing he truly had no intention of making a move did she slowly rise. “Is 100,000 taels of gold worth it for this little bit of information?” “Whether it is worth it or not is up to me,” Chu Dingjiang said calmly. Ling-Xi did not ask any more questions. She quickly slipped out. An Jiu, who had been waiting outside for a long time, looked dazed but did not stop her. Hearing An Jiu’s footsteps, Chu Dingjiang turned around and said, “Why are you here?” “I have a bad feeling.” An Jiu’s pale face was bloodless, and her eyes held a fear Chu Dingjiang had never seen in her before. “He’s here.” “He?” An Jiu had spent most of the years with Chu Dingjiang, and he was certain she had not provoked Xiao Che, so he had a bold guess in his mind: Xiao Che was like them. An Jiu suddenly felt very cold. No matter how tightly she pulled her cloak, it was no use. Chu Dingjiang hugged her. “Chu Dingjiang, I am really scared,” An Jiu buried her face in his chest, her voice muffled. “I am very content now. That is why I am afraid of going back to the past.” With a goal, with hope, with Chu Dingjiang… An Jiu felt life could not be better. “He should have been here long ago. Why did he not show up sooner? Of all times…” An Jiu hugged Chu Dingjiang tightly, telling him about him. “He’s our commander. He used to be a top assassin, a born criminal with super-high intelligence, capable of anything. Later, he injured his leg and stopped taking on missions, founding an organization and training many younger assassins. Seven of the world’s top ten assassins were personally trained by him. I am one of them.” In An Jiu’s memory, he never lost his temper, spoke gently, taught her how to hold a gun, and taught her how to vent the rage in her blood through killing. In those dull and lonely days, she had been attached to him, but now, looking back, his gentleness seemed terrifying. “Actually, he’s been here for a while, has he not?” The blue-fire crossbow was an extraordinary artifact, completely out of place in this world. Xiao Che brought it here, and An Jiu had long harbored suspicions, but had not thought much of it or sought confirmation. “Fortunately, he arrived late, giving me enough time to be with you,” Chu Dingjiang said. If Xiao Che had appeared two years earlier, An Jiu might have followed the same old path. “I am not afraid,” Chu Dingjiang grasped her hand. “Whether it is an abyss or being reduced to ashes, I will be there with you.” Looking at their tightly clasped hands and listening to his heroic words, An Jiu gradually calmed down. “Xue Sha,” Chu Dingjiang said. “My Lord!” “Kill Old Madam Mei.” “Yes!” Xue Sha accepted the order and left, but returned swiftly in the blink of an eye. “My Lord, Old Madam Mei has taken poison.” An Jiu was somewhat surprised. “How could she take poison?” Old Madam Mei was clearly not a simple person; she was also resilient and would never commit suicide unless absolutely necessary. Chu Dingjiang walked to the room where Old Madam Mei was imprisoned. The lamps were already lit, teacups were shattered on the floor, and her once neatly dressed, well-preserved face was now deathly pale. She slowly opened her eyes, her pupils gleaming brightly. “That wretched servant, she actually thought that by letting her go, she would be free forever…Ha…Hahaha!” Blood gushed from her mouth, staining her clothes red. Old Madam Mei’s face was deathly pale with a bluish-gray tinge. She laughed, tears streaming down her face. “She did not even consider why I did not choose that path! Today, the truly free one is me!” Not a drifting duckweed, not someone else’s dog; only death could bring liberation. Ling-Xi would understand sooner or later. Watching Old Madam Mei breathe her last, Chu Dingjiang said, “Bury her.” She was a second wife and a traitor; the Mei family would not accept her in the ancestral cemetery. Xue Sha ordered someone to fetch a mat, wrap the body in it, and have it carried out to find a place to bury her. “Every person in a position of power has their own way of controlling such people. Old Madam Mei and Ling-Xi were one entity. Since Ling-Xi betrayed them, she will not have a good end either,” Chu Dingjiang explained to her, revealing the reason for Old Madam Mei’s suicide. An Jiu said, “Yelu Quancang’s method of controlling people should not be poison.” If both of them were poisoned, there’s no reason why one would know and the other wouldn’t. No one poisoned her initially, yet she still sank deeper into the swamp. “Right!” An Jiu remembered why she had chased after him. “Is it difficult to treat illnesses with heart’s blood? Is it only someone like Mo Sigui who can do it?” “It’s said that obtaining heart’s blood is very difficult.” Chu Dingjiang understood her worries. “Do not make a fuss about this for now; let’s observe quietly.
