You’ve just been reforged and cannot run around recklessly. Even if Yelu Quancang wants to capture Mo Sigui, he’s not in immediate danger.” An Jiu nodded. The night was quiet and still. The full moon hung high. Mo Sigui, with two tigers in tow, rushed towards Lou Mingyue with great excitement. Yelu Huangwu was dead. This was the best news he’s heard in his life. Lou Mingyue should no longer be so stubborn and would go back with him to live a peaceful and quiet life. “A perfect day for a family reunion,” Mo Sigui said, glancing at the bright moon in the sky, then lowering his head and asking with a smile, “Da Jiu, how many children do you think I want in the future?” Da Jiu stared wide-eyed, turning his head blankly. “I definitely want a daughter. I will teach her from a young age to be gentle and kind, not like her mother. Tsk, what do you think I should say to her when I see her?” Mo Sigui sat on Xiao Yue’s tiger back, his dark hair flying in the wind, his peach blossom eyes shimmering with a light crimson that seemed to dye the quiet night a pale pink. He had not shown such elegance in a long time. What should he say in his first words to her to make her more touched? “Mingyue, I was wrong before. I did not protect you properly. Give me a chance to make it up to you with my whole life.” Mo Sigui smiled, tapping his palm with his folding fan. “I am really talented; any woman would be moved to tears. No, our Mingyue is not an ordinary woman.” He frowned again. After agonizing over this the whole way, Xiao Yue and Da Jiu stopped. Mo Sigui looked up and saw the plaque above—it was the inn where he had stayed when he helped Lou Mingyue with her illness! Mo Sigui was certain that Lou Mingyue still cared about him, and his heart leaped with joy. Standing at the door, he carefully straightened his clothes and hair, then turned Da Jiu’s tiger-like face to look at himself through its big eyes. “A dashing figure.” Whether he truly saw himself clearly or not, he made a satisfied judgment and turned to step onto the stairs. Just as he approached the main entrance, Mo Sigui faintly sensed a murderous aura. He paused slightly, then quietly retreated to a secluded corner. He took out paper and brush from his medicine box, quickly wrote a letter, sealed it in a bamboo tube, tied it around Da Jiu’s neck, and patted its neck. Da Jiu turned and ran back. Mo Sigui heard a loud bang from upstairs, followed by a muffled groan from Xiao Yue behind him. His heart skipped a beat. He tossed a pill to Xiao Yue, leaped over the courtyard wall, and swiftly rushed towards the room from which the sound had come. “Young Lady, do not be foolish, we mean no harm!” Mo Sigui did not hesitate and immediately kicked open the door. “Mingyue!” A misty haze filled the room. Lou Mingyue heard the voice and slowly turned around. The room was filled with smoke, and a dozen black-clad men had her trapped. She stood by the window, and seeing Mo Sigui rush in, she abruptly pushed open the window to let the wind disperse the mist. Moonlight streamed in from behind, casting a silvery glow around her and outlining her beautiful figure. Her expression was indistinct in the darkness. “Go!” She only managed a hoarse cry before a thick black mist billowed from her body, filling the room with the stench of burning flesh. Spring Breeze Know Not Words! It was the bone-corroding poison he had concocted! Mo Sigui’s eyes widened in horror. His trembling hands opened the medicine chest, scattering bottles and jars across the floor. He knelt and grabbed the antidote for Spring Breeze Know Not Words. Lou Mingyue looked down at him, tears streaming down her face. Mo Sigui looked up again, only to see her once beautiful face now fragmented, turning into withered butterflies swept away by the night wind. Tears fell to the ground, but she was gone. It all happened in an instant. The smoke drifted out the door, and the room quickly returned to silence, leaving only piles of ashes and bones. Mo Sigui stared blankly around, his gaze finally settling on the bright moon outside the window. What happened? Just now…he thought he saw the moon. His clothes were soaked in the antidote, and he was immune to all poisons…but Lou Mingyue had just used her last strength to push open the window, clearly afraid that he would be exposed to a large amount of poisonous mist and would not have time to take the antidote. Mo Sigui’s face was blank and expressionless. Xiao Yue whimpered softly, reaching forward to nudge the pile of wreckage by the window, but was afraid of accidentally breaking it. Standing there for a long time, Mo Sigui slowly began to react. A sharp pain suddenly overwhelmed him, so intense that he could not utter a sound. He had prepared so many words, but he had not had a chance to say them. They had been separated for so long, he had not even had a chance to look at her properly, had not even had a chance to say sorry, and she had vanished from his sight forever. In the blink of an eye, without warning. She died from the poison he himself had concocted?! Thud! Mo Sigui felt a sweet taste in his throat and coughed up a mouthful of blood. The blood was bright red, almost dripping, but his face was deathly pale, making him look more than ten years older in an instant. “Ha, ha ha ha! Ha ha ha!” Overwhelmed with grief, not a single tear could flow; instead, he wanted to laugh—to laugh at this cruel fate! After laughing, his body trembled as he pointed at the pile of remains, his voice hoarse, “I, Mo Sigui, can bring the dead back to life, and I can also grind people to ashes. But who can tell me how to resurrect someone whose bones have been ground to ashes?” Mo Sigui had never felt such profound hatred. It was not just hatred for those who had driven Lou Mingyue to her death, but also hatred for Lou Mingyue herself. Why could she be so resolute, leaving no room for maneuver, and so cruel, using the poison he had personally concocted? A wave of anger pressed down on his heart like a mountain, almost suffocating him. … “Mo Sigui!” An Jiu suddenly sat up. Chu Dingjiang woke with a start, got up, and patted her. “Had a nightmare?” “I dreamt that Mo Sigui jumped off a cliff,” An Jiu said, still shaken. “I saw him standing on the edge of the cliff and screamed for him. He turned around, smiled at me, and said, ‘Ah Jiu, I want to go down and see,’ and then he jumped!” “You are overthinking things before bed.” “No!” An Jiu grabbed his arm, anxiously saying, “You do not know; I used to only dream about the past. But ever since I used Wei Yuzhi’s blood, I’ve started having strange dreams, and they all come true.” “It does not necessarily mean he jumped off a cliff. Maybe it is a premonition that he will be in danger,” Chu Dingjiang comforted her. “I will take you to see him tomorrow.” An Jiu lay back down, tossing and turning, unable to fall asleep again. Chu Dingjiang could not sleep either, so he asked her, “When you dreamt of Xiao Che, what did you dream about?” “The dream was chaotic; some scenes were from before, and some were things I’d never seen before. But what I remember most clearly is a sentence he once said to me.” “What did he say?” “You are the most perfect weapon I’ve ever seen. With you, I can destroy everything, so I will never let you out of my grasp.” Chu Dingjiang felt that the “perfect weapon” this person spoke of was not a real weapon. After all, no matter how powerful a person was, they could not destroy everything. And judging from An Jiu’s simple description, this person was a genius, and geniuses were often arrogant; he would not really entrust such a thing to someone else. Most likely, this person was dependent on An Jiu. “What are you thinking about?” An Jiu asked. Chu Dingjiang joked, “I was wondering if you’ve become a prophet.” An Jiu, however, was very serious. “I will have to ask Wei Yuzhi.” Chu Dingjiang smiled and hugged her. “Sleep well. I will only feel at ease letting you go out once you’ve recovered.”

chapters.title: Farewell at Second Meeting
chapters.content: The next day at noon, Da Jiu returned with Mo Sigui’s letter. The letter contained only a few words, requesting a favor from Chu Dingjiang, along with an address. When he rescued An Jiu, Chu Dingjiang had also promised to go to Liao to rescue Lou Mingyue. The address on the letter was still within the Song Dynasty, but Chu Dingjiang was in a dilemma. Someone was eyeing An Jiu covetously, and he absolutely could not bear to leave her alone to fulfill his promise; besides, he was not exactly a gentleman. An Jiu knew what he was worried about, so she said, “I will go with you. Even if we stay in Hexi County, we cannot escape Xiao Che when he wants to make his move.” Chu Dingjiang knew this perfectly well, but staying here would at least allow him to make arrangements; he did not like doing things without certainty. “This place is not far from Hexi County, is it?” An Jiu murmured, clutching the note. “Give me half an hour to make arrangements,” Chu Dingjiang said, seeing her still frowning. “Yelu Quancang is ultimately asking Mo Sigui for help; he will not do anything rash. At most, he might capture Lou Mingyue to threaten him in case he disobeys. Do not rush.” ​​ Indeed, Chu Dingjiang’s guess proved correct. However, no one expected that Lou Mingyue, upon hearing that she was to be captured to threaten Mo Sigui and fearing she would implicate him, would immediately use her life-threatening technique, leaving no trace of her body. Having teetered on the brink of death so many times, she had long forgotten to leave herself a chance to survive. With Yelu Huangwu dead, her mind was at ease, her thoughts entirely focused on Mo Sigui, unwilling to let him suffer even the slightest harm. She could not have imagined that such a resolute departure would be Mo Sigui’s deepest pain. An Jiu felt she understood Lou Mingyue better than others. With her fierce temperament, if she were ambushed before reuniting with Mo Sigui, things might go badly. Therefore, she did not want to waste a single moment. Mo Sigui was An Jiu’s first friend and, so far, the only person besides Chu Dingjiang to whom she could completely trust. She truly did not want to see him continue to succumb to the allure of drugs, wasting away day by day. Chu Dingjiang fell into deep thought. He was a very vigilant man; if there was a traitor within the Self-Defense Forces sending out messages, it could not have escaped his notice. The most reasonable explanation was that the traitor might have already infiltrated but had not yet sent messages out. He did not have time to catch the traitor immediately, so he found some trusted former subordinates to take control of the entire camp and begin a round of closed, brutal training. No one was allowed to leave. After completing all this, he rushed back to the city to instruct Wu Lingyuan on some matters before quietly setting off with An Jiu. Da Jiu was left outside to guard the gate. The two rushed to the location mentioned in Mo Sigui’s letter, but found that it was too late. The inn was quiet; not a soul could be seen. Chu Dingjiang searched the inn thoroughly before finally finding a festering, barely alive coachman. Upon questioning, he learned what had happened that night. The inn itself was not large; a single drop of the “Spring Breeze Know Not Words” poison was enough to kill twenty or thirty people. It was nighttime. Everyone was asleep inside; as long as they did not venture out to their deaths, they would not be exposed to the poison. “That scholar-like man had extremely beautiful peach blossom eyes. He asked the innkeeper a few questions and then took him away. He killed everyone else.” The coachman was still shaken, his head throbbing from the pain of his festering sores. He was filled with regret. “Seeing the inn was deserted, I had a wicked thought and went to steal valuables from the guest rooms. Who would have thought I’d contract such a serious illness? It must be divine punishment.” He knelt nervously on the ground, repeatedly kowtowing despite the excruciating pain. An Jiu knew this was not divine punishment. It was simply that he had inadvertently come into contact with the lingering effects of the “Spring Breeze Know Not Words” while stealing. Chu Dingjiang inspected all the rooms and noticed piles of black ash in one of them, while the pile near the window appeared to have been carefully cleaned. “Lou Mingyue is probably gone,” he said, staring at the marks on the ground. “According to the coachman, things were probably already irreversible when Mo Sigui wrote to me. I just hope Mo Sigui did not witness her death at the hands of Spring Breeze Know Not Words. On the bright side, perhaps Mo Sigui used it to poison the pursuers and take Lou Mingyue away.” Mo Sigui taking the innkeeper away likely meant the innkeeper knew something. Given Mo Sigui’s personality, he preferred to avoid trouble. If Lou Mingyue was not dead, he could have simply escaped back to Hexi County with her and his tiger; why would he have captured the innkeeper? An Jiu looked at the cleaned-up marks on the floor by the window and the bloodstains in front of the chair, knowing that the optimistic explanation was impossible. “He must have already guessed the truth.” An Jiu rubbed her head, looking at Chu Dingjiang with a troubled expression. “What do we do?” “Mo Sigui witnessed Lou Mingyue die from ‘Spring Breeze Know Not Words’ without being able to save her. What do you think he will do?” “I do not know.” An Jiu could not understand Mo Sigui. He seemed affectionate, yet also heartless. She truly could not guess how he would choose in this situation. Just like when he had a deep relationship with Elder Qi, An Jiu thought he would seek revenge, but he acted as if nothing had happened, immersing himself in medicine every day, as if he had already forgotten Elder Qi’s tragic death. Lou Mingyue was trapped in hatred, her life hanging in the balance, and he also pretended not to know, at most, only rushing to save her life in times of crisis. What was the difference between his feelings for Lou Mingyue and his feelings for Elder Qi? However, if he remained silent, how could he explain the pool of blood in front of him? “What do we do?” An Jiu really wanted to drag Mo Sigui over and give him a good beating. He was too impulsive, never consulting anyone. “Everyone has their own destiny…” An Jiu suddenly opened her eyes wide and looked up at Chu Dingjiang, only to find him frowning as well. She held up four fingers and mouthed, “Forty. Eighth- and ninth-rank.” There were forty eighth- and ninth-rank experts! Chu Dingjiang glanced at the sky outside, walked to the desk, and wrote: “You cannot fight now. Go southeast alone and return to Hexi to find Ling Ziyue.” An Jiu could fight, but her body had not fully recovered. Using her mental power would damage her internal organs, negating the purpose of rebuilding her body. However, her exceptionally high mental power allowed her to conceal herself naturally, preventing these eighth- and ninth-ranked martial artists from detecting her. Escaping this place would not be a problem, but Chu Dingjiang’s mental power was unstable and might be discovered. Staying with her would only be a burden. An Jiu took the brush and wrote: “And you?” He wrote: “Unable to fight head-on, but able to retreat unscathed.” Being together would only burden the other. An Jiu’s current advantage was concealment, but Chu Dingjiang lacked this advantage against a ninth-rank enemy. And once their whereabouts were exposed, she would become a liability to him. An Jiu believed that with Chu Dingjiang’s strength and intelligence, he could easily escape unscathed without being a burden. Therefore, she decided to follow his advice and split up. Chu Dingjiang wrote: “No matter what happens, do not return. I promise I will return.” Chu Dingjiang took a brocade pouch from his robes and placed it in her hand, writing: “Every five li, drop one of the items in this pouch.” An Jiu did not ask any questions and nodded in agreement. With everything settled, they both jumped out of the window, one heading east and the other west. After running for several li, An Jiu realized that the pursuers were getting further and further away—they were all chasing Chu Dingjiang! Her heart leaped into her throat. Even if they could not sense her when she jumped, they should have seen her, so why was no one chasing her? Thinking this, An Jiu kept going. She still decided to trust Chu Dingjiang’s judgment. After running about five li, she opened her brocade pouch, took out a pill, and tossed it into a corner. She continued running southeast. From noon until nightfall, An Jiu did not encounter a single pursuer. She saw the city walls of Hejian Prefecture in the distance, and her heart relaxed slightly. She was almost at the Hexi garrison… “Fourteenth Young Lady?” someone called softly from behind. An Jiu felt a chill instantly creep down her spine. “An Jiu,” the person said again. An Jiu stiffened and slowly turned around. A person sat beneath a sturdy ancient pine tree, dressed in black robes. A half-silver mask covered his face, making him seem like part of the darkness, except for his white-gloved hands, which resembled butterfly wings, abrupt and eerie. “Come here,” he said, extending his hand to her, his voice gentle. An Jiu almost burst into tears, both from fear and from hatred for the hands that had destroyed everything beautiful before her. She did not run; the chilling feeling clung to her like a leech, making her acutely aware that escape was impossible. An Jiu drew her Dragon-Subduing Bow. Xiao Che chuckled, “You’ve become disobedient.” Then he chuckled again, “You were never obedient to begin with.” Xiao Che was puzzled by his own words. In his original memory, An Jiu had been both obedient and rebellious. He had not yet regained his memories, but he was certain that the girl before him was the one he was searching for. An Jiu saw Xiao Che clearly. Moonlight filtered through the pine branches, casting dappled patterns on him. The parts of his face not covered by the mask were exquisitely handsome, as if every feature had been meticulously measured by the Creator, so perfectly proportioned, without a single flaw. A white undergarment covered his long, powerful neck, the collar as neatly trimmed as if just cut. Every strand of hair was impeccably styled. It was clearly a different face, different clothes, yet An Jiu instantly saw that man again. He had been a soldier, always impeccably neat, almost to the point of being harsh. The atmosphere was tense, but Xiao Che seemed oblivious, speaking gently, “Two hundred eighth- or ninth-level experts, even if only activated by drugs, would be enough to entangle that Master Chu for two or three hours. Do you think he can escape? Look, dozens of experts are coming this way; he’s using all his subordinates to protect you.” An Jiu’s mind exploded. In that instant of distraction, a whip in Xiao Che’s hand flashed like lightning, wrapping around her wrist. An Jiu’s delicate skin immediately bled, and she simultaneously felt a tremendous surge of mental power bearing down on her. Mental power was a very subtle thing. The difference between An Jiu and Xiao Che was not vast, but she feared him and was suppressed from the very beginning. An Jiu quickly realized this. Thinking of Chu Dingjiang’s predicament, she suddenly felt a surge of malice, wanting nothing more than to tear the man before her to pieces! “You should not have appeared!” An Jiu’s mental power suddenly burst forth like a torrent breaking through a dam, surging toward Xiao Che. “Huh.” His mind reeled from the shock, the whip loosened slightly, and An Jiu broke free. “Why are you haunting me? I owe you nothing in this life or the last!” An Jiu spat out blood, drew her Dragon-Subduing Bow, and unleashed an arrow imbued with immense mental power. The accuracy was unparalleled, surpassing any of his Hunters. Xiao Che’s eyes narrowed, his interest deepening. He flicked his left wrist, revealing a powerful crossbow strapped to his arm. In an instant, he drew his trigger, and an arrow, also imbued with immense mental power, collided with the incoming arrow in mid-air. With a deafening roar, both arrows, unable to withstand the force, shattered into dust, scattering in all directions. Through the thin smoke, Xiao Che vaguely saw the woman’s beautiful face transform into another. That face was even more exquisite and beautiful than the one he saw now, with snow-white skin, a high nose bridge, slightly deep-set eyes, and brownish-yellow hair, possessing a subtle exotic charm. An Jiu noticed nearly a hundred martial artists rapidly approaching, some heading towards Xiao Che, others towards her. Before the two could launch a second attack, reinforcements from both sides had already arrived. Chu Dingjiang had indeed used all his forces to protect her…An Jiu closed her eyes slightly. When she opened them again, her gaze was as sharp as before. “Actually, I was not planning to make a move now. I happened to hear about your relationship with Mo Sigui and wondered if you would come, so I came myself,” Xiao Che said softly and smiled. “I heard Chu Dingjiang is quite shrewd and very composed. If you had not begged him, he certainly would not have come to his death, would he?” An Jiu’s mind was slightly flustered, but she quickly calmed down. Regardless of what had happened before, she had to leave alive now. Chu Dingjiang would never break his promise! He must have a way. An Jiu pursed her lips tightly and drew the Dragon-Subduing Bow again. Xiao Che sat in a wheelchair, his legs crippled. He was not actually that strong; his greatest strengths were probably his crossbow and mental power. Seeing her draw her bow, but her gaze shifting slightly, Xiao Che offered a rather “thoughtful” explanation. “Are you looking for the crossbow? Some were left over, all in the hands of my Hunters. They are currently besieging Chu Dingjiang.” Every word he spoke was an attempt to sway her mind. And in fact, he succeeded. The crossbow, the Hunters, and even those whose power had been activated by Yelu Huangwu—all of them were besieging one person. Could that person possibly survive? Now, An Jiu could only repeatedly tell herself that Chu Dingjiang was omnipotent. A strong mental power also had the advantage of making it easy to hypnotize oneself. After repeating it a few times, she firmly believed that Chu Dingjiang truly was omnipotent. Swish swish swish! An arrow, carrying two invisible arrows of mental energy, hurtled towards Xiao Che. Chu Dingjiang’s old subordinates were all experienced fighters. They had long seen that An Jiu’s battle with Xiao Che was a contest of mental energy; they were of no use in helping her. Now that they could no longer escape, their only chance was to assassinate Xiao Che while he was focused on fighting An Jiu. So, the moment An Jiu’s arrow was released, they drew their swords and charged forward. Those behind Xiao Che instantly surrounded him. The clash between the hundred-strong forces was imminent. As An Jiu’s arrow drew near, two men immediately stepped forward from behind Xiao Che to block it. Xiao Che knew these two were overestimating themselves, but remained silent. The arrow’s power was weakened after piercing them, and Xiao Che easily dispersed it with a flick of his sleeve. “An Jiu, I have no intention of making things difficult for you; I just want to talk,” Xiao Che said, frowning. An Jiu sneered, “Too late!” The moment he mentioned the large group surrounding Chu Dingjiang, she already harbored deep hatred for Xiao Che. What was there to talk about? Besides, Xiao Che’s initial intention was to control her, not simply to have a chat. “I am no longer that homeless child, and I will not blindly believe your lies!” An Jiu angrily drew her bow again, her killing intent almost bursting forth. Three arrows, each carrying overwhelming hatred and resentment. Xiao Che grabbed his bow and arrows, instantly releasing three to meet her attack, his tone excited. “You really do know who I am!” Hearing this, An Jiu understood. Xiao Che truly had no intention of killing her; he had forgotten who she was! “If you want to know, come here yourself.” An Jiu suddenly lowered her bow. Xiao Che looked at her across the fighting, remaining still. An Jiu raised an eyebrow. “Afraid?” A faint smile appeared on Xiao Che’s face. He discarded his bow and arrows and slowly approached her, leaning on the wheel of his carriage. Upon seeing this, his subordinates exclaimed, “Grand Preceptor! No!” An Jiu was also somewhat surprised, not expecting him to abandon his bow and come over so easily. Spending so much time with Chu Dingjiang had inevitably led her to view things through a scheming lens; she cautiously took a step back. Xiao Che, however, seemed completely unprepared, slowly approaching. His subordinates were almost all restrained; he had already broken free of the protective circle. The two were less than ten chi apart; a faint scent of pine emanated from him, carried on the breeze. The handsome face opposite her was extremely pale, the veins and blood vessels visible beneath the skin. A faint smile remained on his face. The moment he saw An Jiu, Xiao Che’s empty heart filled with a sense of fullness. Vague images flashed through his mind, all of them resembling a lithe, agile figure running towards him with a weapon on her back. In an instant, he felt at ease. An Jiu slowly approached him. Her fingers, hanging by her side, seemingly brushed against the dagger hidden at her thigh. She herself rarely engaged in close combat, not because she was unskilled, but because the thrill would overwhelm her. However, she knew very well that since his leg injury, he had forbidden anyone from getting close, and his physical limitations meant his strength was likely inferior to hers. “You used to be a devil.” An Jiu stopped half a zhang away from him. “You could kill anyone you wanted, take all the money you wanted, have unrestricted access to the Military Intelligence Bureau, and even take on two assassination missions against the leaders of two nations out of boredom.” Xiao Che clasped his hands together, staring intently at her, listening intently. “Who are you?” “I am merely a weapon in your hand. You enjoy watching me repeatedly escape death,” An Jiu said coldly. Behind him, the fighting raged, but Xiao Che remained calm and composed. His memories seemed to be waiting for this woman to unlock them; many things that had disappeared were resurfacing, perhaps to be gradually recovered in the future. An Jiu’s eyes flashed, and she drew her dagger, lunging at him. A knife plunged into Xiao Che’s chest, yet An Jiu heard him laugh. A night breeze suddenly rose, ruffling his robes. He suddenly opened his arms and embraced her. An Jiu, thinking she’d fallen for a trap, steeled her heart and twisted the dagger in her hand. She swirled it inside his heart, then struggled and pushed him away! The violent struggle caused her to stumble and fall to the ground. Xiao Che lost a white glove, revealing a hand covered in burns. “My dear An Jiu, you know, before, I only dared to hold you when you were unconscious.” Just as the knife pierced his body, memories surged forth like a wild beast released from its cage, wildly and fiercely. He laughed radiantly, as if the wounded one was not him at all. “But I knew I was raising a venomous snake. If this snake were awake, it might bite me. Finally, this day has come, and you truly have not disappointed me.” Their first embrace while awake, and she stabbed him. An Jiu stared at him in shock, as if meeting him for the first time. She never knew that this man would embrace her while she was injured and unconscious. “Grand Preceptor!” Finally, two assassins broke through the encirclement and approached. Yelu Quancang had given a death order: the Grand Preceptor must be protected at all costs. If Xiao Che died, none of them would survive. Seeing him stabbed in the heart, all the Liao assassins’ eyes turned bloodshot, and a fierce, death-defying resolve erupted within them. An Jiu reacted quickly, drawing her twin swords to meet the attack. She had not run yet because she was not sure if Xiao Che was alive or dead. This man had to die! He was the only one who mattered in this world! No matter what, if he had not interfered, her life would not have gone astray. Xiao Che frowned slightly, watching An Jiu’s boiling killing intent. My girl, I gave you everything; why do you hate me so much…And what did that Chu Dingjiang give you that made you protect him so fiercely? “Young Lady, you go first!” Chu Dingjiang’s former subordinates rushed over. “The lord ordered that everything be done to save your life!” An Jiu’s heart skipped a beat; she almost got entangled here! If Xiao Che were not a demon and without the help of a Divine Physician like Mo Sigui, that one strike would have been fatal. An Jiu quickly retreated under the cover of the others. After running a dozen paces, she could not help but look back. Xiao Che was also looking at her in the crowd, a slight smile on his lips, just like many times before when he waited for her to complete her mission. An Jiu’s steps faltered; she almost rushed over without thinking. “Young Lady, hurry!” someone beside her tugged at her arm. An Jiu quickly followed. She ran all the way to the Hexi camp, feeling as if she had run a lifetime. The sentry went inside to report, and An Jiu stood in front of the camp, stunned. “Ah Jiu!” Lou Xiaowu skipped over, showing her token to the guards at the gate and pulling An Jiu inside. “I heard you were attacked?” The Hexi camp was, indeed, a very safe place. Even the most skilled martial artists were only a minority; after all, they could not withstand hundreds of thousands of troops. “He’s summoning the generals to discuss the war. Why not change clothes with me?” Lou Xiaowu said. “War?” An Jiu asked, puzzled. Lou Xiaowu pulled her into a tent, leaning close and whispering, “I was just guessing. I saw that unkempt uncle looking at a map of the Sixteen Prefectures of Yan and Yun, drawing on it. He’s probably planning to take advantage of the internal strife in Liao to reclaim lost territory.” The unkempt uncle was undoubtedly Ling Ziyue. Relaxing slightly, An Jiu felt her chest heaving with blood and waves of tearing pain. She must have injured her internal organs again. Her body was temporarily much weaker after the reconstruction, but her mental strength had improved significantly. Otherwise, she would not have been able to contend with Xiao Che today. An Jiu forced herself to wipe herself down, apply medicine, change into clean clothes, and rest briefly on the soft couch. Seeing her pale face, Lou Xiaowu wisely refrained from disturbing her. An Jiu did not know how long she had slept, but suddenly thought of Chu Dingjiang in her dream and woke up with a start. “You are awake! I will go tell that old man,” Lou Xiaowu darted out like a rabbit. An Jiu woke up. Ling Ziyue had become the old man Lou Xiaowu had mentioned. If she did not know Lou Xiaowu, An Jiu would have thought she had slept for over ten years. A moment later, Ling Ziyue, dressed in military uniform, entered. “Fourteenth Young Lady.” “General Ling.” An Jiu tried to get up, but Ling Ziyue stopped her. “Young Lady, you are injured; do not stand on ceremony. Master Chu had Magistrate Wu deliver a message to me, saying that the Liao Kingdom’s Grand Preceptor has left the capital. The Northern King has been detained for treason, and all the Liao Kingdom’s ghosts have gone out on missions. Is this true?” So he had already anticipated this. An Jiu felt relieved. “It’s all true. The injuries I sustained were from my encounter with Xiao Che. I stabbed him, and his fate is unknown.” “Good!” Ling Ziyue clapped his hands in approval. “Please stay in the camp and rest, young lady. I will reclaim the Sixteen Prefectures of Yan and Yun!” An Jiu was truly uninterested in this. “If there is any news of Chu Dingjiang, please inform me first, General.” “Alright!” Ling Ziyue stood up. “I will have someone prepare food for you, Young Lady. You can rest after you eat.” Ling Ziyue was tall and imposing, and his demeanor possessed a similar composure to Chu Dingjiang, which reassured An Jiu. “Alright.” After Ling Ziyue left, Lou Xiaowu wrinkled her nose. “What? He did not even glance at us! We are hungry too!” An Jiu twitched her lips. “You have not won him over yet.” Lou Xiaowu crossed her arms and huffed, “His mind is full of the Sixteen Prefectures of Yan and Yun. He does not even give me a second glance!” It took her a while to realize what she had said, and she blushed instantly. “You…how did you know I…?” The food was served, and An Jiu sat down at the table and began to eat. “Tell me!” Lou Xiaowu had always thought she had hidden it well. An Jiu said, “Even a fool could see that.” “No way!” Lou Xiaowu’s mouth dropped open, and after a long pause, she said, “They all saw it?” An Jiu took a bite of her steamed bun. “What’s shameful about it? General Ling is a very good person.” She paused, wondering if Lou Xiaowu still did not know her second sister was dead. Thinking about everything that had happened these past two days, and with no news from Chu Dingjiang, An Jiu suddenly lost her appetite. But she still forced herself to eat a lot; only by getting better could she help. Seeing her sudden low spirits, Lou Xiaowu assumed she was just worried about Chu Dingjiang. “I heard Master Chu is very capable; he will definitely be alright.” “Mm,” An Jiu replied listlessly. After three days in the military camp, the army had not moved, but supplies had already been sent. The atmosphere was tense with preparations everywhere, and Lou Xiaowu was also busy. She led a group to build a weapons factory in the nearby mountains to provide the army with some weapons, backed by Zhu Pianxian. Zhu Pianxian was working for Chu Dingjiang; her intentions were Chu Dingjiang’s intentions. Chu Dingjiang had been staying home, tending to his flowers, birds, hawks, and tigers; it turned out he’d been doing all this behind the scenes. An Jiu watched the soldiers hurrying to and fro, her anxiety growing. The moon was bright and the stars few. An Jiu lay awake, wide awake, only feeling sleepy as dawn approached. Lying in bed, she drifted off to sleep, only to find herself amidst a hail of swords and spears. Hundreds of black-clad men were surrounding a single man, clad in black like a monument, each sword strike carrying the force of a thousand armies. However, the hundreds of black-clad men were also highly skilled; though they could not kill him immediately, they had him trapped. In the heat of the battle, An Jiu noticed several crossbowmen silently hidden in the surrounding trees, their eyes focused like those of cheetahs, as if ready to strike at any moment. She did not see why so many assassins suddenly retreated, creating an excellent opening for the ambush. A blinding blue light flashed. An Jiu broke out in a cold sweat! “Chu Dingjiang…” she murmured, clutching the blanket. “Do not lie to me.” … An Jiu patiently stayed in the Hebei camp for ten days, but finally could not bear it any longer. She was used to obeying orders, especially Chu Dingjiang’s. If it were not for that haunting dream, she would have waited a lifetime. But not now. An Jiu’s wounds had long since healed, and her rebuilt body had become strong. She clearly felt her agility had increased several times over, and her movement speed was even faster than that of those who cultivated internal energy. On the eve of the great battle, Ling Ziyue was extremely busy. An Jiu left a letter and quietly left the Hebei camp, returning to Hexi. The Self-Defense Army’s trial had ended, and the original army of over five hundred had been reduced to just over three hundred. However, these men were different in overall demeanor from before. Xue Sha, seeing An Jiu return, immediately reported, “Master, two people were discovered during the trial; we suspect they are traitors.” An Jiu pushed away Da Jiu, who was clinging to her affectionately, and asked, “What do you mean?” “Most of the people Master recruited know martial arts, but these two performed exceptionally well during the trial. They aren’t chivalrous heroes, but rather seem like assassins from the Konghe Army. However, we’ve kept records of anyone from the Konghe Army or on the bounty list.” Assassins and ordinary people, especially on their first kill, would definitely behave very differently. “What ranks are they?” “Both are fourth-rank.” “Then observe them for now. If they send messages, intercept them secretly.” “Yes!” Da Jiu’s enormous tiger head almost pushed An Jiu off the stool. An Jiu finally felt something was strange; she’d never seen it so clingy before! Thinking this, An Jiu reached out and touched its belly; it was indeed flat, indicating it had not eaten for days. Da Jiu had always had a fondness for poisonous creatures, especially those concocted by Mo Sigui. Normally, if there were no poison, it would hunt for itself in the mountains. This time, Chu Dingjiang entrusted it with guarding the gate, and it was just obediently lying here without eating or drinking. Impossible! An Jiu saw it constantly rubbing against her with the bamboo tube around its neck and knew there must be Mo Sigui’s poison here. Normally, if it had any, it would rather eat just one pill than hunt for more. The bamboo tube was too small, almost completely hidden in the folds of the tiger’s flesh; no wonder it could not reach it. An Jiu untied the bamboo tube and struggled to unscrew it. Inside, besides the pills, a scroll of paper fell out. Da Jiu trembled with excitement, burying its head in picking up the pills from the ground. An Jiu opened the note; inside was Chu Dingjiang’s handwriting! It turned out that Da Jiu generally needed to eat once every fifteen days and absolutely forbade unfamiliar people from approaching. He deliberately placed the medicine where Da Jiu could smell it but could not eat it, so that if it wanted to eat, it could only go to someone close to it. It was a tracking tiger specifically used to track An Jiu, so it would definitely go looking for her first. Moreover, he simply did not believe she would obediently stay in the Hebei camp. Chu Dingjiang’s letter said that this time he was going to help Ling Ziyue attack the Liao Kingdom, but Yelu Quancang was not someone who acted recklessly. This seemed like a good opportunity, but he feared there would be many unforeseen events. He sent her with two hundred trusted self-defense troops to guard the rear of the main army. Furthermore, there might be spies among the guards from Piaomiao Mountain Mansion. “You cannot even protect yourself, and you still have the mind to scheme about these things!” An Jiu was so angry that her internal organs ached. In the blink of an eye, she saw Da Jiu squeezing its tiger face between the bed leg and the box, desperately trying to reach the pills that had fallen inside. “You are so stupid! Can you not even reach for it with your paws?” An Jiu did not help, letting it do whatever it wanted.

chapters.title: The Grand Finale
chapters.content:
The main army had already left the Hebei camp. Knowing time was of the essence, An Jiu immediately went to gather her forces. Internally, she announced it would be a phased field training program lasting half a month. An Jiu selected mostly former members of the Konghe Army and those with clear backgrounds; the rest remained for training. Konghe Army assassins excelled at stealth attacks and were often solo, so An Jiu had previously focused on training their teamwork. Everyone knew she enjoyed putting these men through the wringer, so no one found it strange. An Jiu first sent a letter, then led over two hundred men to the Hebei camp under the cover of night. On the third day after their arrival, the Song army launched its first direct attack on the Liao Kingdom in ten years! With internal strife still raging in Liao, and the Northern King, their most skilled strategist, imprisoned, the border defenses were caught off guard, and the Song army easily captured a city. This initial victory greatly boosted the morale of the Song army. No matter how kind the superiors sounded, all the soldiers were initially apprehensive. After all, this was their first foray into the enemy’s lair, and the initial success made them believe that the Liao Kingdom was indeed preoccupied with its own problems, as General Ling had said. In reality, this was merely a deliberate tactic by Ling Ziyue. The following battles were less successful, but the Song army advanced swiftly, capturing another city the next day! The Song soldiers’ fighting spirit developed a certain ferocity. Each subsequent battle was less successful, but no one retreated. An Jiu, listening to the reports of victory after victory from the rear, grew increasingly worried. Almost a month had passed, and there was still no news from Chu Dingjiang. Thunder rumbled all night; dark clouds pressed down on the city, making it difficult to breathe. Until dawn, streaks of lightning, like silver snakes, flashed through the clouds, followed by a deafening clap of thunder that startled the heavens and earth. Hundreds of black-clad cavalry galloped across the open fields. Rain began to fall from the sky, large raindrops pattering on the grass. In the blink of an eye, the rain intensified. Those lurking in the bushes, having spotted the cavalry, quietly returned, dismounted from their horses, and galloped towards the Hebei camp. “Report—” An Jiu, who was scratching Da Jiu’s itch, immediately became serious upon hearing the urgent report. The man, dripping with rain, rushed in, knelt on one knee, and bowed, saying, “Master, indeed, a hundred-man cavalry unit is galloping this way. Every single one of them is a martial arts master.” “Go and inform the general guarding the camp,” An Jiu ordered. “Yes!” Seeing the man leave to obey, An Jiu glanced at the armor hanging on the clothes rack, took it down, and quickly put it on. The armor was heavy, but for her body, which had been tempered twice, it was almost negligible. An Jiu gathered her soldiers but still felt that these men might not make a move tonight. This cavalry unit belonged to the Piaomiao Mountain Mansion; their attack from the rear was mainly to disrupt the Song army’s morale and buy some time for the Liao army. The bigger the commotion, the better; arson would be inevitable, but the weather was not suitable for fire today. An Jiu’s biggest worry was that Piaomiao Mountain Mansion might still have some blue-fire crossbows left, even just one. Their destructive power should not be underestimated. Thinking this, An Jiu personally went to see the garrison general and also summoned Lou Xiaowu. After some discussion, they decided to set up an ambush. They might have blue-fire crossbows. Lou Xiaowu had also produced many powerful explosive weapons in recent years. Upon hearing about the ambush, she volunteered and enthusiastically led her men to “set the net” that very night. The torrential rain stopped in the latter half of the night. After completing setting up the ambush, Lou Xiaowu went to An Jiu’s tent. Patting her chest, she said, “I guarantee not even a mosquito can fly in.” An Jiu closed her eyes to rest and, upon hearing this, hummed in agreement. “Fourteenth, the way you look now reminds me of the first time I met you,” Lou Xiaowu said, sitting opposite her, hugging her knees. An Jiu opened her eyes, waiting for her to continue. Lou Xiaowu first met An Jiu during the ancient temple trial. At that time, she found An Jiu cold and aloof, which made her envious. Later, the Lou clan was destroyed, and the Mei clan suffered heavy losses. They spent more and more time together, and Lou Xiaowu could clearly sense An Jiu’s changes. These changes were mainly due to one person. “With Master Chu gone, you seem to have become as cold as before,” Lou Xiaowu said sullenly. She already had few friends, and even staying in the military camp, she was constantly disliked by Ling Ziyue. Everyone kept her at arm’s length, and now even An Jiu had become like this; she felt increasingly lonely. “I am worried about him; I am not in the mood for jokes,” An Jiu said. Lou Xiaowu knew that any words she spoke now would only be pale and powerless comfort. An Jiu’s ears twitched slightly. Seeing that Lou Xiaowu was about to speak again, she immediately raised her index finger. Several martial artists loitered outside the camp, then quietly retreated after about the time it takes to brew a cup of tea. “They are conducting reconnaissance,” An Jiu said. “Wow, so bold!” Lou Xiaowu exclaimed. An Jiu asked, “Will they not trigger the ambush?” “That is hard to say. I’ve buried plenty of detonators around here. As long as they step on the silkworm threads attached to them, they will explode.” Lou Xiaowu paused, then added, “Most of the traps are attached to the fence. As long as they do not try to sneak in, they should be fine.” As they were talking, a horn suddenly pierced the dark night. An Jiu grabbed her bow and arrows and went out of the tent. She heard soldiers running and shouting, “Liao cavalry! Liao cavalry is attacking!” More than two hundred people from Hexi County had gathered in front of An Jiu’s tent. The ground beneath their feet trembled, indicating a large number of them! This was not the cavalry force they had previously scouted. With the urgent sound of the horns, the cavalry charged towards them with ghostly speed. They were clad in black armor, only their cold eyes visible. “Fire!” At the Song General’s command, the archers, already poised for battle, unleashed a volley of arrows. The arrows rained down like locusts, sweeping across the land. The Liao cavalrymen at the forefront were battered and bruised, but they quickly dispersed, skillfully avoiding the arrows and the fallen men and horses. The torrential rain of arrows continued, and Liao cavalrymen fell frequently, but this did nothing to slow their advance! As they drew ever closer to the palisades and the main gate, Lou Xiaowu clenched her fists nervously. Boom! A deafening roar, like a thunderclap, sent mud, blood, and flesh flying from a corner of the gate, then raining down like snow. But the cavalry behind them charged through this bloody storm. Chaos erupted in the camp! The Song army, already terrified of the Liao cavalry, was now thrown into disarray by their unstoppable advance into their camp. Some even began to flee in all directions. The explosions continued unabated. The Liao cavalry, however, showed no fear. Lou Xiaowu watched breathlessly for a moment, then stammered, “Are they not afraid of death…?” Who was not afraid of death? It was just that people were too easily swayed by the atmosphere. Under the Liao Ghost Cavalry’s unstoppable, death-defying momentum, all their bloodlust was ignited; how could they be afraid? “Protect the commander,” An Jiu ordered. The assassins beside her immediately obeyed and headed towards the defending general. Although the Liao Ghost Cavalry was fierce, their small numbers were not enough to overturn the Hebei camp, especially since it had just rained. If they were not setting fires to disrupt morale, they were probably trying to kill the commander. An Jiu followed them. After the Ghost Cavalry, an even more formidable cavalry charged forward. No one could withstand them; they seemed to slice through layers of obstacles with a single stroke, heading straight for the commander’s tent. The cavalryman at the very front of the charge, clad in black armor, suddenly raised his arm! A sudden burst of blue light erupted, like a gigantic umbrella instantly enveloping everything! The main camp collapsed with a deafening roar, engulfed in flames. Fortunately, the general who remained at the camp was not inside. An Jiu drew her Dragon-Subduing Bow. A crane’s cry pierced the air, and the Liao ghost cavalry at the forefront froze, falling straight to the ground. Then, behind him, appeared a lithe cavalryman. Her phoenix eyes reflected flames, displaying unparalleled ferocity. An Jiu frowned slightly. As she raised her bow again, she saw the cavalryman retrieve a large crossbow from behind her back, aiming it in the direction where An Jiu and the general stood. “Sister,” The cavalryman paused, startled upon seeing An Jiu. “Mei Ruyan!” An Jiu was somewhat surprised. This Mei Ruyan, who only knew how to curry favor, had actually led a cavalry raid herself! If today she had attacked the Liao camp, An Jiu would have shouted, “Good!” but this woman from the Song Dynasty had actually led Liao cavalry to attack the Song army camp! Lou Xiaowu was even more shocked than An Jiu. “Mei Ruyan, you homeless and countryless woman!” Mei Ruyan sneered, pulling the trigger of her weapon without hesitation. An Jiu flashed, pushing Lou Xiaowu out. The blinding light caused everyone’s vision to go white, resulting in temporary blindness. At this moment, the Song army had already assembled. The continuous reports of victories from the front greatly encouraged the soldiers in the rear. Therefore, after a brief period of panic, under the command of the defending general, they began to fight in an orderly manner. An Jiu’s men stayed close to the defending general, not giving the Ghost Cavalry and the assassins from Piaomiao Mountain Mansion any chance. An Jiu grabbed Lou Xiaowu. “Tell me, where are all those threads?!” The Liao cavalry had only opened a gap, but it was quickly blocked by the Song army. At this time, many Liao cavalrymen were still trying to break through the palisade. Lou Xiaowu pointed to the eastern fence. “Counting from the first log, there’s a thread every four logs.” Even with her excellent eyesight, An Jiu could not see the fine silk threads from this distance, but she could clearly see the fence! She drew her Dragon-Subduing Bow, channeling all her strength into the arrow. The arrow whistled through the night, striking a log with a loud thud! In an instant, the entire log shattered, scattering fragments across the ground. Boom! The first deafening thunderclap destroyed the entire row of fences, followed by a continuous barrage of explosions, instantly engulfing the nearby Liao cavalry! This saved An Jiu a lot of trouble. She was secretly pleased, but turning around, she saw Lou Xiaowu chasing Mei Ruyan towards the grain depot. In this weather, ordinary fire would not work for the grain depot, but if she used blue-fire crossbows, the fire at the commander’s camp earlier served as a cautionary tale! Lou Xiaowu’s martial arts skills were probably on par with Mei Ruyan’s, but her mind was not as deep. An Jiu quickly led her men to give chase. Neither Lou Xiaowu nor the supplies could be lost! Seeing she could not catch Mei Ruyan’s mount, Lou Xiaowu took out a small thunderbolt, infused it with her inner strength, and hurled it. With a deafening roar, Mei Ruyan was caught in the aftershock, feeling a tearing pain in her chest. Unable to withstand the jolting, she swayed and fell. Lou Xiaowu was also affected, but she could not care less. Seeing Mei Ruyan fall, she seized the opportunity to pounce and grab the crossbow. When An Jiu arrived, the two were already grappling. She drew her bow, only to find it impossible to aim. This time, the Liao Kingdom sent two cavalry units to attack the Hebei camp: one was the Ghost Cavalry, with about three or four hundred riders, and the other was a group of assassins from the Piaomiao Mountain Mansion, with about two hundred men. The people from Piaomiao Mountain Mansion deliberately disguised themselves as cavalry and did not attempt to conceal their movements, all to divert the scouts’ attention. The first wave of Liao cavalrymen to storm the camp had already suffered heavy losses, and those outside the camp were scattered by the triggered thunderclaps, yet these men showed no sign of retreat. They were clearly suicide soldiers. Other Ghost riders were already charging in, crashing through the Song soldiers in their path. An Jiu saw one of them holding a crossbow and immediately drew her bow and fired an arrow. So far, no one had been able to dodge An Jiu’s arrow, but that person vanished on horseback in a flash, and An Jiu’s arrow missed! An Jiu snorted. The second and third arrows were already fired. Although the person was fast, they never escaped An Jiu’s mental range. With her current sharp mental power, she could not only accurately pinpoint the target’s location but also sense the direction of their movement without even needing to calculate or observe. Bang! The heavily armored cavalryman plummeted from the sky. A single arrow to the throat, killing him instantly. An Jiu rushed forward to retrieve the crossbow, only to be astonished to find it empty! She turned back and saw Mei Ruyan tightly gripping Lou Xiaowu’s neck. Lou Xiaowu’s face was deathly pale, her lips bluish-purple; she was not suffocating. She was poisoned! An Jiu fired an arrow, sparing a vital spot. An Jiu rushed over, retrieved a pill for treating all poisons, and was about to feed it to her when she caught a glimpse of a smile in Mei Ruyan’s eyes. She turned and stomped on Mei Ruyan’s foot. “An antidote!” “Ha, sister, you are not so stupid,” Mei Ruyan laughed maniacally. “This is a poison specially prepared by Physician Ning for Physician Mo’s antidote. Taking it will not neutralize the poison; instead, it will enhance its toxicity.” “An antidote!” An Jiu tightened her grip, thankful she had not impulsively killed Mei Ruyan outright. “I will give you the antidote.” Mei Ruyan’s internal organs had just been injured by the deafening thunderbolt, and now, after being stomped on by An Jiu, she could not help but spit out a mouthful of blood. “Before that, I want to tell you something, sister. Chu Dingjiang…” An Jiu was about to strike when she heard this name and stopped abruptly. “He single-handedly killed two hundred experts,” Mei Ruyan laughed heartily, “but they all perished together!” An Jiu was shocked. “Nonsense! Give me the antidote!” Mei Ruyan’s laughter was too piercing. An Jiu kicked her hard in the face, drew her short sword, slashed open her armor, and searched for the antidote. “Mei Ruyan, you vile woman!” Lou Xiaowu struggled to her feet, snatched the crossbow from her hand, and dismantled it in a few swift movements. “Traitor! You do not deserve to be called a Song citizen!” “Bah! Do you think I care?!” Mei Ruyan was far too weak against An Jiu and unable to move under An Jiu’s restraint; she could only glare fiercely at Lou Xiaowu, saying, “When I was forcibly bought by the brothel, why did no one remember that I was a Song citizen? When I was locked up and beaten in the brothel, why did no one remember that I was a Song citizen? I am a Song citizen, and what has the Song Dynasty given me?!” Mei Ruyan had no home, no country; all her beauty and love were tied to one person, and she would not regret it even in death! “Ah Jiu! That man has a crossbow!” Lou Xiaowu exclaimed. “No arrows!” An Jiu had been fooled once before and would not believe it a second time. “He does! Trust me!” Black blood streamed from Lou Xiaowu’s nose; she was utterly weak, yet she clung tightly to An Jiu’s leg. “We cannot let him destroy the supplies!” Lou Xiaowu was an expert in this; if she said it was true, it was very likely true. An Jiu knocked Mei Ruyan unconscious. “Find the antidote first!” The man had already raised his hand to aim at the supplies. Without hesitation, An Jiu released two mental energy arrows. The man’s mental energy was damaged, and his body was temporarily unable to move. The other Song soldiers swarmed in and hacked him to death. Legs and remains were everywhere. The hundreds of cavalrymen who had stormed into the camp were quickly cut down. Some were still struggling in the front, but the fighting here had come to an end. An Jiu’s mental energy was rapidly depleted; she was utterly exhausted, her internal organs strained, and the injuries from her previous battle with Xiao Che had flared up. She felt completely drained, wanting nothing more than to collapse and sleep. However, she still wanted to ask Mei Ruyan about Chu Dingjiang. Mei Ruyan was Yelu Quancang’s woman, so her words carried some weight. Just as she turned around, she saw a Ghost Calvaryman, not quite dead, suddenly raise his hand. A large blue-fire crossbow was strapped to his arm. With its power, if an arrow were to be fired, it could instantly destroy the entire granary and even affect the nearby armory. An Jiu was about to draw her bow when she saw Lou Xiaowu get up and thrust an arrow she had just removed from the crossbow into its chamber. Chu Dingjiang had said that guarding the camp was a minor matter; survival was paramount. In his heart, nothing in this world could compare to her life; she had to live, and he would not allow her to personally risk her life. But An Jiu did not have time to think of any other solutions. Almost instinctively, she mustered all her strength, rushing forward like a beam of light to grab Lou Xiaowu and pull her aside. A burst of light erupted, instantly engulfing their figures. Everyone felt the ground shake beneath their feet; those within ten chi were not spared, blood and flesh flying everywhere, raining down like a storm. The world before their eyes turned pure white. An Jiu felt that everything was over, but she still regretted not seeing Chu Dingjiang. The Song army pressed on with renewed vigor. In just two months, news of victories came one after another. In the Bianjing court, another round of debate arose over the issue of food supplies. According to regulations, the authority to dispatch troops rested with the Privy Council; Ling Ziyue’s attack on the Liao Kingdom without warning constituted unauthorized military action! A capital offense! The Emperor was furious. His anger was not directed at Ling Ziyue’s unauthorized military action, but rather at the court officials who feared the Liao Kingdom would retaliate once it recovered. “You! You! You!” The Emperor pointed at the ministers who opposed continuing the war. “If any of you can guarantee to reclaim the Sixteen Prefectures of Yan and Yun for me, I will immediately issue an edict summoning Ling Ziyue back to court for trial!” The hall was deathly silent. The Emperor sneered. “If you cannot, then keep your mouths shut! Since I dared to appoint Ling Ziyue as the commander of three routes, I dare to allow him to disobey imperial orders while in the field!” The Emperor longed to lead the army himself; he had already suffered enough humiliation as a prince. This time, he could not let the opportunity slip by. If Ling Ziyue truly usurped the throne, it would be his bad luck and inferior skills! However, it was also time to promote someone who could restrain Ling Ziyue. His gaze swept over the court officials below, lingering on Hua Rongtian. “I have heard that the garrison of Hexi County rendered outstanding service in defending the Hebei camp, with their two hundred soldiers suffering heavy casualties, a truly admirable feat,” the Emperor said, looking at Hua Rongtian. “Wu Lingyuan, the magistrate of Hexi County, is a protégé of Minister Hua, is he not?” Hua Rongtian stepped forward and bowed, replying, “Your Majesty, indeed.” “Excellent,” the Emperor praised. With this simple word of approval, everyone knew that the Hua family was on the rise again. … Three months after the start of the war, the Liao Kingdom sent envoys to Bianjing to negotiate peace. In truth, the Liao Kingdom was not powerless to resist. The Song army had been weak for a long time and could not be transformed into an elite force overnight. However, the Liao Emperor was seriously ill, the national advisor’s fate was uncertain, the Northern King was imprisoned, and there was no one to restrain the tribal leaders, each harboring ambitions. The entire Liao Kingdom’s internal affairs had become precarious. And all of this stemmed from Yelu Quancang’s coma. At the Liao-Song border. Mo Sigui lay leisurely in the tall grass, fanning himself. Beside him lay a person on the verge of death. All the sunlight seemed to be drawn to this person’s face; even in this wretched state, his beauty remained undiminished. When Mo Sigui saw this face again, it felt like a lifetime had passed. Years ago, a man named Gu Jinghong had asked him to take his heart’s blood; years later, he had taken the heart’s blood of a man who looked exactly like Gu Jinghong. “Divine Physician,” Yelu Jinglie said, “Had Jinghong ever suffered as I have?” Whether it was because he was speaking kindly on the verge of death or because Mo Sigui had concealed the fact that his heart’s blood was poisoned, Yelu Jinglie, who was usually cruel and eccentric, spoke to him with unusual gentleness. Yelu Quancang was nearing death, yet Mo Sigui remained unmoved. Hearing this, his hand, which had been fanning himself, paused. “Him? He suffered far more than you, died a far more gruesome death, his face disfigured beyond recognition, and he died by his enemy’s sword.” Gu Jinghong knew perfectly well that after obtaining the heart’s blood, he was no match for Yelu Quancang and Yelu Huangwu, yet he still went to assassinate them. His purpose was not to kill anyone but to make them witness firsthand the destruction of the medicine person they had painstakingly nurtured for over twenty years! He destroyed himself, but also destroyed their hope. Yelu Jinglie had sought some solace in his dying moments, but this man deliberately rubbed salt into his wounds. This was probably retribution. He smirked. “I know the woman you’ve always loved; her name is Lou Mingyue, is it not?” Mo Sigui’s face darkened. “A life devoted to a single drink, both unconventional and earnest,” Yelu Jinglie said, smiling. A casual remark pierced Mo Sigui’s heart, leaving him utterly devastated. “You should have realized long ago that you would never love another woman in your life but her. Even if you were separated by death, you would not be so filled with regret now.” It was just a statement of the truth; why was he so hurt? Mo Sigui angrily retorted, “You, Yelu family members, are all so vengeful; you all deserve a bad end!” “Lou Mingyue is one of us,” Yelu Jinglie said, coughing up blood with a smile. Mo Sigui ignored him. “In my life, I’ve never truly thanked anyone, but now I want to say thank you to you. Dying here is much more dignified than I imagined,” he said. Mo Sigui scoffed, “Do not promise me anything about a next life. I am too busy for a next life; there’s a whole line of people saying they will repay my kindness in the next; it is not your turn.” Yelu Jinglie scoffed, “Too much. So far…you are the only one qualified to hear…hear me say thank you. I only wish… to become a wisp of wind after death, never to be reincarnated.” He faced the light, his beautiful phoenix eyes holding a triumphant smile, gradually losing focus. Yet, under the sunlight, those eyes remained dazzling. “Someone as wicked as you, even as a wisp of wind, would be a chilling breeze.” Mo Sigui touched the ashes hidden in his bosom. “So many people promised me a next life; I did not believe it before, but if the bonds of this life can truly lead to a meeting in the next, I only promise you.” He did not avenge Elder Qi back then because he knew Elder Qi wanted him to achieve something in medicine, not waste time on other things. But Mingyue, what did you want me to do? There was nothing else to do. The hatred in his heart was so unbearable to keep hidden, yet even after revenge, he found no real satisfaction. When Yelu Jinglie’s rebellion failed, he ingested a blood-poisoning agent. This poison not only destroyed the original medicinal properties but also remained in his blood. However, Yelu Jinglie only knew one side of the story; the poison required years to take hold in the heart. In other words, Yelu Jinglie’s blood was not enough to kill Yelu Quancang. Mo Sigui reached out and closed his eyes, whispering, “But you do not need to worry. I came here specifically to make amends.” This time, he had over a dozen physicians overseeing the blood draw. Although the opportunity to poison was less, there was nothing he could not do if he wanted to. Upon arriving in Liao, Mo Sigui pretended to know nothing, insisting that Yelu Jinglie had forced Lou Mingyue to her death. He offered to help with the medical treatment, but afterwards, Yelu Jinglie had to be handed over to him for punishment. Those people indeed believed he had mistakenly identified the mastermind. Mo Sigui succeeded because Yelu Quancang was already unconscious before taking the medicine. He was shrewd his entire life, capable of manipulating events at will, yet in the end, even his life was in the hands of the fools around him. No matter how hard he fought, he could not fight against fate. The ending was beyond his control, but the process was in everyone’s hands. Ultimately, he still regretted it. Even if his enemies died a thousand times, it would not dispel the slightest pain in his heart. “Elder, you said, ‘Do not betray love’; I thought it was a simple matter.” Of all the people he knew, only An Jiu truly upheld this word, but that person probably did not even know what love was. Mo Sigui lay back down, flicking open his folding fan to cover his face. In the eleventh month. Bianjing was already covered in a blanket of snow. A woman in a dark blue robe emerged from the palace, holding an umbrella. As the only female general of the Song Dynasty, even with only a fifth-rank official position, she was still the most dazzling one. The current Emperor was a very decisive person. He wanted to cultivate someone who could rival Ling Ziyue. However, Hua Rongtian was a civil official, and he also needed someone he could control on the military side. But he had many concerns about the candidate until Fourteenth Young Lady stood out in the battle of the Hebei camp. The Emperor recalled Fourteenth Young Lady, who was recuperating from her injuries. Upon seeing her, he immediately recognized her as Chu Dingjiang’s wife. Her martial arts skills were formidable, comparable to any man’s, and she had seemingly forgotten her past after the explosion. He secretly investigated and confirmed that Chu Dingjiang had perished, surrounded by hundreds of Liao experts. While the Emperor felt regret, he was also secretly pleased. Only with such a formidable strategist as Chu Dingjiang dead could he confidently use Fourteenth Young Lady. A woman, alone and vulnerable, could be easily controlled; even if she later held significant military power, there were countless reasons to withdraw her. Therefore, the Emperor devised ways to elevate her, transferring her back to Bianjing to a high-ranking position in the Military Affairs Department, intending to send her out for further training after her recovery… Many in the court could not fathom the Emperor’s intentions, assuming that such outstanding beauty would ultimately lead her to become one of the palace’s consorts. An Jiu herself knew that although her future was fraught with peril, it was also limitless. However, she felt she had lost the most important thing in her life. According to Lou Xiaowu, she saw a Ghost Cavalryman preparing to fire a crossbow bolt, but it was too late to stop him. So she picked up some scattered bolts and stuck them into the crossbow chamber to block the arrowheads, causing the two bolts to collide and explode. An Jiu saved Lou Xiaowu with incredible speed but was also severely injured by the explosion. Upon waking, she forgot everything from her past. During her months of recuperation, fragments of memories occasionally surfaced. The most vivid memory was of a woman with phoenix eyes laughing maniacally amidst the flames of war, seemingly saying something. But no matter how hard she tried to recall, she could not remember what the woman had said. An Jiu surmised that this must have been something that happened before the explosion that left a deep impression on her. The snow fell heavily. An Jiu stood alone for a long time when a carriage stopped in front of her. Hua Rongjian leaned out of the carriage. “Ah Jiu, want to eat?” An Jiu stared at his features, lost in thought. “Hey!” Hua Rongjian leaned out halfway and flicked her forehead with his finger. The gesture was so familiar; it seemed to stir up memories! An Jiu felt a buzzing in her head. She swayed, then fell flat on her back in the snow, her umbrella blown far away by the wind. She stared wide-eyed at the swirling snowflakes, motionless, desperately trying to grasp the fleeting memory in her mind. “Hey! Hey! Ah Jiu! Fourteenth!” Hua Rongjian ran down from the carriage, calling anxiously. An Jiu snapped out of her daze and snapped, “What are you yelling for? I was thinking!” Hua Rongjian sighed in relief and slumped down beside her. He exhaled puffs of steam, “Is this how you think? You scared the hell out of me.” An Jiu got up, put her hands on her hips, and walked straight ahead. Hua Rongjian ordered the coachman to fetch an umbrella and held it over her head. The two walked for a while, then An Jiu said, “You should go back first. I want to walk alone.” Hua Rongjian sighed and shoved the umbrella into her hand. “Go back early. You are a big shot now; many people have designs on you.” “Alright,” she replied absentmindedly, turning to leave. The streets were a blanket of white; it was nearing evening, and there were not many pedestrians. Hua Rongjian watched her walk alone on the Imperial Street, his smile gradually fading. “Ah Jiu, even if you do not remember him, no one can replace him.” Houses lined both sides of the Imperial Street. The wind was gentle, and goose-feather snowflakes drifted down leisurely. The sky was beginning to darken, and red lanterns hung outside the shops, casting a warm orange glow over the world. She was a female general, a master of the Transcendent Realm, the strongest woman in the Song Dynasty. Yet, probably no one in the world knew that she was now filled with confusion and utter loneliness. Looking out, the Imperial Street seemed so long. When would she ever reach the end? An Jiu aimlessly wandered until she reached the entrance of Pan Tower Street, where she suddenly sensed a familiar mental force faintly emerging. She followed the guiding thread slowly. She ventured deeper into the alley next to Jubaozhai, circling several times before finally finding a small wonton stall. The stall owner was a tall man, so tall that even bending over to look at the wontons in the pot seemed a bit strenuous. He wore a dark blue robe, his hair and beard were neatly trimmed, his face was sharply defined, and his features were handsome. He did not seem like the kind of person who would set up a stall in the snow for a few coins. The rising steam enveloped his face. As if noticing her approach, he naturally looked up and smiled warmly at her, asking in a deep voice, “Would you like some wontons, young lady?” Looking at this face that seemed both familiar and unfamiliar, An Jiu felt a lump in her throat, a slight pain. She slowly walked over and sat down at the table. He said nothing, simply ladled a steaming bowl of wontons in front of her, and turned to leave. An Jiu grabbed his sleeve. “Uncle, I…” The man stiffened, turned back, and looked at her with emotion, his deep black eyes sparkling like stars. An Jiu’s eyes reddened. “You are just like my mother.” This brat! Chu Dingjiang, who prided himself on his good temper and patience, could not resist the urge to grab her by the collar and throw her out of the alley. From the moment she found her purpose in life, he had been planning for her, devising ways to make Ling Ziyue the commander of the three armies, changing the political landscape, arranging for her to achieve military merit in the rescue of the Hebei camp, and even mobilizing his long-hidden forces to help her. Finally, he painstakingly faked his death so the Emperor would trust her to use him. If nothing unexpected happened, she would embark on the bright path he had paved! And he, even if he had to live in anonymity for the rest of his life, would not care. Even with Mo Sigui’s antidote to the power-enhancing drug and after dealing with those pseudo-experts, he would still have a slim chance of survival. But she, with reinforcements arriving only slightly late, had already put herself in grave danger. Chu Dingjiang, severely injured and to make his feigned death seem more convincing, had refrained from sending her any messages for over a month. During that time, he was deeply worried about what shocking things she might do in her anxiety. Finally, he learned that he had been presumptuous; she, in her serious injury, had completely forgotten everything! All this planning and scheming, and this brat was now eating wontons and calling for her mother—what kind of situation was this? Whom was he working so hard for anyway? However… Looking at her red eyes and nose, Chu Dingjiang could only let out a sigh, his turbulent emotions turning into a gentle pat on the head. Even though she did not remember who he was, she still had the instinct to cling to him. She had their relationship etched into her very bones; what was there to complain about? An Jiu’s nose stung from the steam; the warmth was so familiar and so dear to her. Clinging to a sliver of hope, she asked, “Uncle, do you have a long-lost daughter?” Chu Dingjiang, having just calmed himself, was suddenly struck again. He tossed a rag onto the table and sat imposingly opposite her, the warm firelight illuminating their faces. His gaze was intense as he stared at her. “Uncle does not have a long-lost daughter. Uncle lost a woman who bore me a daughter.” Snowflakes fell silently around the shed, steam rising from the bowl. An Jiu’s cheeks burned. She lowered her head, stirred her wontons for a moment, and whispered, “Should I be angry? But I am really enjoying being teased by you…” She looked up at Chu Dingjiang, puzzled. Their eyes met, and in an instant, Chu Dingjiang leaned in and kissed her lips. In that instant, the alleyway became a world unto itself, snow blurring time.
