Dancing under the autumn moon, riding the river breeze,  both unrestrained and true to themselves. Sword in hand, inquiring the route; the road is rugged;  leaning on the clouds, my feelings rising and falling. Looking back on my life, realizing it all was just  recklessly drinking and getting drunk to forget my worries. The autumn equinox, the bright moon, stirring longing;  the river’s strings flutter, the wind singing, and ripping Once possessing boundless ambition that soared to the heavens,  and also once living a carefree and unfettered life.

Extra Chapter Her Appearance

The glazed lanterns of Guanghua Palace swayed in the night wind, casting long, shallow shadows in the snow. In the warm pavilion, the young Emperor, dressed in magnificent robes, reclined on the bed, a eunuch serving him a hangover soup. “Is the Deputy Commander in such a hurry to return?” The Emperor set down his teacup, his gaze indifferent as he looked at An Jiu. Just now, after the grand banquet, he saw her hurrying out. The Emperor had already discovered that the Mei family had all moved beyond the Great Wall and that they had no family in Bianjing. An Jiu’s eyelids drooped. “This subject is not used to such occasions.” “Actually, I met the Commander’s husband years ago.” The Emperor’s gaze remained fixed on her. An Jiu was not good at lying, but she could remain completely emotionless. She did not intend to waste time beating around the bush. “Your Majesty dares to employ me, which shows you are a wise and decisive ruler. You had such courage when the Song Dynasty was in turmoil, so why are you becoming increasingly timid now that things are stable? Rest assured, not everyone is after your position.” “Insolence!” a eunuch beside the Emperor shouted shrilly. The Emperor laughed instead. “You are right. But I must understand, why would a woman like you willingly serve as my puppet?” “I used to be a puppet too, but I did not like being in the dark; I wanted to bask in the sun.” An Jiu raised her eyes, meeting the Emperor’s gaze directly. Her gaze, as tangible as a blade, made him tense. If she wanted to kill him now, it would be incredibly easy. The Emperor suddenly relaxed. “Go.” An Jiu bowed and left the warm pavilion. In a short time, the Emperor had repeatedly tested An Jiu. Perhaps, as An Jiu said, when the empire was in turmoil, one could risk everything, but once things were stable, one was constantly worried about being overthrown. No emperor desired to relinquish their hold on the throne. An Jiu’s figure disappeared into the snow, arriving at the palace gates in an instant, leaving her followers far behind, and went straight to Jubaozhai. A pot was already set up in the hall, steaming hot, and Sheng Changying and Mei Yanran were busy preparing. Mo Sigui leaned back in a round chair, looking half-dead. Xiao Yue lay at his feet, Da Jiu squatted by the table, staring intently at the meat on the plate, and Lou Xiaowu used a rattle to tease the chubby-faced child in Zhu Pianxian’s arms. Chu Dingjiang was the first to see An Jiu and came over to take her hand. “Your Excellency is back!” Sui Yuntong led Hu Niu to her feet to greet her. Mo Sigui raised his eyelids slightly and grunted twice. “Ah Jiu!” Lou Xiaowu shoved the rattle drum into Zhu Pianxian’s hands, then rushed over and hugged An Jiu’s arm. “Why are you only back now? Has the Emperor appointed you to a post at the border?” “He has not said yet,” An Jiu replied. Lou Xiaowu puffed out her cheeks. She glanced timidly at Chu Dingjiang. “Brother-in-law said the Emperor will definitely send you to the border…” Chu Dingjiang was not usually inclined to talk to people, but Lou Xiaowu’s “brother-in-law” made him quite pleased. “Just wait patiently. It will take at least three to five months, maybe a year.” “Ah, a year!” Lou Xiaowu exclaimed. “Then I’d better not count on you.” It would take Lou Xiaowu a year to fully recover from her injuries, and she could not do without Mo Sigui until then. If An Jiu went to the border, Mo Sigui would definitely follow…then she could see Ling Ziyue sooner. And then, Chu Dingjiang would not have to hide as he did now. “What’s the rush? Do not worry. I think General Ling will eventually fall for you!” Zhu Pianxian laughed. “How could I not be anxious? I am very anxious!” Lou Xiaowu said with no embarrassment, her voice filled with melancholy. “He’s already this old; every year apart means one less year left!” Mo Sigui stirred. He slowly sat up, rubbed his slightly disheveled hair, yawned, and swayed out. “Where is the Divine Physician going?” Sui Yuntong asked. “Tired. Going to sleep,” Mo Sigui said. “Eat first, then sleep,” Sui Yuntong said. Mo Sigui did not answer, swaying as he left. “I will go see him.” An Jiu chased after him. Since Lou Mingyue’s death, his insomnia had miraculously disappeared. Whether it was due to his state of mind or the excessive use of sleeping pills, he now slept at least seven or eight hours a day. He seemed capable of falling asleep anytime, anywhere, unless he was handling his medicines. He had become increasingly withdrawn, especially disliking crowded places. The courtyard was brightly lit, and the crisp air of the snow made him clear-headed. Mo Sigui quickened his pace. Because the more awake he was, the more painful it became. An Jiu silently followed him to his room, which was piled high with medicinal herbs, before speaking, “Mo Sigui.” “What are you doing following me?” Mo Sigui waved his hand. “Go eat.” “Move to the valley,” An Jiu said. Mo Sigui brought back Lou Mingyue’s ashes and buried them in a beautiful valley. An Jiu bought the valley to avoid the disturbance of strangers passing by. An Jiu originally thought leaving him here would prevent him from being lonely, but the more lively the days, the more isolated he seemed. Mo Sigui used to be such a carefree person, but now even a joke from Lou Xiaowu could trigger his heartache. An Jiu finally understood that leaving him here was an extremely cruel thing to do. Mo Sigui raised an eyebrow, his peach blossom eyes slightly narrowed, and said irritably, “My legs are my own; do not worry about things that do not concern you! Go away, do not disturb my sleep.” Bang! The door closed. An Jiu stood there for a moment but ultimately did not force him. An Jiu returned to the hall, where steam rose, but the atmosphere was somewhat heavy. “Did I say something that upset him?” Lou Xiaowu asked. “He’s crazy; ignore him.” An Jiu sat down at the table. “Let’s eat; I am starving.” Everyone took their seats. Zhu Pianxian sat next to An Jiu. Seeing the tense atmosphere and An Jiu’s frantic eating while the others hesitated to eat, Zhu Pianxian became furious. She tapped the edge of the table with her chopsticks. “Do not eat yet!” An Jiu stopped, her cheeks puffed out, and turned to look at her with a frown. “I work myself to the bone to earn money, and you spendthrift! Tell me! Where did the 150,000 taels of gold go?!” Zhu Pianxian asked, heartbroken. She thought she was particularly good at making money, but it turned out her two employers were squandering it much faster than she was earning it! An Jiu mumbled, “I only spent 50,000 taels of gold to buy a few hills for Mo Sigui. My husband spent 100,000 taels last time to buy information.” Just like that, Chu Dingjiang was sold out… “Ahem,” Chu Dingjiang cleared his throat. “The person who took the money will not live past this year. This money is tied up in a dead man’s account. If anyone takes the money to exchange, they will be arrested and sent to the authorities. We will just redo the accounts.” “You are a cunning old fox.” Zhu Pianxian nodded in satisfaction. “At least you have some conscience; this is all hard-earned money!” Chu Dingjiang said, “You are not allowed to say the word ‘old’ in front of me from now on.” Everyone burst into laughter. The atmosphere in the room finally eased a bit, but a corner of the courtyard seemed frozen solid, never to thaw. Mo Sigui had fallen asleep, her image as clear as it was yesterday.
